b: A.J. Finn is the pen name of Dan Mallory, who was vice president and executive editor at William Morrow but now writes full time. Mallory has written for numerous publications, including the Los Angeles Times, the…
f: A.J. Finn is the pen name of Dan Mallory, who was vice president and executive editor at William Morrow but now writes full time. Mallory has written for numerous publications, including the Los Angeles Times, the Washington Post and The Times Literary Supplement . He is an Oxford graduate with a life-long love of the thriller noir genre and a particular appreciation of Hitchcockian cinema.

b: A.K. Bhattacharya is currently the Editorial Director at Business Standard , India’s leading business newspaper. He previously served as Editor of Business Standard and as Editor of The Pioneer . His first book on…
f: A.K. Bhattacharya is currently the Editorial Director at Business Standard , India’s leading business newspaper. He previously served as Editor of Business Standard and as Editor of The Pioneer . His first book on economic disruptions, The Rise of Goliath: Twelve Disruptions That Changed India , was published in 2019, followed by a three-volume series on India’s Finance Ministers, also published between 2023 and 2025. He co-edited a Festschrift titled A World in Flux in honour of Shankar Acharya. His long-running column, Raisina Hill , published in Business Standard , explores government affairs and economic policy.

b: A.R. Venkatachalapathy , Professor at MIDS Chennai, is a recipient of the VKRV Rao Prize and the Iyal Viridhu. His English works include Swadeshi Steam , Who Owns That Song? and In Those Days There Was No Coffee .
f: A.R. Venkatachalapathy , Professor at MIDS Chennai, is a recipient of the VKRV Rao Prize and the Iyal Viridhu. His English works include Swadeshi Steam , Who Owns That Song? and In Those Days There Was No Coffee .

b: Aadil Raza Mansoori is a prominent Urdu poet, writer and editor. His edited anthology Khidki Mein Khawab, is considered as one of best young poet collections by the Urdu fraternity and his poetry collection Sannate ki…
f: Aadil Raza Mansoori is a prominent Urdu poet, writer and editor. His edited anthology Khidki Mein Khawab, is considered as one of best young poet collections by the Urdu fraternity and his poetry collection Sannate ki Parchhaain has been widely acknowledged in India and abroad. Mansoori has been awarded the prestigious Akhtar Sheerani Award 2023.

b: Aakriti Patni is a dynamic entrepreneur and media professional, recognised for her innovative spirit and passion for storytelling. After earning her master’s degree in journalism from City, University of London, she…
f: Aakriti Patni is a dynamic entrepreneur and media professional, recognised for her innovative spirit and passion for storytelling. After earning her master’s degree in journalism from City, University of London, she launched her career as a journalist with renowned publications such as Vogue India, building a strong foundation in media and communications. Transitioning to leadership roles at her family office, RAAY Global Investments, Aakriti spearheaded major projects in media and entertainment, including the critically acclaimed film Poorna. Driven by her vision to amplify global authors & diverse voices, she founded The Bombay Circle Press—an independent, modern publishing house committed to redefining Indian publishing and bringing global perspectives to local readers. Through her work, Aakriti continues to empower writers and foster a vibrant literary community, championing creativity and inclusivity.

b: Aanchal Malhotra is an artist and oral historian working with memory and material culture. She received a BFA in Traditional Printmaking and Art History from the Ontario College of Art and Design, Toronto and an MFA in…
f: Aanchal Malhotra is an artist and oral historian working with memory and material culture. She received a BFA in Traditional Printmaking and Art History from the Ontario College of Art and Design, Toronto and an MFA in Studio Art from Concordia University, Montréal. She is the author of Remnants of a Separation: A History of the Partition Through Material Memory . Malhotra is also the co-founder of the Museum of Material Memory, a digital repository of material culture from the Indian subcontinent, tracing family histories and social ethnography through heirlooms, collectibles and objects of antiquity.

b: Aarathi Prasad is the author of 3 books including Silk: A History in Three Metamorphoses, and In The Bonesetter’s Waiting Room: Travels Through Indian Medicine . She is National Geographic’s Regional Manager for…
f: Aarathi Prasad is the author of 3 books including Silk: A History in Three Metamorphoses, and In The Bonesetter’s Waiting Room: Travels Through Indian Medicine . She is National Geographic’s Regional Manager for Europe and Western Asia and an Honorary Research Fellow in Genetics, Evolution and Environment at University College London.

b: Aasha Kapur Mehta is a Professor of Economics. Her books, articles and working papers are on different dimensions of poverty and poverty dynamics, multidimensional deprivation, human and gender development indicators…
f: Aasha Kapur Mehta is a Professor of Economics. Her books, articles and working papers are on different dimensions of poverty and poverty dynamics, multidimensional deprivation, human and gender development indicators and data gaps, gender budgeting, reviewing policies for gender inclusion, ill health, poverty and care. She Chairs the Centre for Gender Studies, Institute for Human Development, Delhi.

b: Aasha Mehreen Amin is the Head of Editorial and Opinion, and a Senior Deputy Editor of The Daily Star, Bangladesh, and has been working for the paper for the last 31 years. She was former editor of The Star, a weekly…
f: Aasha Mehreen Amin is the Head of Editorial and Opinion, and a Senior Deputy Editor of The Daily Star, Bangladesh, and has been working for the paper for the last 31 years. She was former editor of The Star, a weekly magazine of The Daily Star for which she also wrote a satirical column – ‘Postscript’. Amin currently writes on human rights and social trends in her column ‘No Strings Attached’.

b: Abdul Wahed Chowdhury , widely known as a pioneer war hero of Bangladesh, remained a sound naval officer of the Executive Branch of the Navy during his 35 years of service. He led the Operation Jackpot at Chittagong…
f: Abdul Wahed Chowdhury , widely known as a pioneer war hero of Bangladesh, remained a sound naval officer of the Executive Branch of the Navy during his 35 years of service. He led the Operation Jackpot at Chittagong Port and cut the lifeline of Pakistani Forces by sinking ships in the Karnaphuli river with limpet mine. Chowdhury also represented Bangladesh in 1995 for South-East Asia Symposium under Pacific Command in Hawaii, Japan, South Korea and Singapore and received the Best Award for International Human Relationship. He was highly praised for leading the submarine from France and subsequently leading the Naval Commandos for operations. He was awarded the highest gallantry award, BU and BB, as a recognition.

b: H.E. Abdullah Mohammed Abu Shawesh was born in 1970 in the Nusayrat Refugee Camp in Gaza. He grew up and completed his early education in UNRWA schools before moving to the West Bank to pursue higher studies. He…
f: H.E. Abdullah Mohammed Abu Shawesh was born in 1970 in the Nusayrat Refugee Camp in Gaza. He grew up and completed his early education in UNRWA schools before moving to the West Bank to pursue higher studies. He attended Birzeit University, where he earned a Bachelor’s degree in Economics with a minor in Business Administration in 1997, followed by a Master’s degree in Economics in 2003. He also completed a Professional Diploma in Marketing at Birzeit University’s, in addition to undertaking certified Project Management Professional (PMP) training in 2007.

b: Abdulnasser Alshaali was recently appointed as the Ambassador of the UAE to India. He was previously the Assistant Minister for Economic and Trade Affairs within the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International…
f: Abdulnasser Alshaali was recently appointed as the Ambassador of the UAE to India. He was previously the Assistant Minister for Economic and Trade Affairs within the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation.

b: Abdulrazak Gurnah is the winner of the Nobel Prize in Literature 2021. He is the author of ten novels: Memory of Departure, Pilgrims Way, Dottie, Paradise (shortlisted for the Booker Prize and the Whitbread Award),…
f: Abdulrazak Gurnah is the winner of the Nobel Prize in Literature 2021. He is the author of ten novels: Memory of Departure, Pilgrims Way, Dottie, Paradise (shortlisted for the Booker Prize and the Whitbread Award), Admiring Silence, By the Sea (longlisted for the Booker Prize and shortlisted for the Los Angeles Times Book Award ), Desertion (shortlisted for the Commonwealth Writers’ Prize) The Last Gift, Gravel Heart, and Afterlives , which was shortlisted for the Orwell Prize for Fiction 2021 and longlisted for the Walter Scott Prize. He was Professor of English at the University of Kent, and was a Man Booker Prize judge in 2016. He lives in Canterbury.

b: Abeer Kapoor is a game designer, author, and founder of Civic Games Lab, a games-for-social-change studio. He and his team design and deploy participatory tools such as games, simulations and scenarios to tackle complex…
f: Abeer Kapoor is a game designer, author, and founder of Civic Games Lab, a games-for-social-change studio. He and his team design and deploy participatory tools such as games, simulations and scenarios to tackle complex challenges in governance, sustainability, digitalisation and public health. He is the author of The Most Notorious Jailbreakers, co-author of Zoraver and the Lost Gods , and a former German Chancellor Fellow. During the fellowship, he developed a curriculum on building game ecosystems in developing nations.

b: Abeer Y. Hoque is a Nigerian-born Bangladeshi-American writer and photographer. Her books include The Long Way Home, a travel photography and poetry monograph, The Lovers and the Leavers, a collection of linked stories…
f: Abeer Y. Hoque is a Nigerian-born Bangladeshi-American writer and photographer. Her books include The Long Way Home, a travel photography and poetry monograph, The Lovers and the Leavers, a collection of linked stories and the memoir Olive Witch . See more at olivewitch.com .

b: Abhay K is the author of eight poetry collections and editor of The Bloomsbury Anthology of Great Indian Poems, CAPITALS and New Brazilian Poems. His forthcoming poetry collection is titled The Alphabets of Latin…
f: Abhay K is the author of eight poetry collections and editor of The Bloomsbury Anthology of Great Indian Poems, CAPITALS and New Brazilian Poems. His forthcoming poetry collection is titled The Alphabets of Latin America. His 'Earth Anthem' has been translated into over 50 languages. He received SAARC Literary Award 2013 and was invited to record his poems at the Library of Congress, Washington DC in 2018.

b: Starting in 1978 with his Oscar-nominated short film, An Encounter with Faces, Vidhu Vinod Chopra has won countless awards over the years for his path-breaking work as director, screenwriter and producer. His unique…
f: Starting in 1978 with his Oscar-nominated short film, An Encounter with Faces, Vidhu Vinod Chopra has won countless awards over the years for his path-breaking work as director, screenwriter and producer. His unique approach to filmmaking is evident in films such as Parinda, Khamosh, 1942: A Love Story and in the films that can today be defined as the modern classics of our era, Munna Bhai M.B.B.S. and 3 Idiots. In 1992, Abhijat Joshi wrote a critically acclaimed play , A Shaft of Sunlight , that Chopra happened to see in Birmingham. Their subsequent encounter was the start of an enduring and fruitful collaboration resulting in films like Mission Kashmir, Eklavya, and most recently, Shikara. The team of director Rajkumar Hirani, writer Joshi and producer Chopra has also helmed major blockbusters in recent years like Lage Raho Munna Bhai, 3 Idiots, PK and Sanju.

b: Abhijit Vinayak Banerjee is the Ford Foundation International Professor of Economics at MIT and co-founder of the Abdul Latif Jameel Poverty Action Lab (J-PAL). He has authored numerous articles and six books, including…
f: Abhijit Vinayak Banerjee is the Ford Foundation International Professor of Economics at MIT and co-founder of the Abdul Latif Jameel Poverty Action Lab (J-PAL). He has authored numerous articles and six books, including Poor Economics , which won the Goldman Sachs Business Book of the Year, and Good Economics for Hard Times . A Nobel laureate, Banerjee is a trustee of Save the Children USA and the British Museum.

b: Abhijit Kothari is a businessman and academic specialising in the relationship between communities and economic strategies. He has translated The Glory of Patan by K.M. Munshi and his forthcoming translations of the…
f: Abhijit Kothari is a businessman and academic specialising in the relationship between communities and economic strategies. He has translated The Glory of Patan by K.M. Munshi and his forthcoming translations of the same Patan trilogy include The Lord and Master of Gujarat (2018) and The King of Kings (2019).

b: Abhijit Vinayak Banerjee is the Ford Foundation International Professor of Economics at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology and a founder and co-Director of the Abdul Latif Jameel Poverty Action Lab (J-PAL) along…
f: Abhijit Vinayak Banerjee is the Ford Foundation International Professor of Economics at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology and a founder and co-Director of the Abdul Latif Jameel Poverty Action Lab (J-PAL) along with Esther Duflo and Sendhil Mullainathan. His latest book is Good Economics for Hard Times, co-authored with Professor Esther Duflo. Banerjee is a 2019 co-winner of the Nobel Prize for Economics.

b: Abhimanyu Singh Arha is an Environmental Historian who has taught at St. Stephen’s College, Delhi, Maharaja Ganga Singh University, Bikaner and University of Rajasthan, Jaipur. He graduated from St. Stephen’s…
f: Abhimanyu Singh Arha is an Environmental Historian who has taught at St. Stephen’s College, Delhi, Maharaja Ganga Singh University, Bikaner and University of Rajasthan, Jaipur. He graduated from St. Stephen’s College and holds a PhD from Jawaharlal Nehru University. His research area includes studying the nexus between ecology, trade and state-building and the history of diplomacy and self-writings. His research papers have been published widely. Arha writes both verse and prose in Rajasthani, his mother-tongue.

b: Abhinandan Sekhri is co-founder of Newslaundry , which has won several awards for its journalism including the Ramnath Goenka and RedInk Award. He is also co-founder of Small Screen, makers of award-winning shows like…
f: Abhinandan Sekhri is co-founder of Newslaundry , which has won several awards for its journalism including the Ramnath Goenka and RedInk Award. He is also co-founder of Small Screen, makers of award-winning shows like Highway On My Plate and OMG India . He worked for TV Today Network from 1995 to 1999 that made Newstrack and Aaj Tak and was the chief scriptwriter for news-satire show Gustaakhi Maaf and The Great Indian Tamsha on NDTV. Sekhri has also worked as a camera assistant for Mira Nair’s award-winning feature film Monsoon Wedding .

b: Abhinav Chandrachud is an advocate who practices at the Bombay High Court. He graduated from Harvard Law School where he was a Dana Scholar and from Stanford Law School where he was a Franklin Family Scholar. He has…
f: Abhinav Chandrachud is an advocate who practices at the Bombay High Court. He graduated from Harvard Law School where he was a Dana Scholar and from Stanford Law School where he was a Franklin Family Scholar. He has worked as an associate attorney at Gibson, Dunn & Crutcher, a global law firm, and as a paralegal at AZB & Partners, a leading law firm in India. He is the author of Republic of Rhetoric: Free Speech and the Constitution of India, An Independent, Colonial Judiciary, The Informal Constitution and Due Process of Law .

b: Abhishek Choudhary is a bilingual writer best known for his two-part study of former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee and the Hindu Right. An NIF Fellow and a Robert B. Silvers grantee, his debut won the 2023 Tata…
f: Abhishek Choudhary is a bilingual writer best known for his two-part study of former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee and the Hindu Right. An NIF Fellow and a Robert B. Silvers grantee, his debut won the 2023 Tata Literature Award. His work has been cited by the BBC, The New York Times , and several other platforms.

b: Abhishek K. Choudhary is the author of a two-part study on the former Prime Minister A. B. Vajpayee. The first volume, Vajpayee: The Ascent of the Hindu Right 1924–77 was released in May 2023 to great critical…
f: Abhishek K. Choudhary is the author of a two-part study on the former Prime Minister A. B. Vajpayee. The first volume, Vajpayee: The Ascent of the Hindu Right 1924–77 was released in May 2023 to great critical acclaim. The second volume will be published in early 2024, followed by the single-volume UK edition and Hindi and Marathi translations.

b: Abhishek Singh ’s work is known for its unique story-telling and has been showcased all around the world. His artworks have been exhibited in museums like Los Angeles County Museum of Art (LACMA); Asia Society Texas…
f: Abhishek Singh ’s work is known for its unique story-telling and has been showcased all around the world. His artworks have been exhibited in museums like Los Angeles County Museum of Art (LACMA); Asia Society Texas Center, Houston; Hopp Museum of Asian Arts, Budapest, Hungary; Mori Museum, Japan. He has multiple books to his credit, the most recent being Purnam and Namaha , all critically and widely renowned. His Ramayana 3392 A.D, with Deepak Chopra and Kali and Shiva with Shekhar Kapur have cumulatively sold over half a million copies.

b: Abhishek Singh Rajpurohit is a researcher with Electronic Village, cultural partners of UNESCO for a project called ‘In Footsteps of Ibn Battuta’. He is researching on Ibn Battuta’s travels in India and…
f: Abhishek Singh Rajpurohit is a researcher with Electronic Village, cultural partners of UNESCO for a project called ‘In Footsteps of Ibn Battuta’. He is researching on Ibn Battuta’s travels in India and video-logging the cities he visited. He is also working with CIIE – IIM-A promulgating the entrepreneurial culture in India.

b: Abubakar Adam Ibrahim is a Nigerian writer. His debut novel, Season of Crimson Blossoms, won the NLNG Nigeria Prize for Literature. His short story collection, The Whispering Trees , was longlisted for the Etisalat…
f: Abubakar Adam Ibrahim is a Nigerian writer. His debut novel, Season of Crimson Blossoms, won the NLNG Nigeria Prize for Literature. His short story collection, The Whispering Trees , was longlisted for the Etisalat Prize for Literature and shortlisted for the 2013 Caine Prize for African Writing.

b: Adam Burakowski has served as an Ambassador of Poland to India since 2017. He is a professor at the Institute of Political Studies of the Polish Academy of Sciences and a long-term employee of public media. He has…
f: Adam Burakowski has served as an Ambassador of Poland to India since 2017. He is a professor at the Institute of Political Studies of the Polish Academy of Sciences and a long-term employee of public media. He has authored a number of publications on India and Central Europe.

b: Adam Foulds was born in London. He is the author of four novels and a book-length narrative poem. He has been the recipient of numerous literary awards, including the European Union Prize for Literature. He now lives in…
f: Adam Foulds was born in London. He is the author of four novels and a book-length narrative poem. He has been the recipient of numerous literary awards, including the European Union Prize for Literature. He now lives in Toronto, Canada.

b: Adam Gopnik has been a staff writer at The New Yorker since 1986. His books include P aris to the Moon, At The Strangers’ Gate and, most recently, A Thousand Small Sanities: The Moral Adventure of Liberalism . Gopnik…
f: Adam Gopnik has been a staff writer at The New Yorker since 1986. His books include P aris to the Moon, At The Strangers’ Gate and, most recently, A Thousand Small Sanities: The Moral Adventure of Liberalism . Gopnik has won the National Magazine Award for Essays and for Criticism three times, as well as the George Polk Award for Magazine Reporting. In January of 2021, he was named a chevalier of the Legion D’Honneur, France’s highest civilian and military award, by President Emmanuel Macron.

b: Adam Nicolson has written about Homer, seabirds, Sissinghurst, the house where he grew up, and the making of the King James Bible. He has been a journalist and columnist for a variety of English newspapers and has made…
f: Adam Nicolson has written about Homer, seabirds, Sissinghurst, the house where he grew up, and the making of the King James Bible. He has been a journalist and columnist for a variety of English newspapers and has made several series for BBC television and radio.

b: Aditi Maheshwari Goya l is the executive director at Vani Prakashan Group (Vani Prakashan and Bharatiya Jnanpith) and the managing trustee at Vani Foundation. She teaches publishing and editing at the University of…
f: Aditi Maheshwari Goya l is the executive director at Vani Prakashan Group (Vani Prakashan and Bharatiya Jnanpith) and the managing trustee at Vani Foundation. She teaches publishing and editing at the University of Delhi and the Seagull School of Publishing, Kolkata. She is an advisor to Jaipur BookMark - South Asia’s largest publishing platform, and also manages the award secretariat of the Vani Foundation Distinguished Translator Award. Aditi holds a Master’s degree in English Literature, and Business Management from the Strathclyde Business School, Scotland, and an M.Phil. degree in Social Sciences

b: Aditi Mehta is a retired IAS officer of the Rajasthan cadre who first encountered the Gavri while on tour in the early 1980s. This chance “jeep moment” led to a lifelong engagement with the form, which presented itself…
f: Aditi Mehta is a retired IAS officer of the Rajasthan cadre who first encountered the Gavri while on tour in the early 1980s. This chance “jeep moment” led to a lifelong engagement with the form, which presented itself simultaneously as play, dance, satire, and philosophy. It allowed for more intimate interactions with the Bhil community and provided a lens to explore larger issues of marginality, community, and voice, particularly of those rendered invisible by the media and mainstream society.

b: Aditya Arya is an eminent commercial and travel photographer. He has played a pivotal role in the establishment of India Photo Archive Foundation for the practice of photographic conservation and is the founder of Museo…
f: Aditya Arya is an eminent commercial and travel photographer. He has played a pivotal role in the establishment of India Photo Archive Foundation for the practice of photographic conservation and is the founder of Museo Camera, the only photography and camera museum in India.

b: Vijai Singh Shekhawat retired from the Indian Navy in 1996 as the Chief of the Naval Staff and Chairman, Chiefs of Staff Committee. Admiral Shekhawat then became a member of the National Security Advisory Board from…
f: Vijai Singh Shekhawat retired from the Indian Navy in 1996 as the Chief of the Naval Staff and Chairman, Chiefs of Staff Committee. Admiral Shekhawat then became a member of the National Security Advisory Board from 1999 to 2001. He has travelled extensively and is a frequent participant in seminars on current international security issues in India and abroad. He was commissioned into the Indian Navy in 1956. Senior staff appointments included ACNS (Operations), Director Ship Systems Development and Director General, Defense Planning Staff. He was Flag Officer, Commanding-in-Chief, Eastern Naval Command, and Vice Chief of Naval Staff.

b: Adrian Levy is a former staff writer and foreign correspondent for The Sunday Times and the Guardian . Along with Cathy Scott-Clark, he won the One World award for foreign reporting and was a Press Journalist of the…
f: Adrian Levy is a former staff writer and foreign correspondent for The Sunday Times and the Guardian . Along with Cathy Scott-Clark, he won the One World award for foreign reporting and was a Press Journalist of the Year. His third book, Deception , co-authored with Scott-Clark , was a finalist in the Royal United Services Institute, Duke of Westminster’s medal for Military History. The Meadow won the Ramnath Goenka Award. The Siege won the CWA Gold Dagger for Non-Fiction. The Exile: Al Qaeda in Flight was published in May 2017. Together, Levy and Scott-Clark have produced award-winning documentaries for HBO, PBS, BBC 1, BBC 2 and C4, and are now working on a documentary feature on interrogation.

b: Adriana Lisboa was born in Rio de Janeiro. She has published, among other books, the novels Symphony in White , winner of the José Saramago Award, Crow Blue , chosen as a book of the year by The Independent , and Hut…
f: Adriana Lisboa was born in Rio de Janeiro. She has published, among other books, the novels Symphony in White , winner of the José Saramago Award, Crow Blue , chosen as a book of the year by The Independent , and Hut of Fallen Persimmons , awarded a Japan Foundation Fellowship, as well as collections of poetry, short stories and books for children. Her poems and stories have appeared in Modern Poetry in Translation , The Missing Slate and Granta . Her books have been translated and published in more than 20 countries. Lisboa has an MA in Brazilian Literature and a PhD in Comparative Literature from Rio de Janeiro State University. She was a visiting scholar at Nichibunken (Kyoto), the University of Texas and the University of New Mexico as well as writer in residence at the University of California Berkeley.

b: Afra Atiq is an Emirati poet, spoken word artist and PhD candidate. Her current research centres around the effects of Instagram on the Arab literary ecosystem. Additionally, she has published academic research about…
f: Afra Atiq is an Emirati poet, spoken word artist and PhD candidate. Her current research centres around the effects of Instagram on the Arab literary ecosystem. Additionally, she has published academic research about reading in the UAE. She has been featured on numerous international and local stages, including Dubai Opera and Louvre Abu Dhabi. With a passion for languages, she writes and performs in a blend of bilingual and trilingual poems.

b: Afshan D'Souza-Lodhi joined the Literature team at British Council as Programme Manager for South Asia in November 2018. She is based in British Council’s Manchester office. Afshan is also a poet and playwright and…
f: Afshan D'Souza-Lodhi joined the Literature team at British Council as Programme Manager for South Asia in November 2018. She is based in British Council’s Manchester office. Afshan is also a poet and playwright and seeks to support newer and emerging writers. She also sits on the board of Manchester Literature Festival and Pie Radio.

b: Ahdaf Soueif is the author of the bestselling novel The Map of Love . Her account of the Egyptian revolution of 2011, Cairo: a City Transformed , came out in 2014. She is the Founder and Chair of the Palestine Festival…
f: Ahdaf Soueif is the author of the bestselling novel The Map of Love . Her account of the Egyptian revolution of 2011, Cairo: a City Transformed , came out in 2014. She is the Founder and Chair of the Palestine Festival of Literature (PalFest) and a widely published political and cultural commentator.

b: Ahlawat Gunjan is an award-winning designer, self-taught painter, TEDx speaker and design educator. A graduate of the National Institute of Design, Ahmedabad, he has a master’s degree in graphic design from The…
f: Ahlawat Gunjan is an award-winning designer, self-taught painter, TEDx speaker and design educator. A graduate of the National Institute of Design, Ahmedabad, he has a master’s degree in graphic design from The Glasgow School of Art, UK. Trained at Lars Mullers Switzerland and Faber & Faber, UK, Gunjan has worked closely with Penguin, Faber and Faber, Hachette, Little Brown, Hodder, Random House, Quercus, Hurst, Scribe AUS, Pantheon and Knopf Doubleday, USA. Currently, he is Head of Design at Penguin Random House, India.

b: Aishwarj Kumar is an Associate Professor at the Faculty of Asian and Middle Eastern Studies, University of Cambridge. He teaches Hindi to undergraduates, and offers expertise in Hindi and Urdu to MPhil students at the…
f: Aishwarj Kumar is an Associate Professor at the Faculty of Asian and Middle Eastern Studies, University of Cambridge. He teaches Hindi to undergraduates, and offers expertise in Hindi and Urdu to MPhil students at the Centre of South Asian Studies. His research interests include the history of North Indian languages and the social and cultural history of colonial North India.

b: Aishwarya Jha is a Delhi-based writer, designer, and entrepreneur. Her debut novel, The Scent of Fallen Stars , received critical and commercial acclaim and earned her the prestigious Ram Nath Goenka Sahithya Samman for…
f: Aishwarya Jha is a Delhi-based writer, designer, and entrepreneur. Her debut novel, The Scent of Fallen Stars , received critical and commercial acclaim and earned her the prestigious Ram Nath Goenka Sahithya Samman for Fiction.

b: AJ Thomas is a poet, editor, and translator who writes in English. He has more than twenty books to his credit and is the former editor of ‘Indian Literature’, Sahitya Akademi’s bi-monthly journal. Thomas taught…
f: AJ Thomas is a poet, editor, and translator who writes in English. He has more than twenty books to his credit and is the former editor of ‘Indian Literature’, Sahitya Akademi’s bi-monthly journal. Thomas taught English at Benghazi University, Libya, and worked as a Senior Consultant at IGNOU. He is a recipient of the Katha Award, AKMG Prize, and the Vodafone Crossword Award for Translation. Thomas holds a Senior Fellowship, Government of India, and was an Honorary Fellow, Department of Culture, Government of South Korea.

b: Ajai Chowdhry is co-founder of HCL and Padma Bhushan recipient. Regarded as the ‘father of Indian hardware’, he has been a relentless advocate of self-sufficiency in electronics and continues to shape India's future…
f: Ajai Chowdhry is co-founder of HCL and Padma Bhushan recipient. Regarded as the ‘father of Indian hardware’, he has been a relentless advocate of self-sufficiency in electronics and continues to shape India's future as a member of several government committees. His journey is chronicled in his memoir, Just Aspire .

b: Ajay Bisaria is a corporate strategic advisor and Distinguished Fellow at the Observer Research Foundation. Formerly a diplomat, he served as Indian envoy to Canada, Pakistan, Poland, and Lithuania. He is the author of…
f: Ajay Bisaria is a corporate strategic advisor and Distinguished Fellow at the Observer Research Foundation. Formerly a diplomat, he served as Indian envoy to Canada, Pakistan, Poland, and Lithuania. He is the author of the recently released Anger Management, the troubled diplomatic relationship between India and Pakistan .

b: Ajay Sinhji Jadeja played for the Indian cricket team during the 1990s. He was known for his aggressive batting style and exceptional fielding prowess during his time. Beyond the cricket field, Jadeja has transitioned…
f: Ajay Sinhji Jadeja played for the Indian cricket team during the 1990s. He was known for his aggressive batting style and exceptional fielding prowess during his time. Beyond the cricket field, Jadeja has transitioned into an incisive analyst and commentator and has been working with various news and sports channels as well as online platforms for the past two decades. He has also been involved in the game as a coach and mentor for various teams.

b: Ajay Jain is an author, photographer, traveller, and founder of Kunzum, an independent bookstore in New Delhi. He has written sixteen printed works of literature, and over fifty e-books, covering travel, memoirs,…
f: Ajay Jain is an author, photographer, traveller, and founder of Kunzum, an independent bookstore in New Delhi. He has written sixteen printed works of literature, and over fifty e-books, covering travel, memoirs, fiction, marketing, and personal development. His latest books include Charlie’s Boys , Nikita , and a travelogue series, #IndiaisCalling .

b: Ajay Kumar Sharma , a distinguished freelance artist and master of miniature painting, has garnered international acclaim over his illustrious four-decade career. Born in Jaipur, India, his artistic journey began under…
f: Ajay Kumar Sharma , a distinguished freelance artist and master of miniature painting, has garnered international acclaim over his illustrious four-decade career. Born in Jaipur, India, his artistic journey began under the mentorship of the esteemed Master Painter Mahendra Sharma. Ajay’s artistic achievements have been celebrated through numerous exhibitions, and his works reside in esteemed private and public collections worldwide. Among his distinguished patrons are former U.S. President Bill Clinton and the late Czech President Václav Havel.

b: Ajay Mathur is Director General of The Energy and Resources Institute, a former head of the Bureau of Energy Efficiency and a climate change negotiator. He is an ardent advocate of a transition to a renewable energy…
f: Ajay Mathur is Director General of The Energy and Resources Institute, a former head of the Bureau of Energy Efficiency and a climate change negotiator. He is an ardent advocate of a transition to a renewable energy economy and leads the work on analyses and assessment for a carbon-free future.

b: Ajay Pal Lamba is an Electronics & Communication Engineer who has worked in HCL Infosystem, cDOT, BEL, DRDO, Indian railways, Indian Revenue Service before joining the Indian Police Service in 2005. He worked as…
f: Ajay Pal Lamba is an Electronics & Communication Engineer who has worked in HCL Infosystem, cDOT, BEL, DRDO, Indian railways, Indian Revenue Service before joining the Indian Police Service in 2005. He worked as Superintendent of Police in Jhunjhunu, Pali, Jaipur rural, Jodhpur, Udaipur and Alwar. He has been Additional Police Commissioner of Jaipur for last 4 years. He has been instrumental in the arrest of the infamous saint Asaram Bapu and written his memoirs in the book gunning for the Godman.

b: Ajay Shah studied at IIT, Bombay and USC, Los Angeles. He has held positions at the Centre for Monitoring Indian Economy, Indira Gandhi Institute for Development Research and the Ministry of Finance. He is now Professor…
f: Ajay Shah studied at IIT, Bombay and USC, Los Angeles. He has held positions at the Centre for Monitoring Indian Economy, Indira Gandhi Institute for Development Research and the Ministry of Finance. He is now Professor at NIPFP in New Delhi. He does academic and policy-oriented research on India, at the intersection of economics, law and public administration.

b: Ajit Kumar is a fantasy storyteller best known as the creator of Brahmyodha – The Destroyer , a myth-driven narrative that blends ancient Indian philosophy with contemporary storytelling. Through this expansive…
f: Ajit Kumar is a fantasy storyteller best known as the creator of Brahmyodha – The Destroyer , a myth-driven narrative that blends ancient Indian philosophy with contemporary storytelling. Through this expansive universe, Ajit reimagines gods as fallible, heroes as shaped by doubt, and choices as deeply consequential. His storytelling is marked by patience, emotional depth, and a strong focus on inner conflict and long-form narrative arcs. Designed as an immersive audio experience, Brahmyodha – The Destroyer has resonated widely, achieving close to 30 million plays within just four months, establishing Ajit Kumar as a compelling new voice in modern mythic fantasy.

b: Ajit Rai’s bestselling book Hindujas and Bollywood is a historic global cultural journey of about 1200 Hindi films introduced to the world through the efforts of the Hinduja Family (1954-1984). The most prestigious…
f: Ajit Rai’s bestselling book Hindujas and Bollywood is a historic global cultural journey of about 1200 Hindi films introduced to the world through the efforts of the Hinduja Family (1954-1984). The most prestigious Cannes Film Festival has considered him to be one of the most important film journalists of the world. He has been the editor of Rang Prasang (National School Of Drama) and Drishyantar (Doordarshan)

b: Ajoy Bose is a leading television commentator and columnist in India. He has written two widely acclaimed books on the Emergency and a definitive political biography of Dalit leader Mayawati. His retrospective book on…
f: Ajoy Bose is a leading television commentator and columnist in India. He has written two widely acclaimed books on the Emergency and a definitive political biography of Dalit leader Mayawati. His retrospective book on The Beatles in India fifty years after, Across The Universe , will be out in February, 2018.

b: Ajoy Sodani is an avid explorer who resides in the Himalayas. Spellbound by mythology and the folklores, he is the author of Darra-Darra Himalay, Darkate Himalay Par Dar-b-Dar and AvakAtankvadi . He is also a Professor…
f: Ajoy Sodani is an avid explorer who resides in the Himalayas. Spellbound by mythology and the folklores, he is the author of Darra-Darra Himalay, Darkate Himalay Par Dar-b-Dar and AvakAtankvadi . He is also a Professor of neurology.

b: Akanksha Arora serves as the CEO at Tribe Amrapali, and has been instrumental in creating the verticals at Amrapali Jewels Pvt Ltd and launching Tribe Amrapali’s website and retail stores. Under her leadership, they…
f: Akanksha Arora serves as the CEO at Tribe Amrapali, and has been instrumental in creating the verticals at Amrapali Jewels Pvt Ltd and launching Tribe Amrapali’s website and retail stores. Under her leadership, they have created a global footprint as a leading jewellery brand with successful deployments in over twenty outlets across six countries. Arora holds a Bachelor of Arts degree from the University of Rajasthan and a three-year Diploma in Jewellery Manufacturing, Designing, Diamond Grading and Gemology from the Indian Institute of Gems and Jewellery, Mumbai. Over a decade, she has quietly transformed the landscape of modern jewellery design with captivating originality, and ensured that Tribe Amrapali retains its heritage ethos while creating contemporary designs.

b: Akash Kapur is the author of India Becoming: A Journey Through a Changing Landscape , which was named a book of the year by The New Yorker, The New Republic and Indian Express and an Editor’s Choice by The New York…
f: Akash Kapur is the author of India Becoming: A Journey Through a Changing Landscape , which was named a book of the year by The New Yorker, The New Republic and Indian Express and an Editor’s Choice by The New York Times . He is the recipient of a Whiting Nonfiction Grant and his work has appeared in The Atlantic, The Economist, Granta, The Hindu, The New Yorker, Outlook, Time and the Wall Street Journal, among other places. He is the former ‘Letter from India’ columnist for the International New York Times . He is also the editor of an anthology, Auroville: Dream and Reality and is at work on a book about the search for utopia, titled Better to Have Gone. He is a Senior Fellow at the GovLab at New York University and a member of the Academic Advisory Council for Krea University.

b: Akhil Katyal is a Delhi based writer and translator who has authored Like Blood on the Bitten Tongue: Delhi Poems and How Many Countries Does the Indus Cross . He has also translated Ravish Kumar’s book of prose…
f: Akhil Katyal is a Delhi based writer and translator who has authored Like Blood on the Bitten Tongue: Delhi Poems and How Many Countries Does the Indus Cross . He has also translated Ravish Kumar’s book of prose poems, Ishq Mein Shahar Hona as A City Happens in Love . Akhil was the International Writing Fellow at the University of Iowa in Fall 2016 and was awarded the Vijay Nambisan Poetry Fellowship for the year 2021.

b: Akhil Reed Amar is Sterling Professor of Law and Political Science at Yale University. Since joining the Yale faculty in 1985 at age 26, he has been cited by the US Supreme Court in over 40 cases, tops in his…
f: Akhil Reed Amar is Sterling Professor of Law and Political Science at Yale University. Since joining the Yale faculty in 1985 at age 26, he has been cited by the US Supreme Court in over 40 cases, tops in his generation, and has regularly testified before the US Congress.

b: Akshaya Mukul is an independent researcher and writer. He is the author of the award-winning book, Gita Press and the Making of Hindu India . Recipient of the Homi Bhabha, Jawaharlal Nehru Memorial Fund and New India…
f: Akshaya Mukul is an independent researcher and writer. He is the author of the award-winning book, Gita Press and the Making of Hindu India . Recipient of the Homi Bhabha, Jawaharlal Nehru Memorial Fund and New India Foundation fellowships, Mukul has contributed to Keywords for India: A Conceptual Lexicon for the 21st Century , edited by Rukmini Bhaya Nair and Peter Ronald deSouza, and A Functioning Democracy?: Essays for Ramachandra Guha , edited by Srinath Raghvan and Nandini Sundar.

b: Akshita Nanda is the author of the novels Beauty Queens of Bishan and Nimita’s Place , with the latter being adapted for the stage in 2019, and having co-won the Singapore Literature Prize, the country’s highest honour…
f: Akshita Nanda is the author of the novels Beauty Queens of Bishan and Nimita’s Place , with the latter being adapted for the stage in 2019, and having co-won the Singapore Literature Prize, the country’s highest honour for English fiction, in 2020. Akshita is the creative mind behind the online choose-your-own-adventure, Kallang River , and is also a full-time journalist with the Straits Times. She is often invited to contribute academic writing or guest columns; to speak on literary and academic panels; and to teach at educational institutions.

b: Alan Friedman is a journalist, bestselling author, television personality, producer and documentary-maker who has spent the past 30 years as a correspondent with the Financial Times , the International Herald…
f: Alan Friedman is a journalist, bestselling author, television personality, producer and documentary-maker who has spent the past 30 years as a correspondent with the Financial Times , the International Herald Tribune/International New York Times , the Wall Street Journal Europe and Italian television. Friedman is also a former contributing editor at Vanity Fair and The New Yorker . A four-time winner of the British Press Award, his new documentary, My Way: The Rise and Fall of Silvio Berlusconi , is currently available on Netflix in 190 countries.

b: Alan Rosling is an entrepreneur and strategic adviser. He co-founded Kiran Energy and was earlier an Executive Director of Tata Sons. He was a Special Advisor to the British Prime Minister during 1991-93. He now lives…
f: Alan Rosling is an entrepreneur and strategic adviser. He co-founded Kiran Energy and was earlier an Executive Director of Tata Sons. He was a Special Advisor to the British Prime Minister during 1991-93. He now lives in Hong Kong but is frequently in India. His first book is Boom Country? The New Wave of Indian Enterprise .

b: Alastair Lewis is professor of atmospheric chemistry at the University of York and a Director of the National Centre for Atmospheric Science. He is an experimental scientist who has studied the composition of the…
f: Alastair Lewis is professor of atmospheric chemistry at the University of York and a Director of the National Centre for Atmospheric Science. He is an experimental scientist who has studied the composition of the atmosphere and the impacts of pollution from polar regions to megacities, open oceans to tropical forests. He is currently Chair of the UK government’s science advisory committee on air pollution.

b: Albert Read has spent his career working at the intersection of business and creativity, overseeing the lifestyle publisher Condé Nast in the UK, Asia and Europe. His first book, The Imagination Muscle , was described…
f: Albert Read has spent his career working at the intersection of business and creativity, overseeing the lifestyle publisher Condé Nast in the UK, Asia and Europe. His first book, The Imagination Muscle , was described by The Economist as ‘a beautifully written meditation … a moving hymn to creativity’ and by The Spectator as ‘super sharp...brimming with big ideas. An extraordinary book.’ He studied Classics at New College and has an MBA from INSEAD.

b: Albie Sachs is an activist and a former judge on the Constitutional Court of South Africa. He began practising as an advocate at the Cape Bar at the age of 21, defending people charged under the racial statutes and…
f: Albie Sachs is an activist and a former judge on the Constitutional Court of South Africa. He began practising as an advocate at the Cape Bar at the age of 21, defending people charged under the racial statutes and security laws of apartheid. After being arrested and placed in solitary confinement for over five months, Sachs went into exile in England, where he completed a PhD from Sussex University. In 1988, he lost his right arm and his sight in one eye when a bomb was placed in his car in Maputo, Mozambique. After the bombing, he devoted himself to the preparations for a new democratic constitution for South Africa. When he returned home from exile, he served as a member of the Constitutional Committee and the National Executive of the African National Congress. He is the author of several books, including The Jail Diary of Albie Sachs, Soft Vengeance of a Freedom Fighter, The Strange Alchemy of Life and Law and We, the People: Insights of an Activist Judge. His latest book is Oliver Tambo’s Dream. Sachs has travelled to many countries sharing his experiences in order to help heal divided societies.

b: Alex Ellis has been appointed as the British High Commissioner to the Republic of India, bringing a wealth of experience in security, EU affairs, and strategy. Previously, he served as the Deputy National Security…
f: Alex Ellis has been appointed as the British High Commissioner to the Republic of India, bringing a wealth of experience in security, EU affairs, and strategy. Previously, he served as the Deputy National Security Adviser for the Integrated Review on foreign and security policy, as well as the Director General in the Department for Exiting the EU. His roles included overseeing the UK-EU security partnership, international agreements, and engagement on Brexit. Ellis’ diplomatic career also spans key positions, such as the British Ambassador to Brazil and Portugal, Director of Strategy in the Foreign Office, and a member of the cabinet of the President of the European Commission. His civil service journey began in South Africa, supporting the transition to multi-party democracy. Outside of his professional life, Ellis is passionate about music, theatre, and cricket.

b: Alex Renton is a British-Canadian journalist and author. His most recent book, Blood Legacy , long-listed for the Baillie Gifford Prize, examined the legacies of British colonialism and transatlantic slavery through his…
f: Alex Renton is a British-Canadian journalist and author. His most recent book, Blood Legacy , long-listed for the Baillie Gifford Prize, examined the legacies of British colonialism and transatlantic slavery through his own family's history with the EIC and as slave and plantation owners in the Caribbean. Renton’s experiences in elite boarding schools led to a book, Stiff Upper Lip , and TV and radio programmes examining a culture of child abuse and cover-up in British institutions and its effects in the UK and beyond.

b: Alex Ross has been the music critic of The New Yorker since 1996. He is the author of The Rest Is Noise: Listening to the Twentieth Century, Listen to This, and Wagnerism: Art and Politics in the Shadow of Music . He…
f: Alex Ross has been the music critic of The New Yorker since 1996. He is the author of The Rest Is Noise: Listening to the Twentieth Century, Listen to This, and Wagnerism: Art and Politics in the Shadow of Music . He has received a Guggenheim Fellowship and a MacArthur Fellowship.

b: Alex von Tunzelmann ’s first book, Indian Summer , was an international bestseller. Her latest work, Fallen Idols , was shortlisted for the Wolfson History Prize. She wrote the screenplay for ‘Churchill’, starring Brian…
f: Alex von Tunzelmann ’s first book, Indian Summer , was an international bestseller. Her latest work, Fallen Idols , was shortlisted for the Wolfson History Prize. She wrote the screenplay for ‘Churchill’, starring Brian Cox. She writes the BBC podcast series ‘History’s Heroes’. and presents episodes alongside Helena Bonham Carter, Nicola Coughlan, and Ray Winstone.

b: Alexander Ellis is the present British High Commissioner to India. Previously, he was Deputy National Security Adviser for the Integrated Review on diplomacy, development and defence. From 2017 to 2019, Ellis served as…
f: Alexander Ellis is the present British High Commissioner to India. Previously, he was Deputy National Security Adviser for the Integrated Review on diplomacy, development and defence. From 2017 to 2019, Ellis served as the Director-General of the Department for Exiting Europe. He was British ambassador to Portugal 2007–10 and Director of Strategy at the FCO 2011–2013 before being appointed ambassador to Brazil. Ellis has worked on the Government negotiation team on the euro, EU Budget framework, Treaty of the EU and EU Enlargement and has also worked on South Africa’s transition to multi-party democracy.

b: Alexander McCall Smith is one of the best loved story tellers in the English language who has delighted readers across the world with his different series of novels: The No. 1 Ladies’ Detective Agency , 44 Scotland…
f: Alexander McCall Smith is one of the best loved story tellers in the English language who has delighted readers across the world with his different series of novels: The No. 1 Ladies’ Detective Agency , 44 Scotland Street , The Sunday Philosophy Club , Corduroy Mansions and the Professor Dr von Igelfeld Entertainments . He was formerly Professor of Medical Law at the University of Edinburgh and is an amateur bassoonist, who co-founded The Really Terrible Orchestra.

b: Alexandra Harris is a literary critic and art historian. Her books include Romantic Moderns , winner of the Guardian First Book Award, Weatherland , which was shortlisted for the Ondaatje Prize and adapted for BBC…
f: Alexandra Harris is a literary critic and art historian. Her books include Romantic Moderns , winner of the Guardian First Book Award, Weatherland , which was shortlisted for the Ondaatje Prize and adapted for BBC radio, and an introduction to Virginia Woolf. She is Professor of English at the University of Birmingham and a Fellow of the Royal Society of Literature.

b: Alexandra Pringle is Editor-in-Chief of Bloomsbury. She began her career in publishing on the art magazine Art Monthly and joined Virago Press in 1978 where she edited the Virago Modern Classics series, becoming…
f: Alexandra Pringle is Editor-in-Chief of Bloomsbury. She began her career in publishing on the art magazine Art Monthly and joined Virago Press in 1978 where she edited the Virago Modern Classics series, becoming Editorial Director in 1984. In 1990 she moved to Hamish Hamilton as Editorial Director and four years later left publishing to become a literary agent during which time her clients included Amanda Foreman, Geoff Dyer, Maggie O’Farrell and Ali Smith. She joined Bloomsbury in 1999. Her list of authors includes Margaret Atwood, Susanna Clarke, Richard Ford, Esther Freud, Elizabeth Gilbert, Sheila Hancock, Khaled Hosseini, Celia Imrie, Nicole Krauss, Jhumpa Lahiri, Colum McCann, Anne Michaels, Madeline Miller, Ann Patchett, Hannah Rothschild, George Saunders, Kamila Shamsie, Patti Smith, Kate Summerscale and Barbara Trapido. She is a Patron of Index on Censorship, a Trustee of Giffords Circus and the charity Reprieve and an Honorary Fellow of the Royal Society of Literature. She has been awarded Honorary Degrees of Doctor of Letters from Anglia Ruskin University and Warwick University.

b: Ali Eslami is a Distinguished Research Scientist at Google DeepMind. He pioneered the prototype for Google Search AI Mode and currently co-leads the Gemini Prototyping team. Previously, he led Generative AI and…
f: Ali Eslami is a Distinguished Research Scientist at Google DeepMind. He pioneered the prototype for Google Search AI Mode and currently co-leads the Gemini Prototyping team. Previously, he led Generative AI and chemistry research teams at DeepMind. He holds a PhD in Artificial Intelligence from the University of Edinburgh and has conducted research at Microsoft Research and the University of Oxford.

b: Alia Malek is a journalist and former civil rights lawyer. She is the author of The Home That Was Our Country: A Memoir of Syria and A Country Called Amreeka: US History Re-Told Through Arab American Lives . In…
f: Alia Malek is a journalist and former civil rights lawyer. She is the author of The Home That Was Our Country: A Memoir of Syria and A Country Called Amreeka: US History Re-Told Through Arab American Lives . In addition, she is editor of EUROPA Ø£ÙˆØ±ÙˆÙ¾Ø§ : An Illustrated Introduction to Europe for Migrants and Refugees and Patriot Acts: Narratives of Post 9/11 Injustices. She is a recipient of the Marie Colvin Award and of fellowships from the MacDowell Colony, the New York Foundation for the Arts and the Puffin Foundation. In November 2016, she was honoured with the 12th annual Hiett Prize in the Humanities.

b: Alice Oswald is a British poet living in North Devon, known for her inventive treatments of landscape and classical literature. She has published many celebrated collections and will release her prose book Rhapsody: An…
f: Alice Oswald is a British poet living in North Devon, known for her inventive treatments of landscape and classical literature. She has published many celebrated collections and will release her prose book Rhapsody: An Interview with Homer in 2026. From 2019–23 she served as Oxford Professor of Poetry. She has recently worked with young poets in Gaza, co-editing three volumes of their writing, including From Dust We Rise . Her work and mentorship continue to influence contemporary poetry around the world, bringing attention to overlooked voices and renewing the relevance of ancient narratives through her distinctive, resonant style and vision today.

b: Alka Patel (PhD, Harvard) is Professor Emerita at the University of California and joined LA3M in 2025 to direct the Indo-Persian Continuum program. She has held a number of prestigious fellowships, most recently as a…
f: Alka Patel (PhD, Harvard) is Professor Emerita at the University of California and joined LA3M in 2025 to direct the Indo-Persian Continuum program. She has held a number of prestigious fellowships, most recently as a Getty Scholar (2017–18), Josephus Daniels Fellow at the National Humanities Center (2019), and Researcher in Residence at the Institut National d’Histoire de l’Art (INHA) (2023).

b: Alka Saraogi is part of the Marwari diaspora of Calcutta settled there before the First World War. Her first novel Kalikatha via Bypass won the Sahitya Akedemi Award in 2001. She is the youngest writer to win the award…
f: Alka Saraogi is part of the Marwari diaspora of Calcutta settled there before the First World War. Her first novel Kalikatha via Bypass won the Sahitya Akedemi Award in 2001. She is the youngest writer to win the award in Hindi so far. The novel spans a period of 150 years of several generations of Marwaris in Calcutta to become a narrative of writing the nation. She has published six other novels, the latest being Kulbhushan ka Naam Darj Kijiye in 2020 and has two collections of short stories. She is translated into many European and regional languages.

b: Alok Sharma was appointed full-time President for COP 26, the 26th United Nations Climate Change Conference, on 8 January 2021. He was previously Secretary of State for Business, Energy and Industrial Strategy and…
f: Alok Sharma was appointed full-time President for COP 26, the 26th United Nations Climate Change Conference, on 8 January 2021. He was previously Secretary of State for Business, Energy and Industrial Strategy and President for COP 26 between 13 February 2020 and 8 January 2021. He has served as Secretary of State for International Development from 24 July 2019 to 13 February 2020, and Minister of State for Employment at the Department of Work and Pensions from 9 January 2018 until 24 July 2019. He was Minister of State for Housing and Planning, for the Department for Communities and Local Government from 13 June 2017 to 9 January 2018. Alok was Parliamentary Under Secretary of State at the Foreign and Commonwealth Office from 17 July 2016 to 13 June 2017. He has served as a member of the Commons Treasury select committee, a member of the Commons Science and Technology select committee, a Parliamentary Private Secretary at the Treasury and from 2012 to 2015 as a Conservative Party Vice Chairman. Sharma was appointed in 2016 as the Prime Minister’s Infrastructure Envoy to India. He also served as Parliamentary Private Secretary to the Rt Hon Oliver Letwin MP, the former Chancellor of the Duchy of Lancaster who had overall responsibility for the Cabinet Office. He was elected as the Conservative MP for Reading West in May 2010. Prior to entering Parliament, Alok qualified as a chartered accountant with Coopers & Lybrand Deloitte, and then worked for 16 years within banking, first with the Japanese firm Nikko Securities and then Enskilda Securities (the investment banking arm of SE Banken), where he held senior roles based out of London, Stockholm and Frankfurt, including serving as a member of the bank’s Corporate Finance Global Management Committee.

b: ALOK (they/them) is an acclaimed poet, comedian, public speaker, and actor. Their literary works, Beyond the Gender Binary , Femme in Public , and Your Wound, My Garden , have garnered global recognition. ALOK's first…
f: ALOK (they/them) is an acclaimed poet, comedian, public speaker, and actor. Their literary works, Beyond the Gender Binary , Femme in Public , and Your Wound, My Garden , have garnered global recognition. ALOK's first comedy special, ‘BIOLOGY!’ was executive produced by Christopher Guest. They are the subject of the docu-short “ALOK”, which made its debut at the Sundance Film Festival. On screen, they can also be seen in ‘Complicated Order’, ‘The Trans List’, and the forthcoming ‘Absolute Dominion’. On television, they can be seen on ‘Sex Lives of College Girls’, ‘Sort Of’, ‘Random Acts of Flyness’, and ‘Getting Curious with Jonathan Van Ness’.

b: Alokananda Roy is known for her versatility in her innovative dancing styles and creative stage productions. She has initiated impressive welfare work in the secluded world of convicted individuals in the Correctional…
f: Alokananda Roy is known for her versatility in her innovative dancing styles and creative stage productions. She has initiated impressive welfare work in the secluded world of convicted individuals in the Correctional Homes of West Bengal, through Dance and Music. Her organisation Touch World operates to care for the convicts and their families.

b: Amal Allana is the Director of Art Heritage, and a Trustee of the Alkazi Foundation of the Arts. As a renowned theatre director, she has directed over 60 productions including Nati Binodini, Erendira and her Heartless…
f: Amal Allana is the Director of Art Heritage, and a Trustee of the Alkazi Foundation of the Arts. As a renowned theatre director, she has directed over 60 productions including Nati Binodini, Erendira and her Heartless Grandmother, Sonata, King Lear, Himmat Mai, Begum Barve, Mahabhoj etc. Allana is a versatile personality, who writes extensively on art and theatre and is the recipient of several national and international awards, including the Sangeet Natak Academy Award for Direction. She is currently working on a book on her the development of her father, Ebrahim Alkazi’s ideas on theatre and art. Her earlier book on famous stage actors is called The Act of Becoming.

b: Aman Nath has co-written/authored 14 illustrated books on art, history, architecture, corporate biography and photography, two of which have won National Awards. These are also used as the official gifts of the…
f: Aman Nath has co-written/authored 14 illustrated books on art, history, architecture, corporate biography and photography, two of which have won National Awards. These are also used as the official gifts of the President and the Prime Minister of India. His book Jaipur , was the first Indian book chosen to be marketed internationally by Christie’s. He has just completed Changing Skylines , the corporate and family history of the Shapoorji Pallonji group. Nath is involved in the restoration of India’s unlisted architectural ruins, now run as the 24 Neemrana ‘non-hotel’ Hotels, which have won awards from UNESCO, the Indian travel trade industry and National Awards. Nath wrote the catalogue and the publicity campaign for the first Indian contemporary art auction by Sotheby’s for their sesquicentennial celebrations in 1977. He was the curator of Art Today, the gallery of India Today . As an inveterate traveller, after walking 400 kms to Mount Kailash and sub-Antarctica, he has contributed to several travel magazines.

b: Ambarish Satwik is a Delhi-based vascular and endovascular surgeon, serving as Director of the Vascular Cath Lab at Sir Ganga Ram Hospital and Professor of Vascular Surgery at GRIPMER. Beyond his medical career, he is…
f: Ambarish Satwik is a Delhi-based vascular and endovascular surgeon, serving as Director of the Vascular Cath Lab at Sir Ganga Ram Hospital and Professor of Vascular Surgery at GRIPMER. Beyond his medical career, he is an accomplished writer, authoring the critically acclaimed 2007 novel Perineum: Nether Parts of the Empire , a subversive exploration of the sexual history of the British Raj. His incisive columns, essays, and opinion pieces on a wide range of topics have been featured in leading publications such as India Today , The Times of India , Outlook , Open , Tehelka , Time Out , and Hindu Business Line , showcasing his versatility as both a clinician and commentator.

b: Ambi Parameswaran is an independent brand strategist and founder of Brand-Building.com a brand advisory. In a career spanning four decades he has worked on a diverse range of Indian and MNC brands. He was until recently…
f: Ambi Parameswaran is an independent brand strategist and founder of Brand-Building.com a brand advisory. In a career spanning four decades he has worked on a diverse range of Indian and MNC brands. He was until recently the Executive Director and CEO of FCB Ulka, one of India’s largest advertising agencies. He is a best-selling author of several books on consumers, brands and advertising. His latest book, Nawabs Nudes Noodles – India Through 50 Years of Advertising , looks at the rapidly changing Indian society through the lens of advertising.

b: Ambi Subramaniam , hailed as “the new king of Indian Classical violin” and “India’s Itzhak Pearlmann", has been trained by his father and guru, Dr L Subramaniam, since the age of three, and gave his first stage…
f: Ambi Subramaniam , hailed as “the new king of Indian Classical violin” and “India’s Itzhak Pearlmann", has been trained by his father and guru, Dr L Subramaniam, since the age of three, and gave his first stage performance at the age of seven. He has received the Ritz Icon of the Year Award, the Rotary Youth Award, and was named among GQ's 25 Most Influential Young Indians in 2021. A youth delegate at the United Nations for the Sri Chinmoy Peace Meditation group, Subramaniam recently completed his PhD on creating a global violin technique. He has co-authored over 20 textbooks and was a featured soloist in the background score of the film Sardar Uddham, composed by Shantanu Moitra.

b: Ameya Prabhu is an entrepreneur and the Managing Director of NAFA Capital Advisors, an asset management and investment banking firm with offices in Mumbai, Delhi and Chennai. Prabhu is also a Partner in UAP Advisors, a…
f: Ameya Prabhu is an entrepreneur and the Managing Director of NAFA Capital Advisors, an asset management and investment banking firm with offices in Mumbai, Delhi and Chennai. Prabhu is also a Partner in UAP Advisors, a financial services, principal investment and strategic advisory firm focused on India and other emerging markets. He was recently designated President South Asia in Global Alliance of SME (GASME). His expertise lies in nurturing, building, financing and growing early and growth stage businesses. He has a BSc. in Economics, Politics and International Studies from the University of Warwick and an MSc. in Financial Management from IE Business School, Madrid. Prabhu is also a published writer and columnist whose writings have been published by well known media Outlets such as the Huffington Post.

b: Amia Srinivasan is the Chichele Professor of Social and Political Theory at All Souls College, Oxford. She is the author of The Right to Sex, a Sunday Times bestseller. Her essays on feminism, animals, death, anger and…
f: Amia Srinivasan is the Chichele Professor of Social and Political Theory at All Souls College, Oxford. She is the author of The Right to Sex, a Sunday Times bestseller. Her essays on feminism, animals, death, anger and other topics appear in the London Review of Books , where she is a contributing editor, The New Yorker , and elsewhere.

b: Amish Raj Mulmi is the author of All Roads Lead North: Nepal's Turn to China (selected as one of 2021's best nonfiction books by The Guardian). His writings have been published in The Himalayan Arc: Journeys East of…
f: Amish Raj Mulmi is the author of All Roads Lead North: Nepal's Turn to China (selected as one of 2021's best nonfiction books by The Guardian). His writings have been published in The Himalayan Arc: Journeys East of South East and Best Asian Speculative Fiction . Mulmi has written for, among others, Al Jazeera, Roads and Kingdoms, Himal Southasia, India Today, The Kathmandu Post and The Record . He is consulting editor at Writer’s Side Literary Agency, and has previously worked for Juggernaut Books and Hachette India.

b: Amit Chaudhuri is the author of eight novels, the latest of which is Sojourn . He is also a poet, essayist, short-story writer, and musician. His works of non-fiction include Finding the Raga , which received the James…
f: Amit Chaudhuri is the author of eight novels, the latest of which is Sojourn . He is also a poet, essayist, short-story writer, and musician. His works of non-fiction include Finding the Raga , which received the James Tait Black Prize this year. Other awards his work has received include the Commonwealth Writers Prize, the Los Angeles Times Book Prize for Fiction, the Sahitya Akademi Award, and the inaugural Infosys Prize in the Humanities. He is Professor of Creative Writing and Director of the Centre for the Creative and Critical at Ashoka University. He is a Fellow of the Royal Society of Literature and an honorary fellow of the Modern Language Association of America and of Balliol College, Oxford.

b: Amit Kapoor , PhD, is Honorary Chairman at Institute for Competitiveness, India and Lecturer at USATMC, Stanford University where he teaches courses on rebalancing economic systems and competitiveness. He has been…
f: Amit Kapoor , PhD, is Honorary Chairman at Institute for Competitiveness, India and Lecturer at USATMC, Stanford University where he teaches courses on rebalancing economic systems and competitiveness. He has been inducted into the Competitiveness Hall of Fame which is administered by Institute for Strategy and Competitiveness at Harvard Business School in addition to being the recipient of the Ruth Greene Memorial Award by North American Case Research Association (NACRA). Amit is the author of bestsellers Riding the Tiger and The Age of Awakening: The Story of the Indian Economy Since Independence .

b: Amit Khanna is a media professional who has worked in print, radio, television, film, stage, live entertainment and digital media. He started his film career as an executive producer, writer and lyricist with…
f: Amit Khanna is a media professional who has worked in print, radio, television, film, stage, live entertainment and digital media. He started his film career as an executive producer, writer and lyricist with actor-film-maker Dev Anand’s Navketan Films in 1970. He has written the lyrics of 250 film and non-film songs. In the 1980s, he worked numerous critically acclaimed feature films, documentaries, commercials and TV programmes. In 1989, he set up the Plus Channel, India’s first integrated media and entertainment company. He has also served as the founder chairman of Reliance Entertainment and was a member of the Prime Minister’s Committee on Information, Communication and Entertainment from 2007-2008. His anthology of Hindi poetry, Anant Raag (Infinite Verse), was published in 2013.

b: Amit Lodha is an Indian Police Service officer presently holding the rank of Inspector General. Over the course of his career, he has been a part of a number of successful police operations, including the arrest of…
f: Amit Lodha is an Indian Police Service officer presently holding the rank of Inspector General. Over the course of his career, he has been a part of a number of successful police operations, including the arrest of gangsters and rescue of kidnap victims. He has been awarded the prestigious Police Medal for Gallantry and the Internal Security Medal for his work. He regularly writes for the Times of India blog.

b: Amit Majmudar ‘s latest books are Godsong: A Verse Translation of the Bhagavad-Gita, with Commentary and The Sitayana . He is an internationally acclaimed poet, novelist and essayist, the first Poet Laureate of the…
f: Amit Majmudar ‘s latest books are Godsong: A Verse Translation of the Bhagavad-Gita, with Commentary and The Sitayana . He is an internationally acclaimed poet, novelist and essayist, the first Poet Laureate of the state of Ohio and a diagnostic nuclear radiologist.

b: Amit Sen is a child & adolescent psychiatrist with more than 30 years of experience in the field. He is a co-founder and Director at Children First and his main areas of interest include service development, community…
f: Amit Sen is a child & adolescent psychiatrist with more than 30 years of experience in the field. He is a co-founder and Director at Children First and his main areas of interest include service development, community outreach, awareness building and advocacy. After having worked and trained in various Govt. and Non-Govt organisations, both in India and UK, Sen has conceptualised and created models of child mental health care that are dynamic and culture specific. He is the founder of the ever-evolving mental health programme in Salaam Baalak Trust. He has worked with national and international organisations like UN Human Rights Commission and UNICEF in the area of trauma, child sexual abuse and juvenile justice.

b: Amita Baig is the Executive Director of World Monuments Fund, India. She has stewarded conservation and preservation across India for over three decades. She was a core member of the Taj Mahal Conservation Collaborative…
f: Amita Baig is the Executive Director of World Monuments Fund, India. She has stewarded conservation and preservation across India for over three decades. She was a core member of the Taj Mahal Conservation Collaborative and over ten years of engagement at the monument resulted in the book, Taj Mahal Multiple Narratives , co-authored with Rahul Mehrotra where they explore its multiple narratives. She has also published Forts and Palaces of India.

b: Amita Baviskar is Professor of Sociology at the Institute of Economic Growth, Delhi and writes on environment and development in India. Her first book was In the Belly of the River: Tribal Conflicts Over Development in…
f: Amita Baviskar is Professor of Sociology at the Institute of Economic Growth, Delhi and writes on environment and development in India. Her first book was In the Belly of the River: Tribal Conflicts Over Development in the Narmada Valley . Her most recent books are Elite and Everyman: The Cultural Politics of the Indian Middle Classes (with Raka Ray) and First Garden of the Republic: Nature on the President’s Estate .

b: Amita Nigam Sahaya is a social entrepreneur and gender activist. She is the director and founder of three NGOs, including Women Work and Health Initiative. She has authored and edited seven books on women and gender…
f: Amita Nigam Sahaya is a social entrepreneur and gender activist. She is the director and founder of three NGOs, including Women Work and Health Initiative. She has authored and edited seven books on women and gender issues, and translated the Hindi classic Jhansi ki Rani, Lakshmibai by her great grandfather Vrindavanlal Verma. Sahaya is co-founder of the Sweden India Gender Network, co-founder India & Beyond, the Dialogue Series and has established two community education and development centres for the underprivileged in Delhi. Her latest work is The Shaadi Story, Behind the Scenes of the Big Fat Indian Wedding.

b: Amita V. Joseph has accumulated over three decades of experience in the corporate, legal, and development sectors. She is a lawyer with a PhD from Deakin University. She is associated with various non-profits, including…
f: Amita V. Joseph has accumulated over three decades of experience in the corporate, legal, and development sectors. She is a lawyer with a PhD from Deakin University. She is associated with various non-profits, including the Business and Community Foundation, where she has worked on numerous case studies and research papers. Joseph has been a dedicated volunteer for the cause of homelessness since 1999 and actively engaged in public interest matters for many years. As one of the founding members of CRW, she has been analysing Business Responsibility Reports since 2015. She is also a member of CSO Coalition@75, contributing to the 2023 Non-Profit Sector Contribution Report, among other endeavours. In recognition of her significant contribution, she was honoured with the Deakin University Silver Jubilee Award in 2019.

b: Amitabh Mattoo is the CEO and Honorary Director of the Australia India Institute in Delhi and Professor of International Relations at the University of Melbourne. Professor Mattoo also serves as advisor to the Chief…
f: Amitabh Mattoo is the CEO and Honorary Director of the Australia India Institute in Delhi and Professor of International Relations at the University of Melbourne. Professor Mattoo also serves as advisor to the Chief Minister of Jammu and Kashmir. He is a Professor of Disarmament Studies in Jawaharlal Nehru University. He has been a member of the National Security Advisory Board and also a member of the National Knowledge Commission to the Prime Minister of India. Mattoo received his doctorate from the University of Oxford and has been a visiting Professor at Stanford University, the University of Notre Dame, the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign, and at the Maison des Sciences de l’homme at Paris. Mattoo was Vice-Chancellor of the University of Jammu from 2002-2008. Recognising his contribution to education and public life, the President of India honoured Mattoo with the Padma Shri, one of India’s highest civilian awards.

b: Amitabha Bagchi is the author of four novels, the most recent being Half the Night is Gone. His third novel, This Place , was nominated for the Dublin IMPAC Literary Prize 2015 and shortlisted for the Raymond Crossword…
f: Amitabha Bagchi is the author of four novels, the most recent being Half the Night is Gone. His third novel, This Place , was nominated for the Dublin IMPAC Literary Prize 2015 and shortlisted for the Raymond Crossword Book Award 2014.

b: Amitava Kumar is the author of several books of nonfiction and three novels. His latest title is a collection of drawings and diary entries, The Blue Book: A Writer's Journal . Kumar's work has appeared in Granta, The…
f: Amitava Kumar is the author of several books of nonfiction and three novels. His latest title is a collection of drawings and diary entries, The Blue Book: A Writer's Journal . Kumar's work has appeared in Granta, The New York Times, Harper’s , and several other publications. He has been awarded a Guggenheim fellowship and residencies from Yaddo, MacDowell, and the Lannan Foundation. His novel Immigrant, Montana was on the best of the year lists at The New Yorker, The New York Times , and President Obama’s list of favourite books of 2018. His new novel is A Time Outside This Time .

b: Amod K. Kanth is an Indian social entrepreneur and former IPS officer. He founded Prayas in 1988, serving as its General Secretary. He also chaired the DCPCR (Delhi Commission for Protection of Child Rights) and DWSSC…
f: Amod K. Kanth is an Indian social entrepreneur and former IPS officer. He founded Prayas in 1988, serving as its General Secretary. He also chaired the DCPCR (Delhi Commission for Protection of Child Rights) and DWSSC (Domestic Workers Sector Skill Council). Kanth is celebrated for his work with underprivileged children, youth, and women nationwide, earning accolades like the 'Global Hero' against Human Trafficking from the US Government. He received awards for his police work, including Meritorious, Distinguished, and Gallantry awards from the President of India. Kanth is a leading advocate for child rights, juvenile justice, and pro-poor innovations in criminal justice and police reforms. His recent books, Khaki in Dust Storm: Police Diaries Volume-1 and Khaki on Broken Wings: Police Diaries Volume-2 , are bestsellers.

b: Amod Kanth , former DG Police Arunachal & Goa, founder Chairperson Domestic Workers Sector Skill Council and Delhi Child Rights Commission, Jt. Coordinator of NITI Aayog’s CSO Standing Committee, is one of the most…
f: Amod Kanth , former DG Police Arunachal & Goa, founder Chairperson Domestic Workers Sector Skill Council and Delhi Child Rights Commission, Jt. Coordinator of NITI Aayog’s CSO Standing Committee, is one of the most celebrated IPS officers and a nationally known voluntary sector leader. Besides being conferred with President/Police medals for Distinguished, Meritorious and Gallant services, ‘Global Hero’ recognition from the US Government, he has investigated nationally known crimes involving Rajiv Gandhi, Lalit Maken and General AS Vaidya’s assassinations, the Hawala Bank Scam, Jessica Lal and other cases.
