b: Amol Palekar is an artist whose journey spans painting, theatre, and cinema. A graduate of J.J. School of Arts, his encounter with Satyadev Dubey led to pioneering theatre inspired by Badal Sircar’s ‘Third Theatre’…
f: Amol Palekar is an artist whose journey spans painting, theatre, and cinema. A graduate of J.J. School of Arts, his encounter with Satyadev Dubey led to pioneering theatre inspired by Badal Sircar’s ‘Third Theatre’ movement. As a 1970s film star, he offered an alternative to larger-than-life heroes and became a household name. His work as a director examines complex human themes, and his memoir Viewfinder captures his rich experiences and steadfast commitment to artistic freedom.

b: Amrish Kumar is an entrepreneur who has spent over a decade working in Indian textiles as the managing director of brand ‘Ritu Kumar’. His desire to be heard has resulted in him building a record label, and an…
f: Amrish Kumar is an entrepreneur who has spent over a decade working in Indian textiles as the managing director of brand ‘Ritu Kumar’. His desire to be heard has resulted in him building a record label, and an internet film venture. He has an MBA and is a fellow of the Aspen Institute. Gods of Willow is his first novel.

b: Amrit Mathur was Secretary, Sports Authority of India and Advisor, Ministry of Sports. He was instrumental in conceptualising and executing the Target Olympic Podium Scheme, India’s flagship programme for supporting…
f: Amrit Mathur was Secretary, Sports Authority of India and Advisor, Ministry of Sports. He was also part of the core team of the IPL, Chief Operating Officer, Delhi Daredevils, General Manager, BCCI, and held administrative positions in the state associations of Railways, UP, MP, Delhi and Uttarakhand.

b: Amrita Mahale is the author of the recently published Real Life and of Milk Teeth , which was longlisted for the JCB Prize for Literature and shortlisted for the Crossword Book Award for Fiction. By day, she works in…
f: Amrita Mahale is the author of the recently published Real Life and of Milk Teeth , which was longlisted for the JCB Prize for Literature and shortlisted for the Crossword Book Award for Fiction. By day, she works in the AI for social impact space, developing and implementing human-centered technology products for public health. She was trained as an aerospace engineer at IIT Bombay and Stanford University.

b: Amrita Talwar is a Delhi-based publishing professional, with over 15 years of experience. She specialises in book marketing, having worked with commercial and literary fiction, as well as non-fiction of every type.…
f: Amrita Talwar is a Delhi-based publishing professional, with over 15 years of experience. Among other authors, she’s worked with authors like Vikram Seth, Amartya Sen, Amitav Ghosh, Sanjaya Baru, Rujuta Diwekar, Ashdin Doctor, Ravinder Singh, Javed Akhtar, Amol Palekar, Chetan Bhagat, and Manoranjan Byapari. Currently Senior Manager, Marketing at Westland Books, Amrita is a passionate bird-watcher and a worried follower of developments in animal rights and climate change.

b: Amy Tan is the author of The Valley of Amazement , The Joy Luck Club , The Kitchen God’s Wife , The Hundred Secret Senses , The Bonesetter’s Daughter , The Opposite of Fate and two children’s books. Tan was also a…
f: Amy Tan is the author of The Valley of Amazement , The Joy Luck Club , The Kitchen God’s Wife , The Hundred Secret Senses , The Bonesetter’s Daughter , The Opposite of Fate and two children’s books. Tan was also a co-producer and co-screenwriter of the film version of The Joy Luck Club . Her latest book is her memoir Where the Past Begins .

b: Portuguese writer Ana Filomena Amaral is an awarded author, historian and translator in several languages, particularly German. She has already published fourteen novels in Portugal, Mexico, Brazil and the USA. With her…
f: Portuguese writer Ana Filomena Amaral is an awarded author, historian and translator in several languages, particularly German. She has already published fourteen novels in Portugal, Mexico, Brazil and the USA. With her book Vaulted Home. Those who cheated death, she won the Los Angeles Book Review prize.

f: Anabel Loyd has spent much of her adult life travelling in search of the lost, forgotten or obscure, in particular in South and Southeast Asia. Her past work focused on improving communications between grassroots development NGOs and her regular column from London for the Indian Telegraph has cast an increasingly critical eye over Westminster politics for many years.

b: Anand Gandhi is widely regarded as the film auteur who ushered in a new wave of Indian cinema. His first film, Ship of Theseus , won the National Award for Best Picture. His next film, Tumbbad , became the region’s…
f: Anand Gandhi is widely regarded as the film auteur who ushered in a new wave of Indian cinema. His first film, Ship of Theseus , won the National Award for Best Picture. His next film, Tumbbad , became the region’s most-watched genre film of the last two decades. His non-fiction production, An Insignificant Man , was India’s most commercially successful documentary film. Anand’s films have won the highest honors at the international film festivals of Toronto, Venice, Transylvania, Tokyo, and Hong Kong. Anand also produced the best selling board games SHASN and SHASN:AZADI , and launched India’s first VR journalism platform, ElseVR. He is now creating his magnum opus - a truly unprecedented narrative universe, that aims to take South Asia to the world.

f: Anand George is renowned for innovative culinary concepts, winning the House of Commons Tiffin Cup in 2005. He is the author of a best-selling cookery book about his life, times, and influences, entitled My 5,000-mile Journey , published in 2016.

f: Anand Neelakantan is the author of the blockbuster Bahubali trilogy, the prequel to S.S. Rajamouli's movie. He has also written Asura: Tale of the Vanquished and the Ajaya series . Among his other popular works are Vanara, Valmiki's Women, Nala Damayanti, The Very, Extremely, Most Naughty Asura Tales For Kids, and The Tale of the Flying Mountains , to name a few. Rajamouli has announced a mini-series based on Anand's books, on the lines of Game of Thrones. b: Ananda Devi , who has a literary career spanning more than four decades, is considered an important voice in the French literary world, using a poetic style and sensuous language to depict the harsh and violent…
f: Ananda Devi , who has a literary career spanning more than four decades, is considered an important voice in the French literary world, using a poetic style and sensuous language to depict the harsh and violent realities of her own country, Mauritius, as well as other countries, such as India, from which her ancestors originate, and the UK. She is published by the major French publishers, is translated in a dozen languages and has received numerous awards, as well as decorations from the Mauritian and French States. She has published more than twenty-five books, including novels, poetry, short-stories and essays.

f: Anant Rangaswami is the Editor of MELT, a former advisor to Unmetric and the former Editor of Storyboard, the advertising, media and marketing show on CNBC TV18.

Anant Vijay, currently with Dainik Jagran, is a senior journalist, columnist and author with more than two decades of journalistic experience. b: Anantha Padmanabhan is Chief Executive Officer of HarperCollins Publishers India. Since his appointment as CEO, the company has grown its revenues by 300%. Strategic initiatives included investing in new categories and…
f: Anantha Padmanabhan is Chief Executive Officer of HarperCollins Publishers India. Since his appointment as CEO, the company has grown its revenues by 300%. Strategic initiatives included investing in new categories and voices, imprints and new markets and new capabilities. HarperCollins is India's most awarded publisher and has been awarded the Publisher of the Year Award seven times. Anantha is Co-Chair of the Publishing Committee within FICCI. He has also served on the Executive Committee of the Association of Publishers in India (API). He is actively involved in policy making that enables a level playing field for Indian publishing, championing inclusion and diversity, protecting authors against Copyright and Territorial Infringement, and fighting digital and print piracy in the market.

b: Anavila Misra is credited with innovating linen saris and bringing them into fashion's spotlight, thereby creating a new vocabulary for everyday luxury. Over the last decade, she built her brand from one weaver to over…
f: Anavila Misra is credited with innovating linen saris and bringing them into fashion's spotlight, thereby creating a new vocabulary for everyday luxury. Over the last decade, she built her brand from one weaver to over two hundred weavers and craftsmen with sustainable employment. As a designer and champion of Indian craftsmanship, Anavila is guided by her core beliefs of mindful creation and being one with nature.

f: Anay Saxena wrote his first book, Time Adventures: The Jackson Menace , when he was seven. His most recent work is a collection of three short stories titled What a Mysterious World We Live In. Saxena has won the award for Best Story Writing, Prince of the Year along with first position in the Best Krishna Competition and Fashion Show, among others. He has won various awards in dance and music competitions as well. Most recently, he won the Young Achiever Award 2019.

b: Andrea Acri holds the chair of Tantric Studies at the École Pratique des Hautes Études in Paris. He was a faculty member of the research and higher education institutions in India, Singapore, Australia, and the…
f: Andrea Acri holds the chair of Tantric Studies at the École Pratique des Hautes Études in Paris. His main research interests are Śaiva and Buddhist Tantric traditions, and the comparative religious history of South and Southeast Asia, with special emphasis on connected histories and intra-Asian maritime transfers.

f: Andrea di Robilant is an Italian journalist and author of several works of non-fiction. His latest book is Autumn in Venice: Ernest Hemingway and His Last Muse .

He is the author of seven books, most recently Haus ohne Türen (poetry, Droschl, 2025). Unterweger received the manuskripte Styria State Award in 2016 and the Prize of the Akademie Graz in 2009.

f: Andrew Graham-Dixon is an art historian, biographer and broadcaster who has made numerous landmark series on art for the BBC. b: Andrew O'Hagan has been nominated twice for the Booker Prize, was voted one of Granta ’s Best of Young British Novelists in 2003, and won the E. M. Forster Prize from the American Academy of Arts and Letters. He is…
f: Andrew O'Hagan has been nominated twice for the Booker Prize, was voted one of Granta ’s Best of Young British Novelists in 2003, and won the E. M. Forster Prize from the American Academy of Arts and Letters. He is Editor-at-Large of the London Review of Books and a Fellow of the Royal Society of Literature.

b: Andrew Quintman is Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Yale University, specialising in the Buddhist traditions of Tibet and the Himalaya. He has written extensively about the literary corpus of the Tibetan poet…
f: Andrew Quintman is Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Yale University, specialising in the Buddhist traditions of Tibet and the Himalaya. He has written extensively about the literary corpus of the Tibetan poet Milarepa. His English translation of The Life of Milarepa was published in 2010. His latest book, The Yogin and the Madman: Reading the Biographical Corpus of Tibet’s Great Saint Milarepa, won the American Academy of Religion’s 2014 Award for Excellence in the Study of Religion. He also co-directs a long-running workshop on Religion and the Literary in Tibet.

f: Andrew Sean Greer is the New York Times bestselling author of six works of fiction, including the 2018 Pulitzer Prize winning novel Less . f: André Aciman , a memoirist, essayist and New York Times bestselling novelist, is Distinguished Professor of Comparative Literature at the Graduate Center, CUNY. In 2017, his novel Call Me by Your Name was adapted into a widely acclaimed film and named one of the top ten films of the year by the American Film Institute. He is also the author of False Papers , Alibis and three other novels, Eight White Nights , Harvard Square and Enigma Variations . He is currently working on a novel and a collection of essays.

f: André Aciman is an American memoirist, essayist, novelist, and scholar. He is the New York Times bestselling author of Call Me by Your Name and Find Me as well as Out of Egypt . His new memoir, My Roman Year , will be released in October 2024, He teaches at the Graduate Center, CUNY.

f: Angela Paine grew up on a Kent farm, where her botanist father taught her to identify plants. She holds a degree in Human Physiology and a PhD in medicinal plant chemistry. She is the author of several books on healing plants, including Healing Plants of Renaissance Florence .

f: Angela Saini is an award-winning science journalist. She is a regular presenter on BBC Radio and her writing appears in the Guardian and Scientific American , among others. f: Angellica Aribam is a political activist and the founder of Femme First Foundation, which is aimed at amplifying women's political leadership. Her debut novel, The Illuminated, is out in July 2021.

f: Anirban Bhattacharyya is a television content producer, stand-up comedian, and actor. He is the creator, producer, director, and writer of the true crime TV show Savdhaan India , and has also produced the popular series Crime Patrol and Fear Files . Anirban is the bestselling author of eight books, including the true crime trilogy: India’s Money Heist: The Chelembra Bank Robbery , The Deadly Dozen: India’s Most Notorious Serial Killers , and Swipe Right to Kill: The Jaipur Tinder Murder Case . He has also written a children’s book titled The Adventurous 6: The Sinister Summer Holiday , a bestselling memoir The Hills Are Burning , and a horror anthology Enter at Your Own Risk . Anirban has served as the content head at Channel [V] and The Walt Disney Company (India), and also acted in multiple films.

b: Anirudh holds a master’s degree in Management from IMI and brings over 35 years of rich and diverse professional experience. He has worked with reputed organizations such as Sify Technologies, Airtel, Reach Limited, and…
f: Anirudh holds a master’s degree in Management from IMI and brings over 35 years of rich and diverse professional experience. He has worked with reputed organizations such as Sify Technologies, Airtel, Reach Limited, and Hong Kong Telecom, where he played key roles in driving business growth and achieving strategic objectives. As the Co-founder and Executive Director of BluOne Ink, Anirudh is deeply involved in strategic planning and execution. He strongly believes that investing in people and nurturing talent are fundamental to sustainable organizational growth, innovation, and long-term value creation.

b: Anirudh Kanisetti is the award-winning author of Lords of the Deccan, a new history of medieval South India. He received the Sahitya Akademi Yuva Puraskar in 2023 and the Tata Literature Best Nonfiction Book of the Year…
f: Anirudh Kanisetti is the award-winning author of Lords of the Deccan, a new history of medieval South India. He received the Sahitya Akademi Yuva Puraskar in 2023 and the Tata Literature Best Nonfiction Book of the Year award in 2022. He writes the weekly Thinking Medieval column for ThePrint. Kanisetti was featured in THE WEEK’s 40 Under 40 list for India’s most promising creatives, as well as Open magazine’s Open Minds 2022 Soft Power list. His research has received grants from the Princeton Center for Digital Humanities and the India Foundation for the Arts. His writings and work have been featured in The Hindu, The New Indian Express, LiveMint, and other prestigious publications. Kanisetti was formerly Editor at the Museum of Art and Photography and Associate Fellow at the Takshashila Institution. He hosts three popular and critically acclaimed podcasts – Echoes of India, Yuddha and The Altar of Time.

b: Anirudh Suri is the author of the critically acclaimed book, The Great Tech Game: Shaping Geopolitics and the Destinies of Nations . He is also the host of the ‘The Great Tech Game’ podcast, which brings together…
f: Anirudh Suri is the author of the critically acclaimed book, The Great Tech Game: Shaping Geopolitics and the Destinies of Nations . He is also the host of the ‘The Great Tech Game’ podcast, which brings together the world's best thinkers on issues of history, technology, artificial intelligence, geopolitics and business. Previously, his work at McKinsey & Company, Goldman Sachs and the Government of India has helped him view the impact of technology on our society from different vantage points. Now, as Managing Partner at India Internet Fund, and non-resident Scholar at the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace, he continues to explore India’s place in this new technology-shaped world order.

b: Anish Kapoor is considered one of the most influential sculptors working today. He was born in Mumbai in 1954 and lives and works in London. He studied at Hornsey College of Art followed by postgraduate studies at…
f: Anish Kapoor is considered one of the most influential sculptors working today. He was born in Mumbai in 1954 and lives and works in London. He studied at Hornsey College of Art followed by postgraduate studies at Chelsea School of Art, London. Recent solo exhibitions include: Houghton Hall, Norfolk, UK (2020), Pitzhanger Manor, London (2019); Serralves, Museu de Arte Contemorânea, Porto (2018); Parque de la Memoria, Buenos Aires (2017); Museo d’Arte Contemporanea di Roma (MACRO), Rome (2016); Museo Universitario Arte Contemporáneo (MUAC), Mexico City (2016); Château de Versailles, France (2015). Permanent commissions include Cloud Gate (2004) for the Millennium Park in Chicago; Orbit for the London 2012 Olympic Park, and Ark Nova (2013), the world’s first inflatable mobile concert hall, Japan. Kapoor represented Britain at the 44th Venice Biennale for which he was awarded the Premio Duemila and won the Turner Prize in 1991. In 2013, he received a knighthood for services to the arts.

b: Anisur Rahman, formerly a Professor of English at Jamia Millia Islamia, New Delhi, is currently Senior Advisor at Rekhta Foundation. His most recent publications are Earthenware: Sixty Poems, In Translation: Positions…
f: Anisur Rahman, formerly a Professor of English at Jamia Millia Islamia, New Delhi, is currently Senior Advisor at Rekhta Foundation. His most recent publications are Earthenware: Sixty Poems, In Translation: Positions and Paradigms, Hazaaron Khwahishein Aisi: The Wonderful World of Urdu Ghazals, Socioliterary Cultures in South Asia and A Garden of All Senses: Five Centuries of Best Urdu Poetry.

b: Anit Mukherjee is an Assistant Professor at the S. Rajaratnam School of International Studies at the Nanyang Technological University in Singapore. A former officer in the Indian Army, he has a PhD from Paul H. Nitze…
f: Anit Mukherjee is an Assistant Professor at the S. Rajaratnam School of International Studies at the Nanyang Technological University in Singapore. A former officer in the Indian Army, he has a PhD from Paul H. Nitze School of Advanced International Studies, Johns Hopkins University. He is the author of The Absent Dialogue: Politicians, Bureaucrats and the Military in India.

b: Anita Agnihotri writes in Bangla and joined the Indian Administrative Service in 1980 after studying Economics at Presidency College and the University of Calcutta. She has authored over fifty works, including poetry,…
f: Anita Agnihotri writes in Bangla and joined the Indian Administrative Service in 1980 after studying Economics at Presidency College and the University of Calcutta. She has authored over fifty works, including poetry, short stories, and novels for young readers, and writes extensively on development issues. Agnihotri received the Crossword Economist Award for her story collection Seventeen . Her recent trilogy— Mahanadi , Mahakantar , and Plabon Jol —explores India's development.

b: Anita Bhatia is the Assistant Secretary-General and Deputy Executive Director of UN Women. Prior to the UN, Bhatia had a distinguished career at the World Bank Group, serving in various senior leadership and management…
f: Anita Bhatia is the Assistant Secretary-General and Deputy Executive Director of UN Women. Prior to the UN, Bhatia had a distinguished career at the World Bank Group, serving in various senior leadership and management positions. She is recognized as a thought-leader on issues of gender equality, sustainable development and strategic partnerships.

b: Anita Nair is the author of the novels The Better Man, Ladies Coupé, Mistress, Lessons in Forgetting, Idris: Keeper of the Light and Alphabet Soup for Lovers . Her other books include a collection of poems titled…
f: Anita Nair is the author of the novels The Better Man, Ladies Coupé, Mistress, Lessons in Forgetting, Idris: Keeper of the Light and Alphabet Soup for Lovers . Her other books include a collection of poems titled Malabar Mind , a collection of essays Goodnight & God Bless and six books for children. Her books have been translated into over 30 languages. She has also written two plays and the screenplay for the film adaptation of her novel Lessons in Forgetting , which was part of the Indian Panorama at IFFI 2012 and won the National Film Award in 2013. Among other awards, she is the recipient of the Sahitya Akademi Award and the Crossword Prize. She is also the founder of the creative writing and mentorship programme, Anita’s Attic. Her latest novel is Eating Wasps .

b: Anitah Aujayeb is a longstanding educator, Mauritian writer, poet, historian, Chairperson of the President's Fund for Creative Writing, Ministry of Arts and Cultural Heritage, Mauritius. She holds a PhD in English, and…
f: Anitah Aujayeb is a longstanding educator, Mauritian writer, poet, historian, Chairperson of the President's Fund for Creative Writing, Ministry of Arts and Cultural Heritage, Mauritius. She holds a PhD in English, and has published some 15 books. She can speak and write in English, French, Hindi, Bhojpuri and the local dialect, Creole.

b: Anitha Thamp i is a Malayalam poet who has been translated into many Indian and foreign languages. She has published four collections of poetry to significant critical acclaim. Her translations into Malayalam include…
f: Anitha Thamp i is a Malayalam poet who has been translated into many Indian and foreign languages. She has published four collections of poetry to significant critical acclaim. Her translations into Malayalam include writings of Juan Ramón Jiménez, Carlo Collodi, Les Murray and Mourid Barghouti. She lives in Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala.

b: Anja Aronowsky Cronberg studied Fine Art and History of Design before founding Vestoj in 2009 as a platform for critical thinking in fashion. Today, she creates the annual Vestoj Journal , Vestoj Online and the Vestoj…
f: Anja Aronowsky Cronberg studied Fine Art and History of Design before founding Vestoj in 2009 as a platform for critical thinking in fashion. Today, she creates the annual Vestoj Journal , Vestoj Online and the Vestoj Salon series. She currently lives in Paris and produces Vestoj under the partial patronage of London College of Fashion, where she also works as a Senior Research Fellow in Fashion Theory and Practice.

b: Anjan Sundaram is an award-winning author, journalist and television presenter, whose war correspondence has won a Frontline Club Award and a Reuters prize. Hailed as a ‘successor to Kapuscinski’, his previous books…
f: Anjan Sundaram is an award-winning author, journalist and television presenter, whose war correspondence has won a Frontline Club Award and a Reuters prize. Hailed as a ‘successor to Kapuscinski’, his previous books are Bad News: Last Journalists in a Dictatorship (an Amazon Book of the Year) and Stringer: A Reporter’s Journey in the Congo (a Royal African Society Book of the Year). Sundaram has reported from Central Africa for The New York Times, The Washington Post, The Daily Telegraph, The Guardian, The Observer, Granta, Foreign Policy, Politico and The Associated Press.

b: Anjani Raipat is the Festival Director of the Vadodara Literature Festival and the Youth Literature Festival—India’s first and largest youth-led, youth-centric festivals—and serves as the Chief Mentor at I.I.M.U.N. A…
f: Anjani Raipat is the Festival Director of the Vadodara Literature Festival and the Youth Literature Festival—India’s first and largest youth-led, youth-centric festivals—and serves as the Chief Mentor at I.I.M.U.N. A lawyer by training and a passionate advocate for women and youth empowerment, she has spent nearly a decade building platforms that amplify young voices. At VLF and YLF, she leads curation, partnerships, and programming with a vision to create a bipartisan literature festival that connects books to careers, bringing together voices from diverse ideologies and disciplines to inspire young people across fields to read, think, and engage, making literature both relevant and aspirational for India’s youth.

b: Anjula Bedi is a writer, editor, actor, and translator. She is a post-graduate in English Literature from Delhi University. As partner and editor & writer for Eminence Designs Pvt Ltd, a publishing company started in…
f: Anjula Bedi is a writer, editor, actor, and translator. She is a post-graduate in English Literature from Delhi University. As partner and editor & writer for Eminence Designs Pvt Ltd, a publishing company started in 1990, in Mumbai, she has edited over 30 books on art and heritage. Her fascination for oral history resulted in her interest in biographies. Her writings include a commemorative volume for the Indian Navy , Bridges of Friendship ; the English adaptation for Kokilaben Ambani’s book Dhirubhai Ambani- the Man I Knew; The Intrepid Entrepreneur- Shyam Sundar Jhunjhnuwala; Purushottam- Transforming Lives ; and a pictorial biography of the company Indorama. Bedi has also authored Gods and Goddesses of India for BPI. She is co-founder of Mumbai’s Surnai Theatre and Folk Arts Foundation, started 40 years ago with the object of bringing meaningful Hindi theatre to Indian audiences.

b: Anjum Hasan is the author of the novels The Cosmopolitans , Neti, Neti and Lunatic in my Head , and the short story collections A Day in the Life and Difficult Pleasures . Her books have been nominated for the Man Asian…
f: Anjum Hasan is the author of the novels The Cosmopolitans , Neti, Neti and Lunatic in my Head , and the short story collections A Day in the Life and Difficult Pleasures . Her books have been nominated for the Man Asian Literary Prize, the DSC Prize for South Asian Literature, the Hindu Best Fiction Award and the Crossword Fiction Award.

b: Anjum Sharma is an editor, poet and writer, currently serving as Deputy Editor at India Today Hindi. He is best known for ‘Sangat’, a groundbreaking and widely acclaimed video interview series, featuring in-depth…
f: Anjum Sharma is an editor, poet and writer, currently serving as Deputy Editor at India Today Hindi. He is best known for ‘Sangat’, a groundbreaking and widely acclaimed video interview series, featuring in-depth conversations with 100 leading Hindi literary figures. Formerly associated with BBC Hindi, Aaj Tak Radio, All India Radio, and Doordarshan, he consistently carved a distinct space for books in mainstream media. His poetry, reviews, and articles have appeared in prominent journals, Passionate about bringing literature to audio-visual platforms, Dr. Sharma continues to bridge creative writing, media, and cultural discourse through his work.

b: Ankur Sarin is a faculty member at IIM Ahmedabad. His research focuses on bringing attention to the consequences of inequalities and instruments used to counter them, located in public policy and civil society.
f: Ankur Sarin is a faculty member at IIM Ahmedabad. His research focuses on bringing attention to the consequences of inequalities and instruments used to counter them, located in public policy and civil society.

b: Ann Cleeves is the award-winning author of the Vera and Shetland series, both successfully adapted for television. Her latest novel, The Long Call , introduces a new character, Matthew Venn. The book went into the…
f: Ann Cleeves is the award-winning author of the Vera and Shetland series, both successfully adapted for television. Her latest novel, The Long Call , introduces a new character, Matthew Venn. The book went into the Sunday Times and The New York Times bestseller list.

b: Anna Della Subin is a writer, critic, and scholar born in New York. Her essays have appeared in the New York Review of Books, Harper's, the New York Times , and the London Review of Books. A senior editor at Bidoun ,…
f: Anna Della Subin is a writer, critic, and scholar born in New York. Her essays have appeared in the New York Review of Books, Harper's, the New York Times , and the London Review of Books. A senior editor at Bidoun , she studied the history of religion at Harvard Divinity School. Accidental Gods is her first book.

b: Anna Funder is one of Australia’s most acclaimed and awarded writers. Her 2012 novel All That I Am , about some of the earliest resistance to Hitler won many prizes including Australia’s most prestigious, the Miles…
f: Anna Funder is one of Australia’s most acclaimed and awarded writers. Her 2012 novel All That I Am , about some of the earliest resistance to Hitler won many prizes including Australia’s most prestigious, the Miles Franklin. Stasiland , internationally hailed as a ‘classic’, won the BBC4 Samuel Johnson Prize for best nonfiction book in English. Both works are bestsellers published in over 20 countries.

b: Anna Katharina Fröhlich, born in 1971, grew up in Frankfurt and New Delhi, and lives on Lake Garda in Italy. She has published four novels in German, two of which are set in India: Kream Korner and Rückkehr nach…
f: Anna Katharina Fröhlich, born in 1971, grew up in Frankfurt and New Delhi, and lives on Lake Garda in Italy. She has published four novels in German, two of which are set in India: Kream Korner and Rückkehr nach Samthar. Her new book, Die Yacht will be released in March, 2024 . She received several awards, including the Literature Prize of the Association of Arts and Culture of the German Economy. In 2011, Kream Korner was nominated for the Leipzig Book Fair Prize. Fröhlich has translated the work of various authors and works as a lecturer and board member at Adelphi Publishing house in Milan.

b: Anna Keay is a writer, historian and curator, with a special interest in 17th-century British history. Keay became Director of Landmark in July 2012, following two years as a Trustee. From 1996 to 2002, she worked as a…
f: Anna Keay is a writer, historian and curator, with a special interest in 17th-century British history. Keay became Director of Landmark in July 2012, following two years as a Trustee. From 1996 to 2002, she worked as a curator for Historic Royal Palaces. From 2002 until 2012, she was Properties Presentation Director at English Heritage. Keay has published several books, including The Restless Republic: Britain without a Crown; The Magnificent Monarch: Charles II and the Ceremonies of Power and The Last Royal Rebel: The Life and Death of James, Duke of Monmouth. Anna co-wrote Landmark: A History of Britain in 50 Buildings with Landmark’s Historian Caroline Stanford, and has presented several TV documentaries – notably the six-part Channel 4 series about the Landmark Trust Restoring Britain's Landmarks that aired in autumn 2015. She is a Trustee of the Royal Collection Trust, a Governor of Bedales School, a Non-Executive Director of Big Yellow Group PLC and an Ambassador of the Weald & Downland Living Museum. She is also a Visiting Professor at Birmingham City University and has been awarded an Honorary Doctorate in Letters by the University of East Anglia.

b: Imayam is one of India’s most significant contemporary writers, widely acclaimed for his unflinching portrayal of Tamil culture and social realities. His works are noted for their raw authenticity, emotional depth, and…
f: Imayam is one of India’s most significant contemporary writers, widely acclaimed for his unflinching portrayal of Tamil culture and social realities. His works are noted for their raw authenticity, emotional depth, and profound human insight. He is the recipient of the Sahitya Akademi Award (2020) and the Kuvempu Rashtriya Puraskar (2022), among other honors. A prolific literary figure, Imayam has authored ten novels and nine short story collections. His writing consistently foregrounds marginalized voices and everyday struggles, making him a powerful and distinctive presence in modern Indian literature, both in Tamil and in translation.

b: Anne Applebaum is a staff writer for The Atlantic and a senior fellow at the Agora Institute at Johns Hopkins University, where she runs a project on 21 st century disinformation. She was a Washington Post columnist for…
f: Anne Applebaum is a staff writer for The Atlantic and a senior fellow at the Agora Institute at Johns Hopkins University, where she runs a project on 21 st century disinformation. She was a Washington Post columnist for 15 years and a member of the editorial board. She is the author of several history books, including Red Famine: Stalin’s War on Ukraine, Iron Curtain: The Crushing of Eastern Europe 1944-1956 and Gulag: A History , which won the 2004 Pulitzer Prize for non-fiction. Her newest book, Twilight of Democracy, appeared in July 2020. Her writing has also appeared in many publications, including the New York Review of Books, The New Republic, Wall Street Journal, Foreign Affairs, Foreign Policy, among many others.

b: Anne Beate Hovind is Chair and Producer of Future Library, a century-long, globally recognized artwork in Oslo by Scottish artist Katie Paterson. She works at the intersection of art, ecology, and time, fostering…
f: Anne Beate Hovind is Chair and Producer of Future Library, a century-long, globally recognized artwork in Oslo by Scottish artist Katie Paterson. She works at the intersection of art, ecology, and time, fostering enduring cultural projects that connect creativity, community, and environmental imagination across generations.

b: Anne Cheng was trained in European and Chinese intellectual history at the Ecole Normale Supérieure in Paris, at Oxford, Cambridge and at Fudan University in Shanghai. She currently holds the Chair of Chinese…
f: Anne Cheng was trained in European and Chinese intellectual history at the Ecole Normale Supérieure in Paris, at Oxford, Cambridge and at Fudan University in Shanghai. She currently holds the Chair of Chinese intellectual history at the Collège de France. Her main publications include a French translation of the Confucian Analects, a Study of Han Confucianism and a History of Chinese thought, which has won several awards and has been translated into numerous languages. She has also authored articles and chief-edited collective volumes on Chinese philosophy and Chinese thought, past and present. Since 2010, she has been directing a bilingual series of works written in classical Chinese and translated into French at Belles Lettres in Paris.

b: Anne Sverdrup-Thygeson is a Norwegian professor in Conservation Biology, with a passion for the hidden biodiversity of insects, but also for all intricate and fascinating interactions in nature and their importance to…
f: Anne Sverdrup-Thygeson is a Norwegian professor in Conservation Biology, with a passion for the hidden biodiversity of insects, but also for all intricate and fascinating interactions in nature and their importance to human beings. Thygeson writes narrative non-fiction that has been translated into 25 languages for both adults and children.

b: Annick Schrammei is a professor at the University of Antwerp’s Faculty of Business and Economics. Dr. Schrammei is also the Academic Director for the Creative Industries at the Antwerp Management School. Her recent…
f: Annick Schrammei is a professor at the University of Antwerp’s Faculty of Business and Economics. Dr. Schrammei is also the Academic Director for the Creative Industries at the Antwerp Management School. Her recent research includes cultural governance and policy, sustainable business models in fashion and cultural entrepreneurship. She is an expert-advisor for cultural policy and an evaluator for the European Commission. She is also a member of the Flemish UNESCO Commission. From 2013-2017, she was a member of the Arts Council in the Netherlands and the president of the European Network on Cultural Management and Cultural Policy Education and Research.

b: Annie Finch is a poet, translator, librettist, editor and critic. Her books of poetry include Spells: New and Selected Poems and Calendars, shortlisted for the Foreword Poetry Book of the Year Award. She is also the…
f: Annie Finch is a poet, translator, librettist, editor and critic. Her books of poetry include Spells: New and Selected Poems and Calendars, shortlisted for the Foreword Poetry Book of the Year Award. She is also the author of The Body of Poetry: Essays on Women, Form, and the Poetic Self.

b: Annie Montaut is Professor Emeritus of Hindi Language and Literature at INALCO in Paris. She has translated into French the works of Nirmal Verma, Krishna Baldev Vaid, Jainendra Kumar, Alka Saraogi, Geetanjali Shree,…
f: Annie Montaut is Professor Emeritus of Hindi Language and Literature at INALCO in Paris. She has translated into French the works of Nirmal Verma, Krishna Baldev Vaid, Jainendra Kumar, Alka Saraogi, Geetanjali Shree, Kedarnath Singh, Anupam Mishra and Ashis Nandy.

b: Annie Zaidi is the author of Bread, Cement, Cactus: A Memoir of Belonging and Dislocation , Prelude to a Riot, Gulab, Love Stories # 1 to 14 and the editor of Unbound: 2000 Years of Indian Women's Writing . She is the…
f: Annie Zaidi is the author of Bread, Cement, Cactus: A Memoir of Belonging and Dislocation , Prelude to a Riot, Gulab, Love Stories # 1 to 14 and the editor of Unbound: 2000 Years of Indian Women's Writing . She is the recipient of the 2020 Tata Literature Live Award for Fiction, the Nine Dots Prize in 2019 and The 2018 Hindu Playwright Award for her play, Untitled 1 .

b: Anosh Irani’s most recent novel, The Parcel, was a finalist for the Governor General’s Literary Award, the Writers’ Trust Fiction Prize and the Ethel Wilson Fiction Prize. His anthology, The Bombay Plays: The…
f: Anosh Irani’s most recent novel, The Parcel, was a finalist for the Governor General’s Literary Award, the Writers’ Trust Fiction Prize and the Ethel Wilson Fiction Prize. His anthology, The Bombay Plays: The Matka King & Bombay Black, was a finalist for the Governor General’s Literary Award for Drama as was his most recent play, The Men in White. His play, Bombay Black, won five Dora Mavor Moore Awards, including for Outstanding New Play.

b: Anoushka Sabnis is a young author and poet. She published her first book, Once Upon a Verse: Because Poems Tell Stories , in 2017 when she was 10 years old. This is a collection of over 50 of her poems. Sabnis has been…
f: Anoushka Sabnis is a young author and poet. She published her first book, Once Upon a Verse: Because Poems Tell Stories , in 2017 when she was 10 years old. This is a collection of over 50 of her poems. Sabnis has been composing stories and poems since she was 5 years old. She has won several inter-school, national and international writing and art competitions. Most recently, she won the Gold award at the Queen’s Commonwealth Essay Competition in 2018.

b: Anshu Harsh is a Publisher and Editor of Rajasthan's first bilingual monthly lifestyle magazine, Simply Jaipur, and a weekly newspaper, Voice of Jaipur. She is the Founder of the Rajasthan International Film Festival…
f: Anshu Harsh is a Publisher and Editor of Rajasthan's first bilingual monthly lifestyle magazine, Simply Jaipur, and a weekly newspaper, Voice of Jaipur. She is the Founder of the Rajasthan International Film Festival and the Regional Operation Head of Pick a Book, Jaipur. Anshu has written three Hindi Poetry collections - Sabdo ka Samandar, Samandar - The Ocean, and The Platonic Love. She has edited two books by Pt. Vijay Shankar Mehta titled Corona Jung Ki Saptpadi and Kahaniya Jeevan Ki. She also translated Dr Ivan Misner's collection of business lessons in Hindi in the book Knowledgepreneur.

b: Anshul Tewari is a social entrepreneur and the founder of Youth Ki Awaaz, which is India’s largest media platform, online and offline, for young people to speak up, take action and create an impact. He has worked…
f: Anshul Tewari is a social entrepreneur and the founder of Youth Ki Awaaz, which is India’s largest media platform, online and offline, for young people to speak up, take action and create an impact. He has worked across media and citizen advocacy and has also served as a Director on the Board of Jhatkaa, a campaigning organisation committed to building grassroots citizen power across India, and Collectively, a World Economic Forum and Unilever non-profit with a focus on sustainability. Tewari is an Ashoka Fellow for social entrepreneurship and was named a Young Innovator by the United Nations ITU in 2012. He was also named a Forbes 30 Under 30 media influencer in 2018.

b: Antara Naik is an educator and mentor with expertise in the IB Primary Years Programme (PYP), helping to found several IB schools in NCR. She focuses on individualised care, student engagement, and professional…
f: Antara Naik is an educator and mentor with expertise in the IB Primary Years Programme (PYP), helping to found several IB schools in NCR. She focuses on individualised care, student engagement, and professional development for teachers. Currently at The Kulish School of the Patrika Group, Naik is developing a well-being and skills-based curriculum. Outside of work, she supports animal rescue efforts, having rehabilitated several abandoned animals into her home.

b: Anthony Horowitz is one of the most prolific writers in the UK. His Alex Rider series for young adults has sold 18 million copies worldwide and his adult books include James Bond , Sherlock Holmes , the New York Times…
f: Anthony Horowitz is one of the most prolific writers in the UK. His Alex Rider series for young adults has sold 18 million copies worldwide and his adult books include James Bond , Sherlock Holmes , the New York Times bestselling Magpie Murders and the Word is Murder , the start of a ten-part series. He has also worked in film and television, most notably creating the BAFTA-winning series, Foyle’s War .

b: Anthony Miranda is the Cultural and Educational Affairs Counselor for the Public Diplomacy section and leads the U.S. Mission to India’s public engagement strategies and programming. He has served in Munich, Germany;…
f: Anthony Miranda is the Cultural and Educational Affairs Counselor for the Public Diplomacy section and leads the U.S. Mission to India’s public engagement strategies and programming. He has served in Munich, Germany; Kabul, Afghanistan; Sofia, Bulgaria; and Madrid, Spain. He has served at the U.S. Mission to the United Nations in New York City and in Washington in the Executive Secretariat advancing Secretary of State Hillary Clinton’s overseas travel.

b: Anthony Sattin is a history and travel writer. Much of his work focuses on the Middle East and North Africa, including three highly acclaimed books of history and travel, and two biographies, A Winter on the Nile and…
f: Anthony Sattin is a history and travel writer. Much of his work focuses on the Middle East and North Africa, including three highly acclaimed books of history and travel, and two biographies, A Winter on the Nile and Young Lawrence . His latest book, Nomads, The Wanderers Who Shaped Our World , has been described as ”important, generous and beautifully written” and “a treat for any thoughtful traveller, armchair or otherwise”.

b: Antony Beevor’s books include Stalingrad, Berlin, D-Day, and the Second World War . His work, which has received major prizes in this country and abroad, has appeared in thirty-five languages and sold more than eight…
f: Antony Beevor’s books include Stalingrad, Berlin, D-Day, and the Second World War . His work, which has received major prizes in this country and abroad, has appeared in thirty-five languages and sold more than eight and a half million copies. He was knighted in 2017. His latest book is Russia – Revolution and Civil War 1917-1921.

b: Antony Loewenstein is an independent journalist who has written for The New York Times, The Guardian and The New York Review of Books . He is the filmmaker of Disaster Capitalism and author of The Palestine Laboratory:…
f: Antony Loewenstein is an independent journalist who has written for The New York Times, The Guardian and The New York Review of Books . He is the filmmaker of Disaster Capitalism and author of The Palestine Laboratory: How Israel Exports The Technology Of Occupation Around The World and Disaster Capitalism: Making A Killing Out Of Catastrophe .

b: Anu Singh Choudhary, a celebrated author in Hindi, is also an accomplished screenwriter. She has written extensively across print, radio, TV, films, and digital. As a screenwriter, Choudhary has co-written ‘Aarya’,…
f: Anu Singh Choudhary, a celebrated author in Hindi, is also an accomplished screenwriter. She has written extensively across print, radio, TV, films, and digital. As a screenwriter, Choudhary has co-written ‘Aarya’, and 'Grahan', among others. She has written the Hindi adaptation of the Malayalam masterpiece, The Great Indian Kitchen , and has adapted two Bengali films into Hindi. As the co-founder of Dopamine Media, she has written and directed 'The Good Girl Show', a 5-part series for YouTube, and has co-produced 'Alma Matters: Inside the IIT Dream', a 3-part docu-series now streaming on Netflix. Her books Neela Scarf, Mamma Ki Diary, and Bhali Ladkiyaan, Buri Ladkiyaan, are all considered bestsellers. Choudhary has translated well-known authors such as Perumal Murugan, Namita Gokhale, Paulo Coelho, Vir Sanghvi, and Anuja Chauhan into Hindi. She has been awarded Ramnath Goenka Award for Excellence in Journalism and Laadli Media and Advertising Awards.

b: Anubha Mehta has a doctorate in Political Science and over two decades of Canadian public service experience. She has been a Bharatnatyam dancer, theatre-actor, TV-star, painter and a poet. She led the development of…
f: Anubha Mehta has a doctorate in Political Science and over two decades of Canadian public service experience. She has been a Bharatnatyam dancer, theatre-actor, TV-star, painter and a poet. She led the development of the first Inclusion Strategy for the Regional Government of Peel in Canada and has been awarded for her work with diverse Canadian communities. Following a spate of academic writing, Mehta’s novel Peacock in the Snow was selected by Toronto Arts Council’s Lit up platform, a part of the International Festival of Authors. She continues to work with NGOs in both Canada and India on issues of gender enfranchisement, emancipation through education and the harnessing the power of local communities.

b: Anuj Bahri is a second generation bookseller, heading the prestigious group companies at BAHRISONS Booksellers LLP, in Delhi, and seven other cities across India. He is also a publisher of new writings presented through…
f: Anuj Bahri is a second generation bookseller, heading the prestigious group companies at BAHRISONS Booksellers LLP, in Delhi, and seven other cities across India. He is also a publisher of new writings presented through a boutique list at Tara – India Research Press, and a Literary Agent at Red Ink Literary Agency, representing world titles.

b: Anuj Khare is a writer, satirist and journalist with over 20 years experience. He is currently the editor of DainikBhaskar.com and Divyamarathi.com. He is the author of the books Param Shradheya: Mein Khud, Chillar…
f: Anuj Khare is a writer, satirist and journalist with over 20 years experience. He is currently the editor of DainikBhaskar.com and Divyamarathi.com. He is the author of the books Param Shradheya: Mein Khud, Chillar Chintan and Baatein Bematlab . Khare has also written over 200 satires in Dainik Bhaskar, Naidunia, Navbharat Times, Nav Bharat, Peoples Samachar, Haribhoomi, Jan Sandesh Times, Outlook, Vyangya Yatra, Lafz and Attahaas. He also has his own blog titled Shabdayog. His play Nautanki Raja has been performed in Delhi and other Indian cities.

b: Anuja Chandramouli is a bestselling author and modern Indian classicist specialising in mythology, historical fiction, and fantasy. Her 12 books include Arjuna: Saga of a Pandava Warrior-Prince , Kamadeva: The God of…
f: Anuja Chandramouli is a bestselling author and modern Indian classicist specialising in mythology, historical fiction, and fantasy. Her 12 books include Arjuna: Saga of a Pandava Warrior-Prince , Kamadeva: The God of Desire , Padmavati: The Burning Queen , and Mohini: The Enchantress , winner of the 2021 AutHer Award. Her latest, Abhimanyu: Son of Arjuna , is shortlisted for the Atta Galatta Book Prize. A TEDx speaker and storyteller, Chandramouli conducts workshops on creative writing and mythology and shares her Mahabharata and Ramayana series on YouTube and Spotify. She is a trained Bharatnatyam dancer.

b: Anuja Chauhan worked in advertising for 17 years selling colas, chips and chocolates before deciding to do something healthier for a living. She is the author of five best-selling rom-com novels, three of which have…
f: Anuja Chauhan worked in advertising for 17 years selling colas, chips and chocolates before deciding to do something healthier for a living. She is the author of five best-selling rom-com novels, three of which have been procured by Bollywood studios and one of which was adapted into a prime time daily soap on the ZEE network.

b: Anuk Arudpragasam is is the author of the novel The Story of a Brief Marriage , a meditation on language, trauma and marginality set during the last weeks of the Sri Lankan civil war. It won the DSC Prize for South…
f: Anuk Arudpragasam is is the author of the novel The Story of a Brief Marriage , a meditation on language, trauma and marginality set during the last weeks of the Sri Lankan civil war. It won the DSC Prize for South Asian Literature and the Shakti Bhatt Prize, was shortlisted for the 2017 Dylan Thomas Prize and was named one of the top ten novels of 2016 by The Wall Street Journal .

b: Anukrti Upadhyay writes fiction and poetry in both English and Hindi. Her English works, twin novellas Daura and Bhaunri, and novel Kintsugi , have been published by the 4th Estate imprint of Harpercollins in India and…
f: Anukrti Upadhyay writes fiction and poetry in both English and Hindi. Her English works, twin novellas Daura and Bhaunri, and novel Kintsugi , have been published by the 4th Estate imprint of Harpercollins in India and have been nominated for multiple awards. She has been awarded the Sushila Devi Award for the best work of fiction written by a woman author in 2020 for Kintsugi . Her Hindi works including a short story collection, Japani Sarai, and the novel Neena Aunty , have been published by Rajpal and Sons. Upadhyay's writings have appeared in Scroll.in, Kitaab.sg, The Bombay Review, The Bangalore Review, The Bilingual Window , and several other Hindi publications.

b: Anumita Roychowdhury is Executive Director, Research and Advocacy at Centre for Science and Environment. She has had a distinguished career in research, communication and advocacy on sustainable urbanisation…
f: Anumita Roychowdhury is Executive Director, Research and Advocacy at Centre for Science and Environment. She has had a distinguished career in research, communication and advocacy on sustainable urbanisation encompassing clean air action. She has helped to build the campaign on Right to Clean Air at the Centre that has contributed to several policy developments. She is a recipient of the prestigious 2017 Haagen Smit Clean Air Award given by the California Air Resources Board/California Environmental Protection Agency, USA.

b: Anupam Kher is an award-winning international actor, author and motivational speaker, best known for his prolific career in Indian and International cinema. He has appeared in over 500 films and 100 plays, over a span…
f: Anupam Kher is an award-winning international actor, author and motivational speaker, best known for his prolific career in Indian and International cinema. He has appeared in over 500 films and 100 plays, over a span of 35 years, having played iconic characters in critical and commercial hits, including Saaransh, Dilwale Dulhaniya Le Jayenge, Karma, Khosla Ka Ghosla, A Wednesday, Special 26, Maine Gandhi Ko Nahin Mara and The Accidental Prime Minister, to name a few. Kher has worked with acclaimed international directors such as Ang Lee, David O. Russell, Woody Allen, Gurinder Chaddha and the Wachowskis. Some of his international projects include the films Silver Linings Playbook, Hotel Mumbai, The Boy with the Top Knot, The Big Sick and the series Sense 8 and New Amsterdam. Kher is a member of the Academy of Motion Pictures Arts and Sciences (USA). His former national appointments include Chairman of institutions such as the Film and Television Institute of India (FTII), National School of Drama and Film Certification Board of India. He is a recipient of the IIFA Award for Outstanding Achievement in Indian Cinema, was nominated for the prestigious British Academy Film Awards (BAFTA) and received a record breaking eight consecutive Filmfare Awards. In 2004, Kher was bestowed the Padma Shri Award, followed by the Padma Bhushan, the third highest civilian award in India, in 2016, for his distinguished service of higher order in art. In addition to his acting career, he established Kher’s Actor Prepares in 2005, a world-renowned acting school. Kher is also an acclaimed author with two published books, Lessons Life Taught Me, Unknowingly: An Autobiography and The Best Thing About You Is You, which has been translated into six languages and is in its 20th edition. His thi

b: Anupama Chopra is a film critic, National Award-winning book author and journalist. She is the chairperson of the Film Critics Guild and Director of the Jio MAMI Mumbai Film Festival. She has covered cinema since 1993…
f: Anupama Chopra is a film critic, National Award-winning book author and journalist. She is the chairperson of the Film Critics Guild and Director of the Jio MAMI Mumbai Film Festival. She has covered cinema since 1993 in multiple mediums. She has worked with India Today, NDTV 2/7, Star World and is currently the founder and editor of the digital platform Film Companion, which offers a curated look at cinema and entertainment. She has also written about cinema for various international publications, including The New York Times, Variety and Sight and Sound . Anupama has authored several books, including King of Bollywood - Shah Rukh Khan and the Seductive World of Indian Cinema , which was featured on the Editor’s Choice list of the The New York Times’ Sunday book review and translated into German, Indonesian and Polish. Anupama received an MA in journalism from Northwestern University.

b: Anupama Manral is a commissioning editor at Hachette India. She is keen to bring hair-raising suspense novels, gripping murder mysteries, psychological thrillers, cover-your-mouth gore fests and blood-and-gore true…
f: Anupama Manral is a commissioning editor at Hachette India. She is keen to bring hair-raising suspense novels, gripping murder mysteries, psychological thrillers, cover-your-mouth gore fests and blood-and-gore true crime—to the front and centre of storytelling in India.

b: Anuradha Bhagwati is the award-winning author of the critically acclaimed book Unbecoming: A Memoir of Disobedience . She is also an activist, yoga and meditation teacher and Marine Corps veteran. She founded the…
f: Anuradha Bhagwati is the award-winning author of the critically acclaimed book Unbecoming: A Memoir of Disobedience . She is also an activist, yoga and meditation teacher and Marine Corps veteran. She founded the Service Women’s Action Network (SWAN), which brought international attention to sexual violence in the U.S. military and helped repeal the ban on women in combat. Bhagwati is a regular media commentator on issues related to national security, women’s rights, civil rights and mental health. Her writing has appeared in The New York Times, Washington Post, Politico, Foreign Affairs and New Republic.

b: Anuradha Roy is the author of An Atlas of Impossible Longing , The Folded Earth and Sleeping on Jupiter , which won the DSC Prize for Fiction 2016 and was longlisted for the Man Booker Prize 2015. Her latest novel, All…
f: Anuradha Roy is the author of An Atlas of Impossible Longing , The Folded Earth and Sleeping on Jupiter , which won the DSC Prize for Fiction 2016 and was longlisted for the Man Booker Prize 2015. Her latest novel, All the Lives We Never Lived, was published worldwide in 2018 and has won the Tata Book of the Year Award. It has also been nominated for the DSC Prize, the JCB Prize and the Hindu Literary Award. Roy won the Economist Crossword Prize for The Folded Earth, which was longlisted for the Man Asia Prize. Her first novel, An Atlas of Impossible Longing was picked as one of the Best Books of the Year by Washington Post , Huffington Post and Seattle Times . Her books have been translated into over 15 languages. She works as a designer at Permanent Black, an independent press she runs with Rukun Advani.

b: Anuradha Sarma Pujari began her literary career as a journalist and columnist in 1991. She has authored 12 novels, 6 collections of short stories, 1 travelogue, and 8 books of autobiographical essays. In 2021, she was…
f: Anuradha Sarma Pujari began her literary career as a journalist and columnist in 1991. She has authored 12 novels, 6 collections of short stories, 1 travelogue, and 8 books of autobiographical essays. In 2021, she was honoured with the 'Sahitya Akademi Award,' and she has also received numerous prestigious awards from various leading literary organisations in Assam and the country. She has attended both national and international literary events where she has participated as a resource person and panellist. Currently, she serves as the Editor of the prestigious Assamese weekly Sadin and a prominent Assamese literary magazine, Satsori. Additionally, she holds a position as an Executive member of the Assam Publication Board, established by the Government of Assam.

b: Anurag Kashyap is a multi-talented filmmaker who has been credited as a director, producer, writer and also as an actor in over 40 films. Three of his recent films have premiered at Cannes and his epic two-part film…
f: Anurag Kashyap is a multi-talented filmmaker who has been credited as a director, producer, writer and also as an actor in over 40 films. Three of his recent films have premiered at Cannes and his epic two-part film Gangs of Wasseypur is hugely popular. He has also served on the jury of Sundance, Venice, CPH Pix and Marrakech film festivals. He was awarded the Knight of the Order of Arts and Letter by the French government in 2013.

b: Anurag Minus Verma is a podcaster, writer, and cultural critic who explores society, internet culture, and politics with wit and sharp observation. He is the author of The Great Indian Brain Rot: Love, Lies and…
f: Anurag Minus Verma is a podcaster, writer, and cultural critic who explores society, internet culture, and politics with wit and sharp observation. He is the author of The Great Indian Brain Rot: Love, Lies and Algorithms in Digital India , a book that examines the rise of Indian internet culture, and seeks to decode it from a sociological, philosophical, and absurd perspective.

b: Anushka Jasraj is a writer and educator based in Mumbai. She is a two-time winner of the Asia Regional Commonwealth Short Story Prize in 2012 and 2017. Her debut short story collection, Principles of Prediction , was…
f: Anushka Jasraj is a writer and educator based in Mumbai. She is a two-time winner of the Asia Regional Commonwealth Short Story Prize in 2012 and 2017. Her debut short story collection, Principles of Prediction , was published by Westland Books in 2020.

b: Anushree Rathore writes fiction and poetry in Rajasthani and Hindi. Many of her research papers, articles, poems and stories have been published by various journals and broadcast by All India radio. Her books include…
f: Anushree Rathore writes fiction and poetry in Rajasthani and Hindi. Many of her research papers, articles, poems and stories have been published by various journals and broadcast by All India radio. Her books include Nanha Shaheed, Olyu and Jivajuna Ra Kapa . Dr. Rathore has won the Kamla Goenka Foundation’s Kishor Kalpnakant Youth Literary Award, the Gangasagar Literary Award, the second prize at the Nrisingh Rajapurohit Rajasthani Story, first prize at the Shree Bakhtawar Singh Rajapurohit Story Competition and the Bavaji Chatur Singh Literary Award (Haldighati).

b: Aparna Chandra is an Associate Professor of Law at the National Law School of India University, Bengaluru, where she teaches and researches on constitutional law, comparative law, gender and the law, and judicial…
f: Aparna Chandra is an Associate Professor of Law at the National Law School of India University, Bengaluru, where she teaches and researches on constitutional law, comparative law, gender and the law, and judicial process reform. She has previously worked at the National Judicial Academy, Bhopal, and the National Law University, Delhi, where she founded the Centre for Constitutional Law, Policy and Governance.

b: Aparna Piramal Raje is an author, columnist, public speaker and educator. Her latest book is Chemical Khichdi - How I Hacked My Mental Health . She also writes extensively on leadership, business and design.
f: Aparna Piramal Raje is an author, columnist, public speaker and educator. Her latest book is Chemical Khichdi - How I Hacked My Mental Health . She also writes extensively on leadership, business and design.

b: Aparna Sodani , a radiologist by profession, is an art lover and mountain enthusiast. She has set her feet on more than 25 sparingly travelled trails of the Greater Himalayas in the last 17 years, earning her two Limca…
f: Aparna Sodani , a radiologist by profession, is an art lover and mountain enthusiast. She has set her feet on more than 25 sparingly travelled trails of the Greater Himalayas in the last 17 years, earning her two Limca Book of Records entries. One of them is for being the first woman ever to cross the dangerous Auden’s Col.

b: Apoorva Oza is the Chief Executive Officer of Aga Khan Rural Support Programme (India). Oza started his career as a Deputy Manager (Projects and Engineering) with Gujarat Dairy Development Corporation. He joined…
f: Apoorva Oza is the Chief Executive Officer of Aga Khan Rural Support Programme (India). Oza started his career as a Deputy Manager (Projects and Engineering) with Gujarat Dairy Development Corporation. He joined AKRSP(I) as a Field Team Leader in 1988 and in 1994 became the Head of Programmes. He was appointed as the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of AKRSP (India) in 2001. Besides his work with AKRSP(I), Oza is actively involved in founding and supporting NGOs as well as influencing government policy.

b: Apra Kuchhal is a gossamer of vision, tenacity, entrepreneurship and empowerment. Her businesses vary from furniture export to hospitality. She is the founder of WE CARE - an initiative to promote women, youth, art and…
f: Apra Kuchhal is a gossamer of vision, tenacity, entrepreneurship and empowerment. Her businesses vary from furniture export to hospitality. She is the founder of WE CARE - an initiative to promote women, youth, art and culture. Kuchhal was the Chairperson of FICCI FLO from 2014 to 2015, and was instrumental in introducing skill development at self-help groups in and around Jaipur, and for enhancing employability skills for individuals. She is also the Executive Secretary of Rajasthan Forum and the Honorary Convener of Prabha Khaitan Foundation for Rajasthan and Central India affairs. She spoke at the TEDx Youth in 2016 on The Next Chapter in Jaipur, and is the Flag Bearer of the Vital Voices Global Mentoring Walk held in Ajmer every year.

b: Arambam Ongbi Memchoubi is a critic, editor, academic and poet. She is the author of numerous books, including seven collections of poetry and two travelogues. She is the recipient of the Sahitya Akademi Award for her…
f: Arambam Ongbi Memchoubi is a critic, editor, academic and poet. She is the author of numerous books, including seven collections of poetry and two travelogues. She is the recipient of the Sahitya Akademi Award for her poetry collection Idu Ningthou . Her poems have been translated into English, German, Italian and other major Indian languages, and published in various anthologies.

b: Arati R. Jerath is a veteran journalist and political commentator. She has been writing on domestic and international current affairs for four decades. She is a recognised face on television as a political analyst. Her…
f: Arati R. Jerath is a veteran journalist and political commentator. She has been writing on domestic and international current affairs for four decades. She is a recognised face on television as a political analyst. Her special interest is tracking Indian politics and its intersection with society in a rapidly changing order.

b: Archana Mirajkar is an author who writes in English and Marathi. Her latest book, Swayamsiddha , tells the stories of rebellious women from the Mahabharata. Mirajkar hosts a YouTube series called ‘Granthyatra’ that…
f: Archana Mirajkar is an author who writes in English and Marathi. Her latest book, Swayamsiddha , tells the stories of rebellious women from the Mahabharata. Mirajkar hosts a YouTube series called ‘Granthyatra’ that showcases the hundred best books in Marathi literature. She also works as a Senior Media and Communications Officer at a foreign mission in Delhi.

b: Archana Nathan is a senior commissioning editor at Penguin Random House, India, commissioning books for the literary imprints Viking and Penguin. A former journalist, Archana has over a decade's experience working with…
f: Archana Nathan is a senior commissioning editor at Penguin Random House, India, commissioning books for the literary imprints Viking and Penguin. A former journalist, Archana has over a decade's experience working with leading news publications, such as The Hindu and Scroll.in. Her writings have also been published at The Caravan and The Wire. She has worked as a podcast writer and producer for Mission ISRO, the first audio history of the Indian space programme, narrated by Harsha Bhogle, as well as the BBC's My Indian Life, hosted by Kalki Koechlin.

b: Dr. Archana Sharma is a CERN physicist, author, and founder of the LifeLab Foundation. Her journey from Banaras to Geneva reflects a lifelong quest to unite science, art, and education. She champions curiosity, equity,…
f: Dr. Archana Sharma is a CERN physicist, author, and founder of the LifeLab Foundation. Her journey from Banaras to Geneva reflects a lifelong quest to unite science, art, and education. She champions curiosity, equity, and India’s scientific spirit through books, outreach, and pioneering collaborations linking discovery to human purpose.Lyse Doucet from Canada is the BBC's Chief International Correspondent. For the past four decades, she’s reported on major news stories around the world and was based as a correspondent in Jerusalem, Amman, Islamabad, Kabul, and Abidjan. The Finest Hotel in Kabul is her first book.

b: Archana Surana successfully carries forward a legacy of 20 years as the Founder and Director of ARCH College of Design & Business. Through contributions in the space of youth and women empowerment, she has established…
f: Archana Surana successfully carries forward a legacy of 20 years as the Founder and Director of ARCH College of Design & Business. Through contributions in the space of youth and women empowerment, she has established strong pathways in design education as well as mentoring through the Women Mentors Forum founded by her. A widely travelled and noted speaker, she sits on various national and international forums of academia and industry. She is a Vital Voices Lead Fellow and a YUVA ICON awardee at the hands of former Indian President, Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam.

b: Arcopol Chaudhuri is Managing Editor at HarperCollins India, where he oversees audiobook publishing, foreign rights sales and book-to-screen licensing. He is responsible for driving overall rights revenue growth and…
f: Arcopol Chaudhuri is Managing Editor at HarperCollins India, where he oversees audiobook publishing, foreign rights sales and book-to-screen licensing. He is responsible for driving overall rights revenue growth and diversifying HarperCollins India's rich and diverse list of books into new and emerging formats.

b: Arefa Tehsin’s recent novel is The Witch in the Peepul Tree. She is the author of several books on wildlife and environment and also pens social narratives and travel experiences. Her book Wild in the Backyard was…
f: Arefa Tehsin’s recent novel is The Witch in the Peepul Tree. She is the author of several books on wildlife and environment and also pens social narratives and travel experiences. Her book Wild in the Backyard was shortlisted for The Hindu Young World-Goodbooks Award 2017. Her picture book The Elephant Bird was read at 3200+ locations in India on the International Literacy Day, 2016, and has been translated in more than 40 languages. She was also the Honorary Wildlife Warden of Udaipur.

b: Arghya Lahiri is a writer, theatre director, lighting designer and filmmaker. He has worked in the theatre circle in every capacity he could have laid his hands on, for over twenty years. Regrets, None is his second…
f: Arghya Lahiri is a writer, theatre director, lighting designer and filmmaker. He has worked in the theatre circle in every capacity he could have laid his hands on, for over twenty years. Regrets, None is his second book.

b: Arghya Sengupta is the Research Director and founder of the Vidhi Centre for Legal Policy. A constitutional law scholar, he has published in leading journals and authored three books, including The Colonial Constitution…
f: Arghya Sengupta is the Research Director and founder of the Vidhi Centre for Legal Policy. A constitutional law scholar, he has published in leading journals and authored three books, including The Colonial Constitution . He contributes columns to The Times of India and The Telegraph .

b: Arjun Nath , after having been a successful corporate lawyer (and a somewhat less successful heroin addict) hit upon writing as the short route to fame and fabulous riches. White Magic , his recovery memoir, is…
f: Arjun Nath , after having been a successful corporate lawyer (and a somewhat less successful heroin addict) hit upon writing as the short route to fame and fabulous riches. White Magic , his recovery memoir, is documented proof that great hope may be found through a belief in God. And, peanut butter.

b: Arjun Raj Gaind is the author of The Anatomy of Loss , A Very Pukka Murder , Death at the Durbar , and, most recently, The Missing Memsahib , the first of three installments in the critically acclaimed, bestselling…
f: Arjun Raj Gaind is the author of The Anatomy of Loss , A Very Pukka Murder , Death at the Durbar , and, most recently, The Missing Memsahib , the first of three installments in the critically acclaimed, bestselling Maharaja Mystery series. Arjun has also created and written several graphic novels, including Empire of Blood , Project: Kalki , Reincarnation Man , The Mighty Yeti , Blade of the Warrior , and A Brief History of Death .

b: Arjun Subramaniam is a retired fighter pilot from the Indian Air Force. He is one of India’s leading military historians and the author of two definitive volumes on contemporary Indian military history, India’s…
f: Arjun Subramaniam is a retired fighter pilot from the Indian Air Force. He is one of India’s leading military historians and the author of two definitive volumes on contemporary Indian military history, India’s Wars: A Military History 1947-1971 and Full Spectrum: India’s Wars 1972-2020. He is currently the President’s Chair of Excellence at the National Defence College and was earlier a Visiting Fellow at The Harvard Asia Centre and Oxford University’s Changing Character of War Programme.

b: Arpita Das runs the award-winning New Delhi-based independent publishing house, Yoda Press. She is Course Leader at the Tejeshwar Singh College of Publishing, which she co-founded in collaboration with Sage Publishing.…
f: Arpita Das runs the award-winning New Delhi-based independent publishing house, Yoda Press. She is Course Leader at the Tejeshwar Singh College of Publishing, which she co-founded in collaboration with Sage Publishing. For the last four years, Das has curated the Book Award and the Word to Screen Market at the Mumbai Film Festival. Finalist for the Bookseller’s Futurebook Leader of the Year Award in 2017, she also writes for various publications and platforms on book culture, publishing, popular culture and gender.

b: Arshia Sattar has a PhD from the Department of South Asian Languages and Civilizations from the University of Chicago and has worked with Hindu myths and epics and the story traditions of the sub-continent for over…
f: Arshia Sattar has a PhD from the Department of South Asian Languages and Civilizations from the University of Chicago and has worked with Hindu myths and epics and the story traditions of the sub-continent for over thirty years. He has translated the Valmiki Ramayana from Sanskrit to critical acclaim and has also written three collections of essays- Lost Loves: Exploring Rama's Anguish, Uttara: The Book of Answers, and Maryada: Searching for Dharma in the Ramayana. She teaches classical Indian literature at various universities here and abroad and writes about books in numerous magazines.

b: Arshiya Sethi , ARTwice and a Fulbright Fellow, is an independent scholar who established and currently manages the Kri Foundation. Formerly a dance critic for The Times of India , and presenter for four decades of a…
f: Arshiya Sethi , ARTwice and a Fulbright Fellow, is an independent scholar who established and currently manages the Kri Foundation. Formerly a dance critic for The Times of India , and presenter for four decades of a featured music and dance programme on Doordarshan , she rose to advise its DD Bharati channel. Sethi is co-editor and contributor to Dance Under the Shadow of the Nation , a Dance Studies Association’s international publication. Her new areas of work include Indian dance globally, and in its intersection with the law, for which she was instrumental in creating ‘Unmute.help’ as a one-point reference window on the rights and responsibilities of artistes and arts leaders.--> Arshiya Sethi , a two-time Fulbright Fellow, braids arts, activism and knowledge through Kri Foundation. Former dance critic, Times of India; popular TV presenter; advisor, DD Bharati and Creative Head, India Habitat Centre, she co-authored the book Non-Gharanedaar: Pt Mohanrao Kallianpurkar: The Paviour of Kathak (2022); and co-edited and contributed to Dance Under the Shadow of the Nation (2019). She edits the new online international academic journal, South Asian Dance Intersections.

b: Arshya Gaur is a student in New Delhi. She is a passionate learner, debater and writer, and has written 21 articles as a teenage consultant for The DailyO, an online opinion platform and also has her own blog,…
f: Arshya Gaur is a student in New Delhi. She is a passionate learner, debater and writer, and has written 21 articles as a teenage consultant for The DailyO, an online opinion platform and also has her own blog, ‘Phoenix Fantasies’ where she posts her other writing pieces. Gaur was invited for the ‘India Today Conclave’, held in Mumbai in 2019, along with Dr. Shelja Sen, therapist, writer and co-founder of Children First, to give her personal account of her battle with Anorexia and Depression. Since then, she has founded ‘Read Together’, a website that uses multi-media technology to aid and enhance the experience of children who struggle with reading or have learning disabilities and has won the Gold Award in the Queen's Commonwealth Essay Writing Competition. She hopes to pursue English Literature in university and turn her passion for writing into a career.

b: Artemis Cooper is the author of Cairo in the War 1939-1945 and Paris After the Liberation 1944-1949 , co-written with her husband Antony Beevor. She has written biographies of Elizabeth David, Patrick Leigh Fermor and…
f: Artemis Cooper is the author of Cairo in the War 1939-1945 and Paris After the Liberation 1944-1949 , co-written with her husband Antony Beevor. She has written biographies of Elizabeth David, Patrick Leigh Fermor and Elizabeth Jane Howard, and is currently working on the cultural history of Paris.

b: Arthur Japin is one of the Netherlands best loved and bestselling authors. His novel The Big World had a first printing of 815,000 copies. His work is published in over 20 languages and has been awarded many prestigious…
f: Arthur Japin is one of the Netherlands best loved and bestselling authors. His novel The Big World had a first printing of 815,000 copies. His work is published in over 20 languages and has been awarded many prestigious prizes. Japin used to act and sing and also writes for stage and screen. His historical novels The Two Hearts of Kwasi Boachi and In Lucia’s Eyes have been worldwide bestsellers.

b: Arti Jain was one of the first people to work in FM radio in India, and was part of the energetic team that started India’s first 24 hour news channel. She went on to work on an Emmy award winning series in the United…
f: Arti Jain was one of the first people to work in FM radio in India, and was part of the energetic team that started India’s first 24 hour news channel. She went on to work on an Emmy award winning series in the United States, co-found one of the first online bookstores in India in 2008, and start a Hindi podcast in 2020. Arti is an award winning independent filmmaker, a former Dastango, a teacher, and a contributor to various magazines. She is currently the Digital Editor of Nayi Dhara , a Hindi literary magazine. Her podcast, ‘StoryJam’, where she narrates stories, has garnered much popularity.

b: Arun Kumar is the author of The Global Trade Paradigm and two books of poetry. Currently Managing Partner at Celesta Capital, he was formerly chairman and CEO of KPMG India. He served in President Obama’s…
f: Arun Kumar is the author of The Global Trade Paradigm and two books of poetry. Currently Managing Partner at Celesta Capital, he was formerly chairman and CEO of KPMG India.
