He served in President Obama’s administration as assistant secretary of commerce for global markets. He is a member of the Council on Foreign Relations.

b: Arun Maheshwari is the Managing Director of Vani Prakashan Group and Chairman of Vani Foundation. He has showcased Hindi literature in more than thirty-two countries, and among numerous awards, has received the Medal of…
f: Arun Maheshwari is the Managing Director of Vani Prakashan Group and Chairman of Vani Foundation. He has showcased Hindi literature in more than thirty-two countries, and among numerous awards, has received the Medal of Honour at the National Library, Sweden, and by the Ambassador of Norway to India, for his contribution to the field of literature and Indo-Swedish and Indo-Norwegian literary translations. As the Chairman of Vani Foundation, he has institutionalised India's first Vani Distinguished Translator Award and the Hindi Mahotsav, a literature festival dedicated to Hindi language and literature. Under his leadership, Vani Prakashan has entered its 59th year in 2022, having published over 7000 books in more than 32 genres, across 8 Indian languages.

b: Arun Maira has an unusual combination of hands-on leadership experience in the private, government, and social sectors. He was a Member of India’s Planning Commission, Chairman of BCG India, Chairman of Save the…
f: Arun Maira has an unusual combination of hands-on leadership experience in the private, government, and social sectors. He was a Member of India’s Planning Commission, Chairman of BCG India, Chairman of Save the Children India, and Chairman of HelpAge International. He worked leadership positions in the Tata Group for 25 years. He is the author of many books on transformational change and institutional reform. The latest is Shaping the Future: How to Be, Think, and Act in the New World.

b: Arun Mohan Sukumar is a PhD candidate at the Fletcher School, Tufts University and a junior fellow at the school's Centre for International Law and Governance. His first book Midnight’s Machines: A Political History…
f: Arun Mohan Sukumar is a PhD candidate at the Fletcher School, Tufts University and a junior fellow at the school's Centre for International Law and Governance. His first book Midnight’s Machines: A Political History of Technology in India , was published in December 2019. It was named among Bloomberg’s Best Books of 2020 and shortlisted for the New India Foundation’s Kamaladevi Chattopadhyay 2020 Book Prize for Non-Fiction

b: Aruna Chakravarti is a well-known academic, creative writer, and translator with seventeen publications to her credit. Her first novel, The Inheritors , was shortlisted for the Commonwealth Writers’ Prize and her…
f: Aruna Chakravarti is a well-known academic, creative writer, and translator with seventeen publications to her credit. Her first novel, The Inheritors , was shortlisted for the Commonwealth Writers’ Prize and her second, Jorasanko , received critical acclaim, becoming a bestseller. Her novel, Suralakshmi Villa , has been adjudged “Novel of the Year (India 2020)” by the Indian Bibliography published in The Journal of Commonwealth Literature UK. Her translated works include an anthology of songs from Rabindranath Tagore’s Gitabitaan , Saratchandra Chattopadhyay’s Srikanta and Sunil Gangopadhyay’s Those Days, First Light and Primal Woman: Stories. Chakravarti has received the Vaitalik Award, Sahitya Akademi Award, and Sarat Puraskar, among others.

b: Aruna Roy is a socio-political activist and Founder-Member of the Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan, the National Campaign for People’s Right to Information and the School for Democracy. Previously with the Indian…
f: Aruna Roy is a socio-political activist and Founder-Member of the Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan, the National Campaign for People’s Right to Information and the School for Democracy. Previously with the Indian Administrative Service, she left in 1975 to move to Rajasthan to work with the rural poor, providing them with the know-how to access and assert their constitutional rights. She has served as a member of the National Advisory Council and was a member of the steering committee of the Open Government Partnership till 2014. She was the 2016 Professor of Practice at McGill University’s Institute for the Study of International Development and the 2016 George Soros Visiting Practitioner Chair at the Central European University in Budapest. She is President of the National Federation of Indian Women. Her awards include the 2000 Ramon Magsaysay Award, the Nani Palkiwala Award and the Lal Bahadur Shastri National Award. She was listed as one of the 100 most influential people in the world by TIME Magazine in 2011.

b: Arunabha Ghosh is an internationally recognised public policy expert, author, columnist, and institution builder. He is the founder-CEO of the Council on Energy, Environment and Water, one of the world’s 20 best…
f: Arunabha Ghosh is an internationally recognised public policy expert, author, columnist, and institution builder. He is the founder-CEO of the Council on Energy, Environment and Water, one of the world’s 20 best climate think-tanks. Arunabha advises governments, industry, civil society, and international organisations around the world. He currently serves on the Government of India’s G20 Finance Track Advisory Group and advises the Sherpa Track for India’s G20 Presidency in 2022-23. In 2022, the UN Secretary-General appointed him to the High-level Expert Group on the Credibility and Accountability of Net-Zero Announcements by Non-State Actors. Dr Ghosh is currently Vice-Chair of the UN Committee for Development Policy, and is a member of several international expert advisory groups.

b: Arundhathi Subramaniam is a leading Indian poet and writer on spirituality. Her thirteen books of poetry and prose include the recent poetry volume, Love Without a Story, and a book of conversations with female sacred…
f: Arundhathi Subramaniam is a leading Indian poet and writer on spirituality. Her thirteen books of poetry and prose include the recent poetry volume, Love Without a Story, and a book of conversations with female sacred travellers, Women Who Wear Only Themselves . Other works include the anthology of sacred poetry, Eating God, and the bestselling biography, Sadhguru: More Than a Life. Shortlisted for the TS Eliot Prize 2015, she is the winner of the Sahitya Akademi Award 2020, the Khushwant Singh Poetry Prize, the Raza Award, the Il Ceppo Award in Italy, among others. Her new work as editor is a poetry anthology, forthcoming from Penguin India, entitled Wild Women (on the female presence in Indian mystic poetry).

b: Aruni Kashyap is a writer and translator. He is the author of His Father’s Disease and Other Stories, Noikhon Etia Duroit (in Assamese) and The House With a Thousand Stories . He won the Charles Wallace India Trust…
f: Aruni Kashyap is a writer and translator. He is the author of His Father’s Disease and Other Stories, Noikhon Etia Duroit (in Assamese) and The House With a Thousand Stories . He won the Charles Wallace India Trust Scholarship for Creative Writing to the University of Edinburgh and his poetry collection, There is No Good Time for Bad News , was a finalist for the 2018 Marsh Hawk Press Poetry Prize and 2018 Four Way Books Levis Award in Poetry. He is an Assistant Professor of Creative Writing at the University of Georgia, Athens.

b: Arunima Kukreja is a writer, interior designer and philanthropist who heads the CPKA Foundation for Design Excellence. As the Creative Head of the series Deciphering Design with Dikshu that aired on Disney+ Hotstar,…
f: Arunima Kukreja is a writer, interior designer and philanthropist who heads the CPKA Foundation for Design Excellence. As the Creative Head of the series Deciphering Design with Dikshu that aired on Disney+ Hotstar, she, along with Dikshu, explored different facets of design and how they influence our everyday lives. The book, Five Decades of India’s Built Environment is a labour of love and textual research on the process of change in design, technology and materiality from the post-Independence period to post-liberalization until the present times, focusing primarily on the influence of sustainability and cutting-edge technology on buildings.

b: Arupa Patangia Kalita is one of Assam's most celebrated writers, with five novels, fourteen short story collections, several novellas, and children's books to her name. She has received multiple literary awards,…
f: Arupa Patangia Kalita is one of Assam's most celebrated writers, with five novels, fourteen short story collections, several novellas, and children's books to her name. She has received multiple literary awards, including the Sahitya Akademi. Many of her works have been translated into English, Bengali, Hindi, and Marathi.

b: Arushi Raina ’s debut novel, When Morning Comes , has been shortlisted for the Crosswords award. The novel is set in apartheid South Africa and explores the lives of four very different teens at the brink of a youth…
f: Arushi Raina ’s debut novel, When Morning Comes , has been shortlisted for the Crosswords award. The novel is set in apartheid South Africa and explores the lives of four very different teens at the brink of a youth uprising. She likes flawed characters, escapes and sentences that make you stop and wonder.

b: Arvind Kalia is the Vice President of the Rajasthan Patrika group and Director of the Institute of Vedic Studies, as established by the group to promote scientific aspects of the world’s most ancient scriptures - the…
f: Arvind Kalia is the Vice President of the Rajasthan Patrika group and Director of the Institute of Vedic Studies, as established by the group to promote scientific aspects of the world’s most ancient scriptures - the Vedas. With a previous background in marketing, he has management degrees from IIM Ahmedabad and Kellogg School of Business, Chicago. Despite being a core marketing professional, Kalia has devoted a majority of his time over the last 35 years to the study of Indian Vedic literature. Before joining Rajasthan Patrika, he was also a prominent academician at the University of Rajasthan, teaching Marketing to MBA students.

b: Arvind Krishna Mehrotra was born in Lahore in 1947. He taught for many years at the University of Allahabad and lives in Dehradun. Among his recent books are a volume of essays titled Translating the Indian Past & Other…
f: Arvind Krishna Mehrotra was born in Lahore in 1947. He taught for many years at the University of Allahabad and lives in Dehradun. Among his recent books are a volume of essays titled Translating the Indian Past & Other Literary Histories, Blue Is Like Blue , the stories of Vinod Kumar Shukla (translated from the Hindi with Sara Rai) and Selected Poems and Translations in NYRB Poets.

b: Arvind Mayaram has a PhD in Finance and is currently an independent thinker and Economic Adviser to Chief Minister of Rajasthan. He is also Chairman at CUTS Institute for Regulation and Competition. He has earlier held…
f: Arvind Mayaram has a PhD in Finance and is currently an independent thinker and Economic Adviser to Chief Minister of Rajasthan. He is also Chairman at CUTS Institute for Regulation and Competition. He has earlier held the positions of Finance Secretary, Secretary, Ministry of Minorities and Special Secretary in the Ministry of Rural Development in the Government of India. He has also been the Alternate Governor for India on the Boards of the World Bank, the Asian Development Bank and the African Development Bank. In the Government of Rajasthan, he has worked as Commissioner, Investment and Non Resident Indians Investment, Secretary Planning, Secretary Industries and Commerce, Secretary Tourism, Art and Culture and Principal Secretary Training.

b: Arvind Singh Ashiya is a Rajasthani fiction writer and poet. His works in Rajasthani include the short story collections Katha , Katha 2 and Kabarcheetra , the poetry collection Kakido and Sinjhya , a novel. In Hindi,…
f: Arvind Singh Ashiya is a Rajasthani fiction writer and poet. His works in Rajasthani include the short story collections Katha , Katha 2 and Kabarcheetra , the poetry collection Kakido and Sinjhya , a novel. In Hindi, he has published Kachnar and Nishchay . He is the recipient of the Murlidhar Vyas Puraskar and was a member of the Rajasthani language advisory board at Kendriya Sahitya Academy from 2008 to 2012.

b: Arvind Subramanian is senior fellow at the Peterson Institute for International Economics. Previously, he has taught at Brown, Ashoka, and Harvard Universities. He served as the chief economic advisor to the government…
f: Arvind Subramanian is senior fellow at the Peterson Institute for International Economics. Previously, he has taught at Brown, Ashoka, and Harvard Universities. He served as the chief economic advisor to the government of India between 2014 and 2018. He also advises state governments on macro-economic, fiscal and sectoral issues. Foreign Policy magazine named him one of the world's top 100 global thinkers in 2011.

b: AS Barwich is a cognitive scientist and empirical philosopher. She is Assistant Professor at Indiana University Bloomington. Her research specialises in olfaction as a new model for theories of perception and cognition,…
f: AS Barwich is a cognitive scientist and empirical philosopher. She is Assistant Professor at Indiana University Bloomington. Her research specialises in olfaction as a new model for theories of perception and cognition, and the conceptual foundations of neuroscience.

b: Ashok Alexander is author of the memoir How the Light Gets In. His Antara Foundation focuses on averting needless deaths and illness amongst India’s poorest mothers and their children. Alexander has been a Senior…
f: Ashok Alexander is author of the memoir How the Light Gets In. His Antara Foundation focuses on averting needless deaths and illness amongst India’s poorest mothers and their children. Alexander has been a Senior Partner at McKinsey, head of the Gates Foundation in India, and a Senior Fellow at the Harvard School of Public Health.

b: Ashok Chakradhar is a writer, poet and screenwriter with more than 60 books to his name. He has been a professor in the Hindi Department of Jamia Milia Islamia and served as the Vice-Chairman of the Central Hindi…
f: Ashok Chakradhar is a writer, poet and screenwriter with more than 60 books to his name. He has been a professor in the Hindi Department of Jamia Milia Islamia and served as the Vice-Chairman of the Central Hindi Teaching Board (Ministry of Human Resource Development, Government of India) and at the Hindi Academy (Delhi Government). In 2014, he was honoured with a Padmashri. His other awards and honours include the Yash Bharti, the Vidyabhushan Samman, the Bal Sahityakar Puraskar, the Rashtrabhasha Samriddhi Samman, the Kaifi Azmi Award and the Sahitya Shiromani, New York Award, among others.

b: Ashok Chopra is the author of the bestselling Of Love and Other Sorrows and A Scrapbook of Memories: My Life with the Rich, the Famous and the Scandalous . Chopra has occupied some of the hottest seats in the Indian…
f: Ashok Chopra is the author of the bestselling Of Love and Other Sorrows and A Scrapbook of Memories: My Life with the Rich, the Famous and the Scandalous . Chopra has occupied some of the hottest seats in the Indian book trade, having served as executive editor of Vikas Publishing House, vice president of Macmillan India, publishing director of UBS Publishers, executive director and publisher of the India Today Book Club and Books Today as well as chief executive and publisher of HarperCollins India. He is the current chief executive of Hay House Publishers India and is working on his next book, The Lovers from Rampore .

b: Ashok Ferrey is the author of five books, all of them nominated either for Sri Lanka’s Gratiaen Prize or its State Literary Award. In fact, Ferrey’s new book The Unmarriageable Man just won the Gratiaen Prize, Sri…
f: Ashok Ferrey is the author of five books, all of them nominated either for Sri Lanka’s Gratiaen Prize or its State Literary Award. In fact, Ferrey’s new book The Unmarriageable Man just won the Gratiaen Prize, Sri Lanka’s premier literary award, founded by Michael Ondaatje. His book, The Ceaseless Chatter of Demons , was also longlisted for the DSC Prize. By day, Ashok is a personal trainer.

b: Ashok Vajpeyi is a poet, critic, art lover and institution builder. He has 15 books of poetry and seven works of criticism in Hindi. In English, he has written on visual art and Indian classical music. His works have…
f: Ashok Vajpeyi is a poet, critic, art lover and institution builder. He has 15 books of poetry and seven works of criticism in Hindi. In English, he has written on visual art and Indian classical music. His works have been translated in most Indian and many foreign languages including English, French, Polish, Arabic, Spanish, Chinese and Japanese. A well-known culture administrator, he is the founder of the multi-arts centre Bharat Bhavan and was the chairman of the Lalit Kala Akademi. He has been decorated by the President of Poland with the The Officer’s Cross of Merit of the Republic of Poland and is the recipient of France’s Officier De L’Ordre Des Arts Et Des Lettres. He is currently a Managing Trustee of the Raza Foundation.

b: Ashutosh Ramgir is the Head of Publishing at Sakal Media Group. Over the past fifteen years, he has had the privilege of publishing over a thousand books. At Sakal, he leads the 'AnyoneCanPublish' initiative, a movement…
f: Ashutosh Ramgir is the Head of Publishing at Sakal Media Group. Over the past fifteen years, he has had the privilege of publishing over a thousand books. At Sakal, he leads the 'AnyoneCanPublish' initiative, a movement to democratize publishing in Marathi, by empowering authors from all walks of life to bring their stories to print. His mission is simple yet profound: to make publishing accessible to everyone, driven by a passion for literature, and a belief in the transformative power of shared knowledge.

b: Dr. Ashwani Kumar is an eminent lawyer, thinker, author, and veteran parliamentarian who served in the Rajya Sabha for fourteen consecutive years until April 2016. During his tenure, he held several ministerial…
f: Dr. Ashwani Kumar is an eminent lawyer, thinker, author, and veteran parliamentarian who served in the Rajya Sabha for fourteen consecutive years until April 2016. During his tenure, he held several ministerial positions, including Minister for Law and Justice. He also served as Special Envoy of Prime Minister Manmohan Singh to Japan in 2013, chaired the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Science, Technology, Environment and Forests (2015–2016), and led the Rajya Sabha Select Committee on the Prevention of Torture Bill, 2010.

b: Ashwani Lohani, a former Indian Railway Services Officer who holds a LIMCA record for his four engineering degrees besides a Guinness World Record, was the Chairman of Indian Railways, CMD of Air India, CMD of ITDC, DRM…
f: Ashwani Lohani, a former Indian Railway Services Officer who holds a LIMCA record for his four engineering degrees besides a Guinness World Record, was the Chairman of Indian Railways, CMD of Air India, CMD of ITDC, DRM of Delhi, Commissioner & Managing Director of Madhya Pradesh Tourism and Director of National Rail Museum.

b: Asiya Zahoor has written books and articles on the literature of exile, Kashmiri literature, and psycholinguistics. Her film, The Stitch , has won the Critics Award for Best Film at the Second South Asian Film Festival.…
f: Asiya Zahoor has written books and articles on the literature of exile, Kashmiri literature, and psycholinguistics. Her film, The Stitch , has won the Critics Award for Best Film at the Second South Asian Film Festival. Her latest collection of poems is Serpents Under My Veil . She has recently won the Sanford Taylor Fellow at Cornell. She is currently working at a college in Baramulla, Kashmir.

b: Assa Doron is associate professor of anthropology and South Asia Studies at the Australian National University. He is co-author, with Robin Jeffrey, of Waste of a Nation: Garbage and Growth in India. Doron and Jeffrey…
f: Assa Doron is associate professor of anthropology and South Asia Studies at the Australian National University. He is co-author, with Robin Jeffrey, of Waste of a Nation: Garbage and Growth in India. Doron and Jeffrey also wrote of Cell Phone Nation. Doron is author of Life of the Ganga: Boatmen and the Ritual Economy of Banaras .

b: Atharva Pandit is a Mumbai-based writer whose works appear in The Wire and Economic and Political Weekly . A 2021 South Asia Speaks fellow for fiction, his debut novel Hurda was published by Bloomsbury India in 2022.
f: Atharva Pandit is a Mumbai-based writer whose works appear in The Wire and Economic and Political Weekly . A 2021 South Asia Speaks fellow for fiction, his debut novel Hurda was published by Bloomsbury India in 2022.

b: Atima Mankotia received her Master’s in History from St. Stephen’s College where she was awarded the Gold Medal in Ancient Indian History. She worked as an editor for print, publishing and electronic media in…
f: Atima Mankotia received her Master’s in History from St. Stephen’s College where she was awarded the Gold Medal in Ancient Indian History. She worked as an editor for print, publishing and electronic media in well-known media houses for several years and later decided to complete her MBA from XLRI, Jamshedpur. She took a sabbatical to write her debut novel Staring at the Square Moon .

b: Atmaprajnananda Saraswati has a PhD in Sanskrit and is the author of Dasasanti , Rupasiddhi , Nomenclature of the Vedas , Rsikas of the Rgveda, Om: The Sound Symbol and Vision of Advaita Vedanta in Taittiriya Upanishad…
f: Atmaprajnananda Saraswati has a PhD in Sanskrit and is the author of Dasasanti , Rupasiddhi , Nomenclature of the Vedas , Rsikas of the Rgveda, Om: The Sound Symbol and Vision of Advaita Vedanta in Taittiriya Upanishad . She has written 140 blogs for the Speaking Tree and answered 8,000 questions on them. She was conferred the title Vedanta Shiromani in 2017.

b: Atul Chaurasia has fond memories of growing up just 80 kilometres from Ayodhya in Uttar Pradesh, and nightmares of the communal violence sparked by contested claims to the holy city. He has long dreamed of penning his…
f: Atul Chaurasia has fond memories of growing up just 80 kilometres from Ayodhya in Uttar Pradesh, and nightmares of the communal violence sparked by contested claims to the holy city. He has long dreamed of penning his memoir of those turbulent times but has found himself occupied by journalism for the past 15 years. He helped found Tehelka Hindi magazine and Catch News’ Hindi website, which he led as Executive Editor. Currently, he is Executive Editor at Newslaundry. A reporter at heart, he won the Ramnath Goenka Award for Excellence in Journalism in 2010 and 2013.

b: Atul Tiwari is a playwright, screenwriter, actor, and museum-maker trained at the National School of Drama, Deutsches National Theater, and Berliner Ensemble. His productions have reached from Indian villages to global…
f: Atul Tiwari is a playwright, screenwriter, actor, and museum-maker trained at the National School of Drama, Deutsches National Theater, and Berliner Ensemble. His productions have reached from Indian villages to global metropolises. His films and acting roles have won acclaim, and his museums stand in cities across India.

b: Audrey Truschke is Assistant Professor of South Asian History at Rutgers University-Newark. 2015. Her first book, Culture of Encounters: Sanskrit at the Mughal Court , was published in 2016. Her second book, Aurangzeb:…
f: Audrey Truschke is Assistant Professor of South Asian History at Rutgers University-Newark. 2015. Her first book, Culture of Encounters: Sanskrit at the Mughal Court , was published in 2016. Her second book, Aurangzeb: The Man and The Myth , was published in 2017 and is a historical reassessment of one of the most hated kings in South Asian history. More broadly she publishes on cross-cultural exchanges, historical memory and imperial power.

b: Avi Shlaim is an Emeritus Professor of International Relations at the University of Oxford and a Fellow of the British Academy. His books include Collusion across the Jordan: King Abdullah , the Zionist Movement , and…
f: Avi Shlaim is an Emeritus Professor of International Relations at the University of Oxford and a Fellow of the British Academy. His books include Collusion across the Jordan: King Abdullah , the Zionist Movement , and the Partition of Palestine ; W ar and Peace in the Middle East: A Concise History ; The Iron Wall: Israel and the Arab World ; L ion of Jordan: The Life of King Hussein in War and Peace ; Israel and Palestine: Reappraisals, Revisions, Refutations ; and Three Worlds: Memoir of an Arab-Jew .

b: Avijit Michael has worked at the intersection of campaigning and digital technology for the past decade. He worked with the team that pioneered online petitions and digital mobilisation in India with Greenpeace. He then…
f: Avijit Michael has worked at the intersection of campaigning and digital technology for the past decade. He worked with the team that pioneered online petitions and digital mobilisation in India with Greenpeace. He then worked at Change.org as Country Director to set up their India operations before moving to a role as Global Development Director where he built strategy for user engagement globally. He currently leads Jhatkaa.org, with a mission to build the tools that will enable citizen engagement in democracy and increase government accountability.

b: Avinash Das began his career as a journalist in 1996. He has authored five books, with Mohan Shrotriya, titled Saras Gayi Sarsa, Fir se Bahne Lagi Ruparel, Arwari Nadi Ke Punarjanam ki Katha , Sammaan Ka Pani Lane Wali…
f: Avinash Das began his career as a journalist in 1996. He has authored five books, with Mohan Shrotriya, titled Saras Gayi Sarsa, Fir se Bahne Lagi Ruparel, Arwari Nadi Ke Punarjanam ki Katha , Sammaan Ka Pani Lane Wali Bhagani Tildeh and Ji Utthi Jahajwali Nadi . In 2000, Das was a Feature Editor for Prabhat Khabar and later a Resident Editor of the Patna and Deoghar editions. He later became a Senior Output Editor at NDTV India, Executive Editor of Dainik Bhaskar and a Senior Correspondent on ‘Satyamev Jayate’. In 2014, he moved into filmmaking. His Hindi feature feature film debut, Anarkali of Arrah , was released in 2017. been released on 24th March, 2017.

b: Avinash Paliwal is Reader in International Relations at SOAS University of London, specialising in South Asian strategic affairs. A former journalist and foreign affairs analyst, he is the author of India's Near East: A…
f: Avinash Paliwal is Reader in International Relations at SOAS University of London, specialising in South Asian strategic affairs. A former journalist and foreign affairs analyst, he is the author of India's Near East: A New History , and My Enemy's Enemy: India in Afghanistan from the Soviet Invasion to the US Withdrawal , both published by Hurst.

b: Avinash Pandey is Chief Executive Officer, ABP Network, serving President, News Broadcasters & Digital Association and President of the International Advertising Association India Chapter. He has been a member of…
f: Avinash Pandey is Chief Executive Officer, ABP Network, serving President, News Broadcasters & Digital Association and President of the International Advertising Association India Chapter. He has been a member of several committees, including the Media & Entertainment Committee of FICCI, Chairmanship of the National Council on Entertainment and Media – ASSOCHAM , and the Committee of Experts appointed by the I&B Ministry on ethical standards in media coverage. He is the recipient of the CEO of the Year Award at ENBA 2022 and the CEO of the Year Award at the National Awards for Excellence 2022. Under his leadership, the ABP News Channel won the Most Popular Hindi New Channel Award at the ITA Awards in 2022.

b: Avinuo Kire is a writer and teacher from Kohima, Nagaland. She has authored two short story collections, The Last Light of Glory Days and The Power to Forgive. She also writes poetry and has co-authored an anthology of…
f: Avinuo Kire is a writer and teacher from Kohima, Nagaland. She has authored two short story collections, The Last Light of Glory Days and The Power to Forgive. She also writes poetry and has co-authored an anthology of oral narratives from her home state. Her latest book is a novel, Where the Cobbled Path Leads .

b: Avyana Mehta is a 16-year-old climate advocate dedicated to environmental conservation. She founded Plastic2Build, an international environmental non-profit, and authored The Effort . Her work focuses on sustainable…
f: Avyana Mehta is a 16-year-old climate advocate dedicated to environmental conservation. She founded Plastic2Build, an international environmental non-profit, and authored The Effort . Her work focuses on sustainable resource implementation that bridges people and the environment, making climate action practical, accessible, inclusive, and grounded.

b: Ayaan Ali Bangash represents the 7th generation of a musical lineage, as son and disciple of the sarod icon, Amjad Ali Khan. He has performed across the globe, including prestigious venues like Carnegie Hall, Kennedy…
f: Ayaan Ali Bangash represents the 7th generation of a musical lineage, as son and disciple of the sarod icon, Amjad Ali Khan. He has performed across the globe, including prestigious venues like Carnegie Hall, Kennedy Center, Smithsonian, and WOMAD Festivals in many continents. With his brother Amaan Ali Bangash, he has collaborated with guitarist Derek Trucks of the Allman Brothers Band, Guitarist Sharon Isbin, Chicago Philharmonic orchestra, and Avignon symphony orchestra, among others, and established themselves as a duo, carrying forward their musical legacy in sync with both tradition and contemporary times. They performed at the Nobel Peace Prize Concert 2014 in Oslo, and recently won the Gold Medal at the Global Music Awards in Los Angeles for their new album Peace Worshippers .

b: Ayodhya Prasad Gaur is a TEDx speaker, theatre artist, and writer. He began his writing journey during his Master’s degree in Geology and later worked with Dainik Bhaskar, Hindustan Times, and India Today. He is the…
f: Ayodhya Prasad Gaur is a TEDx speaker, theatre artist, and writer. He began his writing journey during his Master’s degree in Geology and later worked with Dainik Bhaskar, Hindustan Times, and India Today. He is the author of several acclaimed books, including The Royal Blue, Durg Gaatha , Chautha Dhandha, and Pintoo , Pankhi aur Rampyari . He also co-authored The Vulture’s Feast: A Story on the Indian Media with Roshni Rajaram. His latest work, Ayodhya Manas Ramleela , is a script based on Goswami Tulsidas’s Ramcharitmanas . He has acted in several stage plays, radio dramas, and television serials including Meera and Duvidha .

b: Ayushi Rastogi was born into a family of artists and was quickly instilled with a drive to seek social responsibility in her work. With that spirit, as a graphic designer and illustrator, she’s created a board game…
f: Ayushi Rastogi was born into a family of artists and was quickly instilled with a drive to seek social responsibility in her work. With that spirit, as a graphic designer and illustrator, she’s created a board game for children with dyslexia, illustrated a children’s series that tackles topics of diversity, and designed books on pressing issues from nature conservation to pollution.

b: Azeem Ibrahim is a Research Professor at the Strategic Studies Institute, U.S. Army War College and member of the Board of Directors at the International Centre for the Study of Radicalisation and Political Violence at…
f: Azeem Ibrahim is a Research Professor at the Strategic Studies Institute, U.S. Army War College and member of the Board of Directors at the International Centre for the Study of Radicalisation and Political Violence at the Department of War Studies at King’s College London University. Over the years, Dr. Ibrahim has advised numerous world leaders on policy development. In his most recent roles, he served as National Security and Defence Policy Advisor to the Leader of the (UK) Labour Party, Rt Hon Ed Miliband MP, and the Shadow Cabinet from 2012 to 2015. He also served as Strategic Policy Advisor to the Chairman of Pakistan’s PTI party, Imran Khan. He has published hundreds of articles in global publication. He is the author of the seminal book, The Rohingyas: Inside Myanmar’s Hidden Genocide, published in 2016. His latest book is Radical Virus: Why We Are Losing the War Against Islamic Extremism .

b: B.N. Goswamy , a leading Indian art historian, is Professor Emeritus of Art History at the Panjab University, Chandigarh. His work covers a wide range and has significantly influenced thinking on Indian painting. A…
f: B.N. Goswamy , a leading Indian art historian, is Professor Emeritus of Art History at the Panjab University, Chandigarh. His work covers a wide range and has significantly influenced thinking on Indian painting. A recipient of several honours, including the Padma Shri and the Padma Bhushan, he is the author of more than 25 books, including Nainsukh of Guler and The Spirit of Indian Painting. His most recent work is on the painter, Manaku of Guler.

b: Badri Narayan is a social historian, cultural anthropologist, and poet. Renowned for his pioneering scholarship on democratic consciousness and the intricate intersections of power and culture, he has made lasting…
f: Badri Narayan is a social historian, cultural anthropologist, and poet. Renowned for his pioneering scholarship on democratic consciousness and the intricate intersections of power and culture, he has made lasting contributions to both social science and literature. His critically acclaimed works include Republic of Hindutva: How the Sangh Is Reshaping Indian Democracy , Fractured Tales: Invisibles in Indian Democracy ,and Women Heroes and Dalit Assertion in North India . Badri Narayan is also a leading literary voice in Hindi literature. He has received the Sahitya Akademi Award for his poetry collection Tumdi ke Shabd . His other poetry collections include Pratinidhi Kavitaye , Shabpadiyam , and Sach Sune Kai Din Huye . Widely respected for his political analyses, he writes regular columns for leading newspapers.

b: Balaji Vittal is a second-generation Calcuttan with his roots in the city dating back to the 1950s. He is the co-author of the National Award-winning book, RD Burman: The Man, The Music , and the MAMI Award-winning…
f: Balaji Vittal is a second-generation Calcuttan with his roots in the city dating back to the 1950s. He is the co-author of the National Award-winning book, RD Burman: The Man, The Music , and the MAMI Award-winning book, Gaata Rahe Mera Dil- 50 Classic Hindi Film Songs. His most recent book, Pure Evil - The Bad Men of Bollywood , is his first solo-authored book.

b: Dr. Balakrishna Pisupati is an internationally renowned conservation and development specialist with nearly three decades of experience at national, regional, and international levels. He has held key positions,…
f: Dr. Balakrishna Pisupati is an internationally renowned conservation and development specialist with nearly three decades of experience at national, regional, and international levels. He has held key positions, including Head of the UNEP Environmental Policy Unit, Head of the Biodiversity and Governance Programme at UNEP, Senior Policy Fellow at the Fridtjof Nansen Institute (Norway), Chairman of the National Biodiversity Authority (India), and Coordinator of the Biodiplomacy Programme at United Nations University (UNU-IAS, Japan). He currently serves as the Country Head of UNEP in India, driving initiatives in environmental policy, biodiversity governance, and sustainable development.

b: Balram Shukla , a faculty member of the Sanskrit department at the University of Delhi, is currently a Fellow at IIAS, Shimla. He holds University degrees in Sanskrit and Persian, with gold medals, and has three…
f: Balram Shukla , a faculty member of the Sanskrit department at the University of Delhi, is currently a Fellow at IIAS, Shimla. He holds University degrees in Sanskrit and Persian, with gold medals, and has three Sanskrit and two Persian poetry collections, among other books, to his credit. Shukla has translated several Persian texts directly into Hindi, and has been frequently invited for academic and cultural programmes in India and Iran. He was conferred with the prestigious Maharshi Badrayan Vyas Samman by the President of India and other awards.

b: Bandeep Singh is a reputed editorial and fine art photographer. Known for his powerful portraits and lighting skills , his images have been published in Time, Fortune, The New York Times, Business Week, Business Today,…
f: Bandeep Singh is a reputed editorial and fine art photographer. Known for his powerful portraits and lighting skills , his images have been published in Time, Fortune, The New York Times, Business Week, Business Today, and numerous other publications. He is currently working as the Group Photo Editor for the India Today Group of Publications. Bandeep has been on the jury of the India Habitat Centre Grant for Photography for more than 10 years, and a part of the core organising team of Photosphere Photography Festival. In 2004, he was the recipient of the Charles Wallace India Trust Award in photography. From 2016 - 2023 his images have won 5 Gold Awards at the WAN IFRA Asian Media Awards. His works are in the permanent collection of the Essl Museum of Contemporary Art, Vienna; The Nirankari Museum of Faith, Delhi, as well as in several private collections.

b: Banu Mushtaq is a celebrated Kannada writer, activist, and lawyer from Karnataka, and a key voice in the Bandaya movement. Her acclaimed short-story collection Heart Lamp is regarded as a landmark in Kannada literature.…
f: Banu Mushtaq is a celebrated Kannada writer, activist, and lawyer from Karnataka, and a key voice in the Bandaya movement. Her acclaimed short-story collection Heart Lamp is regarded as a landmark in Kannada literature. It won the International Booker Prize 2025 and the English PEN Award. Her work powerfully explores caste, gender, and marginalization with striking literary clarity.

b: Barbara Wickham OBE, is Director, British Council India, and leads the India operations of the organisation across their work in English, Education and Arts. She is committed to strengthening the educational and…
f: Barbara Wickham OBE, is Director, British Council India, and leads the India operations of the organisation across their work in English, Education and Arts. She is committed to strengthening the educational and cultural exchange between India and the UK, and over the last year, has led on steering the organisation’s response and innovation in digital delivery since the outbreak of the Covid-19 pandemic. Prior to joining the India team, she led the British Council operation in Bangladesh for over four years. As a committed environmentalist, she is proud to have established a carbon-neutral operation in Bangladesh through a mangrove rehabilitation scheme.

b: Barkha Dutt is an award-winning TV journalist, anchor and columnist. She is India’s only Emmy-nominated journalist who has won multiple national and international awards, including the prestigious Padma Shri. Dutt has…
f: Barkha Dutt is an award-winning TV journalist, anchor and columnist. She is India’s only Emmy-nominated journalist who has won multiple national and international awards, including the prestigious Padma Shri. Dutt has reported from some of the toughest spots and conflict zones in India and across the world, and her frontline reporting of the Kargil war first made her a household name. She is an outspoken feminist voice on the global stage and the Founder-Editor of Mojo, a multi-media events and content venture, and founder of We The Women, a multi-city festival and current affairs website. She is a featured columnist with The Washington Post , appears regularly as an analyst on CNN and BBC , and is a contributing editor at The Week.

b: Barkha Dutt is an award-winning TV journalist, anchor and columnist with more than two decades of reporting experience. She is India’s only Emmy-nominated journalist who has won multiple national and international…
f: Barkha Dutt is an award-winning TV journalist, anchor and columnist with more than two decades of reporting experience. She is India’s only Emmy-nominated journalist who has won multiple national and international awards, including the Padmashri. Dutt has reported from some of the toughest spots from around the world. She is the Founder-Editor of Mojo , and We The Women , a multi-city festival and current affairs website that focuses on the biggest gender debates of our time.

b: Barnaby Rogerson has authored a dozen books on North Africa and Early Islam over the past thirty-five years. His latest work is The House Divided: Sunni, Shia and the Making of the Middle East . He runs Eland Publishing…
f: Barnaby Rogerson has authored a dozen books on North Africa and Early Islam over the past thirty-five years. His latest work is The House Divided: Sunni, Shia and the Making of the Middle East . He runs Eland Publishing with his partner Rose Baring, focusing on preserving classic travel literature.

b: Barry O'Farrell served as a Liberal Party member of the New South Wales Parliament for 20 years, including as Premier. He was Australia’s High Commissioner to India 2020-2023.
f: Barry O'Farrell served as a Liberal Party member of the New South Wales Parliament for 20 years, including as Premier. He was Australia’s High Commissioner to India 2020-2023.

b: Barry O’Farrell was announced as Australia’s High Commissioner to India in February 2020. He served in the Parliament of New South Wales from 1995 to 2015, including as the State’s 43rd Premier between 2011 and…
f: Barry O’Farrell was announced as Australia’s High Commissioner to India in February 2020. He served in the Parliament of New South Wales from 1995 to 2015, including as the State’s 43rd Premier between 2011 and 2014. Australia’s most populous and multicultural State, New South Wales generates a third of the nation’s Gross Domestic Product. As Premier, O’Farrell initiated and led annual trade missions to India to promote economic, cultural and social links between New South Wales and the states of India. He has also served as NSW’s Special Envoy for India and has made a significant contribution as the Deputy Chair of the Australia India Council Board. O’Farrell has a Bachelor of Arts from the Australian National University, Canberra.

b: Barsali Bhattacharyya is a writer and researcher focusing on the intersection of technology, economics, and society. Her debut book, Enter Prompt: Navigating AI in the World’s Largest Democracy , examines the impact of…
f: Barsali Bhattacharyya is a writer and researcher focusing on the intersection of technology, economics, and society. Her debut book, Enter Prompt: Navigating AI in the World’s Largest Democracy , examines the impact of artificial intelligence on Indian lives, livelihoods, and social structures. She brings over 14 years of experience researching and writing on economics, business, and consumer trends, gained at organisations such as The Economist Intelligence Unit and Visa, and through her work as a journalist with Business Standard and India Today . Her work offers a critical, accessible perspective on how emerging technologies shape democracy and everyday life in India.

b: Basharat Peer is an opinion editor at The New York Times. He is the author of A Question of Order: India, Turkey and the Return of Strongmen . His memoir, Curfewed Night, won India’s Crossword Award for Non-Fiction…
f: Basharat Peer is an opinion editor at The New York Times. He is the author of A Question of Order: India, Turkey and the Return of Strongmen . His memoir, Curfewed Night, won India’s Crossword Award for Non-Fiction and was chosen as a Book of the Year by both The New Yorker and The Economist. He wrote the screenplay for Haider, an adaptation of Hamlet set in the conflict in Kashmir. He has been an editor at Foreign Affairs and The New York Times’ India Ink blog, and has written for The New Yorker, Granta, Foreign Affairs, The Guardian, n+1 and The New York Times.

b: Bee Rowlatt’ s In Search of Mary was a “biography of the year” ( Independent ). She co-wrote the best-selling Talking about Jane Austen in Baghdad and features in Virago’s Fifty Shades of Feminism . Rowlatt’s…
f: Bee Rowlatt’ s In Search of Mary was a “biography of the year” ( Independent ). She co-wrote the best-selling Talking about Jane Austen in Baghdad and features in Virago’s Fifty Shades of Feminism . Rowlatt’s done festivals in Russia, Bangladesh, Mexico, Iraq, Colombia and the UK but her heart belongs to Jaipur! She began in BBC World Service and has written for national and international media. Rowlatt chairs the Mary Wollstonecraft campaign.

b: Beena Kamlani is a prize-winning writer, teacher, and editor. At Penguin Random House in New York she edited a wide range of authors, including Nobelists Saul Bellow and Sir Peter Medawar, Booker prize winners Paul…
f: Beena Kamlani is a prize-winning writer, teacher, and editor. At Penguin Random House in New York she edited a wide range of authors, including Nobelists Saul Bellow and Sir Peter Medawar, Booker prize winners Paul Beatty and Jiang Rong, and Robert Fagles on his translations of Homer and Virgil. The English Problem is her debut novel.

b: Ben Judah’s first book, Fragile Empire, was a Financial Times Summer Book of 2013. This Is London was longlisted for the Ballie Gifford Prize and is currently a finalist for the Ryszard Kapuściński Prize for…
f: Ben Judah’s first book, Fragile Empire, was a Financial Times Summer Book of 2013. This Is London was longlisted for the Ballie Gifford Prize and is currently a finalist for the Ryszard Kapuściński Prize for Literary Reportage. His journalism, amongst many other places, has appeared in The Sunday Times, The New York Times, Atlantic and the Financial Times.

b: Ben Macintyre has written a weekly column in The Times since 1998 on history, espionage, art, politics and foreign affairs. Before taking up his current post as Writer at Large and Associate Editor on the newspaper, he…
f: Ben Macintyre has written a weekly column in The Times since 1998 on history, espionage, art, politics and foreign affairs. Before taking up his current post as Writer at Large and Associate Editor on the newspaper, he was the editor of The Times Weekend Review , a weekly supplement covering the arts and literature. He joined the newspaper in 1992 as New York Correspondent and went on to become Paris Bureau Chief and then US Editor, based in Washington, before returning to the UK in 2002 as parliamentary sketch-writer. He is the author of 13 non-fiction history books, including the bestselling wartime trilogy Agent Zigzag, Operation Mincemeat and Double Cross. Operation Mincemeat, shortlisted for the National Book Awards, was the number one Sunday Times bestseller in hardback and paperback, remaining in the top ten for 21 weeks. A Spy Among Friends was also a number one bestseller, as was SAS: Rogue Heroes, which remained in the top ten paperback bestseller chart for 15 weeks. His last six books have each been New York Times and Sunday Times bestsellers. The Spy and the Traitor , was described by John le Carré as “The best true spy story I have ever read.” Agent Sonya was also a bestseller on both sides of the Atlantic. Macintyre’s books have sold more than two million copies worldwide, and have been translated into more than 25 languages.

b: Ben Okri is an acclaimed poet, novelist, essayist, playwright and Man Booker Prize winner for The Famished Road . His work has been translated into 27 languages and won numerous international prizes. His most recent…
f: Ben Okri is an acclaimed poet, novelist, essayist, playwright and Man Booker Prize winner for The Famished Road . His work has been translated into 27 languages and won numerous international prizes. His most recent novel is The Freedom Artist .

b: Benjamin Brose is an Associate Professor of Chinese Religions and Buddhist Studies at the University of Michigan. His most recent publications include Xuanzang: China’s Legendary Pilgrim and Translator and Taming the…
f: Benjamin Brose is an Associate Professor of Chinese Religions and Buddhist Studies at the University of Michigan. His most recent publications include Xuanzang: China’s Legendary Pilgrim and Translator and Taming the Monkey: Reinterpreting the Xiyou ji [Journey to the West] in the Early Twentieth Century .

b: Benjamin Dix began his career as a professional photographer, working in South Asia, and has subsequently worked as a Communications Manager for the United Nations and various international NGOs across Asia and Africa…
f: Benjamin Dix began his career as a professional photographer, working in South Asia, and has subsequently worked as a Communications Manager for the United Nations and various international NGOs across Asia and Africa for 12 years. After working for the UN through the civil war in Sri Lanka, Dr. Dix founded PositiveNegatives to produce literary comics that explore complex social and human rights issues, including conflict, migration and asylum. Each comic has reached over 2 million viewers around the world of all ages and many have been translated into multiple languages reaching diverse international stakeholders.

b: Benoy K. Behl is an art historian, photographer, and filmmaker with 53,000 art heritage photographs, 146 documentaries, and exhibitions in 74 countries. His books include The Ajanta Caves and The Art of India .
f: Benoy K. Behl is an art historian, photographer, and filmmaker with 53,000 art heritage photographs, 146 documentaries, and exhibitions in 74 countries. His books include The Ajanta Caves and The Art of India .

b: Benyamin is a Malayalam novelist and short story writer. He has published 24 books, including nine novels. Aadujeevitham ( Goat Days ) was a huge success that has been reprinted more than 150 times. It won the Kerala…
f: Benyamin is a Malayalam novelist and short story writer. He has published 24 books, including nine novels. Aadujeevitham ( Goat Days ) was a huge success that has been reprinted more than 150 times. It won the Kerala Sahitya Akademi Award and was translated into many languages. The bestselling Jasmine Days won the JCB Prize for Literature 2018 and the Crossword Book Award 2018 for translation.

b: Bernardine Evaristo won the Booker Prize 2019 with her eighth book, Girl, Woman, Other, and became the first black woman and black British person to win it. Her memoir, Manifesto: On Never Giving Up , was published in…
f: Bernardine Evaristo won the Booker Prize 2019 with her eighth book, Girl, Woman, Other, and became the first black woman and black British person to win it. Her memoir, Manifesto: On Never Giving Up , was published in 2021. Her writing spans fiction, poetry, non-fiction, literary criticism and drama. She has founded several successful arts inclusion projects. The recipient of many honours, including two recent British Book Awards, she was named ‘Person of the Year’ by the UK Bookseller magazine in 2021. She is Professor of Creative Writing at Brunel University London; an Honorary Fellow of St. Anne’s College, University of Oxford; an International Honorary Fellow of the American Academy of Arts and Sciences and President of the Royal Society of Literature.

b: Bettany Hughes is an award-winning historian, author and broadcaster. Her previous books, Istanbul: A Tale of Three Cities, Helen of Troy: Goddess, Princess, Whore and The Hemlock Cup: Socrates, Athens and the Search…
f: Bettany Hughes is an award-winning historian, author and broadcaster. Her previous books, Istanbul: A Tale of Three Cities, Helen of Troy: Goddess, Princess, Whore and The Hemlock Cup: Socrates, Athens and the Search for the Good Life, were published to critical acclaim and worldwide success. Hughes is a Research Fellow of King's College London, a Tutor at Cambridge University’s Institute for Continuing Education and a Visiting Professor of History at the New College of the Humanities. She has been honoured with numerous awards, including the prestigious Norton Medlicott Medal for History. She has made a number of documentaries on history, culture and philosophy, including Byzantium Unearthed and a series for BBC Radio 4 Ancient Ways.

b: Bette Dam is a Dutch investigative journalist who made a career working in Afghanistan, Syria and Iraq. She is currently a lecturer at the Sciences Po university in Paris on the subject of Afghanistan. Dam is also the…
f: Bette Dam is a Dutch investigative journalist who made a career working in Afghanistan, Syria and Iraq. She is currently a lecturer at the Sciences Po university in Paris on the subject of Afghanistan. Dam is also the author of A Man and a Motorcycle: How Hamid Karzai Came to Power .

b: Bhajju Shyam is a Gond artist whose best-known work, The London Jungle Book , is a visual travelogue of his 2002 visit to London. He is the first Gond Artist to be conferred with the Padma Shri and he has been a part of…
f: Bhajju Shyam is a Gond artist whose best-known work, The London Jungle Book , is a visual travelogue of his 2002 visit to London. He is the first Gond Artist to be conferred with the Padma Shri and he has been a part of 20 books which have cumulatively sold 100,000 copies.

b: Bharati Shivaji’s pursuit of Mohiniyattam has initiated her into other regional art forms of Kerala, enabling her to imbibe the aesthetics of Mohiniyattam not in isolation but in significant relation to the inter…
f: Bharati Shivaji’s pursuit of Mohiniyattam has initiated her into other regional art forms of Kerala, enabling her to imbibe the aesthetics of Mohiniyattam not in isolation but in significant relation to the inter disciplinary traditions of Kerala, be it sculpture, theatre, music, painting architecture and literature. Her wide experience led her to choreograph some of the classic plays in theatre like Dhootha Vakyam, the National School of Drama's Abhigyana Shakuntalam and Viddyottama. She is the author of the books The Art of Mohiniyattam and Mohiniyattam. She has many group choreographies to her credit, ensuring Mohiniyattam 's place on the world map. For her invaluable contribution, she was awarded the Lasyalakshmi by the Kunchan Nambiar Memorial Trust, Kerala. She is the recipient of the Sangeet Nat Ak Akademi, the Sahitya Kala Parishad Samman and Padmashri by the Government of India and the Nrityacoodamani. The Kerala Kalamanadalam, deemed university for Art and Culture, conferred on her the title Kalaratnam for her unique contribution to Mohiniyattam. She was recently awarded the Nishagandhi Puraskaram by the government of Kerala for her lifelong contribution to Mohiniyattam.

b: Bhavika Govil is the author of Hot Water , her debut novel, which was shortlisted for the 2025 Godrej Literature Live! First Book Award and longlisted for the 2025 Ramnath Goenka Sahitya Samman. The novel is forthcoming…
f: Bhavika Govil is the author of Hot Water , her debut novel, which was shortlisted for the 2025 Godrej Literature Live! First Book Award and longlisted for the 2025 Ramnath Goenka Sahitya Samman. The novel is forthcoming in the UK and is being translated into other languages. Her short fiction has appeared in Granta , Wasafiri , and elsewhere. She also teaches creative writing.

b: Bhavna Roy was educated in Mussoorie, Pune, and Mumbai. After graduating in psychology from Mumbai University, she qualified for the Indian Administrative Services. Having received partial training at the LBSNAA, she…
f: Bhavna Roy was educated in Mussoorie, Pune, and Mumbai. After graduating in psychology from Mumbai University, she qualified for the Indian Administrative Services. Having received partial training at the LBSNAA, she quit and subsequently worked as a volunteer in a school for special children in Malegaon. Following that, she worked in an NGO in Nashik called SOS. Later, she tutored secondary and higher secondary students in software engineering in Mumbai. She is the author of Dharma, Decoding the Epics for a Meaningful Life and Idols, Unearthing the Power of Murti Puja.

b: Bhawana Somaaya is a film critic and an author. She has been writing on cinema for almost 50 years. She is the former editor of Screen and written biographies of superstars such as Hema Malini and Amitabh Bachchan. Her…
f: Bhawana Somaaya is a film critic and an author. She has been writing on cinema for almost 50 years. She is the former editor of Screen and written biographies of superstars such as Hema Malini and Amitabh Bachchan. Her books are a point of reference for students studying Indian cinema in India and abroad. She has translated Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Gujarati books, Saakshi Bhaav and Aankh Aa Dhanya Chhe into English as Letters to Mother and Letters to Self . Somaaya was conferred with the Padma Shri in 2017, an honorary Doctorate by Jagran Lake City University in 2021, and the Kanak Nartan Puraskaar from Nalanda Nrityakala Mahavidyalay in 2022. She is a classical dancer, a broadcaster, a podcaster, and author of twenty books. Her recent book, Farewell Karachi , is the story of her family, and spans more than 100 years and five generations.

b: Bhuchung D Sonam is a poet, translator and publisher. His books include Songs from Dewachen , Yak Horns: Notes on Contemporary Tibetan Writing, Music and Film and Politics and Burning the Sun’s Braids: New Poetry from…
f: Bhuchung D Sonam is a poet, translator and publisher. His books include Songs from Dewachen , Yak Horns: Notes on Contemporary Tibetan Writing, Music and Film and Politics and Burning the Sun’s Braids: New Poetry from Tibet. He is a founding member of TibetWrites and its imprint Blackneck Books. His writings are published in the Washington Post , Journal of Indian Literature, HIMAL Southasian, and Tibetan Review among others.

b: Bibek Debroy is an economist and was educated in Ramakrishna Mission School in Narendrapur, Presidency College in Kolkata, the Delhi School of Economics and Trinity College, Cambridge. Presently, he is Chairman,…
f: Bibek Debroy is an economist and was educated in Ramakrishna Mission School in Narendrapur, Presidency College in Kolkata, the Delhi School of Economics and Trinity College, Cambridge. Presently, he is Chairman, Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister and President, Indian Statistical Institute. He has worked in Presidency College, the Gokhale Institute of Politics and Economics in Pune, the Indian Institute of Foreign Trade, as the Director of a Ministry of Finance/UNDP project on legal reforms, the Department of Economic Affairs, the National Council of Applied Economic Research, the Rajiv Gandhi Institute for Contemporary Studies, the PHD Chamber of Commerce and Industry, the Centre for Policy Research and as Member of NITI Aayog. He has authored/edited several books, papers and popular articles and has also been a Consulting/ Contributing Editor with several newspapers.

b: Bijoya Sawian is a writer and translator from Meghalaya. Her literary works revolve around the indigenous Khasi tribe. Sawian's translations, The Teachings of Elders , The Main Ceremonies of the Khasis and The Book…
f: Bijoya Sawian is a writer and translator from Meghalaya. Her literary works revolve around the indigenous Khasi tribe. Sawian's translations, The Teachings of Elders , The Main Ceremonies of the Khasis and The Book About One God are valuable contributions towards the preservation of the culture and tradition of the tribe she belongs to. Shadow Men & Two Stories and Hill Songs of Love and Longing , narrated in her signature lyrical style, are highly acclaimed works of fiction.

b: Bill Crozier , born in England, trained in medicine at Guy’s Hospital, London, and specialised in anaesthetics and intensive care. His passion for high-altitude medicine stems from his love of the mountains.
f: Bill Crozier , born in England, trained in medicine at Guy’s Hospital, London, and specialised in anaesthetics and intensive care. His passion for high-altitude medicine stems from his love of the mountains.

b: Bill Gates is a technologist, business leader and philanthropist. In 1975, he co-founded Microsoft with his childhood friend Paul Allen. Today he and his wife, Melinda, are co-chairs of the Bill & Melinda Gates…
f: Bill Gates is a technologist, business leader and philanthropist. In 1975, he co-founded Microsoft with his childhood friend Paul Allen. Today he and his wife, Melinda, are co-chairs of the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation. Gates also launched Breakthrough Energy, a network of entities and initiatives, including investment funds, non-profit and philanthropic programmes, and policy efforts linked by a common commitment to scale the technologies we need to achieve a path to net-zero emissions by 2050.

b: Bina Kak is a politician, actor and social activist. She served as Cabinet Minister in the Government of Rajasthan from 1985 to 2013, holding important portfolios such as Tourism Art and Culture, Archaeology, Forests…
f: Bina Kak is a politician, actor and social activist. She served as Cabinet Minister in the Government of Rajasthan from 1985 to 2013, holding important portfolios such as Tourism Art and Culture, Archaeology, Forests and Environment, Women and Child Development. Her work has now become her passion. She works tirelessly towards wildlife conservation and has helped revive several dying arts by promoting performing arts of the state. Kak also started a special school, Umang, that works with children suffering brain damage in Rajasthan.

b: Bishnupriya Dutt is Professor of Theatre and Performance studies, at the School of Arts and Aesthetics, Jawaharlal Nehru University, Delhi. Her area of research includes politics and theatre; as well as feminist…
f: Bishnupriya Dutt is Professor of Theatre and Performance studies, at the School of Arts and Aesthetics, Jawaharlal Nehru University, Delhi. Her area of research includes politics and theatre; as well as feminist readings of Indian Theatre and contemporary performance practices. Her recent publications include Maya Rao and Indian Feminist Theatre ; Theatre, Activism and Subjectivity ; and Searching for the Left in a Fragmented World . She was the distinguished fellow at the Cluster of Excellence (EXC 2020), and is currently a Leverhulme Professor at the Royal Central School of Speech and Drama. Bishnupriya Dutt is also the President of the International Federation for Theatre Research. She has been involved in active theatre in Calcutta since the 1960s, at the Little Theatre Group, and later the People’s Little Theatre, where she performs and directs.

b: Bishwadeep Moitra is an independent graphic designer, photographer and a writer–editor. Associated with publishing for the past 25 years as a visual journalist, launching and relaunching major magazines and newspapers…
f: Bishwadeep Moitra is an independent graphic designer, photographer and a writer–editor. Associated with publishing for the past 25 years as a visual journalist, launching and relaunching major magazines and newspapers in India, he is best known for designing magazine covers as well as illustrated books.

b: Biswadip Chakraborty is an engineer, writer, publisher, and literary organizer. He is the Founder Director of the Antonym Council of Global Arts and Literature (ACGAL), which organizes translation workshops,…
f: Biswadip Chakraborty is an engineer, writer, publisher, and literary organizer. He is the Founder Director of the Antonym Council of Global Arts and Literature (ACGAL), which organizes translation workshops, residencies, and literary events. Biswadip is also the Managing Director of Antonym Collections, a translation-only publishing house based in Kolkata, and Xako Publishing, Assam.

b: Bitan Chakraborty , founder of Hawakal Publishers, is essentially a storyteller. He has authored seven books of fiction and prose, translated two collections of poems, and edited a volume of essays.
f: Bitan Chakraborty , founder of Hawakal Publishers, is essentially a storyteller. He has authored seven books of fiction and prose, translated two collections of poems, and edited a volume of essays.

b: Blaise Fernandes is the President and CEO of the Indian Music Industry- the apex body that represents the recorded music industry in India and has over thirty-four years of experience in the entertainment industry. He…
f: Blaise Fernandes is the President and CEO of the Indian Music Industry- the apex body that represents the recorded music industry in India and has over thirty-four years of experience in the entertainment industry. He headed Warner Bros, India, as CEO for twenty years. Formerly CEO of Gateway House, a foreign policy think-tank, Fernandes currently serves as a Director on the Board of Gateway House. He sits on various committees at apex trade bodies such as CII and FICCI. Fernandes writes and publishes papers regularly on subjects pertaining to IP Monetisation & Protection, Digital Governance and more.

b: BN Goswamy, India’s leading art historian, is Professor Emeritus of Art History at the Panjab University, Chandigarh. His work, especially in the area of Indian painting, has influenced much thinking. The recipient of…
f: BN Goswamy, India’s leading art historian, is Professor Emeritus of Art History at the Panjab University, Chandigarh. His work, especially in the area of Indian painting, has influenced much thinking. The recipient of many honours, including the Jawaharlal Nehru Fellowship, the Rietberg Award for Outstanding Research in Art History, the Padma Shri (1998) and the Padma Bhushan (2008) from the President of India. he has taught, as Visiting Professor, at several universities across the world, among them the Universities of Pennsylvania, Heidelberg, California (at Berkeley and Los Angeles) and Zurich. He has also been responsible for major exhibitions of Indian art at Paris, San Francisco, Zurich, San Diego, New York, Frankfurt and New Delhi. Professor Goswamy has written more than 25 books, among them classics like Pahari Masters, Nainsukh of Guler, The Spirit of Indian Painting and The Great Mysore Bhagavata.

b: Bonnie Garmus is a novelist, copywriter, and creative director, who has worked for a wide range of clients, in the US and abroad, focusing primarily on technology, medicine, and education.
f: Bonnie Garmus is a novelist, copywriter, and creative director, who has worked for a wide range of clients, in the US and abroad, focusing primarily on technology, medicine, and education.

b: Boria Majumdar , a Rhodes scholar, is the author of multiple books on Indian sport and its history. His most recent work, Eleven Gods and a Billion Indians , was awarded the Rabindra Puraskar for Literature in 2018. He…
f: Boria Majumdar , a Rhodes scholar, is the author of multiple books on Indian sport and its history. His most recent work, Eleven Gods and a Billion Indians , was awarded the Rabindra Puraskar for Literature in 2018. He is Senior Research Fellow at the University of Central Lancashire and Adjunct Professor, Monash University, Melbourne. He also serves as Consulting Editor, Sports, for the India Today Group.

b: Brahma Challaney is Professor of Strategic Studies at the Centre for Policy Research in New Delhi, a fellow of the Robert Bosch Academy in Berlin and an affiliate with the International Centre for the Study of…
f: Brahma Challaney is Professor of Strategic Studies at the Centre for Policy Research in New Delhi, a fellow of the Robert Bosch Academy in Berlin and an affiliate with the International Centre for the Study of Radicalisation at King’s College London. He has served as a member of the Policy Advisory Group and as an adviser to India’s National Security Council. He is the author of nine books including the international bestseller, Asian Juggernaut: The Rise of China, India, and Japan . His recent books are Water, Peace, and War: Confronting the Global Water Crisis and Water: Asia’s New Battleground , winner of the 2012 Bernard Schwartz Award.

b: Brian A. Catlos studies Muslim-Christian-Jewish relations in medieval Christendom and the Islamic World, and the history of the pre-Modern Mediterranean. His books have been translated into ten languages and won major…
f: Brian A. Catlos studies Muslim-Christian-Jewish relations in medieval Christendom and the Islamic World, and the history of the pre-Modern Mediterranean. His books have been translated into ten languages and won major awards from the American Historical Association, the Medieval Academy of America and the Middle East Studies Association. He also writes travel guides.

b: Brigitte Singh first came to Sanganer, Jaipur’s hand blockprinting centre, from France as a student of miniatures more than three decades ago. Today, her exquisite work with block prints is a form of re-enacted design…
f: Brigitte Singh first came to Sanganer, Jaipur’s hand blockprinting centre, from France as a student of miniatures more than three decades ago. Today, her exquisite work with block prints is a form of re-enacted design history. Her work yields a truly Indian aesthetic, fully formed and yet open to influences, full of grand narratives but dense with detail and meaning that in every telling, something new and essential is revealed both to the raconteur and the audience.

b: Brigitte Uttar Kornetzky is a German filmmaker based in Switzerland. Amongst her studies are juridical sciences, philosophy, art history and fine arts and classical singing. Her documentary films on human rights issues…
f: Brigitte Uttar Kornetzky is a German filmmaker based in Switzerland. Amongst her studies are juridical sciences, philosophy, art history and fine arts and classical singing. Her documentary films on human rights issues in Africa and conflict between humans and elephants in India have received numerous nominations and awards internationally. She is the Founder and President of Elefanten in Not, a charity in Switzerland, and Swiss Ambassador for Captive Elephants at the Federation of Indian Animal Protection Organisation in India.

b: Brook Eddy is the founder and CEO of Bhakti, Inc., best known for its award-winning chai, innovative iced tea beverages that won first place in the North American Tea Championship, and being one of the first Certified B…
f: Brook Eddy is the founder and CEO of Bhakti, Inc., best known for its award-winning chai, innovative iced tea beverages that won first place in the North American Tea Championship, and being one of the first Certified B Corporations in America. Brook’s first book, STEEPED: Adventures of A Tea Entrepreneur , which is part business memoir and part India travelogue, was a #1 New Release on Amazon and chosen by Colorado Public Radio as one of their ‘Favorite Books in 2023’. She is also a copywriter and has written for Yoga Journal and Mantra Magazine.

b: Bruno Maçães is a senior fellow at the Hudson Institute and the Wilfried Martens Centre for European Studies and a former politician in Portugal. He is the author of several books on international affairs, including…
f: Bruno Maçães is a senior fellow at the Hudson Institute and the Wilfried Martens Centre for European Studies and a former politician in Portugal. He is the author of several books on international affairs, including The Dawn of Eurasia: On the Trail of the New World Order, Belt and Road: The Sinews of Chinese Power and History Has Begun . Bruno is a regular commentator on the international media and has written for the Financial Times, Politico, The Guardian and Foreign Affairs.

b: BS Ajaikumar is a doctorpreneur and the Chairman and CEO of HealthCare Global Enterprises Ltd. Dr. Ajaikumar is a radiation and medical oncologist with over 40 years of experience. A true visionary, he has been actively…
f: BS Ajaikumar is a doctorpreneur and the Chairman and CEO of HealthCare Global Enterprises Ltd. Dr. Ajaikumar is a radiation and medical oncologist with over 40 years of experience. A true visionary, he has been actively involved in various initiatives to help patients win over cancer. He established a cancer center west of Chicago in 1979. A decade later, he founded a not-for- profit hospital in Mysore. Among his other achievements, he has been awarded the prestigious E&Y Start-Up Entrepreneur of the Year Award and the Asian Healthcare Leadership Awards. He has set up a think tank where the primary focus is on issues related to health, education, livelihood, and governance in India.

b: Buddhi Sagar is a Nepali author who has worked as a feature writer and literary editor for two of Nepal’s leading newspapers and as a scriptwriter for radio and television series on children’s issues and lifeline…
f: Buddhi Sagar is a Nepali author who has worked as a feature writer and literary editor for two of Nepal’s leading newspapers and as a scriptwriter for radio and television series on children’s issues and lifeline issues for earthquake survivors. His earliest writings include newspaper articles and poems, for which he has received several awards. In addition to his bestselling novel Karnali Blues, he has authored another novel, Phirphire and a collection of poems called Buddhisagar ka Kabita .

b: Bulaki Sharma is a prominent writer of satires, stories, fictions, biographies, one-act plays and children’s literature. He is known for his lucidity of style, clarity of vision and subtle observation both in…
f: Bulaki Sharma is a prominent writer of satires, stories, fictions, biographies, one-act plays and children’s literature. He is known for his lucidity of style, clarity of vision and subtle observation both in Rajasthani and Hindi writings. The author of more than 25 books, he is also a distinguished translator, editor and column writer. Sharma has received many prizes including much-coveted Sahitya Akademi award for his book Maradjaat Ar Dooji Kahaniyan in 2016.

b: C.K. Meena is a Bengaluru-based journalist who was on the staff of Deccan Herald, a columnist for The Hindu, and a founding member of the Asian College of Journalism in Bengaluru. In her 40-year writing career, she has…
f: C.K. Meena is a Bengaluru-based journalist who was on the staff of Deccan Herald, a columnist for The Hindu, and a founding member of the Asian College of Journalism in Bengaluru. In her 40-year writing career, she has written three novels and innumerable pieces for various publications. Her latest book, The Invisible Majority , co-authored with V.R. Ferose, is a comprehensive overview of disability in India.

b: Camilla Townsend is Distinguished Professor of History at Rutgers, the State University of New Jersey in the United States. A specialist in the Nahuatl (or Aztec) language, she is the author of numerous books, the most…
f: Camilla Townsend is Distinguished Professor of History at Rutgers, the State University of New Jersey in the United States. A specialist in the Nahuatl (or Aztec) language, she is the author of numerous books, the most recent being Fifth Sun: A New History of the Aztecs, which won the 2020 Cundill Prize.

b: Carin Gerhardsen made her literary debut in 1992 with the philosophical novel Escape of Time . She is the author of a bestselling series of crime novels about chief inspector Conny Sjöberg. These include The…
f: Carin Gerhardsen made her literary debut in 1992 with the philosophical novel Escape of Time . She is the author of a bestselling series of crime novels about chief inspector Conny Sjöberg. These include The Gingerbread House, Cinderella Girl, The Last Lullaby, The Saint, Gideon’s Ring, Her Ice Cold Eyes, Thicker than Water, considered by Apple/iTunes as the best Swedish novel of 2014 and winner of the 2014 Stora Ljudbokspriset as the best crime novel, and The Domino Effect . Her books have been translated into more than 20 languages.

b: Carl W. Ernst is a specialist in Islamic studies with a focus on West and South Asia. His publications are mainly devoted to general and critical issues of Islamic studies, pre-modern and contemporary Sufism and…
f: Carl W. Ernst is a specialist in Islamic studies with a focus on West and South Asia. His publications are mainly devoted to general and critical issues of Islamic studies, pre-modern and contemporary Sufism and Indo-Muslim culture. He is the Kenan Distinguished Professor of Religious Studies at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill.

b: Carlo Rovelli is a renowned theoretical physicist who has worked on the foundations of Loop Quantum Gravity. He is known for his worldwide bestsellers Seven Brief Lessons on Physics and The Order of Time , which have…
f: Carlo Rovelli is a renowned theoretical physicist who has worked on the foundations of Loop Quantum Gravity. He is known for his worldwide bestsellers Seven Brief Lessons on Physics and The Order of Time , which have been translated in more than 40 languages. He has been recently listed by Foreign Policy magazine as among the 100 most influential global thinkers.

b: Carol Black is currently Chair of the British Library, the Centre for Ageing Better, and ‘Think Ahead', the Government’s fast-stream training programme for Mental Health Social Workers. She is a member of RAND…
f: Carol Black is currently Chair of the British Library, the Centre for Ageing Better, and ‘Think Ahead', the Government’s fast-stream training programme for Mental Health Social Workers. She is a member of RAND Europe’s Council of Advisers and a Board member of the Institute for Employment Studies and UKActive. She has completed four independent reviews for the UK Government- of the health of the working-age population in 2008 as National Director for Health and Work; of sickness absence in Britain in 2011 as Co-Chair; of employment outcomes of addiction to drugs or alcohol, or obesity, in 2016; and on illicit drugs, demand, supply and treatment. Black is a past-President of the Royal College of Physicians, the Academy of Medical Royal Colleges, and the British Lung Foundation, and past-Chair of the Nuffield Trust for health policy. The Centre she established at the Royal Free Hospital in London is internationally renowned for research and treatment of connective tissue diseases such as scleroderma. She has also been a Trustee of the National Portrait Gallery.

b: Caroline Eden is the author of several award-winning travelogues with recipes including Samarkand , Black Sea and Red Sands and a memoir, Cold Kitchen . She has also written forewords to several books, including They…
f: Caroline Eden is the author of several award-winning travelogues with recipes including Samarkand , Black Sea and Red Sands and a memoir, Cold Kitchen . She has also written forewords to several books, including They Went To Portugal by Rose Macaulay and Through Khiva to Golden Samarkand by Ella Christie.

b: Cass R. Sunstein is the Robert Walmsley University Professor at Harvard, where he is the founder and director of the Program on Behavioral Economics and Public Policy. From 2013 to 2014, he served on President Obama’s…
