f: Cass R. Sunstein is the Robert Walmsley University Professor at Harvard, where he is the founder and director of the Program on Behavioral Economics and Public Policy. From 2013 to 2014, he served on President Obama’s Review Group on Intelligence and Communications Technologies. Winner of the 2018 Holberg Prize from the government of Norway, Sunstein is the author of many articles and books, including two New York Times bestsellers, The World According to Star Wars and Nudge. His other books include How Change Happens and Too Much Information.

b: Dr Cat Jarman is an archaeologist specialising in Viking Age Europe and bioarchaeology. She directs excavations at numerous sites in England and Ukraine. Dr Jarman also works as a historical consultant and presenter for…
f: Dr Cat Jarman is an archaeologist specialising in Viking Age Europe and bioarchaeology. She directs excavations at numerous sites in England and Ukraine. Dr Jarman also works as a historical consultant and presenter for TV and media and hosts the weekly podcast, Gone Medieval by History Hit .

b: Catherine Chidgey is “one of New Zealand’s greatest living writers” ( Radio NZ ). She is the only person to have won the Acorn Prize for Fiction twice – her country’s most prestigious literary award. She has been…
f: Catherine Chidgey is “one of New Zealand’s greatest living writers” ( Radio NZ ). She is the only person to have won the Acorn Prize for Fiction twice – her country’s most prestigious literary award. She has been longlisted for the Women’s Prize in the UK and shortlisted for the Dublin Literary Award.

b: Catherine McClelland is a Director of the Board of the Hong Kong International Literary Festival, and President and Managing Director at Sutton Communications. She is a cultural communications professional with more…
f: Catherine McClelland is a Director of the Board of the Hong Kong International Literary Festival, and President and Managing Director at Sutton Communications. She is a cultural communications professional with more than a decade’s experience directing strategic campaigns for the world’s leading arts organisations.

b: Cathy Brown has been the Arts Programmer at Seamus Heaney HomePlace since it opened in September 2016. An experienced arts programmer, Brown has worked in Clotworthy House and The Old Courthouse in Antrim, Belfast…
f: Cathy Brown has been the Arts Programmer at Seamus Heaney HomePlace since it opened in September 2016. An experienced arts programmer, Brown has worked in Clotworthy House and The Old Courthouse in Antrim, Belfast Waterfront Hall, Belfast Festival at Queens and the Belfast Book Festival. She plans the events at HomePlace, encompassing music, song, poetry, talks and drama, with appeal to all ages and cultural tastes.

b: Cathy Scott-Clark is a former staff writer and foreign correspondent for The Sunday Times and the Guardian . Along with Adrian Levy, she won the One World award for foreign reporting and was a Press Journalist of the…
f: Cathy Scott-Clark is a former staff writer and foreign correspondent for The Sunday Times and the Guardian . Along with Adrian Levy, she won the One World award for foreign reporting and was a Press Journalist of the Year. Her third book, Deception , co-authored with Levy, was a finalist in the Royal United Services Institute, Duke of Westminster’s medal for Military History. The Meadow won the Ramnath Goenka Award. The Siege won the CWA Gold Dagger for Non-Fiction. The Exile: Al Qaeda in Flight was published in May. Together, Scott-Clark and Levy, have produced documentaries for HBO, PBS, BBC 1, BBC 2 and C4 and are now working on a documentary feature on interrogation.

b: Cauvery Madhavan was born in India and moved to Ireland 33 years ago. She is the author of three books of fiction titled Paddy Indian , The Uncoupling and her latest book The Tainted, which has received much critical…
f: Cauvery Madhavan was born in India and moved to Ireland 33 years ago. She is the author of three books of fiction titled Paddy Indian , The Uncoupling and her latest book The Tainted, which has received much critical acclaim. It was picked as one of Ireland's prestigious An Post’s Top Summer Reads 2020. It was the runner-up in the SAHR Prize for Military Fiction and listed by The Times, UK, in their list of top 40 Historical Fiction novels. Cauvery is also a free range farmer, an enthusiastic gardener and a golfer with poorly realised ambitions. She is currently working on her fourth novel.

b: Chand Sur was born in 1925 in Bahawalpur, Undivided India and brought up in Quetta. Her married home was in Lahore. After Partition, she and her husband moved to Lucknow. An inventive cook, her latest book is The…
f: Chand Sur was born in 1925 in Bahawalpur, Undivided India and brought up in Quetta. Her married home was in Lahore. After Partition, she and her husband moved to Lucknow. An inventive cook, her latest book is The Lucknow Cookbook , co-authored with her daughter Sunita Kohli.

b: Chandan Gowda has edited The Way I See It: A Gauri Lankesh Reader and Theatres of Democracy: Selected Essays of Shiv Visvanathan . He has also translated U.R. Ananthamurthy’s story Bara and edited The Post Office of…
f: Chandan Gowda has edited The Way I See It: A Gauri Lankesh Reader and Theatres of Democracy: Selected Essays of Shiv Visvanathan . He has also translated U.R. Ananthamurthy’s story Bara and edited The Post Office of Abachooru , a book of short stories by Purnachandra Tejasvi. A Life in the World , a book of autobiographical interviews he did with U.R. Ananthamurthy is forthcoming. He is currently writing a book on the cultural politics of development in the former princely state of Mysore. He writes regularly for newspapers, including a weekly column on culture and politics in the Bangalore Mirror .

b: Chandan Pandey has one fantastic life partner, two sons, three novels, four story collections, and five awards.
f: Chandan Pandey has one fantastic life partner, two sons, three novels, four story collections, and five awards.

b: Chandra Prakash Deval is an eminent Rajasthani writer. He has written a number of poetry collections and short stories and translated world classics like Dostoyevsky’s Crime and Punishment and Samuel Beckett’s…
f: Chandra Prakash Deval is an eminent Rajasthani writer. He has written a number of poetry collections and short stories and translated world classics like Dostoyevsky’s Crime and Punishment and Samuel Beckett’s Waiting for Godot . For his noted contribution in Rajasthani and Hindi, he has been honoured with the Sahitya Akademi Award for his Rajasthani poetry collection PAGI and the Padma Shri in 2011.

b: Chandrahas Choudhury is the author of the novels Clouds and Arzee the Dwarf . His forthcoming work of fiction, set in a Chinese restaurant in Mumbai, is called Tales of My China Dragon . He is also the editor of a short…
f: Chandrahas Choudhury is the author of the novels Clouds and Arzee the Dwarf . His forthcoming work of fiction, set in a Chinese restaurant in Mumbai, is called Tales of My China Dragon . He is also the editor of a short introduction to Indian literature for the literature-loving traveller titled India: A Traveller’s Literary Companion . Choudhury also writes about literature, travel and politics for a number of periodicals, including the Wall Street Journal , Mint , Washington Post , Conde Nast Traveller , Foreign Policy, EnRoute and The National . He was a visiting fellow at the International Writing Programme at the University of Iowa in 2010 and at Akademie Solitude in Stuttgart, Germany in 2016.

b: Chandrakant Lahariya is a medical doctor, columnist and author who has been at the forefront of the COVID-19 pandemic response of India. Dr Lahariya, a leading medical-epidemiologist, is amongst India’s widely…
f: Chandrakant Lahariya is a medical doctor, columnist and author who has been at the forefront of the COVID-19 pandemic response of India. Dr Lahariya, a leading medical-epidemiologist, is amongst India’s widely acknowledged public policy, vaccines and health systems experts. His opinion pieces appear regularly in The Hindu, The Indian Express and Dainik Bhaskar, and he has co-authored the book titled Till We Win: India’s Fight Against the COVID-19 Pandemic.

b: Chandrakant Singh is a veteran of the Bangladesh Liberation War in which he was wounded and received the Vir Chakra for gallantry. He is now an acknowledged writer and speaker on military history and travel-related…
f: Chandrakant Singh is a veteran of the Bangladesh Liberation War in which he was wounded and received the Vir Chakra for gallantry. He is now an acknowledged writer and speaker on military history and travel-related subjects. In the past year, he has published two books- Cavalier in the Sky , the biography of Air Marshal Chandan Singh and Meghna River of Victory , a definitive account of the defining battle of the Liberation War.

b: Chandramani Singh started her career at the Bharat Kala Bhavan at Banaras Hindu University Museum. Dr. Singh is currently the Tagore National Scholar. She is the author of Protected Monuments of Rajasthan , two volumes…
f: Chandramani Singh started her career at the Bharat Kala Bhavan at Banaras Hindu University Museum. Dr. Singh is currently the Tagore National Scholar. She is the author of Protected Monuments of Rajasthan , two volumes of Rajasthan Re-discovered and Women of Rajasthan .

b: Chandrika Parmar is a faculty member at S. P. Jain Institute of Management and Research (SPJIMR), Mumbai, where she serves as Director of the Department of Corporate Citizenship (DoCC). She leads experiential learning…
f: Chandrika Parmar is a faculty member at S. P. Jain Institute of Management and Research (SPJIMR), Mumbai, where she serves as Director of the Department of Corporate Citizenship (DoCC). She leads experiential learning programs connecting MBA and executive MBA participants with civil society organizations across India. Holding a DPhil in Management Research from Saïd Business School, University of Oxford, her interdisciplinary research integrates management, disaster studies, sociology, environmental values, science and technology studies, pedagogy, and futures thinking. Dr. Parmar examines how institutions, education, and everyday practices shape ethical action, responsibility, and citizenship, and has published widely on COVID-19, ecological responsibility, and active citizenship.

b: Charan Singh Pathik is a prolific and acclaimed story writer from Rajasthan with a very deep understanding of grassroot politics and socio-economic structure of rural life. He works as a teacher in a government school…
f: Charan Singh Pathik is a prolific and acclaimed story writer from Rajasthan with a very deep understanding of grassroot politics and socio-economic structure of rural life. He works as a teacher in a government school and is closely associated with the gram panchayat activities. With more than four collections of short stories to his name, he is known for his bold authentic writings that root for the cause of the oppressed and the poor. Hindi feature films have been made on two of his stories, Pataakha by Vishal Bhardwaj based on ‘Do Bahnein’ and Kasaai by Gajendra S. Shrotriya.

b: Charles Collier is a film, television and literary agent, talent manager, producer and lawyer. His producer credits include five seasons of the award-winning dramas Top Boy (Channel4/Netflix) and The Pursuit of Love…
f: Charles Collier is a film, television and literary agent, talent manager, producer and lawyer. His producer credits include five seasons of the award-winning dramas Top Boy (Channel4/Netflix) and The Pursuit of Love (BBC/Amazon). As a manager and agent, his clients include Rebecca Ferguson, Alicia Vikander, Ronan Bennett, Sam Riley, Freddie Fox, Charles Dance, Rebel Wilson, Lily James and Eva Green. Charles trained as a corporate finance lawyer and went on to develop his own specialised legal practice in IP management, film and television production, and publishing. Charles was a founder partner of Tavistock Wood in 2005 which merged with Curtis Brown in 2018. He went on to establish his own label, Open Book Productions in 2018.

b: Charles Glass is the author of Soldiers Don't Go Mad: A Story of Brotherhood, Poetry and Mental Illness During the First World War; Deserters; Americans in Paris; Tribes with Flags; and The Northern Front: An Iraq War…
f: Charles Glass is the author of Soldiers Don't Go Mad: A Story of Brotherhood, Poetry and Mental Illness During the First World War; Deserters; Americans in Paris; Tribes with Flags; and The Northern Front: An Iraq War Diary; and Syria Burning ; among other books. He was ABC News Chief Middle East correspondent from 1983 to 1993.

b: Charles Spencer is the 9th Earl Spencer and owner of Althorp House, one of England’s premier historic homes and final resting place of his sister Diana, Princess of Wales. To Catch a King is his sixth non-fiction…
f: Charles Spencer is the 9th Earl Spencer and owner of Althorp House, one of England’s premier historic homes and final resting place of his sister Diana, Princess of Wales. To Catch a King is his sixth non-fiction book, following the Sunday Times bestsellers Blenheim and Killers of the King .

b: Charlie English is a British author and former Guardian journalist. He was head of international news at the Guardian from 2010 to 2013, a period that coincided with the Arab Spring, the Japanese tsunami, the deaths of…
f: Charlie English is a British author and former Guardian journalist. He was head of international news at the Guardian from 2010 to 2013, a period that coincided with the Arab Spring, the Japanese tsunami, the deaths of Osama Bin Laden and Nelson Mandela and the wars in Libya and Syria. He is the author of two books, a travelogue titled The Snow Tourist , and The Book Smugglers of Timbuktu , which tells the story of the rescue of the Malian city’s manuscripts in 2012/13.

b: Charlie Jeffery is Vice-Chancellor and President, University of York, and former Senior Vice-Principal at the University of Edinburgh. His academic background is in the study of politics. He is passionate about the role…
f: Charlie Jeffery is Vice-Chancellor and President, University of York, and former Senior Vice-Principal at the University of Edinburgh. His academic background is in the study of politics. He is passionate about the role universities can play in bringing benefit to the places in which they are located, and was a central figure in the negotiation of the £1.3B Edinburgh and South East Scotland City Region Deal. Jeffery is currently working with further and higher education institutions, private sector partners and local authorities in and around York in shaping economic development programmes in the field of biotechnology and around York Central, one of the UK’s biggest brownfield development sites.

b: Charlotte Higgins is chief culture writer of The Guardian, and author of the acclaimed Under Another Sky: Journeys in Roman Britain , which was shortlisted for multiple awards including the Samuel Johnson (now Baillie…
f: Charlotte Higgins is chief culture writer of The Guardian, and author of the acclaimed Under Another Sky: Journeys in Roman Britain , which was shortlisted for multiple awards including the Samuel Johnson (now Baillie Gifford) Prize for non-fiction, and Red Thread: On Mazes and Labyrinths , which was a Radio 4 Book of the Week, and won the Arnold Bennett Prize in 2019. Higgins is a past winner of the Classical Association prize, and a fellow of the Society of Antiquaries.

b: Charlotte Hobson is the author of Black Earth City: A Year in the Heart of Russia , which won the Somerset Maugham Award and was shortlisted for multiple prizes. Her historical novel, The Vanishing Futurist , was also…
f: Charlotte Hobson is the author of Black Earth City: A Year in the Heart of Russia , which won the Somerset Maugham Award and was shortlisted for multiple prizes. Her historical novel, The Vanishing Futurist , was also shortlisted for the Walter Scott Historical Novel Prize. Hobson has contributed short stories to various anthologies and BBC Radio 4, and she has volunteered with Ukrainian refugees since the invasion of Ukraine.

b: Charlotte Wood is the prizewinning author of seven novels and three non-fiction works. Her new book Stone Yard Devotional was shortlisted for the 2024 Booker Prize, and has been praised by authors Anne Enright, Tim…
f: Charlotte Wood is the prizewinning author of seven novels and three non-fiction works. Her new book Stone Yard Devotional was shortlisted for the 2024 Booker Prize, and has been praised by authors Anne Enright, Tim Winton, Karen Joy Fowler, Hannah Kent, and Paula Hawkins, among others.

b: Charmaine Craig is the author of the novels Miss Burma , longlisted for the National Book Award 2017, and The Good Men . She is a faculty member in fiction at the University of California at Riverside, a graduate of…
f: Charmaine Craig is the author of the novels Miss Burma , longlisted for the National Book Award 2017, and The Good Men . She is a faculty member in fiction at the University of California at Riverside, a graduate of Harvard University and the descendant of significant figures in Burma’s modern history.

b: Charty Dugdale is the founder of Artreach India, working with artists to transform the lives of children and women from marginalised communities. She has written on travel and social issues as well as art, and is…
f: Charty Dugdale is the founder of Artreach India, working with artists to transform the lives of children and women from marginalised communities. She has written on travel and social issues as well as art, and is working on a novel.

b: Charu Nivedita is the author of nearly hundred works in Tamil, ranging from collections of essays to novels, anthologies of poetry to short stories. Known as a postmodern, transgressive writer, he is most interested in…
f: Charu Nivedita is the author of nearly hundred works in Tamil, ranging from collections of essays to novels, anthologies of poetry to short stories. Known as a postmodern, transgressive writer, he is most interested in autofiction and metafiction. He is best known for the novel Zero Degree , which was longlisted for the 2013 edition of the Jan Michalski Prize for Literature and has found a place in several academic syllabi in India and overseas. His books Marginal Man , To Byzantium: A Turkey Travelogue , Unfaithfully Yours , Morgue Keeper , Antonin Artaud: The Body of a Rebel and Towards a Third Cinema have been translated into English and published by independent presses.

b: Charu Singh grew up in Chandigarh and moved to Assam with her husband, where she worked as a freelance researcher for UNICEF. She has since worked with Asian Age , Frontline and Tribune . In addition to writing, she is…
f: Charu Singh grew up in Chandigarh and moved to Assam with her husband, where she worked as a freelance researcher for UNICEF. She has since worked with Asian Age , Frontline and Tribune . In addition to writing, she is also a trained classical dancer and is deeply interested in the spiritual.

b: Chetan Bhagat is the author of nine blockbuster books. These include seven novels, Five Point Someone, One Night @ The Call Centre, The 3 Mistakes of My Life , 2 States, Revolution 2020, Half Girlfriend and One Indian…
f: Chetan Bhagat is the author of nine blockbuster books. These include seven novels, Five Point Someone, One Night @ The Call Centre, The 3 Mistakes of My Life , 2 States, Revolution 2020, Half Girlfriend and One Indian Girl , and two non-fiction titles, What Young India Wants and Making India Awesome . His books have remained bestsellers since their release. Four out his five novels have been already adapted into successful Bollywood films and the others are in process of being adapted as well. The New York Times called him the ‘the biggest selling English language novelist in India’s history’. TIME magazine named him amongst the ‘100 most influential people in the world’ and Fast Company listed him as one of the world’s ‘100 most creative people in business’. Bhagat also writes columns for leading English and Hindi newspapers, focusing on youth and national development issues. He is also a motivational speaker and screenplay writer.

b: Chetna Sinha is the Founder and Chairperson of Mann Deshi Bank and Mann Deshi Foundation. She passionately believes that empowering rural women can transform and drive economic growth. In 1997, she established the Mann…
f: Chetna Sinha is the Founder and Chairperson of Mann Deshi Bank and Mann Deshi Foundation. She passionately believes that empowering rural women can transform and drive economic growth. In 1997, she established the Mann Deshi Mahila Sahakari Bank, India's first bank for and by rural women. Operating in Maharashtra, Karnataka, and Silvassa, Man Deshi has supported over 950,000 women and aims to reach one million women by 2024; it continuously develops new financial products to support female micro-entrepreneurs. Chetna is a Yale, Ashoka, and Schwab Fellow. In 2018, she received the Nari Shakti Puraskar, the highest civilian award for women in India, from the President of India.

b: Cheyenne Olivier is a French illustrator. Her images, playfully geometric, address social and environmental issues. She has illustrated picture books on poverty, alongside economist Esther Duflo, and she currently…
f: Cheyenne Olivier is a French illustrator. Her images, playfully geometric, address social and environmental issues. She has illustrated picture books on poverty, alongside economist Esther Duflo, and she currently illustrates a monthly column on food and economics, with Abhijit Banerjee, in the Times Of India newspaper.

b: Chhavi Rajawat has been a two-time Sarpanch/elected head of the Village Council of Soda located in the District of Tonk, Rajasthan, India. Chhavi is recognized as the first MBA Sarpanch of India. She has received…
f: Chhavi Rajawat has been a two-time Sarpanch/elected head of the Village Council of Soda located in the District of Tonk, Rajasthan, India. Chhavi is recognized as the first MBA Sarpanch of India. She has received multiple awards for her service that include First Ladies National award from former Hon’ble President Shri Ram Nath Kovind; Reebok’s Fit To Fight award; Young Indian Leader award by CNN/IBN; Grassroots Women of the Decade Achievers award; Bharat Ratna Rajiv Gandhi Yuva Shakti National award; All India Woman Achiever’s award; Yuva award; Changing Face of Indian Politics award and; has also been felicitated by Former President Late Shri Dr.A.P.J.Abdul Kalam.

b: Chidanand Rajghatta is a Washington DC-based journalist and writer and a long-time foreign correspondent for The Times of India group. He has recently authored Kamala Harris: Phenomenal Woman . His previous books…
f: Chidanand Rajghatta is a Washington DC-based journalist and writer and a long-time foreign correspondent for The Times of India group. He has recently authored Kamala Harris: Phenomenal Woman . His previous books include Illiberal India, Gauri Lankesh and the Age of Unreason, and The Horse That Flew: How India’s Silicon Gurus Spread Their Wings.

b: Chigozie Obioma is an associate professor of Creative Writing at the University of Nebraska,Lincoln. His two novels, The Fishermen and An Orchestra of Minorities were shortlisted for The Booker Prize and have been…

b: CK Mishra joined the Indian Administrative Service (IAS) in 1983 and currently heading the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change. Government of India. He led the Indian negotiations at important Forums such…
f: CK Mishra joined the Indian Administrative Service (IAS) in 1983 and currently heading the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change. Government of India. He led the Indian negotiations at important Forums such as United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (Conference of the Parties (COP)) to assess progress in dealing with climate change; Montreal Protocol on Substances that Deplete the Ozone Layer and various other multilateral events. He leads the government initiative for air pollution mitigation in Delhi and indeed all pollution control strategies for the country. He is also the administrative head of Forest and Wildlife conservation efforts in India. Prior to this, he was Secretary in-charge of Ministry of Health & Family Welfare and also held the additional charge of Ministry of AYUSH for some time. Before his elevation as Secretary, Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, he was Additional Secretary & Mission Director, National Health Mission, who led one of the largest public health programme globally. In more than 30 years of public service, Mishra has served as an administrator, policy-maker and public health strategist holding a wide range of assignments in the fields of Health, Education, Industry and Power. Mishra is recognised for his significant contributions to improving the Indian Public Health landscape. He was earlier also associated with delivering health care at the provincial level and played a key role in eradicating polio in the toughest region of Bihar. He has been the force behind `Mission Indradhanush' — the largest ever focussed campaign to immunise children. His views on Maternal child heath are well accepted globally as he brings a practical implementation perspective to his views.

In national politics, he held important Cabinet portfolios—Rural Development and Panchayati Raj, Road Transport and Highways, and briefly Railways—under Prime Minister Manmohan Singh. He also served as Speaker of the Rajasthan Legislative Assembly from 2019 until 2023. A former professor of psychology and lecturer at Mohanlal Sukhadia University in Udaipur, Joshi entered politics via student leadership in the early 1970s and was first elected as MLA from Nathdwara. Known for his scholarly approach, Joshi holds master’s degrees in physics and psychology, an LLB, and a PhD in psychology. He strengthened the Congress organisation as state party president and has played key roles in legislative and party positions over the decades.

She then wrote a bitter-sweet musical Somewhere Over the Rainbow and dedicated it to her (late) mother who wanted to be a singer. Her next novel Visa to Paradise , about a young rebel being trapped in a psycho-spiritual centre is scheduled for 2018. Rischmann won the nationwide romance writing with her short love story ‘Jilted’, which was published in an anthology, An Atlas of Love , by Rupa Publications.

At Cape, he published Ben Okri, the first African to win the Booker prize. At DGA, he has handled a wide range of writers, including the Poet Laureate Simon Armitage. He has a special interest in Indian writers. His first Indian book was Arundhati Roy’s God of Small Things, which won the Booker prize in 1997. Since then, he has agented Kiran Desai and Aravind Adiga. He now represents William Dalrymple, Jeet Thayil, Manu S. Pillai, Nilanjana S. Roy, David Davidar, Meena Kandasamy, Yashaswini Chandra, Aanchal Malhotra, Shashi Tharoor, Kanishk Tharoor, Arundhati Katju, Menaka Guruswamy, Ruchir Joshi, Raj Kamal Jha, Shehan Karunatilaka, Amitava Kumar, Vikram Seth, Preti Taneja, Salil Tripathi, Monisha Rajesh and Christina Lamb amongst others.

b: David Hare is acclaimed as “the finest living British dramatist” by The Guardian . He has authored nearly forty plays, including Plenty , Skylight , and Stuff Happens , and has also worked as a screenwriter and film…
f: David Hare is acclaimed as “the finest living British dramatist” by The Guardian . He has authored nearly forty plays, including Plenty , Skylight , and Stuff Happens , and has also worked as a screenwriter and film director. In a millennial poll, five of his plays ranked among the top 100 of the 20th century.

b: David Hernández de la Fuente , a Spanish writer and professor of Classics at Complutense University of Madrid, specialises in classical mythology, literature, and philosophy. His acclaimed nonfiction works explore these…
f: David Hernández de la Fuente , a Spanish writer and professor of Classics at Complutense University of Madrid, specialises in classical mythology, literature, and philosophy. His acclaimed nonfiction works explore these fields in depth, while his novels and essays creatively bridge ancient themes with modern ideas, offering new literary perspectives.

b: David McWilliams is an economist, author, journalist and broadcaster. He is adjunct Professor of Global Economics at Trinity College Dublin and is ranked the tenth most influential and third most followed economist on…
f: David McWilliams is an economist, author, journalist and broadcaster. He is adjunct Professor of Global Economics at Trinity College Dublin and is ranked the tenth most influential and third most followed economist on Twitter in the world. The author of five bestsellers, his latest is Renaissance Nation . He founded the Kilkenomics Festival , described by the FT as “simply, the best economics conference in the world”. He also co-founded the Dalkey Book Festival.

b: David Mitchell is a British-Irish novelist, television writer and screenwriter. He has been nominated for the Booker Prize five times, and his work has appeared in over 30 languages. His latest novel, Utopia Avenue ,…
f: David Mitchell is a British-Irish novelist, television writer and screenwriter. He has been nominated for the Booker Prize five times, and his work has appeared in over 30 languages. His latest novel, Utopia Avenue , was published by Sceptre in 2020 and his screenwriting credits include the Matrix: Resurrections .

b: David Nicholls is the author of six novels, including You Are Here , Starter for Ten , One Day , and Us , the latter of which was longlisted for the Booker Prize. David has written adaptations of Far from the Madding…
f: David Nicholls is the author of six novels, including You Are Here , Starter for Ten , One Day , and Us , the latter of which was longlisted for the Booker Prize. David has written adaptations of Far from the Madding Crowd and Great Expectations . His work on Patrick Melrose won him a BAFTA for best writer.

b: David Olusoga is a British-Nigerian historian, producer and presenter. He is the author of Civilizations: Encounters and the Cult of Progress, The World’s War , which won First World War Book of the Year, Black &…
f: David Olusoga is a British-Nigerian historian, producer and presenter. He is the author of Civilizations: Encounters and the Cult of Progress, The World’s War , which won First World War Book of the Year, Black & British: A Forgotten History , which was awarded the Longman-History Today Trustees Award and the PEN Hessell-Tiltman Prize, and The Kaiser’s Holocaust: Germany’s Forgotten Genocide and the Colonial Roots of Nazism . He writes for the Observer , Guardian , New Statesman and BBC History Magazine . His work as a presenter includes Civilizations , Black and British: A Forgotten History , The World’s War , A House Through Tim e and the BAFTA-winning Britain’s Forgotten Slave Owners . He has also worked as an Executive Producer on Generation Windrush , The Unremembered and Britain’s Bloody Heroes .

b: David Reich is a Harvard professor and was named one of ten people who matter in all of science by Nature magazine in 2015. In 2017, he received the Dan David Prize. His 2018 book is Who We Are and How We Got Here:…
f: David Reich is a Harvard professor and was named one of ten people who matter in all of science by Nature magazine in 2015. In 2017, he received the Dan David Prize. His 2018 book is Who We Are and How We Got Here: Ancient DNA and the New Science of the Human Past .

b: David Roche has been Chairman of the Music Department at Cornish College of the Arts, Seattle, Director of Arts Education for Chicago Public Schools and Executive Director at Old Town School of Folk Music, Chicago, Blue…
f: David Roche has been Chairman of the Music Department at Cornish College of the Arts, Seattle, Director of Arts Education for Chicago Public Schools and Executive Director at Old Town School of Folk Music, Chicago, Blue Bear School of Music, San Francisco and the Western Folklife Center, Elko, Nevada. He currently consults on nonprofit arts and culture projects and policies.

b: David Sandalow is the Inaugural Fellow at the Center on Global Energy Policy and Director of the Energy and Environment Concentration at the School of International and Public Affairs at Columbia University. He founded…
f: David Sandalow is the Inaugural Fellow at the Center on Global Energy Policy and Director of the Energy and Environment Concentration at the School of International and Public Affairs at Columbia University. He founded and directs the Center’s US-China Program and is author of the Guide to Chinese Climate Policy. He is a Distinguished Visiting Professor in the Schwarzman Scholars Program at Tsinghua University and a Distinguished Research Fellow at the Oxford Institute for Energy Studies. He has led development of roadmaps on low-carbon ammonia, biomass carbon removal, among other topics. He is also a director of Enagás, SA and Fermata Energy and senior advisor to BCG.

b: David Veevers is Lecturer in Early Modern History at Bangor University, where he teaches and writes on Colonial and Global History. He has authored The Origins of the British Empire in Asia, 1600 – 1750 and The Great…
f: David Veevers is Lecturer in Early Modern History at Bangor University, where he teaches and writes on Colonial and Global History. He has authored The Origins of the British Empire in Asia, 1600 – 1750 and The Great Defiance: How the World Took on the British Empire.

b: David Wallace-Wells is deputy editor at New York magazine and the author of the international bestseller The Uninhabitable Earth: Life After Warming . Wallace-Wells joined New York magazine as literary editor in 2011,…
f: David Wallace-Wells is deputy editor at New York magazine and the author of the international bestseller The Uninhabitable Earth: Life After Warming . Wallace-Wells joined New York magazine as literary editor in 2011, became features director in 2016 and deputy editor in 2017. He writes regularly for the magazine about science and the near future, including his 2017 cover story on worst-case scenarios for climate change, and his regular column on global warming and its humanitarian impacts. He is a national fellow of the New America Foundation.

b: David Walliams is a literary phenomenon whose books have sold more than fifty-nine million copies worldwide and have been translated into fifty-five languages.
f: David Walliams is a literary phenomenon whose books have sold more than fifty-nine million copies worldwide and have been translated into fifty-five languages.

b: David Wengrow is Professor of Comparative Archaeology at the Institute of Archaeology at University College London and has been visiting professor at NYU. He conducted archaeological fieldwork in Africa and the Middle…
f: David Wengrow is Professor of Comparative Archaeology at the Institute of Archaeology at University College London and has been visiting professor at NYU. He conducted archaeological fieldwork in Africa and the Middle East, and is co-author of the international bestseller The Dawn of Everything: A New History of Humanity

b: Dayanand Bhargawa is a Sanskrit scholar, thinker, writer and teacher. He has written and edited a dozen books related to Ved Vigyan and Sanskrit literature, and was conferred with the President’s Award for his…
f: Dayanand Bhargawa is a Sanskrit scholar, thinker, writer and teacher. He has written and edited a dozen books related to Ved Vigyan and Sanskrit literature, and was conferred with the President’s Award for his contributions to the Sanskrit language, among other honours. Bhargawa has served various roles for colleges and universities like Ramjas College, University of Delhi, Central Sanskrit University, Jammu and Allahabad, and Jai Narain Vyas University, Jodhpur. His key works are Vicharhasya, Vedvigyan Vakyamala and Vedvigyan Vimarsh . He has been a member of Rajasthan Sanskrit Academy, Kendriya Sanskrit Samiti and is a syndicate member of Jayanarayan Vyas Vishvidhyalaya, Jodhpur.

b: DBC Pierre is an Australian author who is well known for his black comedies about modern problems. His debut novel Vernon God Little became the first book to win both a Booker and a Whitbread prize and was published in…
f: DBC Pierre is an Australian author who is well known for his black comedies about modern problems. His debut novel Vernon God Little became the first book to win both a Booker and a Whitbread prize and was published in 43 territories. A lover of fanciful humanity, Pierre is also a regular contributor to New Philosopher.

b: Dean Nelson is an award-winning investigative journalist and business intelligence consultant. He spent ten years in Delhi covering India and the South Asia region from Afghanistan to Burma and beyond, first for the…
f: Dean Nelson is an award-winning investigative journalist and business intelligence consultant. He spent ten years in Delhi covering India and the South Asia region from Afghanistan to Burma and beyond, first for the Sunday Times and later for the Daily Telegraph .

b: Debashis Paul is an 'autism dad' and a management and marketing strategy consultant with clients from across the globe. He has worked in the advertising field with top-notch agencies, including McCann, Saatchi &…
f: Debashis Paul is an 'autism dad' and a management and marketing strategy consultant with clients from across the globe. He has worked in the advertising field with top-notch agencies, including McCann, Saatchi & Saatchi, and Lintas, managing campaigns for renowned brands like Coca-Cola, Microsoft, and more. Shifting to consulting, he worked with clients such as Pepsico and Union Bank of India while leading high-profile nationwide public service campaigns for the Indian government on issues like malnutrition and women’s health, winning numerous awards. Beyond his career, he's deeply interested in child development psychology and parenting, providing guidance for projects like the Avaz assistive communication app. He also volunteers to counsel parents of children with learning and communication difficulties. His debut non-fiction book is I Have Autism And I Like to Play Good Bad Tennis.

b: Debasish Chakrabarty is the Founder-Principal of The Kulish School and a Director of Education at the Rajasthan Patrika Group, leading future-ready, inquiry-driven education. An alumnus of JNU, UCL-IOE, Harvard GSE, and…
f: Debasish Chakrabarty is the Founder-Principal of The Kulish School and a Director of Education at the Rajasthan Patrika Group, leading future-ready, inquiry-driven education. An alumnus of JNU, UCL-IOE, Harvard GSE, and IIM Calcutta, he brings 25+ years of teaching experience across NID, The Doon School and GEMS Education.

b: Art historian Debra Diamond’s publications include Garden and Cosmos (Jodhpur painting), Yoga: The Art of Transformation , and A Splendid Land (Udaipur painting). As the Elizabeth Moynihan Curator of South Asian and…
f: Art historian Debra Diamond’s publications include Garden and Cosmos (Jodhpur painting), Yoga: The Art of Transformation , and A Splendid Land (Udaipur painting). As the Elizabeth Moynihan Curator of South Asian and Southeast Asian Art at the National Museum of Asian Art, Smithsonian Institution, her forthcoming exhibition re-examines Pahari painting.

b: Deep Mukherjee is a senior journalist and Assistant Editor at The Wire .He has worked with The Indian Express , Hindustan Times , and DNA , covering politics, human rights, marginalized communities, policy, labour,…
f: Deep Mukherjee is a senior journalist and Assistant Editor at The Wire .He has worked with The Indian Express , Hindustan Times , and DNA , covering politics, human rights, marginalized communities, policy, labour, gender, and farmer suicides. A recipient of a UNICEF Development Journalism Fellowship, he has highlighted the plight of child labourers in Jaipur’s lac bangle industry and the stone quarries of Kota. His forthcoming book, co-authored with Tabeenah Anjum, From Dynasties to Democracy: Politics, Caste and Power Struggles in Rajasthan , offers a comprehensive account of the state’s contemporary politics, princely legacy, and socio-political evolution since 1947. The book will be published by Pan Macmillan in 2025.

b: Deepa Agarwal is a writer, poet and translator who writes for both children and adults and has over 50 books published. She has received the NCERT National Award for Children’s Literature and her historical fiction…
f: Deepa Agarwal is a writer, poet and translator who writes for both children and adults and has over 50 books published. She has received the NCERT National Award for Children’s Literature and her historical fiction Caravan to Tibet was on the IBBY Honour List 2008. Her work has been translated into several Indian and foreign languages.

b: Deepa Anappara ’s debut novel Djinn Patrol on the Purple Line was named as one of the best books of the year by The New York Times , The Washington Post , Time and NPR. It won the Edgar Award for Best Novel and the Tata…
f: Deepa Anappara ’s debut novel Djinn Patrol on the Purple Line was named as one of the best books of the year by The New York Times , The Washington Post , Time and NPR. It won the Edgar Award for Best Novel and the Tata Literature First Book Award for Fiction, and was longlisted for the Women’s Prize for Fiction 2020. Anappara is the co-editor of Letters to a Writer of Colour , a collection of personal essays on fiction, race, and culture, published in 2023. She teaches creative writing, and is a mentor on the South Asia Speaks mentorship programme for emerging writers in South Asia. The Last of Earth , set in mid-19th century Tibet, is her second novel. It’s out in January 2026 in India from Hamish Hamilton.

b: Deepa Bhasthi is a writer and translator working in Kannada and English. Her essays, columns and journalism on the politics of culture have been published widely in national and international publications. Her…
f: Deepa Bhasthi is a writer and translator working in Kannada and English. Her essays, columns and journalism on the politics of culture have been published widely in national and international publications. Her translation of Kota Shivarama Karanth's novel The Same Village, The Same Tree was published in 2022. Her translation of the short stories of Kodagina Gouramma, one of the earliest feminist writers in Kannada in the 20th century, is set to be published in January 2023 by Yoda Press. She is currently working on translating the works of Banu Mushtaq, for which she is the recipient of a PEN Presents grant from EnglishPEN.

b: Deepa Malik , India’s first female Paralympic medallist, has defied chest-down paralysis for 25 years. A recipient of five President of India awards, she has 91 medals, multiple world records, and international honours.…
f: Deepa Malik , India’s first female Paralympic medallist, has defied chest-down paralysis for 25 years. A recipient of five President of India awards, she has 91 medals, multiple world records, and international honours. Beyond sport, she is a biker, swimmer, rallyist, and advocate for disability inclusion. In 2024, she was appointed South Asian Sub-Region Representative of the Asian Paralympic Committee. Her autobiography, Bring It On , chronicles her fearless journey.

b: Deepak Nayyar is Emeritus Professor of Economics at Jawaharlal Nehru University, New Delhi, and an Honorary Fellow of Balliol College, Oxford. He served as Vice Chancellor, University of Delhi. His books include the…
f: Deepak Nayyar is Emeritus Professor of Economics at Jawaharlal Nehru University, New Delhi, and an Honorary Fellow of Balliol College, Oxford. He served as Vice Chancellor, University of Delhi. His books include the bestselling Catch Up and The Intelligent Person’s Guide to Liberalization . His latest books are Resurgent Asia and Asian Transformations.

b: Deepankar Aron is an intrepid traveller, lensman and writer, whose latest book, On The Trail of Buddha: A Journey to the East , explores the spiritual, cultural and philosophical linkages that bind India and East Asia.…
f: Deepankar Aron is an intrepid traveller, lensman and writer, whose latest book, On The Trail of Buddha: A Journey to the East , explores the spiritual, cultural and philosophical linkages that bind India and East Asia. Aron received the Presidential Award for his contributions as an Indian Revenue Service officer. World Heritage Sites of Uttarakhand was his first book.

b: Deepti Kapoor is the author of two novels, Age of Vice and A Bad Character. Age of Vice , forthcoming from Riverhead in January 2023, is currently being translated into 20 languages, and is in development for a TV…
f: Deepti Kapoor is the author of two novels, Age of Vice and A Bad Character. Age of Vice , forthcoming from Riverhead in January 2023, is currently being translated into 20 languages, and is in development for a TV series with FX/Disney.

b: Deepti Naval is an Indian film actor, director, writer, painter, and photographer. Her earlier works include a selection of poems, LAMHA LAMHA , which was published in the year 1981. Her second book of poems, Black Wind…
f: Deepti Naval is an Indian film actor, director, writer, painter, and photographer. Her earlier works include a selection of poems, LAMHA LAMHA , which was published in the year 1981. Her second book of poems, Black Wind and Other Poems , was published in 2004. The Mad Tibetan: Stories From Then and Now was her first anthology of short stories and her most recent book is A Country Called Childhood . Naval is the first American-Indian woman to join Hindi films, and she made her debut in the year 1980 with the path-breaking movie Ek Baar Phir , for which she was awarded the Best Actor award. Since then, she has appeared in more than 90 films and has also worked as a director. She recently made her debut in theatre, with the poetic stage show, EK MULAQAAT , where she plays the celebrated Punjabi writer, Amrita Pritam.

b: Deepti Priya Mehrotra is a social scientist, teacher, and storyteller whose work documents feminist politics, resistance, and counter-cultures in India. Her book Walking Out, Speaking Up: Feminist Street Theatre in…
f: Deepti Priya Mehrotra is a social scientist, teacher, and storyteller whose work documents feminist politics, resistance, and counter-cultures in India. Her book Walking Out, Speaking Up: Feminist Street Theatre in India chronicles a vibrant era of radical theatre aligned with the autonomous women’s movement. She is also the author of Home Truths: Stories of Single Mothers and acclaimed biographies of Irom Sharmila, Jaggi Devi, Gulab Bai, and Her Story . Drawing on oral history, ethnography, and archives, her writing traces oppositional politics. An activist and former street theatre actor, she has taught at universities across Delhi, Agra, and Mumbai and continues to work with grassroots movements.

b: Defne Suman was born in Istanbul. She gained a Masters in sociology from the Boğaziçi University, and worked as a volunteer in Thailand and Laos. She continued her studies in the USA, and now lives in Greece. Her novels…
f: Defne Suman was born in Istanbul. She gained a Masters in sociology from the Boğaziçi University, and worked as a volunteer in Thailand and Laos. She continued her studies in the USA, and now lives in Greece. Her novels and award winning short stories are translated into 25 languages, and are available all around the world.

b: Delphine Clot has worked in the French film industry for over 20 years. After beginning her career as a lawyer, she went on to hold senior legal and business affairs roles with leading industry players. In 2022, she…
f: Delphine Clot has worked in the French film industry for over 20 years. After beginning her career as a lawyer, she went on to hold senior legal and business affairs roles with leading industry players. In 2022, she co-founded Matriochkas, a book-to-screen agency that showcases publishers’ film and television adaptation rights to producers and creative talent.

b: Deo Brat Chaube is currently Professor of Philosophy and Religion at Banaras Hindu University (BHU). Dr. Chaube joined as a lecturer at BHU in 1981 and rose to the position of professor in 2009. Deeply inspired by the…
f: Deo Brat Chaube is currently Professor of Philosophy and Religion at Banaras Hindu University (BHU). Dr. Chaube joined as a lecturer at BHU in 1981 and rose to the position of professor in 2009. Deeply inspired by the noble ideas of Pt Madan Mohan Malaviya, he wrote a very important treatise titled Madan Mohan Malaviya Ka Darshan in the centenary year of BHU. He received Bhagwan Das Award, instituted by Uttar Pradesh Hindi Sansthan, for this. He is also the author of Mind Body Relation in Indian Philosophy, Antahkarana: Ek Vimarsa and Sanskritika Aloka.

b: Deshna Mehta is the co-founder of Studio Anugraha, a Mumbai-based communication design studio that has extensively worked on documenting the Kumbh Melas and produced volumes and documentaries on it. She hold a…
f: Deshna Mehta is the co-founder of Studio Anugraha, a Mumbai-based communication design studio that has extensively worked on documenting the Kumbh Melas and produced volumes and documentaries on it. She hold a master’s in visual communication from the Royal College of Art and has also co-curated and co-directed The Story Of Light and The Story Of Space festivals in Goa.

b: Des Raj Kali is a Punjabi writer. His short story collections include Kath Kali (Stories of Kali), Fakiri ( Mendicancy ) and Yahan Chai Achhi Nahi Banti ( Good Tea is Not Served Here). His novels are Antheen ( Eternal…
f: Des Raj Kali is a Punjabi writer. His short story collections include Kath Kali (Stories of Kali), Fakiri ( Mendicancy ) and Yahan Chai Achhi Nahi Banti ( Good Tea is Not Served Here). His novels are Antheen ( Eternal ), Pratham Pauran ( First Puran ), Shanti Parav and Shehar Vich Sahn Honn da Matlab ( What It Means to be a Bull in the Town ). He has also published research papers on the Ghadar Movement, the literature and culture of Punjab as well as gender and Dalit issues. Kali also edits the literary quarterly Lakeer .

b: Deval Sanghavi co-founded Dasra in 1999. He leads Dasra’s strategic philanthropy efforts, advising foreign and domestic philanthropists on grant-making strategies for the social sector, while supporting numerous NGO…
f: Deval Sanghavi co-founded Dasra in 1999. He leads Dasra’s strategic philanthropy efforts, advising foreign and domestic philanthropists on grant-making strategies for the social sector, while supporting numerous NGO leaders in India scale and deepen their impact

b: Devangana Dash is the author and illustrator of The Jungle Radio: Bird Songs of India . A bookmaker in New Delhi, when she's not designing books for a living, she draws and collects books for her dream library. A…
f: Devangana Dash is the author and illustrator of The Jungle Radio: Bird Songs of India . A bookmaker in New Delhi, when she's not designing books for a living, she draws and collects books for her dream library. A sociology and visual communication design graduate, Dash’s book cover designs have been recognised by the Federation of Indian Publishers Awards for Excellence in Book Production, Publishing Next Industry Awards and twice by the Oxford Bookstore Book Cover Prize.

b: Devapriya Roy is the author of three novels, The Vague Woman's Handbook , The Weight Loss Club and, most recently, Friends from College , which was serialised in The Telegraph for 42 weeks. In 2018, she published Indira…
f: Devapriya Roy is the author of three novels, The Vague Woman's Handbook , The Weight Loss Club and, most recently, Friends from College , which was serialised in The Telegraph for 42 weeks. In 2018, she published Indira , a graphic biography of Mrs Gandhi, created with artist Priya Kuriyan. Roy is best-known for the travel-memoir The Heat and Dust Project: The Broke Couple's Guide to Bharat, co-written with partner Saurav Jha, the story of an eccentric journey around India on the princely budget of 500 rupees a day for bed and board, which debuted at no.1 on the Hindustan Times-A.C. Nielsen list.

b: Devashish Makhija has researched and assisted on the movies Black Friday and Bunty aur Babli . He has written numerous screenplays, notably Anurag Kashyap's yet-to-be-made superhero saga Doga, has had a solo art show…
f: Devashish Makhija has researched and assisted on the movies Black Friday and Bunty aur Babli . He has written numerous screenplays, notably Anurag Kashyap's yet-to-be-made superhero saga Doga, has had a solo art show Occupying Silence , written a collection of short stories Forgetting, the forthcoming book of poems Disengaged, the bestselling children's books When Ali became Bajrangbali and Why Paploo was perplexed , and been featured in numerous anthologies including Mumbai Noir, Penguin First Proof and the Sahitya Akademi's Modern English Poetry. He has also written and directed the multiple award winning short films Taandav, El'ayichi, Agli Baar, Rahim Murge pe mat ro (Don't cry for Rahim LeCock), Absent, Happy, and the critically acclaimed full length feature films Ajji (Granny) and Bhonsle. His films have competed and won awards at the international film festivals of Rotterdam, Gothenberg, Beaune, Black Nights, Busan, Glasgow, Tampere, MOMA, APSA, Barcelona, Singapore, amongst many others. Oonga , a feature film he wrote and directed in 2013 never released in Indian theatres despite a critically acclaimed film festival run so he reverse-adapted it into a gripping novel.

b: Devdutt Pattanaik writes on mythology, which he defines as cultural truths revealed through stories, symbols and rituals. He lectures on the relevance of both Indian and Western myths in modern life. In the last…
f: Devdutt Pattanaik writes on mythology, which he defines as cultural truths revealed through stories, symbols and rituals. He lectures on the relevance of both Indian and Western myths in modern life. In the last twenty-five years, he has authored and illustrated over fifty books, including Book of Ram and Dharmic Leadership. Known for his TED talk and TV shows such as Devlok and Business Sutra, he is a regular columnist for reputed newspapers like The Times of India and Dainik Bhaskar .

b: Devendra Bisaria is a Chartered Accountant by training and an international Banker by profession. His first book of poetry, You, and Others , was launched at the Singapore Writers Festival in 2021. Bisaria is also a…
f: Devendra Bisaria is a Chartered Accountant by training and an international Banker by profession. His first book of poetry, You, and Others , was launched at the Singapore Writers Festival in 2021. Bisaria is also a successfully exhibited photographer.

b: Devendra Jhajharia is an Indian Paralympic javelin thrower. He is the first Indian Paralympian to win two gold medals at the Paralympics, he won his first gold in the javelin throw at the 2004 Summer Paralympics in…
f: Devendra Jhajharia is an Indian Paralympic javelin thrower. He is the first Indian Paralympian to win two gold medals at the Paralympics, he won his first gold in the javelin throw at the 2004 Summer Paralympics in Athens, becoming only the second gold medalist at the Paralympics for his country. At the 2016 Summer Paralympics in Rio de Janeiro, he won a second gold medal in the same event, bettering his previous record. He is also the recipient of numerous national awards.

b: Devendra Tak heads Media and Communication for Save the Children, a leading international child rights agency. Previously a journalist with the Independent, Business India and Indian Express Online , Tak has extensive…
f: Devendra Tak heads Media and Communication for Save the Children, a leading international child rights agency. Previously a journalist with the Independent, Business India and Indian Express Online , Tak has extensive experience in reporting from conflict and disasters situations and is a passionate humanitarian actor having worked with global agencies in national and international roles. He specialises in reporting on children affected by humanitarian crises. An avid writer, Tak never found anything worthwhile to write a book about...until he met the children featured in his work.

b: Devesh Kapur is the Starr Foundation Professor at the Johns Hopkins University School of Advanced International Studies. His books include The World Bank: Its First Half Century ; Diaspora, Democracy and Development ;…
f: Devesh Kapur is the Starr Foundation Professor at the Johns Hopkins University School of Advanced International Studies. His books include The World Bank: Its First Half Century ; Diaspora, Democracy and Development ; The Other One Percent: Indians in America ; and The Oxford Handbook of Higher Education in Asia and the Pacific . He previously taught at Harvard University and the University of Pennsylvania.

b: Devesh Alakh is a contemporary Hindi poet and the author of Kuch Pal Apne Pal and Khwab Adhkhuli Aankhon Ke. His poems cover themes such as satire, romance, beauty of nature and human frailties. His poetry is…
f: Devesh Alakh is a contemporary Hindi poet and the author of Kuch Pal Apne Pal and Khwab Adhkhuli Aankhon Ke. His poems cover themes such as satire, romance, beauty of nature and human frailties. His poetry is characterised by simple language and images strung together to force the readers to go on to a journey to the unexplored recesses of the human mind. While his succinct style of poetry easily connects with readers, his satire is declamatory and profound, forcing the reader to think and ponder. A collection of short stories is forthcoming.

b: Devika Rangachari is an award-winning writer and historian whose debut non-fiction for adults, The Mauryas , was recently published by Simon & Schuster India. Among her books for young adults are Queen of Ice (now part…
f: Devika Rangachari is an award-winning writer and historian whose debut non-fiction for adults, The Mauryas , was recently published by Simon & Schuster India. Among her books for young adults are Queen of Ice (now part of the Penguin Classics series), Queen of Earth, Queen of Fire and The Train to Tanjore .

b: Devika Rege's debut novel Quarterlife is a political bildungsroman set in contemporary India. Her work has received fellowships from Yaddo and the MacDowell Colony. Originally from Pune, she now lives in Bangalore,…
f: Devika Rege's debut novel Quarterlife is a political bildungsroman set in contemporary India. Her work has received fellowships from Yaddo and the MacDowell Colony. Originally from Pune, she now lives in Bangalore, where she teaches at Azim Premji University.

b: Devyani Bharadwaj is a poet, writer, and translator. Her poetry books include Usaki Ichchaon Men Barish Thi (Rajkamal Prakashan, 2025) and Ichcha Nadi ke Pul Par (2016). Her notable translations include Fansi Yard Se…
f: Devyani Bharadwaj is a poet, writer, and translator. Her poetry books include Usaki Ichchaon Men Barish Thi (Rajkamal Prakashan, 2025) and Ichcha Nadi ke Pul Par (2016). Her notable translations include Fansi Yard Se (Sudha Bhardwaj’s jail diary, 2025), Dear Mrs. Naidu by Matangi Subramanian (2022), and London Jungle Book , a travelogue by Bhajju Shyam. Her poems, articles, and translations have appeared in leading Hindi newspapers, magazines, and digital platforms. She received the Prem Bhatia Memorial Fellowship (2001) and Rajasthan Patrika Kavita Samman (2016). After a decade in journalism, she transitioned to the development sector and is currently Program Director at the Piramal Foundation.

b: Dexter Filkins joined The New Yorker as a staff writer in 2011. He has written about the murder of a journalist in Pakistan, the uprisings in Yemen, the war in Afghanistan, the crises in Syria and Lebanon, the Prime…
f: Dexter Filkins joined The New Yorker as a staff writer in 2011. He has written about the murder of a journalist in Pakistan, the uprisings in Yemen, the war in Afghanistan, the crises in Syria and Lebanon, the Prime Minister of Turkey and a troubled Iraq war veteran who tracked down the surviving members of a family his unit had opened fire on. Filkins worked at the Miami Herald and the Los Angeles Times where he was the paper’s New Delhi bureau chief before joining the New York Times, in 2000, reporting from New York, South Asia and Iraq. In 2009, he won a Pulitzer Prize as part of a team of T imes journalists covering Pakistan and Afghanistan. In 2006-07, he was a Nieman Fellow at Harvard University and, from 2007 to 2008, a fellow at the Carr Center for Human Rights Policy at Harvard’s Kennedy School of Government. He has received numerous prizes, including two George Polk Awards and three Overseas Press Club Awards. His book, The Forever War won the 2008 National Book Critics Circle Award for non-fiction and was named a best book of the year by the Times, the Washington Post , TIME and the Boston Globe .

She has been published in an anthology, Day’s End Stories, and in Hindu BLink, Vogue, Mint Lounge and Arré, among other publications. When she isn’t writing, Dharini backpacks, reads and finds immense joy in being brought up by her son.

b: Dhruba Jyoti Borah , known as DJB, is a celebrated literary voice from Assam. Author of over 30 novels, his acclaimed trilogy comprises Kalantarar Gadya ( Prose of the Tempest ), Tejor Andhar ( Darkness of Blood ), and…
f: Dhruba Jyoti Borah , known as DJB, is a celebrated literary voice from Assam. Author of over 30 novels, his acclaimed trilogy comprises Kalantarar Gadya ( Prose of the Tempest ), Tejor Andhar ( Darkness of Blood ), and Arth ( Meaning ), and is focused on the turmoil and tragedy of Assam’s insurgency era. His non-fiction includes a monograph on the Moamoria rebellion, studies on Assamese language development, and works on global revolutions like WWII, the French Revolution, and the Russian Revolution. His writings have been translated into Hindi, English, Bengali, Malayalam, Nepali, and Bodo. Borah received the Sahitya Akademi Award in 2009.

Roy National Award in the category of Eminent Medical Person, the Times Healthcare Achievers Award in the 'Legends' category, the Doctor of the Decade Award by the Indian Medical Association and the National Excellence Award by the TP Jhunjhunwala Foundation. His work has also appeared in Harper’s, The New York Times, The Washington Post and The Guardian . Gibson serves as director of Art Omi: Writers in Ghent, New York, and he co-founded Sangam House, a writers’ residency in India, along with Arshia Sattar.

b: Easterine Kire is a poet, novelist and writer of short stories and children’s books. She was the first Naga writer to publish an English novel, titled A Naga Village Remembered. Her second novel, A Terrible…
f: Easterine Kire is a poet, novelist and writer of short stories and children’s books. She was the first Naga writer to publish an English novel, titled A Naga Village Remembered. Her second novel, A Terrible Matriarchy, has been translated into Norwegian, German and Marathi. In 2011, she was awarded the Governor’s Prize for Excellence in Naga Literature and the Free Word by Catalan PEN, Barcelona in 2013. Her book When the River Sleeps won the 2015 Hindu Literature Prize and was chosen for the inaugural Gordon Graham Prize for Naga Literature in 2019. In 2017, Son of the Thundercloud was awarded the Tata Litlive Book of the Year and the Bal Sahitya Puraskar the following year. Her latest novel, A Respectable Woman, recently won Printed Book of the Year India.

b: Edward Luce was made the FT's chief US commentator in September 2011 with a weekly column and regular editorials on the US economy and politics. Prior to that he was the FT’s Washington Bureau Chief from 2006 until…
f: Edward Luce was made the FT's chief US commentator in September 2011 with a weekly column and regular editorials on the US economy and politics. Prior to that he was the FT’s Washington Bureau Chief from 2006 until 2011 - managing a team of ten DC-based reporters and leading the paper’s coverage of US politics and economy. Previously, he was the FT’s South Asia bureau chief, based in New Delhi, appointed in 2001. He is the author of three highly acclaimed books: In Spite of the Gods: The Rise of Modern India, Time to Start Thinking: The Spectre of American Decline and The Retreat of Western Liberalism, which was listed on the best non-fiction reading lists for 2017 at Amazon, The Economist , the Wall Street Journal , the Financial Times and the Washington Post. Between 1993 and 1994, he was the Geneva-based correspondent for The Guardian newspaper of the UK. He then moved to Manila to be the Philippines correspondent of the Financial Times between 1995 and 1997. Between 1997 and 1999, he was the Financial Times ’ capital markets editor, based in London.

Canning has authored a monograph and papers on Spanish Golden-Age drama, and her short stories have appeared in the Nation. She is also editor of Maggie O'Farrell: Contemporary Critical Perspectives (forthcoming, Bloomsbury) and her debut novel, The Sandstone City, will be published by Aderyn Press in 2022.

b: Elif Shafak is an award-winning British-Turkish novelist. She has published 19 books, 12 of which are novels, including her latest The Island of Missing Trees, shortlisted for the Costa Novel Award. Shafak is a fellow…
f: Elif Shafak is an award-winning British-Turkish novelist. She has published 19 books, 12 of which are novels, including her latest The Island of Missing Trees, shortlisted for the Costa Novel Award. Shafak is a fellow and a Vice President of the Royal Society of Literature, a member of the Weforum Global Agenda Council on Creative Economy, and a founding member of the European Council on Foreign Relations. An advocate for women's rights, LGBTQ+ rights and freedom of expression, Shafak is an inspiring public speaker and two-time TED Global speaker. She was awarded the medal of Chevalier de l’Ordre des Arts et des Lettres and the Halldór Laxness International Literature Prize, among others. A bestselling author in many countries, she has also judged numerous literary prizes, including the PEN Nabokov prize and has chaired the Wellcome Prize.

b: Eliza Griswold is the author of The Tenth Parallel: Dispatches from the Fault Line Between Christianity and Islam , which won the 2011 J. Anthony Lukas Book Prize. Her translation of Afghan women’s folk poems, I Am…

Her latest book, Amity and Prosperity , recounts the true story of how fracking shattered one Pennsylvania town and how one resident brought it to light. Currently a Distinguished Writer in Residence at New York University, Griswold has held fellowships from the New America Foundation, the Guggenheim Foundation and Harvard University.

b: Elizabeth Gilbert is the number one bestselling author of Eat Pray Love , which has sold over 15 million copies worldwide and been translated into over 46 languages, and several other international bestselling books of…
f: Elizabeth Gilbert is the number one bestselling author of Eat Pray Love , which has sold over 15 million copies worldwide and been translated into over 46 languages, and several other international bestselling books of fiction and non-fiction. Her follow-up memoir to Eat Pray Love, Committed, became an instant number one New York Times bestseller. She has published two novels, Stern Men and The Signature of All Things, which was longlisted for the Baileys Women’s Prize for Fiction and shortlisted for the Wellcome Book Prize.
