He is also the former Registrar of Copyrights of the Indian Copyrights office and played a crucial role in introducing the recent amendments to the Copyright Act, 2012, and the Copyright Rules, 2013. He holds several degrees and postgraduate degrees, and is currently pursuing his PhD (IPRs) from GGSIP University, New Delhi.

b: Gabriel Filippelli is a Chancellor’s Professor Executive Director of the Indiana University Environmental Resilience Institute, focusing on climate change and health. Author of over 200 publications, in 2022 he…
f: Gabriel Filippelli is a Chancellor’s Professor Executive Director of the Indiana University Environmental Resilience Institute, focusing on climate change and health. Author of over 200 publications, in 2022 he published the book Climate Change and Life and edited Climate Resilience in Indiana and Beyond .

b: Gabriela Ruivo is a Portuguese author and translator based in the UK. After a career as a psychologist and trainer, she turned to writing, with her first novel UMA OUTRA VOZ winning multiple prestigious awards,…
f: Gabriela Ruivo is a Portuguese author and translator based in the UK. After a career as a psychologist and trainer, she turned to writing, with her first novel UMA OUTRA VOZ winning multiple prestigious awards, including the Prémio LeYa. Her works have been translated into English, including excerpts in YOUR IMPOSSIBLE VOICE and a collaboration with Victor Meadowcroft on O SÍTIO DOS MORTOS VIVOS . She has also published children's books, poetry, and short stories. Ruivo is active in the literary community as chair of the UK Cultural Team at AILD and co-founder of the PinT Book Club. Her second novel, LEI DA GRAVIDADE , was a laureate for the European Union Prize for Literature 2024.

b: Gaea Schoeters is Belgian author who writes in diverse genres, rom novels, children’s books and screenplays to music – on theatre and opera. Her most recent novel, Trofee , was widely translated and shortlisted for…
f: Gaea Schoeters is Belgian author who writes in diverse genres, rom novels, children’s books and screenplays to music – on theatre and opera. Her most recent novel, Trofee , was widely translated and shortlisted for various prizes. She is a keen motor-biker, who translates Kae Tempest and curates the Dead Ladies Show that celebrates ground-breaking women of the past. Additionally, she writes columns and essays for various newspapers and literary magazines.

b: Gagandeep Kang is an infectious disease researcher who links community-based research to high quality laboratory investigation. With 30 years of research at the Christian Medical College, Vellore, Dr. Kang has built…
f: Gagandeep Kang is an infectious disease researcher who links community-based research to high quality laboratory investigation. With 30 years of research at the Christian Medical College, Vellore, Dr. Kang has built collaborative programmes focused on enteric diseases, nutrition and the environment. She supported the development of two rotavirus vaccines made by Indian companies through clinical and laboratory testing. She serves on many advisory committees in India and internationally, including for the World Health Organisation. She was the Executive Director of Translational Health Science and Technology Institute, Faridabad from 2016 to 2020. A fellow of many prestigious academies in India and internationally, in 2019, she became the first woman working in India to be inducted as a Fellow of Royal Society, London.

b: Dr Gajsingh Rajpurohit is a distinguished Rajasthani poet and literary critic, and recipient of the Sahitya Akademi’s highest Rajasthani language award. He currently serves as Head of the Rajasthani Department at Jai…
f: Dr Gajsingh Rajpurohit is a distinguished Rajasthani poet and literary critic, and recipient of the Sahitya Akademi’s highest Rajasthani language award. He currently serves as Head of the Rajasthani Department at Jai Narain Vyas University, Jodhpur, and is a member of the Sahitya Akademi Rajasthani Advisory Board.

b: Galina Lazareva is an award-winning Russian poet, translator, singer and performer. Based in Sydney at the University of NSW, she won the Grand Prix at the 2017 Pushkin in Britain Russian Poetry Festival and a Russian…
f: Galina Lazareva is an award-winning Russian poet, translator, singer and performer. Based in Sydney at the University of NSW, she won the Grand Prix at the 2017 Pushkin in Britain Russian Poetry Festival and a Russian Academy of Sciences Poetry Translation Award. Her critically acclaimed translation of Australian and British poets, Eternity Can Wait, was published in 2011.

b: Ganesh V. Shivaswamy is a lawyer from Bengaluru and a collector of chromolithographs from the Ravi Varma Press. Ganesh is the author of a six-volume book series, Raja Ravi Varma: An Everlasting Imprint , which explores…
f: Ganesh V. Shivaswamy is a lawyer from Bengaluru and a collector of chromolithographs from the Ravi Varma Press. Ganesh is the author of a six-volume book series, Raja Ravi Varma: An Everlasting Imprint , which explores the social, religious and aesthetic impact of the visual legacy of the artist on the people of the Indian sub-continent and beyond.

b: Garfield D'souza is a writer, editor, teacher, and podcaster. His work has been published in Visual Verse and harana poetry. His poems are in Language is a Queer Thing, an anthology by British Council, The Queer Muslim…
f: Garfield D'souza is a writer, editor, teacher, and podcaster. His work has been published in Visual Verse and harana poetry. His poems are in Language is a Queer Thing, an anthology by British Council, The Queer Muslim Project, and Verve Poetry Press. He has designed blended e-learning courses for The Tata Group, Capgemini, and Lionbridge; and written technical documentation for IBM and Rolta. He has also conducted writing workshops at Larsen and Toubro and Tata Lit. Live 2022 and completed a season of About What You Say, a podcast about words.

b: Gargi Rawat is a senior news anchor and environment reporter who has worked with NDTV 24X7 for the last two decades. For many years, she has been a regular face on the channel and has filmed several documentaries and…
f: Gargi Rawat is a senior news anchor and environment reporter who has worked with NDTV 24X7 for the last two decades. For many years, she has been a regular face on the channel and has filmed several documentaries and environment- related programmes. She worked on the first-ever news show on wildlife in India, Born Wild , and anchored its Hindi version, Safari India , for the Hindi channel NDTV India. Rawat has also been editorial head for some of the best-known environmental campaigns carried out by NDTV, including ‘The Greenathon’, ‘Save Our Tigers’, and the ‘Banega Swachh India Campaign’. She received widespread acclaim for her award-winning documentary series on the state of the river Ganga. She has just released her first book Tiger Season , a work of fiction, which has themes of tiger conservation and environmental concerns.

b: Gary Tinterow is Director of the Museum of Fine Arts, Houston, since 2012, and is a transformative leader in the museum world, recognized for his remarkable curatorial career at The Metropolitan Museum of Art in New…
f: Gary Tinterow is Director of the Museum of Fine Arts, Houston, since 2012, and is a transformative leader in the museum world, recognized for his remarkable curatorial career at The Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York. At the MFAH, he has spearheaded groundbreaking initiatives, including a $450-million campus expansion, and fostered international collaborations with institutions such as the British Museum and Museo Nacional del Prado. A Harvard-trained art historian, Tinterow has curated acclaimed exhibitions across contemporary and 19th-century European art and has earned prestigious honors from France and Spain for his contributions to cultural exchange and preservation.

b: Gaur Gopal Das studied electrical engineering at the College of Engineering, Pune. After a brief stint with Hewlett-Packard, he decided to live life as a monk in an ashram in downtown Mumbai. He has remained there for…
f: Gaur Gopal Das studied electrical engineering at the College of Engineering, Pune. After a brief stint with Hewlett-Packard, he decided to live life as a monk in an ashram in downtown Mumbai. He has remained there for twenty-six years, learning the antiquity of ancient philosophy and the modernity of contemporary psychology, to become a life coach to thousands in the city. Gaur Gopal Das has been travelling the world for over two decades, sharing his wisdom with corporate executives, universities and charities, and has also spoken at the United Nations. In 2016, his global popularity exploded as he took his message online. With over one billion views on his videos on social media, he now leads a movement to help others achieve happiness and purpose in their lives. Now one of the most famous monks in the world, Gaur Gopal Das has been conferred with several honours, including the prestigious Dadasaheb Phalke International Film Festival Award and an honorary doctorate (DLitt) by KIIT University.

b: Gaurav Solanki is a Mumbai-based fiction writer, poet, screenwriter and lyricist. After graduating from IIT Roorkee, he worked with Tehelka for a while. He won Bharatiya Gyanpeeth’s Navelkhan Award for his first…
f: Gaurav Solanki is a Mumbai-based fiction writer, poet, screenwriter and lyricist. After graduating from IIT Roorkee, he worked with Tehelka for a while. He won Bharatiya Gyanpeeth’s Navelkhan Award for his first poetry collection Sau Saal Fida . He has also written the lyrics for Ugly . He is currently writing an original series and a feature film.

b: Gautam Sharma is a Professor of Cardiology at the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS). He initiated the Centre for Integrative Medicine and Research at AIIMS, of which he is the current head. He is also a…
f: Gautam Sharma is a Professor of Cardiology at the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS). He initiated the Centre for Integrative Medicine and Research at AIIMS, of which he is the current head. He is also a visiting professor at the S-VYASA University, Bengaluru. He is a senior Interventional Cardiologist and has authored several publications in leading peer reviewed journals and is a regular speaker at national and international cardiology conferences. Dr. Sharma is passionate about integrating yoga and other traditional healing systems with modern medicine.

b: Gautam Trivedi is a Co-Founder & Managing Partner of Nepean Capital. He has over 30 years of experience in the Indian and Asian financial industry. He has worked at Goldman Sachs, Religare Capital Markets, DSP Merrill…
f: Gautam Trivedi is a Co-Founder & Managing Partner of Nepean Capital. He has over 30 years of experience in the Indian and Asian financial industry. He has worked at Goldman Sachs, Religare Capital Markets, DSP Merrill Lynch, CLSA Asia and Jardine Fleming. Gautam graduated from the University of Southern California (USC) with an MBA.

b: Gayatri Rangachari Shah is a journalist and columnist whose work has appeared in both national and international publications. She has a fortnightly column in The Hindu, is a contributing editor at Vogue and…
f: Gayatri Rangachari Shah is a journalist and columnist whose work has appeared in both national and international publications. She has a fortnightly column in The Hindu, is a contributing editor at Vogue and Architectural Digest and India Head at Tina Brown Live Media. She is a graduate of Columbia University’s Graduate School of Journalism.

b: Gayatri Sinha is a writer, art critic and curator who works in New Delhi on the arts resource criticalcollective.in . Her principal interests are art and photography, gender and contemporary Indian social history.
f: Gayatri Sinha is a writer, art critic and curator who works in New Delhi on the arts resource criticalcollective.in . Her principal interests are art and photography, gender and contemporary Indian social history.

b: Gaël Faye is an author, composer and hip hop artist. He released an album in 2010 with the group Milk Coffee & Sugar. In 2013, he released his first solo album Pili Pili sur un Croissant au Beurre . It was recorded…
f: Gaël Faye is an author, composer and hip hop artist. He released an album in 2010 with the group Milk Coffee & Sugar. In 2013, he released his first solo album Pili Pili sur un Croissant au Beurre . It was recorded between Bujumbura and Paris, and is filled with a plethora of musical influences: rap laced with soul and jazz, semba, Congolese rumba. In 2018, he received the prestigious Victoires de la Musique Award. His first novel Small Country was a bestseller in France, winning the Prix Goncourt des Lycéens 2016 and has been published in more than 30 countries. The movie adaptation will be released in 2020.

b: Gaëlle Bohé is the Director of Fontaine O Livres, a Paris-based organization supporting independent publishers. A former journalist specializing in sustainability and a literary programmer for the Festival du Livre de…
f: Gaëlle Bohé is the Director of Fontaine O Livres, a Paris-based organization supporting independent publishers. A former journalist specializing in sustainability and a literary programmer for the Festival du Livre de Paris and La Nuit de la Lecture, she created the Fresque du Livre, a workshop on the environmental challenges of publishing, and founded the Prix Hors Concours, a literary award that recently launched its international edition.

b: Geeta Gopalakrishnan is the Founder and Managing Trustee of Ma Foundation. She has channeled years of advertising experience into fundraising for Sadhana School for Special Children and underprivileged children with…
f: Geeta Gopalakrishnan is the Founder and Managing Trustee of Ma Foundation. She has channeled years of advertising experience into fundraising for Sadhana School for Special Children and underprivileged children with cancer. All proceeds of her book My Grandmother’s Tweets go towards MA Foundation, which supports desperate mothers with children afflicted by cancer at Tata Medical Centre in Kolkata.

b: Geeta Samor is Assistant Professor at Rajasthan University and a Hindi literature critic with an interest in short stories, poetry, Rajasthani literature as well as Dingal and folk literature. Dr. Samor is a three-time…
f: Geeta Samor is Assistant Professor at Rajasthan University and a Hindi literature critic with an interest in short stories, poetry, Rajasthani literature as well as Dingal and folk literature. Dr. Samor is a three-time winner of Rajasthan University’s Gold Medal in academics.

b: Geeta Tandon is a leading stunt artist in the Hindi film industry. Having overcome overcome years of abuse, she puts her survival skills to use while performing daring stunts as a body double in Bollywood. A gutsy and…
f: Geeta Tandon is a leading stunt artist in the Hindi film industry. Having overcome overcome years of abuse, she puts her survival skills to use while performing daring stunts as a body double in Bollywood. A gutsy and inspirational woman, Tandon has chipped away at a male dominated field to establish herself within it.

b: Geetika Kalha has been an Indian Administrative Service ( IAS) officer for over 30 years and has done pioneering work in revival, interpretation, and dissemination of cultural heritage. With a background in history and…
f: Geetika Kalha has been an Indian Administrative Service ( IAS) officer for over 30 years and has done pioneering work in revival, interpretation, and dissemination of cultural heritage. With a background in history and culture, she is now a writer and a consultant who specialises in rural tourism, museums and cultural interpretation. As President of the Village Life Improvement Foundation (Vlife), she works to improve health and hygiene in villages and has provided complete wastewater management and sanitation in many villages. Apart from research and writing her passions include birding, travelling and painting.

b: Geoff Dyer ’s many books include Jeff in Venice, Death in Varanasi , Yoga For People Who Can’t Be Bothered To Do It and, most recently, Homework , a memoir. He is a Fellow of the Royal Society of Literature and a member…
f: Geoff Dyer ’s many books include Jeff in Venice, Death in Varanasi , Yoga For People Who Can’t Be Bothered To Do It and, most recently, Homework , a memoir. He is a Fellow of the Royal Society of Literature and a member of the American Academy of Arts & Sciences. His books have won numerous prizes and have been translated into twenty-six languages.

b: Geoffrey Dean joined the Canadian Public Service in 1995. He has held various roles, including Senior Policy Advisor to Canada's Special Coordinator for the Middle East Peace Process, Chief of Staff to the President of…
f: Geoffrey Dean joined the Canadian Public Service in 1995. He has held various roles, including Senior Policy Advisor to Canada's Special Coordinator for the Middle East Peace Process, Chief of Staff to the President of the Queen’s Privy Council, and Director of Communications for the Afghanistan Task Force. He served at the Canadian Embassy in Seoul, as Deputy Chief of Protocol, and as Head of Political and Public Affairs in Jakarta. Currently, he is Deputy High Commissioner for Canada to India at the Canadian High Commission in New Delhi. He is married to Hyo-Jin Lim.

b: Georg Wirsching is a professionally trained visual artist with a degree in Visual Communications and a specialisation in Photography and Graphic Design from Loyola College Chennai. Since 1998 he has worked as an artist,…
f: Georg Wirsching is a professionally trained visual artist with a degree in Visual Communications and a specialisation in Photography and Graphic Design from Loyola College Chennai. Since 1998 he has worked as an artist, set designer and creative director in advertising, television and marketing companies in Chennai, Coimbatore and Bangalore while following his artistic projects in painting and the Visual Arts. He has also been working on numerous professional commissions for patrons around the world. Wirsching has been maintaining the Josef Wirsching photographic archive since 2009 and has been managing his company- 'Wirsching Enterprises', which owns and administers the rights to accessibility, distribution, exhibition etc., of the entire Josef Wirsching Photographic Collection. He has also been teaching Cambridge IGCSE-level Art and Design in Goa since 2017.

b: George H. Packer is a staff writer for The Atlantic and the author of Our Man: Richard Holbrooke and the End of the American Century . He has published five other works of non-fiction, including The Unwinding: An Inner…
f: George H. Packer is a staff writer for The Atlantic and the author of Our Man: Richard Holbrooke and the End of the American Century . He has published five other works of non-fiction, including The Unwinding: An Inner History of the New America , which won the National Book Award for nonfiction in 2013, as well as two novels and a play.

b: Georgi Gospodinov’s works have now been translated to acclaim in 25 languages, have been shortlisted for more than a dozen international prizes - including the PEN Literary Award for Translation, the Premio Gregor von…
f: Georgi Gospodinov’s works have now been translated to acclaim in 25 languages, have been shortlisted for more than a dozen international prizes - including the PEN Literary Award for Translation, the Premio Gregor von Rezzori, the Brücke Berlin Preis, and the Haus der Kulturen der Welt Literaturpreis - and have won the 2016 Jan Michalski Prize for Literature, the 2019 Angelus Literature Central Europe Prize and the 2021 Premio Strega Europe, among others. His novel Time Shelter, translated into English by Angela Rodel, won the 2023 International Booker Prize.

b: Geraint F. Lewis is a Professor of Astrophysics at the University of Sydney. A leading cosmologist, he unpicks the dark side of the universe, focusing on galactic cannibalism and gravitational lensing. He is the author…
f: Geraint F. Lewis is a Professor of Astrophysics at the University of Sydney. A leading cosmologist, he unpicks the dark side of the universe, focusing on galactic cannibalism and gravitational lensing. He is the author of A Fortunate Universe and The Cosmic Revolutionary’s Handbook , bringing complex physics to global audiences.

b: Germaine Greer is a writer, academic and critic who is widely regarded as one of the most significant feminist voices of our time. Her first book, The Female Eunuch, was published in 1969 and remains one of the most…
f: Germaine Greer is a writer, academic and critic who is widely regarded as one of the most significant feminist voices of our time. Her first book, The Female Eunuch, was published in 1969 and remains one of the most influential texts of the feminist movement. Greer has had a distinguished academic career in Britain and the USA. She makes regular appearances in print and other media as a broadcaster, journalist, columnist and reviewer.

b: Gerður Kristný is a highly versatile and prolific author. For the past 25 years, she has written poems, novels, YA stories, short stories, children books, stage plays and non fictional works. She has received numerous…
f: Gerður Kristný is a highly versatile and prolific author. For the past 25 years, she has written poems, novels, YA stories, short stories, children books, stage plays and non fictional works. She has received numerous awards for her work including the Icelandic Journalism Award for a non-fictional publication on child abuse and the Icelandic Literary Award for her book of poetry Bloodhoof , which was also nominated for the Nordic Council Literary Awards. Her latest work is the novel Smartís .

b: Ghaith Abdul-Ahad was born in Iraq in 1975. He began writing for The Guardian and The Washington Post post-2003 US invasion, reporting across Iraq, Syria, Libya, Yemen, and Afghanistan. His focus on civilian experiences…
f: Ghaith Abdul-Ahad was born in Iraq in 1975. He began writing for The Guardian and The Washington Post post-2003 US invasion, reporting across Iraq, Syria, Libya, Yemen, and Afghanistan. His focus on civilian experiences has earned him numerous accolades, including the British Press Awards' Foreign Reporter of the Year and two Emmys. He lives in Istanbul.

b: Gideon Haigh has contributed to more than a hundred newspapers and magazines, and published 35 books about cricket, business, social affairs and true crime. His latest book, This Is How I Will Strangle You, is a study…
f: Gideon Haigh has contributed to more than a hundred newspapers and magazines, and published 35 books about cricket, business, social affairs and true crime. His latest book, This Is How I Will Strangle You, is a study of incest.

b: Gideon Levy is an Israeli journalist and author. Levy writes opinion pieces and a weekly column for the newspaper Haaretz that often focuses on the Israeli occupation of the Palestinian territories. Levy has won prizes…
f: Gideon Levy is an Israeli journalist and author. Levy writes opinion pieces and a weekly column for the newspaper Haaretz that often focuses on the Israeli occupation of the Palestinian territories. Levy has won prizes for his articles on human rights in the Israeli-occupied territories. In 2021, he won Israel's top award for journalism, the Sokolov Award.

b: Giles Tillotson writes about Indian art and architecture, especially the Rajput courts of Rajasthan, urbanism and landscape painting in colonial and modern India. In recent years he has worked on exhibitions and…
f: Giles Tillotson writes about Indian art and architecture, especially the Rajput courts of Rajasthan, urbanism and landscape painting in colonial and modern India. In recent years he has worked on exhibitions and publications with the Maharaja Sawai Man Singh II Museum in Jaipur City Palace, and with DAG, New Delhi.

b: Giorgio Parisi is an Italian physicist, former President of the Accademia dei Lincei, and became a professor in theoretical physics at the University of Rome in 1981. He received the Boltzmann Medal, the Max Planck…
f: Giorgio Parisi is an Italian physicist, former President of the Accademia dei Lincei, and became a professor in theoretical physics at the University of Rome in 1981. He received the Boltzmann Medal, the Max Planck Medal, the Nonino Prize, the Wolf Prize, and the Nobel Prize in 2021.

b: Girdhar Malaviya is the grandson of Mahamana Pt Madan Mohan Malaviya. His father, Pt. Govind Malaviya, was the youngest son of Mahamana. He is the author of Madan Mohan Malaviya: Ek Jeevan Parichay . In addition to his…
f: Girdhar Malaviya is the grandson of Mahamana Pt Madan Mohan Malaviya. His father, Pt. Govind Malaviya, was the youngest son of Mahamana. He is the author of Madan Mohan Malaviya: Ek Jeevan Parichay . In addition to his writing, he has served as president of many social and educational organisations.

b: Giriraj Kiradoo is a poet, editor, and cultural practitioner with over two decades of experience across education, publishing, and language initiatives. He has held leadership roles at Brio, Storytel India, Jan Suraaj…
f: Giriraj Kiradoo is a poet, editor, and cultural practitioner with over two decades of experience across education, publishing, and language initiatives. He has held leadership roles at Brio, Storytel India, Jan Suraaj Foundation, and YourStory, co-founded Pratilipi, edited multiple books, and received major literary awards for poetry and translation.

b: Girish Kuber , a seasoned journalist since 1985 and a Chevening scholar, previously served as the Political Editor for The Economic Times . Presently, he holds the position of Chief Editor at LokSatta, a part of The…
f: Girish Kuber , a seasoned journalist since 1985 and a Chevening scholar, previously served as the Political Editor for The Economic Times . Presently, he holds the position of Chief Editor at LokSatta, a part of The Indian Express group. As an accomplished author, his notable works include The Tatas: How a Family Built a Business and a Nation , Renaissance State: The Unwritten Story of the Making of Maharashtra , and The Invisible Enemy: A Global Story of Biological and Chemical Warfare – all published by HarperCollins and translated into various languages. Additionally, he has authored 8 books in Marathi. Girish Kuber is also a regular contributor to The Indian Express .

b: Gita Sahgal is a writer and documentary filmmaker on the editorial collective, ‘Feminist Dissent’. Her documentaries include the Rushdie affair, dowry murders, sati, the case of Kiranjit Ahluwalia, who killed her…
f: Gita Sahgal is a writer and documentary filmmaker on the editorial collective, ‘Feminist Dissent’. Her documentaries include the Rushdie affair, dowry murders, sati, the case of Kiranjit Ahluwalia, who killed her husband and ‘The War Crimes File’ about the Jamaat-e-Islami death squads in the 1971 war in Bangladesh.

b: GJV Prasad , formerly Professor of English at Jawaharlal Nehru University, is a writer, critic, and translator. He has translated three books from Tamil to English – Ambai’s A Red-necked Green Bird (2021), Imayam’s A…
f: GJV Prasad , formerly Professor of English at Jawaharlal Nehru University, is a writer, critic, and translator. He has translated three books from Tamil to English – Ambai’s A Red-necked Green Bird (2021), Imayam’s A Woman Burnt (2023), which received the KLF Award for Translation, and Salma’s The Dark Hours of the Night.

b: Glenn Patterson is the author of ten novels and three works of nonfiction. In 2006, he was elected to Aosdána, the affiliation of Irish Artists. In 2007, he became an Arts Council Major Artist. In 2008, he was awarded…
f: Glenn Patterson is the author of ten novels and three works of nonfiction. In 2006, he was elected to Aosdána, the affiliation of Irish Artists. In 2007, he became an Arts Council Major Artist. In 2008, he was awarded a Lannan Literary Fellowship. In 2012, he co-wrote the screenplay of Good Vibrations (BBC Films). His novel, The Mill for Grinding Old People Young, was Belfast’s inaugural One City One Book. In 2017, Dr Patterson was appointed Director of the Seamus Heaney Centre for Poetry at Queen’s University of Belfast.

b: Gloria Berbena joined the U.S. Diplomatic Corps in 1989. A member of the Senior Foreign Service, Berbena has served as the Minister Counselor for Public Diplomacy to the U.S. Mission to India since 2021. She previously…
f: Gloria Berbena joined the U.S. Diplomatic Corps in 1989. A member of the Senior Foreign Service, Berbena has served as the Minister Counselor for Public Diplomacy to the U.S. Mission to India since 2021. She previously served as Charge d’Affaires and Deputy Chief of Mission at the U.S. Embassy in San Jose, Costa Rica; as Minister Counselor for Public Affairs at the U.S. Embassy in Rome; as Senior Advisor to the Executive Secretary in Washington, D.C.; Executive Assistant/Chief of Staff to the Undersecretary for Public Diplomacy and Public Affairs; and as Director of the Office of Public Diplomacy in the Bureau of European and Eurasian Affairs. Other overseas service includes public diplomacy positions in Havana, Athens, Naples, Rome, and Bangkok.

b: Gonçalo M. Tavares is an award-winning author. In 2005, he won the José Saramago Prize for young writers under 35 for Jerusalem , which was also awarded the Prêmio Portugal Telecom de Literatura em Língua Portuguesa…
f: Gonçalo M. Tavares is an award-winning author. In 2005, he won the José Saramago Prize for young writers under 35 for Jerusalem , which was also awarded the Prêmio Portugal Telecom de Literatura em Língua Portuguesa 2007 and the LER/Millenium Prize. His novel Learning to Pray in the Age of Technology won the Prize of the Best Foreign Book 2010 in France and was shortlisted for numerous others. In 2011, Tavares received the Grande Prêmio da Associação Portuguesa de Escritores as well as the prestigious Prémio Literário Fernando Namora 2011. His book, Matteo Lost His Job , is among the five shortlisted works for the prestigious Prix Femina 2016 foreign fiction. Tavares’ work has been published in almost 50 countries.

b: Gopal Mathur is an author, poet and translator. His work has been published in renowned magazines and journals and broadcast on All India Radio and Doordarshan. His critical review of Narendra Nagdev’s collection of…
f: Gopal Mathur is an author, poet and translator. His work has been published in renowned magazines and journals and broadcast on All India Radio and Doordarshan. His critical review of Narendra Nagdev’s collection of stories, Ped Khali Nahi Hain , was published in Hans’ November 2018 issue.

b: Govind Deecee is a commissioning editor at DC Books. Formally trained in the Cinematic Arts and Photography, he also holds a BFA in Economics. He graduated from Syracuse University in New York and prior to his career in…
f: Govind Deecee is a commissioning editor at DC Books. Formally trained in the Cinematic Arts and Photography, he also holds a BFA in Economics. He graduated from Syracuse University in New York and prior to his career in publishing he has worked as a video editor and cinematographer on ad films . At DC Books , he is charged with commissioning new works and managing translations and rights. Since 2019 he also manages the audio books division at DC Books and has been in charge of curating the titles for publication into audiobooks. The audio Division at DC Books since 2019 has around 750 titles in Malayalam.

b: Govindraj Ethiraj is a television and print journalist and most recently founder of BOOM, a fact checking and fake news busting initiative. He is also founder of the award-winning India Spend and Fact Checker, which are…
f: Govindraj Ethiraj is a television and print journalist and most recently founder of BOOM, a fact checking and fake news busting initiative. He is also founder of the award-winning India Spend and Fact Checker, which are the only verified India members of the International Fact Checking Network. He has been a career business journalist who has reported and written on Indian business for over 25 years. Previously, he was Founder-Editor in Chief of Bloomberg TV India, Editor with Business Standard and spent five years CNBC-TV18. He is a Fellow of the Inaugural Class of Ananta Aspen’s 2006 India Leadership Initiative, a 2018 McNulty Laureate and a winner of the 2014 BMW Responsible Leaders Awards

b: Greg Sheridan is a foreign affairs journalist and commentator. He joined The Australian in 1984 and worked in Beijing, Washington and Canberra before starting his tenure as the paper’s foreign editor in 1992. He…
f: Greg Sheridan is a foreign affairs journalist and commentator. He joined The Australian in 1984 and worked in Beijing, Washington and Canberra before starting his tenure as the paper’s foreign editor in 1992. He specialises in Asian politics and has written four books on the topic.

b: Guillermo Rodríguez is the founding director of Casa de la India , a pioneering cultural centre in Spain, which has become the model for India’s cultural diplomacy abroad. A passionate traveller, he lived in South…
f: Guillermo Rodríguez is the founding director of Casa de la India , a pioneering cultural centre in Spain, which has become the model for India’s cultural diplomacy abroad. A passionate traveller, he lived in South India throughout the 1990s. He is the author of When Mirrors Are Windows: A View of AK Ramanujan’s Poetics.

b: Guillermo Rodríguez , an active promoter of Indo-Spanish cultural relations, is the founding director of Casa de la India, a pioneering cultural centre in Spain, which has become the model for India’s cultural…
f: Guillermo Rodríguez , an active promoter of Indo-Spanish cultural relations, is the founding director of Casa de la India, a pioneering cultural centre in Spain, which has become the model for India’s cultural diplomacy abroad. A passionate traveller, it was during an overland trip to India in the early 1990s that he chanced upon A.K. Ramanujan’s poetry and translations, an interest that evolved into a PhD. on the poet-scholar, obtained from the University of Kerala and University of Valladolid. He is the author of When Mirrors Are Windows: A View of A.K. Ramanujan’s Poetics and co-editor of Journeys: A Poet’s Diary by A.K. Ramanujan.

b: Guillermo Rodríguez is the Founding Director of Casa de la India, Spain’s pioneering Indian cultural centre, widely recognized as a model for India’s cultural diplomacy abroad. A multidisciplinary scholar, author, and…
f: Guillermo Rodríguez is the Founding Director of Casa de la India, Spain’s pioneering Indian cultural centre, widely recognized as a model for India’s cultural diplomacy abroad. A multidisciplinary scholar, author, and cultural manager, he was awarded the Friendship Award by India’s Ministry of External Affairs in 2012 for his contribution to Indo-Spanish cultural relations. His publications include the critical study When Mirrors are Windows: A View of A.K. Ramanujan’s Poetics (2016) and edited volumes such as Journeys. A Poet’s Diary (2019), Soma. Poems by A.K. Ramanujan (2023), and The Making of Kijote Kathakali (2026), reflecting his deep engagement with literature and cross-cultural scholarship.

b: Gulab Kothari , Editor-in-Chief of Rajasthan Patrika , is a journalist, writer, poet, researcher and exponent of Ved Vijnana . His treatise Manas, runs in thirteen volumes and has been translated into twelve Indian…
f: Gulab Kothari , Editor-in-Chief of Rajasthan Patrika , is a journalist, writer, poet, researcher and exponent of Ved Vijnana . His treatise Manas, runs in thirteen volumes and has been translated into twelve Indian languages and English. It fathoms the infinite depths of the human psyche and gives us deep insights into human nature. His narrative poems include Adya, O My Mind and Tao of Spirituality . Kothari’s two recent seminal works, titled Samvad Upanishad and Akshar Yatra , are new feathers in his cap. He has been awarded D Lit honoris causa by Amity University Jaipur, Mohan Lal Sukhadia University Udaipur and Rajasthan Sanskrit University Jaipur and is the recipient of many prestigious awards, including Jnan Peeth’s Moorti Devi Award.

b: Gulabo Sapera , a legendary folk artist, not only conceptualised and choreographed the flamboyant dance style ‘kalbeliya’ but also got her nomadic community a never imagined recognition. Today, the dance form is one…
f: Gulabo Sapera , a legendary folk artist, not only conceptualised and choreographed the flamboyant dance style ‘kalbeliya’ but also got her nomadic community a never imagined recognition. Today, the dance form is one of the major features of the state of Rajasthan. Having faced numerous ups and downs both personally and professionally, she is now a visiting faculty at institutions in countries such as Denmark and France. She wishes to set up a dance school in Pushkar for her community. She has also taken up the cause of educating children in her community.In 2011, Sapera featured in reality television show Bigg Boss 5. She is a recipient of the Padma Shri Award and the Maharana Mewar Award.

b: Gulzar is a poet, filmmaker, lyricist and writer. Born in Jhelum, now in Pakistan, he spent his school days in Delhi and then came to Bombay, to a celebrated career in films. The poet in him flourished simultaneously;…
f: Gulzar is a poet, filmmaker, lyricist and writer. Born in Jhelum, now in Pakistan, he spent his school days in Delhi and then came to Bombay, to a celebrated career in films. The poet in him flourished simultaneously; he was closely associated with the Progressive Writers Movement. Many collections of poems, short stories and scripts have flowed from his pen. His creative repertoire also includes plays, ballets, music albums, serials as well as books for children. His works have been translated into many languages and received national and international acclaim. He is a seven-time recipient of the prestigious National Award as well as 21 Filmfare Awards. He won the 2002 Sahitya Akademi Award for Best Urdu Writer and was conferred the Padma Bhushan in 2004. He was awarded the 2009 Academy Award for Best Original Song (‘Jai Ho’ in Slumdog Millionaire ), the 27th Indira Gandhi National Integration Award in 2012, the Dada Saheb Phalke Award in 2013 as well as a degree of Doctor of Letters (Honoris Causa) from Rabindra Bharati, University of Kolkata in 2015.

b: Gunbir Singh is President of Dilbir Foundation; Chairperson of Punjab State for Worldwide Fund for Nature; Senator, Guru Nanak University; Financial Secretary, Khalsa College Charitable Society, Amritsar; and a…
f: Gunbir Singh is President of Dilbir Foundation; Chairperson of Punjab State for Worldwide Fund for Nature; Senator, Guru Nanak University; Financial Secretary, Khalsa College Charitable Society, Amritsar; and a prominent writer and columnist. He was Founder Chairman, Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) - Amritsar Zonal Council and Chairman of Eco Amritsar and CII-Punjab State. Singh has contributed significantly to environmental advocacy, natural farming outreach, citizens' wellness platforms, and awareness programmes for sustainable households. Singh led the CII delegation in 2010 with CM Punjab to Turkey, Egypt, Israel, and UAE, emphasising business and research for Punjab's development, particularly in water, environment, and agriculture. He also chaired the session on Trans-boundary Aquifers in the Indus Basin at the Indo-Pak Roundtable on Water in February 2014 as part of Track II diplomacy in Bengaluru. He has received prestigious awards like the Parman Patra for Service to Society and the Shri Anandpur Sahib Award for Service to Environment. He has written the book Biba The Ginger .

b: Guneet Monga is game-changing producer in Indian cinema who has been redefining the industry with diverse new-age projects, including award-winning and internationally celebrated films like The Lunchbox, Masaan and…
f: Guneet Monga is game-changing producer in Indian cinema who has been redefining the industry with diverse new-age projects, including award-winning and internationally celebrated films like The Lunchbox, Masaan and Gangs of Wasseypur . Monga is the youngest person to receive the ‘Most Powerful Women in Indian Business Award’ by Business Today in 2014 and was voted as one of the top 12 women achievers in the Global Entertainment Industry by The Hollywood Reporter . She had been inducted into the Producer’s Branch of the Academy of Motion Pictures Arts And Sciences and featured in Variety’ s International Women’s Impact Report 2018.

b: Gurcharan Das is the author of the trilogy: The Difficulty of Being Good; India Unbound; and Kama, the Riddle of Desire. He has also written a novel, A Fine Family, and an anthology, Three Plays. He studied philosophy…
f: Gurcharan Das is the author of the trilogy: The Difficulty of Being Good; India Unbound; and Kama, the Riddle of Desire. He has also written a novel, A Fine Family, and an anthology, Three Plays. He studied philosophy at Harvard and was CEO of Procter & Gamble India before becoming a full-time writer. He is general editor of Penguin’s 14 volume Story of Indian Business. His memoir, Another Sort of Freedom, has just been published by Penguin.

b: Gurmehar Kaur is a social activist who published her first book, Small Acts of Freedom, at JLF in 2018. In 2017, Kaur was listed by TIME magazine as a 'Next Generation Leader', a global listing of ten young men and…
f: Gurmehar Kaur is a social activist who published her first book, Small Acts of Freedom, at JLF in 2018. In 2017, Kaur was listed by TIME magazine as a 'Next Generation Leader', a global listing of ten young men and women making a difference in the world. Her second book, The Young and the Restless: Youth and Politics in India, was shortlisted for the Sahitya Akademi Yuva Puraskar in 2021.

b: Commodore Gurnam Singh (Retired), served in the Indian Navy from 1958-1995. He is a qualified marine and aircraft engineer who has been awarded the Nao Sena Medal (Gallantry) during 1971 Indo-Pak War, whilst serving in…
f: Commodore Gurnam Singh (Retired), served in the Indian Navy from 1958-1995. He is a qualified marine and aircraft engineer who has been awarded the Nao Sena Medal (Gallantry) during 1971 Indo-Pak War, whilst serving in INS Vikrant’s Sea Hawk jet fighter squadron. He has authored 11 books on 17 th -20 th century’s India, the freedom struggle and women’s education.

b: Guru Madhavan is the Norman R. Augustine Senior Scholar and Senior Director of Programs at the U.S. National Academy of Engineering. He is a prize-winning author of essays and books, including Applied Minds: How…
f: Guru Madhavan is the Norman R. Augustine Senior Scholar and Senior Director of Programs at the U.S. National Academy of Engineering. He is a prize-winning author of essays and books, including Applied Minds: How Engineers Think and Wicked Problems: How to Engineer a Better World .

b: Guru Prakash Paswan is the National Spokesperson of the Bharatiya Janta Party and an Assistant Professor at Patna University. He has been instrumental with the Dalit Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry since 2015…
f: Guru Prakash Paswan is the National Spokesperson of the Bharatiya Janta Party and an Assistant Professor at Patna University. He has been instrumental with the Dalit Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry since 2015 and has worked as National Youth coordinator and is presently working as an adviser. His columns keep appearing on Dalit issues in the Indian Express and The Print, among others. He has co-authored the book, Makers of Modern Dalit History with Sudarshan Ramabadran.

b: Guy Gunaratne’s first novel, In Our Made and Furious City , won the International Dylan Thomas Prize, the Jhalak Prize and the Club Best First Novel Award for 2019. It was longlisted for the Man Booker Prize and the…
f: Guy Gunaratne’s first novel, In Our Made and Furious City , won the International Dylan Thomas Prize, the Jhalak Prize and the Club Best First Novel Award for 2019. It was longlisted for the Man Booker Prize and the Orwell Prize for Political Fiction and was also shortlisted for the Goldsmiths Prize and the Gordon Burn Prize in 2018.

b: Géraldine Lenain is an art historian, working for more than twenty years on several continents as a specialist in Asian arts recognised internationally on the art market. She currently lives in India and is the wife of…
f: Géraldine Lenain is an art historian, working for more than twenty years on several continents as a specialist in Asian arts recognised internationally on the art market. She currently lives in India and is the wife of the French Ambassador to India. She has already published Monsieur Loo, The novel of an Asian art dealer.

b: Kevin Kelly is the Ambassador of Ireland to India. Prior to his appointment in September 2023, Ambassador Kelly was Head of Press and Communications at the Irish Department of Foreign Affairs. His previous appointments…
f: Kevin Kelly is the Ambassador of Ireland to India. Prior to his appointment in September 2023, Ambassador Kelly was Head of Press and Communications at the Irish Department of Foreign Affairs. His previous appointments include Ambassador to the Netherlands, Ambassador to Uganda & Rwanda and Special Envoy of the Government of Ireland to Africa for Ireland’s UN Security Council campaign. In 2021, Ambassador Kelly was elected by the Assembly of States Parties to the International Criminal Court as a Member of the Board of Directors of the Trust Fund for Victims and he still holds this position.

b: H.E. Vincenzo De Luca took office on 1 February 2016 as Director-General for Cultural and Economic Promotion and Innovation of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Government of Italy, after having served in the same…
f: H.E. Vincenzo De Luca took office on 1 February 2016 as Director-General for Cultural and Economic Promotion and Innovation of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Government of Italy, after having served in the same Directorate General as Deputy Director-General and Principal Director for the Internationalisation of the Italian Economic System (since January 2014). He has been a career diplomat since 1989 and has been given several assignments at the Foreign Ministry and at the diplomatic representations in Khartoum, Tunis, Paris and Shanghai. He has a long-standing expertise in the internationalisation of the economic system of the public and private sector, both in Central Offices, in the capacity of Diplomatic Advisor of the Ministries of Industry, Transports and Economic Development, and in large corporations like ENI and ENEL, where he served as Vice President for Institutional International Relations. During the past few years, he played a relevant role in the organisation of the EXPO Milano 2015 as President of the Foreign Ministry’s Task Force, capitalising on his experience as Consul General in Shanghai. He is serving as the Ambassador of Italy to India and Nepal since December 2019.

n: H.H. Gaj Singh, Maharaja of Jodhpur

b: Habiba Insaf is an art historian and an incoming doctoral student at Humboldt University, Berlin. Her research interest lies in the history of museums, in particular, questions of display and representation in…
f: Habiba Insaf is an art historian and an incoming doctoral student at Humboldt University, Berlin. Her research interest lies in the history of museums, in particular, questions of display and representation in ethnographic museums. She has held awards and fellowships of the Alexander von Humboldt Foundation, Singapore International Foundation and the Prince Claus Fund.

b: Haji Syed Salman Chishty is the 26th-generation Gaddi-Nashin (Hereditary Key Custodian) of the revered shrine of Sultan ul Hind, Hazret Khawaja Moinuddin Hasan Chishty (r.a.). Born on March 9, 1982, into the…
f: Haji Syed Salman Chishty is the 26th-generation Gaddi-Nashin (Hereditary Key Custodian) of the revered shrine of Sultan ul Hind, Hazret Khawaja Moinuddin Hasan Chishty (r.a.). Born on March 9, 1982, into the distinguished Chishty family of Ajmer Sharif, he carries forward a legacy deeply rooted in spirituality and Sufism. His lineage traces directly to the family of the Holy Prophet Muhammad (P.B.U.H) through his grandson, Hazret Syedna Imam Hussain (a.s.). Known for his humility and devotion, Haji Syed Salman Chishty continues to inspire spiritual seekers and uphold the centuries-old traditions of the Chishty Sufi order.

b: Hal Cazalet’s Play on Words pays homage to his step–great-grandfather P.G. Wodehouse, celebrating Wodehouse’s early Broadway career as the first lyricist of the American musical. The show has travelled from London’s…
f: Hal Cazalet’s Play on Words pays homage to his step–great-grandfather P.G. Wodehouse, celebrating Wodehouse’s early Broadway career as the first lyricist of the American musical. The show has travelled from London’s West End to the USA and on tour across the UK. A Juilliard graduate and Shoshana Foundation Award winner, Hal has created leading roles in world premieres by Philip Glass, Roxanna Panufnik and Tod Machover, performing at major venues including Santa Fe Opera, Lincoln Center, BAM and the Kennedy Center. UK credits include ENO, Glyndebourne GTO, Opera North and Wigmore Hall. He also composed the musical adaptation of Oscar Wilde’s The Happy Prince .

b: Hallie Rubenhold is a historian, broadcaster and historical consultant for TV and film. Her book, The Five: The Untold Lives of the Women Killed by Jack the Ripper, won the 2019 Baillie Gifford Prize for non-fiction.…
f: Hallie Rubenhold is a historian, broadcaster and historical consultant for TV and film. Her book, The Five: The Untold Lives of the Women Killed by Jack the Ripper, won the 2019 Baillie Gifford Prize for non-fiction. Her bestselling new book, Story of a Murder: The Wives, The Mistress and Dr Crippen , is a panoramic examination of the 1910 murder of American music hall performer, Belle Elmore. Hallie’s podcast, Bad Women , explores true crime through an ethical and feminist lens. Her earlier work, The Covent Garden Ladies , became the international hit TV series: Harlots .

b: Hamid Karzai was the president of Afghanistan from 2004-2014 and remains a prominent figure in Afghan politics. His father was the hereditary Khan (chief) of the Popalzai tribe in the Kandahar region. Karzai studied in…
f: Hamid Karzai was the president of Afghanistan from 2004-2014 and remains a prominent figure in Afghan politics. His father was the hereditary Khan (chief) of the Popalzai tribe in the Kandahar region. Karzai studied in Kabul and Simla, India in the 1970s. Tense relations with the ruling Taliban led to Karzai living in exile in Pakistan in the late 1990s but by October 2001, he was back in Afghanistan, playing a key role in the Taliban’s fall from power. He stepped into the position of interim president in 2002 and began a worldwide diplomatic effort to help rebuild Afghanistan’s government. Karzai became Afghanistan’s first popularly elected president in September 2004. He was elected to his second five-year term in 2009 after which which he stepped down and was succeeded by Ashraf Ghani.

b: Han Yujoo debuted in 2003 with her short story ‘To the Moon’, which won Literature and Society’s New Writers Award. She won the prestigious Hankook Ilbo Literary Award in 2009. She is the author of three…
f: Han Yujoo debuted in 2003 with her short story ‘To the Moon’, which won Literature and Society’s New Writers Award. She won the prestigious Hankook Ilbo Literary Award in 2009. She is the author of three collections of short stories, To the Moon, Book of Ice and My Left Hand the King My Right Hand the King’s Scribe . Her first novel, The Impossible Fairytale , was published in 2017.

b: Hanako Footman is a British-Japanese actor, author, and director. A LAMDA graduate, her screen and stage credits include The Crown , Mad House , and Crime 101 . Her debut novel, Mongrel , earned major award nominations,…
f: Hanako Footman is a British-Japanese actor, author, and director. A LAMDA graduate, her screen and stage credits include The Crown , Mad House , and Crime 101 . Her debut novel, Mongrel , earned major award nominations, and she recently completed her directorial debut, Emiko Jones . Her second novel will be published by Doubleday in 2028.

b: Hani Farsi founded MSFF in 2009 in tribute to his father, Dr. Mohamed S. Farsi, The Mohammed S. Farsi Foundation is dedicated to supporting initiatives in the arts, education, cultural awareness, and humanitarian…
f: Hani Farsi founded MSFF in 2009 in tribute to his father, Dr. Mohamed S. Farsi, The Mohammed S. Farsi Foundation is dedicated to supporting initiatives in the arts, education, cultural awareness, and humanitarian relief. The foundation work is a continuation of his father's values, aiming to build a more compassionate world and giving a voice to the most vulnerable

b: Hannah Curtis is a creative producer, curator, and project manager working across the fine art, literary, and ideas sectors. She is currently Associate Curator at the UNSW Centre for Ideas, where she develops…
f: Hannah Curtis is a creative producer, curator, and project manager working across the fine art, literary, and ideas sectors. She is currently Associate Curator at the UNSW Centre for Ideas, where she develops thought-provoking programs bringing together leading thinkers, writers, and academics from around the world. Previously, she spent four years as Head of International Program at the Ubud Writers & Readers Festival. With a background spanning creative and strategic practice, Hannah is known for dynamic programming, cross-sector collaboration, and a strong commitment to amplifying diverse voices. She combines creative vision with entrepreneurial thinking to deliver innovative programs that resonate with audiences and collaborators alike.

b: Hannah Kent is the co-founder and deputy editor of the Australian literary journal 'Kill Your Darlings' and is completing her PhD at Flinders University. In 2011, Kent won the inaugural Writing Australia Unpublished…
f: Hannah Kent is the co-founder and deputy editor of the Australian literary journal 'Kill Your Darlings' and is completing her PhD at Flinders University. In 2011, Kent won the inaugural Writing Australia Unpublished Manuscript Award. Burial Rites is her first novel.

b: Hanne Ørstavik was born in Tana, the furthermost north of Norway, in 1969. Her literary production, which consists of 13 novels, essays and articles, texts for theatre and traductions, is marked by its profound…
f: Hanne Ørstavik was born in Tana, the furthermost north of Norway, in 1969. Her literary production, which consists of 13 novels, essays and articles, texts for theatre and traductions, is marked by its profound investigation in language and form. She has received a row of awards and is translated into 26 languages.

b: Hans Jacob Frydenlund is currently the Norwegian Ambassador to India. Prior to this, he was the Director for UN Policy in the Norwegian Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Frydenlund has served in Chile, at the Norwegian…
f: Hans Jacob Frydenlund is currently the Norwegian Ambassador to India. Prior to this, he was the Director for UN Policy in the Norwegian Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Frydenlund has served in Chile, at the Norwegian Mission to the European Union in Brussels, at the Norwegian Mission to the United Nations in New York, and as the Norwegian Representative to the Palestinian Authority. An economist by education, he has worked for thirteen years in different capacities with conflict resolution in Africa. He has also served as the Press Spokesperson for International Development in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

b: Hansaji Yogendra is the Director of The Yoga Institute, Mumbai, the world’s oldest organised yoga center. She is also the Chairperson of Yoga Certification Committee for Quality Council of India, President of…
f: Hansaji Yogendra is the Director of The Yoga Institute, Mumbai, the world’s oldest organised yoga center. She is also the Chairperson of Yoga Certification Committee for Quality Council of India, President of International Board of Yoga and Senior Vice President Indian Yoga Association. Renowned as the First Lady of Yoga, Dr. Yogendra was the only female yoga guru to be invited by Prime Minister Narendra Modi at the first International Yoga Day in New Delhi. Recognising and honouring the philanthropic work done under Dr. Yogendra’s guidance, The Yoga Institute was awarded the prestigious Prime Minister’s Award for spreading the goodness of yoga to all. Dr. Yogendra was also honoured with the 2019 Bharat Gaurav Award for extraordinary contributions and excellence in the field of yoga.

b: Harbans Singh was born in Samba, in the Jammu region of Jammu and Kashmir. He began his career as a college professor before moving on to journalism. He has worked for the Observer of Business and Politics, The Tribune…
f: Harbans Singh was born in Samba, in the Jammu region of Jammu and Kashmir. He began his career as a college professor before moving on to journalism. He has worked for the Observer of Business and Politics, The Tribune and Dainik Bhaskar. Singh has authored books in both Hindi and English. His books include the monumental three-volume A Modern History of Jammu and Kashmir and (in Hindi) of Sufi Satta aur Samaj.

b: Hardeep Singh Puri has had a distinguished four-decade career in diplomacy spanning both the bilateral and the multilateral arena. He held Ambassadorial level posts in the United Kingdom, Brazil and as India’s…
f: Hardeep Singh Puri has had a distinguished four-decade career in diplomacy spanning both the bilateral and the multilateral arena. He held Ambassadorial level posts in the United Kingdom, Brazil and as India’s Permanent Representative to the United Nations in both Geneva and New York. He presided over the UN Security Council in August 2011 and November 2012, and chaired its Counter-Terrorism Committee. He is the author of Perilous Interventions: The Security Council and The Politics of Chaos . He is presently Union Minister of State for Housing and Urban Affairs.

b: Hari Kunzru is the author of five novels, including The Impressionist and White Tears . He was a 2008 Cullman Fellow at the New York Public Library, a 2014 Guggenheim Fellow and a 2015 Fellow of the American Academy in…
f: Hari Kunzru is the author of five novels, including The Impressionist and White Tears . He was a 2008 Cullman Fellow at the New York Public Library, a 2014 Guggenheim Fellow and a 2015 Fellow of the American Academy in Berlin. In 2014 he was made a fellow of the Royal Society of Literature.

b: Hari Ram Meena is a retired IPS officer, writer, and thinker. Nearly one and a half dozen of his books have been published in Hindi, spanning poetry, novels, travelogues, memoirs, and critical and discursive writings.…
f: Hari Ram Meena is a retired IPS officer, writer, and thinker. Nearly one and a half dozen of his books have been published in Hindi, spanning poetry, novels, travelogues, memoirs, and critical and discursive writings. He is widely known as a tribal thinker and an academic activist, engaging deeply with issues of identity, history, and social justice. Many of his literary works have been translated into English, Bengali, Punjabi, and Sanskrit. Through his writing and public engagement, Meena has made a significant contribution to contemporary Indian literature and tribal intellectual discourse.

b: HARINDER BAWEJA is a senior journalist and author. She has been reporting on current affairs, with a particular emphasis on conflict, for over four decades. Her journey has taken her through the battlefield of Punjab…
f: HARINDER BAWEJA is a senior journalist and author. She has been reporting on current affairs, with a particular emphasis on conflict, for over four decades. Her journey has taken her through the battlefield of Punjab and onwards to insurgency-ridden Jammu and Kashmir. She has also mapped various crises in Pakistan and was in Afghanistan when the Taliban first rode into Kabul in 1996. She has been honoured for her work and has won the prestigious Ramnath Goenka Award for excellence in journalism, the Prabha Dutt award, and the Haldighati award. She authored a book on Kargil, A Soldier’s Diary: Kargil the Inside Story , and edited and contributed to various anthologies, including two titled, 26/11: Mumbai Attacked and Most Wanted: Profiles of Terror .

b: Harinder Sidhu has held the post of Australia’s High Commissioner to India since February 2016. She also holds non-resident accreditation to the Kingdom of Bhutan. Sidhu brings over 30 years’ experience in…
f: Harinder Sidhu has held the post of Australia’s High Commissioner to India since February 2016. She also holds non-resident accreditation to the Kingdom of Bhutan. Sidhu brings over 30 years’ experience in government. She began her career as a diplomat with the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade. Between 2008 and 2013, Ms Sidhu held the post of First Assistant Secretary in the Department of Climate Change. Prior to that, she served in several senior roles in government, particularly on defence and national security matters. Sidhu has served overseas at Australian Embassies in Damascus, Moscow and Cairo.

b: Harinder Sikka is currently Group Director for Strategic Business at the Piramal Group. Prior to this, he served in the Indian Navy. Since then, he has produced the film
f: Harinder Sikka is currently Group Director for Strategic Business at the Piramal Group. Prior to this, he served in the Indian Navy. Since then, he has produced the film

b: Harini Rana, a dynamic sports media and management professional, made history as India's second female Sports Editor at Times Now before the age of 30. With a rich background covering major sports events globally,…
f: Harini Rana, a dynamic sports media and management professional, made history as India's second female Sports Editor at Times Now before the age of 30. With a rich background covering major sports events globally, including 5 Cricket World Cups, 2 Olympic Games, Wimbledon, and the Australian Open, she seamlessly transitioned to a leadership role in the business side of sports. Recognised for her contributions, she was appointed a Generation Equality Ally by UN Women India for Women in Sport and joined the International Cricket Council's Future Leaders Programme, focusing on empowering girls in leadership roles in world cricket. Rana’s influence extends beyond sports, as she was invited to address the UK Parliament at the House of Commons and Lords in celebration of Women's Day.

b: Hariprasad Chaurasia is one of India's most-respected classical musicians who has been honoured with several prestigious awards, including the National Award of the Sangeet Natak Academy, the Padma Bhushan, the Konarak…
f: Hariprasad Chaurasia is one of India's most-respected classical musicians who has been honoured with several prestigious awards, including the National Award of the Sangeet Natak Academy, the Padma Bhushan, the Konarak Samman, the Yash Bharati Sanman and the Padma Vibhushan, among others. He has collaborated with several western musicians, such as John McLaughlin and Jan Garbarek, and has composed music for many Indian films. His official biography, Woodwinds of Change by Surjit Singh, was released by veteran actor Amitabh Bachchan in 2008. Pt. Chaurasia has been conferred the title of OFFICER IN THE ORDER OF ORANGE-NASSAU by the Government of the Netherlands and appointed as KNIGHT IN THE ORDER OF ARTS AND LETTERS by the Ministry of Culture, the Republic of France. He heads the World Music Department at the Rotterdam Music Conservatory in The Netherlands.

b: Harish Bhat is a bestselling author, poet, columnist and marketer. Harish has authored six books, in genres spanning business history, marketing and fiction. His latest book, Restless Lives , is his first volume of…
f: Harish Bhat is a bestselling author, poet, columnist and marketer. Harish has authored six books, in genres spanning business history, marketing and fiction. His latest book, Restless Lives , is his first volume of poetry. Harish also writes popular columns for national newspapers. He has worked with the Tata group for 36 years, helping create and nurture many iconic brands. Last year, Forbes listed him as one of the world’s top ten most influential Chief Marketing Officers.

b: Harleen Singh is a writer and researcher focusing on the social and literary history of colonial Punjab and the North West Frontier Province, now Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in Pakistan. In 2014, Harleen began documenting the…
f: Harleen Singh is a writer and researcher focusing on the social and literary history of colonial Punjab and the North West Frontier Province, now Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in Pakistan. In 2014, Harleen began documenting the stories of Partition survivors, which led to the creation of ‘ The Lost Heer ’ Project in 2018, dedicated to uncovering the largely forgotten narratives of women in colonial Punjab. Based in Toronto, Harleen is currently researching the historical relationship between the twin cities of Lahore and Amritsar.

b: Harley Rustad is the author of Lost in the Valley of Death: A Story of Obsession and Danger in the Himalayas and Big Lonely Doug: The Story of One of Canada's Last Great Trees . He is a features editor at The Walrus…
f: Harley Rustad is the author of Lost in the Valley of Death: A Story of Obsession and Danger in the Himalayas and Big Lonely Doug: The Story of One of Canada's Last Great Trees . He is a features editor at The Walrus magazine and is originally from Salt Spring Island, British Columbia, Canada.

b: Harriet Hirshman is the Senior Commissioning Editor at Dead Ink Books in Liverpool, where she commissions and edits titles and manages production and rights. Her authors include Adam S. Leslie, Jordan Prosser, Alice…
f: Harriet Hirshman is the Senior Commissioning Editor at Dead Ink Books in Liverpool, where she commissions and edits titles and manages production and rights. Her authors include Adam S. Leslie, Jordan Prosser, Alice Evelyn Yang, Matt Hill, Tess Sharpe, Micheliny Verunschk, and Gerardo Sámano Cordova. She was recently shortlisted for Future Leader of the Year at the FutureBook Awards.

b: Harsh Mander is a human rights and peace worker, writer, columnist, researcher and teacher who works with survivors of mass violence, hunger, homeless persons and street children. He organises Karwan e Mohabbat for…
f: Harsh Mander is a human rights and peace worker, writer, columnist, researcher and teacher who works with survivors of mass violence, hunger, homeless persons and street children. He organises Karwan e Mohabbat for solidarity with families affected by hate violence. He convenes the India Exclusion Report. His books include Between Memory and Forgetting: Massacre and the Modi Years in Gujarat, Partitions of the Heart: Unmaking the Idea of India, Looking Away: Inequality, Prejudice and Indifference in New India, Fatal Accidents of Birth: Stories of Suffering, Oppression and Resistance, Ash in the Belly: India’s Unfinished Battle against Hunger and Unheard Voices: Stories of Forgotten Lives.

b: Harsh Mariwala is Chairman, Marico Limited, and the Chairman and Managing Director of Kaya Limited. Mariwala’s passion for innovation enthused him to establish the Marico Innovation Foundation in 2003 which works…
f: Harsh Mariwala is Chairman, Marico Limited, and the Chairman and Managing Director of Kaya Limited. Mariwala’s passion for innovation enthused him to establish the Marico Innovation Foundation in 2003 which works towards nurturing innovations in India. In 2012, Mariwala started ASCENT Foundation, a peer-learning entrepreneurial platform, and the Mariwala Health Initiative in 2015, with the philanthropic aim of giving back to society. He was recently named the EY Entrepreneur of the Year 2020 for India, the world’s most prestigious business award for entrepreneurs. Sharrp Ventures is the Family Office of the Harsh Mariwala Family.
