f: Imtiaz Ali is an Indian filmmaker, writer, and producer, raised in Jamshedpur. A graduate in English Literature from Hindu College, Delhi, he co-founded the college's dramatics society IBTIDA . Known for his contribution to Indian cinema, he later moved to Mumbai.

b: Indira Chandrasekhar is a scientist, fiction writer, literary curator, and the founder and principal editor of Out of Print, one of the primary platforms for short fiction bearing a connection to the Indian…
f: Indira Chandrasekhar is a scientist, fiction writer, literary curator, and the founder and principal editor of Out of Print, one of the primary platforms for short fiction bearing a connection to the Indian subcontinent. Her short stories appear in anthologies and literary journals across the world. Her collection of short stories, Polymorphism , was published by HarperCollins.

b: Indira Viswanathan Peterson is Professor Emerita at Mount Holyoke College. She has published widely on Sanskrit, Tamil and Marathi literature and the performing arts. Major translations include Poems to Siva: The Hymns…
f: Indira Viswanathan Peterson is Professor Emerita at Mount Holyoke College. She has published widely on Sanskrit, Tamil and Marathi literature and the performing arts. Major translations include Poems to Siva: The Hymns of the Tamil Saints and Arjuna and the Hunter: Bharavi’s Kiratarjuniya . She is currently working on monographs on the cultural innovations of Serfoji II of Tanjore, Kuravanji and south Indian dance dramas and a translation of the Tamil novel Tillana Mohanambal .

b: Indra K. Nooyi , former CEO and chairperson of PepsiCo, is one of the world’s most sought-after advisors to entrepreneurs, executives, and governments. A role model for women and immigrants, she is celebrated for her…
f: Indra K. Nooyi , former CEO and chairperson of PepsiCo, is one of the world’s most sought-after advisors to entrepreneurs, executives, and governments. A role model for women and immigrants, she is celebrated for her empowering messages on inclusivity. Nooyi has been awarded the Padma Bhushan and the U.S. State Department’s award for Outstanding American by Choice. She has also received 15 honorary degrees, including an honorary doctorate of humane letters from Yale.

b: Indrajit Roy is senior lecturer of Global Development Politics and co-director of the Interdisciplinary Global Development Centre at the University of York. He obtained his PhD at the University of Oxford. His research…
f: Indrajit Roy is senior lecturer of Global Development Politics and co-director of the Interdisciplinary Global Development Centre at the University of York. He obtained his PhD at the University of Oxford. His research on democracy and development has been recognised through several awards and grants. Indrajit leads an international consortium that explores the global politics of hope in our uncertain times.

b: Indran Amirthanayagam is a poet, editor, translator, publisher, YouTube host, and diplomat. He has authored 28 books and translations, writing in English, Spanish, French, Portuguese, and Haitian Creole. He served the…
f: Indran Amirthanayagam is a poet, editor, translator, publisher, YouTube host, and diplomat. He has authored 28 books and translations, writing in English, Spanish, French, Portuguese, and Haitian Creole. He served the United States on diplomatic assignments across Africa, Asia, Europe, and the Americas for thirty years. In 2020, he published three poetry collections in three languages. He edits Beltway Poetry Quarterly , writes for Haiti en Marche and El Acento , and hosts The Poetry Channel . Amirthanayagam has received fellowships from the Foundation for Contemporary Arts, NYFA, and the MacDowell Colony, and is the 2025 Matwaala Poet of Honor and 2022 IFLAC Word Poeta Mundial.

b: Indrani Baruah was born and brought up in the small oil town of Digboi in Assam. After finishing her schooling from Carmel Digboi, she went on to become the topper of her batch in English literature at Dibrugarh…
f: Indrani Baruah was born and brought up in the small oil town of Digboi in Assam. After finishing her schooling from Carmel Digboi, she went on to become the topper of her batch in English literature at Dibrugarh University. She has completed her Masters from Gauhati University and is currently an Indian Police Service officer posted in Assam.

b: Ira Mathur , an Indian-born West Indian journalist, won the 2023 OCM Bocas Prize for Nonfiction for her memoir Love The Dark Days , which traces her lineage to the last Begum of Bhopal and was listed by The Guardian as…
f: Ira Mathur , an Indian-born West Indian journalist, won the 2023 OCM Bocas Prize for Nonfiction for her memoir Love The Dark Days , which traces her lineage to the last Begum of Bhopal and was listed by The Guardian as one of the top memoirs of 2022.

b: Ira Mukhoty is the author of Daughters of the Sun: Empresses, Queens and Begums of the Mughal Empire , Heroines: Powerful Indian Women in Myth and History. Living in one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in…
f: Ira Mukhoty is the author of Daughters of the Sun: Empresses, Queens and Begums of the Mughal Empire , Heroines: Powerful Indian Women in Myth and History. Living in one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world, she developed an interest in the evolution of mythology and history, the erasure of women from these histories, and the continuing relevance this has on the status of women in India. She writes rigorously researched narrative histories that are accessible to the lay reader. Her most recent book is Akbar: The Great Mughal and she is currently working on a text around the women of the Mahabharata due to be released this year.

b: Irenosen Okojie ’s novel, Butterfly Fish , and short story collections, Speak Gigantular and Nudibranch , have won and been nominated for multiple awards. She was awarded an MBE For Services to Literature in 2021. She…
f: Irenosen Okojie ’s novel, Butterfly Fish , and short story collections, Speak Gigantular and Nudibranch , have won and been nominated for multiple awards. She was awarded an MBE For Services to Literature in 2021. She is the director and founder of the Black to the Future festival. Her new novel Curandera is published by Dialogue Books.

b: Irvine Welsh is the author of twelve novels including the international bestsellers Trainspotting, Porno, Filth, Glue, The Blade Artist, and most recently, Dead Men’s Trousers. Both Trainspotting and its sequel Porno…
f: Irvine Welsh is the author of twelve novels including the international bestsellers Trainspotting, Porno, Filth, Glue, The Blade Artist, and most recently, Dead Men’s Trousers. Both Trainspotting and its sequel Porno were adapted into iconic films by Danny Boyle.

b: Irving Finkel is Senior Curator in the Middle East Department of the British Museum, where he reads cuneiform inscriptions in Sumerian and Akkadian. He also works on traditional Indian board games, and is the author of…
f: Irving Finkel is Senior Curator in the Middle East Department of the British Museum, where he reads cuneiform inscriptions in Sumerian and Akkadian. He also works on traditional Indian board games, and is the author of The Ark before Noah and other works for adults and children. Finkel is the founder of the Great Diary Project, which rescues unwanted private diaries for the future.

b: Isabella Tree is an award-winning travel writer and author, married to the conservationist Charlie Burrell. Her latest book Wilding is the story of their daring experiment: the rewilding of 3,500 acres of degraded…
f: Isabella Tree is an award-winning travel writer and author, married to the conservationist Charlie Burrell. Her latest book Wilding is the story of their daring experiment: the rewilding of 3,500 acres of degraded farmland in south England. The astonishing explosion of wildlife at Knepp is changing the way we think about nature and how to bring it back.

b: Ishani Kar-Purkayastha is the author of The Dancing Boy . She has published a number of short stories and essays, including An Epidemic of Loneliness , which won The Lancet Wakley Prize. Her works also include The Sky…
f: Ishani Kar-Purkayastha is the author of The Dancing Boy . She has published a number of short stories and essays, including An Epidemic of Loneliness , which won The Lancet Wakley Prize. Her works also include The Sky is Always Yours in Too Asian, Not Asian Enough , and, most recently, Doctor in the House as part of The Wellcome Collection.

b: Ishrat Husain is a former governor of the State Bank of Pakistan and served as Dean and Director of the Institute of Business Administration, Karachi. Dr. Husain had a distinguished career at the World Bank for two…
f: Ishrat Husain is a former governor of the State Bank of Pakistan and served as Dean and Director of the Institute of Business Administration, Karachi. Dr. Husain had a distinguished career at the World Bank for two decades and was a member of the Mahathir Commission that developed Vision 2020 for the Islamic Development Bank (IDB). Husain is currently a member of the Middle East Advisory Group of the IMF, member of the President Advisory Council of the IDB, Convener of the Economic Advisory Council, Ministry of Finance and Member of the Advisory Council to the Minister for Planning, Development, and Reforms. A graduate of the Executive Development Programme—jointly sponsored by Harvard, Stanford and INSEAD— he was also Chairman of the World Economic Forum Global Advisory Council on Pakistan. Dr. Husain is the recipient of the 2013 Hilal-e- Imtiaz Award and the highest civilian award, the Nishan-e- Pakistan. His publications include Pakistan: The Economy of an Elitist State and Economic Management in Pakistan .

b: Ishtiaq Ahmed holds a PhD in Political Science from Stockholm University. He is Professor Emeritus of Political Science at Stockholm University. He is Honorary Senior Fellow at the Institute of South Asian Studies,…
f: Ishtiaq Ahmed holds a PhD in Political Science from Stockholm University. He is Professor Emeritus of Political Science at Stockholm University. He is Honorary Senior Fellow at the Institute of South Asian Studies, National University of Singapore where he worked as Senior Research Professor. He has taught winter semesters at the Lahore University of Management Sciences and at Government College University Lahore. He has published several books with a special focus on the politics of South Asia discussed in the context of regional and international relations. His research on the partition of the Punjab in 1947 won several national awards in Pakistan and his description of Pakistan as a garrison state is recognized as authoritative. His latest book is Jinnah: His Successes, Failures and Role in History.

b: Itirani Samanta a prominent figure in modern Odia creative writing and editor of Kadambini, a highly popular monthly magazine with a readership of over five million, has an extensive body of work, encompassing 25…
f: Itirani Samanta a prominent figure in modern Odia creative writing and editor of Kadambini, a highly popular monthly magazine with a readership of over five million, has an extensive body of work, encompassing 25 published books, that delve into the complexities of female psychology, exploring themes such as love, affection, sacrifice, self-esteem, and struggle. Demonstrating versatility and a perceptive writing style, she has presented an impressive collection of short stories, novels, essays, features, and translations.

b: Ivo de Figueiredo is a Norwegian historian and writer. He has written several critically acclaimed books, most notably the biographies of Henrik Ibsen and Edvard Munch, and a postcolonial family memoir, A Stranger at My…
f: Ivo de Figueiredo is a Norwegian historian and writer. He has written several critically acclaimed books, most notably the biographies of Henrik Ibsen and Edvard Munch, and a postcolonial family memoir, A Stranger at My Table . Figueiredo is recognized for his engaging style, which makes complex subjects accessible to a wider audience.

b: Ivy Ngeow is a Malaysian-born, London-based author who holds an MA in Writing from Middlesex University, where she won the 2005 Middlesex University Literary Press Prize. Her debut was awarded the International Proverse…
f: Ivy Ngeow is a Malaysian-born, London-based author who holds an MA in Writing from Middlesex University, where she won the 2005 Middlesex University Literary Press Prize. Her debut was awarded the International Proverse Prize 2017 in Hong Kong. The American Boyfriend , published by Penguin Random House, was longlisted for the Avon x Mushens Entertainment Prize for Commercial Fiction Writers of Colour 2022.

b: J. Nandakumar is a prominent thinker, writer, and public intellectual rooted in Bharatiya ethos and traditions. He currently serves as the All India Convener of Prajna Pravaha , a nationwide intellectual movement. Born…
f: J. Nandakumar is a prominent thinker, writer, and public intellectual rooted in Bharatiya ethos and traditions. He currently serves as the All India Convener of Prajna Pravaha , a nationwide intellectual movement. Born into a modest middle-class family in Kerala, he completed his Automobile Engineering degree in 1984 before dedicating his life to full-time RSS work as a Pracharak . A powerful orator, prolific writer, and noted Malayalam poet, he has contributed extensively to intellectual and cultural discourse. He also served for over five years as Chief Editor of Kesari Weekly, one of Kerala’s most respected Malayalam magazines.

b: J.J. Valaya is a part of the pioneering group of Indian fashion designers and one of the few who initiated the concept of fashion in modern India. He is a founding member on the Board of Governors of the FAshion Design…
f: J.J. Valaya is a part of the pioneering group of Indian fashion designers and one of the few who initiated the concept of fashion in modern India. He is a founding member on the Board of Governors of the FAshion Design Council and was the first official brand ambassador for Swarovski in India. A larger than life approach to luxury has been a distinguishing hallmark as has been his love for India. Alongside a successful career in fashion, Valaya has indulged in and fostered an increasing love for the visual arts. In 2011, he debuted ‘Decoded Paradox’, a show based on Delhi and its feudal past through a composition of portraiture that infused art, fashion and photography. In 2012, he presented his second show titled ‘The Soul in Space’, based on key architectural influences in his life. He is currently working on his third show slated for early 2018.

b: Prof Dr Jack Sim is founder of the World Toilet Organization, and created the UN World Toilet Day 19 Nov that was unanimously approved by all 193 countries at the UN General Assembly. Over the last 24 years, his Toilet…
f: Prof Dr Jack Sim is founder of the World Toilet Organization, and created the UN World Toilet Day 19 Nov that was unanimously approved by all 193 countries at the UN General Assembly. Over the last 24 years, his Toilet movement brought proper sanitation to 2.5 billion people. He was named Time Magazine Hero of the Environment in 2008.

b: Jackie Morris is an author and illustrator. She lives and works in a small cottage by the sea in Wales, UK with a chowder of cats and a pack of dogs. Her books include T he Unwinding, Mrs Noah’s Garden with James…
f: Jackie Morris is an author and illustrator. She lives and works in a small cottage by the sea in Wales, UK with a chowder of cats and a pack of dogs. Her books include T he Unwinding, Mrs Noah’s Garden with James Mayhew and The Lost Words and The Lost Spells with Robert Macfarlane.

b: Jaipur’s well-known publicist, Jagdeep Singh has had a stint in Journalism and teaching English Literature. His poems have been published in several poetry journals and magazines. Jagdeep's first collection of poems,…
f: Jaipur’s well-known publicist, Jagdeep Singh has had a stint in Journalism and teaching English Literature. His poems have been published in several poetry journals and magazines. Jagdeep's first collection of poems, ‘My Epitaph’, which was published in 2020, received widespread critical acclaim. It was recognised by the prestigious 'Journal of Commonwealth Literature' as one of the most interesting debut collections of Indo-English poetry in 2020-2021. He has recently published his second anthology ’When Gods Don’t Matter’. He is currently working on a novella as well as reminiscences of his school, Mayo College.

b: Jagdish Giri is an assistant professor at Rajasthan University as well as a poet and literary critic. He contributes regularly to literary journals. His published works include Mevat , a critique of the novel Kala…
f: Jagdish Giri is an assistant professor at Rajasthan University as well as a poet and literary critic. He contributes regularly to literary journals. His published works include Mevat , a critique of the novel Kala Pahad, and a book on the Bhakti movement titled Bhakti Andolan . His edited works include Kavita Ke Rang (parts two and three).

b: Jai Arjun Singh is an independent writer and critic. His books include The World of Hrishikesh Mukherjee , which won the MAMI Excellence in Writing on Cinema Award; Jaane bhi do Yaaro: Seriously Funny Since 1983 ; and…
f: Jai Arjun Singh is an independent writer and critic. His books include The World of Hrishikesh Mukherjee , which won the MAMI Excellence in Writing on Cinema Award; Jaane bhi do Yaaro: Seriously Funny Since 1983 ; and the anthology The Popcorn Essayists . He is currently working on a memoir centred on movie-watching.

b: Jaideep Hardikar is a Nagpur-based journalist, writer and researcher, and currently a Roving Reporter of the People’s Archive of Rural India. He is the author of A Village Awaits Doomsday published by Penguin India,…
f: Jaideep Hardikar is a Nagpur-based journalist, writer and researcher, and currently a Roving Reporter of the People’s Archive of Rural India. He is the author of A Village Awaits Doomsday published by Penguin India, and Ramrao: The Story of India’s Farm Crisis published by HarperCollins. Hardikar is working on his next book in the New India Foundation fellowship.

b: Jairam Ramesh is a Member of Parliament and Chairman of the Standing Committee on Science & Technology, Environment, Forests & Climate Change. He has been Union Minister of Commerce, Power, Environment & Forests,…
f: Jairam Ramesh is a Member of Parliament and Chairman of the Standing Committee on Science & Technology, Environment, Forests & Climate Change. He has been Union Minister of Commerce, Power, Environment & Forests, Drinking Water & Sanitation and Rural Development. He is the author of several well-known books, including Making Sense of Chindia , Green Signals: Ecology, Growth & Democracy in India, To The Brink & Back: India's 1991 Story, Indira Gandhi: A Life in Nature and Intertwined Lives: PN Haksar & Indira Gandhi . His latest book is A Chequered Brilliance: The Many Lives of VK Krishna Menon .

b: James Bradley is an acclaimed writer and critic, author of novels such as Wrack , The Resurrectionist , and Ghost Species . He has also published a poetry collection, Paper Nautilus , and a non-fiction work, Deep Water:…
f: James Bradley is an acclaimed writer and critic, author of novels such as Wrack , The Resurrectionist , and Ghost Species . He has also published a poetry collection, Paper Nautilus , and a non-fiction work, Deep Water: The World in the Ocean .

b: James Champion is a world traveller descended from celebrated natural historians, including a great-grandfather who described thousands of insect species and a grandfather who helped pioneer Indian wildlife photography…
f: James Champion is a world traveller descended from celebrated natural historians, including a great-grandfather who described thousands of insect species and a grandfather who helped pioneer Indian wildlife photography and conservation. Driven by this legacy, James dedicates his work to honouring and preserving his grandfather’s memory while exploring and documenting the natural world.

b: James Crabtree is an author and journalist living in Singapore. He is currently Associate Professor of Practice at the Lee Kuan Yew School of Public Policy. His book, The Billionaire Raj: A Journey Through India’s New…
f: James Crabtree is an author and journalist living in Singapore. He is currently Associate Professor of Practice at the Lee Kuan Yew School of Public Policy. His book, The Billionaire Raj: A Journey Through India’s New Gilded Age , was published in 2018.

b: James Fox is an art historian at the University of Cambridge and a multi-award-winning, BAFTA-nominated broadcaster. He is best known for his broadcasting work for BBC, including the television series, The Art of…
f: James Fox is an art historian at the University of Cambridge and a multi-award-winning, BAFTA-nominated broadcaster. He is best known for his broadcasting work for BBC, including the television series, The Art of Japanese Life and Age of the Image . His latest book, The World According to Colour: A Cultural History , was published by Allen Lane in October 2021.

b: James (Jim) Mallinson is the Boden Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Oxford. The primary focus of his research is the history of yoga, on which he has published extensively, including the anthology Roots of…
f: James (Jim) Mallinson is the Boden Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Oxford. The primary focus of his research is the history of yoga, on which he has published extensively, including the anthology Roots of Yoga . Jim has spent many years living with sadhus in India, and at the 2013 Kumbh Mela, was made a Mahant of the Ramanandi Sampradaya.

b: James Nestor is an author and journalist who has written for Scientific American, Outside, The New York Times, and more. His latest book, Breath: The New Science of a Lost Art, was released May 26, 2020, by…
f: James Nestor is an author and journalist who has written for Scientific American, Outside, The New York Times, and more. His latest book, Breath: The New Science of a Lost Art, was released May 26, 2020, by Riverhead/Penguin Random House and was an instant New York Times and London Sunday Times bestseller. Breath spent 18 weeks on the New York Times bestseller list in the first year of release and became a bestseller in Spain, Italy, Germany, and Croatia. Nestor has spoken at Stanford Medical School, Yale School of Medicine, Harvard Medical School, the United Nations and appeared on more than 60 radio and television shows, including 'Fresh Air' with Terry Gross, the Joe Rogan Show, and more.

b: Jamie Andrews leads Cultural and Learning Programming at the British Library and previously led the development of the Library’s literature collections. He has curated several exhibitions on literature and theatre,…
f: Jamie Andrews leads Cultural and Learning Programming at the British Library and previously led the development of the Library’s literature collections. He has curated several exhibitions on literature and theatre, led major international culture and research collaborative projects, and worked on a number of digital arts programmes. Andrews is a Fellow of the Clore Leadership Programme, a Trustee of Oxford House, a Trustee of the Forward Arts Foundation and a Judge of the 2019 Forward Prizes for Poetry.

b: Jamie O’Connell’s debut novel, Diving for Pearls, was published by Doubleday in June 2021. He was highly commended for the Costa Short Story Award 2018, short-listed for the Maeve Binchy Travel Award and the Sky…
f: Jamie O’Connell’s debut novel, Diving for Pearls, was published by Doubleday in June 2021. He was highly commended for the Costa Short Story Award 2018, short-listed for the Maeve Binchy Travel Award and the Sky Arts Futures Fund, and long-listed for BBC Radio 4 Opening Lines Short Story Competition.

b: Jan Carson is a writer and community arts facilitator based in Belfast, Northern Ireland. She has written a novel, Malcolm Orange Disappears, short story collection, Children’s Children, and a micro-fiction…
f: Jan Carson is a writer and community arts facilitator based in Belfast, Northern Ireland. She has written a novel, Malcolm Orange Disappears, short story collection, Children’s Children, and a micro-fiction collection, Postcard Stories . Her novel The Fire Starters is forthcoming in 2019.

b: Jan Grue is an author and a professor at the University of Oslo. His book, I Live a Life Like Yours , was published in 2018 in Norway, where it won the Critics Prize and was nominated for the Nordic Council Literature…
f: Jan Grue is an author and a professor at the University of Oslo. His book, I Live a Life Like Yours , was published in 2018 in Norway, where it won the Critics Prize and was nominated for the Nordic Council Literature Prize, the first Norwegian nonfiction book to be so honoured in fifty years.

b: Jan Stocklassa is a Swedish writer and journalist focusing on large-scale conspiracies in international politics. In his books, Stocklassa uses a narrative non-fiction style to unveil earlier unknown facts about…
f: Jan Stocklassa is a Swedish writer and journalist focusing on large-scale conspiracies in international politics. In his books, Stocklassa uses a narrative non-fiction style to unveil earlier unknown facts about important events in recent history. His breakthrough came with the critically acclaimed bestseller The Man Who Played with Fire , translated into 27 languages.

b: Jan Thompson served as Deputy High Commissioner/ Acting High Commissioner to India in August 2018, and before that was Ambassador to the Czech Republic. Her previous postings include Canada, Germany and New York.…
f: Jan Thompson served as Deputy High Commissioner/ Acting High Commissioner to India in August 2018, and before that was Ambassador to the Czech Republic. Her previous postings include Canada, Germany and New York. Thompson was also the UK's Lead Climate Change Negotiator. She likes travelling the world and is a semi-professional actress with a particular passion for Shakespeare

b: Janaki Bakhle is professor of history at the University of California, Berkeley. She is the author of Two Men and Music: Nationalism in the Making of a Classical Tradition , published by Oxford University Press, and…
f: Janaki Bakhle is professor of history at the University of California, Berkeley. She is the author of Two Men and Music: Nationalism in the Making of a Classical Tradition , published by Oxford University Press, and more recently Savarkar and the Making of Hindutva by Princeton University Press.

b: Janaki Lenin writes about wildlife science and conservation practice in India. She’s a full-time freelance journalist and the author of My Husband and Other Animals and A King Cobra’s Summer . Her latest book is My…
f: Janaki Lenin writes about wildlife science and conservation practice in India. She’s a full-time freelance journalist and the author of My Husband and Other Animals and A King Cobra’s Summer . Her latest book is My Husband and Other Animals 2: The Wildlife Adventure Continues .

b: Jane Ohlmeyer is Erasmus Smith's Professor of Modern History (1762) at Trinity College Dublin. In 2023 she received an Advanced ERC Grant for VOICES, a project on the lived experiences of women in early modern Ireland.…
f: Jane Ohlmeyer is Erasmus Smith's Professor of Modern History (1762) at Trinity College Dublin. In 2023 she received an Advanced ERC Grant for VOICES, a project on the lived experiences of women in early modern Ireland. Her latest book is Making Empire: Ireland, Imperialism and the Early Modern World (Oxford, 2023). In the same year, she was awarded the Royal Irish Academy Gold Medal in the Humanities. She is currently working with Bríona Ní Dhiarmada on a book titled From That Small Island: The Story of the Irish , based on a four-part documentary and feature film that won the Best International Documentary Award at the 2025 Newport Beach Film Festival.

b: Janice Pariat is the author of Boats on Land: A Collection of Short Stories and Seahorse: A Novel . She was awarded the Young Writer Award from the Sahitya Akademi and the Crossword Book Award for Fiction in 2013. Her…
f: Janice Pariat is the author of Boats on Land: A Collection of Short Stories and Seahorse: A Novel . She was awarded the Young Writer Award from the Sahitya Akademi and the Crossword Book Award for Fiction in 2013. Her novella The Nine Chambered-Heart was recently published and is forthcoming in the UK in May 2018. It is being translated for publication into six languages including Italian, Spanish, French, and German.

b: Professor Janina Ramirez is a best-selling author, Oxford lecturer and award-winning documentarian. Her book 'Femina: A New History of the Middle Ages Through the Women Written Out of It' was an instant Sunday Times…
f: Professor Janina Ramirez is a best-selling author, Oxford lecturer and award-winning documentarian. Her book 'Femina: A New History of the Middle Ages Through the Women Written Out of It' was an instant Sunday Times number 1 best-seller. She will be discussing her new book 'Legenda: The Real Women Behind the Myths That Shaped Europe'.

b: Jason Grunebaum is a writer and translator whose books include Uday Prakash’s The Girl with the Golden Parasol , The Walls of Delhi and, with Ulrike Stark, Manzoor Ahtesham’s The Tale of the Missing Man . His work…
f: Jason Grunebaum is a writer and translator whose books include Uday Prakash’s The Girl with the Golden Parasol , The Walls of Delhi and, with Ulrike Stark, Manzoor Ahtesham’s The Tale of the Missing Man . His work has been shortlisted for the DSC Prize in South Asian Literature, longlisted for the National Translation Award and awarded the Global Humanities Translation Prize, a National Endowment for the Arts Fellowship and a PEN/Heim Translation Grant. He teaches both Hindi and literary translation the University of Chicago.

b: Jaspreet Bindra is the Founder of the advisory firm Digital Matters. He is also a partner of Singularity University in India, a Digital Transformation and Technology Advisor to several companies as well as a leading…
f: Jaspreet Bindra is the Founder of the advisory firm Digital Matters. He is also a partner of Singularity University in India, a Digital Transformation and Technology Advisor to several companies as well as a leading speaker, author and teacher on the subject. Mint and SAP recognised Bindra with the inaugural Digitalist of the Year Award in 2017. His first book on digital transformation and technology is titled The Tech Whisperer.

b: Jassa Ahluwalia is an actor (Peaky Blinders) and created #BothNotHalf to express and explore his British-Punjabi identity. His TEDx talk has over six million views on social media. His BBC documentary Am I English? won…
f: Jassa Ahluwalia is an actor (Peaky Blinders) and created #BothNotHalf to express and explore his British-Punjabi identity. His TEDx talk has over six million views on social media. His BBC documentary Am I English? won an Asian Media Award. Both Not Half: A Radical New Approach to Mixed Heritage Identity, described by William Dalrymple as a brilliant, fresh and moving memoir, was published in 2024, for which Ahluwalia won Best Narrator at the Audio Production Awards.

b: Jatindra Kumar Nayak was educated at Ravenshaw College, Cuttack and Merton College, Oxford and retired as Professor of English, Utkal University in 2016. He won the KATHA Translation Award in 1997 and Hutch-Crossword…
f: Jatindra Kumar Nayak was educated at Ravenshaw College, Cuttack and Merton College, Oxford and retired as Professor of English, Utkal University in 2016. He won the KATHA Translation Award in 1997 and Hutch-Crossword Book Award in 2004. He was a member of the Raja Ram Mohun Ray Library Foundation, Department of Culture, Government of India. At present, he is Member, English Advisory Board, Sahitya Akademi. He is Editor-in-chief of margASIA. His English translation of classic Odia novels have been published by University of California Press, Oxford University Press and Penguin books. Recent publications include the co-edited South Asian Critical Discourse (Odia).

b: Javed Akhtar is a notable Indian poet, lyricist, screenwriter and political activist, currently the chairman and founding member of Muslims For Secular Democracy (MFSD), formed to oppose the regressive rituals of the…
f: Javed Akhtar is a notable Indian poet, lyricist, screenwriter and political activist, currently the chairman and founding member of Muslims For Secular Democracy (MFSD), formed to oppose the regressive rituals of the community and provide a liberal and progressive alternative. He has been one of the eleven members of Citizens For Justice And Peace along with Teesta Setalwad and others who took the Gujarat Government to Court for their complicity in the communal riots of 2002. Akhtar was nominated to Rajya Sabha as a Member of Parliament by the President of India in 2010, and is the architect of the Copyright Amendment Bill passed by both Houses of Indian Parliament, which after a long struggle, has finally given Copyright royalties to Writers and Music Directors. He was the Vice President of CISAC & the first Asian to be on its Governing Board. Akhtar has received countless awards and accolades for his inimitable contribution to Indian Cinema, including the prestigious Padma Shri & Padma Bhushan.

b: Jaya Bhattacharji Rose is an independent international publishing consultant associated with the industry since the early 1990s. She has written reports for Publishers Association and Livres Canada Book . Her articles…
f: Jaya Bhattacharji Rose is an independent international publishing consultant associated with the industry since the early 1990s. She has written reports for Publishers Association and Livres Canada Book . Her articles and interviews have been published in Frontline, The Book Review, The Hindu, Brunch, Scroll, Bookwitty.com, LOGOS , Kitaabnama , the Guardian , the Independent , BBC Radio and Radio France. Her blog has crossed 5.9 million visitors.

b: Jayant Kaikini is a Kannada writer, poet, playwright and lyricist. He has published 20 books so far. His most recently published work is No Presents Please : Mumbai Stories , which has also been translated into English.…
f: Jayant Kaikini is a Kannada writer, poet, playwright and lyricist. He has published 20 books so far. Ghoshal is a teacher and speaker of contemporary media science and is the author of several books written in Bengali, including the biography of West Bengal's chief minister, Mamata Banerjee.

b: Jayanti Naju Seth recently retired as Head of the Department of English, Jesus & Mary College after a career spanning forty years. Dr. Seth’s areas of interest are the modern novel as well as autobiographical writing.…
f: Jayanti Naju Seth recently retired as Head of the Department of English, Jesus & Mary College after a career spanning forty years. Dr. Seth’s areas of interest are the modern novel as well as autobiographical writing. Her reading of Irish literature began while studying at Trinity College, Dublin, and has continued up to the present. Her Masters at the University of Kent at Canterbury was specifically in 20th Century American and British Literature. She has edited and published two collections of essays on Shakespeare’s The Merchant of Venice and on Marquez’s Chronicle of a Death Foretold respectively.

b: Jayaprabha Menon is a danseuse with exceptional artistry, a versatile choreographer and an affectionate Guru to her disciples, she has notched a reputation non-pareil in the firmament of Indian classical dances. Her…
f: Jayaprabha Menon is a danseuse with exceptional artistry, a versatile choreographer and an affectionate Guru to her disciples, she has notched a reputation non-pareil in the firmament of Indian classical dances. Her performances of Mohiniyattam have been eloquent demonstrations of terpsichorean talents groomed by venerated Gurus like Kalamandalam Saraswathy, CV Chandrasekhar and Bharathy Shivaji. Her graceful nritta is phenomenal as one can discern the union of the dance and the dancer into a single entity. Her metamorphosis into the vivid characters on the stage speaks for her histrionic adroitness. Myriad are the choreographies that embrace both puranic and contemporary motifs and further they are quintessential of her insatiable urge to establish the intrinsic identity of the dance form peculiar to Kerala. They are also the end-results of her perennial search for the roots of the dance form. In this endeavour, she has been fortunate to enjoy the guidance of Padmabhushan Kavalam Narayana Panicker, an acclaimed authority of Sopana Sangeetham.

b: Jayapriya Vasudevan has more than 20 years experience of working in publishing. She is the co-founder of India’s first bookstore café in Bangalore. In 1997, she set up Jacaranda, India’s first-ever literary agency.…
f: Jayapriya Vasudevan has more than 20 years experience of working in publishing. She is the co-founder of India’s first bookstore café in Bangalore. In 1997, she set up Jacaranda, India’s first-ever literary agency. Over the years, the agency has grown and now represents a diverse list of authors from Singapore and across South East Asia and beyond. Vasudevan also runs a regular course at Bangalore’s world-famous writing programme. She was the Festival Director for the 2017 and 2018 editions of the Times Lit Fest in Bangalore.

Her students have made it to the most prestigious colleges around the world such as Stanford, Harvard, Yale, Princeton and Oxford, amongst others.

f: Jeffrey Gettleman , a Pulitzer Prize-winning author, is a foreign correspondent for The New York Times. He specialises in covering conflict and has written vivid reports from India, Pakistan, Iraq, Afghanistan, Somalia, Congo and more than eighty other countries. Gettleman served as Bureau Chief in New Delhi and Nairobi, among other places. He studied philosophy at Cornell University before winning a Marshall Scholarship to study Anthropology at Oxford. He is the author of Love, Africa: A Memoir of Romance, War and Survival.

f: Jesús Ruiz Mantilla (Santander, Spain, 1965) is a writer and journalist with nearly twenty published books and a distinguished career at El País . He is also the author of notable works such as Papel , El encuentro , Ahogada en llamas , Gordo , and several music-focused books, including Preludio , Yo, Farinelli, el capón , Contar la música , and Divos . f: Jitendra Kumar Soni is an Indian civil servant, writer and translator. He writes in both Hindi and Rajasthani and his poems include Umeedon ke Chirag and Rankhaar. He has been honoured with the Sahitya Akademi Yuva Puraskar, the Kaka Kalelkar Rashtreey Protsahan Samman 2021 and also the Uttam Jeevan Raksha Padak for saving eight lives in the flood of 2016.

f: General JJ Singh , former Governor of Arunachal Pradesh, is a highly decorated army general with over 48 years contribution to nation-building who was Chief of Army Staff. He is a distinguished international personality, an author and a public speaker with vast experience. He has a strategic perspective on foreign policy and defence relations. Endowed with a vision for strategic defence relations, the defence industry and modernisation of the defence forces, he has contributed significantly towards the evolution of our national defence and security policy.

b: Jo Lendle is a writer and publisher. After studying cultural science and literature in Hildesheim and Montreal, he joined the German Literature Institute in Leipzig, edited the literary magazine Edit and has been a…
f: Jo Lendle is a writer and publisher. He started working as an editor for German literature at DuMont publishing house in 1997 and became publisher in 2010. Since 2014, Lendle is publisher of the Hanser publishing group. His literary work includes four novels, a story collection, translations and a children’s book. Seagull Press published the English edition of his novel All the Land in 2019.

Now living in London, he writes a blog on South Asia current affairs called ‘Riding the Elephant’, and is on the editorial board of the Commonwealth’s Round Table magazine.

A new updated edition of his prize-winning book, IMPLOSION: India’s Tryst with Reality, reviewing the Narendra Modi years, has been published. He writes a blog on South Asia current affairs called ‘Riding the Elephant’ that also appears on the website of Asia Sentinel (Hong Kong). He has also written, among others, for The Economist, Fortune magazine and the New Statesman .

b: John Guy is the senior curator of the Arts of South and Southeast Asia at The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York, an elected Fellow of the American Academy of Arts and Sciences, and of the Society of Antiquaries,…
f: John Guy is the senior curator of the Arts of South and Southeast Asia at The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York, an elected Fellow of the American Academy of Arts and Sciences, and of the Society of Antiquaries, London. Formerly curator of Indian Art at the V&A Museum London, he has curated numerous international art exhibitions and published widely, including ‘Woven Cargoes’ (1997), ‘Indian Temple Sculpture’ (2007), ‘Interwoven Globe’ (2013), ‘Lost Kingdoms: Hindu-Buddhist Sculpture of Early Southeast Asia’ (2014) and ‘Art & Independence: Y.G. Srimati and the Indian Style’ (2019).

b: John J. Mearsheimer is the R. Wendell Harrison Distinguished Service Professor of Political Science at the University of Chicago, where he has taught since 1982. He graduated from West Point, has a PhD in political…
f: John J. Mearsheimer is the R. Wendell Harrison Distinguished Service Professor of Political Science at the University of Chicago, where he has taught since 1982. He graduated from West Point, has a PhD in political science from Cornell University and has written extensively about security issues and international politics. Among his six books, The Tragedy of Great Power Politics won the Joseph Lepgold Book Prize while The Israel Lobby and U.S. Foreign Policy (with Stephen M. Walt) made the New York Times bestseller list and has been translated into 24 languages. His latest book is The Great Delusion: Liberal Ideals and International Realities , which won the 2019 Best Book of the Year Award from the Valdai Discussion Conference, Moscow. He has written numerous articles and op-eds that have appeared in International Security, London Review of Books, Foreign Affairs, The Financial Times , and The New York Times . In 2003, he was elected to the American Academy of Arts and Sciences, and in 2020, he won the James Madison Award, which is given once every three years by the American Political Science Association to ‘an American political scientist who has made a distinguished scholarly contribution to political science.’

b: John Lanchester’s five novels and four works of nonfiction have won numerous prizes and been translated into 30 languages. He is a regular contributor to The New Yorker and the London Review of Books.
f: John Lanchester’s five novels and four works of nonfiction have won numerous prizes and been translated into 30 languages. He is a regular contributor to The New Yorker and the London Review of Books.

b: John Micklethwait is the Editor-in-Chief of Bloomberg where he oversees editorial content across all Bloomberg platforms, including its news, newsletters, magazines, opinion, television, radio and digital properties, as…
f: John Micklethwait is the Editor-in-Chief of Bloomberg where he oversees editorial content across all Bloomberg platforms, including its news, newsletters, magazines, opinion, television, radio and digital properties, as well as its research services including Bloomberg Intelligence. Prior to joining Bloomberg in February 2015, Micklethwait was Editor-in-Chief of The Economist where he led the newspaper into the digital age while expanding its readership and enhancing its reputation. He joined The Economist in 1987 as a finance correspondent and served as Business editor and United States editor before being named Editor-in-Chief in 2006. Micklethwait began his career in banking at Chase Manhattan in London after studying history at Magdalen College, Oxford. He is the co-author of seven books, most recently The Wake Up Call: Why the Pandemic Has Exposed the Weakness of the West, and How to Fix It . In 2010, Micklethwait was named Editors’ Editor by the British Society of Magazine Editors.

b: John Vaillant is an award-winning author and journalist whose work has appeared in The New Yorker , The Atlantic , and National Geographic . His most recent book, Fire Weather: On the Front Lines of a Burning World ,…
f: John Vaillant is an award-winning author and journalist whose work has appeared in The New Yorker , The Atlantic , and National Geographic . His most recent book, Fire Weather: On the Front Lines of a Burning World , was a finalist for the Pulitzer Prize and the U.S. National Book Award, and was named one of the ten best books of 2023 by The New York Times . It also won Britain's Baillie Gifford Prize and Canada's Shaughnessy-Cohen Prize.

b: John Zubrzycki is the author most recently of The House of Jaipur, which tells the inside story of India’s most glamorous royal family. His other books are Jadoowallahs, Jugglers and Jinns, which traces the evolution…
f: John Zubrzycki is the author most recently of The House of Jaipur, which tells the inside story of India’s most glamorous royal family. His other books are Jadoowallahs, Jugglers and Jinns, which traces the evolution of India’s conjuring traditions, The Last Nizam: The Rise and Fall of India’s Greatest Princely State and The Mysterious Mr Jacob: Diamond Merchant, Magician and Spy. A former Deputy Foreign Editor at The Australian newspaper, he has worked in India as a foreign correspondent and diplomat. He has a PhD in Indian history from the University of NSW.

She is the author of Celestial Bodies , the first Arabic-language novel to win the Man Booker International Prize, among other works.

His books include, Che Guevara: A Revolutionary Life, The Fall of Baghdad, The Lion’s Grave: Dispatches from Afghanistan and Guerrillas: Journeys in the Insurgent World .

b: Jonaki Ray is a scientist by education and training, and now a poet, writer, and editor in New Delhi. Honours for her work include 2018 Pushcart and Forward Prize for Best Single Poem nominations, as well the 2019…

Honours for her work include 2018 Pushcart and Forward Prize for Best Single Poem nominations, as well the 2019 Iceland Writers Retreat Alumni Award. Her poetry and essays have been published in Poetry, Poetry Wales, The Rumpus, Indian Literature, The Indian Express, Hindustan Times, and elsewhere. She is the author of Firefly Memories and Lessons in Bending.

f: Jonas Larsson is the Chairman of IPA Sweden. For many years, he has been active in several Swedish organizations working for children’s rights, a child’s right to play and the importance of reading for and with children. In 2017, he was appointed as the secretary to the IPA World Board.

f: Jonathan Franzen is the author of five novels- Purity, Freedom, The Corrections, The Twenty-Seventh City , and Strong Motion , and five works of non-fiction and translation, including Farther Away, How to Be Alone, and The Discomfort Zone . f: Jonathan Freedland is a Guardian columnist and presenter of BBC Radio 4’s contemporary history series, The Long View . He is a past winner of an Orwell Prize for journalism and the author of 12 books, the latest being The Escape Artist: The Man Who Broke Out of Auschwitz to Warn the World , which became a New York Times bestseller.

f: Jonathan Kennedy is the Director Arts India, British Council, is responsible for developing the international arts and culture strategy with the UK and India. From 2007–to 2019, he was Executive Director of Tara Arts, contributing significantly to the capital development of Tara Theatre and leadership of the Black Theatre Live national touring consortium. Before Tara Arts, Kennedy was Arts Programmes Manager of Croydon Clocktower and Head of Studio and Programme Development at Wimbledon Theatre. In the UK, he was a guest lecturer at Birkbeck College, South Bank University, Goldsmiths, King’s College London and St Mary’s University of Minnesota.

f: Jonathan Phillips is Professor of Crusading History at Royal Holloway, University of London. His works are widely translated. Phillips has also presented many radio and television programmes including The Cross and the Crescent and The Road From Christ to Constantine.

f: Jonathan Reeder, a native of New York and longtime resident of Amsterdam, enjoys a dual career as a literary translator and performing musician. Alongside his work as a professional bassoonist he translates opera libretti and essays on classical music, as well as contemporary Dutch fiction by authors including Peter Buwalda, Bram Dehouck, Christine Otten and Rodaan Al Galidi. Jonathan Safran Foer is the author of three award-winning and internationally best-selling novels: Everything Is Illuminated, Extremely Loud and Incredibly Close and Here I Am as well as two works of nonfiction: Eating Animals and The New American Haggadah. His most recent book, We Are the Weather: Saving the Planet Begins at Breakfast, was published in September 2019.

f: Jos Gommans is the Professor of Colonial and Global History at Leiden University in The Netherlands. b: Josef Wirsching studied Visual Communications at Loyola College, Chennai, along with his younger brother Georg but did not follow its path into the creative realm of art and media. He took an alternate route and has…
f: Josef Wirsching studied Visual Communications at Loyola College, Chennai, along with his younger brother Georg but did not follow its path into the creative realm of art and media. He took an alternate route and has been studying massage and healing therapies for 27 years from various systems. He has also been apprenticed to masters of Ayurveda and Kalaripayattu, an ancient form of Martial Art, from Kerala. During his study, he was initiated into several ancient Ayurvedic systems of healing and Yoga and has been working as a therapist and Ayurvedic practitioner in Goa since 2006. He also helps Georg manage and promote 'Wirsching Enterprises'.

b: Josefine Klougart is a writer living in Copenhagen. She has studied Art and Literature at Aarhus University and graduated from The Danish Academy of Creative Writing in 2010. In 2017, she was guest professor at the…
f: Josefine Klougart is a writer living in Copenhagen. She has studied Art and Literature at Aarhus University and graduated from The Danish Academy of Creative Writing in 2010. In 2017, she was guest professor at the University of Bern in Switzerland. Klougart has published five novels and three short prose books. She has also worked on a number of collaborative projects with artists such as Olafur Eliasson. Her work has been translated into 12 languages. Her latest book, New Forest , was published in Denmark in November 2016.

b: Joseph E. Stiglitz is an American economist and a professor at Columbia University. He is also the co-chair of the High-Level Expert Group on the Measurement of Economic Performance and Social Progress at the OECD and…
f: Joseph E. Stiglitz is an American economist and a professor at Columbia University. He is also the co-chair of the High-Level Expert Group on the Measurement of Economic Performance and Social Progress at the OECD and the Chief Economist of the Roosevelt Institute.

b: Joseph Sassoon is the director of the Center for Contemporary Arab Studies and Professor of History and Political Economy at Georgetown University. He holds the al-Sabah Chair in Politics and Political Economy of the…
f: Joseph Sassoon is the director of the Center for Contemporary Arab Studies and Professor of History and Political Economy at Georgetown University. He holds the al-Sabah Chair in Politics and Political Economy of the Arab World. He is also a Senior Associate Member at St Antony’s College, Oxford. In 2013, his book Saddam Hussein’s Ba‘th Party: Inside an Authoritarian Regime won the prestigious British-Kuwait Prize for the best book on the Middle East. Sassoon completed his Ph.D at St Antony’s College, Oxford. He has published extensively on Iraq and its economy and on the Middle East. His latest book which was published in February 2022 by Allen Lane (Penguin) is titled: The Global Merchants: The Enterprise and Extravagance of the Sassoon Dynasty .

b: Josephine Quinn holds the Chair in Ancient History at the University of Cambridge. She has been a Fellow at the Getty Villa and the Cullman Center for Scholars and Writers at the New York Public Library. Her books…
f: Josephine Quinn holds the Chair in Ancient History at the University of Cambridge. She has been a Fellow at the Getty Villa and the Cullman Center for Scholars and Writers at the New York Public Library. Her books include In Search of the Phoenicians (2018) and How the World Made the West (2024).

b: Joshua Ferris is the bestselling author of three novels and a collection of short stories, The Dinner Party. He has been a finalist for the National Book Award, winner of the Barnes and Noble Discover Award and the…
f: Joshua Ferris is the bestselling author of three novels and a collection of short stories, The Dinner Party. He has been a finalist for the National Book Award, winner of the Barnes and Noble Discover Award and the PEN/Hemingway Award, short-listed for the Man Booker Prize, winner of the International Dylan Thomas Prize, and was named one of The New Yorker's ‘20 Under 40’ writers in 2010.

b: Joshua Pollock , a dynamic advocate for meditation, is co-author of the bestselling book, The Heartfulness Way , translated into fifteen languages. Joshua has led seminars at institutions such as Amazon, Google, The New…
f: Joshua Pollock , a dynamic advocate for meditation, is co-author of the bestselling book, The Heartfulness Way , translated into fifteen languages. Joshua has led seminars at institutions such as Amazon, Google, The New York Times , Indian Institute of Technology, Mumbai, and Columbia University, and has been featured on ABC, NBC, and CBS television. As a classical violinist, he has performed internationally and collaborated with composer A R Rahman on seven original film scores.

b: Author, screenwriter, webtoon producer, and entrepreneur, Josselin began his career in 1996 within the comic fanzine scene. He later created Nekowear, the first European brand dedicated to anime culture. After…
f: Author, screenwriter, webtoon producer, and entrepreneur, Josselin began his career in 1996 within the comic fanzine scene. He later created Nekowear, the first European brand dedicated to anime culture. After co-founding Minte in India, he became a pioneering French webtoon author and producer, collaborating with Naver France and Ankama. In 2025, he founded Akogée Studio to develop original transmedia IPs built on a webtoon-driven storytelling strategy.

b: Jovan Mays is the Emeritus Poet Laureate of Aurora, Colorado, a National Poetry Slam Champion, curator of A Story, a student narrative project in Aurora Public Schools, a TED Speaker and Director of Your Writing Counts,…
f: Jovan Mays is the Emeritus Poet Laureate of Aurora, Colorado, a National Poetry Slam Champion, curator of A Story, a student narrative project in Aurora Public Schools, a TED Speaker and Director of Your Writing Counts, a youth poetry programme throughout the Denver Metro that engages over 200,000 students annually.

b: Joya Chatterji is a Fellow of Trinity College, Cambridge, Emeritus Professor of South Asian History at the University of Cambridge and sometime Reader in International History at the London School of Economics. From…
f: Joya Chatterji is a Fellow of Trinity College, Cambridge, Emeritus Professor of South Asian History at the University of Cambridge and sometime Reader in International History at the London School of Economics. From 2010 to 2021, she was first Editor then Editor-in-Chief of Modern Asian Studies, a leading scholarly journal in the field. Between 2014 and her retirement in 2019, she was Director of the Centre of South Asian Studies at Cambridge. She was elected a Fellow of the British Academy in 2018.

b: Juan Antonio March Pujol is a Spanish career diplomat with an extensive trajectory in bilateral and multilateral affairs. He currently serves as Ambassador of Spain to India, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Bhutan, and Maldives. His…
f: Juan Antonio March Pujol is a Spanish career diplomat with an extensive trajectory in bilateral and multilateral affairs. He currently serves as Ambassador of Spain to India, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Bhutan, and Maldives. His previous ambassadorial posts include the Embassies of Spain in the Russian Federation, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan, Belarus, and Armenia, as well as Spain’s Permanent Mission to the United Nations and the World Trade Organization in Geneva, where he chaired the Disarmament Conference, the WTO Finance Committee, and the Council of the International Organization for Migration. Earlier in his career, he served as Political Counsellor in Mexico and the United Kingdom, and held directive responsibilities in Spain’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Latin American and development cooperation affairs.

b: Judy Lief is a Buddhist teacher who trained under the Tibetan meditation master, Ven. Chögyam Trungpa Rinpoche. She has edited many of Trungpa Rinpoche’s books, including Milarepa: Lessons from the Life and Songs…
f: Judy Lief is a Buddhist teacher who trained under the Tibetan meditation master, Ven. Chögyam Trungpa Rinpoche. She has edited many of Trungpa Rinpoche’s books, including Milarepa: Lessons from the Life and Songs Tibet’s Great Yogi and his three-volume Profound Treasury of the Ocean of Dharma . She is the author of Making Friends with Death: A Buddhist Guide to Encountering Mortality .

b: Juergen Boos trained as a publisher at Herder Verlag in the early 1980s and has degrees in both Marketing and Organisational Theory. He became President and CEO of the Frankfurt Book Fair in 2005. He is also President…
f: Juergen Boos trained as a publisher at Herder Verlag in the early 1980s and has degrees in both Marketing and Organisational Theory. He became President and CEO of the Frankfurt Book Fair in 2005. He is also President of LITPROM (Society for the Promotion of African, Asian and Latin American Literature) and Managing Director of LitCam (Frankfurter Buchmesse Literacy Campaign). In 2013, he was awarded the Austrian Cross of Honor for Science and Art. Boos is also a recipient of France’s Chevalier des Arts et des Lettres. He is a member of the Scientific Committee of Sheikh Zayed Book Award and the German Book Prize Academy.

b: Julia Donaldson is the prize-winning author of some of the world’s best-loved children’s books, including modern classics The Gruffalo and The Gruffalo’s Child , which together have sold over 17 million copies…
f: Julia Donaldson is the prize-winning author of some of the world’s best-loved children’s books, including modern classics The Gruffalo and The Gruffalo’s Child , which together have sold over 17 million copies worldwide, and the hugely successful What the Ladybird Heard adventures. Donaldson also writes fiction, including the Princess Mirror-Belle books illustrated by Lydia Monks, as well as poems, plays and songs. She was the UK Children’s Laureate 2011-13 and has been honoured with an MBE for Services to Literature.

b: Julia Lovell is Professor of Modern China at Birkbeck College, University of London. She is the author of Maoism: A Global History (2019 Cundill History Prize), and The Opium War (2012 Jan Michalski Prize). Her many…
f: Julia Lovell is Professor of Modern China at Birkbeck College, University of London. She is the author of Maoism: A Global History (2019 Cundill History Prize), and The Opium War (2012 Jan Michalski Prize). Her many translations of modern Chinese fiction into English include The Real Story of Ah Q and Monkey King.

b: Juliet Nicolson ’s two works of history bookend the First World War, The Perfect Summer: 1911 and The Great Silence: 1918-1920 . Her most recent book, A House Full of Daughters , a memoir, draws on seven generations…
f: Juliet Nicolson ’s two works of history bookend the First World War, The Perfect Summer: 1911 and The Great Silence: 1918-1920 . Her most recent book, A House Full of Daughters , a memoir, draws on seven generations of daughters within her family. She has two daughters and a grand-daughter of her own.

b: Jung Chang is the author of Wild Swans: Three Daughters of China , which has sold more than 15 million copies worldwide with the exception of China, where it is banned, as are all of her other books. She wrote a…
f: Jung Chang is the author of Wild Swans: Three Daughters of China , which has sold more than 15 million copies worldwide with the exception of China, where it is banned, as are all of her other books. She wrote a ground-breaking trilogy on the history and personalities of modern China: Mao: The Unknown Story , which was described by Time magazine as “an atom bomb of a book”. Her books have been translated into more than 40 languages. She has won many awards, including the UK Writers’ Guild Best Non-Fiction and Book of the Year UK, and has received honorary doctorates from a number of universities in the UK and USA. She has been awarded a CBE (Commander of the Order of the British Empire) for services to literature and to history. During the Chinese Cultural Revolution, Jung Chang worked as a peasant, a “barefoot” doctor, a steelworker, and an electrician, in the Sichuan Province, before becoming an English-language student at Sichuan University. Her latest book is, Fly, Wild Swans: My Mother, Myself and China .

b: Juri Baruah born at Dinjan, located in Upper Assam in 1990. Currently she is pursuing PhD from TISS, Guwahati campus, and working as an Assistant Professor of Geography in DCB Girls’ College. She published two short…
f: Juri Baruah born at Dinjan, located in Upper Assam in 1990. Currently she is pursuing PhD from TISS, Guwahati campus, and working as an Assistant Professor of Geography in DCB Girls’ College. She published two short story collections. Her stories are translated to English, Hindi and Bengali.

b: Justice DY Chandrachud has served the Bombay High Court; Allahabad High Court and Supreme Court. His judgments dealt with free speech, gender equality, electoral bonds, climate change, disability, prison reform, and…
f: Justice DY Chandrachud has served the Bombay High Court; Allahabad High Court and Supreme Court. His judgments dealt with free speech, gender equality, electoral bonds, climate change, disability, prison reform, and social justice. His notable dissents were in the Aadhar, marriage equality, and Bhima Koregaon cases.

f: Justice R.S. Chauhan has worked as an Advocate for eighteen years, and served as Judge for seventeen years, including almost three years as a Chief Justice of Telangana and Uttarakhand High Courts. A keen artist and art historian, Justice Chauhan has delivered various lectures on Indian and Western Art History.

b: Jutta Jain-Neubauer is an art historian who has been researching India’s water monuments more than three decades now. Her book The Stepwells of Gujarat in Art: Historical Perspective is considered a pioneering work on…
f: Jutta Jain-Neubauer is an art historian who has been researching India’s water monuments more than three decades now. Her book The Stepwells of Gujarat in Art: Historical Perspective is considered a pioneering work on the subject. Her current research focuses on various genres of water architecture, their structural and aesthetic figurations, cultural and political contexts, surrounding rural and urban topographies and ecological siting, which resulted in her recent edited book Water Design. Environment and Histories .

b: Jyoti Gupta is a media activist and founder of The Colo(u)rism Project. Her latest project is an activity book that introduces skin colour to children in a healthy way. In her spare time, she dreams of making a dent in…
f: Jyoti Gupta is a media activist and founder of The Colo(u)rism Project. Her latest project is an activity book that introduces skin colour to children in a healthy way. In her spare time, she dreams of making a dent in the skin-lightening industry through her work. Gupta has a BFA in applied art (visual communication) from New Delhi and an MA in media studies from New York.

b: Jyoti Kiran Shukla is the first woman to chair the State Finance Commission. She holds the rank of a State Minister in Rajasthan. An accomplished economist of national repute, she has made remarkable contributions as a…
f: Jyoti Kiran Shukla is the first woman to chair the State Finance Commission. She holds the rank of a State Minister in Rajasthan. An accomplished economist of national repute, she has made remarkable contributions as a professor, researcher and advisor to various ministries. She has written extensively on development, policy research, employment, polity and gender. She has four books and more than 100 research papers are to her credit. An eloquent speaker, she was the official spokesperson of BJP Rajasthan for nearly seven years.

b: Jyoti Malhotra is Editor, National and Strategic Affairs of The Print news portal, based in NEw Delhi. She has been a journalist for 35 years and writes on the overlap between foreign affairs and politics, as well as…
f: Jyoti Malhotra is Editor, National and Strategic Affairs of The Print news portal, based in NEw Delhi. She has been a journalist for 35 years and writes on the overlap between foreign affairs and politics, as well as anchors two video shows on the most interesting stories of the time. She has worked in a variety of news media, both print and TV and is comfortable in Hindi and English. She likes to read and loves to travel. She is president of the Indian Women's Press Corps and member of a South Asian network of journalists called South Asian Women in the Media.

b: Jyoti Pande Lavakare is an independent financial journalist, author and clean air evangelist. She started as a radio journalist in 1985 and switched from active journalism between 1990-2001 to writing columns for…
f: Jyoti Pande Lavakare is an independent financial journalist, author and clean air evangelist. She started as a radio journalist in 1985 and switched from active journalism between 1990-2001 to writing columns for national and international newspapers after resigning from Dow Jones Newswires and a stint in California as a trailing spouse and stay-home mother.

b: Jyotika Elhance , an associate professor of English at the University of Delhi, is devoted to bringing to the forefront the rich dynamism of regional literature. She has been translating from Rajasthani and Hindi into…
f: Jyotika Elhance , an associate professor of English at the University of Delhi, is devoted to bringing to the forefront the rich dynamism of regional literature. She has been translating from Rajasthani and Hindi into English and vice versa. Jyotika's works have been recognized and published by Sahitya Akademi and Bharatiya Anuvad Parishad.

b: Jyotika Jhalani established JanaviIndia in 1998, after a colourful decade at the World Bank. Janavi was born from the desire to create designs with 100% pure cashmere in a way the world had never seen. A self-confessed…
f: Jyotika Jhalani established JanaviIndia in 1998, after a colourful decade at the World Bank. Janavi was born from the desire to create designs with 100% pure cashmere in a way the world had never seen. A self-confessed ‘spiritual nomad,’ Jyotika seeks to celebrate the sacred natural rhythms of the universe and wants to harness the inherent creativity that rests deep within the human heart. Since its inception, Janavi has been known for its exceptional cashmere products.

b: Jyotindra Jain , formerly Director of the National Crafts Museum and Professor of Arts and Aesthetics at Jawaharlal Nehru University, has been a Visiting Professor at Harvard, and Humboldt University, Berlin. A scholar…
f: Jyotindra Jain , formerly Director of the National Crafts Museum and Professor of Arts and Aesthetics at Jawaharlal Nehru University, has been a Visiting Professor at Harvard, and Humboldt University, Berlin. A scholar of Indian art and Fellow of the Asiatic Society of Bombay, Jain is a recipient of the Prince Claus Award and Cross of the Order of Merit of Germany.

f: Jérémie Gallon is a lawyer and former diplomat,and a leading foreign policy analyst. He is the author of Henry Kissinger: An Intimate Portrait of the Master of Realpolitik , Georges Pompidou: A Timeless Figure and Diary of a Young Diplomat in Trump's America .

f: K Satchidanandan , President of the Kerala Sahitya Akademi, is a bilingual poet, critic, playwright, editor, fiction writer and travel writer. He has been a Professor of English and of Translation Studies, , editor of Indian Literature bimonthly and Beyond Borders , a SAARC literature quarterly, the executive head of the National Academy of Letters, invited National fellow at the Indian Institute of Advanced Studies, Shimla, He has thirty-two collections of poetry in Malayalam, ten in English, seven in Hindi, and thirty collections in other languages including Arabic, Irish, French, German, Italian, Spanish, Chinese and Japanese besides all major Indian languages. He has won sixty one literary awards - including the National Academy award, Dante Medal from Italy, and the Poet Laureate Award from Tata Literature Festival.

b: K. Srilata is a writer, translator, and academic. Her latest work, This Kind of Child: The ‘Disability’ Story , is a multi-genre book on the experience of disability. Her books include five collections of poetry,…
f: K. Srilata is a writer, translator, and academic. Her latest work, This Kind of Child: The ‘Disability’ Story , is a multi-genre book on the experience of disability. Her books include five collections of poetry, four edited anthologies of poetry, a novel, Table for Four, which was long listed in 2009 for the Man Asian literary prize.

b: K. VijayRaghavan is the Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India and the Chairperson of Prime Minister’s Science, Technology & Innovation Advisory Council (PM-STIAC). He was Secretary, Department of…
f: K. VijayRaghavan is the Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India and the Chairperson of Prime Minister’s Science, Technology & Innovation Advisory Council (PM-STIAC). He was Secretary, Department of Biotechnology, Government of India from January 2013 to February 2018. Professor VijayRaghavan is also a Distinguished Professor at the National Centre of Biological Sciences, Tata Institute of Fundamental Research Bangalore and was the NCBS Director till 2013. He studied Chemical Engineering at the Indian Institute of Technology, Kanpur, holds a PhD in Molecular Biology from the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research was a Senior Research Fellow at the California Institute of Technology. His research is on nerves and muscles and how complex behaviour emerges during animal development. VijayRaghavan is a Fellow of the Indian Science Academies, the Royal Society, the Academy of Medical Sciences (UK) and a Foreign Associate of the US National Academy of Sciences. He was awarded the Padma Shri by the Government of India in 2013.

b: K.J. Alphons , a 1979 batch Indian Administrative Service officer, gained national recognition as an efficient administrator and anti-corruption advocate. As commissioner of the Delhi Development Authority, he pioneered…
f: K.J. Alphons , a 1979 batch Indian Administrative Service officer, gained national recognition as an efficient administrator and anti-corruption advocate. As commissioner of the Delhi Development Authority, he pioneered India’s literacy movement. His mass contact programme as district collector earned the UN’s top award for governance innovation. Named one of Time magazine’s 100 Young Global Leaders, he left the civil service in 2006 to enter politics. As tourism minister, he helped position India third in global tourism. He also served as minister of state for electronics and IT. A motivational speaker and bestselling author, his book Making a Difference reflects his journey.

b: KS Ramesh is India’s finest magician with an amazing repertoire of mind-boggling illusions, magic, conjuring acts, mentalism and more. Ramesh has been enthralling audiences across the country and the world for over…
f: KS Ramesh is India’s finest magician with an amazing repertoire of mind-boggling illusions, magic, conjuring acts, mentalism and more. Ramesh has been enthralling audiences across the country and the world for over three decades. An accomplished actor in feature films and television, Ramesh has also been lauded for his cameos and special magical effects in films. He is a consulting illusionist for the Bollywood musical Zangoora: The Gypsy Prince.

b: Kader Abdolah is a celebrated Iranian-Dutch author known for his poignant storytelling and exploration of identity and exile. Born in Iran in 1954, he fled to the Netherlands post-revolution. His works, including The…
f: Kader Abdolah is a celebrated Iranian-Dutch author known for his poignant storytelling and exploration of identity and exile. Born in Iran in 1954, he fled to the Netherlands post-revolution. His works, including The House of the Mosque , reflect his rich cultural heritage and deep empathy, offering insights into migration and belonging.

b: Kai Bird is a Pulitzer Prize-winning biographer and journalist. He won the Pulitzer Prize for Biography in 2006 for American Prometheus: The Triumph and Tragedy of J. Robert Oppenheimer (co-authored with Martin J.…
f: Kai Bird is a Pulitzer Prize-winning biographer and journalist. He won the Pulitzer Prize for Biography in 2006 for American Prometheus: The Triumph and Tragedy of J. Robert Oppenheimer (co-authored with Martin J. Sherwin). American Prometheus is the basis for Christopher Nolan’s recent film, Oppenheimer. Bird is the Executive Director and Distinguished Lecturer of the Leon Levy Center for Biography at the CUNY Graduate Center in New York City. His book, The Good Spy: The Life and Death of Robert Ames, was a New York Times best-seller and his most recent work is The Outlier: The Unfinished Presidency of Jimmy Carter. His memoir is called Crossing Mandelbaum Gate: Coming of Age Between the Arabs and Israelis and he also authored multiple biographies. His work includes critical writings on the Vietnam War, Hiroshima, Nuclear weapons, the Cold War, the Arab-Israeli conflict and the CIA. He won the National Books Critics Circle Award, the Duff Cooper Prize for History and is an elected member of the prestigious Society of American Historians.

b: Known for his deep, soulful voice, Padma Shri Kailash Kher is now venturing into the literary world with the same passion and enthusiasm that have defined his highly celebrated music career. From humble beginnings to…
f: Known for his deep, soulful voice, Padma Shri Kailash Kher is now venturing into the literary world with the same passion and enthusiasm that have defined his highly celebrated music career. From humble beginnings to becoming an internationally respected singer and composer, Kher's journey is one of immense inspiration. Throughout his musical career, he has sung in over 20 languages, leaving a profound impact on the world of music. His diverse repertoire, filled with soulful albums and memorable compositions, has touched countless hearts globally. Now embarking on this literary journey, Kher brings lyrical magic to prose, crafting stories with the same depth and spiritual essence that define his music. His works stand as a testament to his philosophy of life, personal memoirs, and rich cultural heritage.

b: Nobel Peace Laureate Kailash Satyarthi , a social reformer par excellence, stands as one of the tallest leaders and the loudest voice for the oppressed and voiceless. He was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 2014 for his…
f: Nobel Peace Laureate Kailash Satyarthi , a social reformer par excellence, stands as one of the tallest leaders and the loudest voice for the oppressed and voiceless. He was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 2014 for his ‘struggle against the suppression of children and young people and for the right of all children to education.’ A global thought leader and the founder of the Satyarthi Movement for Global Compassion, his dedication to social reforms is unparalleled. Through his organisation, Bachpan Bachao Andolan, Mr. Satyarthi has liberated more than 138,000 children from child labour, slavery, trafficking, and other forms of exploitation and developed a successful model for their education, rehabilitation, and reintegration into mainstream society. The Global March Against Child Labour, which he led, galvanized support in 103 countries, resulting in the adoption of ILO Convention 182 on the Worst Forms of Child Labour, which went on to become the only universally ratified convention in the history of the ILO.

b: Kairavi Bharat Ram graduated from The Shri Ram School in 2016. She is currently studying Fashion Management at the London College of Fashion. She is also a makeup blogger on instagram under the name of @typsyprincess…
f: Kairavi Bharat Ram graduated from The Shri Ram School in 2016. She is currently studying Fashion Management at the London College of Fashion. She is also a makeup blogger on instagram under the name of @typsyprincess and the co-author of Ramayana and Krishna in Rhyme . She is an advocate for mental health having suffered from depression for many years and wrote this book with the hope of helping other young kids in similar situations. In her free time, she likes to watch Korean dramas, write poems, cuddle her dog Google and dream about starting her own makeup line.

f: Kal Penn is an Emmy-nominated actor, writer, and producer, best known for his roles in Designated Survivor , House , Mira Nair’s The Namesake , How I Met Your Mother , and the Harold & Kumar franchise.
