f: Kala Ramesh is a 2020 Pushcart Prize-nominated poet, editor and anthologist. She is the Founder and Director of Triveni Haikai India, and the founder and managing editor of haikuKATHA journal. She has authored haiku! for children, a book on haiku and haibun - Beyond the Horizon Beyond , which was shortlisted for the Rabindranath Tagore Literary Prize in 2019; and a book on tanka, tanka prose and tanka doha titled the forest i know, published by HarperCollins. Ramesh has been a speaker at international haiku conferences, and was longlisted for the WE Kamala Das Poetry Award 2020, and received the WE Trailblazer Poet Award 2020, from Women Empowered – India.

b: Kallol Bhattacherjee is a Senior Assistant Editor at The Hindu , focusing on India's foreign affairs and South Asia. He authored Nehru’s First Recruits: The Diplomats Who Built Independent India’s Foreign Policy…
f: Kallol Bhattacherjee is a Senior Assistant Editor at The Hindu , focusing on India's foreign affairs and South Asia. He authored Nehru’s First Recruits: The Diplomats Who Built Independent India’s Foreign Policy (HarperCollins, 2024), A Singular Spy: The Untold Story of Coomar Narain (Bloomsbury India, 2024), and The Great Game in Afghanistan (HarperCollins, 2017).

b: Kalpana Purushothaman is a teacher, healer, dreamer and survivor. Professionally, she is a counseling psychologist working with children in difficult circumstances and survivors of child sexual abuse. A queer…
f: Kalpana Purushothaman is a teacher, healer, dreamer and survivor. Professionally, she is a counseling psychologist working with children in difficult circumstances and survivors of child sexual abuse. A queer affirmative therapist and advocate for the mental health of rights of children in the justice system, she believes in competence with compassion.

f: Kalpana Raina was born in Kashmir and lives in New York. She is a senior executive with extensive financial, management and advisory experience internationally. Raina is currently the Vice Chair at Words Without Borders, a premier online journal of translations. Her collaborative translation project of stories from the Kashmiri language, For Now, It Is Night , is her first work of translation.

b: Kamini Dandapani was born and raised in the once sleepy city that was once Madras and now lives in the city that never sleeps, New York. She has had extensive training in Carnatic vocal music, Western Classical piano,…
f: Kamini Dandapani was born and raised in the once sleepy city that was once Madras and now lives in the city that never sleeps, New York. She endured a long stint in the corporate world, which included Chase Manhattan and McKinsey & Company, after which she returned to her true loves, music and writing. Her first book is Rajaraja Chola-King of Kings .

f: Kamini Sawhney is the first Director of the Museum of Art & Photography's (MAP). She has brought together a young, inspired team that is focused on creating a new museum experience for audiences in India. She has helped shape a vision for MAP that seeks to democratise art through an accessible, inclusive space where everyone feels welcome.

f: Kanan Gill is an author, comedian, and actor from Bangalore. f: Kancha Ilaiah Shepherd is a well-known author and activist from Telangana. His memoirs, the first to be written by a Shudra, From a Shepherd Boy to an Intellectual , will be launched at ZEE JLF. f: Kanishka Gupta is a literary agent, writer and publishing commentator best known for his hugely acclaimed series for Scroll.in called 'Publishing and the Pandemic'. His first novel was longlisted for the Asian Booker Prize in 2009 and was published in 2010.

f: Kannan Sundaram is the Managing Director and Publisher of Kalachuvadu Publication Pvt Ltd.. He co-organised ‘Tamil Ini 2000′, an international Tamil conference on 20th century Tamil writing. He has written extensively in Tamil and namita gokhalEnglish on media, politics and publishing, and his writings have appeared in several platforms such as The Hindu, The Indian Express and the Economic and Political Weekly . The French government announced the Chevalier award (Odre National du Mérite) for Sundaram in 2022.

f: Kanta Singh, Deputy Country Representative, UN Women India, has over 25 years of experience in the management of pro-women development programmes. Kanta is a Chevening Gurukul Fellow from the University of Oxford.

f: Kanupriya Kulshreshtha is an illustrator, author, and designer passionate about children's literature. A NIFT New Delhi graduate, she refined her illustration skills at the Riyaaz Academy of Illustration. Her debut book, Dhabba Chala, was published in five languages, and her evocative work for Jirhul , a poetry collection by Jacinta Kerketta, earned widespread recognition. A runner-up for the Room to Read Young Illustrator Award, Kanupriya’s art extends to book covers, posters, and editorial illustrations.

b: Kapil Sibal is a member of the Rajya Sabha and a senior Indian National Congress leader. Sibal previously held the positions of Union Law Minister, Union Telecom Minister and Union Minister for HRD in the UPA I & II…
f: Kapil Sibal is a member of the Rajya Sabha and a senior Indian National Congress leader. Sibal previously held the positions of Union Law Minister, Union Telecom Minister and Union Minister for HRD in the UPA I & II Governments. He was also Minister for Science and Technology.A lawyer by profession, Sibal is also a poet and writer.

f: Kapka Kassabova is the author of three books of narrative non-fiction. Her latest, Border , won the British Academy Al-Rodhan Prize, the Saltire Book of the Year, the Stanford-Dolman Book of the Year and the Highland Book Prize.

b: Karan Singh , born in 1931 to Maharaja Hari Singh and Maharani Tara Devi, was Head of State of Jammu and Kashmir for eighteen years. He joined Indira Gandhi’s Union Cabinet in 1967 at the age of 36, becoming India’s…
f: Karan Singh , born in 1931 to Maharaja Hari Singh and Maharani Tara Devi, was Head of State of Jammu and Kashmir for eighteen years. He joined Indira Gandhi’s Union Cabinet in 1967 at the age of 36, becoming India’s youngest cabinet minister. Singh was appointed Ambassador to the United States in 1989 and also served as India’s Member on the UNESCO Governing Board. He chaired the Auroville Foundation for twenty years and was a four-time Member of the Rajya Sabha. He is recognized as an outstanding thinker both in India and abroad and has written twenty books on a wide range of subjects.

b: Karan Thapar trained as a correspondent, producer, editor and presenter in the United Kingdom. He currently heads Infotainment Television, a production house that makes programmes for the BBC, Channel NewsAsia, CNBC,…
f: Karan Thapar trained as a correspondent, producer, editor and presenter in the United Kingdom. He currently heads Infotainment Television, a production house that makes programmes for the BBC, Channel NewsAsia, CNBC, CNN News 18 and Doordarshan. Perhaps the most prestigious programme Thapar has presented is the BBC series HARDtalk INDIA , modelled on the lines of the BBC’s long standing programme. His other accolades include numerous Asian Television Awards, the Ramnath Goenka Excellence in Journalism Award and, most recently, the 2017 G.K. Reddy Memorial Award for Excellence in Journalism. Since 2004, Thapar has presented India Tonight on CNBC. In 2006, he launched the primetime interview programme Devil’s Advocate on CNN News 18. Also a columnist, he writes for the Hindustan Times. In 2006, a collection of Thapar’s ‘Sunday Sentiments’ columns was published in a book called Sunday Sentiments by Wisdom Tree. Also in 2006, a collection of his Face to Face interviews for the BBC was published as a book called Face to Face India by Penguin. In 2009, HarperCollins published a second collection of ‘Sunday Sentiments’ under the title More Salt than Pepper

b: Karen Anand is widely regarded as one of India’s first food gurus. A prolific writer, she has published numerous books including the bestselling Good Food Good Living and Simple Cooking for Smart Men , and co-authored…
f: Karen Anand is widely regarded as one of India’s first food gurus. A prolific writer, she has published numerous books including the bestselling Good Food Good Living and Simple Cooking for Smart Men , and co-authored The Penguin Food Lovers Guide to India and Nepal . Her twelve-book series entitled Simple Cooking was nominated for the Gourmand World Cookbook Awards in Paris. Anand continues to write extensively about food, with a regular column in the Sunday Telegraph . She is the recipient of the Trophée de l’Esprit Alimentaire (Food & Spirit Award) for Culture from the French Government and the winner of the French Ambassador’s Travel Writer Award. She also runs a successful gourmet business and consults for luxury hotels and restaurants. Between all this, she ensures there is always time to cook!

f: Karima Khalil is a public health doctor and avid photographer. A native of Alexandria, Egypt, she sourced and edited Messages from Tahrir , a photographic documentation of the beginning of Egypt’s Arab Spring.

f: Karin Pettersson is a Swedish journalist and author. She is a 2017 Harvard Nieman and Berkman Klein Fellow. She is director of public policy at Schibsted Media Group and chairwoman of WAN-IFRA Media Freedom Board. Previously, she was political editor-in-chief at Aftonbladet , Scandinavia’s biggest daily newspaper. She is the co-founder and former editor-in-chief of Fokus , Sweden’s leading newsmagazine.

b: Karthik Narayanaswamy joined Novo Holdings in January 2025 as Partner and Head of India, bringing over 20 years of experience in private equity investing, strategy consulting, and operations. Before joining Novo…
f: Karthik Narayanaswamy joined Novo Holdings in January 2025 as Partner and Head of India, bringing over 20 years of experience in private equity investing, strategy consulting, and operations. Before joining Novo Holdings, Karthik was the Co-founder and Partner at SeaLink Capital Partners, a mid-market private equity firm focused on India, where he led the firm’s healthcare investments. Prior to that, he served as a Principal at KKR Capstone, where he oversaw due diligence and drove operational improvements across KKR's investments in India.

b: Kartikeya Sharma is the Executive Editor of India's first news-based OTT Platform News9Plus . Sharma also worked as Political Editor with India's first international news channel WION. He has reported from war-torn…
f: Kartikeya Sharma is the Executive Editor of India's first news-based OTT Platform News9Plus . Sharma also worked as Political Editor with India's first international news channel WION. He has reported from war-torn Syria, Afghanistan and Congo. Earlier he worked as the Political Editor of Headlines Today and covered domestic politics and elections.

b: Kartikeya is a distinguished advocate and the founder of a boutique law firm in New Delhi. He dons several hats and is an MBA by training and a corporate marketing expert who balances boardroom strategy with courtroom…
f: Kartikeya is a distinguished advocate and the founder of a boutique law firm in New Delhi. He dons several hats and is an MBA by training and a corporate marketing expert who balances boardroom strategy with courtroom acumen. Yet it is cricket that first revealed to him the unifying thread of his life’s work: the disciplined pursuit of a meditative flow state. Kartikeya debuted for his state at the under-14 nationals by the young age of eleven and now plays for Team India Lawyers in the Lawyers’ Cricket World Cup. Another deep influence in his life was the early introduction to yogic concentration practice of tratak, later deepened through formal instruction in Transcendental Meditation, Tibetan Mahayana Mahamudra meditation, and Mahavatar Babaji’s Kriya Yoga. His maiden work of fiction gathers the insights of this inner pilgrimage, offering readers a powerful yet fluid testament to the wisdom discovered when professional mastery meets spiritual inquiry.

b: Karuna Ezara Parikh is the author of the novel The Heart Asks Pleasure First and the poetry collection Where Stories Gather . Her work has appeared in The Wire , Vogue , India Today , and Dazed . She is the founder of…
f: Karuna Ezara Parikh is the author of the novel The Heart Asks Pleasure First and the poetry collection Where Stories Gather . Her work has appeared in The Wire , Vogue , India Today , and Dazed . She is the founder of Karuna’s Kitaab Club, a public reading initiative, and the host of The Books Need People podcast. A former travel show host, she is currently working on a memoir reflecting on her years of travel and storytelling. Widely recognized for her activism, Karuna advocates for gender equality, secularism, and climate action, using her voice to spark dialogue and inspire change.

f: Kasturi Gandhi works at Dasra, building research and insights that inform various philanthropic programs across the non-profit sector, and is one of the authors of ‘India’s Million Missions: 75 years of service towards nation building’ by Coalition CSO @75.

f: Kate Evans is an author, illustrator, cartoonist, and textile artist. The subjects of her books are wide-ranging, incorporating historical biography, journalistic graphic reportage, and works explaining the science of climate change, breastfeeding and birth. Patchwork: a graphic biography of Jane Austen is her eighth work of graphic non-fiction.

b: Kate Summerscale is the author of the number one bestselling The Suspicions of Mr Whicher , winner of the Samuel Johnson Prize for Non-Fiction 2008, winner of the Galaxy British Book of the Year Award, a Richard & Judy…
f: Kate Summerscale is the author of the number one bestselling The Suspicions of Mr Whicher , winner of the Samuel Johnson Prize for Non-Fiction 2008, winner of the Galaxy British Book of the Year Award, a Richard & Judy Book Club pick and adapted into a major ITV drama. Her first book, the bestselling The Queen of Whale Cay , won a Somerset Maugham award and was shortlisted for the Whitbread biography award. Summerscale has also judged various literary competitions including the Booker Prize.

b: Katharina Winkler was born in Vienna in 1979 and studied German philology and theatre studies . Blue Jewellery is her debut novel.
f: Katharina Winkler was born in Vienna in 1979 and studied German philology and theatre studies . Blue Jewellery is her debut novel.

b: Katherine Schofield is a historian of Hindustani music and Mughal India. In telling stories about musical lives, she writes on sovereignty and selfhood, affection and desire, sympathy and loss, and power, worldly and…
f: Katherine Schofield is a historian of Hindustani music and Mughal India. In telling stories about musical lives, she writes on sovereignty and selfhood, affection and desire, sympathy and loss, and power, worldly and strange. Her latest book, Music and Musicians in Late Mughal India: Histories of the Ephemeral, 1748–1858 , will be out with Cambridge University Press in 2022.

b: Katherine Eban is an investigative journalist, a Fortune magazine contributor and Andrew Carnegie fellow. Her articles on pharmaceutical counterfeiting, gun trafficking, and coercive interrogations by the CIA have won…
f: Katherine Eban is an investigative journalist, a Fortune magazine contributor and Andrew Carnegie fellow. Her articles on pharmaceutical counterfeiting, gun trafficking, and coercive interrogations by the CIA have won international attention and numerous awards. Her first book, Dangerous Doses: a True Story of Cops, Counterfeiters and the Contamination of America’s Drug Supply, was named one of the Best Books of 2005 by Kirkus Reviews and was a Barnes & Noble Discover Great New Writers pick. Her second book Bottle of Lies: The Inside Story of the Generic Drug Boom is a New York Times bestseller and Editor’s Choice/Staff Pick. It was published in India under the title Bottle of Lies: Ranbaxy and the Dark Side of Indian Pharma . Based on a decade of reporting, the book reveals endemic fraud and dire conditions in the overseas manufacturing plants where the majority of our low-cost generic medicine is made.

b: Katherine Pangonis is a historian specialising in the medieval world of the Mediterranean and Middle East. She has Master’s degrees in Literature and History from Oxford University and University College London.…
f: Katherine Pangonis is a historian specialising in the medieval world of the Mediterranean and Middle East. She has Master’s degrees in Literature and History from Oxford University and University College London. Katherine is particularly interested in rewriting women's voices into the historical narratives and re-examining the understudied areas of history.

b: Katherine Rundell is a Fellow of St Catherine's College, Oxford. She is the author of Super-Infinite , which won the Baillie Gifford Prize, and The Golden Mole and Other Vanishing Treasure, both Sunday Times…
f: Katherine Rundell is a Fellow of St Catherine's College, Oxford. Her award-winning books for children have been translated into more than thirty languages and sold over two million copies worldwide. She has written for, among others, the London Review of Books, the Times Literary Supplement, the New York Review of Books and the New York Times , about books, the natural world and night climbing.

f: Katherine Schofield is a historian of Mughal India and Hindustani music based at King’s College London. f: Kathrin Grün is the Director of PR and Communications at Frankfurter Buchmesse. Reichs is a producer for the TV series Bones , which is loosely based on her novels.

f: Kathy Wong is the Executive Director of Playright Children’s Play Association, a non-official member of Commission on Children of Hong Kong Special Administrative Region and the Vice-President of the International Play Association. b: Katie Hickman is a novelist and historian, and the author of nine books, including the bestselling Daughters of Britannia and Courtesans . Her trilogy of historical novels, The Aviary Gate , The Pindar Diamond and The…
f: Katie Hickman is a novelist and historian, and the author of nine books, including the bestselling Daughters of Britannia and Courtesans . Her trilogy of historical novels, The Aviary Gate , The Pindar Diamond and The House at Bishopsgate, have been translated into 19 languages. Her most recent book, She-Merchants, Buccaneers and Gentlewomen: British Women in India 1600-1900 , is the product of her lifelong interest in India and in women's history.

b: Katie Kitamura’s most recent novel is Intimacies. One of The New York Times’ 10 Best Books of 2021 and one of Barack Obama’s Favorite Books of 2021, it was longlisted for the National Book Award and the…
f: Katie Kitamura’s most recent novel is Intimacies. One of The New York Times’ 10 Best Books of 2021 and one of Barack Obama’s Favorite Books of 2021, it was longlisted for the National Book Award and the PEN/Faulkner Award. The recipient of a Rome Prize in Literature and the Prix Litteraire Lucien Barriere, her work has been translated into 21 languages and is being adapted for film and television.

b: Katy Hessel is an art historian, broadcaster and curator dedicated to celebrating women artists from all over the world. She is the founder of an Instagram account called @thegreatwomenartists, which has grown to almost…
f: Katy Hessel is an art historian, broadcaster and curator dedicated to celebrating women artists from all over the world. Katy has lectured at Tate, National Gallery, Christie’s and University of Cambridge; presented films for the BBC and Royal Academy; and collaborated with Dior on a podcast series featuring interviews with Tracey Emin and Judy Chicago. She lives in London and sits on the Board of Trustees at Charleston, the former home of the Bloomsbury Group.

f: Kaushik Bhaumik is Associate Professor in Cinema Studies at Jawaharlal Nehru University, New Delhi, India. He has been Deputy Director of the Osian's Cinefan Festival of Asian and Arab Cinema. He has written extensively on various aspects of Indian film history in international journals and anthologies. His monograph on early Bombay cinema is due from Jadavpur University Press in 2023.

f: Kaveree Bamzai is an independent journalist. She was the first, and so far, only woman editor of India Today. f: Kavita Kané is a bestselling author of nine novels and a transformative voice in Indian literature, known for bringing feminism to mythology by spotlighting lesser-known women. She is also a columnist, screenwriter and motivational speaker passionate about theatre and the arts. Born in Mumbai and raised in Patna and Delhi, Kavita now lives in Pune with her husband, two daughters and a lively household of pets.

b: Kavita Khosa is the author of Beauty Unbottled – Timeless Ayurvedic Recipes & Rituals. She is the founder and CEO of PUREARTH, an award-winning Ayurvedic skincare and wellness brand. A qualified Ayurvedic…
f: Kavita Khosa is the author of Beauty Unbottled – Timeless Ayurvedic Recipes & Rituals. She is the founder and CEO of PUREARTH, an award-winning Ayurvedic skincare and wellness brand. A qualified Ayurvedic practitioner, she was a former Wall Street firm lawyer and director at Deutsche Bank, before shedding her corporate avatar in 2011. An advocate for women’s rights, Kavita established the Pure Purpose Foundation, a charity that works with rural women and communities on social impact initiatives.

f: Kavita Pant is a senior journalist from Jaipur who has worked with national publications such as Hindustan Times, Times of India and DNA. Pant played an important role in the launch of HT and DNA editions in Jaipur. She is currently News Editor with DNA.

Genç’s writing has appeared in the New York Review of Books, London Review of Books , the Times Literary Supplement and Paris Review , Believer , the Guardian , the Financial Times and The New York Times .

f: Kayo Chingonyi ‘s latest book, Kumukanda , won the 2018 Dylan Thomas Prize and a Somerset Maugham Award. f: Keerthik Sasidharan was born in Palakkad, Kerala and was trained as an economist. His writings have appeared in various publications, including as a regular columnist for The Hindu newspaper and OPEN magazine. He is the author of the recently published The Dharma Forest , volume one of The Dharma Trilogy.

f: Kei Miller , professor of English at the University of Miami, is a Jamaican writer who works across a range of genres. His novel, Augustown won the Bocas Prize for Caribbean Literature and his most recent book, the essay collection titled, Things I Have Withheld , was shortlisted for the Baillie Gifford Prize.

f: Keki N. Daruwalla is one of India’s foremost poets and writers. f: Ken Follett was twenty-seven when he wrote Eye of the Needle , an award-winning thriller that became an international bestseller. Follett’s third novel in the Kingsbridge series is A Column of Fire , and he has also recently published a prequel to the series - The Evening and the Morning . After Kingsbridge, Follett wrote the bestselling Century trilogy, and Never , his first contemporary novel in seventeen years.

b: Ketaki Karnik works at the intersection of technology, business, and society, and is currently with nasscom, the apex body for India’s technology industry. Her books, Secrets for Thriving in the Gig Zone and The…
f: Ketaki Karnik works at the intersection of technology, business, and society, and is currently with nasscom, the apex body for India’s technology industry. f: Kevin Barry is the author of the novels Night Boat To Tangier, Beatlebone and City of Bohane and three short story collections, That Old Country Music, Dark Lies The Island and There Are Little Kingdoms . In 2021, Ambassador Kelly was elected by the Assembly of States Parties to the International Criminal Court as a Member of the Board of Directors of the Trust Fund for Victims and he still holds this position.

b: Kevin Kwan is the author of Crazy Rich Asians, the bestselling novel translated into 40 languages. In 2018, Kwan was named one of the 100 Most Influential People in the World by TIME Magazine. His latest novel, Sex &…
f: Kevin Kwan is the author of Crazy Rich Asians, the bestselling novel translated into 40 languages. In 2018, Kwan was named one of the 100 Most Influential People in the World by TIME Magazine. His latest novel, Sex & Vanity, is being adapted into a feature film by Sony Pictures.

b: Khalid Jawed , one of the leading voices in Urdu fiction and winner of the 2022 JCB Prize for Literature, has published four critically-acclaimed novels, including Maut ki Kitab (2011) and the latest Arsalaan Aur…
f: Khalid Jawed , one of the leading voices in Urdu fiction and winner of the 2022 JCB Prize for Literature, has published four critically-acclaimed novels, including Maut ki Kitab (2011) and the latest Arsalaan Aur Baezaad (2022). Dubbed as ‘Cartographer of Human Existence’, his story worlds are dominated by existential themes where the novelty of subject matter and storytelling work towards creating a new aesthetic idiom.

b: Khushi Anand leads the audiobooks segment at Penguin Random House India and Southeast Asia, working on the English and Hindi list. Apart from audiobooks, she also contributes to shaping the local list, and building all…
f: Khushi Anand leads the audiobooks segment at Penguin Random House India and Southeast Asia, working on the English and Hindi list. Apart from audiobooks, she also contributes to shaping the local list, and building all books published by Penguin Random House India.

b: Kim A. Wagner teaches the history of colonial India and the British Empire at Queen Mary, University of London. He has written extensively on the subject of ‘Thuggee’, the Uprising of 1857 and colonial violence. His…
f: Kim A. Wagner teaches the history of colonial India and the British Empire at Queen Mary, University of London. He has written extensively on the subject of ‘Thuggee’, the Uprising of 1857 and colonial violence. His most recent publications include The Skull of Alum Bheg: The Life and Death of a Rebel of 1857 and Amritsar 1919: An Empire of Fear and the Making of a Massacre .

b: Kim Ghattas is a journalist, author and analyst with more than 20 years of experience in print and broadcast media, covering the Middle East, international affairs and US foreign policy. She is a contributing writer for…
f: Kim Ghattas is a journalist, author and analyst with more than 20 years of experience in print and broadcast media, covering the Middle East, international affairs and US foreign policy. She is a contributing writer for the Atlantic magazine and a non-resident senior fellow at the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace. She has reported for the BBC, the Financial Times and de Volkskrant. She is the author of Black Wave: Saudi Arabia, Iran and the Forty Year Rivalry that Unraveled Culture, Religion and Collective Memory in the Middle East , a NYT notable book of 2020 and The Secretary: A Journey with Hillary Clinton from Beirut to the Heart of American Power, a NYT bestseller. She serves on the board of Trustees of the American University of Beirut and on the board of directors of the organisation of Arab Reporters for Investigative Journalism (ARIJ). She was born and raised in Beirut.

b: Kim Stanley Robinson is an American science fiction writer. He is the author of about twenty books, including the internationally bestselling Mars trilogy, and more recently Red Moon, New York 2140, and The Ministry for…
f: Kim Stanley Robinson is an American science fiction writer. He is the author of about twenty books, including the internationally bestselling Mars trilogy, and more recently Red Moon, New York 2140, and The Ministry for the Future . He was part of the U.S. National Science Foundation’s Antarctic Artists & Writers’ Program in 1995 and 2016. His work has been translated into 25 languages and won awards, including the Hugo, Nebula, and World Fantasy awards. In 2016, asteroid 72432 was named ‘Kimrobinson’.

b: Kinshuk Gupta is a medical student, bilingual writer, poet, and translator based in New Delhi. He writes columns centred around books, gender and sexuality in major newspapers. He has been awarded the Dr Anamika Poetry…
f: Kinshuk Gupta is a medical student, bilingual writer, poet, and translator based in New Delhi. He writes columns centred around books, gender and sexuality in major newspapers. He has been awarded the Dr Anamika Poetry Prize (2021), Ravi Prabhakar Smriti Laghukatha Samman (2022), and Akhil Bhartiya Yuva Kathakar Alankaran (2022). Gupta edits poetry for Mithila Review and Jaggery Lit and works as an Associate Editor for Usawa Literary Review. His debut book of short fiction, Yeh Dil Hai Ki Chordarwaja , the first modern Hindi LGBT short story collection, is published by Vani Prakashan.

b: Kiran Haribhau Kulkarni is an Indian Administrative Service (IAS) officer of the Maharashtra cadre, currently serving as Secretary, Marathi Language Department, Government of Maharashtra. With a Ph.D. in Development…
f: Kiran Haribhau Kulkarni is an Indian Administrative Service (IAS) officer of the Maharashtra cadre, currently serving as Secretary, Marathi Language Department, Government of Maharashtra. With a Ph.D. in Development Economics and qualifications in law and sociology, he brings multidisciplinary expertise to public administration. Over a distinguished career, he has held key leadership roles in municipal governance, tribal development, and capacity building. A prolific writer, academic, and filmmaker, Dr. Kulkarni has contributed to over 30 documentary and training films and authored several books. He is deeply committed to the promotion of Marathi language, literature, and culture through policy, education, and creative engagement.

b: Kiran Nagarkar is a bilingual novelist, playwright, screenplay writer, political, social and literary critic. His novels include Jasoda , God’s Little Soldier , The Rand E trilogy , R avan and Eddie, The Extras, Rest…
f: Kiran Nagarkar is a bilingual novelist, playwright, screenplay writer, political, social and literary critic. His novels include Jasoda , God’s Little Soldier , The Rand E trilogy , R avan and Eddie, The Extras, Rest in Peace, Cuckold and Seven Sixes are Forty-three . His other works are the plays Bedtime Story and What Shall we do with Kabir? and the screenplay Black Tulip. Nagarkar has been awarded several fellowships, two Lifetime Achievement Awards and the Sahitya Akademi Award for Best Novel for Cuckold and The Iron Cross, Germany’s highest civilian award presented by the President of Germany.

b: Kiriti Sengupta , heading the English division of Hawakal Publications, is a widely published author of fourteen books of poetry and prose, two translation volumes, and nine edited anthologies. He was awarded the 2018…
f: Kiriti Sengupta , heading the English division of Hawakal Publications, is a widely published author of fourteen books of poetry and prose, two translation volumes, and nine edited anthologies. He was awarded the 2018 Rabindranath Tagore Literary Prize.

b: Kishore Mahbubani served as a Singapore diplomat for 33 years and was the Founding Dean of the Lee Kuan Yew School of Public Policy. He has authored ten books, including The Asian 21st Century , an open-access volume…
f: Kishore Mahbubani served as a Singapore diplomat for 33 years and was the Founding Dean of the Lee Kuan Yew School of Public Policy. He has authored ten books, including The Asian 21st Century , an open-access volume with 3.86 million downloads. His memoir, Living the Asian Century , was published in August 2024.

b: Kishwar Desai is an award-winning author and playwright who writes both fiction and non-fiction. Her latest book is The Longest Kiss: The Life and Times of Devika Rani , based on the personal papers and letters of the…
f: Kishwar Desai is an award-winning author and playwright who writes both fiction and non-fiction. Her latest book is The Longest Kiss: The Life and Times of Devika Rani , based on the personal papers and letters of the iconic actress. The book has emerged from a 15-year search for documents and material. Desai worked in television as an anchor and producer for over 20 years before becoming a writer. She is the chairperson of The Arts and Cultural Heritage Trust that set up the world’s first Partition Museum at Town Hall, Amritsar. She also helped to install the statue of Mahatma Gandhi outside Westminster in the UK. Desai is the author of Darlingji: The True Love Story of Nargis and Sunil Dutt. Her novel Witness the Night won the Costa First Novel Award in the UK, in 2010, and was followed by two others: Origins of Love and Sea of Innocence. The trilogy featuring Simran Singh has since been optioned for a web series. Desai’s first work of political non-fiction, Jallianwala Bagh: The Real Story , won critical acclaim and inspired exhibitions on the massacre in India, the UK and New Zealand. She also wrote a play, Manto! which won the TAG Omega award for Best Play in 1999. Most recently, in 2019, her play, Devika Rani: Goddess of the Silver Screen, produced by Lillete Dubey, was successfully staged in venues across India.

b: Kjell Ola Dahl is a price-winning Norwegian author of crime fiction, historical fiction and documentaries. His first book, Lethal investments was the first book in the Oslo detectives series. The latest book in the…
f: Kjell Ola Dahl is a price-winning Norwegian author of crime fiction, historical fiction and documentaries. His first book, Lethal investments was the first book in the Oslo detectives series. The latest book in the series is Little Drummer . His latest standalone thriller is The Assistant .

b: Ko Ko Thett’s comfort zone is Burmese, but he also enjoys the discomfort of English, a language most of which he learned, and is still learning, as a poet. An Iowa fellow, he has published and edited several poetry…
f: Ko Ko Thett’s comfort zone is Burmese, but he also enjoys the discomfort of English, a language most of which he learned, and is still learning, as a poet. An Iowa fellow, he has published and edited several poetry collections and translations. His poems are widely translated, and he is a recipient of the English PEN Translates Award. Thett’s most recent poetry collection is BAMBOOPHOBIA .

b: Koral Dasgupta is an author and literary entrepreneur. Having published widely with Westland Books, Niyogi Publishers and Rupa, her books explore the themes of gender studies, art, myth and ecocritical literature, and…
f: Koral Dasgupta is an author and literary entrepreneur. Having published widely with Westland Books, Niyogi Publishers and Rupa, her books explore the themes of gender studies, art, myth and ecocritical literature, and her fourth book, Summer Holidays , has been optioned for screen adaptation. Dasgupta is currently working with Pan Macmillan on the five-book Sati series, a retelling of the stories of the Pancha Kanya from Indian mythology.

b: Kota Neelima is an author, political scientist and former journalist, and writes on poverty, gender, electoral reforms and democratic deficit. Dr. Neelima was Senior Research Fellow, SAIS, Johns Hopkins University,…
f: Kota Neelima is an author, political scientist and former journalist, and writes on poverty, gender, electoral reforms and democratic deficit. Dr. Neelima was Senior Research Fellow, SAIS, Johns Hopkins University, Washington DC and is an alumna of Jawaharlal Nehru University and University of Delhi. Her recent initiative, Rate The Debate/Reform TV News, is an extension of her doctoral research on the role of perception in electoral democracies. She also advises on interventions to mainstream peripheries, especially on gender and rural/urban distress. She has authored seven books, ranging from poverty to spirituality. Her recent book, Widows of Vidarbha, Making of Shadows , is a longitudinal study of farmer suicide households. Two of her books have been optioned for a web-series and one has been optioned for a movie.

b: Koël Purie Rinchet is an award-winning Indian actress, producer and writer. She has interviewed presidents and actors alike on her show On the Couch with Koël , and will be seen in Zoya Akhtar’s The Archies . The…
f: Koël Purie Rinchet is an award-winning Indian actress, producer and writer. She has interviewed presidents and actors alike on her show On the Couch with Koël , and will be seen in Zoya Akhtar’s The Archies . The first play she scripted, Mummy's Dead, Long Live Mummy! , is having a dream run with sold-out shows in Paris, India and London. Her first book is Clearly Invisible in Paris.

b: KR Meera is a writer and winner of Kendra and Kerala Sahitya Akademi awards. Her novel Aaraachaar has sold around 150,000 copies and its translation, Hangwoman , was shortlisted for The DSC Prize. Her works include The…
f: KR Meera is a writer and winner of Kendra and Kerala Sahitya Akademi awards. Her novel Aaraachaar has sold around 150,000 copies and its translation, Hangwoman , was shortlisted for The DSC Prize. Her works include The Poison Of Love, The Gospel Of Yudas, The Unseeing Idol Of Light, Yellow Is The Colour of Longing and The Angel's Beauty Spots.

b: Kripa is a Mumbai-based children’s book illustrator with a Fine Arts degree from Sir JJ School of Art. She has been an art educator for over seventeen years with art and design institutions like Srishti School of Art…
f: Kripa is a Mumbai-based children’s book illustrator with a Fine Arts degree from Sir JJ School of Art. She has been an art educator for over seventeen years with art and design institutions like Srishti School of Art Design and Technology. Kripa has illustrated five children’s books with ‘art’ and ‘city’ featuring as a recurring theme. Kripa is the illustrator of Bombay Ducks, Bombay Docks featured in the Parag Honour List in 2021. In most of her books, her art is rooted in her engagement with her home, her city, its children, people and their problems.

b: Kris Manjapra, born in the Caribbean, works at the intersection of transnational history and the critical study of race and colonialism. He is a professor at Tufts University in Boston, USA.
f: Kris Manjapra, born in the Caribbean, works at the intersection of transnational history and the critical study of race and colonialism. He is a professor at Tufts University in Boston, USA.

b: Krish Ashok is not a chef but cooks daily. He is not a scientist but he can explain science with easy-to-understand clarity. He trained to be an electronic engineer but is now a software engineer. He learnt to cook from…
f: Krish Ashok is not a chef but cooks daily. He is not a scientist but he can explain science with easy-to-understand clarity. He trained to be an electronic engineer but is now a software engineer. He learnt to cook from the women in his family who can make the perfectly fluffy idli without lecturing people on lactobacilli and pH levels. He likes the scientific method not because it offers him the ability to bully people with knowledge but because it confidently lets him say: "I don't know, let me test it for myself. When he is not cooking, he's usually playing subversive music on the violin or cello. He lives in Chennai with a wife, who sagely prevents him from buying more gadgets for the kitchen, and a son, who has the flora and fauna in the neighbourhood terrorised.

b: Krishna Kumar is a bilingual author and columnist. His recent books are: Thank You, Gandhi ; Battle for Peace ; Prejudice and Pride ; Choori bazaar mein larki; and Kaathgodam . He also writes for children. He has been…
f: Krishna Kumar is a bilingual author and columnist. His recent books are: Thank You, Gandhi ; Battle for Peace ; Prejudice and Pride ; Choori bazaar mein larki; and Kaathgodam . He also writes for children. He has been the Director of NCERT and is currently Honorary Professor of education at Punjab University.

b: Krishna Ramanujan is a science writer at Cornell University in Ithaca, New York. Coupled with life-long literary interests, he has worked as a writer for Earthwatch Radio, NASA and Cornell University, and has published…
f: Krishna Ramanujan is a science writer at Cornell University in Ithaca, New York. Coupled with life-long literary interests, he has worked as a writer for Earthwatch Radio, NASA and Cornell University, and has published more than 2,000 news stories on topics related to climate change, ecology, biology and genetics. He is the son of AK Ramanujan.

b: Krishnendu Ray is the Chair of the Department of Nutrition and Food Studies at NYU. He is the author of The Migrant’s Table, The Ethnic Restaurateur and the co-editor of Curried Cultures: Globalisation, Food and South…
f: Krishnendu Ray is the Chair of the Department of Nutrition and Food Studies at NYU. He is the author of The Migrant’s Table, The Ethnic Restaurateur and the co-editor of Curried Cultures: Globalisation, Food and South Asia. He is an Editorial Collective Member of the leading Food Studies journal Gastronomica.

b: Kristín Ragna Gunnarsdóttir from Reykjavík, Iceland, is the author and illustrator of fourteen children's books that have been nominated for various prizes, including The Icelandic Literature Prize, The Nordic…
f: Kristín Ragna Gunnarsdóttir from Reykjavík, Iceland, is the author and illustrator of fourteen children's books that have been nominated for various prizes, including The Icelandic Literature Prize, The Nordic Council Literature Prize, The Icelandic Women's Literature Prize, The West Nordic Council's Literature Prize and was shortlisted for In Other Words. Gunnarsdóttir also won the Icelandic Illustration Prize twice.

b: Krupa Ge is a writer and editor. Her reportage and cultural writings have appeared in publications such as The Hindu, The Caravan, The Wire, Firstpost, Ladies Finger and The New Indian Express amongst others. She won a…
f: Krupa Ge is a writer and editor. Her reportage and cultural writings have appeared in publications such as The Hindu, The Caravan, The Wire, Firstpost, Ladies Finger and The New Indian Express amongst others. She won a Laadli in 2017 for her column on women in cinema. Rivers Remember , her book on the 2015 Chennai floods was published in 2019. She has a novel forthcoming in 2020.

b: Kulpreet Yadav is the author of fourteen books and three screenplays of short films. An ex-armed forces officer, Yadav also an actor, filmmaker and entrepreneur. He divides his time between Delhi and Mumbai, and his…
f: Kulpreet Yadav is the author of fourteen books and three screenplays of short films. An ex-armed forces officer, Yadav also an actor, filmmaker and entrepreneur. He divides his time between Delhi and Mumbai, and his latest book, The Battle of Rezang La , has been published by Penguin India.

b: Kumari Rohini is an author, translator, and Korean language expert working across Korean, English, and Hindi. She has translated several acclaimed international titles, including Becoming , the Booker Prize–winning…
f: Kumari Rohini is an author, translator, and Korean language expert working across Korean, English, and Hindi. She has translated several acclaimed international titles, including Becoming , the Booker Prize–winning novel Orbital , and What You Are Looking for Is in the Library . Her essays and reportage have appeared in The Wire , Jankipul , IDR , and India Water Portal . She holds a PhD in Korean Language and Literature from Jawaharlal Nehru University.

b: Kunzang Choden is a Bhutanese writer and a publisher. Her first novel, The Circle of Karma , has been translated into several languages. Documenting Bhutanese folklore resulted in the compilation of Folktales of Bhutan…
f: Kunzang Choden is a Bhutanese writer and a publisher. Her first novel, The Circle of Karma , has been translated into several languages. Documenting Bhutanese folklore resulted in the compilation of Folktales of Bhutan and Bhutanese Tales of the Yeti . Other books by her include Chilli and Cheese: Food and Society in Bhutan and Dawa: The Story of a Stray Dog in Bhutan .

b: Kunzang Choden i s a writer and storyteller. She began her writing career in 1994 by documenting Bhutanese folktales. Her debut novel, Circle of Karma , was shortlisted for the Elle Prix des Lectrices award. Her books…
f: Kunzang Choden i s a writer and storyteller. She began her writing career in 1994 by documenting Bhutanese folktales. Her debut novel, Circle of Karma , was shortlisted for the Elle Prix des Lectrices award. Her books have been translated into multiple languages. Her latest work, Telling Me My Stories , published by Bloomsbury, is a collection of stories from her childhood.

b: Kushanava Choudhury grew up in Calcutta and New Jersey. After graduating from Princeton University, he worked as a newspaper reporter at The Statesman in Calcutta. He has received a Mellon Early Career Fellowship, been…
f: Kushanava Choudhury grew up in Calcutta and New Jersey. After graduating from Princeton University, he worked as a newspaper reporter at The Statesman in Calcutta. He has received a Mellon Early Career Fellowship, been a Senior Writing Fellow at the University of Pennsylvania and held visiting faculty positions at universities in New Delhi and Istanbul. He has reported for The New York Times , Business Day , The Caravan and other publications in the U.S., India and South Africa. T he Epic City: The World on the Streets of Calcutta is his first book. It is the product of a scholar’s mind, a reporter’s hustle and a writer’s heart.

b: Kynpham Sing Nongkynrih is an award-winning poet and writer who writes in Khasi and English. His latest works are Funeral Nights, The Yearning of Seeds and Time’s Barter: Haiku and Senryu. In 2018, he was awarded a…
f: Kynpham Sing Nongkynrih is an award-winning poet and writer who writes in Khasi and English. His latest works are Funeral Nights, The Yearning of Seeds and Time’s Barter: Haiku and Senryu. In 2018, he was awarded a Tagore Fellowship by IIAS Shimla. At present, he teaches literature at North-Eastern Hill University.

b: L. P. Pant is a writer and journalist focusing on the environment. His 18-year career has seen him write for a majority of the country’s leading Hindi newspapers as well as several literary magazines. Himalaya ka…
f: L. P. Pant is a writer and journalist focusing on the environment. His 18-year career has seen him write for a majority of the country’s leading Hindi newspapers as well as several literary magazines. Himalaya ka Kabristan , his book on the 2013 Kedarnath tragedy, was featured on several annual lists of acclaimed books in 2017. The book includes first hand reporting on the disaster known as the ‘Himalayan tsunami’ in which thousands lost their lives and remain missing. An avid traveller, his reporting on tiger poaching and the impact of militancy on the environment have brought him recognition across India. Pant currently works as State Editor, Rajasthan for Dainik Bhaskar .

b: Lakshmi Puri was the youngest entrant into the Indian Foreign Service. After representing India abroad in key bilateral and multilateral diplomatic assignments for twenty-eight years, she went on to serve at the United…
f: Lakshmi Puri was the youngest entrant into the Indian Foreign Service. After representing India abroad in key bilateral and multilateral diplomatic assignments for twenty-eight years, she went on to serve at the United Nations for fifteen years in various leadership capacities. She has been honoured with the Eleanor Roosevelt Human Rights Award, the Novus Award for Championing the Sustainable Development Goals, the Millennium Campus Award, and the Global Generation Award as an Inspiration for Youth, among others. She is a distinguished fellow of the Indian Association of International Studies, and a visiting professor at the South Asian University, New Delhi. Puri is also the author of the national bestseller and critically acclaimed novel Swallowing the Sun. The book has received several literary honours, including the Kalinga Literary Award, the Delhi Literature Festival Fiction Prize, the Pandit Hari Dutt Sharma Award, the Special Jury Award at the FICCI Publishing Awards for Book of the Year–Fiction (English), and the REC-VoW Book Award for English Fiction. It is being translated into multiple Indian languages and adapted into a web series by Abundantia Entertainment.

b: Lakshya Datta is an entrepreneur, writer and podcaster. He is the founder of Launchora, a storytelling platform and narrative podcast company, home to 200,000 storytellers and six podcasts. He is the host of the Jaipur…
f: Lakshya Datta is an entrepreneur, writer and podcaster. He is the founder of Launchora, a storytelling platform and narrative podcast company, home to 200,000 storytellers and six podcasts. He is the host of the Jaipur Literature Festival podcast, Jaipur Bytes . Before setting up Launchora, Datta was a lecturer at San Diego State University.

b: Lamorna Ash is a writer whose debut book Dark Salt Clear won the Somerset Maugham Prize. She is currently working on her second book, Don’t Forget We’re Here Forever: A New Generation’s Search for Religion , set for…
f: Lamorna Ash is a writer whose debut book Dark Salt Clear won the Somerset Maugham Prize. She is currently working on her second book, Don’t Forget We’re Here Forever: A New Generation’s Search for Religion , set for release in May 2025. Ash’s writing appears in The Guardian , Times , TLS , and other major publications. She is a MacDowell Fellow.

b: Lathika George is a writer, landscape designer, environmentalist and organic gardener. She is the author of The Kerala Kitchen , adapted for India as The Suriani Kitchen. She has published articles on food, design,…
f: Lathika George is a writer, landscape designer, environmentalist and organic gardener. She is the author of The Kerala Kitchen , adapted for India as The Suriani Kitchen. She has published articles on food, design, travel, gardening and the environment in Inside Outside , Architectural Digest , Food 52 , Conde Nast Traveller and Hindu BLink . Her garden design column, ‘The Constant Gardener’, ran in the Business Standard weekend’s supplement in 2011. She has a column on organic kitchen gardening in the Hindu Metro Plus called ‘The Essential Kitchen Gardener’. Her next book Mother Earth, Sister Seed, Travels to India’s Farmlands will be published in January, 2018.

b: Latika Nath is one of the first wildlife biologists with a D.Phil on Tiger Conservation and Management from the University of Oxford. She is the first female wildlife biologist in India to work on tigers and entered the…
f: Latika Nath is one of the first wildlife biologists with a D.Phil on Tiger Conservation and Management from the University of Oxford. She is the first female wildlife biologist in India to work on tigers and entered the field of tiger conservation at a time when no holistic scientific work had been done on the tiger in India. Nath has spent over 25 years working at the grassroots level for tiger conservation. Her life and work have been featured on National Geographic in a documentary called The Tiger Princess and on the Discovery Channel’s Wild Things / She has recently published the acclaimed coffee table book titled Hidden India on the wildlife and wilderness spaces of India.

b: Laura Lindstedt became a critical darling with her adoption-themed debut novel Scissors , which earned her a nomination for the Finlandia Prize, the country’s most prestigious literary honour. Lindstedt’s second…
f: Laura Lindstedt became a critical darling with her adoption-themed debut novel Scissors , which earned her a nomination for the Finlandia Prize, the country’s most prestigious literary honour. Lindstedt’s second novel Oneiron is a work of speculative fiction that takes place in the mysterious moments that follow one’s death and won the coveted 2015 Finlandia Prize. Lindstedt’s third novel My Friend Natalia will be published in March 2019.

b: Laura Spinney is the author of Pale Rider: The Spanish Flu of 1918 and How it Changed the World , a non-fiction account of the 20th century’s worst disaster The Observer called “magisterial”. She writes on science…
f: Laura Spinney is the author of Pale Rider: The Spanish Flu of 1918 and How it Changed the World , a non-fiction account of the 20th century’s worst disaster The Observer called “magisterial”. She writes on science for The Economist , National Geographic and the Guardian, and has published novels.

b: Lavinia Frey has been the Director of the International Literature Festival Berlin since 2023. She previously worked as a director, choreographer, and dramaturg at renowned theatres, including Schauspielhaus Zurich and…
f: Lavinia Frey has been the Director of the International Literature Festival Berlin since 2023. She previously worked as a director, choreographer, and dramaturg at renowned theatres, including Schauspielhaus Zurich and Maxim Gorki Theatre Berlin. In 2007, she co-founded the cultural and concept agency Graf & Frey. From 2016 to 2023, she held senior leadership roles at the Humboldt Forum in Berlin, overseeing international exhibitions and cultural programs.

b: Laxmi Prasad Pant is the National Editor, Dainik Bhaskar Group. Better known as a Writer and Journalist for nature. With a PhD. in City Reporting, he has a knack for leading path breaking journalism. He has written a…
f: Laxmi Prasad Pant is the National Editor, Dainik Bhaskar Group. Better known as a Writer and Journalist for nature. With a PhD. in City Reporting, he has a knack for leading path breaking journalism. He has written a Book on Kedarnath Tragedy ‘Himalaya ka kabristan’. The Himalayan tsunami in 2013 destroyed Kedarnath, in which thousands of people died and thousands are still missing. He himself reported for the Disaster and book contains his firsthand account of tragedy. He has also written a book titled ‘Newsman at work’ based on sensitive examples from city reporting which was released in JLF 2019. He is currently working for Dainik Bhaskar as National Editor. From last 25 years he has worked with almost all leading Hindi newspaper and few literary magazines. He has reported a number of stories on Environment, mountains, rivers, forest and animals. His love for Mother Nature has made him an avid traveler, writer and mountaineer. His reporting on Uttarakhand tragedy and tiger poaching in Sariska has brought him recognition all over the nation.

b: Leeladhar Mandloi is a writer, poet, filmmaker and photographer. He has published 36 books on poetry, literature and culture and produced/directed documentary films on numerous culturarl and literary personalities. In…
f: Leeladhar Mandloi is a writer, poet, filmmaker and photographer. He has published 36 books on poetry, literature and culture and produced/directed documentary films on numerous culturarl and literary personalities. In 2018, he displayed his abstract photography work in a solo exhibition at Bharat Kala Bhawan in Banares. He is the recipient of various national awards and honours including, the Kabir Sammam, the Sharmsher Samman, the Pushkin Sammam, Nagarjun Samman, the Dushyant Samman, the Raza Award, the Ram Vilas Sharma Samman, the Kriti Samman and the Sahityakar Samman. He is currently the Chief Executive Officer of Vani Prakashan and the Vani Foundation.

b: Leïla Slimani is the author of a well-received first novel, Dans le jardin de l’ogre ( In the Ogre’s Garden ), and Chanson douce ( Lullaby ), which won several awards including the Goncourt Prize in 2016.
f: Leïla Slimani is the author of a well-received first novel, Dans le jardin de l’ogre ( In the Ogre’s Garden ), and Chanson douce ( Lullaby ), which won several awards including the Goncourt Prize in 2016.

b: Lemn Sissay is a poet, playwright, artist performer and broadcaster. He has read on stage throughout the world from The Library of Congress in The United States to the University of Addis Ababa as well as Singapore, Sri…
f: Lemn Sissay is a poet, playwright, artist performer and broadcaster. He has read on stage throughout the world from The Library of Congress in The United States to the University of Addis Ababa as well as Singapore, Sri Lanka, Bangalore, Dubai, Bali, Greenland and Wigan library.

b: Lena Khalaf Tuffaha is a poet, essayist, and translator and the author of three acclaimed poetry collections. Her most recent book, Something About Living (UAkron, 2024), won the National Book Award and the Akron Prize…
f: Lena Khalaf Tuffaha is a poet, essayist, and translator and the author of three acclaimed poetry collections. Her most recent book, Something About Living (UAkron, 2024), won the National Book Award and the Akron Prize for Poetry. Her earlier works include Kaan & Her Sisters (2023), a Firecracker Award finalist, and Water & Salt (2017), winner of the Washington State Book Award. Her writing appears in major journals such as Los Angeles Review of Books , The Nation , and Poets.org , and in several anthologies. She holds a BA in Comparative Literature and an MFA, and lives in Redmond, Washington.

b: Lenora Chu is a Chinese-American journalist and author of the award-winning Little Soldiers, about China’s education system. She is an internationally-recognised expert on education in China, one of the world’s top…
f: Lenora Chu is a Chinese-American journalist and author of the award-winning Little Soldiers, about China’s education system. She is an internationally-recognised expert on education in China, one of the world’s top suppliers of students and talent abroad. Chu has appeared on NPR, BBC and the CBC, and her articles have been published in The Wall Street Journal, The New York Times, Business Insider , and others.

b: Leo Varadkar served as Prime Minister (Taoiseach) of Ireland from 2017 to 2020 and again from 2022 to 2024. He was the youngest person ever elected to the office and the first of Indian heritage. His father is from…
f: Leo Varadkar served as Prime Minister (Taoiseach) of Ireland from 2017 to 2020 and again from 2022 to 2024. He was the youngest person ever elected to the office and the first of Indian heritage. His father is from Maharashtra. Currently a senior fellow at the Harvard Kennedy School, he also writes a column for the Sunday Times and serves on the board of Global Citizen Europe. His memoir, Speaking My Mind , was a non-fiction bestseller and has been nominated for an Irish Book Award. A medical doctor by training, he is a graduate of Trinity College Dublin.

b: Léonora Miano is the author of 14 books, most of which have been translated into various languages. Born in Cameroon, she moved to France as a student. Her award-winning first novel, L’intérieur de la nuit , was…
f: Léonora Miano is the author of 14 books, most of which have been translated into various languages. Born in Cameroon, she moved to France as a student. Her award-winning first novel, L’intérieur de la nuit , was released in 2005. Her other books include Contours du jour qui vient , which was awarded the Prix Goncourt des Lycéens, Ecrits pour la parole , which won the Prix Seligmann contre le racisme and La saison de l’ombre , winner of the Prix Fémina and the Grand prix du roman metis.

b: Leïla Slimani’s first novel Dans le Jardin de l'ogre was published in 2014. Two years later, she won the Prix Goncourt with her second novel, Chanson douce . She is also a journalist, activist and author of the…
f: Leïla Slimani’s first novel Dans le Jardin de l'ogre was published in 2014. Two years later, she won the Prix Goncourt with her second novel, Chanson douce . She is also a journalist, activist and author of the nonfiction book Sexe et mensonges, about the sexual life of Moroccan women.

b: Likla writes for children about art, including the IPPY award-winning book Art is a Verb, published by Art1st. She also writes for Little Light on a curriculum about the Self, and for PanicNot!, a TTRPG publisher and…
f: Likla writes for children about art, including the IPPY award-winning book Art is a Verb, published by Art1st. She also writes for Little Light on a curriculum about the Self, and for PanicNot!, a TTRPG publisher and storytelling collective. Beyond an ardent love for books, she finds joy in a lifelong practice of dance and movement.

b: Lilly Singh is a multi-faceted entertainer, actress, producer, writer and creator. A leading force in the digital world, she has amassed a global audience of over 38 million followers across her social media channels,…
f: Lilly Singh is a multi-faceted entertainer, actress, producer, writer and creator. A leading force in the digital world, she has amassed a global audience of over 38 million followers across her social media channels, where she writes, directs, produces and stars in comedic and inspirational videos. Singh recently struck a first-look deal with Universal Television Alternative Studio (UTAS) with her Unicorn Island Productions banner. Currently, she is developing numerous projects across film and television. This April, Singh will appear in the second season of Hulu’s comedy Dollface and appear on the big screen starring in DreamWorks Animation’s action-comedy Bad Guys.

b: Linda Spalding edits Brick, A Literary Journal . Her novels include Daughters of Captain Cook , The Paper Wife and Mere , co-authored with Esta Spalding. Her nonfiction books, A Dark Place in the Jungle and Who Named…
f: Linda Spalding edits Brick, A Literary Journal . Her novels include Daughters of Captain Cook , The Paper Wife and Mere , co-authored with Esta Spalding. Her nonfiction books, A Dark Place in the Jungle and Who Named the Knife , were followed by the novels The Purchase , which won Canada’s highest literary award, and A Reckoning , forthcoming in spring 2018.

b: Lindsay Pereira is a journalist and editor. He holds a PhD in literature for his work on gender attitudes implicit in nineteenth-century Indian fiction. He was co-editor of the anthology Women’s Voices published by…
f: Lindsay Pereira is a journalist and editor. He holds a PhD in literature for his work on gender attitudes implicit in nineteenth-century Indian fiction. He was co-editor of the anthology Women’s Voices published by Oxford University Press, and his first novel, Gods and Ends , was shortlisted for the 2021 JCB Prize for Literature, and Tata Literature Live! First Book Award for Fiction.

b: Lindsey Hilsum is the author of In Extremis: the Life of War Correspondent Marie Colvin , which won the 2019 James Tait Black prize for Biography and has been shortlisted for the Costa Award. She is also International…
f: Lindsey Hilsum is the author of In Extremis: the Life of War Correspondent Marie Colvin , which won the 2019 James Tait Black prize for Biography and has been shortlisted for the Costa Award. She is also International Editor of Britain’s Channel 4 News and has covered many of the conflicts of the last 30 years. Her first book was Sandstorm: Libya in the Time of Revolution.

b: Lindy Cameron CB OBE has been British High Commissioner to the Republic of India since April 2024. Previously, Lindy was CEO of the UK’s National Cyber Security Centre (2020-2024), following more than two decades of…
f: Lindy Cameron CB OBE has been British High Commissioner to the Republic of India since April 2024. Previously, Lindy was CEO of the UK’s National Cyber Security Centre (2020-2024), following more than two decades of international development and national security policy and crisis management. Before that she served as Director-General in the Northern Ireland Office (2019-2020) and as Director General Country Programmes at the Department for International Development (2016-2019). Lindy is from Northern Ireland. After starting her career in the private sector, she joined the Department for International Development (DFID) in 1998, working as an adviser in Nigeria, Vietnam and the Balkans, before moving on to run DFID’s offices in Baghdad and Kabul. She led DFID humanitarian, conflict and Middle East policy after the Arab Spring. She has worked across government: for the Cabinet Office during the financial crisis; for the Foreign Office as the Head of the Provincial Reconstruction team in Helmand, Afghanistan; with the Ministry of Defence on their senior staff courses, and as head of the joint cross-government Stabilisation Unit.

b: Lisa Randall studies theoretical particle physics and cosmology at Harvard University. Professor Randall’s research connects theoretical insights addressing puzzles in our understanding of the properties of matter,…
f: Lisa Randall studies theoretical particle physics and cosmology at Harvard University. Professor Randall’s research connects theoretical insights addressing puzzles in our understanding of the properties of matter, the universe, and space. Her current focus is on dark matter. Her latest book, Dark Matter and the Dinosaurs , is a sweeping overview of the evolution of the Universe, the Milky Way, the Solar System and life. Randall’s books Warped Passages and Knocking on Heaven’s Door were featured on the New York Times’ lists of ‘100 Notable Books’. Her e-book, Higgs Discovery: The Power of Empty Space , was published in 2012. In 2003, she received the Premio Caterina Tomassoni e Felice Pietro Chisesi Award, from the University of Rome, La Sapienza. In 2006, she received the Klopsteg Award from the American Society of Physics Teachers (AAPT) for her lectures and in 2007 she received the Julius Lilienfeld Prize from the American Physical Society for her work on elementary particle physics and cosmology and for communicating this work to the public. Randall’s studies have made her among the most cited and influential theoretical physicists.

b: Lisa Ray is an internationally acclaimed performer, philanthropist, author and public speaker with a reputation for taking on challenging issue-oriented films. She is one of India’s most successful models and an…
f: Lisa Ray is an internationally acclaimed performer, philanthropist, author and public speaker with a reputation for taking on challenging issue-oriented films. She is one of India’s most successful models and an award-winning actress who starred in Canada’s Oscar nominated film Water. After Ray was diagnosed with Multiple Myeloma in 2009, her forthright, courageous and humorous approach to navigating her experiences with this incurable blood cancer, which she chronicled in her blog, ‘The Yellow Diaries’, earned her international respect. She is the author of the memoir Close to the Bone and recently signed a deal with her publisher Harper Collins to write three more books.

b: Lisa Taddeo is an author, journalist and a two-time recipient of the Pushcart Prize for her short stories 42 (2017) . Her 2019 non-fiction book, Three Women , became a #1 New York Times and the international bestseller…
f: Lisa Taddeo is an author, journalist and a two-time recipient of the Pushcart Prize for her short stories 42 (2017) . Her 2019 non-fiction book, Three Women , became a #1 New York Times and the international bestseller and is currently being adapted by Showtime as a TV series. Taddeo's debut novel, Animal , was published in June 2021.

b: Livia Manera Sambuy is an Italian cultural journalist, documentary filmmaker, and author. Her book of profiles of American writers, Don’t Write About Me, was published in 2015. She is the author of two documentary films…
f: Livia Manera Sambuy is an Italian cultural journalist, documentary filmmaker, and author. Her book of profiles of American writers, Don’t Write About Me, was published in 2015. She is the author of two documentary films on Philip Roth. Her narrative nonfiction book In Search of Amrit Kaur won the Capalbio International Award in 2023.

f: Lorenzo Angeloni is an Italian diplomat who has served in Uruguay, Germany, Algeria, Sudan AND Vietnam. He is currently the Italian Ambassador to India and Nepal. He is the author of numerous works of fiction and non-fiction. Angeloni’s most recent publications are the novels The Perfet Crises and The Quarantine.

b: Louis-Philippe Dalembert is a Haitian poet and novelist who writes in both French and Haitian Creole. His works have been translated into several languages, and he has received many prizes and awards, including a…
f: Louis-Philippe Dalembert is a Haitian poet and novelist who writes in both French and Haitian Creole. His works have been translated into several languages, and he has received many prizes and awards, including a residency at the Villa Medicis in Rome, the Grand Prix de la langue française, Polish and Swiss Goncourt Choice 2019, and Goncourt des lycéens shortlist for his novel, The Mediterranean Wall. Dalembert has traveled widely as a teacher and visiting poet, and taught briefly at the University of Wisconsin, the Freie Universität (Berlin) and the University of Bern. He currently holds the Writer-in-Residence Chair at Sciences Po, Paris.

b: Gen. Nanavatty was commissioned in December 1962 into the Second Battalion of the Eighth Gorkha Rifles (2/8GR). Over a distinguished 40-year career, he served as Northern Army Commander during turbulent times,…
f: Gen. Nanavatty was commissioned in December 1962 into the Second Battalion of the Eighth Gorkha Rifles (2/8GR). Over a distinguished 40-year career, he served as Northern Army Commander during turbulent times, commanding units such as the Para Commando Task Force in Sri Lanka, the Siachen Brigade, and a corps in the northeast during heightened insurgencies. Post-retirement, Nanavatty authored Internal Armed Conflict in India .

b: Lucy Beresford is an award-winning writer, broadcaster and psychotherapist whose books have been translated into multiple languages. She is the author of three novels - Something I’m Not, Invisible Threads and Hungry…
f: Lucy Beresford is an award-winning writer, broadcaster and psychotherapist whose books have been translated into multiple languages. She is the author of three novels - Something I’m Not, Invisible Threads and Hungry For Love , and a self-help book titled Happy Relationships at Home, Work and Play. Invisible Threads is set in New Delhi and was shortlisted for the Rubery International Prize. Beresford is currently working on the book-to-film adaptation.

b: Lucy Caldwell is the author of four novels, several stage plays and radio dramas, and three collections of stories. A Fellow of the Royal Society of Literature, her many awards include the BBC National Short Story…
f: Lucy Caldwell is the author of four novels, several stage plays and radio dramas, and three collections of stories. A Fellow of the Royal Society of Literature, her many awards include the BBC National Short Story Award, the Walter Scott Prize for Historical Fiction and the EM Forster Award from the American Academy of Arts & Letters.

b: Lucy Hughes-Hallett ’s biography of Gabriele d’Annunzio, The Pike , won all three of the UK’s most prestigious awards for nonfiction. Her novel, Peculiar Ground , has been acclaimed for its compelling…
f: Lucy Hughes-Hallett ’s biography of Gabriele d’Annunzio, The Pike , won all three of the UK’s most prestigious awards for nonfiction. Her novel, Peculiar Ground , has been acclaimed for its compelling story-telling and the light it sheds on the urgent contemporary issues of migration and exclusion.

b: Luke Coutinho is India’s leading voice in Integrative and Lifestyle Medicine, making wellness simple, accessible, and transformative. As the Wellness Champion for Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Fit India Movement and a…
f: Luke Coutinho is India’s leading voice in Integrative and Lifestyle Medicine, making wellness simple, accessible, and transformative. As the Wellness Champion for Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Fit India Movement and a bestselling author, he inspires millions with practical guidance to prevent disease, strengthen foundational health, and create lasting lifestyle change for all.

b: Luke Harding is a journalist, writer, and award-winning correspondent for The Guardian . He is a former Moscow bureau chief and reported from Delhi between 2000-2003. Harding is the author of numerous books, including…
f: Luke Harding is a journalist, writer, and award-winning correspondent for The Guardian . He is a former Moscow bureau chief and reported from Delhi between 2000-2003. Harding is the author of numerous books, including Invasion: The Inside Story of Russia's Bloody War and Ukraine's Fight for Survival , published in November by Faber in London and Vintage in New York.

b: Luke Syson is the fourteenth Director of the Fitzwilliam Museum. From 2012-19, he was Chairman of European Sculpture and Decorative Arts at the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York, where he led on the complete…
f: Luke Syson is the fourteenth Director of the Fitzwilliam Museum. From 2012-19, he was Chairman of European Sculpture and Decorative Arts at the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York, where he led on the complete refurbishment of the British Galleries, a $22m project, which opened in March 2020. Luke has held curatorial positions at the British Museum, the V & A and the National Gallery – where he led the successful campaign to acquire Raphael’s Madonna of the Pinks for the nation and curated the highly-acclaimed exhibition, ‘Leonardo da Vinci – Painter at the Court of Milan’ in 2011. Since arriving in Cambridge, he has overseen the refurbishment of the Fitzwilliam’s primary painting galleries.

b: Lulu Raghavan , President of APAC at Landor, is a branding leader with 24 years of experience across global studios. She spearheaded Landor's growth in India, leading brand transformation programmes for Tata, Mahindra,…
f: Lulu Raghavan , President of APAC at Landor, is a branding leader with 24 years of experience across global studios. She spearheaded Landor's growth in India, leading brand transformation programmes for Tata, Mahindra, Godrej and others. A mentor, educator, and women’s advocate, Lulu serves on advisory boards, teaches branding, and champions leadership.

b: M Mukundan is a well-known fiction writer from Kerala and has over forty books to his credit. He was presented with the Ezhuthachan Puraskaram, the highest State award in Kerala, the insignia of Chevalier in the Order…
f: M Mukundan is a well-known fiction writer from Kerala and has over forty books to his credit. He was presented with the Ezhuthachan Puraskaram, the highest State award in Kerala, the insignia of Chevalier in the Order of Arts and Letters by the Government of France, and is a two-time winner of the Crossword Award. He was President of the Kerala Sahitya Akademi, and won the JCB Prize for Literature in 2021 for his novel Delhi: A Soliloquy .

b: M.K. Raina is a celebrated theatre personality with over four decades of experience as an actor, director, and filmmaker. He has played a key role in reviving Kashmir’s traditional folk theatre, Bhand Pather , and has…
f: M.K. Raina is a celebrated theatre personality with over four decades of experience as an actor, director, and filmmaker. He has played a key role in reviving Kashmir’s traditional folk theatre, Bhand Pather , and has worked with urban and rural communities in South Asia. A recipient of the Sangeet-Natak Akademi Award and several other honours, Raina is also a social and cultural activist, founder of SAHMAT, and Artistic Director of the theatre group Prayog. He has taught at various institutions and held fellowships at Stanford and Jamia Millia University.

b: M.K. Ranjitsinh , from the royal family of Wankaner, joined the IAS in 1961. As the collector of Mandla, MP, he played a key role in saving the central Indian ‘barasingha’ from extinction. During his tenure as secretary…
f: M.K. Ranjitsinh , from the royal family of Wankaner, joined the IAS in 1961. As the collector of Mandla, MP, he played a key role in saving the central Indian ‘barasingha’ from extinction. During his tenure as secretary for forests and tourism in MP, he established fourteen new sanctuaries and eight national parks, significantly expanding protected areas.

b: MS Jodha was commissioned into the Indian Army in December 1985. He is a third-generation officer with both his sons now also serving officers in the Indian Army. Brig. Jodha’s interest in the Indian story of the…
f: MS Jodha was commissioned into the Indian Army in December 1985. He is a third-generation officer with both his sons now also serving officers in the Indian Army. Brig. Jodha’s interest in the Indian story of the Great War grew out of his research into the wartime experience of his grandfather Lt. Col.Aman Singh, OBI, IOM, who led the famous cavalry charge by the Jodhpur Lancers at Haifa on 23 September, 1918. His research spanning more than a decade paved the way for immortalising the valour of Indian soldiers in the eyes of India and the world. The Story of the Jodhpur Lancers is his first book.

b: Ma Thida is a Burmese medical doctor, writer, human rights activist and former prisoner of conscience. She was awarded several international human rights awards, including the Reebok Human Rights Award, the PEN/Barbara…
f: Ma Thida is a Burmese medical doctor, writer, human rights activist and former prisoner of conscience. She was awarded several international human rights awards, including the Reebok Human Rights Award, the PEN/Barbara Goldsmith Freedom to Write Award, the Freedom of Speech Award and the Vaclav Havel’s Courageous Writer at Risk Award. She was elected as the first president of PEN Myanmar in late 2013 and was elected as one of the board members of PEN International in 2016. She currently edits Info Digest journal.

b: Justice Madan B. Lokur , presently a Judge of the Supreme Court of Fiji, was enrolled as a lawyer in 1977. He was appointed the Additional Solicitor General of India, and has also been a Judge of the Delhi High Court…
f: Justice Madan B. Lokur , presently a Judge of the Supreme Court of Fiji, was enrolled as a lawyer in 1977. He was appointed the Additional Solicitor General of India, and has also been a Judge of the Delhi High Court and later the Chief Justice, Gauhati and Andhra Pradesh High Courts. He was a Judge of the Supreme Court of India till December, 2018.

b: Madhav Kaushik is a Hindi-language poet and writer. A recipient of the 2006 Akhil Bhartiya Balraj Sahni Award, the 2010 MahaKavi Surdas Samman and the 2012 Shiromani Sahityakar Samman, he has 33 books of poetry and…
f: Madhav Kaushik is a Hindi-language poet and writer.
