Some of his work has been translated into Punjabi, Urdu, Sanskrit, Oriya and Assamese. He also serves as Chairman of the Chandigarh Sahitya Akademi and Vice President of the National Sahitya Akademi in New Delhi.

b: Madhav Khosla is an Associate Professor of Political Science at Ashoka University, the Ambedkar Visiting Associate Professor of Law at Columbia University and a Junior Fellow at the Harvard Society of Fellows. His most…
f: Madhav Khosla is an Associate Professor of Political Science at Ashoka University, the Ambedkar Visiting Associate Professor of Law at Columbia University and a Junior Fellow at the Harvard Society of Fellows. His most recent book, India’s Founding Moment, is on the making of India’s Constitution.

b: Madhavan Narayanan is an editor, journalist, writer and columnist with more than 35 years of experience in both Indian and international environments. He has worked for media organisations and publications including…
f: Madhavan Narayanan is an editor, journalist, writer and columnist with more than 35 years of experience in both Indian and international environments. He has worked for media organisations and publications including Reuters, The Economic Times, Business Standard and Hindustan Times . Narayanan regularly features as a commentator on BBC radio, ET Now and Mirror Now, in addition to writing for The Quint, The Economic Times and other publications. His recent ventures with partners include Knowledge Factory, an annual festival of insights and ideas. He has also translated a Tamil novel into English which is due for publication by HarperCollins.

b: Madhavi Menon is Professor of English at Ashoka University and the author, most recently, of Infinite Variety: A History of Desire in India . She is also the Director of the Centre for Studies in Gender and Sexuality at…
f: Madhavi Menon is Professor of English at Ashoka University and the author, most recently, of Infinite Variety: A History of Desire in India . She is also the Director of the Centre for Studies in Gender and Sexuality at Ashoka University.

b: Madhu Acharya is a renowned Rajasthani writer, journalist and poet. Acharya has also worked in theatre having acted in, written and directed over 200 plays. Acharya is the executive editor of Dainik Bhaskar (Bikaner)…
f: Madhu Acharya is a renowned Rajasthani writer, journalist and poet. Acharya has also worked in theatre having acted in, written and directed over 200 plays. Acharya is the executive editor of Dainik Bhaskar (Bikaner) and a recipient of the Shambhu-Shekhar Saxaina Journalism Award. With 66 books in Hindi and Rajasthani to his name, he has won numerous awards for his work, including the Sahitya Akademi for Rajasthani's first postmodern novel Gawad. His literature has been included in the syllabus of Maharaja Ganga Singh University. He currently serves as Convener of the Rajasthani Language Advisory Board of the Sahitya Akademi.

b: Madhu Sharma is the author of a poetry book titled Moh ke Dhaage. She launched a page called Madhu ke Shabd on Facebook to share poetry and quotes, which has gained a strong following of 1.7K+ members. She is a…
f: Madhu Sharma is the author of a poetry book titled Moh ke Dhaage. She launched a page called Madhu ke Shabd on Facebook to share poetry and quotes, which has gained a strong following of 1.7K+ members. She is a participant in talk shows relating to literature on All India Radio. She from the position of News Anchor on Doordarshan for over 12 years on prime time Hindi news.

b: Madhu Trehan is the co-founder and Editor-in-Chief of Newslaundry . A veteran journalist and writer, Trehan was also the founding editor of India Today and founded, produced and anchored Newstrack , India’s first…
f: Madhu Trehan is the co-founder and Editor-in-Chief of Newslaundry . A veteran journalist and writer, Trehan was also the founding editor of India Today and founded, produced and anchored Newstrack , India’s first video news magazine. She has authored the book Prism Me a Lie Tell Me A Truth, Tehelka As Metaphor .

b: Madhur Jaffrey is the author of several cookbooks, seven of which have won James Beard Awards, and named the Who’s Who of Food and Beverage in America by the James Beard Foundation. She is the recipient of an honorary…
f: Madhur Jaffrey is the author of several cookbooks, seven of which have won James Beard Awards, and named the Who’s Who of Food and Beverage in America by the James Beard Foundation. She is the recipient of an honorary CBE and is also an award-winning actress, having won the Silver Bear for Best Actress at the Berlin Film Festival, with numerous films to her credit.

b: Madhura Godbole is a senior professor at the American Institute of Indian Studies. She also works as a part time faculty of Sanskrit for YALE - NUS University of Singapore. Professor Godbole is widely acclaimed for her…
f: Madhura Godbole is a senior professor at the American Institute of Indian Studies. She also works as a part time faculty of Sanskrit for YALE - NUS University of Singapore. Professor Godbole is widely acclaimed for her original contributions in the teaching of Sanskrit to western PhD. students and scholars. She has written numerous short stories in Sanskrit and has composed dance dramas in Sanskrit for Bharatanatyam and Kuchipudi dancers. She is also a professional classical singer of north Indian music.

b: Madhureeta Anand is a highly accomplished filmmaker, with a directorial record comprising two narrative feature films. Her repertoire extends to encompass numerous documentary films and series, spanning various genres.…
f: Madhureeta Anand is a highly accomplished filmmaker, with a directorial record comprising two narrative feature films. Her repertoire extends to encompass numerous documentary films and series, spanning various genres. She is also a fervent advocate for the rights of women and children. Notably, she recently launched a global mobile application titled Phree For Safety, dedicated to women's safety. Madhureeta is also developing a series based on the influential book, Autobiography Of A Yogi , a collaborative venture involving several international partners. Furthermore, her fourth feature film, O Mere Piya , is set to start production in October 2025. Her debut novel, Krishna Circus , is currently in bookstores.

b: Madhushree Ghosh is an author & social justice activist who is an expert on South Asian (and global) food and the science and social ramifications of food, immigrant food and journeys, women in science and food. She is…
f: Madhushree Ghosh is an author & social justice activist who is an expert on South Asian (and global) food and the science and social ramifications of food, immigrant food and journeys, women in science and food. One Point Two Billion , his collection of short stories, was published in 2015, and his second novel, Polite Society , has just been published to critical acclaim.

f: Mahfuz Anam is the co-founder of The Daily Star, Bangladesh’s leading English daily, and is its editor-publisher from 1993, till date. b: Mahim Sagar is a professor at the Department of Management Studies at the Indian Institute of Technology in Delhi. He works in consumer-based and community driven marketing/branding of public and private goods and…
f: Mahim Sagar is a professor at the Department of Management Studies at the Indian Institute of Technology in Delhi. He works in consumer-based and community driven marketing/branding of public and private goods and services, which includes streams such as the challenges encountered in marketing public policy, ethical branding and product management. His research covers IT, telecoms, health, FMCG and Public Policy by using inductive and deductive protocols. He is a recipient of the Teaching Excellence Award at IIT Delhi.

b: Mahinda Deshapriya studied at Dharmasoka College, Ambalangoda. Graduated in Physical Science from the University of Peradeniya , joined his Alma Mater as a teacher of Chemistry and Mathematics. In 1982, he was recruited…
f: Mahinda Deshapriya studied at Dharmasoka College, Ambalangoda. Graduated in Physical Science from the University of Peradeniya , joined his Alma Mater as a teacher of Chemistry and Mathematics. In 1982, he was recruited to the Sri Lanka Administrative Service and was appointed as an Assistant Commissioner of the Department of Elections. He served in several districts, acquired Post Graduate Diploma from International Management Institute in New Delhi. He has served as a Deputy and an Additional Commissioner of Elections. He was appointed the Commissioner in March, 2011. He chaired the Forum of Election Management Bodies of South Asia for 2015-2016. He is the first Chairman of the Election Commission from 2015-2020 established under the 19th Amendment to the Constitution. He was awarded ‘The Sri Lankan of the Year’ by Lanka Market Digest in 2015 and ‘The Public Servant of the Year 2016’ by Derana TV-Sri Lanka. For his unstinted commitment to the Public Service he was felicitated by the University of Peradeniya. At present, he serves as the Chairman of the National Delimitation Commission.

b: Mahmood Farooqui was educated at The Doon School Dehradun, St Stephen's College Delhi and at the Universities of OXford and Cambridge where he studied as an Indian Rhodes Scholar and topped the University of Oxford in…
f: Mahmood Farooqui was educated at The Doon School Dehradun, St Stephen's College Delhi and at the Universities of OXford and Cambridge where he studied as an Indian Rhodes Scholar and topped the University of Oxford in History. He is an award winning writer and performer. He was awarded the Bismillah Khan Yuva Puraskar in 2010 for reviving Dastangoi.under the tutelage and mentorship of S R Faruqi. His books include Besieged: Voices from Delhi, 1857 on the uprising of 1857 which was' awarded the Ram Nath Goenka Award for best non-fiction book of 2010, and A Requiem for Pakistan: the World of Intizar Husain. apart from two books on Dastangoi in Hindi and Urdu. He has been a journalist and a columnist for numerous newspapers and has been a Visiting Fellow at the Universities of Michigan and Berkeley in the US Of the stories he has written for stage Dastan-e Chauboli and Dastan-e Karn az Mahabharat have enjoyed immense popularity with both enjoying hundreds of outings. He heads the Dastangoi Collective which is spearheading the revival of Dastangoi in India.

b: Maithree Wickramasinghe is the Chair and Senior Professor of English at the University of Kelaniya, Sri Lanka, and the founding Director of the Centre for Gender Studies. She's also a Visiting Professor at the…
f: Maithree Wickramasinghe is the Chair and Senior Professor of English at the University of Kelaniya, Sri Lanka, and the founding Director of the Centre for Gender Studies. She's also a Visiting Professor at the University of Sussex and an Honorary Professor at the University of Wolverhampton, UK. With over thirty years of experience, she's an expert in gender equity and equality policies, training, and programme evaluation for organisations like the ILO, UNFPA, and UNESCO. She is the author of From Theory to Action - Women, Gender and Development and was an Associate Editor of the Wiley Blackwell Encyclopaedia on Gender and Sexuality Studies . Other work includes an influential training module, An Introduction to Gender Mainstreaming Universities . Wickramasinghe is a Champion for the Commonwealth Secretariat's ‘Say No More Campaign’ and serves on various university boards, including the Asian University for Women in Bangladesh.

b: Maitreyi Bordia Das is the World Bank’s Global Lead for Social Inclusion. She started her career as a lecturer in St Stephen’s College, University of Delhi, was a MacArthur Fellow at the Harvard Centre of Population…
f: Maitreyi Bordia Das is the World Bank’s Global Lead for Social Inclusion. She started her career as a lecturer in St Stephen’s College, University of Delhi, was a MacArthur Fellow at the Harvard Centre of Population and Development Studies and advisor to UNDP in Guyana. Before joining the World Bank, Dr. Das was in the IAS.

b: Maja Lunde ’s first novel The History of Bees is a worldwide success and was the best-selling book in any genre in Germany in 2017 with more than 90 consecutive weeks on the German Bestseller list. The sequel Blue…
f: Maja Lunde ’s first novel The History of Bees is a worldwide success and was the best-selling book in any genre in Germany in 2017 with more than 90 consecutive weeks on the German Bestseller list. The sequel Blue will also be translated worldwide . Lunde has written several books for children and young adults as well as film/TV scripts. Her 2018 children’s book The Snow Sister is one of the biggest literary successes in Norway in decades and was instantly sold to publishing houses throughout the world. Lunde’s books have been translated into 36 languages.

b: Makarand R. Paranjape is a distinguished scholar, writer, and public intellectual. He served for nearly twenty-five years as Professor of English at Jawaharlal Nehru University, New Delhi, and was Director of the Indian…
f: Makarand R. Paranjape is a distinguished scholar, writer, and public intellectual. He served for nearly twenty-five years as Professor of English at Jawaharlal Nehru University, New Delhi, and was Director of the Indian Institute of Advanced Study, Shimla. Author or editor of over fifty books and hundreds of academic papers, he is also a poet, novelist, and columnist. His recent books include Hindutva and Hind Swaraj: History’s Forgotten Doubles (2025), Mahatma Gandhi: Mrityu aur Punarutthan (2024), The Penguin Sri Aurobindo Reader (2023), and Identity’s Last Secret (2022). He is currently Sri Aurobindo Chair (Honorary) at Vedere University and Director of Education at Access Health Care Physicians, Florida.

b: Malala Yousafzai is an education advocate, youngest Nobel laureate, Oxford University graduate and co-founder of Malala Fund. At age 15, she was attacked by the Taliban for advocating for girls' education in Pakistan.…
f: Malala Yousafzai is an education advocate, youngest Nobel laureate, Oxford University graduate and co-founder of Malala Fund. At age 15, she was attacked by the Taliban for advocating for girls' education in Pakistan. She won the Nobel Peace Prize for her efforts to see every girl in school.

b: Malavika Rajkotia is a leading divorce lawyer in Delhi. She has worked with various NGOs on civil liberties and human rights issues. She has also been active in theatre and involved in about thirty Hindi and English…
f: Malavika Rajkotia is a leading divorce lawyer in Delhi. She has worked with various NGOs on civil liberties and human rights issues. She has also been active in theatre and involved in about thirty Hindi and English productions. She anchored Shakti, the first television talk show in India which focused on women’s rights.

b: Malchand Tiwari is a senior scholar and has been associated with Rajasthan Sahitya Akademi, Udaipur as an Advisor, Editor and Member of the General Assembly. He also has been the Secretary of Rajasthani Bhasha, Sahitya…
f: Malchand Tiwari is a senior scholar and has been associated with Rajasthan Sahitya Akademi, Udaipur as an Advisor, Editor and Member of the General Assembly. He also has been the Secretary of Rajasthani Bhasha, Sahitya Evam Sanskriti Academy, Bikaner. Many of his books have been published in Hindi and Rajasthani. He has been awarded with many prestigious honours such as the Rajasthani Sahitya Puraskar, GaneshiLal Vyas Ustad Rajsthani Padm Puraskar, and Lakhotiya Puraskar. He has knowledge of many languages including Hindi, Rajasthani, English, Assamese and Bengali.

b: Malcolm Donaldson qualified in medicine at Bristol University in 1973. From 1989 until his retirement in 2012, he worked as a Senior Lecturer in Child Health at Glasgow University. Since retirement, Dr Donaldson has…
f: Malcolm Donaldson qualified in medicine at Bristol University in 1973. From 1989 until his retirement in 2012, he worked as a Senior Lecturer in Child Health at Glasgow University. Since retirement, Dr Donaldson has continued to be active in international teaching, research and some clinical work. He also accompanies his wife, the children’s writer Julia Donaldson, at book festivals, school and library events where he acts and plays the guitar in her sell-out shows.

b: The Honourable Malcolm Turnbull AC, Australia’s 29th Prime Minister, reformed Australia’s personal income tax, education and childcare systems, oversaw the legalisation of same-sex marriage and announced the…
f: The Honourable Malcolm Turnbull AC, Australia’s 29th Prime Minister, reformed Australia’s personal income tax, education and childcare systems, oversaw the legalisation of same-sex marriage and announced the construction of Snowy Hydro 2.0, the biggest pumped hydro scheme in the southern hemisphere. As a young lawyer, he successfully defended former MI5 agent Peter Wright against the British Government in the 1986 ‘Spycatcher’ trial before running his own investment banking firm and joining Goldman Sachs as partner. Mr Turnbull has been a successful venture capitalist and co-founded OzEmail Limited, the first Australian tech company to be listed on NASDAQ. He is currently a senior adviser to KKR and a director of the International Hydropower Association and Chairman of Australian Fortescue Future Industries. Mr Turnbull speaks and writes on a range of issues including cyber security, geopolitics and renewable energy.

b: Malika Verma Kashyap is the founder of Border&Fall , a digital publication and strategic agency. Her work acknowledges change makers of India’s fashion and craft community and the multi-disciplinary agency specialises…
f: Malika Verma Kashyap is the founder of Border&Fall , a digital publication and strategic agency. Her work acknowledges change makers of India’s fashion and craft community and the multi-disciplinary agency specialises in business development across branding, digital, retail and creative direction. B order&Fall ’s portfolio includes ongoing talks, residencies and ‘The Sari Project’, a cultural film documentation of India’s regional sari drapes.

b: Padmashree Malini Awasthi is a celebrated exponent of Hindustani classical and folk music of India, renowned for upholding the rich musical legacy of Uttar Pradesh, especially from Banaras and Awadh region. Malini is a…
f: Padmashree Malini Awasthi is a celebrated exponent of Hindustani classical and folk music of India, renowned for upholding the rich musical legacy of Uttar Pradesh, especially from Banaras and Awadh region. Malini is a disciple of the legendary artist PadmaVibhushan Girija Devi and Ustad Rahat Ali Khan. A “top-grade” artist at the All India Radio, she is a connoisseur of the Banaras gharana’s “four-pat” style, and known for her melodious rendering of semi-classical genres like thumri, dadra, kajri and tappa . A very popular face across India’s TV channels, she has also lent her voice to many films like Agent Vinod, Dum Laga Ke Haisha , amongst others. From performing a jugalbandi with a jazz band at the Lincoln Center in New York to receiving the ‘Vishva Bhojpuri Samman’ by the Government of Mauritius and the ‘Tulsi Samman’ by the Dutch Government, Malini has been invited across the globe to spread the magic of India’s folk music.

b: Malini Saran, an independent Delhi-based researcher who did the fieldwork for her book during the twelve years she lived in Indonesia, Malaysia and the Philippines. Her papers on the Indonesian Ramayanas have appeared…
f: Malini Saran, an independent Delhi-based researcher who did the fieldwork for her book during the twelve years she lived in Indonesia, Malaysia and the Philippines. Her papers on the Indonesian Ramayanas have appeared in leading academic publications in India and abroad. Currently, Saran is completing a translation of Camille Bulcke’s book, Ramakatha: Uttapati aur Vikas, from Hindi into English, with co-author Vinod C Khanna.

b: Mallika Kapur is an international news journalist. She is currently a Senior Editor at Bloomberg Live, APAC. In her 20 year career that spans three countries, she has been a producer, anchor and correspondent for CNN in…
f: Mallika Kapur is an international news journalist. She is currently a Senior Editor at Bloomberg Live, APAC. In her 20 year career that spans three countries, she has been a producer, anchor and correspondent for CNN in London, Mumbai and Hong Kong. Kapur attended Brown University and Columbia’s University’s Graduate School of Journalism.

b: Malvika Singh is the publisher of Seminar, a prestigious journal of ideas, debate and discussion. She is the author of New Delhi: The Making of a Capital and Perpetual City: A Short Biography of Delhi , among others and…
f: Malvika Singh is the publisher of Seminar, a prestigious journal of ideas, debate and discussion. She is the author of New Delhi: The Making of a Capital and Perpetual City: A Short Biography of Delhi , among others and has edited a series on eight cities of India, extracted from the volumes of Seminar. Malvika was also the editor of the India magazine- the country's first cultural monthly and recently served as a member of the Advisory Council to the former Chief Minister of Rajasthan, Vasundhara Raje. She is currently working on Jewel in the Crown, a 14 part series based on Paul Scott's quartet, filmed in India and produced by Granada Television, London.

b: Mamang Dai is a poet and novelist from Arunachal Pradesh. A former journalist, Dai’s first publication, Arunachal Pradesh, the hidden land documented the culture and customs of her state for which she received the…
f: Mamang Dai is a poet and novelist from Arunachal Pradesh. A former journalist, Dai’s first publication, Arunachal Pradesh, the hidden land documented the culture and customs of her state for which she received the Verrier Elwin Award. Her other publications include novels, poetry and children’s literature. Dai also worked with the Worldwide Fund for Nature in the Eastern Himalayas Biodiversity Hotspots programme. In 2011, she was awarded the Padma Shri for literature and education.

b: Mamta Kalia is an Indian author, teacher and poet, writing primarily in Hindi and focusing predominantly on the lived experiences of women from middle-class families in India. Kalia won the Vyas Samman in 2017 for her…
f: Mamta Kalia is an Indian author, teacher and poet, writing primarily in Hindi and focusing predominantly on the lived experiences of women from middle-class families in India. Kalia won the Vyas Samman in 2017 for her novel Dukkham Sukkham and several other literary awards, including the Yashpal Katha Samman, Sahitya Bhushan Samman, Ram Manohar Lohiya Samman, Mahadevi Varma Samman and the Sita Award. She was felicitated with the KLF book award 2020 for Ravi Katha: Andaaz-E-Bayan Urf Ravi Katha .

b: Mamta Pandit is a co-editor with the Hindi magazine Mahi Sandesh, published from Jaipur. She has a keen interest in poetry-writing and her works have been published in magazines as well as on many websites. Chabiyan…
f: Mamta Pandit is a co-editor with the Hindi magazine Mahi Sandesh, published from Jaipur. She has a keen interest in poetry-writing and her works have been published in magazines as well as on many websites. Chabiyan Umeedon ki is her first poetry collection to be published by Mahi Sandesh publications.

b: Manal Younus is an Australian-based storyteller from Eritrea who believes that language and stories are the very fabric of our existence. Using her writing and performance, Younus explores different aspects of life from…
f: Manal Younus is an Australian-based storyteller from Eritrea who believes that language and stories are the very fabric of our existence. Using her writing and performance, Younus explores different aspects of life from perseverance, identity, travel and truth. She speaks on a vast number of issues including youth leadership, gender and female empowerment, faith, blackness, culture, language, migration, displacement, racism and interculturalism. In 2015, she released her first book of poetry called Reap . In the same year, she founded Soul Lounge, a monthly open mic night that centres the voices of people of colour.

b: Manan Ahmed Asif was born in Lahore. He is currently an Associate Professor of History at Columbia University. He is the author of A Book of Conquest and The Loss of Hindustan: The Invention of India . He is the founder…
f: Manan Ahmed Asif was born in Lahore. He is currently an Associate Professor of History at Columbia University. He is the author of A Book of Conquest and The Loss of Hindustan: The Invention of India . He is the founder of the blog Chapati Mystery and his writings have appeared in magazines and newspapers in South Asia, Middle East, Northern Europe and North America.

b: Manasi Joshi is an Indian Para-Athlete and a change-maker. She is the current Para Badminton World Championship Gold medalist and a National Award winner for Best sportsperson with a disability in India. Beginning her…
f: Manasi Joshi is an Indian Para-Athlete and a change-maker. She is the current Para Badminton World Championship Gold medalist and a National Award winner for Best sportsperson with a disability in India. Beginning her professional journey in 2015, at present, she is ranked World No. 2 in Women Singles SL3. She was recently recognised by BBC as one of the 100 most inspirational & powerful women across the world in 2020. An advocate of rights for people with disability, Manasi was recently listed as the Next Generation Leader 2020 by TIME Magazine and appeared in their Asia cover, making her the first para-athlete in the world and the first Indian athlete to receive such recognition. Barbie celebrated Joshi and her achievements by modelling a one-of-a-kind doll to her likeness to inspire young girls. From setting examples to breaking stereotypes, she has been a trailblazer ever since she took up para-sport following an accident. An engineer by qualification, Joshi has worked as a Software Engineer with MNC, Banks, etc. Presently she is employed with Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited as a sports person. She is based out of Hyderabad, India, and trains at Gopichand academy, where she is currently preparing to qualify at the Tokyo 2020 Paralympics to be held later this year.

b: Manav Kaul is a versatile writer and actor, known for his engaging stories that have resonated with audiences worldwide. With significant contributions to theatre and films, Kaul’s creative work continues to inspire…
f: Manav Kaul is a versatile writer and actor, known for his engaging stories that have resonated with audiences worldwide. With significant contributions to theatre and films, Kaul’s creative work continues to inspire readers and viewers alike.

b: Mandira Sen has worked for over 40 years in publishing in the USA, UK and India, and is the director of Stree (gender studies) and Samya (writings from the margins, on caste, dissent) both founded in the 1990s. Since…
f: Mandira Sen has worked for over 40 years in publishing in the USA, UK and India, and is the director of Stree (gender studies) and Samya (writings from the margins, on caste, dissent) both founded in the 1990s. Since 2015, a partnership was formed with Sage to publish a select list in the social sciences under Sage-Stree and Sage-Samya.

b: Mangalam Maloo is a Journalist and Consumer Sector Expert. He is currently Anchor and Deputy Editor at CNBC-TV18.
f: Mangalam Maloo is a Journalist and Consumer Sector Expert. He is currently Anchor and Deputy Editor at CNBC-TV18.

b: Mani Rao is the author of twelve poetry books and chapbooks including Love Me in a Hurry (Atta Galatta 2022), New & Selected Poems (Poetrywala 2015) and three books in translation from Sanskrit including Kalidasa for…
f: Mani Rao is the author of twelve poetry books and chapbooks including Love Me in a Hurry (Atta Galatta 2022), New & Selected Poems (Poetrywala 2015) and three books in translation from Sanskrit including Kalidasa for the 21st Century Reader (Aleph Books 2015) and Saundarya Lahari ( Wave of Beauty ; HarperCollins 2022).

b: Mani Shankar Aiyar served 26 years in the Indian Foreign Service, including a deputation to the Office of Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi. Thrice elected to the Lower House of Parliament from Tamil Nadu, he also served a…
f: Mani Shankar Aiyar served 26 years in the Indian Foreign Service, including a deputation to the Office of Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi. Thrice elected to the Lower House of Parliament from Tamil Nadu, he also served a six-year term in the Upper House. In 2006, he was conferred the Outstanding Parliamentarian Award. A cabinet minister from 2004 to 2009, he held various portfolios. He has published nine books to date, including his latest, Memoirs of a Maverick . The companion volume to his memoirs, The Rajiv I Knew, was published and launched in January 2024.

b: Mani Shankar Mukherjee is the writer of classic novels like Kato Ajanare and Chowringhee . His enormous oeuvre, spanning fiction, non-fiction, travelogues, biographies, and more, continues to be a bestselling one in…
f: Mani Shankar Mukherjee is the writer of classic novels like Kato Ajanare and Chowringhee . His enormous oeuvre, spanning fiction, non-fiction, travelogues, biographies, and more, continues to be a bestselling one in Bengali and has received both critical and popular acclaim through translations into English and other European and Asian languages. Several of his works have been filmed, including Seemabaddha and Jana Aranya by Satyajit Ray. Mukherjee won the Sahitya Akademi award for his collection of autobiographical essays, Eka Eka Ekashi, which will be published in English translation in 2022.

b: Manimugdha S. Sharma is a Delhi-based journalist with the Times of India and is the author of Allahu Akbar: Understanding the Great Mughal in Today's India, a non-fiction title that looks at the life and times of…
f: Manimugdha S. Sharma is a Delhi-based journalist with the Times of India and is the author of Allahu Akbar: Understanding the Great Mughal in Today's India, a non-fiction title that looks at the life and times of Emperor Akbar from a modern perspective. An avid quizzer and a quizmaster, Sharma takes a keen interest in politics, military history, the Mughal and British empires and the two World Wars.

b: Manish Malhotra is an Indian fashion designer, couturier, costume stylist, entrepreneur, filmmaker, revivalist based in Mumbai, India. The founder of the eponymous label, Manish Malhotra, has styled and designed for…
f: Manish Malhotra is an Indian fashion designer, couturier, costume stylist, entrepreneur, filmmaker, revivalist based in Mumbai, India. The founder of the eponymous label, Manish Malhotra, has styled and designed for more than thousands of movies and won numerous awards, including the Priyadarshini Memorial Award, among several others. Accoladed as a pioneer in the Indian design space, Manish Malhotra’s areas of creativity span the broad spheres of cinema, design, styling, diffusion, timeless bridal couture, jewellery, beauty, film direction, Virtual Store, and now Tech with his recent launch of NFT’S in the blockchain business.

b: Manish Tewari is a lawyer and a Member of Parliament representing Sri Anandpur Sahib in Punjab in the 17th Lok Sabha. He served as the Union Minister of State Independent Charge in the Ministry of Information and…
f: Manish Tewari is a lawyer and a Member of Parliament representing Sri Anandpur Sahib in Punjab in the 17th Lok Sabha. He served as the Union Minister of State Independent Charge in the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, Government of India, and was the Spokesperson of the Cabinet and the United Progressive Alliance (UPA) Government. He is currently the Senior National Spokesperson of the Indian National Congress (INC). Tewari was also a Distinguished Senior Fellow at the South Asia Centre of the Atlantic Council - a Washington DC-based think tank. He currently serves on the Standing Committee of Finance and Joint Committee of Parliament examining the Data Protection Bill, as well as the Parliamentary Consultative Committee of Defense. He has authored four books - Decoding a Decade: The Politics of Policy Making, Fables of Fractured Times, Tidings of Troubled Times and 10 Flash Points 20 Years – National Security situations that impacted India.

b: Manisha Chaudhry has many years of experience as a publishing professional and as a consultant in the social development sector. An editor, translator and writer fluent in Hindi and English, her work has been published…
f: Manisha Chaudhry has many years of experience as a publishing professional and as a consultant in the social development sector. An editor, translator and writer fluent in Hindi and English, her work has been published by Kali for Women, Oxford University Press, Zubaan Books, Niyogi Books, Pratham Books and Permanent Black. Manisha runs her own not for profit publishing house, Manan Books with a strong focus on equity in education, publishing multilingually for children and teachers. Among many initiatives to democratise the joy of reading among all children, she also spearheaded the initiative of the Children’s Outreach of the Jaipur Literature Festival. She is a severally published author of children’s books and has translated numerous others.

b: Manisha Koirala is one of India’s leading film actors. Born in Nepal, Koirala made her Bollywood debut with Saudagar in 1991 and went on to establish herself with films such as 1942: A Love Story, Akele Hum Akele Tum,…
f: Manisha Koirala is one of India’s leading film actors. Born in Nepal, Koirala made her Bollywood debut with Saudagar in 1991 and went on to establish herself with films such as 1942: A Love Story, Akele Hum Akele Tum, Bombay, Khamoshi: The Musical, Dil Se, Mann, Lajja and Company . She took a break from acting in 2012 to return five years later with the coming-of-age drama Dear Maya , Netflix’s Lust Stories and Sanju . She was appointed as the Goodwill Ambassador for the United Nations Population Fund in 1999 and 2015, and was involved in the relief works after the Nepal earthquake 2015. She promotes causes such as women’s rights, prevention of human trafficking and cancer awareness. Koirala was diagnosed with ovarian cancer in 2012 and has been cancer-free since 2015.

b: Manisha Kulshreshtha is an eminent Hindi novelist. She has written six well received novels and eight short story collections. Her latest novel Mallika is a bestseller and it has been already signed for a film series by…
f: Manisha Kulshreshtha is an eminent Hindi novelist. She has written six well received novels and eight short story collections. Her latest novel Mallika is a bestseller and it has been already signed for a film series by a renowned production group of Bollywood. Presently, Kulshreshtha is writing a travelogue named Meghmarg , which is an account of the 'Meghdoot Trail' described by Kalidasa. For writing this book, she travelled from Ramgiri to Mount Kailash for exclusive first hand experience and authentic research on the great poet Kalidasa.

b: Manjari Sinha is an acclaimed music and dance critic, recognised both for her depth and understanding of the Indian classical arts as well as her effortless command of languages. Roli Books commissioned her to write a…
f: Manjari Sinha is an acclaimed music and dance critic, recognised both for her depth and understanding of the Indian classical arts as well as her effortless command of languages. Roli Books commissioned her to write a book on Ustad Bade Ghulam Ali Khan, published in their series of Rare Biographies . She has also contributed a chapter on Kathak in Indian Dance: The Ultimate Metaphor .

b: Manjeet Hirani is the wife of Rajkumar Hirani, a renowned Indian film director. She is a Deputy General Manager, commander and trainer with Air India, flying Airbus 320 aircrafts for over 25 years with flying experience…
f: Manjeet Hirani is the wife of Rajkumar Hirani, a renowned Indian film director. She is a Deputy General Manager, commander and trainer with Air India, flying Airbus 320 aircrafts for over 25 years with flying experience of more than 15,000 hours. She is the author of How to be Human: Life Lessons from Buddy Hirani , which has been into Gujarati, Marathi and Hindi.

b: Manjeet Kripalani is the co-founder of Gateway House and acts as the executive director of the institution. Prior to the founding of Gateway House, Kripalani was India Bureau chief of Businessweek magazine. During her…
f: Manjeet Kripalani is the co-founder of Gateway House and acts as the executive director of the institution. Prior to the founding of Gateway House, Kripalani was India Bureau chief of Businessweek magazine. During her extensive career in journalism, she has won several awards, including the Gerald Loeb Award, the George Polk Award, Overseas Press Club and Daniel Pearl Awards. Her political career spans being the deputy press secretary to Steve Forbes during his first run in 1995-96 as Republican candidate for U.S. President in New Jersey, to being press secretary for the Lok Sabha campaign for independent candidate Meera Sanyal in 2008 and 2014 in Mumbai.

b: Manjima Bhattacharjya is a researcher, writer and activist. She has been part of the Indian women’s movement for over two decades. She holds a PhD in sociology. Her areas of specialisation include gender and…
f: Manjima Bhattacharjya is a researcher, writer and activist. She has been part of the Indian women’s movement for over two decades. She holds a PhD in sociology. Her areas of specialisation include gender and sexuality, and labour and the body. Bhattacharjya is the author of Mannequin: Working Women in India’s Glamour Industry .

b: Titled as the ‘Indian Agatha Christie’, Manjiri Prabhu is an award-winning international author of 19 mystery and thriller novels, a short film maker and the Curator & Founder/Director of two international festivals…
f: Titled as the ‘Indian Agatha Christie’, Manjiri Prabhu is an award-winning international author of 19 mystery and thriller novels, a short film maker and the Curator & Founder/Director of two international festivals - Pune International Literary Festival and International Festival of Spiritual India (for Humanity & Wisdom). Acknowledged as a pioneer in India among women writers of mystery fiction, she is the first female mystery author to be published outside India.

b: Manju Kapur’s Difficult Daughters won the Commonwealth Prize for best first novel, Eurasia region. Her other books have been shortlisted for the Encore Award, the Hutch-Crossword prize, the India Plaza Golden Quill…
f: Manju Kapur’s Difficult Daughters won the Commonwealth Prize for best first novel, Eurasia region. Her other books have been shortlisted for the Encore Award, the Hutch-Crossword prize, the India Plaza Golden Quill Award, and the DSC Prize of South Asian Literature. Her novel, Custody was made into one of Balaji’s longest running serials, Yeh Hai Mohabbatein . Her latest book is The Gallery .

b: Manjula Padmanabhan is a playwright, novelist, artist and cartoonist. She is best known for her plays Lights Out and Harvest that won the first-ever Onassis Award for Theatre in 1997 in Greece. Padmanabhan has published…
f: Manjula Padmanabhan is a playwright, novelist, artist and cartoonist. She is best known for her plays Lights Out and Harvest that won the first-ever Onassis Award for Theatre in 1997 in Greece. Padmanabhan has published several books of prose, including Hot Death, Cold Soup, Kleptomania, Escape, The Island of Lost Girls and Getting There. In 2020 , she published two volumes of her collected plays, Blood and Laughter and Laughter and Blood .

b: Manjunath Kamath works in diverse mediums – painting, drawing, digital art and terracotta. In 2015, the Scad Museum of Art, Savannah hosted his solo show. The Art Institute of Chicago, Museum of Sacred Art in Belgium,…
f: Manjunath Kamath works in diverse mediums – painting, drawing, digital art and terracotta. In 2015, the Scad Museum of Art, Savannah hosted his solo show. The Art Institute of Chicago, Museum of Sacred Art in Belgium, Kiran Nadar Museum of Art and National Gallery of Modern Art, New Delhi have his works in their collections. He was also a part of Ojas Art’s ‘Expressions at Tihar,’ ‘Freedom to March,’ and ‘Conference of the Birds’.

b: Manjushree Thapa is the author of ten books of fiction, non-fiction and literary translation. Her latest novel is All of Us in Our Own Lives , set in the cynical, moneyed world of international aid in Nepal. She has…
f: Manjushree Thapa is the author of ten books of fiction, non-fiction and literary translation. Her latest novel is All of Us in Our Own Lives , set in the cynical, moneyed world of international aid in Nepal. She has recently translated Indra Bahadur Rai’s classic Darjeeling novel, There’s a Carnival Today , into English. Her essays have appeared in The New York Times , the London Review of Books, Newsweek and the Globe and Mail .

b: Manmohan Vaidya , born in Nagpur in 1955 holds a doctorate in Radiochemistry from Nagpur University. In 2018, he was appointed as Sah-Sarkaryawah (Joint General Secretary) of RSS. Since 1983, when he became an RSS…
f: Manmohan Vaidya , born in Nagpur in 1955 holds a doctorate in Radiochemistry from Nagpur University. In 2018, he was appointed as Sah-Sarkaryawah (Joint General Secretary) of RSS. Since 1983, when he became an RSS pracharak, Dr. Vaidya has held various responsibilities which have taken him from the remotest parts of Bharat to the foremost corners of the world. He frequently writes on contemporary issues in various magazines and newspapers. With the guidance of his father Shri M.G. Vaidya, one of RSS's stalwart ideologues, his own experience as Akhil Bharatiya Prachar Pramukh (All-India In-charge of Media Relations) and a long stint abroad with HSS (Hindu Swayamsevak Sangh), Dr. Vaidya is as one of the critical voices of Bharatiya intelligentsia.

b: Manoj Bajpayee is an Indian film actor who predominantly works in Hindi cinema and is often regarded as a method actor known for his unconventional, versatile roles. He has worked in more than 60 films, including…
f: Manoj Bajpayee is an Indian film actor who predominantly works in Hindi cinema and is often regarded as a method actor known for his unconventional, versatile roles. He has worked in more than 60 films, including Pinjar, 1971 Prisoners of War, Rajneeti and Gangs of Wasseypur, among many others, and his debut in the global phenomenon series 'The Family Man' won him critical acclaim. Bajpayee is the recipient of the Padma Shri Award, the National Film Awards in the Best Supporting Actor category & the Best Actor category for films Satya, Pinjar, and Bhonsle . He has also received three Filmfare Awards and two Best Actor Screen Awards for his performance in Satya and Aks . Bajpayee has bagged International awards in the Best Actor category at the Asia Pacific Screen Awards 2016 for the film Aligarh & the Best Actor award at the New York Indian Film Festival and Indian Film Festival of Melbourne for the film Gali Guleiya.

b: Manoj Joshi, a New Delhi-based journalist and commentator, and Distinguished Fellow at the Observer Research Foundation, is the author of Understanding the India-China Border: The Enduring Threat of War in High Himalaya…
f: Manoj Joshi, a New Delhi-based journalist and commentator, and Distinguished Fellow at the Observer Research Foundation, is the author of Understanding the India-China Border: The Enduring Threat of War in High Himalaya and Kashmir: The Lost Rebellion. He was a member of a Government of India task force on reforming India's national security system.

b: Manoj Pandey is a Delhi-based writer. His works have appeared in World Literature Today, Tate and Motherland , among others. His book of short fiction featuring stories from Salman Rushdie, Margaret Atwood, Shashi…
f: Manoj Pandey is a Delhi-based writer. His works have appeared in World Literature Today, Tate and Motherland , among others. His book of short fiction featuring stories from Salman Rushdie, Margaret Atwood, Shashi Tharoor, among others, was published in 2016. He is the India-representative of the New Prize in Literature.

b: Manoj Rupda writes in Hindi and is the author of the novel, I Named My Sister Silence , which was shortlisted for the JCB Prize for Literature 2023 and the Atta Galatta Bangalore Literature Festival Book Prize 2023. He…
f: Manoj Rupda writes in Hindi and is the author of the novel, I Named My Sister Silence , which was shortlisted for the JCB Prize for Literature 2023 and the Atta Galatta Bangalore Literature Festival Book Prize 2023. He is also the author of the novel, Pratisansaar ; the collections of short stories, Tower of Silence , Saaz-Naasaaz , and Aamaajgaah ; and the book of essays, Kalaa Ka Aaswaad . He is a recipient of the Indu Sharma Katha Puraskar and the Vanmali Katha Samman.

b: Manoj Satti currently oversees the entire sales, product, and marketing portfolio at Penguin, covering both local and international markets. With over 19 years of experience at the company, he brings deep expertise in…
f: Manoj Satti currently oversees the entire sales, product, and marketing portfolio at Penguin, covering both local and international markets. With over 19 years of experience at the company, he brings deep expertise in product management, sales, and marketing. During the 2013 merger of Random House and Penguin, he played a key role in integrating the two companies, demonstrating strong leadership and strategic vision. Manoj believes in dreaming big and working hard to achieve goals. His growth strategies are data-driven and backed by thorough research and insights, reflecting his commitment to informed decision-making and sustainable business growth.

b: Manoranjan Byapari is a prolific writer in Bengali, whose important works include Chhera Chhera Jibon, Ittibrite Chandal Jibon and the Chandal Jibon trilogy. He taught himself to read and write at the age of twenty-four…
f: Manoranjan Byapari is a prolific writer in Bengali, whose important works include Chhera Chhera Jibon, Ittibrite Chandal Jibon and the Chandal Jibon trilogy. He taught himself to read and write at the age of twenty-four when he was in prison. He has worked as a rickshaw-puller, a sweeper and a porter. Until 2018, he was working as a cook at the Hellen Keller Institute for the Deaf and Blind in West Bengal. In 2018, the English translation of his memoir, Ittibrite Chandal Jibon (Interrogating My Chandal Life), received the Hindu Prize for non-fiction. The English translation of his novel Batashe Baruder Gandha (There’s Gunpowder in the Air) was shortlisted for the JCB Prize 2019, the DSC Prize for South Asian Literature 2019 & the Mathrubhumi Book of the Year Prize 2020. In 2021, Byapari became a member of the Bengal Legislative Assembly.

b: Manpreet Vohra recently retired as High Commissioner to Australia, concluding a distinguished diplomatic career. Over the years, he has lived in 10 countries across six continents and served as Ambassador to…
f: Manpreet Vohra recently retired as High Commissioner to Australia, concluding a distinguished diplomatic career. Over the years, he has lived in 10 countries across six continents and served as Ambassador to Afghanistan, Mexico, and Peru, as well as Deputy High Commissioner in Pakistan and Kenya. His postings also included roles in Hong Kong, China, Mongolia, and the United Kingdom. A devoted Arsenal fan, he now occasionally explores acting.

b: Manreet Sodhi Someshwar is an award-winning and bestselling writer of eight books, including the Mehrunisa series , the critically-acclaimed The Long Walk Home and The Radiance of a Thousand Suns , and most recently,…
f: Manreet Sodhi Someshwar is an award-winning and bestselling writer of eight books, including the Mehrunisa series , the critically-acclaimed The Long Walk Home and The Radiance of a Thousand Suns , and most recently, The Partition Trilogy . She has been hailed as 'a star on the literary horizon' by Khushwant Singh and has garnered endorsements from Gulzar for two of her books

b: Manu Joseph is the author of the widely acclaimed and bestselling novels, Serious Men and The Illicit Happiness of Other People , which have been translated into many languages, and have been nominated for several…
f: Manu Joseph is the author of the widely acclaimed and bestselling novels, Serious Men and The Illicit Happiness of Other People , which have been translated into many languages, and have been nominated for several prizes. Among other honours, he is the winner of The Hindu Literature Prize and The American Pen Open Book Award whose jury described him “…that rare bird who can wildly entertain the reader as forcefully as he moves them.” The Tamil translation of Serious Men won the Sahitya Akademi Award. Among India’s most popular commentators, he is a former columnist for The New York Times . His latest novel is Miss Laila, Armed and Dangerous.

b: Manu S. Pillai is the author of the critically acclaimed The Ivory Throne, Rebel Sultans and The Courtesan, the Mahatma & the Italian Brahmin. Formerly chief of staff to Shashi Tharoor MP, he is a winner of the Sahitya…
f: Manu S. Pillai is the author of the critically acclaimed The Ivory Throne, Rebel Sultans and The Courtesan, the Mahatma & the Italian Brahmin. Formerly chief of staff to Shashi Tharoor MP, he is a winner of the Sahitya Akademi Yuva Puraskar. His other essays on history have appeared in Mint Lounge, The Hindu, Hindustan Times, Open Magazine, New Statesman and other publications.

b: Manvendra Singh has served as a Member of Parliament from Barmer, Rajasthan and a member of the Rajasthan Assembly 2013. He has also written for the Indian Express, The Statesman, The Hindu, DNA , and the Hindustan…
f: Manvendra Singh has served as a Member of Parliament from Barmer, Rajasthan and a member of the Rajasthan Assembly 2013. He has also written for the Indian Express, The Statesman, The Hindu, DNA , and the Hindustan Times , amongst others. He is the author of Campaign Diary, released in 2013.

b: Marc Quinn makes art about what it is to be a person living in our world – creating portraits about humanity. Quinn is one of the leading artists of his generation whose sculptures, paintings and drawings explore the…
f: Marc Quinn makes art about what it is to be a person living in our world – creating portraits about humanity. Quinn is one of the leading artists of his generation whose sculptures, paintings and drawings explore the relationships between art and science, man and nature, the human body and the perception of beauty. His work also connects frequently and meaningfully with art history, from modern masters right back to antiquity.

b: Laureate Professor Marcia Langton AO is a Yiman and Bidjara author, scholar, and curator at the University of Melbourne, Australia. A leading voice on Indigenous rights, her acclaimed works include Dhoombak Goobgoowana:…
f: Laureate Professor Marcia Langton AO is a Yiman and Bidjara author, scholar, and curator at the University of Melbourne, Australia. A leading voice on Indigenous rights, her acclaimed works include Dhoombak Goobgoowana: A History of Indigenous Australia and the University of Melbourne – Vol. 1 Truth and Vol. 2 Voice ; Indigenous Knowledge: Australian Perspectives ; First Knowledges: Law – The Way of the Ancestors ; and 65,000 Years: A Short History of Australian Art .

b: Marco Moneta holds a PhD in philosophy from Florence University. In 2006, he authored a volume on the great Italian poet and philosopher Giacomo Leopardi. Over the last decade, his interests and research have been aimed…
f: Marco Moneta holds a PhD in philosophy from Florence University. In 2006, he authored a volume on the great Italian poet and philosopher Giacomo Leopardi. Over the last decade, his interests and research have been aimed at the encounter between Europeans and Indians in the early modern age.

b: Marcus Moench works on water, climate and social change issues in South Asia, the United States and globally. Combining narratives of transformation and resilience in complex social-ecological systems, his work spans…
f: Marcus Moench works on water, climate and social change issues in South Asia, the United States and globally. Combining narratives of transformation and resilience in complex social-ecological systems, his work spans culture, art and science in pursuit of change. He founded the Institute for Social and Environmental Transition in 1997.

b: Margaret Alva has traversed a wide canvas with many achievements to her credit. A lawyer by profession, she was first elected to Parliament in 1974 and served four consecutive six-year terms in the Rajya Sabha and one…
f: Margaret Alva has traversed a wide canvas with many achievements to her credit. A lawyer by profession, she was first elected to Parliament in 1974 and served four consecutive six-year terms in the Rajya Sabha and one in the Lok Sabha. During her 30 years in Parliament, she served on several prestigious committees, chaired the Parliamentary committee on Empowerment of woman for five years and was part of the Indian delegation to many international conferences. She was Union Minister for ten years handling important portfolios in the governments of Rajiv Gandhi and P.V.Narasimha Rao. She served as Advisor to the Bureau of Parliamentary Studies and Training between 2004 and 2009 while working closely with the AiCC President – Sonia Gandhi, as General Secretary in charge of eight states. Founder President of Karuna, an NGO championing the cause of women, she has been active in the Women’s Movement for over five decades. She is the recipient of several awards in India and abroad including the First Nelson Mandela Award for Minority Empowerment in New York, The Shiromani Award for her contribution to Public Life and the Global Leadership Award from Vital Voices, Washington. She has served as Governor of Uttarakhand, Rajasthan, Goa and Gujarat.

b: Margaret MacLeod is the First Secretary for the Public Diplomacy section at U. Embassy India. She coordinates public engagement with established opinion leaders focusing, in particular, on U.S. Mission to India’s…
f: Margaret MacLeod is the First Secretary for the Public Diplomacy section at U. Embassy India. She coordinates public engagement with established opinion leaders focusing, in particular, on U.S. Mission to India’s goals related to the Indo-Pacific Strategy. Her domestic assignments include International Security and Non-proliferation, International Organizations.

b: Margit Walsø has been the director of NORLA (Norwegian Literature Abroad) since 2011. NORLA is responsible for organising Norway as Guest of Honour at the Frankfurt Book Fair 2019. Walsø is also an experienced…
f: Margit Walsø has been the director of NORLA (Norwegian Literature Abroad) since 2011. NORLA is responsible for organising Norway as Guest of Honour at the Frankfurt Book Fair 2019. Walsø is also an experienced publisher and worked for the publishing house Det Norske Samlaget for 18 years. She is also an author and has written three novels, including most recently, The Parfumier .

b: Maria Balshaw is Director of Tate, a role she has held since June 2017. She has overall responsibility for Tate’s strategic direction and day-to-day operations. She has worked to reframe the context and perspective of…
f: Maria Balshaw is Director of Tate, a role she has held since June 2017. She has overall responsibility for Tate’s strategic direction and day-to-day operations. She has worked to reframe the context and perspective of this long-established institution to engage with sensitive times, furthering the mission of inclusiveness and equality to connect with a wider audience. As Director, Balshaw is also the Accounting Officer appointed by the Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport. Previously, Balshaw was Director of the Whitworth, University of Manchester, Director of Manchester City Galleries and Director of Culture for Manchester City Council. She holds a Bachelor of Arts degree in English Literature and Cultural Studies from the University of Liverpool and a Master of Arts degree in Critical Theory and a DPhil in African American Visual and Literary Culture from the University of Sussex. She is board member of the Clore Leadership Programme, Manchester International Festival and the National Museum Directors’ Council Executive Committee. In 2015, she was awarded a CBE for services to the arts.

b: Maria Goretti is a passionate dancer, specialising in jazz and tap. She lent her charm to numerous prestigious advertising campaigns and enjoyed significant popularity as an MTV VJ, where she interviewed and toured with…
f: Maria Goretti is a passionate dancer, specialising in jazz and tap. She lent her charm to numerous prestigious advertising campaigns and enjoyed significant popularity as an MTV VJ, where she interviewed and toured with renowned musicians for over five years. Additionally, she worked as a roaming presenter, covering the ICC Champions Trophy in Sri Lanka in 2002 and the Cricket World Cup in South Africa in 2003. Goretti is also known for her cooking shows, including Do it Sweet, I Love Cooking, I Want to Bake Free, and Cafe Maria on Disney Hotstar. In 2011, she excelled in the Cordon Bleu Certificate Course at the Tante Marie Culinary Academy in the UK, and in 2018, she completed her Diploma in patisserie from Cordon Bleu in Paris and London.

b: Mariam Khan is the editor of the bestselling anthology It's Not About the Burqa: Muslim Women on Faith, Feminism, Sexuality and Race. She is also a journalist and has written for the Guardian, Vice, Metro, Stylist and…
f: Mariam Khan is the editor of the bestselling anthology It's Not About the Burqa: Muslim Women on Faith, Feminism, Sexuality and Race. She is also a journalist and has written for the Guardian, Vice, Metro, Stylist and more and is a columnist at i News. She is currently a postgraduate student at SOAS University in London.

b: Marie Darrieussecq has published more than 20 books, including novels, short stories, biographies, and non-fiction, and has also written for theatrical productions. She was a psychoanalyst before turning exclusively to…
f: Marie Darrieussecq has published more than 20 books, including novels, short stories, biographies, and non-fiction, and has also written for theatrical productions. She was a psychoanalyst before turning exclusively to writing, releasing her debut, best-selling novel, Truismes , in 1996, and has since been a laureate of the Prix Médicis and the Prix des Prix in 2013. Her work has been translated into several languages. Sleepless is her most recent publication to be translated into English. Her newest novel is Fabriquer une femme .

b: Marie-Anne Lacoma began her publishing career as a publicist at Editis before gaining broad experience at independent publishers, mastering marketing, bookseller relations, partnerships, and festival strategy. She…
f: Marie-Anne Lacoma began her publishing career as a publicist at Editis before gaining broad experience at independent publishers, mastering marketing, bookseller relations, partnerships, and festival strategy. She joined Montreal-based Éditions Les Allusifs to help expand into the French market, then spent eight years in business development at Éditions Gallmeister, followed by seven years at La Manufacture de livres. In 2020, she co-founded Éditions Dalva with Juliette Ponce, focusing on promoting women writers. Alongside her publishing roles, Lacoma has consistently worked as a freelancer, providing consulting and commercial support to various publishing houses.

b: Marina Warner is a writer of fiction and cultural history. Her award-winning books explore myths and fairy tales such as From the Beast to the Blonde: On Fairy Tales and their Tellers and Stranger Magic: Charmed States…
f: Marina Warner is a writer of fiction and cultural history. Her award-winning books explore myths and fairy tales such as From the Beast to the Blonde: On Fairy Tales and their Tellers and Stranger Magic: Charmed States and the Arabian Nights . She is currently Professor of English and Creative Writing, Birkbeck College, a distinguished Fellow of All Souls College, Oxford, and a Fellow of the British Academy. In 2015, she was awarded the Holberg Prize in the Arts and Humanities, and has served as the first woman President of the Royal Society of Literature. Her most recent book, Inventory of a Life Mislaid , explores her childhood in Egypt.

b: Marina Wheeler is an Anglo-Indian, London-based barrister specialising in constitutional and human rights law. She was made Queen’s Counsel in 2016 and also teaches mediation and conflict resolution. She writes…
f: Marina Wheeler is an Anglo-Indian, London-based barrister specialising in constitutional and human rights law. She was made Queen’s Counsel in 2016 and also teaches mediation and conflict resolution. She writes regularly for the UK Human Rights Blog as well as national newspapers, usually on legal subjects.

b: Mark Haddon is the author of four novels including The Porpoise and The Curious Incident of the Dog in the Night-Time. He has also written a collection of short stories, The Pier Falls, a collection of poetry, a stage…
f: Mark Haddon is the author of four novels including The Porpoise and The Curious Incident of the Dog in the Night-Time. He has also written a collection of short stories, The Pier Falls, a collection of poetry, a stage play, TV screenplays and numerous books for children.

b: Markiyan Kamysh is a Ukrainian novelist who represents Chernobyl underground. For seven years, he has been illegally investigating and writing about the Chernobyl Exclusion Zone and Pripyat. He made more than 100…
f: Markiyan Kamysh is a Ukrainian novelist who represents Chernobyl underground. For seven years, he has been illegally investigating and writing about the Chernobyl Exclusion Zone and Pripyat. He made more than 100 expeditions behind the barbed wire and lived in the Zone for more than a year. Kamysh’s debut novel La Zone about illegal Chernobyl tourists (stalkers) has been welcomed with great warmth by French critics. Cult French magazine Le Nouvel Observateur has called it ‘stunning’ while Monaco Hebdo magazine included it in the list of choices of the month.

b: Markus Dohle is the CEO of Penguin Random House, where he leads the world’s largest trade book publisher with operations in 20 countries and sales into over 100. He oversees Penguin Random House’s worldwide…
f: Markus Dohle is the CEO of Penguin Random House, where he leads the world’s largest trade book publisher with operations in 20 countries and sales into over 100. He oversees Penguin Random House’s worldwide publishing divisions whose 250 editorially independent imprints publish 15,000 new adult and children’s fiction and nonfiction titles annually in English, German, Portuguese and Spanish. Penguin Random House’s worldwide roster of fiction and non-fiction writers includes many of the world’s most widely read and beloved authors, more than 60 Nobel Prize laureates, and over 100 Pulitzer Prize winners. Dohle’s entire professional life has been devoted to the support and service of authors, publishers, booksellers, and readers. Before the merger of Penguin and Random House in 2013, Dohle headed Random House, where he led the company’s transition to digital publishing while maintaining its world market leadership in print books. As a combined company, Penguin Random House now has more than 100,000 new and backlist books available digitally, and over 100,000,000 eBooks were sold worldwide in 2015. As a member of the Bertelsmann Executive Board, Dohle and his fellow colleagues are responsible for setting the strategic direction for one of the world’s foremost media companies. He began his career with Bertelsmann in 1994, rising quickly to several subsequent leadership positions. Additionally, Dohle is Vice Chairman of the Association of American Publishers. He also serves on the PEN Board of Trustees, the Board of Directors of the National Book Foundation, and on the International Advisory Committee of the Atlantic Council.

b: Markus Zusak is the author of five books, including the international bestseller, The Book Thief , which spent more than a decade on the New York Times bestseller list and has been translated into more than 40 languages…
f: Markus Zusak is the author of five books, including the international bestseller, The Book Thief , which spent more than a decade on the New York Times bestseller list and has been translated into more than 40 languages – establishing Zusak as one of the most successful authors to come out of Australia. To date, Zusak has held the number one position on Amazon.com, Amazon.co.uk, the New York Times bestseller list, as well as in countries across South America, Europe and Asia.

b: Martin Gelin is an award-winning author of six books on American politics and culture. Since 2010, he has been the US Correspondent for Dagens Nyheter , a national newspaper in Sweden. His writing and commentary on US…
f: Martin Gelin is an award-winning author of six books on American politics and culture. Since 2010, he has been the US Correspondent for Dagens Nyheter , a national newspaper in Sweden. His writing and commentary on US politics have been featured on BBC, CNN, The New York Times, NPR, Slate, Quartz and in Granta Sweden .

b: Martin Goodman is the author of twelve books of award-winning nonfiction and fiction, including his account of eco-lawyers saving the planet, Client Earth . Other books on India include a spiritual biography, In Search…
f: Martin Goodman is the author of twelve books of award-winning nonfiction and fiction, including his account of eco-lawyers saving the planet, Client Earth . Other books on India include a spiritual biography, In Search of the Divine Mother , and On Sacred Mountains . He is emeritus professor of Creative Writing at the University of Hull.

b: Martin Puchner is the Byron and Anita Wien Professor of English at Harvard University. His prize-winning books range from philosophy to the arts and his Norton Anthology of World Literature and his online courses have…
f: Martin Puchner is the Byron and Anita Wien Professor of English at Harvard University. His prize-winning books range from philosophy to the arts and his Norton Anthology of World Literature and his online courses have reached students in 160 countries. His new book, The Written World , tells the story of literature from clay tablets to the Internet.

b: Mary Beard , one of the world’s best-known Classicists, has written numerous books including the prize-winning Pompeii, the best-selling SPQR and the thought-provoking Women & Power . Mary is a regular media…
f: Mary Beard , one of the world’s best-known Classicists, has written numerous books including the prize-winning Pompeii, the best-selling SPQR and the thought-provoking Women & Power . Mary is a regular media commentator, committed blogger and has made many highly-acclaimed television documentaries on the Ancient world. Her latest book, Roman Emperor, delves into the world of that extraordinary role.

b: Marya Shakil works as a Political Editor and Anchor with CNN-News18. She is a recipient of multiple awards, including the prestigious Ramnath Goenka Award in the Politics and Govt category in 2012 and 2014. Her daily…
f: Marya Shakil works as a Political Editor and Anchor with CNN-News18. She is a recipient of multiple awards, including the prestigious Ramnath Goenka Award in the Politics and Govt category in 2012 and 2014. Her daily debate show NewsEpicentre also won the award for the best debate show recently. Travelling and reporting on elections and reading a trend is something she loves doing.

b: Mathew Cherian is a civil engineer from BITS Pilani and a rural management graduate from IRMA, Anand. He is an author of two books – A Million Missions and Ageing and Poverty in India . Mathew has set up Credibility…
f: Mathew Cherian is a civil engineer from BITS Pilani and a rural management graduate from IRMA, Anand. He is an author of two books – A Million Missions and Ageing and Poverty in India . Mathew has set up Credibility Alliance, GuideStar India, and Charities Aid Foundation. He worked with HelpAge India as the CEO for 18 years and is now the Global Ambassador for Ageing with HelpAge international. Currently he serves as an honorary Chair of Care India.

b: Matt Frei is a presenter at Channel 4 News and the current Europe Editor. In October 2012, Frei headed the Channel’s coverage of the U.S. Presidential election, including making a documentary, The American Road Trip:…
f: Matt Frei is a presenter at Channel 4 News and the current Europe Editor. In October 2012, Frei headed the Channel’s coverage of the U.S. Presidential election, including making a documentary, The American Road Trip: Obama’s Story , in which he visited middle-class voters in the midwest communities. In January 2016, Frei reported on his own documentary investigating the world of Donald Trump and those that surround him, The Mad World of Donald Trump ’, and made a series of documentaries on the rise of Trump. Frei has written two books, Italy: The Unfinished Revolution and Only in America .

b: Matt Preston is a globally recognised food critic, TV personality, and author. A founding mentor of MasterChef Australia , Preston spent 11 years captivating audiences worldwide. He has authored eight bestselling…
f: Matt Preston is a globally recognised food critic, TV personality, and author. A founding mentor of MasterChef Australia , Preston spent 11 years captivating audiences worldwide. He has authored eight bestselling cookbooks and the memoir Big Mouth . Passionate about food history and travel, he explores unique culinary traditions, from Mozambique to Sulawesi. His recent ventures include working as a vet's assistant with large wildlife and discovering ancient art.

b: Matt Reed is CEO of the Aga Khan Foundation in London. Previously, he was the CEO of AKF in Delhi and Assistant Vice President and Secretary of the Board at the Keck Graduate Institute, one of the Claremont Colleges. He…
f: Matt Reed is CEO of the Aga Khan Foundation in London. Previously, he was the CEO of AKF in Delhi and Assistant Vice President and Secretary of the Board at the Keck Graduate Institute, one of the Claremont Colleges. He has worked at the Getty Research Institute, the Salzburg Seminar, and the MacArthur Foundation.

b: Matt Ridley's books on evolution, genetics, technology and innovation have sold more than a million copies. They include The Rational Optimist , How Innovation Works , and Viral: The Search for the Origin of Covid-19 .…
f: Matt Ridley's books on evolution, genetics, technology and innovation have sold more than a million copies. They include The Rational Optimist , How Innovation Works , and Viral: The Search for the Origin of Covid-19 . He has been a newspaper columnist and served in the House of Lords for nine years. His next book is called Birds, Sex and Beauty .

b: Matthew Parker was born in El Salvador and grew up in Britain, Norway and Barbados. An elected Fellow of the Royal Historical Society, he has lectured in Europe, the United States and the Caribbean. His books include…
f: Matthew Parker was born in El Salvador and grew up in Britain, Norway and Barbados. An elected Fellow of the Royal Historical Society, he has lectured in Europe, the United States and the Caribbean. His books include The Sugar Barons and Goldeneye: Ian Fleming’s Jamaica .

b: Max Hollein is the Director and Chief Executive Officer of The Metropolitan Museum of Art. As leader of The Met, Hollein oversees its artistic vision, fiscal and institutional priorities, and local and international…
f: Max Hollein is the Director and Chief Executive Officer of The Metropolitan Museum of Art. As leader of The Met, Hollein oversees its artistic vision, fiscal and institutional priorities, and local and international relations. Since joining the Museum in 2018, he has overseen over 100 exhibitions, launched several historic capital projects, secured significant acquisitions and donations, and re-envisioned the Museum’s education and digital initiatives.

b: Max Rodenbeck is South Asia bureau chief for The Economist. He was born in the US but has rarely lived there. He studied history in Egypt and from 1989-2015 roamed the Middle East as a reporter, latterly as regional…
f: Max Rodenbeck is South Asia bureau chief for The Economist. He was born in the US but has rarely lived there. He studied history in Egypt and from 1989-2015 roamed the Middle East as a reporter, latterly as regional bureau chief for The Economist. He has authored a biography of the Egyptian capital, Cairo: The City Victorious, and often writes for the New York Review of Books.

b: May-Elin Stener is the Ambassador of Norway to India, Sri Lanka, Bhutan and the Maldives. Prior to this, she was the Deputy Director General of the Regional Department in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Norway,…
f: May-Elin Stener is the Ambassador of Norway to India, Sri Lanka, Bhutan and the Maldives. Prior to this, she was the Deputy Director General of the Regional Department in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Norway, covering Africa, Asia, Latin America and the Middle East, as well as peace and reconciliation issues. She was Norway’s Deputy Permanent Representative to the United Nations headquarters in New York, as well as Deputy Head of the Norwegian Embassy in Pretoria, South Africa. She has worked for the Norwegian Foreign Service since 1995, and has extensive diplomatic experience multilaterally, with a focus on humanitarian affairs. She has also been posted to the UN offices in Geneva, and has headed the Section for Humanitarian Affairs in the Ministry.

b: Maya Jasanoff is the XD and Nancy Yang Professor of the Arts and Sciences at Harvard University. She is the author of the prize-winning books Edge of Empire, Liberty’s Exiles, which received the 2012 National Book…
f: Maya Jasanoff is the XD and Nancy Yang Professor of the Arts and Sciences at Harvard University. She is the author of the prize-winning books Edge of Empire, Liberty’s Exiles, which received the 2012 National Book Critics Circle Award for Non-Fiction and the George Washington Book Prize, and The Dawn Watch: Joseph Conrad in a Global World, which won the 2018 Cundill Prize in History. A 2013 Guggenheim Fellow, Jasanoff won the 2017 Windham-Campbell Prize for Nonfiction. She is a frequent contributor to publications including The New Yorker and the Guardian, and is Chair of judges for the 2021 Booker Prize.

b: Maya Mirchandani is an award-winning broadcast journalist, Associate Professor of Practice, and Head of the Department of Media Studies at Ashoka University. In 2023, she received the New India Foundation Book…
f: Maya Mirchandani is an award-winning broadcast journalist, Associate Professor of Practice, and Head of the Department of Media Studies at Ashoka University. In 2023, she received the New India Foundation Book Fellowship for a multigenerational biography of the Abdullahs of Kashmir, to be published by HarperCollins India. Before academia, she spent twenty-three years at NDTV as a correspondent, anchor, and editor covering politics, diplomacy, and conflict. A two-time recipient of the Ramnath Goenka Award for Excellence in Journalism, she has also won the Red Ink Award for Human Rights Reporting and the Exchange for Media Broadcast Journalism Award. From 2017 to 2023, she researched extremism, hate speech, and disinformation as a Senior Fellow at the Observer Research Foundation and continues to write as a columnist and analyst for The Wire .

b: Maya Mrig was born in Punjab. He has worked at Bodhi Publishing since 1995. He is the author of Words , That Life Will Not Stop, Frozen Greenpeace, Diary of a Silent Man and Kat Ray Man Kat. Mrig has also initiated…
f: Maya Mrig was born in Punjab. He has worked at Bodhi Publishing since 1995. He is the author of Words , That Life Will Not Stop, Frozen Greenpeace, Diary of a Silent Man and Kat Ray Man Kat. Mrig has also initiated publishing experiments such as curating poems centred around women from 127 poets on Facebook. In 2015, an anthology of these poems was published as Shathdal.

b: Maÿlis Vauterin has extensive experience in publishing. After working at the French Embassy in London, she sold film, TV, and translation rights for French publishers. In 2022, she co-founded a book-to-screen bureau…
f: Maÿlis Vauterin has extensive experience in publishing. After working at the French Embassy in London, she sold film, TV, and translation rights for French publishers. In 2022, she co-founded a book-to-screen bureau dedicated to initiating and supporting adaptations of literary works.

b: Friedenthal is active in both academia and literature. Academically, his main research topic is intellectual history, and the same interest is expressed in historical fiction, but also in speculative literature. He has…
f: Friedenthal is active in both academia and literature. Academically, his main research topic is intellectual history, and the same interest is expressed in historical fiction, but also in speculative literature. He has published novels, short stories and plays. In 2013, he won the European Union Prize for Literature.

b: Meena Kandasamy is an anti-caste activist, poet, novelist and translator. She deconstructs trauma and violence, most notably in her books of poems, Touch and Ms Militancy, as well as her three novels, The Gypsy Goddess…
f: Meena Kandasamy is an anti-caste activist, poet, novelist and translator. She deconstructs trauma and violence, most notably in her books of poems, Touch and Ms Militancy, as well as her three novels, The Gypsy Goddess , When I Hit You, and Exquisite Cadavers . Her latest work is a collection of essays called, The Orders Were to Rape You: Tamil Tigresses in the Eelam Struggle . Her novels have been shortlisted for the Women's Prize for Fiction, International Dylan Thomas Prize, Jhalak Prize and The Hindu Lit Prize.

b: Meena Sharma is Editor Patrika TV and a well-known Indian journalist and TV host, who received the Nari Shakti Puraskar from the President of India in 2016 for India’s Outstanding Women Achievers. She has also worked…
f: Meena Sharma is Editor Patrika TV and a well-known Indian journalist and TV host, who received the Nari Shakti Puraskar from the President of India in 2016 for India’s Outstanding Women Achievers. She has also worked as a consultant, director and anchor of the ZEE News’ flagship show Nayika and as Executive Editor of News 18 where she hosted Desh Ki Baat, Dr Meena Sharma Ke Sath. Dr. Sharma is also the first and only woman journalist to receive the Panna Dhai National Award for ventures beyond the call of duty and through her work with the Maharana Mewar Foundation.

b: Meenakshi Narula Ahamed was born in 1954 in Calcutta, India. After finishing school in India, she obtained an MA from Johns Hopkins University’s School of Advanced International Studies in 1978. She has had a varied…
f: Meenakshi Narula Ahamed was born in 1954 in Calcutta, India. After finishing school in India, she obtained an MA from Johns Hopkins University’s School of Advanced International Studies in 1978.
