She has had a varied career as a journalist and prior to that as a development consultant. She has worked at the World Bank in Washington D.C. as well as for the Ashoka Society. In 1989, she moved to London and became the foreign correspondent for NDTV. Among the leaders she interviewed were Nelson Mandela, John Major and Bill Clinton during his presidential campaign. She covered the race riots in London and reported on the rise of Indian entrepreneurs in the US in the mid nineties. After returning to the US in 1996, she worked as a freelance journalist. Her op-eds and articles have been published in Asian Age, Seminar, Foreign Policy, Wall Street Journal and the Washington Post. She has served on the board of Doctors Without Borders, The Turquoise Mountain Foundation and Drugs for Neglected Diseases. She divides her time between the US and India.

b: Meenakshi Narula Ahamed is a freelance journalist and author of A Matter of Trust: U.S.-India Relations from Truman to Trump . Her work has appeared in The New York Times and The Washington Post . Ahamed has also worked…
f: Meenakshi Narula Ahamed is a freelance journalist and author of A Matter of Trust: U.S.-India Relations from Truman to Trump . Her work has appeared in The New York Times and The Washington Post . Ahamed has also worked with the World Bank and divides her time between New York, Los Angeles, and New Delhi.

b: Meenakshi Sharma is a trained journalist and management educator. She has an MBA in Human Resources and has completed a programme in Management of Social Initiatives from IIM Kozhikode. She continues to manage a popular…
f: Meenakshi Sharma is a trained journalist and management educator. She has an MBA in Human Resources and has completed a programme in Management of Social Initiatives from IIM Kozhikode. She continues to manage a popular book club in Gurgaon which she founded in 2011. Soldier On is her debut book. It is a memoir and a tribute to every soldier.

b: Meenakshi Reddy Madhavan ’s first book You Are Here was based on her hugely popular blog ‘Compulsive Confessions’ and was the first book to speak of the concerns of a certain type of modern Indian woman. Since…
f: Meenakshi Reddy Madhavan ’s first book You Are Here was based on her hugely popular blog ‘Compulsive Confessions’ and was the first book to speak of the concerns of a certain type of modern Indian woman. Since then, Madhavan has written four more novels, two for young adults, and a collection of short stories as well as contributing to several anthologies. The One Who Had Two Lives is her seventh book and the second in the Girls of the Mahabharata series. She is currently working on a crime novel.

b: Meenal Baghel is an editor and writer. Most recently, she headed the Mumbai Mirror . She is the author of Death in Mumbai.
f: Meenal Baghel is an editor and writer. Most recently, she headed the Mumbai Mirror . She is the author of Death in Mumbai.

b: Meeran Chadha Borwankar was Director General, Bureau of Police Research and Development & National Crime Records Bureau. She is also the former Commissioner, Pune, Chief of Maharashtra Prisons, Chief of Crime Branch…
f: Meeran Chadha Borwankar was Director General, Bureau of Police Research and Development & National Crime Records Bureau. She is also the former Commissioner, Pune, Chief of Maharashtra Prisons, Chief of Crime Branch Mumbai. She also worked in the Central Bureau of Investigation. She was the first woman District Police Chief in Maharashtra and has authored Leaves of Life , Inspector Chougule and Madam Commissioner .

b: Meeta Pandit belongs to the Gwalior Gharana and is the sixth in the unbroken lineage of legendary musicians. She is the first woman in the family to take up music professionally. The granddaughter and disciple of Padma…
f: Meeta Pandit belongs to the Gwalior Gharana and is the sixth in the unbroken lineage of legendary musicians. She is the first woman in the family to take up music professionally. The granddaughter and disciple of Padma Bhushan Krishnarao Shankar Pandit and daughter of Laxman Krishnarao Pandit, Pandit is a leading artist and has been invited to perform in more than 20 countries. A doctorate in music, she is a Top Graded artist of All India Radio. Prasar Bharati and Public Service Broadcasting Trust jointly made a film on her titled Meeta: Linking a Tradition with Today . She is a recipient of many awards and honours including the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award, the Bismillah Khan Award, the Indira Gandhi Priyadarshini Award, the Jayprakash Narayan Award, the Sur Mani, the Yuva Ojaswini, the Yuva Ratna and the FICCI Award for music. She has also many albums to her credit.

b: Meeti Shroff Shah was shortlisted for the Times of India AuTHer Awards in 2023 for The Death Of Kirti Kadakia . Prior to this, she has written the critically acclaimed memoir, Do You Know Any Good Boys? . Shroff is also…
f: Meeti Shroff Shah was shortlisted for the Times of India AuTHer Awards in 2023 for The Death Of Kirti Kadakia . Prior to this, she has written the critically acclaimed memoir, Do You Know Any Good Boys? . Shroff is also an award winning copywriter and creative consultant. Her new mystery novel , A Matrimonial Murder , will be out in February 2024.

b: Megan Nolan is a London-based Irish writer. Her writing includes essays, fiction and reviews which have been published widely, including in The New York Times, The White Review, The Sunday Times, The Village Voice, The…
f: Megan Nolan is a London-based Irish writer. Her writing includes essays, fiction and reviews which have been published widely, including in The New York Times, The White Review, The Sunday Times, The Village Voice, The Guardian and in the literary anthology, Winter Papers . Regular columns of her cultural commentary appear in the New Statesman . Her debut novel Acts of Desperation was published by Jonathan Cape and Little, Brown in 2021, and has now been sold in 13 languages.

b: Megha Majumdar is the author of the novel A Guardian and a Thief , Oprah’s Book Club selection for October 2025. The novel is a finalist for the National Book Award and the Kirkus Prize, and has been longlisted for the…
f: Megha Majumdar is the author of the novel A Guardian and a Thief , Oprah’s Book Club selection for October 2025. The novel is a finalist for the National Book Award and the Kirkus Prize, and has been longlisted for the American Library Association’s Andrew Carnegie Medal. Her first book, A Burning , won the Sahitya Akademi Yuva Puraskar, among other honors.

b: Meghna Gulzar began her film career assisting director Saeed Akhtar Mirza on the National Award-winning Naseem and went on to study filmmaking at the Tisch School of Arts, New York University. She also assisted her…
f: Meghna Gulzar began her film career assisting director Saeed Akhtar Mirza on the National Award-winning Naseem and went on to study filmmaking at the Tisch School of Arts, New York University. She also assisted her father, poet, writer and director Gulzar, on some of his notable films. Along writing her own scripts, Gulzar has made documentaries for Doordarshan on contemporary issues. Her film based on the Arushi Talwar murder case of 2008, Talvar, received rave reviews as did her latest film Raazi , based on the true story of a young girl married into a Pakistani military family and sent as a spy for India in 1971. She is currently working on her next film, based on the life of Field Marshal Sam HFJ Manekshaw MC.

b: Meghna Pant is an award-winning author, journalist, feminist and speaker. She is the recipient of various honours, including the Frank O’Connor International Award , the Commonwealth Short Story Prize, the Laadli…
f: Meghna Pant is an award-winning author, journalist, feminist and speaker. She is the recipient of various honours, including the Frank O’Connor International Award , the Commonwealth Short Story Prize, the Laadli Media Award, the Bharat Nirman Award, the Muse India Young Writer Award, the FON South Asia Short Story Award and the Amazon Breakthrough Novel Award.Among her books are two short story collections The Trouble with Women and Happy Birthday and anthologies including The Himalayan Arc , where her short story ‘Boong thing was critically acclaimed by all major publications.Her short stories have been published in over a dozen international literary magazines, including Avatar Review, Wasafari, Guernica, Eclectica, The Bombay Review, QLRS and The Indian Quarterly . Her new book How to Get Published is India’s first guide on publishing a book, and it includes never-before tips and essays from top authors like Jeffrey Archer, Twinkle Khanna, Shobhaa De and Ashwin Sanghi.

b: Meghnad Desai is an economist by profession and taught at the London School of Economics for forty years. He is a keen observer of British politics and participates in it from his perch in the House of Lords. He has…
f: Meghnad Desai is an economist by profession and taught at the London School of Economics for forty years. He is a keen observer of British politics and participates in it from his perch in the House of Lords. He has written books on economics, Marxism, Islamist terrorism, Ezra Pound and Bollywood. This is his first novel.

b: Mehr Farooqi is an author and literary critic. She is drawn to translation, literary modernism, intersections between religion and literature, history and art history and writes a regular column for the Pakistani…
f: Mehr Farooqi is an author and literary critic. She is drawn to translation, literary modernism, intersections between religion and literature, history and art history and writes a regular column for the Pakistani newspaper Dawn’s Sunday magazine. Farooqi teaches at the University of Virginia.

b: Mehreen Chida-Razvi is an Art Historian specialising in the art and architecture of Mughal South Asia. She is the Deputy Curator and In-House Editor of the Nasser D Khalili Collection of Islamic Art, is an Assistant…
f: Mehreen Chida-Razvi is an Art Historian specialising in the art and architecture of Mughal South Asia. She is the Deputy Curator and In-House Editor of the Nasser D Khalili Collection of Islamic Art, is an Assistant Editor for the International Journal of Islamic Architecture and lectures on Islamic and Indo-Islamic art at universities and museums in London. She has published extensively on Mughal art and architecture and has widely shared her academic expertise through programming on BBC, documentaries, literary festivals, podcasts and as an expert lecturer on cultural tours.

b: Mehul Jangir , a high school student at Jayshree Periwal International School, published his first book, Survival: Sandstorm , in 2018. He is currently penning his second book. A regular columnist for Rajasthan Patrika…
f: Mehul Jangir , a high school student at Jayshree Periwal International School, published his first book, Survival: Sandstorm , in 2018. He is currently penning his second book. A regular columnist for Rajasthan Patrika , his passion for writing is only disrupted by his love for astrophysics, mathematics and debating.

b: Melizarani T. Selva is a spoken word poet, journalist and poetry educator from Kuala Lumpur. Having represented Malaysia in the International Literature Showcase in Norwich, she has performed in six countries with…
f: Melizarani T. Selva is a spoken word poet, journalist and poetry educator from Kuala Lumpur. Having represented Malaysia in the International Literature Showcase in Norwich, she has performed in six countries with notable performances at TEDxGateway in Mumbai and Ubud Writers and Readers Festival. Her first book, Taboo , made the Top 10 Best-Seller List on Malaysia’s No.1 Online Bookstore. To date, her poems have been translated in French and Bahasa. She is the founder of Kuala Lumpur’s monthly spoken word poetry open mic ‘If Walls Could Talk’, a bilingual poetry slam ‘Slamokrasi’ and teaches performance poetry at international and national schools.

b: Meredith Broussard is an associate professor at the Arthur L. Carter Journalism Institute of New York University and the author of Artificial Unintelligence: How Computers Misunderstand the World . Her research focuses…
f: Meredith Broussard is an associate professor at the Arthur L. Carter Journalism Institute of New York University and the author of Artificial Unintelligence: How Computers Misunderstand the World . Her research focuses on artificial intelligence in investigative reporting, with a particular interest in using data analysis for social good. Follow her on Twitter @merbroussard or contact her via meredithbroussard.com .

b: Merlin Sheldrake is a biologist and author of Entangled Life: How Fungi Make Our Worlds, Change Our Minds, and Shape Our Futures, a New York Times and Sunday Times bestseller, and winner of the Royal Society Book Prize…
f: Merlin Sheldrake is a biologist and author of Entangled Life: How Fungi Make Our Worlds, Change Our Minds, and Shape Our Futures, a New York Times and Sunday Times bestseller, and winner of the Royal Society Book Prize and the Wainwright Prize. Sheldrake is a research associate of the Vrije University Amsterdam, and works with the Society for the Protection of Underground Networks and the Fungi Foundation.

b: Meru Gokhale is a seasoned publishing professional with two decades of experience in the literary world. She is the founder of Editrix, a new platform that aims to bring professional-grade editing to writers, editors,…
f: Meru Gokhale is a seasoned publishing professional with two decades of experience in the literary world. She is the founder of Editrix, a new platform that aims to bring professional-grade editing to writers, editors, and publishers worldwide. Before launching this venture, Gokhale served as Publisher of The Penguin Press Group in India for nearly a decade. She is recognized internationally as a deeply experienced editor and has worked with authors including Salman Rushdie, Arundhati Roy, Amitav Ghosh, Ramachandra Guha, Jhumpa Lahiri, and Siddhartha Mukherjee.

b: Merve Emre is the Shapiro-Silverberg Professor of Creative Writing and Criticism at Wesleyan University and the director of the Shapiro Center for Creative Writing and Criticism. Her books include Paraliterary: The…
f: Merve Emre is the Shapiro-Silverberg Professor of Creative Writing and Criticism at Wesleyan University and the director of the Shapiro Center for Creative Writing and Criticism. Her books include Paraliterary: The Making of Bad Readers in Postwar America, The Personality Brokers, The Ferrante Letters, and The Annotated Mrs. Dalloway. She has been awarded the Philip Leverhulme Prize, the Robert B. Silvers Prize for Literary Criticism, and the Nona Balakian Citation for Excellence in Reviewing by the National Book Critics Circle. She is a contributing writer at the New Yorker.

b: Michael Breen is the Seoul-based author of The New Koreans . A former correspondent for American and British newspapers, he became a consultant advising companies on market entry into North Korea before switching his…
f: Michael Breen is the Seoul-based author of The New Koreans . A former correspondent for American and British newspapers, he became a consultant advising companies on market entry into North Korea before switching his consulting focus to South Korea. His previous books include Kim Jong-il: North Korea’s Dear Leader .

b: Michael Buckley is a writer, photographer, documentary filmmaker and environmental explorer. He has a passionate interest in environmental issues concerning Tibet. He is author of the ground-breaking expose Meltdown in…
f: Michael Buckley is a writer, photographer, documentary filmmaker and environmental explorer. He has a passionate interest in environmental issues concerning Tibet. He is author of the ground-breaking expose Meltdown in Tibet and a companion digital photobook Tibet , Disrupted . He is the author of ten books related to Himalayan and South Asian regions.

b: Michael Dwyer is Managing Director and Publisher at Hurst Publishers, London, which was established in 1969. Dwyer joined Hurst in 1985 after studying African history at SOAS, University of London, and working at…
f: Michael Dwyer is Managing Director and Publisher at Hurst Publishers, London, which was established in 1969. Dwyer joined Hurst in 1985 after studying African history at SOAS, University of London, and working at Heffers Booksellers in Cambridge. His firm publishes some 75 books a year focussing on the politics, culture and history of Asia, Africa and the Middle East. Hurst's authors include Shashi Tharoor, Ilhan Omar, Faisal Devji and Christophe Jaffrelot, to name a few. Two Hurst books have been shortlisted for the Orwell Prize in recent years: Gaiutra Bahadar's Coolie Woman and Alpa Shah's Nightmarch .

b: Michael Hofmann is an English poet, critic, and translator known for his two essay collections and six poetry volumes. He has translated notable twentieth-century German authors, including Kafka, Koeppen, Fallada, Benn,…
f: Michael Hofmann is an English poet, critic, and translator known for his two essay collections and six poetry volumes. He has translated notable twentieth-century German authors, including Kafka, Koeppen, Fallada, Benn, and Roth.

b: Michael Houlgate is the British Council’s Deputy Director in India, leading the British Council’s work across education, English, and the arts in India. He also leads the British Council’s work in North India. Michael…
f: Michael Houlgate is the British Council’s Deputy Director in India, leading the British Council’s work across education, English, and the arts in India. He also leads the British Council’s work in North India. Michael joined the British Council in 2012, and has worked in China, Egypt, Afghanistan and Pakistan. He worked to introduce the UK apprenticeship model in China for the first time; set up and managed the £20m Newton-Mosharafa Fund to support UK-Egypt research partnerships, delivered the British Council’s work on education and civil society in Afghanistan, and led the British Council’s work across education, English, and arts in Pakistan.

b: Michael Menezes is considered a veteran and leader in the Experiential Event Industry in India. With more than 40 years of experience in the advertising and event management field, he has also played a pivotal role in…
f: Michael Menezes is considered a veteran and leader in the Experiential Event Industry in India. With more than 40 years of experience in the advertising and event management field, he has also played a pivotal role in creating and building an apex industry body for the Indian Event Fraternity as the Founder President of the Indian Event and Entertainment Management Association that has over 300 members and has been recognised across national and international fora. He currently serves as the Chairman of Showtime Events (India) Pvt Ltd.

b: Michael Ondaatje was born in Sri Lanka in 1943 and moved to Canada in 1962. He is the author of several novels, books of poetry, a memoir, and a nonfiction book on film editing. His works include The English Patient ,…
f: Michael Ondaatje was born in Sri Lanka in 1943 and moved to Canada in 1962. He is the author of several novels, books of poetry, a memoir, and a nonfiction book on film editing. His works include The English Patient , In the Skin of a Lion , Anil’s Ghost , Divisadero and The Cat’s Table . He has received the Man Booker Prize, the Giller Prize, the Governor General’s Award and the Prix Médicis Étranger for his fiction. His new novel Warlight will be out in May, 2018.

b: Michael Puett is the Walter C. Klein Professor of Chinese History and Anthropology at Harvard University. His course on Chinese philosophy is the third highest enrolled at Harvard. He is most recently the co-author,…
f: Michael Puett is the Walter C. Klein Professor of Chinese History and Anthropology at Harvard University. His course on Chinese philosophy is the third highest enrolled at Harvard. He is most recently the co-author, with Christine Gross-Loh, of The Path: What Chinese Philosophy Can Teach Us About the Good Life .

b: Michael Rezendes is a Pulitzer Prize-winning investigative reporter for The Boston Globe and was played by Mark Ruffalo in the Oscar-winning movie Spotlight . He is also a co-author of two books, Betrayal: The Crisis in…
f: Michael Rezendes is a Pulitzer Prize-winning investigative reporter for The Boston Globe and was played by Mark Ruffalo in the Oscar-winning movie Spotlight . He is also a co-author of two books, Betrayal: The Crisis in the Catholic Church and Sin Against the Innocents: Sexual Abuse by Priests and the Role of the Catholic Church .

b: Michael Sandel teaches political philosophy at Harvard University. He has been described as ‘the most relevant living philosopher’, a ‘rock-star moralist’ by Newsweek and ‘the most famous teacher of philosophy…
f: Michael Sandel teaches political philosophy at Harvard University. He has been described as ‘the most relevant living philosopher’, a ‘rock-star moralist’ by Newsweek and ‘the most famous teacher of philosophy in the world’ by The New Republic . His books What Money Can’t Buy: The Moral Limits of Markets and Justice: What’s the Right Thing to Do? were international best sellers and have been translated into 27 languages. His BBC series The Global Philosopher explores the ethical issues lying behind the headlines with participants from around the world. Sandel’s new book is The Tyranny of Merit: What’s Become of the Common Good? with The New York Times Book Review describing it as ‘required reading for all’ in a polarised age.

b: Michael Vatikiotis is a private diplomat, journalist and author of fiction and non-fiction. Formerly editor of the Far Eastern Economic Review , Michael is currently senior advisor at the Centre for Humanitarian…
f: Michael Vatikiotis is a private diplomat, journalist and author of fiction and non-fiction. Formerly editor of the Far Eastern Economic Review , Michael is currently senior advisor at the Centre for Humanitarian Dialogue, working to resolve conflicts across Asia, Africa and the Middle East. His latest book, Lives between the Lines: A Journey in Search of the Lost Levant, explores his family's Levantine roots.

b: Michelle Gallen grew up in Northern Ireland during the Troubles a few miles from the border. She studied English Literature at Trinity College Dublin and Publishing at Stirling University. Her debut novel, Big Girl,…
f: Michelle Gallen grew up in Northern Ireland during the Troubles a few miles from the border. She studied English Literature at Trinity College Dublin and Publishing at Stirling University. Her debut novel, Big Girl, Small Town was shortlisted for the Costa First Novel Award. Her critically acclaimed second novel, Factory Girls, won the Comedy Women in Print award and was shortlisted for the RSL Encore Award. Both books are being adapted for TV. She has just finished her third novel, China Bull.

b: Mihir A. Desai is the Mizuho Financial Group Professor of Finance at Harvard Business School and Professor of Law at Harvard Law School. His books include The Wisdom of Finance: Discovering Humanity in the World of Risk…
f: Mihir A. Desai is the Mizuho Financial Group Professor of Finance at Harvard Business School and Professor of Law at Harvard Law School. His books include The Wisdom of Finance: Discovering Humanity in the World of Risk and Return and How Finance Works , forthcoming in 2019.

b: Mihir S. Sharma is Senior Fellow and Head, Economy and Growth Programme, at the Observer Research Foundation in New Delhi. He is the author of Restart: The Last Chance for the Indian Economy and in 2019 co-edited What…
f: Mihir S. Sharma is Senior Fellow and Head, Economy and Growth Programme, at the Observer Research Foundation in New Delhi. He is the author of Restart: The Last Chance for the Indian Economy and in 2019 co-edited What the Economy Needs Now. Mihir S Sharma is Director and Senior Fellow at the Observer Research Foundation in New Delhi. In 2019 he co-edited What the Economy Needs Now with Abhijit Banerjee, Gita Gopinath and Raghuram Rajan. He is also a columnist for Bloomberg in New York and an Aspen Fellow.-->

b: Milan Vaishnav is a senior fellow and Director of the South Asia Program at the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace. His primary research focus is the political economy of India. He is the author of When Crime…
f: Milan Vaishnav is a senior fellow and Director of the South Asia Program at the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace. His primary research focus is the political economy of India. He is the author of When Crime Pays: Money and Muscle in Indian Politics , published by Yale University Press and HarperCollins India in 2017.

b: Milee Ashwarya is the Publisher of the Adult Publishing Group at Penguin Random House India. Over her career, she has published numerous acclaimed and bestselling books across genres. An award-winning publisher, she is…
f: Milee Ashwarya is the Publisher of the Adult Publishing Group at Penguin Random House India. Over her career, she has published numerous acclaimed and bestselling books across genres. An award-winning publisher, she is committed to championing diverse voices and discovering debut talent. Milee has published three Booker Prize–winning books in three consecutive years: The Seven Moons of Maali Almeida by Shehan Karunatilaka; The Tomb of Sand by Geetanjali Shree, translated by Daisy Rockwell; and Heart Lamp by Banu Mushtaq, translated by Deepa Bhasthi. She has been instrumental in building Penguin Random House India’s inclusive publishing program. Her authors include Orhan Pamuk, Salman Rushdie, Jhumpa Lahiri, and Sudha Murty, among others.

b: Minakshi Achan is Head, Brand and Creative Communications at Disney Star. She joined the organisation in 2016 and since then, has been passionately driving creative communications and helping businesses across verticals…
f: Minakshi Achan is Head, Brand and Creative Communications at Disney Star. She joined the organisation in 2016 and since then, has been passionately driving creative communications and helping businesses across verticals deliver impact at scale. She is also the custodian of the brand ‘Disney Star’ and helps devise the marketing and communication strategy for various verticals across Disney Star.

b: Minam Apang is a visual artist from Arunachal Pradesh. Her works have been shown at several international platforms. She has had four solo shows in Mumbai where she first began showing her works at a gallery. She lives…
f: Minam Apang is a visual artist from Arunachal Pradesh. Her works have been shown at several international platforms. She has had four solo shows in Mumbai where she first began showing her works at a gallery. She lives in Goa and Arunachal Pradesh, spending time between drawing, farming and making music.

b: Mini Krishnan is an editor and publishing professional who worked with Macmillan India (1980 to 2000) and Oxford University Press (2000 to 2018), where she sourced and edited literary translations for national and…
f: Mini Krishnan is an editor and publishing professional who worked with Macmillan India (1980 to 2000) and Oxford University Press (2000 to 2018), where she sourced and edited literary translations for national and international audiences. She is currently Managing Editor at the Tamil Nadu Textbook and Educational Services Corporation, collaborating with twenty English-language publishers to bring Tamil literature to a global audience. She also serves as Series Editor for Early Indian Fiction and for Five Long Stories From , covering Odia, Kannada, Konkani, Malayalam, Sinhala, Bangla, Urdu, and Hindi, and is on the editorial board of the Harvard University Press Murty Classical Library of India project.

b: Mini Nanda is an academic with 37 years of teaching experience at the University of Rajasthan, where she served as Head of the Department of English and held leadership roles in the University Senate and Academic…
f: Mini Nanda is an academic with 37 years of teaching experience at the University of Rajasthan, where she served as Head of the Department of English and held leadership roles in the University Senate and Academic Council. She has contributed significantly to curriculum development from undergraduate to Ph.D. levels and has been instrumental in initiatives supporting marginalised children. With over 50 published papers, her research spans Cultural Studies, Film Studies, Women’s Writing, Diasporic Literature, and South Asian, Canadian, and Latin American Literatures. She has co-edited Literary Constructs of the Self and contributed to Joginder Paul Reader . Her translations appear in Where is My Home and Other Stories . A sought-after resource person, she has engaged with institutions worldwide, including Visva-Bharati, Sorbonne, and the University of Washington Rome Center. She has also been a prominent voice on All India Radio and Doordarshan.

b: Ministhy S is an IAS officer working in Uttar Pradesh cadre who translates between three languages: Malayalam, English and Hindi. Her translations of the Malayalam novels by KR Meera featured in the DSC Prize for South…
f: Ministhy S is an IAS officer working in Uttar Pradesh cadre who translates between three languages: Malayalam, English and Hindi. Her translations of the Malayalam novels by KR Meera featured in the DSC Prize for South Asian literature 2017 longlist for The Poison of Love , and the Crossword Book Jury Awards shortlist 2018 for The Unseeing Idol of Light. Anti-Clock , the latest translation of VJ James's novel featured in the 2021 JCB Prize for Literature shortlist.

b: Minna Lindgren is a renowned journalist and expert of classical music in Finland. She is also the author of several nonfiction books. Lindgren was inspired to write The Lavender Ladies Detective Agency after researching…
f: Minna Lindgren is a renowned journalist and expert of classical music in Finland. She is also the author of several nonfiction books. Lindgren was inspired to write The Lavender Ladies Detective Agency after researching treatment of the elderly in Finland for a magazine article. The article won the 2009 Bonnier Journalism Prize, considered the highest journalism honour in Finland.

b: Minnie Vaid is a journalist, documentary filmmaker, author, researcher, television professional and creative producer for feature films in India. She has written four non-fiction books on human rights activists,…
f: Minnie Vaid is a journalist, documentary filmmaker, author, researcher, television professional and creative producer for feature films in India. She has written four non-fiction books on human rights activists, peoples’ struggles, activism and ISRO’s women scientists. Her fifth book is her first narrative fiction, a story of women empowerment in a male-dominated profession, the army.

b: Mira Nair began her career as an actress before going on to make documentaries. Her narrative feature debut, Salaam Bombay! won the Camera d’Or and was nominated for an Academy Award for Best Foreign Language film. A…
f: Mira Nair began her career as an actress before going on to make documentaries. Her narrative feature debut, Salaam Bombay! won the Camera d’Or and was nominated for an Academy Award for Best Foreign Language film. A resourceful and determined independent filmmaker who casts unknowns alongside Hollywood stars, Nair has directed Mississippi Masala , The Perez Family, Kama Sutra: A Tale of Love , Hysterical Blindness , Vanity Fair , The Namesake , Amelia and The Reluctant Fundamentalist . Her most recent film, Queen of Katwe , about a rural Ugandan girl with an aptitude for chess, stars Lupita Nyong’o and David Oyelowo. Nair’s acclaimed film Monsoon Wedding was recently brought to the stage as a highly anticipated musical at Berkeley Repertory Theatre where it closed an extended, sold out run this past summer.

b: Miranda (MJ) Carter is the author of five books, including the award-winning Anthony Blunt: His Lives about the World War two Cambridge spy, The Three Emperors , which is about the dysfunctional family relationships of…
f: Miranda (MJ) Carter is the author of five books, including the award-winning Anthony Blunt: His Lives about the World War two Cambridge spy, The Three Emperors , which is about the dysfunctional family relationships of European royalty before World War One and an acclaimed series of historical thrillers, the first of which, The Strangler Vine , is set in India in 1837. She is a Fellow of the Royal Society of Literature.

b: Miriam Margolyes is a veteran of stage and screen, an award-winning actress who achieved success on both sides of the Atlantic. Winner of the BAFTA Best Supporting Actress award in 1993 for The Age of Innocence , she…
f: Miriam Margolyes is a veteran of stage and screen, an award-winning actress who achieved success on both sides of the Atlantic. Winner of the BAFTA Best Supporting Actress award in 1993 for The Age of Innocence , she also received Best Supporting Actress at the 1989 LA Critics Circle Awards for her role in Little Dorrit , and a Sony Radio Award for Best Actress in 1993 for her unabridged recording of Oliver Twist . She was the voice of the Matchmaker in Mulan and Fly, the mother dog, in Babe .

b: Mishi Saran’s first novel, The Other Side of Ligh t, was shortlisted for the Commonwealth Book Prize. A new edition of her acclaimed 2005 travelogue Chasing the Monk’s Shadow: A Journey in the Footsteps of Xuanzang…
f: Mishi Saran’s first novel, The Other Side of Ligh t, was shortlisted for the Commonwealth Book Prize. A new edition of her acclaimed 2005 travelogue Chasing the Monk’s Shadow: A Journey in the Footsteps of Xuanzang was published in 2018. She is finishing a novel about 1930s’ Shanghai.

b: Mita Kapur is the founder and CEO of Siyahi, India’s leading literary consultancy. Her first book, The F-Word , is a food book, memoir and travelogue. She has edited Chillies and Porridge: Writing Food, an anthology…
f: Mita Kapur is the founder and CEO of Siyahi, India’s leading literary consultancy. Her first book, The F-Word , is a food book, memoir and travelogue. She has edited Chillies and Porridge: Writing Food, an anthology of essays on food. As a freelance journalist, she writes regularly for different newspapers and magazines on social and development issues along with travel, food and lifestyle. She has received many awards, including the 2018 Femina Women Super Achiever Award, the 2014 Maharani Gayatri Devi Award for Woman of Excellence and the Karamveer Puruskar in 2009 for her work as a journalist in creating social awareness and for being the best literary consultant in the country. She is also the producer for Mountain Echoes: The Bhutan Festival of Arts, Literature and Culture, The Woman Up! Summit and Soul Connect Experiences.

b: One of the most elegant batters in world cricket, Mithali Raj first gave a glimpse of her class with her performance with the willow at a tender age of 19 where she scored 214 runs against England in the second and…
f: One of the most elegant batters in world cricket, Mithali Raj first gave a glimpse of her class with her performance with the willow at a tender age of 19 where she scored 214 runs against England in the second and final Test at Taunton. Her calm and composed batting style has always grabbed eyeballs. She led India to their first World Cup final in 2005 and 2017 and first-ever Test series victory in England in 2006.

b: Mitra Phukan is a writer, translator, columnist and trained classical vocalist. Her published works include four children’s books, a biography, the novels The Collector’s Wife and A Monsoon of Music , and a…
f: Mitra Phukan is a writer, translator, columnist and trained classical vocalist. Her published works include four children’s books, a biography, the novels The Collector’s Wife and A Monsoon of Music , and a collection of her newspaper columns titled Guwahati Gaze . Her latest works are a translation of the Assamese novel Blossoms in the Graveyard and A Full Night’s Thievery , her own collection of short stories.

b: Mmhonlumo Kikon , a poet with three published books, holds a Masters in English Literature from Delhi University and is an ASPEN Fellow. He served as the MLA for the Bhandari Assembly Constituency in Nagaland for two…
f: Mmhonlumo Kikon , a poet with three published books, holds a Masters in English Literature from Delhi University and is an ASPEN Fellow. He served as the MLA for the Bhandari Assembly Constituency in Nagaland for two consecutive terms from 2013 to 2023. Additionally, he held the position of Minister in the Government of Nagaland and served as an Advisor on Information Technology and Communication, New & Renewable Energy, Science & Technology.

b: Mohammad Hasan , a Fulbright and British Council Fellow, studied human geography at Jodhpur and Syracuse Universities and management at Manchester University. He taught in the Jodhpur and Nairobi Universities and HCM…
f: Mohammad Hasan , a Fulbright and British Council Fellow, studied human geography at Jodhpur and Syracuse Universities and management at Manchester University. He taught in the Jodhpur and Nairobi Universities and HCM Rajasthan State Institute of Public Administration. His concern for human rights and environment is embedded in his book of poetry Sediments of Silence and other writings.

b: MNR Samant headed a covert warfare unit under the Directorate of Naval Intelligence. In the run up to the 1971 India-Pakistan war, Captain Samant conducted an eight-month long campaign of covert naval warfare against…
f: MNR Samant headed a covert warfare unit under the Directorate of Naval Intelligence. In the run up to the 1971 India-Pakistan war, Captain Samant conducted an eight-month long campaign of covert naval warfare against the army in East Pakistan. During the 1971 war, he led a gunboat raid into Bangladesh for which he was awarded India’s second highest gallantry award, the Maha Vir Chakra.

b: Mohana Gill is a multi-award-winning author whose cookbooks encourage healthy eating habits. Her books have won Gourmand World Cookbook Awards and other awards. She writes books for adults and children, focusing on…
f: Mohana Gill is a multi-award-winning author whose cookbooks encourage healthy eating habits. Her books have won Gourmand World Cookbook Awards and other awards. She writes books for adults and children, focusing on educating, creating awareness and informing readers about the benefits of natural foods.

b: Mohinder (Jimmy) Amarnath is the son of the legendary cricketer Lala Amarnath. He played for the Indian national team from 1969 to 1989, scoring 4378 Test runs. Nine of his eleven Test centuries were scored overseas. He…
f: Mohinder (Jimmy) Amarnath is the son of the legendary cricketer Lala Amarnath. He played for the Indian national team from 1969 to 1989, scoring 4378 Test runs. Nine of his eleven Test centuries were scored overseas. He was Man of the Match in the semi-final and the final when India won the World Cup in 1983. He was named one of the Wisden Cricketers of the Year in 1984 and also received the Arjuna Award the same year

b: Mohini Gupta works at the Vedica Scholars Programme for Women, a postgraduate programme designed to empower young women professionals, in New Delhi. As the Charles Wallace India Trust Translator-Writer Fellow 2017, she…
f: Mohini Gupta works at the Vedica Scholars Programme for Women, a postgraduate programme designed to empower young women professionals, in New Delhi. As the Charles Wallace India Trust Translator-Writer Fellow 2017, she spent three months in Wales working on her Indian language poetry project for young readers. She has written for publications such as Huffington Pos t, The Caravan , TheWire.in and Scroll.in . Her English-Hindi translations have been published by Tulika Publishers.

b: Mohit Batra is a third-generation bookseller and the founder of the initiative A Book is the Smartest Hand Held Device , which aims to position books as meaningful tools for children through author discussions. He has…
f: Mohit Batra is a third-generation bookseller and the founder of the initiative A Book is the Smartest Hand Held Device , which aims to position books as meaningful tools for children through author discussions. He has curated sessions with Sudha Murty, Vishwanathan Anand, Malcolm Gladwell, Robin Sharma, Indira Nooyi, Jeffrey Archer, and Dr. Raghuram Rajan. A gold medalist from XLRI, Jamshedpur, Mohit left a corporate career to continue his family legacy of celebrating books. He also leads the literary agency Paper Sparrows, introducing new and classic voices, believing in the power of reading to connect us to ourselves.

b: Mohit Satyanand is an entrepreneur and investor and has been instrumental in establishing businesses that produce packaged foods, promote the arts and teach languages. He is currently the Chairperson of Teamwork Arts…
f: Mohit Satyanand is an entrepreneur and investor and has been instrumental in establishing businesses that produce packaged foods, promote the arts and teach languages. He is currently the Chairperson of Teamwork Arts and also serves on the boards of several other companies, both public and private. Satyanand is an active angel investor and mentors a wide range of start-ups.

b: Moin Mir is a London-based writer of Indian origin. He began his writing career under the influence of his grandfather, a scholar of Sufism, Mirza Ghalib and Omar Khayyam. Mir is the author of the critically acclaimed…
f: Moin Mir is a London-based writer of Indian origin. He began his writing career under the influence of his grandfather, a scholar of Sufism, Mirza Ghalib and Omar Khayyam. Mir is the author of the critically acclaimed book, Surat: Fall of a Port. Rise of a Prince . His upcoming book is a historical novel set against the backdrop of Sufism and its philosophies. Through a life journey, the book will give Sufism and its contribution to humanity, art, mathematics, spirituality and science a much deserved voice. The book will be published in June 2021.

b: Mona Zote lives in Aizwal, Mizoram. Her poetry has appeared in Cordite Poetry Review , Carapace , Poetry International Web , Indian Literature as well as in Dancing Earth: An Anthology of Poetry from North-East India .
f: Mona Zote lives in Aizwal, Mizoram. Her poetry has appeared in Cordite Poetry Review , Carapace , Poetry International Web , Indian Literature as well as in Dancing Earth: An Anthology of Poetry from North-East India .

b: Moneeza Hashmi wears several prominent and professional hats - she was President of the Commonwealth Broadcasting Association (later Public Media Alliance) for three terms; General Manager, International Relations at…
f: Moneeza Hashmi wears several prominent and professional hats - she was President of the Commonwealth Broadcasting Association (later Public Media Alliance) for three terms; General Manager, International Relations at HUM TV; Director of Programmes, Pakistan TV, and at present, she is the Creative and Media Head of KASHF Foundation, a women’s organisation working on giving micro-credit to women all over Pakistan. A recipient of various national and international awards, she received the President of Pakistan’s Pride of Performance Award in 2002. At present, Hashmi is Chairperson, Lahore Arts Council.

b: Moni Mohsin was born and raised in Pakistan. She has written two novels, The End of Innocence and Tender Hooks aka Duty Free and two books of collected columns, The Diary of a Social Butterfly and The Return of the…
f: Moni Mohsin was born and raised in Pakistan. She has written two novels, The End of Innocence and Tender Hooks aka Duty Free and two books of collected columns, The Diary of a Social Butterfly and The Return of the Butterfly . She now lives between London and Lahore.

b: Monica Ali is an award-winning, bestselling writer whose work has been translated into twenty-six languages. Her debut novel, Brick Lane, was shortlisted for the Booker Prize. Her other novels include Alentejo Blue, In…
f: Monica Ali is an award-winning, bestselling writer whose work has been translated into twenty-six languages. Her debut novel, Brick Lane, was shortlisted for the Booker Prize. Her other novels include Alentejo Blue, In the Kitchen and Untold Story. Ali was chosen as one of Granta’s 2003 Best of Young British Novelists, and has judged a number of literary prizes including as Chair of the Asian Man Booker. Her writing has appeared in The Guardian, The Times, The New Yorker and The New York Times , among several other publications. She is a Fellow of the RSA and of the Orwell Prize, and was, from 2015 to 2018, Distinguished Writer in Residence at the University of Surrey.

b: Monika Shergill is Vice President, Content at Netflix India and oversees the development, creation and licensing and acquisition of all Indian language content on Netflix, including films, series, reality shows, comedy…
f: Monika Shergill is Vice President, Content at Netflix India and oversees the development, creation and licensing and acquisition of all Indian language content on Netflix, including films, series, reality shows, comedy specials and documentaries. Shergill joined Netflix in 2019. She and her team have entertained audiences in India and around the world with local stories such as Ludo (film), AK vs AK (film), Ginny Weds Sunny (film), Masaba Masaba (series), Jamtara: Sabka Number Aayega (series) and Fabulous Lives of Bollywood Wives (reality series) and licensed films across languages including, Miss India (Telugu), Axone (Hindi) and Super Deluxe (Tamil). She is a seasoned media professional with over two decades of experience as a journalist, producer and network executive. She was earlier at Viacom 18 Digital Ventures as EVP and Head of Content for VOOT. Prior to this, she headed the network non-fiction programming and strategy for Star India Network. In this role, she helmed the biggest network multilingual content project, the series, Satyamev Jayate for Star Plus and nine other network channels. Shergill has worked across genres in all major broadcast networks including Zee and Sony Entertainment Television in key programming roles creating successful scripted and unscripted series.

b: Monisha Rajesh is a British journalist whose writing has appeared in The Guardian, The Financial Times and Time magazine. Her first book Around India in 80 Trains was one of The Independent’s top ten books on India. Her…
f: Monisha Rajesh is a British journalist whose writing has appeared in The Guardian, The Financial Times and Time magazine. Her first book Around India in 80 Trains was one of The Independent’s top ten books on India. Her second book, Around the World in 80 Trains won the National Geographic Traveller Book of the Year and was shortlisted for the Stanford Dolman Award. Her third book, Epic Train Journeys was shortlisted for the National Geographic Traveller Photography Book of the Year. In 2023 she was named in the Condé Nast Traveller Women Who Travel Power List and her new book, Moonlight Express: Around the World by Night Train was published in August.

b: Mozhdah Jamalzadah is an Afghan-Canadian singer, media personality and women’s rights activist. She has been called the Oprah of Afghanistan for having had a talk show debating taboo subjects like child marriage,…
f: Mozhdah Jamalzadah is an Afghan-Canadian singer, media personality and women’s rights activist. She has been called the Oprah of Afghanistan for having had a talk show debating taboo subjects like child marriage, violence against women and divorce in post-Taliban Afghanistan. Jamalzadah has guested on the 'Oprah Winfrey Show' and performed at the Whitehouse for the Obamas on International Women’s Day. Her biography, The Voice of Rebellion , written by Roberta Staley, was released in October 2019. She recently made her acting debut in the movie Red Snow , written and directed by award-winning Canadian director Marie Clements.

b: Mridul Haloi is one of the most prominent and original voices in contemporary Assamese poetry.He received Assam’s prestigious Munin Borkotoky Award for his debut collection Akole Aso, Kushale Aso . In 2015, he…
f: Mridul Haloi is one of the most prominent and original voices in contemporary Assamese poetry.He received Assam’s prestigious Munin Borkotoky Award for his debut collection Akole Aso, Kushale Aso . In 2015, he received the Sahitya Akademi Yuva Puraskar for the same book. Aamar Bhal Hobo is his second poetry collection. He has also written various prose, essays, and articles, and done a series of interviews with authors and political personalities. He is a journalist by profession and currently works as a sub-editor for the Assam Tribune Group.

b: Mridul Kirti has translated highly respectable Hindu scriptures such as Samaveda and Ashtavakra Gita written in the classic Sanskrit language into an easily understandable Hindi and Brij Bhasha. She has received…
f: Mridul Kirti has translated highly respectable Hindu scriptures such as Samaveda and Ashtavakra Gita written in the classic Sanskrit language into an easily understandable Hindi and Brij Bhasha. She has received prestigious awards, including the Vishwa Hindi Samman at the World Hindi Conference in Fiji 2023, Hindi Sevi Samman Padmabhushan Moturi Satya Narayan Award from the Central Hindi Institute, and Overseas Indian Hindi Bhushan Samman from the Uttar Pradesh Hindi Institute.

b: Mridula Behari is an award-winning author, novelist and playwright. She has authored 15 books including several short story collections, novels and plays. She has also written numerous plays for radio, TV and theatre.…
f: Mridula Behari is an award-winning author, novelist and playwright. She has authored 15 books including several short story collections, novels and plays. She has also written numerous plays for radio, TV and theatre. Her works have been translated into other languages. She speaks extensively at literary forums in India and abroad on women’s issues and her works. She represented India at the 2010 Beijing International Book Fair. Her association with Chicago artists and authors has led to a series of translations of their works into Hindi. She divides her time between Jaipur,Chicago and San Francisco.

b: Mridula Garg is proficient in both Hindi and English. She has written prolifically in Hindi, covering various genres, including 8 novels, 4 plays, 6 collections of essays, and 90 short stories. Additionally, she has…
f: Mridula Garg is proficient in both Hindi and English. She has written prolifically in Hindi, covering various genres, including 8 novels, 4 plays, 6 collections of essays, and 90 short stories. Additionally, she has authored 1 novel in English, titled The Last Email. Her most recent publication is a memoir titled VE NAYAAB AURTEIN, reflecting on her life experiences. Garg has earned several awards, including the 2004 Vyas Samman for her novel Kathgulab and the Sahitya Akademi Award in 2013 for Miljul Mann . She was also honoured with the Hellman-Hammett Grant by The Human Rights Watch, New York, in 2001. Her novel Chittacobra has been translated into English, French, Russian, and German. Miljul Mann is available in Bengali, Tamil, Telugu, Punjabi, Rajasthani, and Malayalam. Kathgulab has been translated into Marathi, Malayalam, and Japanese. Anity is available in English and Marathi, and Main Aur Main in Odiya and Marathi. In 1990, she served as the keynote speaker at the UN Colloquium for Women at IOWA and worked as a Research Associate at UC Berkeley, USA.

b: Mridula Koshy is a free library movement activist, a member of Free Libraries Network's Steering Committee and a Trustee of The Community Library Project in Delhi NCR. She feels lucky to work as a librarian and…
f: Mridula Koshy is a free library movement activist, a member of Free Libraries Network's Steering Committee and a Trustee of The Community Library Project in Delhi NCR. She feels lucky to work as a librarian and community organiser because every day there is a chance to work with others to create a more just world.

b: Mridula Ramesh is the author of critically acclaimed, The Climate Solution: India’s Climate Change Crisis and What We Can Do About It . She is founder of the Sundaram Climate Institute, which focuses on waste and…
f: Mridula Ramesh is the author of critically acclaimed, The Climate Solution: India’s Climate Change Crisis and What We Can Do About It . She is founder of the Sundaram Climate Institute, which focuses on waste and water solutions and education. She is an active angel investor in cleantech start-ups, with a portfolio of over 15 start-ups. Ramesh sits on several angel management groups, including the Indian Angels and the Chennai Angels, and is involved in several initiatives to spur entrepreneurship to build climate resilience. A graduate with distinction of Cornell University (with majors in Chemistry and Microbiology) with an MBA from the Kellogg School of Management, she worked at McKinsey in Silicon Valley before returning to India. She writes regularly on climate change, with her columns appearing in Firstpost and earlier in The Hindu, Live Mint, Bloomberg Quint and Conde Nast . She is the Executive Director of Sundaram Textiles and lives and experiments in Madurai in a net zero-waste house with her husband and two children. She is part of the Advisory Committee, UNDP India National Circular Economy Project, and the Chairperson of the Board of Governors, of NIT, Andhra Pradesh.

b: Mrinal Pande has taught at the Universities of Allahabad, Delhi and Bhopal before switching to journalism in mid 1980s . She has edited well known Hindi periodicals, Vama and Saptahik Hindustan for the Times of India…
f: Mrinal Pande has taught at the Universities of Allahabad, Delhi and Bhopal before switching to journalism in mid 1980s . She has edited well known Hindi periodicals, Vama and Saptahik Hindustan for the Times of India and the Hindustan Times group respectively. She has worked in the visual media as Editor- Anchor for Hindi news at NDTV and India’s public broadcaster, Doordarshan. In 2000, she became India’s first woman Chief Editor of a multi edition Hindi daily, Hindustan (Hindustan Times Group). She was also the first woman to be Secretary General of the Editors’ Guild of India. She is the founder President of the Indian Women’s Press Corps , a national body of India’s women journalists. Pande has been a member of the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation in India and also a member of the National Board for Film Certification . She was a member of the group that prepared Shramshakti , India’s first documentation of the status and lives of women workers in the unorganised informal sector . The report was published in 1989 . After retiring in 2009, she was appointed Chairman of India’s national broadcaster, Prasar Bharati in 2010. She completed her term in March 2014. Currently she is Group Editorial Advisor to The National Herald Group. Pande writes in both Hindi and in English. Her work covers fiction, plays and essays on contemporary India and its women and a study of India’s rural women and their sexual and reproductive lives. She was awarded the Padmashree in 2006 for her services in the field of journalism.

b: Mrinalini Venkateswaran is museum consultant to the Maharaja Sawai Man Singh II Museum, Jaipur. A fellow of the Royal Asiatic Society and former Board Member of the Commonwealth Association of Museums, she has published…
f: Mrinalini Venkateswaran is museum consultant to the Maharaja Sawai Man Singh II Museum, Jaipur. A fellow of the Royal Asiatic Society and former Board Member of the Commonwealth Association of Museums, she has published on museum collections, and Monuments of India for young readers. She holds the Rajiv Gandhi Cambridge Scholarship, for a PhD in History.

b: Mugdha Sinha is a career civil servant with twenty years of wide ranging experience in governance, policy making and International trade negotiations. She has worked in the Ministries of Textiles, Industry and Commerce…
f: Mugdha Sinha is a career civil servant with twenty years of wide ranging experience in governance, policy making and International trade negotiations. She has worked in the Ministries of Textiles, Industry and Commerce both at the Centre and in her cadre, the state of Rajasthan, and also in Food, Public Distribution & Consumer Affair, and Science and Technology. She is currently Secretary Art, Literature, Culture and Archaeology and Director General, Kala Kendra, Jaipur for the Government or Rajasthan.

b: Muhamed ÄŒengiÄ‡ is a career diplomat with more than two decades of experience in the Bosnia and Herzegovina Foreign Service. He has a degree from the faculty of Political Science at Sarajevo University, Bosnia and…
f: Muhamed ÄŒengiÄ‡ is a career diplomat with more than two decades of experience in the Bosnia and Herzegovina Foreign Service. He has a degree from the faculty of Political Science at Sarajevo University, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and has done a diplomatic training course from the Institute of Diplomacy and Foreign Relations, Kula Lumpur, Malaysia. His interests include photography and beekeeping. Apart from the Bosnian language, Ambassador Muhamed ÄŒengiÄ‡ speaks English and Russian.

b: Muhammad Yunus is a Nobel Laureate professor, the father of both social business and microcredit, the founder of Grameen Bank and of more than 50 other companies in Bangladesh. For his constant innovation and…
f: Muhammad Yunus is a Nobel Laureate professor, the father of both social business and microcredit, the founder of Grameen Bank and of more than 50 other companies in Bangladesh. For his constant innovation and enterprise, in 2012 Fortune Magazine named Yunus as “one of the greatest entrepreneurs of our time.” In 2006, Yunus and Grameen Bank were jointly awarded Nobel Peace Prize. He is one of only seven individuals to have received the Nobel Peace Prize, the United States Presidential Medal of Freedom and the United States Congressional Gold Medal.

b: Mujib Mashal is the South Asia bureau chief for The New York Times , reporting from New Delhi on India and its neighbours. Previously, he was the paper’s senior Afghanistan correspondent and has written for TIME, The…
f: Mujib Mashal is the South Asia bureau chief for The New York Times , reporting from New Delhi on India and its neighbours. Previously, he was the paper’s senior Afghanistan correspondent and has written for TIME, The Atlantic, and Harpers . Born in Kabul, he holds a degree in South Asian history from Columbia University.

b: Mujibur Rehman teaches at Jamia Millia Central University, New Delhi. He is the author of the book, Shikwa-e-Hind: The Political Future of Indian Muslims ( Simon and schuster, 2024) . His other works include Rise of…
f: Mujibur Rehman teaches at Jamia Millia Central University, New Delhi. He is the author of the book, Shikwa-e-Hind: The Political Future of Indian Muslims ( Simon and schuster, 2024) . His other works include Rise of Saffron Power (Routledge, 2018) and he regularly writes on contemporary affairs for major Indian publications.

b: Mukesh Bansal is a computer science engineer from IIT Kanpur and a technology entrepreneur. He founded India’s largest fashion retailer Myntra and headed the ecommerce division for Flipkart after a highly successful…
f: Mukesh Bansal is a computer science engineer from IIT Kanpur and a technology entrepreneur. He founded India’s largest fashion retailer Myntra and headed the ecommerce division for Flipkart after a highly successful acquisition. He is the co-founder of Cure Fit Healthcare Pvt Ltd. where he is involved in building a next-generation health platform that makes holistic health easy and accessible for everyone. He has over twenty years of experience in multiple early-stage start-ups in Silicon Valley (NexTag, eWanted, Centrata, newScale) where he held various senior management positions in Product Management and Marketing.

b: Mukesh Mathur is an Indian journalist, who is currently the State Editor of Dainik Bhaskar, Rajasthan. He started his media journey as a front line reporter and later served as the editor of Dainik Bhaskar's Indore,…
f: Mukesh Mathur is an Indian journalist, who is currently the State Editor of Dainik Bhaskar, Rajasthan. He started his media journey as a front line reporter and later served as the editor of Dainik Bhaskar's Indore, Surat, Shimla and Jodhpur editions. With his twenty-five years of association with the Dainik Bhaskar group, Mathur has championed numerous award-winning product initiatives and innovations, and played a pivotal role in strengthening facts-based reporting and journalism. A strong opinion maker, Mathur is known for his interesting styles and differentiated stands on relevant issues clubbed with creative uses of Graphics and Photo Ops, which has been the hallmark of his overall journalistic career.

b: Mukul Goyal is amongst the leading product designers of India. He is an engineering graduate from IIT, Kanpur, and has trained in design at the National Institute of Design, Ahmedabad and Domus Academy, Milan. Goyal…
f: Mukul Goyal is amongst the leading product designers of India. He is an engineering graduate from IIT, Kanpur, and has trained in design at the National Institute of Design, Ahmedabad and Domus Academy, Milan. Goyal embarked on his professional journey in 1991 and has accumulated a rich and varied work experience having worked in the design and manufacturing of Jewellery, Small objects of indulgence and Home & Builder Hardware, to name a few. Goyal is the Principal Designer & Director of Designwise India Pvt. Ltd.

b: Mukul Kumar is a distinguished civil servant, novelist, and poet, belonging to the 1997 batch of the Indian Railway Traffic Service. Currently, he serves in the Ministry of Railways. His literary contributions include…
f: Mukul Kumar is a distinguished civil servant, novelist, and poet, belonging to the 1997 batch of the Indian Railway Traffic Service. Currently, he serves in the Ministry of Railways. His literary contributions include two novels, As Boys Become Men and Seduction by Truth , along with three poetry anthologies titled The Irrepressible Echoes, Catharsis, and Rhythm of the Ruins. Kumar has received recognition for his outstanding service to the Indian Railways with the National Award, and he has been honoured for literary excellence with the Bharat Nirman Award by the Bharat Nirman Foundation. He has also been conferred the Poorvanchal Gaurav Samman. Mukul's latest fiction work is titled Lost in the Love Maze.

b: Mukul Sharma is a Delhi-based scholar, writer and development professional, specialising in environment, social, human rights and media. He is Professor, Environmental Studies at Ashoka University. His research…
f: Mukul Sharma is a Delhi-based scholar, writer and development professional, specialising in environment, social, human rights and media. He is Professor, Environmental Studies at Ashoka University. His research interests lie in examining the relations between nature, culture, ideology and politics. He is presently working on Dalit Ecologies and Religion, Sacrality and Environmental Politics.

b: Mukulika Banerjee was inaugural Director of the LSE South Asia Centre from 2015-2020 and is Associate Professor in Social Anthropology at the London School of Economics. She studied in Delhi and Oxford universities and…
f: Mukulika Banerjee was inaugural Director of the LSE South Asia Centre from 2015-2020 and is Associate Professor in Social Anthropology at the London School of Economics. She studied in Delhi and Oxford universities and taught at Oxford and UCL before joining LSE. Her books include Why India Votes?, The Pathan Unarmed and The Sari and edited Muslim Portraits . She has just completed a monograph Cultivating Democracy: Politics and citizenship in agrarian India .

b: Mukund Padmanabhan is a Professor of Public Practice at the newly-established Krea University, north of Chennai, where he teaches philosophy. He spent most of his working years in journalism, retiring as Editor of The…
f: Mukund Padmanabhan is a Professor of Public Practice at the newly-established Krea University, north of Chennai, where he teaches philosophy. He spent most of his working years in journalism, retiring as Editor of The Hindu in 2019. Prior to this, he was the editor of The Hindu Businessline , a sister publication from the same group. Padmanabhan is an M-Phil in Philosophy and worked briefly as a lecturer at the University of Delhi before switching to journalism. He is interested in and has written about politics, legal affairs, and literature.

b: Munizae Jahangir is a broadcast journalist and documentary filmmaker, currently anchoring a flagship current affairs show, ‘Spotlight with Munizae Jahangir’, on Aaj TV, one of Pakistan’s leading news media…
f: Munizae Jahangir is a broadcast journalist and documentary filmmaker, currently anchoring a flagship current affairs show, ‘Spotlight with Munizae Jahangir’, on Aaj TV, one of Pakistan’s leading news media networks. She is a co-founder and Editor-in-Chief of Voicepk.net, and was the first Pakistani journalist to have reported for an Indian news channel, NDTV, as their country correspondent for ten years. Jahangir’s high profile interviews include Hillary Clinton, Sadiq Khan, Benazir Bhutto, Nawaz Sharif and Malala Yousafzai. She was honoured as a Young Global Leader by the World Economic Forum and is a founding member of South Asian Women in Media.

b: Murali is a seasoned bookseller with over two decades of experience in the book retail industry. He currently serves as the Deputy General Manager of Retail and Procurement at Higginbothams Pvt. Ltd., the iconic…
f: Murali is a seasoned bookseller with over two decades of experience in the book retail industry. He currently serves as the Deputy General Manager of Retail and Procurement at Higginbothams Pvt. Ltd., the iconic 180-year-old bookstore chain headquartered in Chennai, with a presence across three states. Before joining Higginbothams, Murali spent ten years with Landmark, a bookselling career he entered by chance but went on to embrace with passion. His deep industry insight, commitment to readers, and lifelong dedication to books continue to shape his distinguished journey in the world of literature and retail.

b: Muthusami Kumaran is the Associate Professor of Nonprofit Management, University of Florida, USA. He is an internationally recognised expert in NGO capacity building, and has trained numerous NGO leaders across nine…
f: Muthusami Kumaran is the Associate Professor of Nonprofit Management, University of Florida, USA. He is an internationally recognised expert in NGO capacity building, and has trained numerous NGO leaders across nine countries.

b: Myna Mukherjee is a cultural producer, curator, and the founder/director of Engendered, a New York/New Delhi-based transnational arts and human rights organisation. She was the founder & artistic Director of Nayikas,…
f: Myna Mukherjee is a cultural producer, curator, and the founder/director of Engendered, a New York/New Delhi-based transnational arts and human rights organisation. She was the founder & artistic Director of Nayikas, NY's first South Asian classical & feminist dance theater company. She has curated internationally at the Lincoln Center, Asia Society, Tribeca Film Center, and Queens Museum, among others, and brought to India in 2016, North America’s largest South Asian Human Rights film festival, ‘I View World’. Mukherjee was the co-curator of HUB INDIA, the largest exhibition of Indian art to the West comprising of 3 museum shows and the centerpiece for ARTISSIMA, Italy's pivotal art fair.

b: K.R. Mythili Sundaram is the founder and director of Sudarsan Books & Crafts, established in 2001. Over the past two decades, she has transformed it into a thriving hub for readers and artisans in Nagercoil. With a deep…
f: K.R. Mythili Sundaram is the founder and director of Sudarsan Books & Crafts, established in 2001. Over the past two decades, she has transformed it into a thriving hub for readers and artisans in Nagercoil. With a deep passion for books and the arts, she actively promotes literary culture through collaborations with educational institutions and organizations. She is also a director at Kalachuvadu Publications, a pioneering force in the Tamil literary landscape. At Kalachuvadu, she played a pivotal role in its early initiatives, focusing on production, design, technical innovation and accounting. Mythili has also served as Deputy Area Commander in the Kanyakumari Home Guards for the past 15 years, and has been honoured with the Chief Minister's Anna Medal for distinguished service.

b: N. Kalyan Raman has translated and published 11 works of Tamil fiction by several important writers, including Ashokamitran and Perumal Murugan. His translations of contemporary Tamil poetry have been widely published…
f: N. Kalyan Raman has translated and published 11 works of Tamil fiction by several important writers, including Ashokamitran and Perumal Murugan. His translations of contemporary Tamil poetry have been widely published in journals and anthologies. He writes essays and review articles on literature, politics and cinema for a variety of publications across India. In 2017, he received the prestigious Pudumaipithan award for his contribution to Tamil literature through translations.

b: N. Ram , chairman of the Hindu Publishing Group and former Editor-in-Chief of The Hindu and Group Newspapers, is a political journalist. He has written on a range of socio-political subjects and specialised in…
f: N. Ram , chairman of the Hindu Publishing Group and former Editor-in-Chief of The Hindu and Group Newspapers, is a political journalist. He has written on a range of socio-political subjects and specialised in investigative journalism. Along with Susan Ram, he is the biographer of the Indian writer R.K. Narayan. He is the author of Why Scams Are Here To Stay: Understanding Political Corruption in India . Honours and awards include the Padma Bhushan (for journalism), and the Press Council of India’s Raja Rammohan Roy Award.

b: N.S. Madhavan is an award-winning Malayalam writer, essayist and columnist. His first story collection, Chulaimedile Savangal ( Corpses of Chulaimede ), was published in 1981. Thereafter, he lapsed into a decade long…
f: N.S. Madhavan is an award-winning Malayalam writer, essayist and columnist. His first story collection, Chulaimedile Savangal ( Corpses of Chulaimede ), was published in 1981. Thereafter, he lapsed into a decade long silence and returned in 1991 with his comeback story, the critically acclaimed Higuita . His second collection of stories was also called Higuita . Since then he has published five collections of stories, a novel, a collection of plays, a collection of travelogues and a book of literary criticism. He is a four-time winner of the Katha Prize series (Delhi) for Malayalam and an annual award for best stories in regional languages. His only novel, Lanthan Batheriyile Luthiniyakal , came out in 2003. The English translation, Litanies of Dutch Battery , won the Crossword Award for Best Indian Fiction in translation.

b: Nadifa Mohamed was born in Hargeisa in 1981. Her first novel, Black Mamba Boy , won the Betty Trask Prize, was longlisted for the Orange Prize and shortlisted for the Guardian First Book Award, the John Llewellyn Rhys…
f: Nadifa Mohamed was born in Hargeisa in 1981. Her first novel, Black Mamba Boy , won the Betty Trask Prize, was longlisted for the Orange Prize and shortlisted for the Guardian First Book Award, the John Llewellyn Rhys Prize, the Dylan Thomas Prize, and the PEN Open Book Award. In 2013, she was selected as one of Granta’s Best of Young British Novelists. Her second novel, The Orchard of Lost Souls , won a Somerset Maugham Prize and the Prix Albert Bernard, was longlisted for The Dylan Thomas Prize and shortlisted for the Hurston/Wright Legacy Award. In 2017, she was selected as one of Freeman’s Journal’s ‘Future of New Writing’.

b: Naina Lal Kidwai is the Chairperson of Altico Capital India Ltd and Advent Private Equity India Advisory board and a Non-Executive Director on the boards of Max Financial Services, CIPLA, Nayara Energy and Larsen and…
f: Naina Lal Kidwai is the Chairperson of Altico Capital India Ltd and Advent Private Equity India Advisory board and a Non-Executive Director on the boards of Max Financial Services, CIPLA, Nayara Energy and Larsen and Toubro. She has served as President of the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry and headed the boards of HSBC Asia Pacific, HSBC India and Nestle. An MBA from Harvard Business School, she is the recipient of numerous honours, including the Padma Shri. She is the author of 30 Women in Power: Their Voices, Their Stories and Survive Or Sink: An Action Agenda for Sanitation, Water, Pollution and Green Finance .

b: Naintara Maya Oberoi is a writer based in Paris and Delhi. Her work has appeared in Time Out, Caravan, National Geographic Traveller, The Hindu, The Indian Quarterly and Outlook Traveller. She is currently a doctoral…
f: Naintara Maya Oberoi is a writer based in Paris and Delhi. Her work has appeared in Time Out, Caravan, National Geographic Traveller, The Hindu, The Indian Quarterly and Outlook Traveller. She is currently a doctoral researcher in political philosophy at the Archives Husserl, at the École Normale Supérieure in Paris.

b: Justice Najmi Waziri, with extensive legal practice in the Supreme Court of India and High Court of Delhi, served as the Standing Counsel for the Government of National Capital Territory of Delhi for 5 years. Later, he…
f: Justice Najmi Waziri, with extensive legal practice in the Supreme Court of India and High Court of Delhi, served as the Standing Counsel for the Government of National Capital Territory of Delhi for 5 years. Later, he became a Judge at the High Court of Delhi for over a decade, contributing to social justice, environmental preservation, and sports law development. Notable initiatives include establishing the Aasra Fund-Green Delhi Account for acid attack victims, conducting social disability audits for accessibility, and planting native trees in Delhi's Central and Southern Ridge, known as Insaaf Bagh and Maafi Bagh.

b: Nalinakshya Talukdar, born in Assam in 1999 and currently based in Vadodara, Gujarat, is an emerging contemporary artist. He earned his Bachelor’s degree in Fine Art from Assam in 2021 and a Master’s in Visual Art from…
f: Nalinakshya Talukdar, born in Assam in 1999 and currently based in Vadodara, Gujarat, is an emerging contemporary artist. He earned his Bachelor’s degree in Fine Art from Assam in 2021 and a Master’s in Visual Art from the prestigious Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda in 2023. Nalinakshya has participated in numerous art events, exhibitions, and residencies, including the India Printmaker House Manorama Grant and Awards (2025), Space Studio Baroda (2024), MAIR Mumbai (2024), Vadehra Art Gallery (2025), Exhibit320 (2025), ArtIncept Exhibition (2024), Taiwan International Print Biennale (2024), and Bengaluru International Print Exchange (2023). His work reflects a strong engagement with contemporary visual practices.

b: Naman P. Ahuja is Professor at Jawaharlal Nehru University, New Delhi and the Editor of Marg . A specialist in the field of ancient Indian art, his writings have explored the history of aesthetics through shifts in…
f: Naman P. Ahuja is Professor at Jawaharlal Nehru University, New Delhi and the Editor of Marg . A specialist in the field of ancient Indian art, his writings have explored the history of aesthetics through shifts in iconography and trans culturalism in antiquity, the legacy of the Arts and Crafts Movement in the modern period and the changing narratives for Indian art in museums.

b: Naman P. Ahuja is a curator and Professor at Jawaharlal Nehru University, New Delhi. His studies on Indian art have explored the aesthetics of Indian visual culture, iconography and transculturalism in antiquity, as…
f: Naman P. Ahuja is a curator and Professor at Jawaharlal Nehru University, New Delhi. His studies on Indian art have explored the aesthetics of Indian visual culture, iconography and transculturalism in antiquity, as well as the legacy of the Arts and Crafts Movement in the modern period. Apart from various research papers, he is the author of the following books: Divine Presence: The Art of India and the Himalayas (Casa Asia and Five Continents Editions: Barcelona and Milan, 2003) , The Making of the Modern Indian Artist-Craftsman: Devi Prasad (Routledge, 2011), The Body in Indian Art and Thought (Ludion, Antwerp, 2013) , The Arts and Interiors of Rashtrapati Bhavan: Lutyens and Beyond (Publications Division, Delhi, 2016) , India and the World: a history in nine stories (Delhi: Penguin, 2017) and more recently: The Art & Archaeology of Ancient India, Oxford: Ashmolean Museum, November 2018.

b: Namita Bhandare is an award-winning journalist with nearly 30 years of reporting experience for various publications including magazines Sunday and India Today , and the daily The Hindustan Times. In 2013, she was…
f: Namita Bhandare is an award-winning journalist with nearly 30 years of reporting experience for various publications including magazines Sunday and India Today , and the daily The Hindustan Times. In 2013, she was appointed India’s first gender editor for Mint newspaper and remained in that position until 2016. She is at present an independent journalist who writes a fortnightly column on gender for The Hindustan Times and also writes for Mint, IndiaSpend and Foreign Policy.

b: Namita Devidayal is the author of four books. Her most recent, published this year, is Tangerine: How to Read the Upanishads Without Giving Up Coffee . Her earlier works include the award-winning memoir The Music Room ,…
f: Namita Devidayal is the author of four books. Her most recent, published this year, is Tangerine: How to Read the Upanishads Without Giving Up Coffee . Her earlier works include the award-winning memoir The Music Room , the bestselling novel Aftertaste , and the critically acclaimed biography of the genius musician Vilayat Khan, The Sixth String .Namita is also a journalist with The Times of India and was co-director of the Times LitFest in Mumbai. A trained Hindustani classical singer, she is a graduate of Princeton University, USA.

b: Namita S. Kalla is the Features Editor at Patrika Plus, Rajasthan Patrika . A writer and journalist with more than 15 years of experience, she has written for numerous outlets, including the Times Of India, Hindustan…
f: Namita S. Kalla is the Features Editor at Patrika Plus, Rajasthan Patrika . A writer and journalist with more than 15 years of experience, she has written for numerous outlets, including the Times Of India, Hindustan Times, DNA, Femina, Woman’s Era, Cosmopolitan and Catch News. She has also co-authored the book 101 Ways to Experience Jaipur and has written three coffee table books. She is currently working on a collection of short stories.

b: Namita Waikar is a writer and translator. She is the author of the novel The Long March. She is the managing editor of People’s Archive of Rural India (PARI) and writes on gender,women, society and culture with a…
f: Namita Waikar is a writer and translator. She is the author of the novel The Long March.
