She is the managing editor of People’s Archive of Rural India (PARI) and writes on gender,women, society and culture with a focus on rural life. She leads the Grindmill Songs Project and oversees PARI’s Indian languages translations programme. She is a partner in a chemistry databases firm in Pune, which is the culmination of her work of over 20 years as a biochemist and a software project manager.

b: Nancy Silberkleit , daughter-in-law of Louis H. Silberkleit, one of the founders of Archie Comics Publications, stepped into her role as Co-CEO of the company in 2009 with a vision that the comic book as a graphic novel…
f: Nancy Silberkleit , daughter-in-law of Louis H. Silberkleit, one of the founders of Archie Comics Publications, stepped into her role as Co-CEO of the company in 2009 with a vision that the comic book as a graphic novel is a valuable tool for developing literacy among first-time readers and instilling a love of reading for everyone. As a former public school educator, homemaker and mother, she knows the importance of learning to read and coined a personal motto that “Children+Comic Books=Reading, Knowledge and Confidence.”

b: Nand Bharadwaj is a well-known Rajasthani and Hindi writer and a media expert. He has written a number of books on poetry, fiction and literary criticism, as well as a collection of articles on contemporary media.…
f: Nand Bharadwaj is a well-known Rajasthani and Hindi writer and a media expert. He has written a number of books on poetry, fiction and literary criticism, as well as a collection of articles on contemporary media. Bhardwaj translated Albert Camus’s novel The Stranger in Rajasthani. He has received the Sahitya Akademi Award for his novel Samhi Khulto Marag , and the Bihari Award by K. K. Birla Foundation, among numerous others. As a former media professional, Bhardwaj worked with All India Radio and Doordarshan for more than three decades, retiring as the Senior Director, Doordarshan Kendra, Jaipur. He has been associated with the Jaipur Literature Festival as a regional advisor up till 2019.

b: Nand Bhardwaj is a well-known Rajasthani and Hindi writer as well as a media expert. He has more than two dozen books in Rajasthani and Hindi as poetry, novels, short stories, literary criticism and interviews with…
f: Nand Bhardwaj is a well-known Rajasthani and Hindi writer as well as a media expert. He has more than two dozen books in Rajasthani and Hindi as poetry, novels, short stories, literary criticism and interviews with eminent scholars including books on electronic media and culture are published at his credit. He has also translated Albert Camus’ The Outsider into Rajasthani. He is a recipient of numerous awards, including the Sahitya Akademi Award, Bhartendu Harishchandra Award, Bihari Award of Birla Foundation, Suryamal Misan Shikhar Puraskar, by Rajasthani Bhasha Sahitya Akademi and Outstanding Contribution Award by Doordarshan on Indian Classics. Bhardwaj is a retired Senior Director of Doordarshan Kendra, Jaipur and currently works as regional advisor for the Jaipur Literature Festival.

b: Nandakumar K. started his career as a sub-editor at Financial Express after doing his Master’s degree in Economics, followed by stints in international marketing and general management in India and abroad. Delhi: A…
f: Nandakumar K. started his career as a sub-editor at Financial Express after doing his Master’s degree in Economics, followed by stints in international marketing and general management in India and abroad. Delhi: A Soliloquy is his first published translation from Malayalam. His other translations are The Lesbian Cow and Other Stories, In the Name of the Lord. He lives and works in Dubai.

b: Nandan Nilekani is the Co-Founder and Chairman of Infosys Technologies Limited. He was the Founding Chairman of the Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI) in the rank of a Cabinet Minister from 2009- 2014.…
f: Nandan Nilekani is the Co-Founder and Chairman of Infosys Technologies Limited. He was the Founding Chairman of the Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI) in the rank of a Cabinet Minister from 2009- 2014. Most recently, Nilekani has co-founded and is the Chairman of EkStep, a not-for-profit effort to create a learner centric tech. In 2006, he was awarded the Padma Bhushan and was also named Businessman of the Year by Forbes Asia. Time magazine listed him as one of the 100 most influential people in the world in 2006 & 2009 , and Foreign Policy magazine listed him as one of the Top 100 Global thinkers in 2010. He won The Economist Social & Economic Innovation Award for his leadership of India’s Unique Identification initiative (Aadhaar). In 2017, he received the Lifetime Achievement Award from E & Y. Nilekani is the author of Imagining India. He co-authored his second book, Rebooting India: Realizing a Billion Aspirations , with Viral Shah, and co-authored his third book, The Art of Bitfulness: Keeping Calm in the Digital World, with Tanuj Bhojwani.

b: Nandini Krishnan is the author of Hitched: The Modern Indian Woman and Arranged Marriage and Invisible Men: Inside India's Transmasculine Networks. She is also the award-winning translator of Perumal Murugan's Estuary…
f: Nandini Krishnan is the author of Hitched: The Modern Indian Woman and Arranged Marriage and Invisible Men: Inside India's Transmasculine Networks. She is also the award-winning translator of Perumal Murugan's Estuary and Four Strokes of Luck and Other Stories. Her translation of Kalki's magnum opus Ponniyin Selvan is being released in ten parts. She has translated Charu Nivedita's Conversations with Aurangzeb: A Novel Krishnan novel-in-manuscript won the Writers of the World Festival prize, 2014. Her translation of Sajjad Haider Yaldram's Save Me from My Friends was shortlisted for the Jawad Memorial Prize for Urdu-English Translation 2022. Nandini lives with dozens of animals, thousands of books, and a varying number of humans in Madras

b: Nandini Nair has been a journalist for more than 15 years. She is the literary and culture editor of Open magazine . She has previously worked as a writer and commissioning editor in the feature sections of The Indian…
f: Nandini Nair has been a journalist for more than 15 years. She is the literary and culture editor of Open magazine . She has previously worked as a writer and commissioning editor in the feature sections of The Indian Express and The Hindu . She is the founder of Talking Books, Pune, a series of monthly conversations with authors. In her spare time, she teaches the craft of writing and editing.

b: Nandini Oberoi is an Associate Professor of Economics at the College of Vocational Studies, University of Delhi. For over a decade, she published and edited India’s first weekly newspaper for children, NewsJoy .…
f: Nandini Oberoi is an Associate Professor of Economics at the College of Vocational Studies, University of Delhi. For over a decade, she published and edited India’s first weekly newspaper for children, NewsJoy . Oberoi has also authored two children’s books and written on travel, food and culture for various magazines and newspapers. She has been a consultant editor for UNDP spanning diverse areas including human development.

b: Nandita Das has acted in more than 40 feature films in 10 different languages. Her directorial debut in 2008 was Firaaq . She has been twice on the jury of the Cannes Film Festival, among others. She has a master’s…
f: Nandita Das has acted in more than 40 feature films in 10 different languages. Her directorial debut in 2008 was Firaaq . She has been twice on the jury of the Cannes Film Festival, among others. She has a master’s degree in Social Work and is a strong advocate for social justice and human rights. She was conferred the ‘Knight of the Order of Arts and Letters’ by the French Government. Das was the Chairperson of the Children’s Film Society and wrote a monthly column for eight years in the magazine, The Week . Manto , Nandita’s second directorial film premiered in 2018 at the Cannes Film Festival, and can be seen on Netflix. Her first book Manto & I chronicles her six-year long journey of making the film. She has been supporting the campaign ‘Dark Is Beautiful’ and to further the conversation, she produced a short in 2019, called India’s Got Colour . During the lockdown, Das wrote, directed, produced and acted in a 7min. film called, Listen to Her, that sheds light on the increase in domestic violence and overburden of work that women have been facing during the pandemic.

b: Narendra Bishnoi is a government teacher from a community known for its commitment to environmental and wildlife protection. Guided by the teachings of Guru Jambhoji, he aims to promote environmental conservation and…
f: Narendra Bishnoi is a government teacher from a community known for its commitment to environmental and wildlife protection. Guided by the teachings of Guru Jambhoji, he aims to promote environmental conservation and raise awareness among his students.

b: N arendra Kohli is a novelist, short story writer, playwright and satirist. His first published story was ‘Do Haath’ , which came out in 1960. He is a modernist and yet well-connected to his Indian roots. His unique…
f: N arendra Kohli is a novelist, short story writer, playwright and satirist. His first published story was ‘Do Haath’ , which came out in 1960. He is a modernist and yet well-connected to his Indian roots. His unique approach makes him distinct from his contemporaries.

b: Naresh Trehan is a renowned cardiovascular and cardiothoracic surgeon. A graduate from King George Medical College, he subsequently trained and practiced at New York University Medical Center Manhattan USA from 1971 to…
f: Naresh Trehan is a renowned cardiovascular and cardiothoracic surgeon. A graduate from King George Medical College, he subsequently trained and practiced at New York University Medical Center Manhattan USA from 1971 to 1988, where he obtained a Diplomat from the American Board of Surgery and the American Board of Cardiothoracic Surgery. Dr. Trehan is the Chairman and Managing Director and Chief Cardiac Surgeon, Medanta: The MediCity. He founded the Escorts Heart Institute and Research Centre where he was the Executive Director. He has received many prestigious awards, including the Padma Shree and the Padma Bhushan.

b: Narmada Prasad Upadhyaya is a Hindi essayist and art critic who is working as the Additional Commissioner in the Commercial Tax Department in Madhya Pradesh. Upadhyaya has been invested in the study of Indian miniature…
f: Narmada Prasad Upadhyaya is a Hindi essayist and art critic who is working as the Additional Commissioner in the Commercial Tax Department in Madhya Pradesh. Upadhyaya has been invested in the study of Indian miniature paintings and murals for more than thirty years and has forty-six books to his credit, including translations, edited works and joint ventures. He is the recipient of several prestigious awards in the field of literature and art, including the distinguished Kala Bhushan Award.

b: Nasera Sharma is one of the most eminent writers of the modern world. As the author of 12 prolific novels, 9 short stories, numerous articles as well as translations, including 150 Urdu stories into Hindi, she takes…
f: Nasera Sharma is one of the most eminent writers of the modern world. As the author of 12 prolific novels, 9 short stories, numerous articles as well as translations, including 150 Urdu stories into Hindi, she takes readers of Hindi literature to the pinnacle of human emancipation. Her vast and extensive travel across the globe with special focus on West and Central Asia, particularly Afghanistan, Iraq and Iran, differentiates her and have made her an expert on the region. Her latest works include the novels Doosri Jannat and Shabd Pakheru as well as Adab Mai Bayi Pasli , a six-volume collection of Urdu, Persian and Arabic translations of modern literature. The recipient of several prizes, she was awarded the Hindi Sahitya Akademi Award in 2016 for her book Parijaat.

b: Nasreen Munni Kabir is a renowned UK-based documentary filmmaker and the author of 20 books on Hindi film. Her latest publication is In the Year of the Sahir. Her television programmes made for Channel 4 TV, UK, include…
f: Nasreen Munni Kabir is a renowned UK-based documentary filmmaker and the author of 20 books on Hindi film. Her latest publication is In the Year of the Sahir. Her television programmes made for Channel 4 TV, UK, include the series Movie Mahal, In Search of Guru Dutt, Follow that Star -profile of Amitabh Bachchan and the two-part programme, The Inner and Outer World of Shah Rukh Khan . She has also directed a profile on Bismillah Khan and the making of Bombay Dream s, the musical produced by Andrew Lloyd Webber for BBC Television, UK. Nasreen won the first Women of Achievement Award in Arts & Culture in 1999 for her promotion of Indian cinema in the UK, and became a Governor on the board of the British Film Institute in 2000, serving a six-year term. She continues to curate Channel 4's annual Indian cinema season.

b: Natasha Badhwar is a documentary film-maker, columnist and author of the memoirs, My Daughters' Mum and Immortal For A Moment . She leads the media team at Karwan e Mohabbat, a people’s campaign devoted to the…
f: Natasha Badhwar is a documentary film-maker, columnist and author of the memoirs, My Daughters' Mum and Immortal For A Moment . She leads the media team at Karwan e Mohabbat, a people’s campaign devoted to the universal values of the constitution – equality, freedom, justice and compassion. Badhwar has co-edited the books- Reconciliation: Karwan e Mohabbat’s Journey of Solidarity Through a Wounded India and When The Mask Came Off: Lockdown 2020.

b: Nathalie Handal ’s recent books include The Republics , lauded as ‘one of the most inventive books by one of today’s most diverse writers’ and winner of the Virginia Faulkner Award for Excellence in Writing, the…
f: Nathalie Handal ’s recent books include The Republics , lauded as ‘one of the most inventive books by one of today’s most diverse writers’ and winner of the Virginia Faulkner Award for Excellence in Writing, the acclaimed Poet in Andalucía and Love and Strange Horses , winner of the Gold Medal Independent Publisher Book Award, which The New York Times says, ‘trembles with belonging and longing’.

b: Nathan Thrall received the 2024 Pulitzer Prize for General Nonfiction for A Day in the Life of Abed Salama . He is also the author of The Only Language They Understand: Forcing Compromise in Israel and Palestine . He…
f: Nathan Thrall received the 2024 Pulitzer Prize for General Nonfiction for A Day in the Life of Abed Salama . He is also the author of The Only Language They Understand: Forcing Compromise in Israel and Palestine . He lives in Jerusalem.

b: Naveen Valsakumar is CEO and Co-Founder of Notion Press Publishing, India’s leading self-publishing platform. An aeronautical engineer turned publishing entrepreneur, he has spent the past decade helping over 50,000…
f: Naveen Valsakumar is CEO and Co-Founder of Notion Press Publishing, India’s leading self-publishing platform. An aeronautical engineer turned publishing entrepreneur, he has spent the past decade helping over 50,000 indie authors reach readers worldwide and distributing more than 120,000 books. Driven by a passion for solving problems, he continues to innovate in publishing, shaping one story at a time.

b: Navin Chawla studied at the Lawrence School, Sanawar and thereafter at St Stephen’s College, University of Delhi; University of London; and the London School of Economics. Later, he was a visiting fellow at the…
f: Navin Chawla studied at the Lawrence School, Sanawar and thereafter at St Stephen’s College, University of Delhi; University of London; and the London School of Economics. Later, he was a visiting fellow at the University of Oxford. He joined the Indian Administrative Service in 1969 and retired as secretary to the Government of India. He was appointed election commissioner in 2005 and Chief Election Commissioner in April 2009, when he conducted the general election to national and international acclaim.

b: Navroz K. Dubash is a Professor at the Centre for Policy Research and has been actively engaged in global and national debates on climate change, air quality, energy and water for over 25 years. Dubash is Coordinating…
f: Navroz K. Dubash is a Professor at the Centre for Policy Research and has been actively engaged in global and national debates on climate change, air quality, energy and water for over 25 years. Dubash is Coordinating Lead Author for the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change and serves on the UNEP Emissions Gap Report Steering Committee. He was conferred the TN Khoshoo Memorial Award in 2015 for his work on climate change. In 2018, his paper was awarded the Emerging Nations Award by the journal Environmental Research Letters. He has written two books, edited ten volumes and published more than 70 journal articles and book chapters. His most recent edited book is India in a Warming World: Integrating Climate Change and Development.

b: Navsangeet Kaur is a successful entrepreneur, a creative writer, and a poet. She is a university gold medalist in her graduation and post graduation from the Dept. of Biotechnology, Panjab University, Chandigarh and an…
f: Navsangeet Kaur is a successful entrepreneur, a creative writer, and a poet. She is a university gold medalist in her graduation and post graduation from the Dept. of Biotechnology, Panjab University, Chandigarh and an MBA from Symbiosis International University, Pune. Her love for books led her to take the entrepreneurial plunge to start White Falcon Publishing in 2014.

b: Nawaz Modi Singhania is a Fitness and Wellness Icon in India, founding Body Art Fitness Centres. An author of Pause Rewind , she focuses on natural anti-aging techniques and has over 30 years of experience in the…
f: Nawaz Modi Singhania is a Fitness and Wellness Icon in India, founding Body Art Fitness Centres. An author of Pause Rewind , she focuses on natural anti-aging techniques and has over 30 years of experience in the fitness industry.

b: Nawazuddin Siddiqui is an Indian film actor known for his work in Hindi cinema. An alumnus of the National School of Drama, Siddiqui’s breakthrough role was with Anurag Kashyap’s Black Friday , which won the Grand…
f: Nawazuddin Siddiqui is an Indian film actor known for his work in Hindi cinema. An alumnus of the National School of Drama, Siddiqui’s breakthrough role was with Anurag Kashyap’s Black Friday , which won the Grand Jury Prize at the Indian Film Festival of Los Angeles and was nominated for the Best Film (Golden Leopard) Award at the Locarno International Film Festival. Siddiqui has won many national and international awards, including the National Film Award for his role in Gangs of Wasseypur . He has also portrayed the acclaimed author Saadat Hasan Manto in Manto , an upcoming Indian biographical historical period drama film, written and directed by Nandita Das. He is the only Indian actor who has received a ‘thumbs-up’ from the great film critic Roger Ebert.

b: Nayanjot Lahiri is Professor of History at Ashoka University. Her books include Finding Forgotten Cities – How the Indus Civilization was Discovered, Monuments Matter – India’s Archaeological Heritage Since…
f: Nayanjot Lahiri is Professor of History at Ashoka University. Her books include Finding Forgotten Cities – How the Indus Civilization was Discovered, Monuments Matter – India’s Archaeological Heritage Since Independence, Time Pieces – A Whistle-Stop Tour of Ancient India and Archaeology and the Public Purpose – Writings on and by M.N. Deshpande . Her book Ashoka in Ancient India won the 2016 John F Richards Prize for the best book in South Asian History.

b: Nayantara Sahgal has written ten novels, a collection of short stories and 8 works of nonfiction, including three autobiographical works, apart from wide-ranging literary and political commentary. She is now at work on…
f: Nayantara Sahgal has written ten novels, a collection of short stories and 8 works of nonfiction, including three autobiographical works, apart from wide-ranging literary and political commentary. She is now at work on her 11th novel. She calls herself a political writer and her novels reflect the making of modern post-independence India. Her literary Awards include the Sinclair Fiction Prize, the Sahitya Akademi Award, the Commonwealth Writers’ Prize and an Honorary Doctorate of Letters from the University of Leeds. The Chandigarh Literary Festival and the Times Literary Festival have honoured her with Lifetime Achievement Awards. Some of her novels have been published in Japanese, German, Dutch and Italian. She has received a Diploma of Honour from Italy’s International Order of Volunteers for Peace and was associated with the founding of the People’s Union for Civil Liberties, which she served as a Vice-President during the 1980’s. She is a Member of the American Academy of Arts and Sciences and has held Fellowships in the United States at the Bunting Institute, the Woodrow Wilson International Center for Scholars and the National Humanities Center. She has received Distinguished Alumna Awards from Wellesley College, Massachusetts and Woodstock School, Mussoorie as well as a Doon Ratna from Dehradun. She returned her Sahitya Akademi Award in 2014 in protest against the murder of three writers known for their rejection of superstition and bigotry and the Akademi’s silence at the time. She has written and spoken strongly against the savage assaults taking place mainly on Muslims and on all those who oppose the ruling Hindutva ideology. She is an active member of the Indian Writers’ Forum, which highlights attacks on freedom of expression, on the Constitutio

b: Nayantara Violet Alva has worked in the television and OTT space as a creative producer in Mumbai. At Disney-Star she was a Senior Producer on several primetime Star Plus shows, including the massive hit Anupama .…
f: Nayantara Violet Alva has worked in the television and OTT space as a creative producer in Mumbai. At Disney-Star she was a Senior Producer on several primetime Star Plus shows, including the massive hit Anupama . Currently she works at Viacom18, producing and developing original web series for JioCinema across genres, two of which are slated for release in early 2025. Nayantara’s debut novel Liberal Hearts was published by Penguin in October 2024.

b: Needrup Zangpo is the executive director of the Bhutan Media Foundation (BMF). He previously served as the founding executive director of the Journalists' Association of Bhutan and editor of the Bhutan Observer .
f: Needrup Zangpo is the executive director of the Bhutan Media Foundation (BMF). He previously served as the founding executive director of the Journalists' Association of Bhutan and editor of the Bhutan Observer .

b: Neel Patel is the author of the story collection, If You See Me, Don't Say Hi, and the novel, Tell Me How to Be . His work has appeared in Elle India, The Paris Review , and more. He lives in Los Angeles, where he…
f: Neel Patel is the author of the story collection, If You See Me, Don't Say Hi, and the novel, Tell Me How to Be . His work has appeared in Elle India, The Paris Review , and more. He lives in Los Angeles, where he writes for television and film.

b: Neel Soni is a young conservationist and keen wildlife photographer. He was recognised as one of India’s leading young wildlife photographers by NDTV when one of his photographs was selected for their 10 best photos…
f: Neel Soni is a young conservationist and keen wildlife photographer. He was recognised as one of India’s leading young wildlife photographers by NDTV when one of his photographs was selected for their 10 best photos in 2015. His work has been published in Sanctuary magazine and in a coffee table book on tigers called The Tadoba Inheritance. His new book, A Walk On The Wildside , is a deeply personal memoir in the form of a picture book and refreshingly candid account of his love for the tiger and the mighty forest that he calls his second home.

b: Neelesh Misra is India’s most loved oral storyteller, reaching more than 100 million people every week across radio and digital platforms. He is also the founder of Gaon Connection , India’s biggest rural media…
f: Neelesh Misra is India’s most loved oral storyteller, reaching more than 100 million people every week across radio and digital platforms. He is also the founder of Gaon Connection , India’s biggest rural media platform. He has written five books and lyrics for more than 30 Hindi films. He is an award-winning journalist, formally Deputy Executive Editor of the Hindustan Times and South Asia correspondent for the Associated Press .

b: Neelkanth Mishra is Chief Economist, Axis Bank, Head of Global Research and a Whole Time Director of Axis Capital. He is a part-time member of the Indian Prime Minister’s Economic Advisory Council and part-time…
f: Neelkanth Mishra is Chief Economist, Axis Bank, Head of Global Research and a Whole Time Director of Axis Capital. He is a part-time member of the Indian Prime Minister’s Economic Advisory Council and part-time Chairman of UIDAI (Aadhaar). He is a member of the CII’s Economic Affairs Council. He is a gold-medallist and Distinguished Alumnus Awardee from IIT-Kanpur.

b: Neelum Saran Gour is the author of six novels, four short story collections, and two works of non-fiction, and has translated one of her novels from English to Hindi. She has reviewed for the TLS, the Book Review, the…
f: Neelum Saran Gour is the author of six novels, four short story collections, and two works of non-fiction, and has translated one of her novels from English to Hindi. She has reviewed for the TLS, the Book Review, the Indian Review of Books and Biblio , has been a columnist on the Allahabad page of Hindustan Times and currently writes a literary column for Firstpost . Her latest novel, Requiem In Raga Janki , won The Hindu Prize for Fiction, 2018. She works as a Professor in English Literature at the University of Allahabad.

b: Neena Gupta is a two-time National Award-winning actor, filmmaker, producer and television personality. She has starred in several critically-acclaimed television shows such as Khandaan and Mirza Ghalib . She has also…
f: Neena Gupta is a two-time National Award-winning actor, filmmaker, producer and television personality. She has starred in several critically-acclaimed television shows such as Khandaan and Mirza Ghalib . She has also worked extensively in art-house and independent films such as Mandi, Trikal and Jaane Bhi Do Yaaron . Neena has directed, produced and acted in several television shows including, Saans, Siski and Son Pari . Her most recent works include her award-winning performances in Badhai Ho, Shubh Mangal Zyaada Saavdhan, Panchayat and The Last Colour .

b: Neeraj Jain’s commitment to advancing Indian education and promoting reading, as the Managing Director for Scholastic India, has led to significant growth and expansion into ed-tech and education domains. In light of…
f: Neeraj Jain’s commitment to advancing Indian education and promoting reading, as the Managing Director for Scholastic India, has led to significant growth and expansion into ed-tech and education domains. In light of his contributions and calibre, he has been elevated to the role of President – Asia, overseeing the company’s publishing and distribution strategies across the continent. Outside of Scholastic, he has actively represented the publishing industry, serving as the Chair of the FICCI Publishing Committee and the immediate past president of the Association of Publishers in India.

b: Neeraj Kumar , a 1976 batch IPS officer, retired as the Delhi Police Commissioner in 2013. During the 9 years he spent on deputation in the CBI, he investigated several high-profile cases, bringing dreaded criminals and…
f: Neeraj Kumar , a 1976 batch IPS officer, retired as the Delhi Police Commissioner in 2013. During the 9 years he spent on deputation in the CBI, he investigated several high-profile cases, bringing dreaded criminals and underworld elements to justice. He has authored two books, Dial D for Don and Khaki Files . Season 1 and Season 2 of Delhi Crime on Netflix are based on stories from his second book. His third book, Cop in Cricket , is based on his experiences as the Head of the Anti-Corruption Unit of the BCCI between 2015 and 2018, where he recounts his campaigns against corrupt practices in Indian cricket.

b: Neerja Birla , a passionate educationist and a mental health champion, is the founder and chairperson of Aditya Birla Education Trust. Winner of many national and international awards, she currently holds the G100 â€“…
f: Neerja Birla , a passionate educationist and a mental health champion, is the founder and chairperson of Aditya Birla Education Trust. Winner of many national and international awards, she currently holds the G100 – Global Chair Mental Health and serves as a trustee of the Mumbai Police Foundation.

b: Neerja Chowdhury is an award-winning journalist, columnist, and political commentator. In the course of a distinguished career of over forty years, she was political editor of the Indian Express for ten years and…
f: Neerja Chowdhury is an award-winning journalist, columnist, and political commentator. In the course of a distinguished career of over forty years, she was political editor of the Indian Express for ten years and covered the terms of eight prime ministers and ten Lok Sabha elections. She has won several prestigious awards for her journalism including the first Chameli Devi Jain Award for Outstanding Women Mediapersons, the India Today–PUCL Journalism for Human Rights Award, and the Prem Bhatia Award for Best Political Reporting. She is contributing editor, the Indian Express , and her weekly column, The Neerja Chowdhury Column , is widely followed by participants and observers of contemporary Indian politics.

b: Neeta Gupta is the publisher at Yatra Books and a literary consultant with a special emphasis on translations. She is also the editor of Bharatiya Anuvad Parishad’s quarterly journal on translation, Anuvad. Yatra…
f: Neeta Gupta is the publisher at Yatra Books and a literary consultant with a special emphasis on translations. She is also the editor of Bharatiya Anuvad Parishad’s quarterly journal on translation, Anuvad. Yatra Books and Bharatiya Anuvad Parishad share strategic strengths and draw synergy and creativity from their complementary activities. She has been working towards creating publishing connectivities across different languages and cultures.

b: Neha Bhatt has been a journalist for sixteen years and reports on current affairs, health and human rights for international publications such as The Guardian, The Globe and Mail, The British Medical Journal, among many…
f: Neha Bhatt has been a journalist for sixteen years and reports on current affairs, health and human rights for international publications such as The Guardian, The Globe and Mail, The British Medical Journal, among many others. She has won multiple awards for her features on women's rights and mental health for Outlook magazine, where she worked for a long time. Bhatt is an advocate for conscious parenting and co-founder of the pioneering Facebook support network - Gentle Baby Sleep India. Sleeping Like A Baby , co-authored with Himani Dalmia, is her first book.

b: Neha Dixit is an independent journalist and author based in New Delhi. She covers intersections of politics, gender, and social justice. She reports for Al Jazeera, The Washington Post, Caravan , and other notable…
f: Neha Dixit is an independent journalist and author based in New Delhi. She covers intersections of politics, gender, and social justice. She reports for Al Jazeera, The Washington Post, Caravan , and other notable publications. She has won over a dozen international and national journalism awards, including the International Press Freedom Award 2019 from the Committee to Protect Journalists and the Chameli Devi Jain Award for Outstanding Woman Journalist 2017. The Many Lives of Syeda X is her first full-length non-fiction book.

b: Neha Hiranandani has spent the last two decades working on development issues, with a focus on gender equity in various organisations, including the United Nations. She completed her undergraduate degree with honours…
f: Neha Hiranandani has spent the last two decades working on development issues, with a focus on gender equity in various organisations, including the United Nations. She completed her undergraduate degree with honours from Wellesley College and has a master’s in education policy from Harvard University. Neha’s columns on social and economic issues have appeared in several prominent publications, including Indian Express , Huffington Post, NDTV and Vogue. Her first book, Girl Power ! was a national bestseller. Her new book examines a global, uncontrolled experiment – no generation before us has had to parent a generation that is born with a phone in their hands.

b: Neha Kirpal’s entrepreneurial journey over two decades spans across the creative & social sectors. Having founded India Art Fair and run it for ten years, she successfully sold the business and shifted her attention…
f: Neha Kirpal’s entrepreneurial journey over two decades spans across the creative & social sectors. Having founded India Art Fair and run it for ten years, she successfully sold the business and shifted her attention to mainstreaming mental health awareness & access. As co-founder of Amaha she joined Dr Amit Malik in 2019 to build India’s largest specialised mental health organisation with over 160 in-house clinicians today providing quality care & support in 16 languages, across 600 cities in India and reaching over 5 million lives on the digital platform globally. A mental health ambassador & recipient of numerous business awards; Kiral is an Aspen fellow, an Eisenhower fellow, and part of the World Economic Forum’s Young Global Leaders’ community.

b: Neha Sinha is a conservation biologist and acclaimed author with over a decade of experience in wildlife conservation. Trained in conservation at Oxford University and in literature at St. Stephen’s College, Delhi, she…
f: Neha Sinha is a conservation biologist and acclaimed author with over a decade of experience in wildlife conservation. Trained in conservation at Oxford University and in literature at St. Stephen’s College, Delhi, she blends scientific rigour with a distinctive literary voice. She is the author of Wild and Wilful: Tales of Fifteen Iconic Indian Species . Recognised for both her conservation work and her writing, Neha is committed to making the wonder and challenges of nature accessible to all. She works with WWF-India, lives in Delhi, and is often found birdwatching—especially drawn to species that are overlooked or considered “ugly.”

b: Neige Sinno is a French writer, who has lived for almost twenty years in Mexico. She has taught literature at various universities, and has written essays, stories and novels. Her book, Sad Tiger , a creative memoir on…
f: Neige Sinno is a French writer, who has lived for almost twenty years in Mexico. She has taught literature at various universities, and has written essays, stories and novels. Her book, Sad Tiger , a creative memoir on the subject of child abuse, has received many literary prizes, and has been translated into thirty languages.

b: Neel Kantha Uprety was the Chief Election Commissioner of Nepal from March 2013 to May 2015. He has over 25 years of experience in managing and strengthening the electoral process, specialized experience in election…
f: Neel Kantha Uprety was the Chief Election Commissioner of Nepal from March 2013 to May 2015. He has over 25 years of experience in managing and strengthening the electoral process, specialized experience in election management, project management, negotiation and conflict resolution and in-depth knowledge in electoral systems and procedures. He also has extensive experience of working in post-conflict and conflict-ridden areas. He was the International Commissioner for Electoral Justice System in Afghanistan from May 2019 to August 2020. He has visited to over 31 countries in Asia, Europe, North and South America and Africa to monitor elections and work on election management.

b: Niamh Campbell is an Irish writer from Dublin. She is the author of This Happy (2020), We Were Young (2022) and Make Strang e (2026). She has won the Sunday Times Audible Short Story Award and the Rooney Prize for Irish…
f: Niamh Campbell is an Irish writer from Dublin. She is the author of This Happy (2020), We Were Young (2022) and Make Strang e (2026). She has won the Sunday Times Audible Short Story Award and the Rooney Prize for Irish Writing.

b: Nicholas Allan is a former finance professional with a deep passion for music and the arts. After a successful career in the financial sector, he now focuses on Indian hotels. A former Deputy Chair of the English…
f: Nicholas Allan is a former finance professional with a deep passion for music and the arts. After a successful career in the financial sector, he now focuses on Indian hotels. A former Deputy Chair of the English National Opera, Allan is the current Chair of the National Opera Studio. He is also an avid walker, singer, and cryptic crossword enthusiast.

b: Nicholas Coleridge spent 30 years as Editorial Director, Managing Director, President and Chairman of Conde Nast. He is Chairman of the Victoria & Albert Museum and the author of 14 books, including his memoirs The…
f: Nicholas Coleridge spent 30 years as Editorial Director, Managing Director, President and Chairman of Conde Nast. He is Chairman of the Victoria & Albert Museum and the author of 14 books, including his memoirs The Glossy Years , Paper Tigers, The Fashion Conspiracy and novels including Godchildren, With Friends Like These and A Much Married Man.

b: Nicholas Shakespeare is a prize-winning British novelist and biographer whose works have been translated into 22 languages. His 1994 novel, The Dancer Upstairs , was adapted into a film by John Malkovich, featuring…
f: Nicholas Shakespeare is a prize-winning British novelist and biographer whose works have been translated into 22 languages. His 1994 novel, The Dancer Upstairs , was adapted into a film by John Malkovich, featuring Javier Bardem. His most recent publication is the critically acclaimed authorised biography of Ian Fleming.

b: Nick Perry is deputy news editor for AFP’s South Asia bureau in New Delhi. He has reported from India and Bangladesh and extensively across Indonesia as a foreign correspondent. Previously he was a political reporter…
f: Nick Perry is deputy news editor for AFP’s South Asia bureau in New Delhi. He has reported from India and Bangladesh and extensively across Indonesia as a foreign correspondent. Previously he was a political reporter in Australia covering international affairs.

b: Nicky Arscott writes and illustrates poetry comics, which have been published in INK BRICK , New Welsh Review and Nashville Review and have been exhibited at MOMA Wales. She is the founder of a small comics press,…
f: Nicky Arscott writes and illustrates poetry comics, which have been published in INK BRICK , New Welsh Review and Nashville Review and have been exhibited at MOMA Wales. She is the founder of a small comics press, Mother Mary, which focuses on publishing poetry comics.

b: Nicolas Idier holds a PhD in Art History from Sorbonne University. His last three novels have been shortlisted for major literary awards such as the Prix Décembre, the Prix Médicis, the Prix Jean Freustié de…
f: Nicolas Idier holds a PhD in Art History from Sorbonne University. His last three novels have been shortlisted for major literary awards such as the Prix Décembre, the Prix Médicis, the Prix Jean Freustié de l’Académie française, the Prix Saint-Malo/Etonnants Voyageurs and the Prix Le Figaro. His last book, A Chinese Youth , was recently awarded the 2017 Prix Printemps du Roman. He is currently working as a diplomat at the French Institute in India and the French Embassy, running the French Book Office.

b: Nida Hasan has been part of Change.org India since 2014. Currently the Country Director for Change.org, she is responsible for developing a vision for Change.org's work in India that aims to more effectively empower…
f: Nida Hasan has been part of Change.org India since 2014. Currently the Country Director for Change.org, she is responsible for developing a vision for Change.org's work in India that aims to more effectively empower Indians who use Change.org to create the change they want to see. Under her leadership, the platform has reached 3.7 crore users and continues to grow. In her previous capacity as Campaigns Director for Change.org India, Hasan was responsible for executing the vision for Change.org's Women and Girls project. She led a team of campaigners to support women leaders through content, mobilization, and strategy support, which has led to some of the most iconic digital campaigns by women in the country. Before Change.org, Hasan worked as a journalist for over nine years in top media organisations. She covered South Asia and South East Asia for France's national TV, France 2, and reported on a wide range of issues for CNN-News18.

b: Nidhi Chawla is the CEO and Co-founder of Silver Talkies, a community-led platform focused on making healthy ageing a viable goal for older adults. She has received several leadership awards for her work in the…
f: Nidhi Chawla is the CEO and Co-founder of Silver Talkies, a community-led platform focused on making healthy ageing a viable goal for older adults. She has received several leadership awards for her work in the eldercare space and is also the co-author of the book Rethink Ageing .

b: Nijesh Shah is the Group President and Director of Sapna Book House, India’s largest bookstore chain, and the country’s leading regional-language publisher, recognized by the Limca and India Book of Records. Passionate…
f: Nijesh Shah is the Group President and Director of Sapna Book House, India’s largest bookstore chain, and the country’s leading regional-language publisher, recognized by the Limca and India Book of Records. Passionate about making books accessible, he launched SapnaOnline.com, SapnaInk, Diyara Press, and SapnaRise—platforms that make books available through e-commerce, empower authors through self-publishing, and connect readers with writers worldwide through author events and author podcast. Sapna has published over 8,000 titles, with a strong presence in Kannada and academic publishing, and operates over twenty four flagship bookstores.

b: Nikesh Shukla is a novelist and screenwriter.He is the author of CoconutUnlimited, shortlisted for the Costa First Novel Award, Meatspace and the critically acclaimed, The One Who Wrote Destiny . Shukla is a…
f: Nikesh Shukla is a novelist and screenwriter.He is the author of CoconutUnlimited, shortlisted for the Costa First Novel Award, Meatspace and the critically acclaimed, The One Who Wrote Destiny . Shukla is a contributing editor to the Observer Magazine and was previously their columnist. He is the editor of the bestselling essay collection, The Good Immigrant, which won the reader's choice at the Books Are My Bag Awards. He co-edited The GoodImmigrant USA with Chimene Suleyman . He is the author of two YA novels, Run,Riot , shortlisted for a National Book Award, and The Boxer , long listed for the Carnegie Medal . Shukla was one of TIME Magazine’s cultural leaders,ForeignPolicy magazine's 100 Global Thinkers and The Bookseller's 100 most influential people in publishing in 2016 and in 2017. He is the co-founder of the literary journal, The Good Journal and The Good Literary Agency. Shukla is a fellow of the Royal Society Of Literature and a member of the Folio Academy. His new book, Brown Baby: A Memoir Of Race, Family And Home will be released on Bluebird in February 2021.

b: Nikhil J. Alva is an award-winning producer, director and writer. His work has been screened on major networks and at festivals all over the world. A chronic supporter of underdog causes, Alva loves the challenge of…
f: Nikhil J. Alva is an award-winning producer, director and writer. His work has been screened on major networks and at festivals all over the world. A chronic supporter of underdog causes, Alva loves the challenge of trudging off-the-beaten-path. If I Have To Be A Soldier is his first novel.

b: Nikhil Kumar is CNN’s New Delhi Bureau Chief responsible for the strategic planning of the network’s multi-platform news coverage from India and the region. Kumar was previously the South Asia Bureau Chief for TIME…
f: Nikhil Kumar is CNN’s New Delhi Bureau Chief responsible for the strategic planning of the network’s multi-platform news coverage from India and the region. Kumar was previously the South Asia Bureau Chief for TIME magazine. Before moving to India in early 2015, he was a Senior Editor based in New York, editing and managing TIME ’s international editions, as well as foreign coverage in the U.S. edition. Kumar has reported on several key regional and global political, economic and social stories including the devastating Nepal earthquake in 2015, the global financial crisis, the Eurozone sovereign debt crisis and the Boston marathon bombings. He has also interviewed leaders from the region including Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Afghanistan’s President Ashraf Ghani, Sri Lanka’s President Maithripala Sirisena and Bangladesh’s Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina.

b: Nikko Odiseos published his first book when he was in the fourth grade. As President of Shambhala Publications, he has established its growing Indian imprint and overseen acquisitions of Snow Lion Publications (for…
f: Nikko Odiseos published his first book when he was in the fourth grade. As President of Shambhala Publications, he has established its growing Indian imprint and overseen acquisitions of Snow Lion Publications (for Buddhism) and Rodmell Press (for yoga).

f: Dr. Nikky-Guninder Kaur Singh is the Chair and Crawford Professor of Religious Studies at Colby College in the USA. Her interests focus on poetics and feminist issues. She has published extensively in the field of Sikh Studies. Her books hot from the press include Poems From the Sikh Sacred Tradition and Janamsakhi Paintings of Guru Nanak .

b: Nilanjana Bhowmick is an award-winning journalist and author based in New Delhi. Her debut nonfiction book Lies Our Mothers Told Us - The Indian Woman’s Burden was published to wide acclaim by Aleph Books in July…
f: Nilanjana Bhowmick is an award-winning journalist and author based in New Delhi. Her debut nonfiction book Lies Our Mothers Told Us - The Indian Woman’s Burden was published to wide acclaim by Aleph Books in July 2022. She has written and reported for some of the world’s most prestigious print publications and radio channels over the last two decades.

b: Nilanjana S. Roy is the author of the award-winning fantasy novels The Wildings and The Hundred Names of Darkness, and writes a regular column on books for the Financial Times. She has edited several anthologies, a…
f: Nilanjana S. Roy is the author of the award-winning fantasy novels The Wildings and The Hundred Names of Darkness, and writes a regular column on books for the Financial Times. She has edited several anthologies, a collection of essays on reading titled The Girl Who Ate Books and has just finished her third novel, Black River.

b: Nilosree Biswas is an author, filmmaker and columnist who writes about the history, culture, food and cinema of South Asia, the Middle East and the Asian diaspora.
f: Nilosree Biswas is an author, filmmaker and columnist who writes about the history, culture, food and cinema of South Asia, the Middle East and the Asian diaspora.

b: Nipun Malhotra is the Co-Founder and CEO of the Nipman Foundation that works in the areas of health and advocacy for Persons with Disabilities. He is a visiting Research Fellow at World Enabled, a Pineda Foundation…
f: Nipun Malhotra is the Co-Founder and CEO of the Nipman Foundation that works in the areas of health and advocacy for Persons with Disabilities. He is a visiting Research Fellow at World Enabled, a Pineda Foundation initiative. He is the Founder Chair of the FICCI D&I Working Group on Empowering Persons with Disability and is on the board of Directors at Vishwas, a non-profit working on disability and development. Malhotra launched a volunteer-led initiative called ‘Project Delhi’ during the Covid-19 lockdown to deliver groceries to Persons with Disabilities, which has impacted 2,100+ lives. His writings have appeared on Scroll.in, The Indian Express, NDTV Blogs, The Print and The Quint , among other publications.

b: Nirupama Dutt is a poet, journalist, translator and literary columnist. She penned the biography of Punjab’s Dalit icon, The Ballad of Bant Singh , and a translation into English of Gulzar’s anthology of poetry,…
f: Nirupama Dutt is a poet, journalist, translator and literary columnist. She penned the biography of Punjab’s Dalit icon, The Ballad of Bant Singh , and a translation into English of Gulzar’s anthology of poetry, Pluto , an anthology of Punjabi stories, Stories of the Soil , and the biography and poems of Lal Singh Dil.

b: Nirupama Singh Dar is a sociologist who works in the areas of fashion, popular culture and feminism. She has done her post graduate studies, Doctorate and Post Doctoral research from Jawaharlal Nehru University. Being…
f: Nirupama Singh Dar is a sociologist who works in the areas of fashion, popular culture and feminism. She has done her post graduate studies, Doctorate and Post Doctoral research from Jawaharlal Nehru University. Being the first doctorate on Fashion in India, she pioneered fashion research in India. She also studied Design at National institute of Fashion Technology, New Delhi and has been designing collections for her brand ‘Body Politic’. Her design work has been chronicled by the Indian embassy in Paris in their magazine Nouvelle De L’Inde . Dar is the director of Fashion Research Foundation . She consults on fashion and lectures on Sociology of Fashion and Popular Culture.

b: Nish Kumar is a comedian and host of The Mash Report on the BBC. He was nominated for the Edinburgh Comedy Award in 2015 and 2016. He has a half hour on Netflix as part of the Comedians of the World series. He was a…
f: Nish Kumar is a comedian and host of The Mash Report on the BBC. He was nominated for the Edinburgh Comedy Award in 2015 and 2016. He has a half hour on Netflix as part of the Comedians of the World series. He was a contributor to The Good Immigrant.

b: Nisha Susan is the author of the short story collection, The Women Who Forgot to Invent Facebook and Other Stories (2020, Westland). Her non-fiction deals with ideas of gender, culture and the internet. In 2021, she…
f: Nisha Susan is the author of the short story collection, The Women Who Forgot to Invent Facebook and Other Stories (2020, Westland). Her non-fiction deals with ideas of gender, culture and the internet. In 2021, she wrote a short book called Seventeen Years and a Pandemic: What Watching Grey's Anatomy Taught Me and has recently translated KR Meera's Qabar from Malayalam.

b: Nishant Jain is an IAS officer and a writer who has authored non-fiction books in Hindi and English. He was awarded an M.Phil. degree in Hindi Literature by the University of Delhi, and his self-help books Ruk Jaana…
f: Nishant Jain is an IAS officer and a writer who has authored non-fiction books in Hindi and English. He was awarded an M.Phil. degree in Hindi Literature by the University of Delhi, and his self-help books Ruk Jaana Nahi and Don't You Quit have been very well-received by young readers. Presently, he is posted as Director of Tourism, Government of Rajasthan.

b: Nishtha Gautam is an academic, author and translator examining the intersections of global culture and politics. Her latest book Sita’s Veil (Yatra, 2025) is a translation of a Hindi novel. She has also coedited a…
f: Nishtha Gautam is an academic, author and translator examining the intersections of global culture and politics. Her latest book Sita’s Veil (Yatra, 2025) is a translation of a Hindi novel. She has also coedited a critically acclaimed volume on strategic affairs In Hard Times: Security in Times of Insecurity (Bloomsbury, 2022).

b: Nishtha Satyam was appointed as the Deputy Country Representative for UN Women in 2018. She is the youngest Deputy Country Representative for the Entity of the UN across 193 countries. She formerly managed Strategic…
f: Nishtha Satyam was appointed as the Deputy Country Representative for UN Women in 2018. She is the youngest Deputy Country Representative for the Entity of the UN across 193 countries. She formerly managed Strategic Partnerships, Policy Impact and Public Relations for the UN Women Multi Country Office for India, Bhutan, Maldives and Sri Lanka. Satyam has also served as the Private Sector Partnerships Specialist with the Office of the Resident Coordinator of the United Nations and UNDP. As a futurist and feminist, she is an advocate of the urgency to mainstream women across the marketplace, workplace and community.

f: Nitya Ramakrishnan , a criminal lawyer, is passionate about mathematics, cricket, and cryptic crosswords. A graduate of St Stephen’s College and Delhi University’s Campus Law Centre, her book In Custody: Law, Impunity, and Prisoner Abuse in South Asia is widely regarded.

He also presided as Chairman of the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Review Committee in 2016.

f: Noa Avishag Schnall i s a Yemeni author, journalist, photographer, and human rights activist based in Paris, born and raised in Los Angeles. Her work spans multiple continents, focusing on amplifying stories of justice, resistance, and cultural celebration while collaborating with underrepresented communities. Her writing and photography have been published internationally across news, arts, and culture outlets. Recently, she sailed with the Freedom Flotilla Coalition aboard The Conscience as part of a mission to break the siege on Gaza.

b: Considered the founder of modern linguistics, Noam Chomsky is one of the most cited scholars in modern history. Among his groundbreaking books are S yntactic Structures, Language and Mind, Aspects of the Theory of…
f: Considered the founder of modern linguistics, Noam Chomsky is one of the most cited scholars in modern history. Among his groundbreaking books are S yntactic Structures, Language and Mind, Aspects of the Theory of Syntax and The Minimalist Program , each of which has made distinct contributions to the development of the field. He has received numerous awards, including the Kyoto Prize in Basic Sciences, the Helmholtz Medal and the Ben Franklin Medal in Computer and Cognitive Science. Chomsky introduced the Chomsky hierarchy, generative grammar and the concept of a universal grammar, which underlies all human speech and is based in the innate structure of the mind/brain. Chomsky has not only transformed the field of linguistics, his work has influenced fields such as cognitive science, philosophy, psychology, computer science, mathematics, childhood education, and anthropology. Chomsky is also one of the most influential public intellectuals in the world. He has written more than 100 books, his most recent being Climate Crisis and the Global Green New Deal: The Political Economy of Saving the Planet . Chomsky joined the UA in fall 2017, coming from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, where he worked since 1955 as professor of linguistics, then Institute Professor, now emeritus.

f: Norbert Peabody is Editor of the Cambridge University Press journal Modern Asian Studies and the author of Hindu Kingship and Polity in Precolonial India. f: Norman Ohler is a novelist and filmmaker. In 1995, he published the first hypertext-novel worldwide titled, Die Quotenmaschine , a detective story set in New York. In 2001, his acclaimed Berlin-novel Mitte was published, followed by a story about Johannesburg called Ponte City . In 2004, Ohler was writer-in-residence in Ramallah and wrote his Ramallah-Blog . In 2008, Ohler co-wrote Palermo Shooting , a film by Wim Wenders. In 2015, his first nonfiction book Der totale Rausch was published. It was translated as Blitzed: Drugs in Nazi Germany by Allen Lane and was a New York Times bestseller, currently translated into 28 languages. In 2017, Ohler’s fourth novel, Die Gleichung des Lebens , was published.

f: Oken Tayeng is the Founder of the award-winning firm Abor Country Travels and Expeditions (ACTE), a leading tour operator in North East India. Om Swami writes on his blog twice a month and stays away from all forms of social media.

f: Om Thanvi is former editor of Jansatta, a prominent Hindi daily of Indian Express group. f: Ornit Shani is the author of How India Became Democratic: Citizenship and the Making of the Universal Franchise and Communalism, Caste and Hindu Nationalism: The Violence in Gujarat . f: Oscar Guardiola-Rivera t eaches philosophy, human rights, and global affairs at Birkbeck College, University of London. b: Oscar Pujol has published several books and translations from Sanskrit, among them The Wisdom of the Forest: Translations from the Upani á¹£ads ; Hymn to the Earth from the Atharvaveda ; The BhagavadgÄ«tÄ ; The…
f: Oscar Pujol has published several books and translations from Sanskrit, among them The Wisdom of the Forest: Translations from the Upani ṣads ; Hymn to the Earth from the Atharvaveda ; The Bhagavadgītā ; The Yogasūtra of Patañjali ; Rasa: Aesthetic Pleasure in Indian Aesthetic ; and two monographs - one on Śa ṃkara and another on Patañjali . He has also published the Sanskrit-Catalan Dictionary and the Sanskrit-Spanish Dictionary . He played a key role in establishing Casa Asia (Barcelona) as the Director of Educational Programmes, introducing the teaching of Asian languages, promoting the creation of Asian degrees at Spanish Universities, and fostering Indo-Spanish relations. In 2007, he founded the Instituto Cervantes of New Delhi. He has also directed the Instituto Cervantes of Porto Alegre, Rio de Janeiro, and Fez. Currently, he serves again as the Director of the Instituto Cervantes of New Delhi.

f: P. Sainath is founder editor of the People’s Archive of Rural India (PARI) and a rural reporter who has covered the Indian countryside with passion and conscience. He is the author of Everybody Loves a Good Drought: Stories From India’s Poorest Districts , an enduring and classic text of rural reportage.

b: Padma Kaimal is the Batza Family Chair in Art History at Colgate University in New York. Her research questions common assumptions about art from the Tamil region. Did kings build the only architecture that matters? Did…
f: Padma Kaimal is the Batza Family Chair in Art History at Colgate University in New York. Her research questions common assumptions about art from the Tamil region. Did kings build the only architecture that matters? Did men? Are the boundaries of India’s modern states meaningful for understanding beautiful temples of the past? How do narrative sculptures tell their stories? Are fierce goddesses demonic? Are museums the problem, the solution, or both to contentions over cultural property? Kaimal is the author of Opening Kailasanatha: The Temple in Kanchipuram Revealed in Time and Space and Scattered Goddesses: Travels with the Yoginis.

b: Padmini Ray Murray has a PhD from the University of Edinburgh, and is a Research Consultant at the Art X Company. She founded Design Beku in 2018, a collective that works towards making design and technology local,…
f: Padmini Ray Murray has a PhD from the University of Edinburgh, and is a Research Consultant at the Art X Company. She founded Design Beku in 2018, a collective that works towards making design and technology local, decolonial and ethical. While in the UK, Padmini (along with Peggy Hughes and Claire Stewart) founded and ran The Electric Bookshop, a very successful quarterly event hosted by New Media Scotland (2010-2014). She was a lead researcher for the Consortium for Research into the Arts, and Technology in Scotland, funded by NESTA UK. Padmini joined the Srishti Institute of Art, Design and Technology in 2015, where she established the first Master’s programme in Digital Humanities in India.

b: Dr Palanivel Thiaga Rajan serves as the Minister for Information Techno;ogy & Digital Services, Earlier he served as the Minister for Finance & Human Resources Management in the Government of Tamil Nadu, India. During…

f: Pallavi Aiyar is a foreign correspondent, columnist, and author with a reporting career spanning more than two decades across China, Belgium, Japan, Indonesia, Spain, and beyond. Pallavi writes a weekly Substack newsletter on global travel and culture titled The Global Jigsaw. His upcoming title is Love Curry .

f: Pankaj Sekhsaria is the author of four books on the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. f: Paola Antonelli is Senior Curator at The Museum of Modern Art (MoMA) in the Department of Architecture & Design as well as MoMA’s founding Director of Research & Development. b: Parag Khanna is a leading global strategy advisor, world traveller and best-selling author. He is Founder & Managing Partner of FutureMap, a data and scenario based strategic advisory firm. Khanna’s newest book is The…
f: Parag Khanna is a leading global strategy advisor, world traveller and best-selling author. He is Founder & Managing Partner of FutureMap, a data and scenario based strategic advisory firm. Khanna’s newest book is The Future is Asian: Commerce, Conflict & Culture in the 21st Century . He is author of a trilogy of books on the future of world order beginning with The Second World: Empires and Influence in the New Global Order followed by How to Run the World: Charting a Course to the Next Renaissance and Connectography: Mapping the Future of Global Civilisation .He is also the author of Technocracy in America: Rise of the Info-State and co-author of Hybrid Reality: Thriving in the Emerging Human-Technology Civilisation . He was named one of Esquire ’s 75 Most Influential People of the 21st Century and featured in WIRED magazine’s Smart List. He holds a P.D. from the London School of Economics and Bachelors and Masters degrees from the School of Foreign Service at Georgetown University. He has travelled to nearly 150 countries and is a Young Global Leader of the World Economic Forum.

f: Parakala Prabhakar studied at JNU and the London School of Economics. He was the Communications Adviser to the Government of Andhra Pradesh between 2014 and 2018 and held a Cabinet rank. His latest book is The Crooked Timber of New India: Essays on a Republic in Crisis (Speaking Tiger).

b: Paramswaran Iyer is currently the Global Lead for Strategic Initiatives in the World Bank’s Water Global Practice. Prior to this, he served as Secretary to the Government of India at the Department of Drinking Water…
f: Paramswaran Iyer is currently the Global Lead for Strategic Initiatives in the World Bank’s Water Global Practice. Prior to this, he served as Secretary to the Government of India at the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation from March 2016 until August 2020 where he led the implementation of the flagship Swachh Bharat Mission. A former IAS officer, Iyer headed the innovative community-led Swajal Project in Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand in the 1990s, has over 25 years of global experience in the water and sanitation sector and has worked in many countries, including Vietnam, China, Egypt and Lebanon.

f: Pardis Mahdavi is the President of the University of La Verne. f: Pariksith Singh , MD, is board certified in Internal Medicine. His poetry, stories, literary critiques, and his many translations (from Hindi, Sanskrit, Persian, and Urdu) carry a strikingly original and creative interplay of form and content, technique and narrative, style and substance.

f: Partha Mitter is an Emeritus Professor of Art History at the University of Sussex, the UK and Research Adjunct Professor, Carleton University, Canada.
