f: Ramachandra Guha is a historian and biographer based in Bengaluru. He has taught at the universities of Yale and Stanford, held the Arné Naess Chair at the University of Oslo and served as the Philippe Roman Professor of History and International Affairs at the London School of Economics and as the Satish Dhawan Visiting Professor at the Indian Institute of Science. Guha’s books include a pioneering environmental history, The Unquiet Woods and an award-winning social history of cricket, A Corner of a Foreign Field, which was chosen by the Guardian as one of the ten best books on cricket ever written. India after Gandhi was chosen as a book of the year by The Economist, the Washington Post, Wall Street Journal, the San Francisco Chronicle, Time Out and Outlook, and as a book of the decade in the Times of India, the Times of London and The Hindu. Guha’s most recent book is a two-volume biography of Mahatma Gandhi. The first volume, Gandhi Before India, was chosen as a notable book of the year by The New York Times and the San Francisco Chronicle. The second volume, Gandhi: The Years That Changed the World, was chosen as a notable book of the year by The New York Times and The Economist . Guha’s books and essays have been translated into more than 20 languages. The New York Times has referred to him as ‘perhaps the best among India’s non fiction writers’ while TIME has called him ‘Indian democracy’s pre-eminent chronicler’. Guha’s awards include the Leopold-Hidy Prize of the American Society of Environmental History, the Daily Telegraph/Cricket Society prize, the Malcolm Adideshiah Award for excellence in social science research, the Ramnath Goenka Prize for excellence in journalism, the Sahitya Akademi Award and the R. b: Ramesh Paliwal is Founding Member and Secretary of TAABAR, an NGO that supports street children and trafficked children. He has worked for I-India and Population of Services International. During this period, he lived…
f: Ramesh Paliwal is Founding Member and Secretary of TAABAR, an NGO that supports street children and trafficked children. He has worked for I-India and Population of Services International. His book Mi, Manu ani Sangh has been translated into Hindi and other regional languages. Patange is recipient of various awards, including the Tilak Samarasta Purskar, the 2017 Lokmany Tilak Lifetime Achievement Award for Journalism and the Manikchand Vajpayee National Award of Journalism.

b: Ramesh Sharma is an award-winning feature film and documentary producer and director. He is the recipient of six National Awards for his work and numerous international accolades, including the Caviliere dell’Ordiine…
f: Ramesh Sharma is an award-winning feature film and documentary producer and director. He is the recipient of six National Awards for his work and numerous international accolades, including the Caviliere dell’Ordiine della Stella Della Solidarieta’ Italiana and the Opera Prima at the Karlovy Vary International Film Festival for his feature film New Delhi Times. His documentary, The Journalist and The Jihadi: The Murder of Daniel Pearl, was nominated for two Emmy awards in and won the National Award in India. To commemorate 150 years of Gandhi’s birth anniversary, Sharma produced and directed a 103 minute feature documentary titled Ahimsa: Gandhi: The Power of the Powerless , which was awarded the Global Peace Award.

b: ‘Becoming the Storm’ marks Rami Chhabra ’s debut into the world of fiction at age 87. But she is a well-known media-personality and social-activist. Her life and work represent sustained commitment to women and social…
f: ‘Becoming the Storm’ marks Rami Chhabra ’s debut into the world of fiction at age 87. But she is a well-known media-personality and social-activist. Her life and work represent sustained commitment to women and social development issues, addressed through multiple roles over a near-seven-decades career that has spanned media, administration, international consultancies, public advocacy and social activism. Pioneer woman-journalist/TV-personality, Rami Chhabra carved column-space in national newspapers (1960-1980) initiating early attention to gender-equality issues; her edit-page column: ‘Feminist Viewpoint’ (Indian Express, 1977–80) broke political ground for women’s issues.

b: Ramie Targoff’s scholarly area of interest is the English Renaissance with a strong secondary interest in the Italian Renaissance. An award-winning writer, she is the author of three books on Renaissance English…
f: Ramie Targoff’s scholarly area of interest is the English Renaissance with a strong secondary interest in the Italian Renaissance. An award-winning writer, she is the author of three books on Renaissance English literature titled Common Prayer: The Language of Public Devotion, John Donne, Body and Soul and Posthumous Love: Eros and the Afterlife in Renaissance England . Most recently, she has written a biography of the 16th century Italian poet Vittoria Colonna titled Renaissance Woman: The Life of Vittoria Colonna and has completed the first English translation of Colonna’s 1538 book of sonnets, entitled Sonnets of Widowhood . Her forthcoming book, Shakespeare’s Sisters , is a group biography of four women writers in Renaissance England: Mary Sidney Herbert, Aemilia Lanyer, Elizabeth Cary and Anne Clifford.

f: Rana Ayyub is a prominent Indian investigative journalist and the Global Opinions Writer at the Washington Post. She has a Masters' degree in Cultural and Creative Industries from King’s College London and is the recipient of the ARThink South Asia Fellowship (2011-12), a participant fellow at ‘The Academy—a program of Carnegie Hall, The Juilliard School and the Weill Music Institute’ and a 2017 Global Fellow of the International Society for Performing Arts (ISPA), New York. Dhanwani has also founded Arts Culture Resources India, a network and platform for cultural professionals in India and South Asia.

b: Rashmi Dickinson is a campaigning author. She is a cardiologist by training and an ex UK senior civil servant. From a family of freedom fighters, she now devotes her life to improving the quality of life of people in…
f: Rashmi Dickinson is a campaigning author. She is a cardiologist by training and an ex UK senior civil servant. From a family of freedom fighters, she now devotes her life to improving the quality of life of people in Amber. As an eco activist, she has published previously on climate change in Saving our Planet: The First Steps . She created Amber Eco Trail, where she teaches children about environmental conservation. While writing Secrets of Amber, she realised that responsible and sustainable tourism is the way forward for uplifting this impoverished heritage town. All royalties go to the development of Amber.

b: Rashmi Narzary is an independent editor and writer. She received the Sahitya Akademi Award for Children’s Literature, English and multiple accolades in 2025, including the FICCI Book of the Year and Delhi Literature…
f: Rashmi Narzary is an independent editor and writer. She received the Sahitya Akademi Award for Children’s Literature, English and multiple accolades in 2025, including the FICCI Book of the Year and Delhi Literature Festival Award for Whistles of the Siphoong: Tales from Assam’s Bodo Heartland . Her debut novel, Bloodstone: Legend of the Last Engraving , was followed by An Unfinished Search and The Lost Soul of the Joukhoorei , a YA novel praised by Gulzar. She was also honored with the Prag Prerona Award for Literature in 2020,

b: Rashmi Uday Singh was recently conferred a prestigious knighthood from the French Government, Chevalier ordre des Art et des Lettres, and is a Gourmand World Cookbook Award-winner. Singh has been synonymous with good…
f: Rashmi Uday Singh was recently conferred a prestigious knighthood from the French Government, Chevalier ordre des Art et des Lettres, and is a Gourmand World Cookbook Award-winner. Singh has been synonymous with good food and health for the past two decades. She is an author of 39 books and is a regular columnist with The Times of India, Bombay Times and Chennai Times . She also writes regularly for many national and international magazines. It is for her extraordinarily popular Good Food Guide that she is most celebrated (India's first-ever city-restaurant guide). This handy, first-of-its-kind, insider's guide to good food established Singh as the nation's most clued-in commentator on all things edible. She also runs the highly esteemed 'Rashmi Uday Singh's Good Food Academy ' .

b: Rashna Imhasly-Gandhy is a Jungian analyst and transpersonal psychologist whose work bridges Eastern wisdom and Western depth psychology. Married to a Swiss national, she lives and practices between India and…
f: Rashna Imhasly-Gandhy is a Jungian analyst and transpersonal psychologist whose work bridges Eastern wisdom and Western depth psychology. Married to a Swiss national, she lives and practices between India and Switzerland, inspiring therapists and seekers to explore individuation and awaken the authentic Self. An accomplished author, her writings integrate Indian mythology with Jungian thought. Her works include Eros Versus Kama—The Psychology of Love: Wisdom of Indian Mythology (new edition), Sita Rising: Discovering the Heroine Within (new edition), and her latest book, The Courage to Be You: Love, Identity, and Healing in a Changing India .

b: Rati Saxena is a poet, translator, editor, traveller and academic scholar. She has five collections of poetry in Hindi and six in English (translated). Saxena has translated twenty books, three travelogues, a memoir,…
f: Rati Saxena is a poet, translator, editor, traveller and academic scholar. She has five collections of poetry in Hindi and six in English (translated). Saxena has translated twenty books, three travelogues, a memoir, one critical study and two research-oriented books. Her work has been translated into eight international languages. She is the editor of the first bilingual poetry web journal, and founder and festival director of the Kritya International Poetry Festival.

b: Ravi Agrawal is the managing editor of Foreign Policy magazine and the author of India Connected: How the Smartphone Is Transforming the World’s Largest Democracy . Before joining FP , Agrawal worked at CNN for more…
f: Ravi Agrawal is the managing editor of Foreign Policy magazine and the author of India Connected: How the Smartphone Is Transforming the World’s Largest Democracy . Before joining FP , Agrawal worked at CNN for more than a decade in London, New York and New Delhi, where he served as the network’s India bureau chief and correspondent.

b: Ravi Deecee is the Publisher, CEO and Managing Director of DC Books, one of India’s leading publishing houses and a top publisher in Kerala and Malayalam literature. He also heads Current Books, the largest retail…
f: Ravi Deecee is the Publisher, CEO and Managing Director of DC Books, one of India’s leading publishing houses and a top publisher in Kerala and Malayalam literature. He also heads Current Books, the largest retail bookshop chain in South India, and serves as Secretary of the DC Kizhakemuri Foundation. Under his leadership, DC Books has grown internationally and championed translations and literary culture. Deecee co-founded and facilitates the Kerala Literature Festival, now among the world’s largest literary events. In 2025, he was honoured with the French civilian award Chevalier de l’Ordre des Arts et des Lettres for his contribution to literature and cultural exchange.

b: Ravi Dharamshi , Founder and CIO of ValueQuest Investment Advisors, leads a premier alternate investment firm, managing over Rs. 22,000 crores. Known for its exceptional performance, ValueQuest, operates across six…
f: Ravi Dharamshi , Founder and CIO of ValueQuest Investment Advisors, leads a premier alternate investment firm, managing over Rs. 22,000 crores. Known for its exceptional performance, ValueQuest, operates across six Indian cities and Dubai, offers diverse investment products, including AIFs, PMS, and an offshore fund in GIFT City.

b: Ravi Mantri was born in Andhra Pradesh, South India. He pursued a Master’s degree from the College of Engineering, JNTU, before moving to Ireland for work. As a techie by profession, Ravi embarked on his literary…
f: Ravi Mantri was born in Andhra Pradesh, South India. He pursued a Master’s degree from the College of Engineering, JNTU, before moving to Ireland for work. As a techie by profession, Ravi embarked on his literary journey in 2019 with his debut novel, Amma Dairylo Konni Pageelu . The novel became a best-seller and won the hearts of many readers. In addition to novels, Ravi has penned several short stories that have been published in renowned Telugu magazines.

b: Ravi Purohit is a reputed literary icon, continually treading corridors of Rajasthani and Hindi literature. An innovative writer on issues of social concern, he has garnered recognition as a translator, editor and…
f: Ravi Purohit is a reputed literary icon, continually treading corridors of Rajasthani and Hindi literature. An innovative writer on issues of social concern, he has garnered recognition as a translator, editor and critic. He has received awards from the Sahitya Akademi and the Hindi-Rajasthani Akademi, among others.

f: Ravi Shankar Etteth is a journalist, political cartoonist, graphic designer and author who has edited magazines and newspapers and worked in television. He has been the editorial cartoonist of the

b: Ravi Singh is publisher and co-founder of Speaking Tiger Books, one of India’s most distinctive independent publishing companies. He was also publisher and editor-in-chief with Penguin Books India and co-publisher with…
f: Ravi Singh is publisher and co-founder of Speaking Tiger Books, one of India’s most distinctive independent publishing companies. He was also publisher and editor-in-chief with Penguin Books India and co-publisher with Aleph Book Company. Over three decades, he has worked closely with many of the finest authors writing from or about South Asia.

b: Ravi Subramanian , India’s bestselling thriller writer, has spent two decades working his way up the ladder of power in the amazingly exciting and adrenaline-pumping world of global banks in India. It is but natural…
f: Ravi Subramanian , India’s bestselling thriller writer, has spent two decades working his way up the ladder of power in the amazingly exciting and adrenaline-pumping world of global banks in India. It is but natural that his works reflect all that he has seen and experienced. Four of Ravi’s eight titles have been award winners.

b: Ravi Venkatesan is a business leader, author and social entrepreneur who is currently UNICEF’s Special Representative for Young People and Innovation. He is the founder of the Global Alliance for Mass Entrepreneurship…
f: Ravi Venkatesan is a business leader, author and social entrepreneur who is currently UNICEF’s Special Representative for Young People and Innovation. He is the founder of the Global Alliance for Mass Entrepreneurship and serves on the boards of Hitachi Ltd and Rockefeller Foundation. Ravi was the chairman of Microsoft India, Bank of Baroda and Cummins India and is the author of Conquering the Chaos: Win in India, Win Everywhere .

b: Ravina Aggarwal is an anthropologist who has written extensively about the Himalayas. She was a professor at Smith College and worked for the Ford Foundation before assuming the leadership of Columbia University's…
f: Ravina Aggarwal is an anthropologist who has written extensively about the Himalayas. She was a professor at Smith College and worked for the Ford Foundation before assuming the leadership of Columbia University's Global Center in India. Her publications include Beyond Lines of Control: Performing the Border in Ladakh, India, Into the High Ranges: The Penguin Book of Mountain Writing, Forsaking Paradise, and the novel, Searching for the Songbird.

b: Born in Kenya, to Indian parents, Ravinder Bhogal’s food is inspired by her mixed heritage and the UK’s diverse immigrant culture. Bhogal is a journalist, chef and restaurateur. Her debut restaurant, Jikoni, was…
f: Born in Kenya, to Indian parents, Ravinder Bhogal’s food is inspired by her mixed heritage and the UK’s diverse immigrant culture. Bhogal is a journalist, chef and restaurateur. Her debut restaurant, Jikoni, was ranked 56th in the UK by the National Restaurant Awards within 7 months of opening, and she has penned two books, Cook in Boots and Jikoni: Proudly Inauthentic Recipes from an Immigrant Kitchen , which was released in July this year. She has twice been named in the Evening Standard Progress 1000 as one of London’s leading influencers of progress and diversity in the capital. She also launched a home delivery brand Comfort and Joy, a sister brand to Jikoni in June this year. She is a monthly food columnist for the FT Weekend Magazine.

b: Ravinder Reddy is an internationally renowned Indian sculptor whose monumental works feature in major museums and distinguished private collections across India, Southeast Asia, Europe, the UAE, and the USA. His…
f: Ravinder Reddy is an internationally renowned Indian sculptor whose monumental works feature in major museums and distinguished private collections across India, Southeast Asia, Europe, the UAE, and the USA. His sculptures have been showcased in leading curated exhibitions and international biennales, earning global acclaim. Reddy’s practice reimagines India’s vernacular sculptural traditions through a contemporary lens, marked by bold scale, radiant colour, and distinctive surface treatment. His commanding forms possess a striking vitality and presence, merging cultural memory with modern expression. The luminosity, material strength, and inventive handling of form make his work instantly recognizable and set it apart within contemporary global sculpture.

b: Ravinder Singh is a well-known bestselling author, considered the ‘King of Romance’. An alumnus of Indian School of Business and an ex Senior Programme Manager at Microsoft, Singh once felt it's more fun writing…
f: Ravinder Singh is a well-known bestselling author, considered the ‘King of Romance’. An alumnus of Indian School of Business and an ex Senior Programme Manager at Microsoft, Singh once felt it's more fun writing stories than software programmes. Now a full time storyteller, he has sold more than 3.5 million copies of his novels. He also runs the publishing venture Black Ink, where he publishes debut authors.

b: Ravindra Rathee started his career as a journalist with the Times of India i n Delhi, writing on human rights and conflict resolution. After graduating from St Stephen’s College in Delhi, he did an MA in politics at…
f: Ravindra Rathee started his career as a journalist with the Times of India i n Delhi, writing on human rights and conflict resolution. After graduating from St Stephen’s College in Delhi, he did an MA in politics at the University of Hull as a British Chevening Scholar. For the past two decades, he has worked as a banker. True to Their Salt: The British Indian Army and an Alternative History of Decolonization is his first book, stemming from extensive research on the military life of his grandfather.

b: Ravish Kumar is an Indian journalist, author and media personality. He is the author of two published works, The Free Voice in English and Ishq Mein Sheher Hona in Hindi. The Free Voice has been translated into Hindi,…
f: Ravish Kumar is an Indian journalist, author and media personality. He is the author of two published works, The Free Voice in English and Ishq Mein Sheher Hona in Hindi. The Free Voice has been translated into Hindi, Marathi, Kannada and Nepali. Kumar was recently awarded the Ramon Magsaysay Award for 'giving voice to the voiceless'.

b: Rebecca Wragg Sykes is a prehistorian, an Honorary Fellow at the University of Liverpool, and a writer. She is the author of one of the 2021 New York Times list of 100 Notable Books, Kindred: Neanderthal Life, Love,…
f: Rebecca Wragg Sykes is a prehistorian, an Honorary Fellow at the University of Liverpool, and a writer. She is the author of one of the 2021 New York Times list of 100 Notable Books, Kindred: Neanderthal Life, Love, Death and Art- winner of the 2021's PEN Hessell-Tiltman prize.

b: Redmond O’Hanlon is known for his journeys into some of the most remote jungles of the world, in Borneo, the Amazon basin and Congo. He has also written a harrowing account of a trip to the North Atlantic on a…
f: Redmond O’Hanlon is known for his journeys into some of the most remote jungles of the world, in Borneo, the Amazon basin and Congo. He has also written a harrowing account of a trip to the North Atlantic on a trawler. Between September 2009 and May 2010, O’Hanlon was a guest and co-presenter on the programme Beagle: In Darwin’s Wake where re-traced the route that Charles Darwin took aboard HMS Beagle (1831–36), a journey that played a seminal role in his thinking on evolution. He also presented O’Hanlon’s Heroes , in which he introduces the viewer to his heroes of the 19th century. The programme was awarded with the prestigious Dutch television award, De Zilveren Nipkowschijf. He is the author of the books Joseph Conrad and Charles Darwin: The Influence of Scientific Thought on Conrad’s Fiction, Into the Heart of Borneo, In Trouble Again: A Journey Between the Orinoco and the Amazon, Congo Journey, Trawler , with Rudy Rotthier, God and Darwin en natuur ( The Fetish Room ).

b: Reena Lath is Director, Akar Prakar, with two art galleries in Kolkata and New Delhi, which showcase art by Indian modern and contemporary artists. As a director of Akar Prakar, she has hosted several exhibitions of art…
f: Reena Lath is Director, Akar Prakar, with two art galleries in Kolkata and New Delhi, which showcase art by Indian modern and contemporary artists. As a director of Akar Prakar, she has hosted several exhibitions of art nationally and internationally, collaborating with important museums, institutions and galleries. She has also spearheaded several publications/books on Indian artists, which includes Somnath Hore: Wounds with art1st.

b: Reena Menaria , a prolific author of Hindi and Rajasthani books serves as Research Assistant at JRN Rajasthan Vidyapeeth University. She excels in Rajasthani literature, with broadcasts on Jaipur Doordarshan Kendra and…
f: Reena Menaria , a prolific author of Hindi and Rajasthani books serves as Research Assistant at JRN Rajasthan Vidyapeeth University. She excels in Rajasthani literature, with broadcasts on Jaipur Doordarshan Kendra and All India Radio for two decades. An accomplished speaker at the Jaipur Literature Festival, she has received numerous awards, including Premji Prem Yuva Puraskar and All India Sahitya Samman.

b: Reena Saini Kallat's work is widely exhibited at major international institutions, including the Museum of Modern Art in New York, Migros Museum of Contemporary Art in Zurich and Mori Art Museum in Tokyo. Her recent…
f: Reena Saini Kallat's work is widely exhibited at major international institutions, including the Museum of Modern Art in New York, Migros Museum of Contemporary Art in Zurich and Mori Art Museum in Tokyo. Her recent solo exhibitions include the Manchester Museum (2017) and an ongoing solo show at the National Museum of Asian Arts – Guimet in Paris (2020).

b: Dr. Rekha Bhatnagar is a postgraduate in Painting from Udaipur University and former Head of the Department of Art at Kanoria College, Jaipur. She is also an active contemporary artist. She completed her doctoral thesis…
f: Dr. Rekha Bhatnagar is a postgraduate in Painting from Udaipur University and former Head of the Department of Art at Kanoria College, Jaipur. She is also an active contemporary artist. She completed her doctoral thesis on the folk art of the Udaipur region and has authored two books: Dhulichitra and Gobar Dhan .

b: Rekha Sethi is a Professor, Vice-Principal and the coordinator of the Translation and Translation Studies Centre at Indraprastha College for Women, University of Delhi. She has authored five books, edited eight, and…
f: Rekha Sethi is a Professor, Vice-Principal and the coordinator of the Translation and Translation Studies Centre at Indraprastha College for Women, University of Delhi. She has authored five books, edited eight, and translated a poetry collection from English to Hindi. She has also published extensively in leading literary journals and presented her work at international and national fora.

b: Remo Fernandes is an Indian singer and musician from Goa whose work is a fusion of many different cultures and styles that he was exposed to in his lifetime. Writing and singing songs in English made his success more…
f: Remo Fernandes is an Indian singer and musician from Goa whose work is a fusion of many different cultures and styles that he was exposed to in his lifetime. Writing and singing songs in English made his success more distinctive in the context of the Bollywood dominated, Hindi language based music scene that was popular in the 80s and 90s. Remo recently composed and recorded a full-fledged opera on Mother Teresa.

b: Renata Dessallien has served the United Nations for 35 years in Africa and Asia in many capacities, including 15 years as a UN Resident Coordinator, Humanitarian Coordinator, and UNDP Resident Representative. Before…
f: Renata Dessallien has served the United Nations for 35 years in Africa and Asia in many capacities, including 15 years as a UN Resident Coordinator, Humanitarian Coordinator, and UNDP Resident Representative. Before taking up her assignment as UN Resident Coordinator in India, she was a senior fellow at the Oslo Governance Centre at UNDP in Norway. Prior to that she was UN Resident/Humanitarian Coordinator and UNDP Resident Representative in Bhutan, Bangladesh, China and Myanmar between 2002 and 2017. She also served in various capacities with the UN in Mali, Laos and in New York, making important contributions in the field of good governance and poverty reduction. She holds a Master of Public Administration from Harvard University, a Master of Arts from Columbia University, and a Bachelor of Music from the University of Ottawa.

b: Renata Lok-Dessallien has served the United Nations for 30 years in Africa and Asia in many capacities, including 15 years as a UN Resident Coordinator, Humanitarian Coordinator and UNDP Resident Representative. Before…
f: Renata Lok-Dessallien has served the United Nations for 30 years in Africa and Asia in many capacities, including 15 years as a UN Resident Coordinator, Humanitarian Coordinator and UNDP Resident Representative. Before taking up her assignment in India, she was a senior fellow at the Oslo Governance Centre at UNDP in Norway. She was UN Resident/Humanitarian Coordinator and UNDP Resident Representative in Bhutan, Bangladesh, China and Myanmar between 2002 and 2017, where she worked to strengthen to UN system and improve coordination among agencies. Prior to that she served in various capacities in Mali, Laos and at UN HQ, making important contributions in the field of poverty reduction.

b: Rene Singh is a singer trained in semi-classical music. She has a vast knowledge of Sufi and Urdu poetry, which has led her to delve into its history and musically present the lives of various poets to the people across…
f: Rene Singh is a singer trained in semi-classical music. She has a vast knowledge of Sufi and Urdu poetry, which has led her to delve into its history and musically present the lives of various poets to the people across the globe. Singh curates and designs modules and workshops through poetry and music. Her work is based on her vast travels and interactions with different communities and music across the country, including conflict zones. She has partnered with UNICEF to create musical stories for community radio in the remote villages of the country and has earned great appreciation for her work in Kashmir with orphan girls affected by terrorism. She is the founding member of HUM: Hamari Urdu Mohabbat, which has become a leading group for performing this form of poetry and singing.

b: Renee Singh is a poet weaving the mystique of life in words that resound with love and a passion for life in its purest form. There is a divine theme underlying her poems and a Sufi flavour that transcends the realms of…
f: Renee Singh is a poet weaving the mystique of life in words that resound with love and a passion for life in its purest form. There is a divine theme underlying her poems and a Sufi flavour that transcends the realms of inner and outer consciousness. Singh is also a columnist, writer, metaphysicist, practicing psychotherapist, an acclaimed speaker, entrepreneur, stress management consultant and a TV show presenter. Her main work lies in maximising human potential.

b: Reni Eddo-Lodge is an award-winning journalist. Why I’m No Longer Talking to White People about Race is her first book. It was longlisted for the Baillie Gifford Prize and the Orwell Prize. It won the Jhalak Prize and…
f: Reni Eddo-Lodge is an award-winning journalist. Why I’m No Longer Talking to White People about Race is her first book. It was longlisted for the Baillie Gifford Prize and the Orwell Prize. It won the Jhalak Prize and Non-Fiction Narrative Book of the Year at the British Book Awards.

b: Renu Roy is a well-known personality in the field of the performing, visual and fine arts and has been founder-director of Spandan, a reputed cultural foundation in Kolkata, and Spandan Films, a cinematic initiative…
f: Renu Roy is a well-known personality in the field of the performing, visual and fine arts and has been founder-director of Spandan, a reputed cultural foundation in Kolkata, and Spandan Films, a cinematic initiative with the celebrated. Renu also spearheaded her own theatre group as an acclaimed actor, script writer, producer and director. She is a recipient of several important theatre and cultural awards that include the Bharat Nirman, and a National Film Festival Award for ‘Best Feature Film’ (for Unishe April ), directed by the late Rituparno Ghosh. ‘The Far Side and Other Poems’ is her third volume of poems.

b: Renuka Chatterjee started out as a journalist with the Times of India in the late ‘80s, and helped launch The Saturday Times, the country’s first colour weekend supplement. She switched tracks to enter publishing in…
f: Renuka Chatterjee started out as a journalist with the Times of India in the late ‘80s, and helped launch The Saturday Times, the country’s first colour weekend supplement. She switched tracks to enter publishing in 1992 as Associate Editor with Penguin Books, and publishing has been her home ever since. After Penguin, she has been editor-in-chief of HarperCollins India and subsequently, Roli Books and Westland Ltd. She is currently Vice-President, Publishing, with Speaking Tiger Publishing, an independent publishing house with a focus on quality fiction and non-fiction.

b: Reshma Qureshi is an acid attack survivor and the face of Make Love Not Scars (MLNS(. She was attacked with acid at the age of 17 yet went on to create history by becoming the first acid attack survivor to walk the New…
f: Reshma Qureshi is an acid attack survivor and the face of Make Love Not Scars (MLNS(. She was attacked with acid at the age of 17 yet went on to create history by becoming the first acid attack survivor to walk the New York Fashion Week. She is an activist, model and vlogger. She was the face of the #EndAcidSale campaign. Her videos for the campaign went on to garner over 2 million views overnight and received 350,000 signatures on a petition addressed to the Prime Minister of India, demanding an end to over-the-counter sale of acid. She is the co-author of Being Reshma , a powerful first hand account of her inspiring journey.

b: Reshma Ruia is a British Indian writer. Her first novel, Something Black in the Lentil Soup, was described in the Sunday Times as ‘a gem of straight-faced comedy’. She has published a poetry collection, A Dinner…
f: Reshma Ruia is a British Indian writer. Her first novel, Something Black in the Lentil Soup, was described in the Sunday Times as ‘a gem of straight-faced comedy’. She has published a poetry collection, A Dinner Party in the Home Counties , winner of the 2019 Word Masala Award and a short story collection, Mrs Pinto Drives to Happiness , shortlisted for the 2022 Eastern Eye ACTA Awards. Her new novel, Still Lives was awarded the 2023 Diverse Books Readers’ Choice Award and selected for the 2023 Peoples Book Prize. Reshma is also the co-founder of The Whole Kahani – a writers’ collective of British South Asian writers.

b: Reshmi Chakraborty is the co-founder and chief editor of Silver Talkies, a social impact platform for healthy and active ageing. She has worked as a journalist for over 20 years and continues to write for various…
f: Reshmi Chakraborty is the co-founder and chief editor of Silver Talkies, a social impact platform for healthy and active ageing. She has worked as a journalist for over 20 years and continues to write for various national and international publications. Rethink Ageing is her first book.

b: Revati Laul is an independent journalist, filmmaker and author of The Anatomy of Hate , an account of the perpetrators of the 2002 Gujarat violence. She started out reporting for NDTV and has more recently written for…
f: Revati Laul is an independent journalist, filmmaker and author of The Anatomy of Hate , an account of the perpetrators of the 2002 Gujarat violence. She started out reporting for NDTV and has more recently written for Tehelka , Hindustan Times and a weekly column called `Civil Disobedience’ for Quint .

b: Rheea Mukherjee is the author of The Body Myth and was shortlisted for the TATA Literature Live First Book Award 2019. Her work has been featured in the Los Angeles Times, Buzzfeed, Scroll.in, Electric Literature, Out…
f: Rheea Mukherjee is the author of The Body Myth and was shortlisted for the TATA Literature Live First Book Award 2019. Her work has been featured in the Los Angeles Times, Buzzfeed, Scroll.in, Electric Literature, Out of Print Magazine and Southern Humanities Review , among others. She co-founded Bangalore Writers Workshop in 2012 and currently co-runs Write Leela Write, a Design and Content Laboratory in Bangalore.

b: Rhiannon Jenkins Tsang is a British writer whose work focuses on historical fault lines. Her latest novel, The Last Vicereine , was published in 2017. The Tamil language edition is due in January 2019. Her debut novel,…
f: Rhiannon Jenkins Tsang is a British writer whose work focuses on historical fault lines. Her latest novel, The Last Vicereine , was published in 2017. The Tamil language edition is due in January 2019. Her debut novel, The Woman Who Lost China , was published in 2013. Jenkins Tsang is the Nottingham Writers’ Studio Novelist of the Year 2018.

b: Ria Chopra writes about the internet, pop culture, and India’s young people. Her essays have been published by Vogue, VICE, The Hindu, Indian Express, Refinery29, Insider etc. Her portfolio career and innumerable side…
f: Ria Chopra writes about the internet, pop culture, and India’s young people. Her essays have been published by Vogue, VICE, The Hindu, Indian Express, Refinery29, Insider etc. Her portfolio career and innumerable side quests have taken her from the Google HQ in Mountainview, California, to the University of Michigan, Ann Arbor, to the hotseat of Kaun Banega Crorepati. Never Logged Out is her first book.

b: Ria Sharma is a social activist and the founder of Make Love Not Scars, an NGO that works in all aspects of rehabilitation for acid attack survivors. Sharma is the first Indian to receive a UN award for sustainable…
f: Ria Sharma is a social activist and the founder of Make Love Not Scars, an NGO that works in all aspects of rehabilitation for acid attack survivors. Sharma is the first Indian to receive a UN award for sustainable development amongst other prestigious recognition. Her memoir will be released at the ZEE Jaipur Literature Festival in 2019.

b: Richa Jha is a children’s author and the founder of Pickle Yolk Books, an independent children's publishing house, shortlisted for the 2022 BOP at Bologna. Books written and published by her, all of which delve into the…
f: Richa Jha is a children’s author and the founder of Pickle Yolk Books, an independent children's publishing house, shortlisted for the 2022 BOP at Bologna. Books written and published by her, all of which delve into the internal world of children and adults, have won both national and international recognition. She is a passionate advocate for picture books being a wholesome read for all ages.

b: Richard Blurton trained as an archaeologist, excavating in North Africa, Afghanistan, and southern India. In 1986 he joined the British Museum working on the Indian collections, becoming Head of the South and Southeast…
f: Richard Blurton trained as an archaeologist, excavating in North Africa, Afghanistan, and southern India. In 1986 he joined the British Museum working on the Indian collections, becoming Head of the South and Southeast Asia section before retiring in 2018. He presented many exhibitions, including the British Museum/British Council 1997 exhibition, ‘The Enduring Image’ in India. His published books include Hindu Art and Krishna in the Garden of Assam .

b: Richard J. Evans is the author of The Coming of the Third Reich and many other books on Nazi Germany. His latest publication is a major biography of the world’s best-known historian titled Eric Hobsbawm: A Life in…
f: Richard J. Evans is the author of The Coming of the Third Reich and many other books on Nazi Germany. His latest publication is a major biography of the world’s best-known historian titled Eric Hobsbawm: A Life in History , forthcoming in February 2019. A former Regius Professor of History at Cambridge University, he was knighted for services to scholarship in 2012.

b: Richard Flanagan was born in Tasmania in 1961. His books have received numerous honours and are published in more than 40 languages. He won the Booker Prize for The Narrow Road to the Deep North in 2014 and the Baillie…
f: Richard Flanagan was born in Tasmania in 1961. His books have received numerous honours and are published in more than 40 languages. He won the Booker Prize for The Narrow Road to the Deep North in 2014 and the Baillie Gifford Prize for Non-Fiction for Question 7 in 2024.

b: Richard Horton is Editor in Chief of The Lancet and one of the world’s most influential voices in global health. Trained in physiology and medicine at the University of Birmingham, he joined The Lancet in 1990 and…
f: Richard Horton is Editor in Chief of The Lancet and one of the world’s most influential voices in global health. Trained in physiology and medicine at the University of Birmingham, he joined The Lancet in 1990 and became Editor in Chief in 1995. Horton has chaired and served on major international health bodies, including UN expert groups on health employment and women’s and children’s health. A recipient of numerous global honours, he champions the concept of planetary health. His books include The COVID-19 Catastrophe . He was awarded an OBE in 2023.

b: Richard M. Eaton has been obsessed with India ever since riding an elephant at the St. Louis Zoo at age three, especially its long-term relations with Persian culture, Islam and the Iranian plateau before the British…
f: Richard M. Eaton has been obsessed with India ever since riding an elephant at the St. Louis Zoo at age three, especially its long-term relations with Persian culture, Islam and the Iranian plateau before the British period. He teaches history at the University of Arizona.

b: Richard Osman is a London-based author, producer and television presenter. His first three novels, The Thursday Murder Club, The Man Who Died Twice and The Bullet That Missed were multi-million-copy record-breaking…
f: Richard Osman is a London-based author, producer and television presenter. His first three novels, The Thursday Murder Club, The Man Who Died Twice and The Bullet That Missed were multi-million-copy record-breaking bestsellers around the world. The Last Devil to Die is his fourth book .

b: Rick Stroud is a producer, director and writer. As well as Lonely Courage, he has written The Book of the Moon , The Phantom Army of Alamein and Kidnap in Crete . With Victor Gregg, he has co-authored R ifleman. A Front…
f: Rick Stroud is a producer, director and writer. As well as Lonely Courage, he has written The Book of the Moon , The Phantom Army of Alamein and Kidnap in Crete . With Victor Gregg, he has co-authored R ifleman. A Front Line Life, King’s Cross Kid and Soldier Spy . He is trustee of the London Library.

b: Rijul Kataria is the Co-Founder of Violet Gold Arc, and the Head of Research at The Yuva Ekta Foundation. An arts practitioner, public speaking trainer, and researcher, he is driven by the power of theatre and the…
f: Rijul Kataria is the Co-Founder of Violet Gold Arc, and the Head of Research at The Yuva Ekta Foundation. An arts practitioner, public speaking trainer, and researcher, he is driven by the power of theatre and the performing arts. He designs and implements arts-based programs for self-expression, confidence-building, and meaningful dialogue. His research explores the impact of Expressive Arts in marginalised spaces, including published work on the role of the arts in engaging Children in Conflict with Law. Passionate about innovative pedagogy, Rijul pushes creative boundaries in order to reimagine learning, advocate for equity, and harness the arts as a force for transformation and social change.

b: Rijula Das's debut novel, A Death in Shonagachhi , won the Tata Lit Live First Book Award and was longlisted for the JCB Prize in 2021. It is forthcoming as Small Deaths in USA and the world in June 2022 by Amazon…
f: Rijula Das's debut novel, A Death in Shonagachhi , won the Tata Lit Live First Book Award and was longlisted for the JCB Prize in 2021. It is forthcoming as Small Deaths in USA and the world in June 2022 by Amazon Crossing. Rijula is a recipient of the 2019 Michael King Writers Centre Residency in Auckland and the 2016 Dastaan Award for her short story, Notes From A Passing. Her short story, The Grave of The Heart Eater , was longlisted for the Commonwealth Short Story Prize in 2019.

b: Rita Chowdhury is an award-winning Assamese poet and writer. A former associate professor at Cotton University, Chowdhury is currently the director of the National Book Trust. An important voice in contemporary Assamese…
f: Rita Chowdhury is an award-winning Assamese poet and writer. A former associate professor at Cotton University, Chowdhury is currently the director of the National Book Trust. An important voice in contemporary Assamese literature, Chowdhury has written 15 novels that portray a vivid picture of her strife-torn state. Chinatown Days is one of her best-known works.

b: Rita Kothari , a multilingual scholar and translator whose work spans different disciplines, is Professor of English and Co-director of the Ashoka Centre for Translation at Ashoka University. Kothari has translated…
f: Rita Kothari , a multilingual scholar and translator whose work spans different disciplines, is Professor of English and Co-director of the Ashoka Centre for Translation at Ashoka University. Kothari has translated extensively from Gujarati and Sindhi into English and occasionally vice versa. She is a Vani Distinguished Translator and recipient of the Fulbright, Rockefeller fellowships and awards. Her book, Translating India: The Cultural Politics of English, was the first seminal study of translation. The edited volume, A Multilingual Nation , and the monographs, The Burden of Refuge and Uneasy Translations , are among her notable works. Kothari is currently working on a Hindi translation of Shah Abdul Latif's Sindhi Sufi poetry.

b: Rithvik Singh is the bestselling author of I Don’t Love You Anymore and Warmth . Known for his ability to instill hope through words, his Instagram handle (@wordsofrithvik) boasts over 570,000 followers, with…
f: Rithvik Singh is the bestselling author of I Don’t Love You Anymore and Warmth . Known for his ability to instill hope through words, his Instagram handle (@wordsofrithvik) boasts over 570,000 followers, with celebrities like Britney Spears and Huda Kattan sharing his work. Singh has spoken at institutions like IIT Mumbai and AIIMS Bhubaneswar and recently won the Atta Galatta-Bangalore Literature Festival Book Prize (popular choice) for I Don’t Love You Anymore .

b: Ritu Kumar is one of India’s foremost designers. She has developed a unique style of her own, reflecting the ancient traditions of Indian craftsmanship in a contemporary vocabulary. With a background in art history…
f: Ritu Kumar is one of India’s foremost designers. She has developed a unique style of her own, reflecting the ancient traditions of Indian craftsmanship in a contemporary vocabulary. With a background in art history and museology, which has enriched her horizons, her understanding of ancient designs and the innovative use of traditional crafts has created a new classicism. She began her work with four hand-block printers and two tables in a small village near Kolkata 40 years ago and was the first woman to introduce the ‘boutique’ culture in India under the brand name ‘Ritu’. Today, she has around 84 outlets, both India and abroad. Her boutiques feature a multifaceted showcase encompassing the very best of Indian design featuring a specially produced range of high fashion garments and accessories using silk, leather and cotton. She is credited as being one of the first Indian designers who was catalytic in bringing a contemporary idiom to several ancient skills and has been a strong force in marketing them to a dynamic modern India. In 2002, Kumar, joined by her son Amrish, launched a sub-brand, Ritu Kumar, LABEL, which uses the established forte of traditional Indian design and converts it into a fashion oriented international product. LABEL retails from most Ritu Kumar stores as well as some stand-alone stores. Her book Costumes and Textiles of Royal India chronicles the history of textiles and art design in India. Kumar was awarded the Indira Gandhi Priyadarshini Award in 2007 for her achievements and contribution in the field of fashion. To add to her achievements, the French government bestowed the prestigious Chevalier des arts et des lettres (Knight of the Order of Arts and Letters) for her contribution to Indian textile, crafts and traditional technique

b: Ritu Menon is a feminist, publisher and writer who has been active in the women’s movement in India and South Asia for almost three decades. She is the author and editor of several books and anthologies, including the…
f: Ritu Menon is a feminist, publisher and writer who has been active in the women’s movement in India and South Asia for almost three decades. She is the author and editor of several books and anthologies, including the ground-breaking text Borders & Boundaries: Women in India’s Partition; Out of Line: A Literary and Political Biography of Nayantara Sahgal; Address Book: A Publishing Memoir in the Time of COVID; and most recently, ZOHRA! A Biography in Four Acts .

b: Rituparna Neog (they/she) is a queer rights activist and library educator based in Assam. As the Founder & Director at Akam Foundation, she works on education, gender justice, and advocates for a free public library…
f: Rituparna Neog (they/she) is a queer rights activist and library educator based in Assam. As the Founder & Director at Akam Foundation, she works on education, gender justice, and advocates for a free public library system in India through the Free Libraries Network. Rituparna actively mobilises and organises the queer community in Assam, with a focus on rural areas. She played a key role in establishing the Chandraprabha Saikiani Feminist Library & Resource Centre and currently serves as a member representative from the northeast region to the National Council for Transgender Person, Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment, Govt. Of India.

b: Ritupriya is Assistant Editor of Taabar Toli, a fortnightly newspaper for children. A recipient of the Kendriya Sahitya Academy Yuva Puraskar in Rajasthani, she is the author of the Rajasthani poetry collections Sapna…
f: Ritupriya is Assistant Editor of Taabar Toli, a fortnightly newspaper for children. A recipient of the Kendriya Sahitya Academy Yuva Puraskar in Rajasthani, she is the author of the Rajasthani poetry collections Sapna Sanjovati Heeran and Thah ni kad hujyavai Prem.

b: Ritwij Shandilya is an author and a world record holder based in the city of Taj. He is the youngest Indian to write a French novel and also a 4-time national award winner for his contribution in literary industry. He…
f: Ritwij Shandilya is an author and a world record holder based in the city of Taj. He is the youngest Indian to write a French novel and also a 4-time national award winner for his contribution in literary industry. He is the author of the English fiction novel The Rise of Queen Revathi and a French novel titled La Couronne De Kanchipuram . He was named India’s most impactful author of 2018 by Indian Awaz.

b: Riva Ganguly Das joined the Indian Foreign Service in 1986. She has served as High Commissioner to Bangladesh and Ambassador to Romania, Albania and Moldova and has served as Consul General in Shanghai and New York.…
f: Riva Ganguly Das joined the Indian Foreign Service in 1986. She has served as High Commissioner to Bangladesh and Ambassador to Romania, Albania and Moldova and has served as Consul General in Shanghai and New York. Ganguly has also done postings in Spain and The Netherlands and has served in various capacities at Headquarters dealing with Nepal, Public Diplomacy, Passport & Consular, and United Nations. She was the Director-General of ICCR. Before her retirement, she was Secretary at the Ministry of External Affair.

b: Ambassador Riva Ganguly Das joined the Indian Foreign Service in 1986. She has been Consul General in two important financial capitals Shanghai and New York. Ambassador Das has extensive experience of multilateral…
f: Ambassador Riva Ganguly Das joined the Indian Foreign Service in 1986. She has been Consul General in two important financial capitals Shanghai and New York. Ambassador Das has extensive experience of multilateral Diplomacy, and has participated in many environmental negotiations, particularly concerning climate change. As an Alternate Permanent Representative of India to the Organization for Prohibition of Chemical Weapons (OPCW) at The Hague, she has worked on Non proliferation and disarmament issues. Prior to her retirement in 2021, Ambassador Das was Secretary (East) in the Ministry of External Affairs, handling India’s Relations with ASEAN, Korea, Mongolia, Latin America, and the Caribbean. Following her retirement, Ambassador Das has been elected as a member of the Advisory Committee of the UN Human Rights Council. She is also in the Governing Council of the Shillong based think tank Asian Confluence.

b: Roanna Gonsalves is the award-winning author of Sunita De Souza Goes To Sydney, published in Australia as The Permanent Resident . Her book won the NSW Premier’s Literary Award Multicultural Prize 2018 and was…
f: Roanna Gonsalves is the award-winning author of Sunita De Souza Goes To Sydney, published in Australia as The Permanent Resident . Her book won the NSW Premier’s Literary Award Multicultural Prize 2018 and was longlisted for the Dobbie Literary Award 2018. Gonsalves is a recipient of the Prime Minister’s Australia Asia Endeavour Award. Her acclaimed four-part radio series on multilingual Indian writing ‘On the Tip of a Billion Tongues’ was commissioned and broadcast by ABC RN's Earshot programme.

b: Robert Bickers is a historian of modern China and its relationship with the West. He grew up on Royal Air Force bases, studied in London, and has worked at the University of Bristol since 1997. He is currently a…
f: Robert Bickers is a historian of modern China and its relationship with the West. He grew up on Royal Air Force bases, studied in London, and has worked at the University of Bristol since 1997. He is currently a Professor of History at the University of Bristol and has authored six books, including China Bound: John Swire & Sons and Its World, Out of China: How the Chinese Ended the Era of Western Domination and Britain in China.

b: Robert Dessaix is an Australian writer and translator whose best-known books are the autobiography A Mother’s Disgrace , the novel Night Letters , the travel memoirs Twilight of Love and Arabesques , and his…
f: Robert Dessaix is an Australian writer and translator whose best-known books are the autobiography A Mother’s Disgrace , the novel Night Letters , the travel memoirs Twilight of Love and Arabesques , and his meditation on love, friendship, religion and mortality, What Days Are For . His most recent work of literary nonfiction is The Pleasures of Leisure , which is mostly set in India.

b: Robert Elgood has a BA in Islamic History from the School of Oriental and African Studies (SOAS), where he is now a Research Associate, and a DPhil from Oxford University in Indian Anthropology. He worked for some years…
f: Robert Elgood has a BA in Islamic History from the School of Oriental and African Studies (SOAS), where he is now a Research Associate, and a DPhil from Oxford University in Indian Anthropology. He worked for some years in the 1980s as Sotheby’s Oriental arms expert and from 2007 to 2013, he was Research Fellow, Eastern European, Islamic and Asian Arms and Armour at the Wallace Collection in London. He catalogued the arms collection at Belmont House, Kent and wrote the arms section to a catalogue for Jodhpur’s exhibition at the Museum of Fine Art, Houston. He has lectured at SOAS on the Asian Arts Diploma since the 1980s, at seminars such as the ICOMAN Conference in Oman in 2012, in Cairo in 2014 and at many of the major museums of Europe, America, the Arab world and India including the Victoria and Albert Museum, London, the Metropolitan Museum, New York, The Islamic Art Museum, Qatar and the Dar al Athar al-Islamiyyah, Kuwait where he was a guest scholar. He is a previous speaker at the Jaipur Literature Festival. He has also advised museums, dealers and collectors. He a Fellow of the Society of Antiquaries and the Royal Asiatic Society. He commissioned and edited Islamic Arms and Armour and is the author of Arms and Armour of Arabia in the 18th, 19th and 20th centuries , Firearms of the Islamic World in the Tareq Rajab Museum, Kuwait , Hindu Arms and Ritual: Arms and Armour from India 1400-1865 . Articles include three for Macmillan’s’ World Dictionary of Art and another for Brill’s Encyclopedia of Islam. In 2008, he wrote an introductory essay to a new edition of Sir Caspar Purdon Clarke’s Catalogue of the Collection of Indian Arms and Objects of Art at Marlborough House , originally published in 1898 and his Arms and Armour at Sandringham, published in

b: Robert Macfarlane is the author of a number of award-winning books on nature, people and place including Underland , The Old Ways , Mountains of the Mind and, with artist Jackie Morris, The Lost Words and The Lost…
f: Robert Macfarlane is the author of a number of award-winning books on nature, people and place including Underland , The Old Ways , Mountains of the Mind and, with artist Jackie Morris, The Lost Words and The Lost Spells . His books have been published in 30 languages and have been widely adapted for stage, film, television and radio

b: Robert Service is Emeritus Professor of Russian History at Oxford University and Senior Fellow at the Hoover Institution. His notable works include The Penguin History of Modern Russia and biographies of Lenin, Stalin,…
f: Robert Service is Emeritus Professor of Russian History at Oxford University and Senior Fellow at the Hoover Institution. His notable works include The Penguin History of Modern Russia and biographies of Lenin, Stalin, and Trotsky. His Blood on the Snow offers a panorama of the First World War and the Russian Revolution, 1914-1924.

b: Robin Coningham is the co-author of The Archaeology of South Asia , Appropriating the Past , and Archaeology, Cultural Heritage Protection and Community Engagement in South Asia . He holds UNESCO's 2014 Chair on…
f: Robin Coningham is the co-author of The Archaeology of South Asia , Appropriating the Past , and Archaeology, Cultural Heritage Protection and Community Engagement in South Asia . He holds UNESCO's 2014 Chair on Archaeological Ethics and Practice in Cultural Heritage and directs Durham University’s MA in International Cultural Heritage Management. He promotes heritage as a driver of sustainable development and advocates for revitalising ancient infrastructure to address global challenges.

b: Robin Gupta is the author of And What Remains in the End: The Memoirs of an Unrepentant Civil Servant , acclaimed for its rare and revealing investigation of the Indian bureaucracy. As an IAS officer, he has had the…
f: Robin Gupta is the author of And What Remains in the End: The Memoirs of an Unrepentant Civil Servant , acclaimed for its rare and revealing investigation of the Indian bureaucracy. As an IAS officer, he has had the distinction of serving the country in four provinces: Bengal, Madhya Pradesh, Haryana, and Punjab—apart from a long period of deputation with the central government. He retired as Financial Commissioner Revenue in the rank of Secretary to the Government of India.

b: Robin Jeffrey is a visiting research professor at the Institute of South Asian Studies, Singapore. His recent book, written with Assa Doron, is Waste of a Nation: Garbage and Growth in India . He is also the co-author…
f: Robin Jeffrey is a visiting research professor at the Institute of South Asian Studies, Singapore. His recent book, written with Assa Doron, is Waste of a Nation: Garbage and Growth in India . He is also the co-author with Doron of Cell Phone Nation and the author of India’s Newspaper Revolution .

b: Robyn Monro Miller is President of the International Play Association and has spent 25 years working with children and families across education, NGOs and government. This includes 13 years as Editor of Children’s…
f: Robyn Monro Miller is President of the International Play Association and has spent 25 years working with children and families across education, NGOs and government. This includes 13 years as Editor of Children’s Services newspaper. In 2012, she was part of the international delegation to the UN to progress development on the UN General Comment on Article 31 “The child’s right to play”.

b: Rochelle Potkar 's poems ‘To Daraza’ and ‘The Girl from Lal Bazaar’ have both won awards. An alumna of Iowa’s International Writing Programme and a Charles Wallace Writer’s fellow, Stirling, her book of…
f: Rochelle Potkar 's poems ‘To Daraza’ and ‘The Girl from Lal Bazaar’ have both won awards. An alumna of Iowa’s International Writing Programme and a Charles Wallace Writer’s fellow, Stirling, her book of stories Bombay Hangovers is due soon. She is also the author of Paper Asylum and Four Degrees of Separation while her poetry book The Inglorious Coins of the Counting House was shortlisted for international awards.

b: Rodaan Al Galidi is a writer of Iraqi descent. As his native country didn’t register births when he was born, he does not know his birth date. He studied as an engineer in Iraq before fleeing to escape military…
f: Rodaan Al Galidi is a writer of Iraqi descent. As his native country didn’t register births when he was born, he does not know his birth date. He studied as an engineer in Iraq before fleeing to escape military service, arriving in the Netherlands in 1998. However, his request for asylum was rejected, and since he was not allowed to follow the official courses of Dutch language, he taught himself the language and started writing. In 2007, Al Galidi was one of the people to benefit from the general pardon given by the Dutch parliament to asylum seekers arriving before 2001, and he still lives in the country.He has published a number of poem-books and novels in Dutch. The novel Hoe ik talent voor het leven kreeg was published in English as Two blankets, three sheets. In 2021, his Arabische sprookjes and Holland will also be translated into English.

b: Roger Cohen has worked at The New York Times for 34 years, holding positions such as foreign correspondent, foreign editor, columnist, and now Paris Bureau Chief. In 2023, he earned a Pulitzer Prize and a George Polk…
f: Roger Cohen has worked at The New York Times for 34 years, holding positions such as foreign correspondent, foreign editor, columnist, and now Paris Bureau Chief. In 2023, he earned a Pulitzer Prize and a George Polk Award with The Times teams covering the Ukraine war. He is the author of five books, including a family memoir, The Girl from Human Street: Ghosts of Memory in a Jewish Family and his recent work is An Affirming Flame: Meditations on Life and Politics . His work has been recognised with the 1994 Overseas Press Club of America Burger Human Rights Award for his investigation of torture and murder at a Serb-run Bosnian concentration camp. In 2017, he was awarded the Society of Publishers in Asia (SOPA) prize for opinion writing for a series on Australian mistreatment of refugees. He won the same award in 2018 for a piece about the Rohingya crisis in Burma. In 2021, Cohen received the Légion d’Honneur from the French Republic – France’s highest order of merit – for his work over four decades.

b: Rohan Champanerkar joined Rohan Prakashan 16 years ago and has significantly expanded the family publishing business with his thoughtful and creative vision. Under his leadership, the house has published over 750 books,…
f: Rohan Champanerkar joined Rohan Prakashan 16 years ago and has significantly expanded the family publishing business with his thoughtful and creative vision. Under his leadership, the house has published over 750 books, establishing itself as a leading name in Marathi publishing. While catering to a wide readership among Marathi readers, Rohan Prakashan also focuses on engaging young readers through creative, contemporary, and high-quality publications. The publishing house was recognized as Publisher of the Year in 2014 by the Public Relations Council of India (PRCI) and has won numerous state-level awards, reflecting its commitment to excellence and innovation in publishing.

b: Rohan Murty founded the Murty Classical Library of India at Harvard University, whose mission is to present the greatest literary works of India from the past two millennia to the largest readership in the world. He has…
f: Rohan Murty founded the Murty Classical Library of India at Harvard University, whose mission is to present the greatest literary works of India from the past two millennia to the largest readership in the world. He has a PhD in computer science from Harvard and an undergraduate degree from Cornell. He was a Junior Fellow at the Society of Fellows at Harvard.

b: Rohina Thapar is a visual designer with an interest in editorial design. Graduating from Srishti School of Art, Design and Technology in 2015, she has been working in the field of communication ever since. Presently at…
f: Rohina Thapar is a visual designer with an interest in editorial design. Graduating from Srishti School of Art, Design and Technology in 2015, she has been working in the field of communication ever since. Presently at Art1st, she is responsible for executing various design projects, from curriculum publications to brand design. She approaches her work as a self-reflective process and a quest to understand the bigger picture.

b: Rohini Chowdhury is literary translator. Her primary languages are pre-modern and modern Hindi as well as English. Her translations include the Ramcharitmanas , a 16th- century retelling of the story of Ram by Tulsidas,…
f: Rohini Chowdhury is literary translator. Her primary languages are pre-modern and modern Hindi as well as English. Her translations include the Ramcharitmanas , a 16th- century retelling of the story of Ram by Tulsidas, and universally regarded as the greatest achievement of Hindi literature. She also writes for children and has more than 20 books and several short stories to her credit. Her published writing covers a wide spectrum of literary genres, including novels, short fiction and nonfiction. She runs a story website at www.longlongtimeago.com .

b: Rohit Chawla is a leading Indian contemporary photographer with a background in advertising, having spent nearly two decades at JWT as national film chief and creative director. He founded his own design and film…
f: Rohit Chawla is a leading Indian contemporary photographer with a background in advertising, having spent nearly two decades at JWT as national film chief and creative director. He founded his own design and film production company and has held numerous solo exhibitions. Represented by Art Alive Gallery, his editorial work includes over 400 magazine covers for India Today Group and Open magazine. Chawla’s recent work earned India its first-ever Industry Craft Gold Lion at Cannes in 2023 and Grand Prix at Spikes Asia and the Abbies in 2024. He is the visiting dean for photography at AAFT University. A culinary aesthete, he enjoys food photography and has done three food books: The Indian Accent Cookbook , The Fine Art of Food and The Bangla Table from Chettinad .

b: Rohit Kumar Singh has been an officer of the Indian Administrative Service since 1989. He has a diverse sets of skills in management and has worked extensively and provided leadership in the area of Public Health,…
f: Rohit Kumar Singh has been an officer of the Indian Administrative Service since 1989. He has a diverse sets of skills in management and has worked extensively and provided leadership in the area of Public Health, Finance, Infrastructure, Public Private Partnerships, Information & Communication Technology and External Aid Portfolio Management. He has handled managerial responsibilities in the Government of India and Government of Rajasthan in various departments such as National Highways, Information Technology, Finance, Commercial Taxes, Urban Infrastructure Development, Road Transport, Rural Development and Information & Public Relations.

b: Rohit Lamba is an assistant professor of economics at Pennsylvania State University and a visiting assistant professor of economics at New York University Abu Dhabi. He received a PhD in economics from Princeton…
f: Rohit Lamba is an assistant professor of economics at Pennsylvania State University and a visiting assistant professor of economics at New York University Abu Dhabi. He received a PhD in economics from Princeton University and was a postdoctoral fellow at the University of Cambridge. He publishes regularly in leading academic journals and newspapers. He has also worked as an economist at the office of the chief economic adviser to the Government of India.

b: Rohit Sarin is a thought leader with nearly three decades of experience in Family Offices and Private Banking. Before founding Client Associates, he worked with Deutsche Bank, ANZ Grindlays Bank, and Kotak Bank. Rohit’s…
f: Rohit Sarin is a thought leader with nearly three decades of experience in Family Offices and Private Banking. Before founding Client Associates, he worked with Deutsche Bank, ANZ Grindlays Bank, and Kotak Bank. Rohit’s vision and focus on excellence has led to Client Associates becoming India’s most trusted and admired wealth management firm, with a proven track record across market cycles. Rohit has garnered goodwill amongst wealthy families and family offices for offering unbiased advice based on globally accepted investment processes. Rohit is also an author of the best-selling book “Unlocking Wealth: Secrets to Getting Rich at Any Age”. The book is living its purpose of spreading the message of wealth and has become Rohit’s bridge with the world around him.

b: Rolee Agarwal, IRS, Pr. Commissioner of Income Tax is a renowned bureaucrat, singer, poet, spiritual thinker and speaker at various forums like CII, ELETS and various educational institutions. Apart from being a finance…
f: Rolee Agarwal, IRS, Pr. Commissioner of Income Tax is a renowned bureaucrat, singer, poet, spiritual thinker and speaker at various forums like CII, ELETS and various educational institutions. Apart from being a finance expert with 30 years of experience, she has avidly pursued her interest in music, performing at various programmes for organisations like Urdu Academy, Sanskrit Academy, Tarannum, Sur se Sukoon, and Ghazal Ki Kahani. She is the recipient of multiple accolades, including the Lady Shri Ram Distinguished Alumni award, 'The Precious Daughters of India Award' and the Business Rankers Women Achievers Award, among others.

b: Roly Keating has been Chief Executive of the British Library since September 2012. In his tenure so far, he has overseen a series of significant developments including the historic move to large-scale digital collecting…
f: Roly Keating has been Chief Executive of the British Library since September 2012. In his tenure so far, he has overseen a series of significant developments including the historic move to large-scale digital collecting through legal deposit; the incorporation into the Library of the Public Lending Right service; the Library’s successful and popular 800th anniversary commemorations of Magna Carta; the launch of the Knowledge Quarter, an innovative partnership of over 70 knowledge-based organisations near the Library’s London HQ; the creation of a national network of Business and IP Centres in major regional libraries; and the launch in 2015 of Living Knowledge, which sets out an ambitious vision and strategy for the Library’s growth and development towards its fiftieth anniversary in 2023. Keating joined the Library after a long and successful career as a programme-maker and broadcasting executive at the BBC where he played key roles in the launch of UKTV, as its first Head of Programming, and BBC Four, as its launch Controller in 2002, before moving on to become Controller of BBC Two and Director of Archive Content, with editorial oversight of the BBC’s online services including BBC iPlayer. Keating is a member of the board of Channel 4 and a Trustee of the Clore Leadership Programme. He chairs the Knowledge Quarter Board and the Conference of European National Librarians. He holds Honorary Doctorates from the Universities of Lincoln, Warwick and York.

b: Rom Whitaker was born in New York in 1943 and came to India in 1951 with mother Doris and step-father Rama, son of Kamaladevi and Harindranath Chattopadhyaya. He set up the Madras Snake Park in 1969, Crocodile Bank in…
f: Rom Whitaker was born in New York in 1943 and came to India in 1951 with mother Doris and step-father Rama, son of Kamaladevi and Harindranath Chattopadhyaya. He set up the Madras Snake Park in 1969, Crocodile Bank in 1976, the Andamans Centre of Island Ecology in 1989 and Agumbe Rainforest Station in 2005. His awards include Whitley Fund for Nature, Rolex, Peter Scott, Salim Ali and a Padma Shri.

b: Chef Romy Gill MBE was appointed Member of the Order of the British Empire (MBE) in 2016. She received the ICAP Culinary Award for her book On The Himalayan Trail in 2023. Her other publications include Zaika – Vegan…
f: Chef Romy Gill MBE was appointed Member of the Order of the British Empire (MBE) in 2016. She received the ICAP Culinary Award for her book On The Himalayan Trail in 2023. Her other publications include Zaika – Vegan Recipes from India , and Romy Gill’s India – Recipes from Home .

b: Ronojoy Sen is Senior Research Fellow at the Institute of South Asian Studies & South Asian Studies Programme, National University of Singapore. His most recent book is House of the People: Parliament and the Making of…
f: Ronojoy Sen is Senior Research Fellow at the Institute of South Asian Studies & South Asian Studies Programme, National University of Singapore. His most recent book is House of the People: Parliament and the Making of Indian Democracy . He has also authored Nation at Play: A History of Sport in India and Articles of Faith: Religion, Secularism, and the Indian Supreme Court and has edited several books. He has worked for over a decade with leading Indian newspapers, most recently as an editor with The Times of India.

b: Roobina Karode is the Director and Chief Curator at the Kiran Nadar Museum of Art (KNMA), New Delhi, since it opened its doors in 2010. As an art educator, writer and curator, Karode has extensively contributed to the…
f: Roobina Karode is the Director and Chief Curator at the Kiran Nadar Museum of Art (KNMA), New Delhi, since it opened its doors in 2010. As an art educator, writer and curator, Karode has extensively contributed to the field, teaching Art History, both Indian Modern and Western art from 1990 to 2006, at various institutions in Delhi. She was awarded the Fulbright Fellowship, the Ford Teaching Fellowship, and received the ‘Curator of the Year 2016’ award by India Today Art Awards. In 2019, she was the curator for the must-see Indian Pavilion at the 58th Venice Biennale. Karode has, over the years, curated more than sixty significant exhibitions both within India and abroad.

b: Roshan Ali is a novelist. His work has appeared in The Hindu and Huffington Post India . His debut novel Ib's Endless Search for Satisfaction has been shortlisted for the 2019 Shakti Bhatt First Book Prize and the 2019…
f: Roshan Ali is a novelist. His work has appeared in The Hindu and Huffington Post India . His debut novel Ib's Endless Search for Satisfaction has been shortlisted for the 2019 Shakti Bhatt First Book Prize and the 2019 JCB Prize for Literature.

b: Rosinka Chaudhuri is Director and Professor of Cultural Studies at the Centre for Studies in Social Sciences, Calcutta (CSSSC). She was inaugural Mellon Professor of the Global South at Oxford University, 2017-18, and…
f: Rosinka Chaudhuri is Director and Professor of Cultural Studies at the Centre for Studies in Social Sciences, Calcutta (CSSSC). She was inaugural Mellon Professor of the Global South at Oxford University, 2017-18, and has held visiting positions at King’s College, London, Delhi University, Cambridge University and Columbia University. Her books include Gentlemen Poets in Colonial Bengal: Emergent Nationalism and the Orientalist Project, Freedom and Beef-Steaks: Colonial Calcutta Culture and The Literary Thing: History, Poetry and the Making of a Modern Cultural Sphere She has edited Derozio, Poet of India: A Definitive Edition, The Indian Postcolonial, A History of Indian Poetry in English, An Acre of Green Grass and Other English Writings of Buddhadeva Bose, and a series titled Social Science Across Discipline. Her translation of Rabindranath Tagore’s letters, titled Letters from a Young Poet (1887-94) received an Honourable Mention in the category A.K. Ramanujan Prize for Translation (S. Asia) at the Association for Asian Studies Book Prizes 2016.

b: Roy Jacobsen is an original, strong, and analytical writer with a special interest in the underlying psychology at play in human relationships and actions. He is a wonderful storyteller who has twice been nominated for…
f: Roy Jacobsen is an original, strong, and analytical writer with a special interest in the underlying psychology at play in human relationships and actions. He is a wonderful storyteller who has twice been nominated for the Nordic Council's Literary Award for The Conquerors in 1991, and Frost in 2003. His books have been published in thirty-nine territories, and was shortlisted for the IMPAC Dublin Literary Award in 2009 for his novel The Burnt-Out Town of Miracles . In 2017, he was shortlisted for The Man Booker International Prize for The Unseen – as the first Norwegian writer ever.

b: Ru Freeman is the the award-winning Sri Lankan and American author of A Disobedient Girl and On Sal Mal Lane , a NYT Editor's Choice, and editor of Extraordinary Rendition: (American) Writers on Palestine and…
f: Ru Freeman is the the award-winning Sri Lankan and American author of A Disobedient Girl and On Sal Mal Lane , a NYT Editor's Choice, and editor of Extraordinary Rendition: (American) Writers on Palestine and Indivisible: Global Leaders on Shared Security. Her latest work is the forthcoming Sleeping Alone.

b: Ruben Banerjee is the editor in chief of Outlook . He was earlier the National Affairs Editor of Hindustan Times . A journalist with more than three decades of experience, he worked previously as an editor with Al…
f: Ruben Banerjee is the editor in chief of Outlook . He was earlier the National Affairs Editor of Hindustan Times . A journalist with more than three decades of experience, he worked previously as an editor with Al Jazeera English, India Today and the Indian Express . An incurable news junkie, Banerjee is particularly fascinated by anything that is interesting and significant and impacts the world. He is also an author with his latest book Naveen Patnaik, an unauthorised biography of the Odisha chief minister receiving rave reviews. He is also the author of The Orissa Tragedy: A Cyclone’s Year of Tragedy .

b: Ruby Hembrom is an Adivasi publisher, cultural documentarian, and practitioner who founded adivaani in 2012 as a non-profit organization. She is the author of adivaani’s Santal Creation Stories for Children , a…
f: Ruby Hembrom is an Adivasi publisher, cultural documentarian, and practitioner who founded adivaani in 2012 as a non-profit organization. She is the author of adivaani’s Santal Creation Stories for Children , a retelling of the Santal creation narratives in English, and the prize-winning Disaibon Hul , which focuses on the Santal Rebellion of 1855. Her publishing initiative, now with 19 titles, emerged from the need to assert Adivasi presence in historical, contemporary, social, cultural, and literary spaces, and her advocacy through publishing and knowledge production extends into broader campaigning and movement building for Adivasi communities.

b: Ruby Lal is an acclaimed historian of Mughal India. Her recently published biography, Empress: The Astonishing Reign of Nur Jahan, has been lauded by The New Yorker , the Guardian , The New York Times , the BBC , The…
f: Ruby Lal is an acclaimed historian of Mughal India. Her recently published biography, Empress: The Astonishing Reign of Nur Jahan, has been lauded by The New Yorker , the Guardian , The New York Times , the BBC , The Indian Express , Business Standard and other national and international journals and newspapers. She is Professor of South Asian History at Emory University and divides her time between Atlanta and Delhi.

b: Ruby Wax began her career with the Royal Shakespeare Company followed by a successful TV career with the BBC for 25 years along with writing and editing scripts for Absolutely Fabulous . In 2014, she received a…
f: Ruby Wax began her career with the Royal Shakespeare Company followed by a successful TV career with the BBC for 25 years along with writing and editing scripts for Absolutely Fabulous .
