In 2014, she received a Master’s degree in Mindfulness Based Cognitive Therapy from Oxford and in 2015 was awarded an OBE for services to mental health. Her last three books have been number one bestsellers.

b: Rubén Montoya is an adjunct professor of Humanities and Archaeology at IE University. He combines research and writing, bringing the past closer through engaging and insightful narratives. His latest book is Pompeii: A…
f: Rubén Montoya is an adjunct professor of Humanities and Archaeology at IE University. He combines research and writing, bringing the past closer through engaging and insightful narratives. His latest book is Pompeii: A Roman City in 100 Objects . He regularly contributes to National Geographic and Historia y Vida .

b: Ruchika Mehta is one of India's senior most Lifestyle Editors, having launched various international titles like Femina and Grazia, and edited magazines like Femina. She is currently the Editor of HELLO! magazine and…
f: Ruchika Mehta is one of India's senior most Lifestyle Editors, having launched various international titles like Femina and Grazia, and edited magazines like Femina. She is currently the Editor of HELLO! magazine and the EDITOR AT LARGE, Luxury & Lifestyle, INDIA TODAY GROUP. As an award winning journalist, in her career spanning over 25 years as Editor, she has interviewed various domestic and international celebrities, and been on various prestigious television shows and panels.

b: Ruchir Joshi is the author of Great Eastern Hotel , published in 2025. His other works include The Last Jet-Engine Laugh , a novel, and Poriborton! , a nonfiction account of West Bengal’s 2011 state elections. A regular…
f: Ruchir Joshi is the author of Great Eastern Hotel , published in 2025. His other works include The Last Jet-Engine Laugh , a novel, and Poriborton! , a nonfiction account of West Bengal’s 2011 state elections. A regular columnist, he has written for The Telegraph , The Hindu , and The Economic Times , and has contributed to Granta , Seminar , The Indian Quarterly , and others. Joshi is also a filmmaker, known for his award-winning documentary Tales from Planet Kolkata and other essay films.

b: Ruchira Gupta is an Emmy winning journalist and Founder of NGO, Apne Aap with a mission to create a world in which no child is bought or sold. I Kick and I Fly is her debut novel. She advises the UN on child protection…
f: Ruchira Gupta is an Emmy winning journalist and Founder of NGO, Apne Aap with a mission to create a world in which no child is bought or sold. I Kick and I Fly is her debut novel. She advises the UN on child protection and women’s empowerment issues, especially related to sex-trafficking. She has been awarded the French Ordre National du Mérite, the Clinton Global Citizen Award , and the UN NGO CSW Woman of Distinction , among other honors, for her Activism. She has co-written a book with Gloria Steinem, As if Women Matter and edited two anthologies, River of Flesh and Renu’s letters to Birju Babu .

b: Rudraneil Sengupta i s a journalist and author. Between 2016 and 2018, he embedded with the Delhi Police for a series of investigative reports for a national broadsheet. Drawing on this experience, he wrote his debut…
f: Rudraneil Sengupta i s a journalist and author. Between 2016 and 2018, he embedded with the Delhi Police for a series of investigative reports for a national broadsheet. Drawing on this experience, he wrote his debut novel, The Beast Within . He is also the author of Enter the Dangal: Travels through India’s Wrestling Landscape , a work of narrative nonfiction exploring India’s wrestling culture.

b: Rujuta Diwekar is India’s leading public health advocate and amongst the most followed nutritionists globally. Her books have sold more than 1.75 million copies and her videos have received more than 300 million views.…
f: Rujuta Diwekar is India’s leading public health advocate and amongst the most followed nutritionists globally. Her books have sold more than 1.75 million copies and her videos have received more than 300 million views. Her clear and simple message to eat local, seasonal, and traditional, has redefined the discourse on health and wellness, nudging it away from diet trends and towards sustainable well-being of people and the planet.

b: Rukmini S is an award-winning independent data journalist based in Chennai. She is the former National Data Editor of The Hindu and HuffPost India. Her first book, Whole Numbers and Half Truths: What Data Can and Cannot…
f: Rukmini S is an award-winning independent data journalist based in Chennai. She is the former National Data Editor of The Hindu and HuffPost India. Her first book, Whole Numbers and Half Truths: What Data Can and Cannot Tell Us About Modern India was published in December 2021 by Context, an imprint of Westland Publications.

b: Rupert Everett is an actor, writer and director. He first appeared on stage in 1981 as Guy Bennett in the West End production of Julian Mitchell’s play, Another Country, a role which he repeated in the 1984 film…
f: Rupert Everett is an actor, writer and director. He first appeared on stage in 1981 as Guy Bennett in the West End production of Julian Mitchell’s play, Another Country, a role which he repeated in the 1984 film version that saw him nominated for a BAFTA as Best Newcomer. Subsequent nominations include a BAFTA and Golden Globe for My Best Friend’s Wedding .

b: Rupert Snell has studied, taught and delighted in Hindi and its literature for half a century. In retirement from academia, he contemplates the aesthetics of certain favourite works, and has books forthcoming on the…
f: Rupert Snell has studied, taught and delighted in Hindi and its literature for half a century. In retirement from academia, he contemplates the aesthetics of certain favourite works, and has books forthcoming on the Ramcharitmanas and on autobiographical writing in Hindi. He is also drafting a novel ‘by’ a fictional pupil of Biharilal.

b: Rupi Kaur is a poet, artist and performer. Over the last three years, her works have taken the literary world by storm. Her new book, the sun and her flowers , an instant global bestseller, is an artistic sibling to her…
f: Rupi Kaur is a poet, artist and performer. Over the last three years, her works have taken the literary world by storm. Her new book, the sun and her flowers , an instant global bestseller, is an artistic sibling to her debut, milk and honey, America’s best selling book of 2017. “i am the product of all the ancestors getting together and deciding these stories need to be told” Kaur sees her work as an articulation of this vision. She’s an eternal artist. At the age of five, her mother handed her a paintbrush and said, “draw her heart out”. At 17, she happened upon a local open mic night where she performed her first spoken word poem. She fell in love with performance poetry that night. Kaur continued performing across Canada, while building a community of readers and poetry enthusiasts. While studying at the University of Waterloo, Kaur wrote, illustrated and self-published her first collection, milk and honey . In the years since, milk and honey has become an international phenomenon. It’s sold over 2.5 million copies, been translated into more than 30 languages and landed as a #1 New York Times Bestseller where it continues to sit for over the 80th straight week. “i am the first woman in my lineage with freedom of choice. to craft her future whichever way i choose. say what is on my mind when i want to. without the whip of the lash. there are hundreds of firsts i am thankful for” Kaur explores a variety of themes in her work ranging from love, loss, trauma, healing, femininity, migration and revolution. She’s a storyteller and chronicler, a repository of community and history. There’s a simplicity and nuance to her work that has found a home in the hearts of millions. This magic is captured in her stage performances, which are magnetic musical in

b: Rupleena Bose works as an Associate Professor of English at Sri Venkateswara College, University of Delhi. Her doctorate is on the urban new-wave Bangla Music of the Nineties. She has written several screenplays,…
f: Rupleena Bose works as an Associate Professor of English at Sri Venkateswara College, University of Delhi. Her doctorate is on the urban new-wave Bangla Music of the Nineties. She has written several screenplays, including a non-fiction film, You Don’t Belong , that won a National Film Award. Summer of Then is her debut novel, spanning a decade of the personal and political, moving between a woman’s interiority, and the nation outside.

b: Ruth Harris is the author of Lourdes and the Man on Devil’s Island , which won the Wolfson Prize and the National Jewish Book Awards respectively. She is Senior Research Fellow at All Souls’ College, University of…
f: Ruth Harris is the author of Lourdes and the Man on Devil’s Island , which won the Wolfson Prize and the National Jewish Book Awards respectively. She is Senior Research Fellow at All Souls’ College, University of Oxford, Fellow of the British Academy, and Professor of Modern History at the University of Oxford.

b: Ruth Ozeki is a novelist, filmmaker, and Zen Buddhist priest. She is the author of four novels. Her work, The Book of Form and Emptiness , won the 2022 Women’s Prize for Fiction. Her nonfiction work includes a memoir,…
f: Ruth Ozeki is a novelist, filmmaker, and Zen Buddhist priest. She is the author of four novels. Her work, The Book of Form and Emptiness , won the 2022 Women’s Prize for Fiction. Her nonfiction work includes a memoir, Timecode of a Face , and the documentary film, Halving the Bones .

b: Ruthvika Rao is a novelist from Hyderabad, India. Her debut novel, The Fertile Earth , was a finalist for the Center for Fiction First Novel Prize, the Chautauqua Prize, the Ramnath Goenka Sahitya Samman, and the…
f: Ruthvika Rao is a novelist from Hyderabad, India. Her debut novel, The Fertile Earth , was a finalist for the Center for Fiction First Novel Prize, the Chautauqua Prize, the Ramnath Goenka Sahitya Samman, and the Crossword Book Award, and was longlisted for the Dylan Thomas Prize. Her second novel, All Our Evenings , is forthcoming in 2026. She is a graduate of the Iowa Writers’ Workshop and currently lives in Michigan.

b: S. Hareesh is the author of the short story collections Rasavidhyayude charithram, Adam and Appan as well as the novel Moustache. His screen plays include Aedan , winner of best screenplay at the Kerala State Film…
f: S. Hareesh is the author of the short story collections Rasavidhyayude charithram, Adam and Appan as well as the novel Moustache. His screen plays include Aedan , winner of best screenplay at the Kerala State Film Awards, Jallikkattu , India’s Oscar nomination for this year, and the upcoming Churuli . He won the JCB Prize for Literature 2020 and Kerala Sahitya Akademi awards for his short story collections.

b: S Prasannarajan is an editor and essayist who has written extensively on politics, books, ideas and international affairs. He is currently the editor of Open Magazine. Prasannarajan has previously held senior editorial…
f: S Prasannarajan is an editor and essayist who has written extensively on politics, books, ideas and international affairs. He is currently the editor of Open Magazine. Prasannarajan has previously held senior editorial positions in The Times of India, the Indian Express and India Today . He lives in Delhi.

b: S Irfan Habib has worked in the area of history of science as well as political history. His book To Make the Deaf Hear: Ideology and Programme of Bhagat Singh and his Comrades , has been translated into several Indian…
f: S Irfan Habib has worked in the area of history of science as well as political history. His book To Make the Deaf Hear: Ideology and Programme of Bhagat Singh and his Comrades , has been translated into several Indian languages like Hindi, Tamil, Malayalam, Punjabi and Bengali. Maulana Azad-A Life is his most recent book.

b: S. Muralidhar practised law in the Supreme Court of India and the Delhi High Court for nearly two decades. He conducted several pro bono and PIL cases. Apart from being the counsel for the Election Commission of India…
f: S. Muralidhar practised law in the Supreme Court of India and the Delhi High Court for nearly two decades. He conducted several pro bono and PIL cases. Apart from being the counsel for the Election Commission of India and the National Human Rights Commission, he was a part-time member of the Law Commission from December 2002 till May 2006. Muralidhar was appointed as a Judge of the High Court of Delhi in May 2006 and became the Chief Justice of the High Court of Orissa in January 2021. Many of his judgments have contributed to the development of laws. Among his notable initiatives include the setting up of the Centre for Judicial Archives and the Museum of Justice in Cuttack.

b: Dr. S. Natesh is an honorary fellow at Ashoka Trust for Research in Energy and the Environment. After teaching botany at Delhi University for nearly a decade, Dr. S. Natesh moved to the Department of Biotechnology,…
f: Dr. S. Natesh is an honorary fellow at Ashoka Trust for Research in Energy and the Environment. After teaching botany at Delhi University for nearly a decade, Dr. S. Natesh moved to the Department of Biotechnology, Government of India, where he headed several divisions. His leadership and vision led to many successful programmes in HRD, management, and the conservation of bioresources, as well as international collaboration. Dr. Natesh received the Biospectrum Lifetime Achievement Award for his contribution to raising the Indian Bioscience Sector to new heights. A new plant species, Aponogeton Nateshii, has been named in his honour.

b: S. Vijay Kumar is a self-taught sculpture and Indian temple art enthusiast who started writing extensively on the nuances of the art form on a bilingual blog site called- poetryinstone. For the past 16 years, Vijay has…
f: S. Vijay Kumar is a self-taught sculpture and Indian temple art enthusiast who started writing extensively on the nuances of the art form on a bilingual blog site called- poetryinstone. For the past 16 years, Vijay has been instrumental in assisting the restitution efforts of high profile trafficked Indian artefacts. His background work led to the dramatic 20 million raids conducted by HomeLand Security, USA during the Asia Week in NYC, and the same has been chronicled in his non-fiction book, The Idol Thief , published by Juggernaut Books. Vijay is a regular speaker and columnist for the Hindu, Times of India and other dailies.

b: S.R. Faruqi has written extensively in Urdu and English, including novels and a collection of stories. Much of his work has focussed on a range of subjects related to Urdu literature and language.
f: S.R. Faruqi has written extensively in Urdu and English, including novels and a collection of stories. Much of his work has focussed on a range of subjects related to Urdu literature and language.

b: Saad Mohseni , co-founder and Chairman of MOBY Group, has pioneered high-quality news and media content across emerging markets for over two decades. Recognized by the Asia Society as an “Asia Game Changer” for his…
f: Saad Mohseni , co-founder and Chairman of MOBY Group, has pioneered high-quality news and media content across emerging markets for over two decades. Recognized by the Asia Society as an “Asia Game Changer” for his contributions, Mohseni launched his first network in Afghanistan in 2002, transforming MOBY Group into a leading media company across South and Central Asia, the Middle East, and Africa. In 2012, 21st Century Fox acquired a strategic stake in the company, which the Mohseni family regained after Disney’s acquisition of Fox. MOBY Group, known for its award-winning content, spans TV, radio, digital, and strategic communications. Mohseni has been named among Time magazine’s “100 Most Influential People” and BBC’s “10 Men Globally Championing Gender Equality” for promoting civil society and women’s rights in Afghanistan. He also serves on advisory boards of the International Crisis Group (ICG) and the Middle East Institute (MEI).

b: Saanya Kanwar is the newest agent at Jacaranda Literary Agency, building the agency’s children’s list. She was most recently acquiring and editing projects at Paw Prints Publishing, an imprint of Baker & Taylor. She has…
f: Saanya Kanwar is the newest agent at Jacaranda Literary Agency, building the agency’s children’s list. She was most recently acquiring and editing projects at Paw Prints Publishing, an imprint of Baker & Taylor. She has also worked at Writers House and DeFiore & Company, two literary agencies based in New York.

b: Saaz Aggarwal has a master’s degree in Mathematics but has established herself as a writer and artist. Her work includes biographies, translations, critical reviews, humour columns, themed painting collections, and…
f: Saaz Aggarwal has a master’s degree in Mathematics but has established herself as a writer and artist. Her work includes biographies, translations, critical reviews, humour columns, themed painting collections, and mixed-media installations. Her books on Sindh are in university libraries around the world.

b: Saba Naqvi is one of India's best-known journalists. The former political editor of Outlook magazine, she now writes columns in leading Indian dailies including the Times of India,The Tribune and several websites. She…
f: Saba Naqvi is one of India's best-known journalists. The former political editor of Outlook magazine, she now writes columns in leading Indian dailies including the Times of India,The Tribune and several websites. She is also a well-known election analyst and political commentator. She is currently visiting professor at the Jindal School of Journalism. She has published four books: In Good Faith, Capital Conquest, Shades of Saffron:From Vajpayee to Modi and her latest The Coalition Handbook . She is currently working on her next book on India’s backsliding democracy.

b: Sabeena Gadihoke is Professor, Video and Television Production at the AJK Mass Communication Research Centre at Jamia Millia Islamia University, New Delhi, where she also teaches courses in Cinematography and…
f: Sabeena Gadihoke is Professor, Video and Television Production at the AJK Mass Communication Research Centre at Jamia Millia Islamia University, New Delhi, where she also teaches courses in Cinematography and Photography Studies. She has worked as an independent documentary filmmaker and cameraperson. Her book, Camera Chronicles , is a biography of Homai Vyarawalla, India’s first woman press photographer. Gadihoke is also a photo historian and curator, her most recent co-curated project being ‘Twin Sisters with Cameras’, an exhibition of photographs by Debalina Mazumder and Manobina Roy at the India International Centre, Delhi, and the JBMCRC, Centre for Studies of Social Sciences, Kolkata.

b: Sabrina Mahfouz is a writer and performer, raised in London and Cairo. She is a Fellow of the Royal Society of Literature (FRSL) and resident writer at Shakespeare’s Globe Theatre. Her most recent theatre show was A…
f: Sabrina Mahfouz is a writer and performer, raised in London and Cairo. She is a Fellow of the Royal Society of Literature (FRSL) and resident writer at Shakespeare’s Globe Theatre. Her most recent theatre show was A History of Water in the Middle East (Royal Court) and her most recent publications as editor include Smashing It: Working Class Artists on Life, Art and Making it Happen and Poems From a Green and Blue Planet . Mahfouz’s published and produced theatre work includes Chef , a Fringe First Award winner, Dry Ice , for which she was nominated in The Stage Awards for Acting Excellence, With a Little Bit of Luck , which won Best Drama Production in the BBC Radio & Music Awards 2019, Clean , a Herald Angel Award winner which transferred to New York and she recently adapted Malorie Blackman’s celebrated YA novel Noughts & Crosses for Pilot Theatre. She also writes for children and her play Zeraffa Giraffa (based on the book by Diane Hofmeyr and Jane Ray, for Omnibus Theatre and Little Angel Theatre) won a 2018 Off West End Award. Her poetry collection, How You Might Know Me was a 2017 Guardian Best Summer Read and she was an essay contributor to the award-winning anthology The Good Immigrant . She is the editor of The Things I Would Tell You: British Muslim Women Write , a 2017 Guardian Book of the Year, a London's Big Read finalist and selected by Emma Watson for her feminist book club, Our Shared Shelf. She's a regular on BBC Radio 4 recently presenting Word of Mouth , Poetry Please and writing fiction for Short Works .

b: Sachin Pilot is the Deputy Chief Minister of Rajasthan. A member of the Indian National Congress, he was elected from the Tonk assembly seat in the recent assembly election with a record margin of 55,000 votes. He was a…
f: Sachin Pilot is the Deputy Chief Minister of Rajasthan. A member of the Indian National Congress, he was elected from the Tonk assembly seat in the recent assembly election with a record margin of 55,000 votes. He was a member of the Indian Parliament in the 14th Lok Sabha from Dausa and in the 15th Lok Sabha from the Ajmer parliamentary constituency of Rajasthan. He has been the Union Minister for Telecom, IT and Postal Services from 2009 to 2011 and then the Minister of Corporate Affairs in the Manmohan Singh Ministry until 2014. He was nominated as a Young Global Achiever by the World Economic Forum in 2009. He has been the President of the Rajasthan Pradesh Congress Committee since January 2014. Pilot has a private pilot’s license and is an avid adventure sports enthusiast.

b: Sadaf Saaz is a poet, writer, entrepreneur and women’s rights advocate. She is a festival director and producer of Dhaka Lit Fest, which she co-founded in 2011 and runs an arts management and production company in…
f: Sadaf Saaz is a poet, writer, entrepreneur and women’s rights advocate. She is a festival director and producer of Dhaka Lit Fest, which she co-founded in 2011 and runs an arts management and production company in Dhaka. A member of the Bangladeshi women’s activist organisation Naripokkho , she has done extensive research and advocated for violence against women, women’s political participation, women’s legal rights, women’s health and reproductive rights, and sexuality. Sadaf is the author of a collection of poems titled Sari Reams and her monologues based on Bangladeshi women’s stories Je Kotha Jai Na Bola (That which cannot be said) have been performed in various locations in Bangladesh.

b: Sadhana Rao is a research-led writer and curator in the Arts & Culture spaces. She has written on Arts, Film festivals, Music, Crafts, Travel, Literature, & Socio-Economics for leading publications. As a curator,…
f: Sadhana Rao is a research-led writer and curator in the Arts & Culture spaces. She has written on Arts, Film festivals, Music, Crafts, Travel, Literature, & Socio-Economics for leading publications. As a curator, Sadhana works with artists and conservatories across genres to weave narrative-backed lecture demonstrations and performances. Amalgamating pedagogy, artistic diversity and inclusivity, her endeavours find home among myriad platforms, from academic conclaves to cultural festivals to the community at large.

b: Sadhna Shanker is an author and civil servant. Ascendance is her second work of fiction after Never a Disconnect . She has written for several publications including, the International Herald Tribune, Christian Science…
f: Sadhna Shanker is an author and civil servant. Ascendance is her second work of fiction after Never a Disconnect . She has written for several publications including, the International Herald Tribune, Christian Science Monitor, The Hindu , Huffington Post and The Wire .

b: Sadhvi Bhagawati Saraswati is a renowned spiritual leader, author, and motivational speaker. She’s authored Hollywood to the Himalayas: A Journey of Healing and Transformation. She is the Secretary-General of the…
f: Sadhvi Bhagawati Saraswati is a renowned spiritual leader, author, and motivational speaker. She’s authored Hollywood to the Himalayas: A Journey of Healing and Transformation. She is the Secretary-General of the Global Interfaith WASH Alliance; president of Divine Shakti Foundation; and director of the International Yoga Festival at Parmarth Niketan Ashram, Rishikesh. She serves on the United Nations Advisory Council on Religion and on the steering committees of the International Partnership for Religion and Sustainable Development (PaRD) and the Moral Imperative to End Extreme Poverty, a campaign by the United Nations and World Bank. She was awarded the Lifetime Achievement Award by U.S. President Joe Biden for her lifelong commitment to volunteer service. She has been ordained into the sacred order of Sanyas by her guru HH Pujya Swami Chidanand Saraswatiji and has been living at Parmarth Niketan Ashram for the past twenty-six years.

b: Safeena Husain has worked extensively with rural and urban underserved communities in South America, Africa and Asia. Armed with a degree from London School of Economics, Husain first worked in a start-up in Silicon…
f: Safeena Husain has worked extensively with rural and urban underserved communities in South America, Africa and Asia. Armed with a degree from London School of Economics, Husain first worked in a start-up in Silicon Valley, USA. She soon switched gears to lead a US-based non-profit organization for seven years. In 2004, she returned to India to take on an issue close to her heart and launched Educate Girls in 2007. She has shepherded the organization through dramatic growth since then to bring back over 2 million out-of-school girls across more than 30,000 villages. In 2025, Educate Girls became the first Indian organization to win the Ramon Magsaysay Award.

b: Safir Anand is the author of Chrysalis and the creative genius behind many leading brands in India proffering inputs on brand strategy, business models, marketing and commercial insights, blended with an astute mastery…
f: Safir Anand is the author of Chrysalis and the creative genius behind many leading brands in India proffering inputs on brand strategy, business models, marketing and commercial insights, blended with an astute mastery of IP Law. His career of over 25 years reconnoitred multiple facets of monetization with his sagacity, adding to accruing diverse recognitions on numerous global platforms. Accredited as India’s Top Attorney, Safir Anand is the Senior Partner & Head of Trademarks, Contractual & Commercial IP at Anand & Anand.

b: Sagarika Ghose is a senior journalist and author. She is currently Consulting Editor at the Times Of India . She joined journalism in 1991 and has been a journalist and media personality for over 25 years. She started…
f: Sagarika Ghose is a senior journalist and author. She is currently Consulting Editor at the Times Of India . She joined journalism in 1991 and has been a journalist and media personality for over 25 years. She started her career at the Times Of India , was part of the startup team of Outlook magazine and went on to work for The Indian Express . She was deputy editor and prime time news anchor on the news network CNN IBN. She is also the author of the novels The Gin Drinkers and Blind Faith , both published worldwide, and the recently published bestselling biography, Indira, India’s Most Powerful Prime Minister . Ghose is a Rhodes Scholar and completed her postgraduate studies in Modern History from Oxford University.

b: Saharu Nusaiba Kannanari is a writer based out of Kerala. His first novel, Chronicle of an Hour and a Half , published earlier this year won the Crossword Book Award and the Atta Galatta Bangalore Literature Festival…
f: Saharu Nusaiba Kannanari is a writer based out of Kerala. His first novel, Chronicle of an Hour and a Half , published earlier this year won the Crossword Book Award and the Atta Galatta Bangalore Literature Festival Book Prize in the fiction category. The book was also shortlisted for the JCB Prize for Literature and Godrej-Mumbai Lit Live! Literary Award. His next book, The Menon Investigation , is scheduled for publication in 2025.

b: Sahiba Bali has captivated audiences as a presenter for the IPL and the World Cup, conducting insightful interviews with cricket legends. She is the host of Shark Tank Season 4 and has acted alongside Diljit Dosanjh in…
f: Sahiba Bali has captivated audiences as a presenter for the IPL and the World Cup, conducting insightful interviews with cricket legends. She is the host of Shark Tank Season 4 and has acted alongside Diljit Dosanjh in the acclaimed film Chamkila , as well as in Laila Majnu , the Netflix original Bard of Blood , and Tannav . Recognized in the “30 Under 30” for her work in marketing, she has held roles at Zomato and Unacademy, earned degrees in Economics and Marketing from Delhi University and Oxford University, and completed marketing masterclasses at ISB and IIMs.

b: Saif Mahmood is the author of the recent bestseller Beloved Delhi: A Mughal City and Her Greatest Poets. He is a poetry and literature critic, commentator, translator and rights activist. An advocate of the Supreme…
f: Saif Mahmood is the author of the recent bestseller Beloved Delhi: A Mughal City and Her Greatest Poets. He is a poetry and literature critic, commentator, translator and rights activist. An advocate of the Supreme Court of India, holding a doctorate in Constitutional Law in South Asia, he frequently appears before superior courts in India as well as in international and domestic tribunals. Founder of South Asian Alliance for Literature, Art & Culture, Dr. Mahmood’s works have appeared in various prestigious publications and his English translations of Urdu poets have received critical acclaim.

b: Saikrishna Prakash is the James Monroe Professor of Law at the University of Virginia. His new book, The Presidential Pardon , will be published by Harvard University Press in January 2026. His earlier book, The Living…
f: Saikrishna Prakash is the James Monroe Professor of Law at the University of Virginia. His new book, The Presidential Pardon , will be published by Harvard University Press in January 2026. His earlier book, The Living Presidency , offers a critique of the modern presidency. Prakash is a graduate of Stanford University and Yale Law School.

b: Sajeev Kumarapuram is Design Editor at The Times of India . After editorial stints at publications including The Miami Herald and translating Yellow Lights of Death , he made a rare and risky shift to the world of…
f: Sajeev Kumarapuram is Design Editor at The Times of India . After editorial stints at publications including The Miami Herald and translating Yellow Lights of Death , he made a rare and risky shift to the world of infographics and illustrations. Over a decade on, there hasn’t been a single day of regret.

b: Author and bureaucrat Sajjan Yadav is an officer of the Indian Administrative Service (IAS) 1995 batch. His last book, titled India’s Vaccine Growth Story: From Cowpox to Vaccine Maitri , is a national bestseller,…
f: Author and bureaucrat Sajjan Yadav is an officer of the Indian Administrative Service (IAS) 1995 batch. His last book, titled India’s Vaccine Growth Story: From Cowpox to Vaccine Maitri , is a national bestseller, translated and published in Spanish and sixteen Indian languages. Presently he is Additional Secretary in the Ministry of Finance, Government of India. He holds a doctorate from the prestigious London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine.

b: Sajjid Z. Chinoy is Managing Director and Chief India Economist at J.P. Morgan. Dr. Chinoy also serves as a member of the Prime Minister’s Economic Advisory Council. He was a member of the 15th Finance Commission’s…
f: Sajjid Z. Chinoy is Managing Director and Chief India Economist at J.P. Morgan. Dr. Chinoy also serves as a member of the Prime Minister’s Economic Advisory Council. He was a member of the 15th Finance Commission’s Advisory Council, and has served on several committees instituted by the Reserve Bank of India. He has previously worked at the International Monetary Fund and McKinsey & Company. He received his PhD In economics from Stanford University.

b: Saket Suman is a writer, journalist and literary chronicler. He is the author of The Psychology of a Patriot . As a journalist, he has worked at The Statesman , Indo Asian News Service (IANS) and Times Group, besides…
f: Saket Suman is a writer, journalist and literary chronicler. He is the author of The Psychology of a Patriot . As a journalist, he has worked at The Statesman , Indo Asian News Service (IANS) and Times Group, besides being published extensively on popular culture, politics and human rights in reputed newspapers, magazines and news portals

b: Saksham Garg , bestselling author of Samsara , and former Penguin editor, leads a literary agency that champions emerging voices in experimental formats. Passionate about innovative marketing strategies, he and his…
f: Saksham Garg , bestselling author of Samsara , and former Penguin editor, leads a literary agency that champions emerging voices in experimental formats. Passionate about innovative marketing strategies, he and his authors consistently work to expand readership in new ways, efforts that regularly place them on Nielsen charts, as well as Amazon’s overall Top 100.

b: Salil Misra is a historian of modern India, currently at the Ambedkar University Delhi. His publications include the monograph A Narrative of Communal Politics: Uttar Pradesh, 1937-39 and a small booklet in Hindi on the…
f: Salil Misra is a historian of modern India, currently at the Ambedkar University Delhi. His publications include the monograph A Narrative of Communal Politics: Uttar Pradesh, 1937-39 and a small booklet in Hindi on the Swaraj Party. He has also published articles on themes related to communal politics, language questions, Hindi and Urdu, partition of India, social science teaching and identity politics.

b: Salil Tripathi is the author of Offence: The Hindu Case , The Colonel Who Would Not Repent , and Detours: Songs of the Open Road . His next book is about the Gujaratis. He chairs PEN International’s Writers in Prison…
f: Salil Tripathi is the author of Offence: The Hindu Case , The Colonel Who Would Not Repent , and Detours: Songs of the Open Road . His next book is about the Gujaratis. He chairs PEN International’s Writers in Prison Committee. Born in Bombay, he studied in the United States, and has been a correspondent in India and Singapore. He lives in London and writes for Mint and Caravan .

b: Salma is a well-known name to readers of contemporary Tamil literature. With two volumes of poetry collections, a short story collection and two novels, several of which have been translated into several languages, she…
f: Salma is a well-known name to readers of contemporary Tamil literature. With two volumes of poetry collections, a short story collection and two novels, several of which have been translated into several languages, she has made her mark as a distinctive literary voice. Lakshmi Holmstrom’s English translation of her novel The Hour Past Midnight was shortlisted for the Crossword Book Prize and longlisted for Man Asian prize DSC Award. Her second novel Manaamiyangal and short story collection Saabam are forthcoming. She is the recipient of several awards and honours. Salma has also served as a public servant. She was the elected President of the Ponnampatti Panchayat from 2001-2006. She also served as the Chairman of the Social Welfare Board in Tamil Nadu during which time she was instrumental in establishing several welfare schemes, including those related to the state’s transgender community.

b: Sam Kiley is the author of Desperate Glory , an account of a six-month of war in Helmand and an Economist ‘Book of the Year’. He has contributed essays and articles to several anthologies among them ‘Eating Mud…
f: Sam Kiley is the author of Desperate Glory , an account of a six-month of war in Helmand and an Economist ‘Book of the Year’. He has contributed essays and articles to several anthologies among them ‘Eating Mud Crabs in Kandahar’. Kiley has overed conflicts in Africa, Europe, the Middle East and Asia for more than 25 years and is a Senior International Correspondent at CNN.

b: Sam Leith is the literary editor of The Spectator and the author of The Haunted Wood: A History of Childhood Reading. His previous books include You Talkin' To Me? Rhetoric from Aristotle to Trump... And Beyond and…
f: Sam Leith is the literary editor of The Spectator and the author of The Haunted Wood: A History of Childhood Reading. His previous books include You Talkin' To Me? Rhetoric from Aristotle to Trump... And Beyond and Write to the Point: How to be Clear, Correct and Persuasive on the Page .

b: Journalist Sam McBride writes for the Belfast Telegraph, Sunday Independent and The Economist . His first book, Burned: The Inside Story of the ‘Cash-for-Ash’ Scandal and Northern Ireland’s Secretive New Elite , was a…
f: Journalist Sam McBride writes for the Belfast Telegraph, Sunday Independent and The Economist . His first book, Burned: The Inside Story of the ‘Cash-for-Ash’ Scandal and Northern Ireland’s Secretive New Elite , was a Sunday Times UK bestseller. His second, For and Against a United Ireland , co-written with Fintan O’Toole, was published in October 2025.

b: Sam Miller was born and brought up in London but has spent much of the last 25 years in India. He has worked for the BBC as a reporter and editor and as Country Director for the organisation’s development arm, BBC…
f: Sam Miller was born and brought up in London but has spent much of the last 25 years in India. He has worked for the BBC as a reporter and editor and as Country Director for the organisation’s development arm, BBC Media Action. He continues to work, on and off, for the BBC. He is the author of Delhi: Adventures in a Megacity and A Strange Kind of Paradise: India Through Foreign Eyes . He was the translator of the first English-language version of Alfred Assollant’s Once Upon a Time in India: The Marvellous Adventures of Captain Corcoran . His most recent book is Fathers .

b: Sam Mills is a British guitarist, composer and producer known for his work with British experimental group 23 Skidoo as well as Bengali singer Paban Das Baul and Susheela Raman with whom he has worked closely for two…
f: Sam Mills is a British guitarist, composer and producer known for his work with British experimental group 23 Skidoo as well as Bengali singer Paban Das Baul and Susheela Raman with whom he has worked closely for two decades, producing her eight albums and co-directing acclaimed collaborations with musicians from many traditions such as Qawwali and Javanese Gamelan.

b: Sam Santhosh is an entrepreneur. He made his mark by setting up California Software Co Ltd (Calsoft) and taking it public in India. He has led the Genomic revolution in India by incubating and launching multiple…
f: Sam Santhosh is an entrepreneur. He made his mark by setting up California Software Co Ltd (Calsoft) and taking it public in India. He has led the Genomic revolution in India by incubating and launching multiple companies leveraging Next Generation Sequencing (NGS) and Bioinformatics, through his incubator SciGenom Labs in Kochi and San Francisco. He established MedGenome as the leading genomic diagnostics and research company and he is often called the 'Genome man of India'. Santosh established SciGenom Research Foundation (SGRF), a non-profit Trust in 2011.

b: Samanth Subramanian is an award-winning journalist whose work has appeared in The New Yorker, The New York Times Magazine, BusinessWeek, Granta, WIRED and Harper's . His most recent book, A Dominant Character , is a…
f: Samanth Subramanian is an award-winning journalist whose work has appeared in The New Yorker, The New York Times Magazine, BusinessWeek, Granta, WIRED and Harper's . His most recent book, A Dominant Character , is a biography of the scientist and Communist JBS Haldane. His first book, Following Fish: Travels Around the Indian Coast , won the Shakti Bhatt First Book Prize in 2010 and was shortlisted for the Andre Simon Award in 2013. His second book, This Divided Island: Stories from the Sri Lankan War , won the 2015 Crossword Prize for Non Fiction and was shortlisted for the Samuel Johnson Non Fiction Prize and the Royal Society of Literature's Ondaatje Prize the same year.

b: Sameer Mahale currently oversees the complete sales portfolio for Penguin in India, bringing 22 years of experience in general trade publishing. He joined Penguin in 2017 as General Manager of Sales, managing children’s…
f: Sameer Mahale currently oversees the complete sales portfolio for Penguin in India, bringing 22 years of experience in general trade publishing. He joined Penguin in 2017 as General Manager of Sales, managing children’s sales, custom publishing, DK sales, and the North India region, and later headed the Online Sales Team in 2021. Offering a 360-degree publishing perspective, Sameer leads sales and manages the Penguin Enterprise division. He has been instrumental in driving eCommerce growth and is recognized as an industry expert. Sameer also teaches courses on the Indian publishing landscape and sales and distribution strategy at the National Book Trust.

b: Samhita Arni is the author of The Mahabharata: A Child’s View , New York Times bestselling graphic novel Sita’s Ramayana and The Missing Queen . Arni was a screenwriter on the feature film Good Morning Karachi and…
f: Samhita Arni is the author of The Mahabharata: A Child’s View , New York Times bestselling graphic novel Sita’s Ramayana and The Missing Queen . Arni was a screenwriter on the feature film Good Morning Karachi and the head scriptwriter on The Defenders , a TV show in Kabul, Afghanistan. She writes regularly for The Hindu .

b: Samir Saran is the President of the Observer Research Foundation, one of Asia’s most influential think tanks. He writes frequently on India's foreign policy, and issues of global governance, climate change, energy…
f: Samir Saran is the President of the Observer Research Foundation, one of Asia’s most influential think tanks. He writes frequently on India's foreign policy, and issues of global governance, climate change, energy policy, global development architecture, artificial intelligence, cyber security and internet governance. Dr. Saran is the author of four books, numerous academic papers and is featured regularly in Indian and international print and broadcast media. He curates the Raisina Dialogue, India’s flagship platform on geopolitics and geo-economics, and chairs CyFy, India’s annual conference on technology, security and society.

b: Samira Shackle is a freelance British-Pakistani writer and reporter based in London. She is the editor of the New Humanist magazine and a regular contributor to the Guardian Long Read. Her first book, Karachi Vice ,…
f: Samira Shackle is a freelance British-Pakistani writer and reporter based in London. She is the editor of the New Humanist magazine and a regular contributor to the Guardian Long Read. Her first book, Karachi Vice , tells the story of five ordinary citizens of Pakistan's largest city.

b: Samit Basu ’s most recent book, Chosen Spirits, a near-future anti-dystopian Delhi novel, was shortlisted for the JCB Prize for Literature, and is out in North America as The City Inside from Tordotcom in June 2022.…
f: Samit Basu ’s most recent book, Chosen Spirits, a near-future anti-dystopian Delhi novel, was shortlisted for the JCB Prize for Literature, and is out in North America as The City Inside from Tordotcom in June 2022. He is the author of several novels, the co-writer/director of a Netflix film, a comics writer and children's writer.

b: Sampat Saral is a Hindi satirist and currently the only name after Sharad Joshi and K.P. Saxena, who writes humorous prose in Kavisammelan and Mushayara. Saral exposes the social, cultural and political inconsistencies…
f: Sampat Saral is a Hindi satirist and currently the only name after Sharad Joshi and K.P. Saxena, who writes humorous prose in Kavisammelan and Mushayara. Saral exposes the social, cultural and political inconsistencies through sharp satire that is conceptual and objective. He writes in Hindi and Rajasthani. His two books are Chaki Dekh Chunav Ki and Chhadmvibhushan .

b: Sampurna Chattarji is the author of 14 books including the poetry book Absent Muses , the children’s book The Fried Frog and Other Funny Freaky Foodie Feisty Poem s, the novels Rupture and Land of the Well as well as…
f: Sampurna Chattarji is the author of 14 books including the poetry book Absent Muses , the children’s book The Fried Frog and Other Funny Freaky Foodie Feisty Poem s, the novels Rupture and Land of the Well as well as a collection of short stories about Mumbai titled Dirty Love. Chattarji is the editor of the anthology Sweeping the Front Yard , which brings together poetry and prose by women writing in English, Malayalam, Telugu and Urdu. Her 2004 translation of Sukumar Ray’s poetry and prose has been a Puffin Classic since 2008, under the title Wordygurdyboom! . Her translation of the Selected Poems of Joy Goswami was shortlisted for the inaugural Khushwant Singh Memorial Prize for Poetry. Chattarji was the 2012 Charles Wallace writer-in-residence at the University of Kent where she wrote her latest poetry book, Space Gulliver: Chronicles of an Alien .

b: Sanah Ahsan is an award-winning poet, liberation psychologist and educator. Their work includes delivering a TED Talk, writing for The Guardian, and presenting a Channel 4 documentary. Ahsan is working on a non-fiction…
f: Sanah Ahsan is an award-winning poet, liberation psychologist and educator. Their work includes delivering a TED Talk, writing for The Guardian, and presenting a Channel 4 documentary. Ahsan is working on a non-fiction book about liberation psychology and embracing madness. Their debut poetry collection is forthcoming with Bloomsbury in 2024/25.

b: Sanchaita Gajapati is the Founder Trustee of SANA, a non-profit that uses technology to provide safe drinking water, sanitation and renewable energy to underserved communities. Winner of the Google Impact Challenge and…
f: Sanchaita Gajapati is the Founder Trustee of SANA, a non-profit that uses technology to provide safe drinking water, sanitation and renewable energy to underserved communities. Winner of the Google Impact Challenge and supported by Oracle, SANA’s foot print is in over 40 sites in Andhra Pradesh and Delhi. Gajapati champions the cause of recycled water and set up a Toilet to Tap initiative converting sewage waste into safe drinking water in association with Delhi Jal Board. In association with Cornell University, she is setting up a pilot project, demonstrating the future of farming and sustainable water management in urban and rural areas. She has recently joined mainstream politics as a member of the BJP and has been appointed as a National Executive Member of the BJYM and a media panellist.

b: Sandeep Dahisarkar is an independent archaeologist, art historian, and one of the youngest authors on Mumbai’s history, publishing three consecutive books in 2022–2024, with a fourth on artist Rao Bahadur M. V.…
f: Sandeep Dahisarkar is an independent archaeologist, art historian, and one of the youngest authors on Mumbai’s history, publishing three consecutive books in 2022–2024, with a fourth on artist Rao Bahadur M. V. Dhurandhar set for 2025. With over a decade of research experience, he has taught at Sathaye College and as visiting faculty at Sophia College and IES College of Architecture. He has delivered 28+ lectures, conducted heritage walks, and presented at national and international conferences. Recognized with the Sane Guruji Yuva Puraskar (2022) and Yuva Sanman Puraskar (2023), he has also served as cultural consultant to the royal family of Indore.

b: Sandeep Jauhar has written three books, all published by Farrar, Straus, and Giroux. A practising cardiologist, he is also a frequent contributor to the Opinion section of The New York Times. Jauhar has appeared…
f: Sandeep Jauhar has written three books, all published by Farrar, Straus, and Giroux. A practising cardiologist, he is also a frequent contributor to the Opinion section of The New York Times. Jauhar has appeared frequently on National Public Radio, CNN and MSNBC to discuss issues related to medicine, and his essays have been published in The Wall Street Journal, Time, and Slate .

b: Sandeep Purohit is the Editor of Rajasthan Patrika , Jodhpur. His journalistic career spans 23 years and includes print, TV and digital media experience. He has also been the Editor of the Patrika's Udaipur edition,…
f: Sandeep Purohit is the Editor of Rajasthan Patrika , Jodhpur. His journalistic career spans 23 years and includes print, TV and digital media experience. He has also been the Editor of the Patrika's Udaipur edition, prior to which he was the Editor of Daily News , Jaipur. In his noted column, Nigahbaan, Dr Purohit writes on current issues and politics.

b: Sandeep Sethi is Director (Education) MSMSII Museum Trust, Jaipur. An alumnus of Narsee Monjee, Sethi is an educationist to the core and a firm believer of experiential pedagogies. He thinks out of the box and believes…
f: Sandeep Sethi is Director (Education) MSMSII Museum Trust, Jaipur. An alumnus of Narsee Monjee, Sethi is an educationist to the core and a firm believer of experiential pedagogies. He thinks out of the box and believes in making education fun by experimenting, evolving, collaborating and sharing experiences. Sethi pioneered educating through theatre and developed the pedagogy of studies through graphic novels at the Jaipur History Festival

b: Sandhya Gokhale is a multifaceted civil rights attorney, filmmaker, and advocate blending law, art, and activism. Known for her powerful women-centric narratives, she has authored eight feature film scripts, including…
f: Sandhya Gokhale is a multifaceted civil rights attorney, filmmaker, and advocate blending law, art, and activism. Known for her powerful women-centric narratives, she has authored eight feature film scripts, including Paheli —India's official entry to the 2006 Oscars. Gokhale directed Bhinna Shadja , a documentary celebrating Kishori Amonkar, which she considers her most significant work. Alongside her husband, Amol Palekar, she champions collective action for social change.

b: Sandip Roy is a writer, columnist and podcaster living in Kolkata. He is a columnist for Mint Lounge and the Hindu , and the host of the Sandip Roy Show on Indian Express . His weekly audio dispatches from Kolkata have…
f: Sandip Roy is a writer, columnist and podcaster living in Kolkata. He is a columnist for Mint Lounge and the Hindu , and the host of the Sandip Roy Show on Indian Express . His weekly audio dispatches from Kolkata have been airing on public radio KALW in San Francisco since 2012. His work has appeared in the New York Times , the San Francisco Chronicle , the Times of India , Firstpost , Huffington Post , Condé Nast Traveller , BBC and NPR, among others. He has been part of numerous anthologies and served as the editor of Trikone , the world’s oldest magazine on LGBTQ+ South Asian issues. His first novel is Don’t Let Him Know .

b: Sangeeta Gupta is a poet, artist and filmmaker. A number of her works have been translated into other languages. Antas Se , Samundra Se Lautati Nadi and Iss Par Uss Par have been translated into Bangla. Her collection…
f: Sangeeta Gupta is a poet, artist and filmmaker. A number of her works have been translated into other languages. Antas Se , Samundra Se Lautati Nadi and Iss Par Uss Par have been translated into Bangla. Her collection of poems Pratinaad was translated into Bangla, English and German. Weaves of Time is a collection of English poetry and was translated in Greek while Sparsh Ke Gulmohar , a collection of Hindi poems, were translated into Dogri. Her other works include Nagfani Ke Jungle , a collection of short stories, Ladakh: Knowing the Unknown , a collection of poems in English and photography and the anthologies Song of Silence and Beparwah Ruh . Her book Lekhak ka Samay is a compilation of interviews of eminent women writers in Hindi. She is also an artist with 32 solo exhibitions to her credit. She has also directed seven documentary films.

b: Sanghamitra Chakraborty is a journalist and editor. In a career spanning thirty years, she has been the editor of India Today Group magazines Reader’s Digest , Prevention and Women’s Health , and worked at several other…
f: Sanghamitra Chakraborty is a journalist and editor. In a career spanning thirty years, she has been the editor of India Today Group magazines Reader’s Digest , Prevention and Women’s Health , and worked at several other leading publications at the start of her career, including the Times of India , Outlook , the Statesman and Sunday, writing on cinema, gender, health and environment, apart from news reporting. She lives and works in New Delhi.

b: Sanjana Nanodkar works with Anugraha, a Mumbai-based publication design studio as a Graphic Designer, Photographer and Content Developer. She holds a degree in Applied Art from Sir J.J. Institute of Applied Art, Mumbai…
f: Sanjana Nanodkar works with Anugraha, a Mumbai-based publication design studio as a Graphic Designer, Photographer and Content Developer. She holds a degree in Applied Art from Sir J.J. Institute of Applied Art, Mumbai and a MA in Graphic Design from London College of Communication, London. She has worked as a Design Associate at the National Institute of Design, Ahmedabad on government projects and as an independent designer with the Indian Air Force. Her eagerness to explore the medium of films led her to work on two short fiction films at NID as a Production Manager and a documentary film for The Story of Light Festival, Goa 2015. She has also co-curated the Film Program for The Story Of Space Festival Goa, 2017 that had over 850 entries from across the globe.

b: Sanjay Jha serves as the Executive Director of Dale Carnegie and is a former National Spokesperson for Congress. He is the author of the bestselling book The Great Unravelling: India after 2014 and has written The…
f: Sanjay Jha serves as the Executive Director of Dale Carnegie and is a former National Spokesperson for Congress. He is the author of the bestselling book The Great Unravelling: India after 2014 and has written The Superstar Syndrome, co-authored with Dr. Myra White, and My Illegitimate Son: A True Story . His background includes working with international asset management companies and foreign banks. He is also the Co-Founder of CricketNext.com

b: Lt Gen Sanjay Kumar Jha, a highly decorated soldier, was commissioned into the 17th Battalion of the Sikh Regiment on December 13, 1980, and was the Colonel of the Sikh Regiment. He was also the Commandant of the…
f: Lt Gen Sanjay Kumar Jha, a highly decorated soldier, was commissioned into the 17th Battalion of the Sikh Regiment on December 13, 1980, and was the Colonel of the Sikh Regiment. He was also the Commandant of the prestigious Indian Military Academy, Dehradun, before retiring in January 2020. Lt Gen SK Jha has held appointments at Indian Military Academy, Indian Military Training Team (Bhutan) and Army War College and served as Deputy Commander and Chief of Staff of an Infantry Brigade in the United Nations Mission at Congo.

b: Sanjeeb Mukherjea is an independent journalist and presenter who has spent over a decade closely following Indian sport. A former cricket editor with CNN IBN, he has been equally prolific with his in-depth reportage and…
f: Sanjeeb Mukherjea is an independent journalist and presenter who has spent over a decade closely following Indian sport. A former cricket editor with CNN IBN, he has been equally prolific with his in-depth reportage and presentations with a special focus on the intersection of sport and corruption.

b: Dr Sanjeev Chopra is the Festival Director of VoW, as well as a Senior Fellow at the Prime Minister’s Memorial and a Trustee of the Lal Bahadur Shastri Memorial. He serves on various academic councils. His recent books…
f: Dr Sanjeev Chopra is the Festival Director of VoW, as well as a Senior Fellow at the Prime Minister’s Memorial and a Trustee of the Lal Bahadur Shastri Memorial. He serves on various academic councils. His recent books include The Great Conciliator: Lal Bahadur Shastri and the Transformation of India, and We the People of the States of Bharat: The Making and Remaking of India's Internal Boundaries.

b: Sanjeev Jha is the Director for Kindle Content, India at Amazon. He is a global leader for e-commerce and consumer goods and helped shape several Fortune 100 companies and consulting firms such as Perfetti, PepsiCo,…
f: Sanjeev Jha is the Director for Kindle Content, India at Amazon. He is a global leader for e-commerce and consumer goods and helped shape several Fortune 100 companies and consulting firms such as Perfetti, PepsiCo, Sears, Motorola and McKinsey before joining Amazon.

b: Sanjeev Paliwal is considered to be one of the pioneering Hindi TV journalists. He has been in the industry for 30 years and has worked with many prestigious Hindi newspapers such as Dainik Jagran, Amar Ujala and Aaj as…
f: Sanjeev Paliwal is considered to be one of the pioneering Hindi TV journalists. He has been in the industry for 30 years and has worked with many prestigious Hindi newspapers such as Dainik Jagran, Amar Ujala and Aaj as well as leading channels like Doordarshan, BITV, IBN7/News18 and TV Today. He currently works at Aaj Tak as a senior executive editor. Naina is his first novel in Hindi.

b: Sanjeev Sanyal is currently a member of the Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister (EAC-PM). He was the Principal Economic Adviser to the Finance Minister for five years till February 2022 and the Co-Chair of…
f: Sanjeev Sanyal is currently a member of the Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister (EAC-PM). He was the Principal Economic Adviser to the Finance Minister for five years till February 2022 and the Co-Chair of the G20’s Framework Working Group. Sanyal was awarded the Eisenhower Fellowship in 2007 for his work on urban dynamics. In 2010, he was named a Young Global Leader by the World Economic Forum in Davos. He is the author of several best-selling books, including Land of the Seven Rivers, The Ocean of Churn, India in the Age of Ideas, and the Indian Renaissance . Sanyal has also published over two hundred articles and columns in leading national and international publications.

b: Sanjiv Chadha , Managing Director and CEO of Bank of Baroda has over 35 years’ experience in banking and financial services. He is Chairman on the boards of Bank of Baroda (UK) Ltd., IndiaFirst Life Insurance Co.…
f: Sanjiv Chadha , Managing Director and CEO of Bank of Baroda has over 35 years’ experience in banking and financial services. He is Chairman on the boards of Bank of Baroda (UK) Ltd., IndiaFirst Life Insurance Co. Ltd., BOB Capital Markets Ltd. and BOB Financial Solutions Ltd. He also serves on the board of National Insurance Co. Ltd and is on the Governing Board of National Institute of Bank Management (NIBM).

b: Sanjiv Saraf is an entrepreneur, investor and mentor. He set up Rekhta Foundation, which hosts the world’s largest and most popular resource for the Urdu language and literature. He is a recipient of several awards…
f: Sanjiv Saraf is an entrepreneur, investor and mentor. He set up Rekhta Foundation, which hosts the world’s largest and most popular resource for the Urdu language and literature. He is a recipient of several awards and honours, including the distinguished Doctor of Letters (D. Litt.) degree by Maulana Azad National Urdu University and the National Sir Syed Excellence Award 2018 by Aligarh Muslim University for his contribution to the cause of preserving and promoting Urdu.

b: Sanjna Kapoor is co-founder of Junoon, a social enterprise that aims to create platforms for theatre in India. She is responsible for having brought to Indian audiences some of the finest of world and Indian theatre,…
f: Sanjna Kapoor is co-founder of Junoon, a social enterprise that aims to create platforms for theatre in India. She is responsible for having brought to Indian audiences some of the finest of world and Indian theatre, being the first to introduce a touring theatre festival into the Indian scene. She currently spearheads Junoon’s school programme and continues the legacy of both the Kapoors and the Kendals to take theatre to people across the country. Her current focus is working towards an all-India theatre alliance, based on a practical sharing of resources and ideas as well as consolidating and strengthening theatre practice in India. She is a core team member and facilitator of SMART (Strategic Management in the Art of Theatre) India.

b: Sanket Mhatre was the chief assistant director of Kavyotsav 2001, the first bilingual poetry reading festival of Marathi and Kannada poets. His title song for the daily soap Radha Hi Bawari was awarded the best song at…
f: Sanket Mhatre was the chief assistant director of Kavyotsav 2001, the first bilingual poetry reading festival of Marathi and Kannada poets. His title song for the daily soap Radha Hi Bawari was awarded the best song at ZEE Alpha Gaurav. Crossover Poems is his brainchild that unifies poets from multiple languages embracing sensibilities unique to every language. He is also the film director of Kavita Cafe . Mhatre has performed at multiple festivals both in India and abroad.

b: Sanket Upadhyay has been a print and broadcast journalist for 18 years and has worked with HT Jaipur . With NDTV as his first TV job, Sanket moved to Times Now, India Today, CNN News 18 and then back to NDTV in a second…
f: Sanket Upadhyay has been a print and broadcast journalist for 18 years and has worked with HT Jaipur . With NDTV as his first TV job, Sanket moved to Times Now, India Today, CNN News 18 and then back to NDTV in a second stint. He specialises in political reportage and hosts popular prime time shows on NDTV 24x7 and NDTV India.

b: Santanu Das is Professor of Modern Literature and Culture and Senior Research Fellow at All Souls College, University of Oxford. His latest book India, Empire and First World War Culture: Writings, Images, Songs ,…
f: Santanu Das is Professor of Modern Literature and Culture and Senior Research Fellow at All Souls College, University of Oxford. His latest book India, Empire and First World War Culture: Writings, Images, Songs , published with Cambridge University Press, won the Hindu Non-Fiction Prize, the ESSE Book Award, and the Coomaraswamy Award in the US in 2020. He is currently writing on the sea and editing the Oxford Book of Empire and War .

b: Santiago Iñiguez de Onzoño is the President of IE University and is a global influencer in higher education. A former Dean of IE Business School, he was named ‘Dean of the Year’ by Poets & Quants . Author of several…
f: Santiago Iñiguez de Onzoño is the President of IE University and is a global influencer in higher education. A former Dean of IE Business School, he was named ‘Dean of the Year’ by Poets & Quants . Author of several books on management and education, his latest is Philosophy Inc.

b: Santiago Roncagliolo (Lima, 1975) explores the darkest moments of Latin American history, through thriller and noir novels. Red April (Grove Atlantic) won the Alfaguara Prize and Independent Prize for Foreign Fiction.…
f: Santiago Roncagliolo (Lima, 1975) explores the darkest moments of Latin American history, through thriller and noir novels. Red April (Grove Atlantic) won the Alfaguara Prize and Independent Prize for Foreign Fiction. Pudor and La Pena Máxima have been adapted into motion pictures. Y Líbranos del Mal stood for a year in Peruvian best seller lists. He also writes screenplays for cinema and serials, often based on books.

b: Santosh Desai is an author, columnist, and brand strategist. He is best known for his insightful books on Indian culture, including Mother Pious Lady and Memes for Mummyji. Beyond his writing, he serves as a brand…
f: Santosh Desai is an author, columnist, and brand strategist. He is best known for his insightful books on Indian culture, including Mother Pious Lady and Memes for Mummyji. Beyond his writing, he serves as a brand consultant and Co-founder of Think9 Consumer Technologies.

b: Santosh Kumar Das’ works are in the The Art Institute of Chicago, Oberlin Museum, Ethnic Art Foundation, USA, Mary C Lanius Collection, Denver and Devi Art Foundation, Delhi. His best-known work is the Gujarat Series.…
f: Santosh Kumar Das’ works are in the The Art Institute of Chicago, Oberlin Museum, Ethnic Art Foundation, USA, Mary C Lanius Collection, Denver and Devi Art Foundation, Delhi. His best-known work is the Gujarat Series. In 2017, Tara Books published, ‘Black,’ his autobiographical style book. In 2019 he had his first solo show in India, titled Rerouted Realities, curated by Kathryn Myers.

b: Santosh Kumar Gupta , an alumnus of The Doon School and the NDA, was commissioned into the Indian Navy in 1958, specialising in naval aviation. Serving aboard INS Vikrant for 13 years, he earned gallantry awards during…
f: Santosh Kumar Gupta , an alumnus of The Doon School and the NDA, was commissioned into the Indian Navy in 1958, specialising in naval aviation. Serving aboard INS Vikrant for 13 years, he earned gallantry awards during the 1971 Indo-Pak War, commanding Sea Hawks strike force. Gupta later commanded ships, including INS Vikrant, retiring as Rear Admiral in Dec 1990.

b: Sara Rai is a writer and literary translator. She has published three collections of stories and a novel in Hindi. The German translation by Johanna Hahn of her selected short fiction, Im Labyrinth, won the Coburg…
f: Sara Rai is a writer and literary translator. She has published three collections of stories and a novel in Hindi. The German translation by Johanna Hahn of her selected short fiction, Im Labyrinth, won the Coburg Rückert Prize 2019. Her most recent work of translation (with Arvind Krishna Mehrotra) is of Vinod Kumar Shukla’s Blue is Like Blue . She is currently working on a volume of stories in Hindi and a memoir in English.

b: Sarah J. Maas is the #1 New York Times and internationally bestselling author of the Throne of Glass, Court of Thorns and Roses and Crescent City series. Her books have sold more than 13 million copies and are published…
f: Sarah J. Maas is the #1 New York Times and internationally bestselling author of the Throne of Glass, Court of Thorns and Roses and Crescent City series. Her books have sold more than 13 million copies and are published in 37 languages.

b: Sarah Jacob is a journalist and Senior Editor at NDTV 24×7. She is the anchor of We the People, one of NDTV’s flagship primetime shows. Previously, Jacob was the US correspondent for NDTV and covered both the 2008…
f: Sarah Jacob is a journalist and Senior Editor at NDTV 24×7. She is the anchor of We the People, one of NDTV’s flagship primetime shows. Previously, Jacob was the US correspondent for NDTV and covered both the 2008 and 2012 Presidential elections. Sarah has reported extensively on health and the environment and as part of a series titled Save India’s Coast, she has travelled India’s entire coastline reporting on the environmental destruction taking place along it. Jacob graduated on a full scholarship from New York University with a Master’s degree in Broadcast and Documentary Journalism.

b: Sarah Parcak is Professor of Anthropology at the University of Alabama and President of Globalxplorer. She co-Directs the Joint Archaeological Mission to Lisht with Egypt’s Ministry of Antiquities. She is the author…
f: Sarah Parcak is Professor of Anthropology at the University of Alabama and President of Globalxplorer. She co-Directs the Joint Archaeological Mission to Lisht with Egypt’s Ministry of Antiquities. She is the author of Archaeology From Space: How the Future Shapes Our Past and winner of the 2016 TED Prize.

b: Sarah Raven ’s gardening and cookery books have won her a number of awards including Best Specialist Gardening Book for The Cutting Garden and Cookery Book of the Year for Sarah Raven’s Garden Cookbook . Her other…
f: Sarah Raven ’s gardening and cookery books have won her a number of awards including Best Specialist Gardening Book for The Cutting Garden and Cookery Book of the Year for Sarah Raven’s Garden Cookbook . Her other titles include Vita Sackville-West’s Sissinghurst – The Creation of a Garden , Food for Friends and Family and Complete Christmas . Raven latest book is Good Good Food , which explores healthy eating through combining her medical training as a GP with her love for growing and cooking food. Raven has written for The Saturday Telegraph , Country Living , Gardens Illustrated , Gardeners’ World Magazine , The English Garden and Sainsbury’s Magazine among others. She has also presented on BBC’s Gardeners’ World and an episode of Great British Garden Revival series.

b: Saranya Subramanian is a poet, writer, and founder of The Bombay Poetry Crawl. An MFA in Writing graduate from the University of San Francisco, her work has appeared in Frontline , Lit Hub , The Bombay Literary Magazine…
f: Saranya Subramanian is a poet, writer, and founder of The Bombay Poetry Crawl. An MFA in Writing graduate from the University of San Francisco, her work has appeared in Frontline , Lit Hub , The Bombay Literary Magazine , The Caravan , Madras Courier , South Asian Avant Garde , Outlook , Vayavya , Kitaab , Scroll , the Yearbook of Indian Poetry , and publications by the Museum of Art & Photography. Her poems were nominated for the Best of the Net Awards 2024. Her essay “The Cockroach and I” was published by Penguin Random House after winning runner-up for the FT/Bodley Head Essay Prize (2020). She has performed and taught at TEDx, G5A, and numerous arts and educational institutions—and writes because it’s what she knows best.

b: Sarbpreet Singh ’s most recent book is Night of the Restless Spirits, a collection of short fiction about the events of 1984. His podcast, Story of the Sikhs , has listeners in 90 countries. He is also the author of…
f: Sarbpreet Singh ’s most recent book is Night of the Restless Spirits, a collection of short fiction about the events of 1984. His podcast, Story of the Sikhs , has listeners in 90 countries. He is also the author of The Camel Merchant of Philadelphia , set in Maharaja Ranjit Singh’s court.

b: Sarnath Banerjee is a pioneering Indian graphic novelist and visual artist. He has authored six books of graphic fiction, including Corridor , The Harappa Files , and All Quiet in Vikaspuri , works that blend history,…
f: Sarnath Banerjee is a pioneering Indian graphic novelist and visual artist. He has authored six books of graphic fiction, including Corridor , The Harappa Files , and All Quiet in Vikaspuri , works that blend history, politics, and urban life with distinctive wit and visual style. His art has been exhibited at major biennials and collected by museums worldwide. Banerjee’s commissioned project Gallery of Losers was created for the London Olympics, further cementing his international profile. Through his drawings and narratives, he reimagines contemporary India with sharp observation and satire. He currently lives in Berlin with his son.

b: Dr Sarosh Zaiwalla founded Zaiwalla & Co in 1982. The firm recently celebrated its 40th Anniversary with a reception at the Victoria & Albert Museum. It is the first English solicitors firm in the one ‘Square Mileâ€™…
f: Dr Sarosh Zaiwalla founded Zaiwalla & Co in 1982. The firm recently celebrated its 40th Anniversary with a reception at the Victoria & Albert Museum. It is the first English solicitors firm in the one ‘Square Mile’ financial and commercial district of the City of London started by a solicitor from India. In 2019, Zaiwalla authored his first memoir titled Honour Bound – Adventures of an Indian Lawyer in the English Courts.

b: Sarthak Malhotra is a PhD scholar at the Department of Social Anthropology, University of Cambridge. His dissertation explores the multiple lives of the Taj Mahal through long term ethnographic fieldwork with people who…
f: Sarthak Malhotra is a PhD scholar at the Department of Social Anthropology, University of Cambridge. His dissertation explores the multiple lives of the Taj Mahal through long term ethnographic fieldwork with people who work in and live around the Taj. He has previously studied at the universities of Oxford and Delhi.

b: Saskya Jain is a writer based in New Delhi and Berlin. Her debut novel, Fire Under Ash , was published by Random House India in 2014 and shortlisted for the Shakti Bhatt Prize in 2015. She has an MFA in Fiction from…
f: Saskya Jain is a writer based in New Delhi and Berlin. Her debut novel, Fire Under Ash , was published by Random House India in 2014 and shortlisted for the Shakti Bhatt Prize in 2015. She has an MFA in Fiction from Boston University and her short stories and non-fiction have appeared in numerous journals including Intelligent Life, The Economist, Caravan and The Baffler . She has taught creative writing and literature at Hong Kong University and Grinnell College, and her most recent writing residency was at Hedgebrook.

b: Colonel Satchit Kumar Basu is a Director at IST Limited, and an erstwhile army officer. An alumni of Officers Training Academy and College of Military Engineering, he has served for 31 years at numerous outposts in…
f: Colonel Satchit Kumar Basu is a Director at IST Limited, and an erstwhile army officer. An alumni of Officers Training Academy and College of Military Engineering, he has served for 31 years at numerous outposts in India and abroad, including during the Manipur insurgency and Kargil War. Despite his busy day job, he manages to be a theatre artist, and a tabla exponent.

b: Sathnam Sanghera , born to Punjabi parents in the West Midlands in 1976, entered the education system unable to speak English, but after attending Wolverhampton Grammar School, graduated from Christ’s College,…
f: Sathnam Sanghera , born to Punjabi parents in the West Midlands in 1976, entered the education system unable to speak English, but after attending Wolverhampton Grammar School, graduated from Christ’s College, Cambridge with a first class degree in English Language and Literature. He has been shortlisted for the Costa Book Awards twice, for his memoir The Boy With The Topknot and his novel Marriage Material , the former being adapted by BBC Drama in 2017. His third book, Empireland: How Imperialism Has Been Shaped Modern Britain , became an instant Sunday Times bestseller in 2021, was named Book of the Year (non-fiction: narrative) at the 2022 British Books Awards, and inspired Channel 4’s Empire State of Mind .

b: Sathya Saran spent 30 years in magazine journalism, with 17 years served as Editor – the initial 12 with Femina and the subsequent years with DNA . Saran has transitioned to being a full-time writer. Her repertoire…
f: Sathya Saran spent 30 years in magazine journalism, with 17 years served as Editor – the initial 12 with Femina and the subsequent years with DNA . Saran has transitioned to being a full-time writer. Her repertoire comprises much-loved biographies of cinema and music legends such as Guru Dutt, SD Burman, Jagjit Singh, and Hariprasad Chaurasia. Additionally, she has penned biographies of S. Kumar of S.Kumars and Ritu Nanda. Additionally, work in progress includes a translation of Yatindra Mishra’s Gulzar Saab , a critical biography of the poet, lyricist, and filmmaker. Saran also has a book of short stories titled The Dark Side . She curates the 'Spaces between Words' festival, a one-of-a-kind writer’s retreat launched in 2017. Saran has also written a series for TV, offering solutions for real-life marital issues, titled Kashmakash . She is currently the Consulting Editor at Penguin India.

b: Satish Gokhale is the owner of Design Directions Pvt. Ltd. A graduate of the National Institute of Design, Gokhale is the Founding Member of the Association of Designers of India (ADI) and has received several awards,…
f: Satish Gokhale is the owner of Design Directions Pvt. Ltd. A graduate of the National Institute of Design, Gokhale is the Founding Member of the Association of Designers of India (ADI) and has received several awards, including the Design of the Decade Award for a low-cost water filter – Tata Swach and the Lexus Design Awards –2018, 2019 and 2021. He also recently received a Red Dot Award in Germany and a ‘G’ Mark (Good Design Mark) in Japan for an indigenously designed solar-based computing device – Mobiliz. Gokhale has successfully designed and launched over 700 products in the Indian and international markets.

b: Satish Gupta is a painter, sculptor, poet, writer, printmaker, muralist, designer and calligrapher. His works have a deep engagement with mysticism and Zen spirit. His works were exhibited at the Venice Biennale and at…
f: Satish Gupta is a painter, sculptor, poet, writer, printmaker, muralist, designer and calligrapher. His works have a deep engagement with mysticism and Zen spirit. His works were exhibited at the Venice Biennale and at important museums internationally including Shanghai Museum of Modern Art. Gupta is known for his monumental copper sculptures.

b: Satish Mehta retired as Director General, ICCR and served inter alia as Director to two Prime Ministers of India, handled relations with crucial neighbours and represented India in the UN. He is Honorary Director at…
f: Satish Mehta retired as Director General, ICCR and served inter alia as Director to two Prime Ministers of India, handled relations with crucial neighbours and represented India in the UN. He is Honorary Director at Jaipur-based charity BMVSS-Jaipur Foot, the world’s largest organization for rehabilitation of handicapped persons, where he has implemented on-the-spot artificial limb fitment camps in over fifteen countries benefiting over 7000 amputees under the Ministry of External Affairs’ ‘India for Humanity’ program.

b: Satish Poonia is an Indian politician from the Bharatiya Janata Party. A long-time BJP MLA, Poonia represented the Amber constituency in the Rajasthan Legislative Assembly from 2018 to 2023 and served as President of…
f: Satish Poonia is an Indian politician from the Bharatiya Janata Party. A long-time BJP MLA, Poonia represented the Amber constituency in the Rajasthan Legislative Assembly from 2018 to 2023 and served as President of the BJP Rajasthan unit from 2019 to 2023. He was also Deputy Leader of the Opposition in the state assembly. Poonia has been involved in organisational work, including outreach and election strategy, and was appointed as the BJP’s in-charge for Haryana affairs during elections there. In 2025, he authored and released his first book, titled “Agnipath Nahin Janpath”, which reflects on his political journey, challenges faced as an MLA and leader, and commentary on broader political issues.
