b: Satya Vyas’ first novel Banaras Talkies is a bestseller with eight editions and a number of reprints in the last two years. The novel was selected as one of the top five Hindi books of 2015 by Amazon India. His second…
f: Satya Vyas’ first novel Banaras Talkies is a bestseller with eight editions and a number of reprints in the last two years. The novel was selected as one of the top five Hindi books of 2015 by Amazon India. His second novel, Dilli Darbaar, topped the Jagran-Neilsen survey for best selling Hindi novel. He is currently working on a number of screenplays.

b: Dr. Satyadeep S Chhetri is an author of two books. Gorkhaland Diaries (2022, Fiction) and Sikkim: From Autocracy to Half Democracy (2023, Non-Fiction). An associate professor at a government college in Gangtok, his…
f: Dr. Satyadeep S Chhetri is an author of two books. Gorkhaland Diaries (2022, Fiction) and Sikkim: From Autocracy to Half Democracy (2023, Non-Fiction). An associate professor at a government college in Gangtok, his articles and essays in local dailies are also widely read across the region and in various digital platforms. He lives between Siliguri and Gangtok.

b: Satyanand Nirupam is the editorial director of Rajkamal Prakashan Group. He has also been the Associate Editor of Delhi Press and Editor (Hindi) at Penguin Books India. He conceptualised Samanvay, the first literature…
f: Satyanand Nirupam is the editorial director of Rajkamal Prakashan Group. He has also been the Associate Editor of Delhi Press and Editor (Hindi) at Penguin Books India. He conceptualised Samanvay, the first literature festival in India dedicated to Indian languages and dialects. Known in the Hindi public sphere for introducing novelty to Hindi publishing, his work is geared towards making the language more accessible, especially to the youth.

b: Satyarth Nayak is an author and screenwriter based in Mumbai and a former SAARC Award-winning Correspondent with CNN-IBN. Satyarth best-selling biography, Sridevi – The Eternal Screen Goddess met with high acclaim.…
f: Satyarth Nayak is an author and screenwriter based in Mumbai and a former SAARC Award-winning Correspondent with CNN-IBN. Satyarth best-selling biography, Sridevi – The Eternal Screen Goddess met with high acclaim. His debut novel, The Emperor’s Riddles , released in 2014, became a bestselling thriller, earning comparisons with Dan Brown for being a ‘history meets mystery.’ His new book, the magnum-opus Mahagatha , is an epic collection of 100 greatest mythological tales from the Puranas. Satyarth is currently scripting the next instalment of one of Bollywood’s biggest sci-fi film franchises and penning the biography of Shabana Azmi.

b: Saurabh Dwivedi is the Founding Editor of The Lallantop, India's most popular vernacular digital-first news venture known for its political coverage and new-age writing style. He is also the editor of India Today…
f: Saurabh Dwivedi is the Founding Editor of The Lallantop, India's most popular vernacular digital-first news venture known for its political coverage and new-age writing style. He is also the editor of India Today Magazine -Hindi. Currently, Dwivedi hosts popular shows, including ‘The Lallantop Show’, ‘Duniyadaari’, and ‘Netanagri’ and has been instrumental in changing the landscape of news, offering audiences an alternative to television by establishing a credible medium via The Lallantop.

b: Saurabh Kirpal studied physics at St. Stephen's College, law at Oxford, and earned his Masters at Cambridge. A Senior Advocate at the Supreme Court, he has worked on significant cases, including the decriminalisation of…
f: Saurabh Kirpal studied physics at St. Stephen's College, law at Oxford, and earned his Masters at Cambridge. A Senior Advocate at the Supreme Court, he has worked on significant cases, including the decriminalisation of homosexuality in India. He is the managing trustee of the Naz Foundation Trust. He edited Sex and the Supreme Court , an anthology about issues relating to law, gender and sexuality; and has also authored the books Fifteen Judgments: Cases that Shaped India’s Financial Landscape and Who is Equal: The Equality Code of the Constitution .

b: Saurav Jha is a geostrategic affairs expert and director of Delhi Defence Review, a think-tank focused on the analysis of technology, war, and ideas. Trained in economics at Presidency College, Calcutta, and Jawaharlal…
f: Saurav Jha is a geostrategic affairs expert and director of Delhi Defence Review, a think-tank focused on the analysis of technology, war, and ideas. Trained in economics at Presidency College, Calcutta, and Jawaharlal Nehru University, New Delhi, Jha has worked as an energy economist in the past, besides serving as a consultant to FICCI’s International Division. His first book, The Upside Down Book of Nuclear Power , was released in 2010 and is being used by India's Department of Atomic Energy as a nuclear awareness-building read. In 2015, he published The Heat and Dust Project, co-written with Devapriya Roy, which chronicles a backpacking trip through India on an extremely tight budget.

b: Savi Sharma self-published her inspirational novel Everyone Has a Story , which became India’s fastest selling debut novel and was later acquired by Westland Publications. She went on to write two more romances, This…
f: Savi Sharma self-published her inspirational novel Everyone Has a Story , which became India’s fastest selling debut novel and was later acquired by Westland Publications. She went on to write two more romances, This Is Not Your Story and Everyone Has A Story 2 , both instant bestsellers. She is currently India’s highest selling female author.

b: Sayari Debnath is a culture journalist at Scroll, where she writes about books and literary trends. She translates from Hindi and Bengali into English.
f: Sayari Debnath is a culture journalist at Scroll, where she writes about books and literary trends. She translates from Hindi and Bengali into English.

b: Sayeeda Leghari was born in Karachi. Her desire to give back to Pakistan and the pride she takes in her culinary heritage prompted her to introduce the world to the country’s rich, diverse culture through food. Since…
f: Sayeeda Leghari was born in Karachi. Her desire to give back to Pakistan and the pride she takes in her culinary heritage prompted her to introduce the world to the country’s rich, diverse culture through food. Since 2013, Leghari has been heading Sukkur Beverages (PepsiCo Bottling Plant) as Chairperson and Managing Director. Pakistan Heritage Cuisine: A Food Story is her first published title.

b: Scott Anderson is the author of two novels and six nonfiction books, including Lawrence in Arabia, an international bestseller. His current work, King of Kings , was a New York Times bestseller and winner of the Kirkus…
f: Scott Anderson is the author of two novels and six nonfiction books, including Lawrence in Arabia, an international bestseller. His current work, King of Kings , was a New York Times bestseller and winner of the Kirkus Prize. A contributing writer of the New York Times Magazine, Anderson’s 2016 landmark report on the Middle East, “Fractured Lands,” remains the longest sole-author article in American magazine history.

b: Scott McDonald is Chief Executive of the British Council. He is committed to leading the organisation to build trust around the world. Previously, Scott was the President & CEO of the Oliver Wyman Group. Scott has…
f: Scott McDonald is Chief Executive of the British Council. He is committed to leading the organisation to build trust around the world. Previously, Scott was the President & CEO of the Oliver Wyman Group. Scott has degrees in Finance & Economics from McGill University and International Relations from Cambridge University.

b: Seema Goswami is a columnist and author. Her long-running column Spectator in Hindustan Times Brunch has a vast and dedicated following. Of her several books, Woman On Top became a bestseller and was translated into…
f: Seema Goswami is a columnist and author. Her long-running column Spectator in Hindustan Times Brunch has a vast and dedicated following. Of her several books, Woman On Top became a bestseller and was translated into several languages. Her political thriller Race Course Road was published in 2018 to critical acclaim. Her latest book, Madam Prime Minister is a pacy thriller that follows up on the events of Race Course Road.

b: Seema Jain is a bilingual poet, translator and editor. She is a former Head of the Department of English at KMV college, Jalandhar, and has authored, edited and translated fifteen books, including Vibrant Voices ,…
f: Seema Jain is a bilingual poet, translator and editor. She is a former Head of the Department of English at KMV college, Jalandhar, and has authored, edited and translated fifteen books, including Vibrant Voices , published by the Sahitya Akademi.

b: Seema Jayachandran is a Professor of Economics and Public Affairs at Princeton University. She conducts research on gender equality and on environmental conservation. She co-leads the Jameel Poverty Action Lab's (J-PAL)…
f: Seema Jayachandran is a Professor of Economics and Public Affairs at Princeton University. She conducts research on gender equality and on environmental conservation. She co-leads the Jameel Poverty Action Lab's (J-PAL) gender sector. She has a PhD in economics from Harvard University and a bachelor's degree in electrical engineering from MIT.

b: Seema Kohli is multi-disciplinary artist, a poet, a dreamer thriving on imagination, ideas, philosophies, narratives, oral histories and myths and recreating these as images or words. Kohli has had over 32 solo shows…
f: Seema Kohli is multi-disciplinary artist, a poet, a dreamer thriving on imagination, ideas, philosophies, narratives, oral histories and myths and recreating these as images or words. Kohli has had over 32 solo shows and she explores the themes of beauty, sensuality and spirituality expressed through her works based on the concept of ‘Hiranayagarbha’ or ‘The Golden Womb’ from which we have emerged, which is self-pervading, engulfs every single thing. Decay, hybridisation and transformation, creating new identity, reshaping belongings, intimacy; a dialogue of matter and memory all constitute a visual language of her work. Her work is primarily a celebration of the female form and energy, the source of the twin forces of creation and destruction. For Kohli, as an experimental artist, poetry is a recorded conversation between her, the canvas and the rendered image. In 2013, she self-published a compilation of verses, I Am , which was performed at TEDx, Chennai. She co-authored her second book, Experiencing The Goddesses and is working on another book, which is a compilation of poetry written in the last 7 years. She received acclaim for her creativity at the Florence Biennale, 2009 where she received a Gold Award for her video Swayamsiddha-Myth, Mind and Movement. She has also received the Young Federation of Indian Chamber of Commerce and Industry- Ladies Organisation Women Achievers Award in 2010 and the Lalit Kala National Award for Women in 2008. Her works have been shown at the collateral events Kochi Biennale, Birth Rights Collective, Venice Biennale of Art/Architecture. At Arco, Art Basil, and at India Art Fair among many others. She has been invited by the TEDx, WIN Conference, NGMA and various universities in India and all over the world including UConn, C

b: Seema Sirohi is a Washington DC-based columnist for The Economic Times , India’s largest business daily, and an analyst for the Observer Research Foundation, India’s premier think tank. She writes on foreign policy…
f: Seema Sirohi is a Washington DC-based columnist for The Economic Times , India’s largest business daily, and an analyst for the Observer Research Foundation, India’s premier think tank. She writes on foreign policy and India’s place in the world. She has covered India-US relations for more than three decades, tracking their progress through difficult times. She has also reported from Rome, Vienna, Jerusalem, Bratislava, Islamabad and New Delhi. She has appeared on BBC, NDTV, India Today TV, CNN and NPR as a commentator. Her first book Sita’s Curse: Stories of Dowry Victims was published in 2003.

b: Sejal Mehta has navigated the publishing industry for over 20 years. She has worked in the core teams of publications, including Femina, Lonely Planet, National Geographic Traveller, and Nature inFocus . Apart from…
f: Sejal Mehta has navigated the publishing industry for over 20 years. She has worked in the core teams of publications, including Femina, Lonely Planet, National Geographic Traveller, and Nature inFocus . Apart from writing for national and international publications, she has contributed to children's books and two anthologies. Her science communication work with Marine Life of Mumbai, an initiative documenting wildlife around Mumbai's coasts, led to a book on coastal creatures titled Superpowers On The Shore , published by Penguin Random House. She is currently handling science communication and outreach at The Habitats Trust.

b: Selma Dabbagh is a British Palestinian writer and lawyer. Author of Out of It (2011), a novel which is set mainly in Gaza, Selma writes short stories and radio plays, as well as for stage and screen. She is the editor…
f: Selma Dabbagh is a British Palestinian writer and lawyer. Author of Out of It (2011), a novel which is set mainly in Gaza, Selma writes short stories and radio plays, as well as for stage and screen. She is the editor of We Wrote In Symbols; Love and Lust by Arab Women Writers (2021). A judge for the EBRD Literature Prize 2025, she also blogs regularly for the London Review of Books.

b: Sethu has been writing under this pen-name in Malayalam for five decades with around 37 titles to his credit. He has won the Sahitya Akademi and other major awards. Many of his works have been translated into other…
f: Sethu has been writing under this pen-name in Malayalam for five decades with around 37 titles to his credit. He has won the Sahitya Akademi and other major awards. Many of his works have been translated into other languages including English, Hindi, German and Turkish. His novels translated into English include The Saga of Muziris , Aliyah and Pandavapuram .

b: Shabana Azmi is an internationally celebrated Indian film actress who believes art should be used as an instrument for social change. Her entry into films marked the way for the Parallel Cinema Movement with Shyam…
f: Shabana Azmi is an internationally celebrated Indian film actress who believes art should be used as an instrument for social change. Her entry into films marked the way for the Parallel Cinema Movement with Shyam Benegal’s Ankur in 1974. She has won five National Awards for Best Actress and five International Awards for Best Actress. Azmi is also highly respected as a social activist and tireless campaigner for the rights of women, slum dwellers and the underprivileged.A former UN Goodwill Ambassador for Population and Development,she was recently been nominated as a Global Leadership Ambassador for Women in a public service project initiated by Hillary Clinton. Azmi was nominated to the Rajya Sabha by the President of India in 1997. She is a recipient of the Padma Shri and Padma Bhushan.She was awarded the Gandhi International Peace Prize at the House of Lords in 2006.

b: Shabir Ahmad Mir is a poet and writer based in Pulwama, Jammu and Kashmir. He is the author of The Plague Upon Us (Hachette, 2020).

f: Shekhar Gupta is Founder and Editor-in-Chief of ThePrint, a digital start-up building a new editorial space of non-hyphenated liberalism, neither left, nor right, liberal on society, liberal on economy. A selection of these columns were collected in the bestselling book, Anticipating India. Gupta, a recipient of the Padma Bhushan, hosts Off the Cuff, an offering from ThePrint, which sees him in conversation with an eminent guest twice a month. He also hosts Walk the Talk on NDTV 24x7 every week. A collection of his news-making interviews has been published recently as a book Walk the Talk: Decoding Politicians. In his four-decade career, Gupta has reported on key Indian and international events, including the Nellie massacre in Assam, Operation Blue Star, the student uprising in Tiananmen Square in Beijing, the fall of the Berlin Wall, the first Gulf War from Baghdad, the first, US-backed ‘jihad’ in Afghanistan and the many twists and turns in the troubled 1983-1993 decade in Sri Lanka’s Tamil North. The NIMHANS Community Child and Adolescent Mental Health Service Project conceptualised and initiated by Dr Seshadri, has now extended into the national initiative SAMVAD (Support, Advocacy and Mental health interventions for children in Vulnerable circumstances And Distress), supported by the Ministry of Women and Child Development, Government of India.

She is a curator possessing the unique skills, expertise and know-how of children and the youth, with whom she has the honour of working with.

f: Shivshankar Menon is currently a Visiting Professor at Ashoka University, Chairman of the Advisory Board at the Institute of Chinese Studies, aDistinguished Visiting Research Fellow at the National University of Singapore, Member of the Board of Trustees at International Crisis Group and a Distinguished Fellow at the Asia Society Policy Institute.He served as national security advisor to the Prime Minister of India from January 2010 to May 2014 and previously as Foreign Secretary of India from October 2006 to August 2009. f: Shubha Mudgal has specialised in the Hindustani classical genres of khayal and thumi-dadra. She is the recipient of several national and international awards. f: Shubhangi Swarup is a novelist, educationist and most recently, a playwright. b: Shubhendra Rao is an internationally acclaimed performer, composer, cultural entrepreneur and music educator. His relentless service in promoting Indian music has made him a highly respected figure in the field of music…
f: Shubhendra Rao is an internationally acclaimed performer, composer, cultural entrepreneur and music educator. His relentless service in promoting Indian music has made him a highly respected figure in the field of music across the world. A protégé of Bharat Ratna Pandit Ravi Shankar, Pandit Rao has established himself “not only as a master of his instrument but also as a thinking musician” and “a musical bridge to many cultures. Internationally, he has performed at major music festivals and prestigious concert halls including Kennedy Center for Performing Arts, Sydney Opera House, Salzburg International Music festival, National Centre for the Performing Arts in Beijing and Theatre de le Ville in Paris. As a composer, Rao distinguishes himself by pushing the boundaries of classical music and creating music for artists across cultures. When Gods Meet and Apa Deepo Bhava were commissioned by Padma Vibhushan Dr Sonal Mansingh. The New York Times described his composition, Yathra as ‘movingly meditative’. His composition, Ekta, to honour German Chancellor Angela Merkel’s visit to India was described as ‘exemplifying the very best in the musical traditions of the East & West’. Leading magazines and newspapers like India Today , The Hindu and Indian Express invite Rao to write articles as an expert on music and music education. A co-founder of the Shubhendra and Saskia Rao Foundation, he is working tirelessly to revolutionise music education in India. Together with his wife, Saskia Ra, who has authored India’s first ever music curriculum for children, Sangeet4All, they are transforming the way music is taught in schools in India.

b: Shubhra Gupta is a senior columnist and film critic at The Indian Express. She has written a widely-read weekly review column for over 20 years and is one of India’s most well-known and respected film critics. She is…
f: Shubhra Gupta is a senior columnist and film critic at The Indian Express. She has written a widely-read weekly review column for over 20 years and is one of India’s most well-known and respected film critics. She is a frequent traveller to film festivals around the world (Berlin, Cannes, Toronto, Doha, Macao, Tehran, Bangkok) and has served on national and international juries. She curates and conducts the hugely popular platform, The Indian Express Film Club, in Delhi and Mumbai. The screening is followed by animated discussion, which she moderates. One of the most rewarding aspects of her work is the creation and running of modules on `Understanding Cinema’ for students at media and technology institutes. She served as a member of the Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC) between 2012-2015.

He is currently Life Trustee of India International Centre, Member of the Governing Board of the Centre for Policy Research and of the Institute of Chinese Studies, Member of the Advisory Board of World Wildlife Fund (India) and Member of the International Advisory Council of the Confederation of Indian Industry(CII). He has recently published a book, How India Sees the World . Saran was awarded the Padma Bhushan, the third highest civilian award, in 2011 for his contributions to civil service. In May 2019, he was conferred the Spring Order Gold and Silver Star by the Emperor of Japan for promoting India-Japan relations.

f: Siddhartha Mukherjee is a pioneering physician, oncologist, and author who has redefined our public discourse on human health, medicine and science. His published works exhibit an outstanding literary skill that has left an indelible mark on our culture, as The Emperor of All Maladies has been adapted into a documentary by filmmaker Ken Burns, and was included among Time magazine’s 100 best nonfiction books of the past century. His latest book The Song of the Cell has been named a New York Times Notable Book of 2022.

f: Sonal Mansingh is a classical Indian dancer, guru, choreographer, scholar, author on Indian socio-cultural traditions and member of Parliament. She is now the Kalapeethadheesh of Kalayoga Peetham at S-YVASA University, Bangalore and has previously served as Chairperson of the Central Sangeet Natak Akademi and several other official and cultural bodies. f: Sonali Bendre Behl is an award-winning Film & TV personality and author of The Modern Gurukul: My Experiments with Parenting . It has over fifty thousand members across platforms and has featured acclaimed authors like Amish, Chitra Banerjee Divakaruni, A.J.Finn, Kevin Kwan, Charlie Mackesy and Sophie Kinsella.

f: Mumbai-based Sonali Gupta is one of India’s leading clinical psychologists with 16 years of experience. She has been the official consulting psychologist for Tinder India since January 2018 and advises several leading businesses and organisations in addition to her own practice. With over 60,000 subscribers, her YouTube channel ‘Mental Health with Sonali’ is one of, if not the, largest for a mental health professional in India. She is passionate about causing a breakthrough and ending the stigma around mental health in India. She envisions a world

f: Sonali Khan leads Sesame Workshop India, creating innovative educational content to help children grow smarter, stronger, and kinder, particularly in marginalized communities. Formerly Director at Dasra and India Country Director for Breakthrough, Khan has spearheaded large-scale programmes and campaigns. f: Sonam Wangchuk is the founding-director of the Students' Educational and Cultural Movement of Ladakh. In January 2014, Wangchuk established a project called Ice Stupa which aimed at finding a solution to the water crisis being faced by the farmers of Ladakh.

f: Sonia Faleiro is the author of The Good Girls: An Ordinary Killing and Beautiful Things: Inside the Secret World of Baombay's Dance Bars . f: Sonia Mehta is a children’s author whose body of work ranges from creating one of India’s first dedicated children’s newspaper sections; to conceptualising the Bournvita Quiz Contest for television; to writing books, songs, poems and stories for publishers in India, Africa, USA and UK. f: Sonia Singh has been one of the country’s most prominent broadcast television journalists, anchor and editor over the last three decades. f: Sonora Jha , professor of journalism and an associate dean at Seattle University, USA, is the author of three books, most recently the novel The Laughter (2023), which is long listed for the 2024 Aspen Words Literary Prize and named one of the Best Books of 2023 by the New Yorker , NPR, and others. f: Sooni Taraporevala is the writer of the films Mississippi Masala , The Namesake and the Oscar-nominated Salaam Bombay! amongst others. f: Soumya Gupta , a career diplomat from the Indian Foreign Service (IFS), is currently serving in the Ministry of External Affairs. Previously, she worked in the Indian Embassy in Berlin. f: Sreenivasan Jain is Group Editor of NDTV, India's most respected 24hrs news and current affairs broadcaster. He presently anchors the award-winning daily show Reality Check , which aims at debunking official myths and government propaganda in a post-truth environment. For seven years, he reported and anchored an award-winning weekly ground reportage and investigative show, Truth vs Hype , which focuses on political corruption, conflict zones and untold stories of social and economic tensions. He has been with NDTV since 1995, during which time he has done stints as Managing Editor of Profit, NDTV's business channel, and as head of NDTV's Mumbai bureau for 8 years. He has anchored major prime time news telecasts and discussion-based shows ( The 9 o'clock News, India Decides, Star News on Sunday, The Newshour ). Jain was selected as Journalist of the Year by the Ramnath Goenka Awards in 2014, by the Red Ink Awards in 2015, and Anchor of the Year at ENBA Awards, 2016. Other awards include the World Media Summit Awards in Beijing, the World Silver Medal at the New York Festivals, the Hero Honda Indian Television Academy Awards, the Indian Telly Awards, the ENBA Awards, and the GQ Man of the Year (Media) in 2009. He was a recipient of the Eisenhower Fellowship in 2000.

f: Sri M is a spiritual teacher, author, social reformer, educationist and global speaker. Sri M established The Satsang Foundation 20 years ago and his mission has resulted in several initiatives in areas of education, community health, environment and the oneness of humanity. Among the many awards and honours he has received, Sri M was conferred the Padma Bhushan by the Government of India in January 2020 for distinguished service of high order in spirituality.

f: Srishti Arya is Director for International Original Film-India at Netflix. f: Srivatsan Iyer is the global CEO of Hero Future Energies. He last worked for Braskem, the largest petrochemical company in the Americas, based in São Paulo, Brazil, as their Vice President of Strategy & Planning, Innovation & Technology. Prior to joining Braskem in 2010, Iyer spent five years with McKinsey & Company, where he served a variety of clients in the Energy and Chemicals sector on a range of topics, including Strategy and Operations. Through his various roles, he worked towards strengthening and simplifying the manufacturing and business processes bringing focus on performance management and delivery of results. Iyer holds a PhD in Materials Science and Engineering from Virginia Polytechnic Institute and State University, and an MBA from the University of Texas.

f: Stephanie Schrader is curator at the Department of Drawings at the J. Paul Getty Museum, specialising in 16th to 18th century Dutch and Flemish art. Dedicated to bringing diverse audiences to the J. Paul Getty Museum, her innovative exhibitions engage the public in new and unexpected ways.

f: Stephen Alter is the author of more than 20 books of fiction and no-fiction. He was born in Mussoorie, Uttarakhand and much of his writing focuses on the Himalayan region where he continues to live and work. The Greatest Game: Being the Further Adventures of Kimball O’Hara is his most recent book.

f: Stephen Frederic Dale is an Emeritus Professor of South Asian and Islamic History and a Distinguished University Scholar at The Ohio State University. He first visited India in 1963 as a Fulbright Lecturer in English at the Banaras Hindu University and returned in 1967 to work in the Madras/Chennai archives to carry out research for his dissertation on the Muslims of Kerala. His published works include Islamic Society on the South Asian Frontier: the Mappilas of Malabar 1498-1922, Indian Merchants and Eurasian Trade 1600-1750, The Garden of the Eight Paradises: Babur and the Culture of Empire in Central Asia, Afghanistan and India, The Muslim Empire of the Ottomans, Safavids and Mughals, The Orange Trees of Marrakesh: Ibn Khaldun and the Science of Man and Babur: Timurid Prince and Mughal Emperor.

f: Stephen Dunbar-Johnson is the President, International, The New York Times Company, overseeing the global digital and print business. With a background in the Financial Times , he played a key role in integrating operations with the New York Times. Dunbar-Johnson holds executive management credentials from the Wharton School and the Columbia School of Journalism.

f: Stephen Fry is an English actor, writer, poet, comedian, television presenter, and film director. f: Stephen Green worked for McKinsey before joining HSBC in 1982. He was Group Chairman from 2006-2010. Lord Green was Trade Minister in the British Government from 2011-2013. He is Cogan University Professor of the Humanities at Harvard University. His latest book Dark Renaissance, reveals the daring and subversive life of Christopher Marlowe - Shakespeare’s contemporary, inspiration, and rival.

f: Stephen R. Platt is an award-winning historian specialising in China and the West, authoring acclaimed books like Imperial Twilight and Autumn in the Heavenly Kingdom . He teaches at the University of Massachusetts, Amherst.

f: Stephen Sexton’s first book, If All the World and Love Were Young was the winner of the Forward Prize for Best First Collection in 2019 and the Shine / Strong Award for Best First Collection. b: Steve Brusatte is a paleontologist who hunts and writes about dinosaurs. He is a professor at the University of Edinburgh in Scotland but grew up in the Midwestern USA. Brusatte has travelled around the world digging up…
f: Steve Brusatte is a paleontologist who hunts and writes about dinosaurs. He is a professor at the University of Edinburgh in Scotland but grew up in the Midwestern USA. He has written several books for kids and adults, most notably the adult pop science book The Rise and Fall of the Dinosaurs , which was a New York Times bestseller in the USA and Sunday Times bestseller in the UK.

b: Steve Coll has been Dean of Columbia Journalism School since 2013. A former president of the New America Foundation, he has been a staff writer at The New Yorker since 2005 where he writes on politics, national security…
f: Steve Coll has been Dean of Columbia Journalism School since 2013. He is the author of eight non-fiction books, a two-time Pulitzer Prize winner, a former reporter, foreign correspondent and senior editor at the Washington Post .

b: Steve MinOn was an internationally awarded advertising copywriter and a restaurateur before becoming a writer of fiction. His debut novel First Name Second Name won the Glendower Award for an Emerging Queensland Writer…
f: Steve MinOn was an internationally awarded advertising copywriter and a restaurateur before becoming a writer of fiction. f: Steven Pinker , a Johnstone Professor of Psychology at Harvard, is an experimental psychologist who researches visual cognition, psycholinguistics, and social relations. An elected member of the National Academy of Sciences, two-time Pulitzer Prize finalist, Humanist of the Year, recipient of nine honorary doctorates and several other accolades, Pinker was Chair of the Usage Panel of the American Heritage Dictionary. Some of his critically-acclaimed books include The Language Instinct, How the Mind Works, The Blank Slate, The Better Angels of Our Nature, The Sense of Style, Enlightenment Now and Rationality: What It Is, Why It Seems Scarce, Why It Matters.

b: Stewart Gordon is an independent scholar long associated with the Center for South Asian Studies, University of Michigan. Dr. Gordon is the author of The Marathas: 1600 – 1818 , translated this year into Marathi, and…
f: Stewart Gordon is an independent scholar long associated with the Center for South Asian Studies, University of Michigan. Recent writing includes When Asia was the World , A History of the World in Sixteen Shipwrecks , Shackles of Iron: Slavery Beyond the Atlantic and There and Back: Twelve of the Great Routes of Human History . He is currently writing a world history textbook for Oxford University Press based on seven themes common to all societies such as gender channeling, food and slavery.

b: Stewart Wheeler began his assignment as Deputy High Commissioner for Canada in India (with concurrent accreditation to Nepal and Bhutan) in September 2023, following more than four years 0f service as Chief of Protocol…
f: Stewart Wheeler began his assignment as Deputy High Commissioner for Canada in India (with concurrent accreditation to Nepal and Bhutan) in September 2023, following more than four years 0f service as Chief of Protocol of Canada. f: Thiru Su. Venkatesan is a distinguished Tamil writer, orator, and Member of Parliament from Madurai. His novel Veerayuga Nayagan Velpaari , exploring the bond between nature and humanity, became a literary phenomenon and was adapted for cinema. His ten-volume historical fiction Chandrahasam: A War with No End has been translated into English by Harvard scholar Jonathan Ripley. An authority on Sangam literature and archaeology, Su. Venkatesan is internationally acclaimed for his literary contributions and is widely respected for his advocacy of Tamil language, heritage, and social justice.

f: Subhro Bandopadhyay is a poet. His first chapbook, Dahankhata Theke , was published in 2000. He has also published two poetry collections in Spain, La ciudad leopardo and Poemas metálicos .

f: Sucheta Dalal is among the best known financial journalists in India, in 2006, Dalal was awarded the Padma Shri, India government’s third highest civilian award, based on her outstanding investigative journalism since the early 1990s. Ramanujan Translation Award, T he HarperCollins Book of English Poetry (editor), Fractals: New & Selected Poems | Translations 1980-2015 and EroText . Blue Nude: New Poems & Ekphrasis , winner of the Jorge Zalamea International Poetry Prize, is forthcoming. Sen’s works have been translated into over 25 languages. His words have appeared in several publications including, the Times Literary Supplement , Newsweek , the Guardian , the Financial Times , Poetry Review , Literary Review , Harvard Review , The Hindu , the Hindustan Times , the Times of India , and broadcast on BBC, PBS, CNN IBN, NDTV, AIR and Doordarshan. Sen’s newer work appears in Granta , Language for a New Century, Leela: An Erotic Play of Verse and Art , Indian Love Poems, Out of Bounds , Initiate: Oxford New Writing and Name Me a Word. He is the editorial director of AARK ARTS and the editor of Atlas. Sen is the first Asian to speak and read at the Nobel Laureate Festival. The Government of India awarded him the senior fellowship for ‘outstanding persons in the field of culture/literature’.

b: Sudeshna Chatterjee is an urban designer and researcher working on creating safe, inclusive, resilient and child-friendly cities. Her leadership of the Urban Design of the new capital city of Chattisgarh, Naya Raipur,…
f: Sudeshna Chatterjee is an urban designer and researcher working on creating safe, inclusive, resilient and child-friendly cities. Her leadership of the Urban Design of the new capital city of Chattisgarh, Naya Raipur, is widely acclaimed. Chatterjee is deeply committed to promoting the rights of children in all aspects of governance and planning of cities and has written extensively on these topics. Chatterjee is the founder and CEO of the non-profit, Action for Children’s Environments and a member of the global board of the International Play Association.

b: Sudha Sadhanand began her career in publishing and is now the Managing Editor for Westland/Tranquebar Press. She has spent several years in the television industry and worked with Times Now, the National Geographic…
f: Sudha Sadhanand began her career in publishing and is now the Managing Editor for Westland/Tranquebar Press. She has spent several years in the television industry and worked with Times Now, the National Geographic Channel and is credited for having launched Fox History in India. A keen observer of Indian politics and current affairs, Sadhanand manages the non-fiction list for Westland Tata.

b: Sudha Sadhanand has spent more than three decades in various fields of mainstream media and allied streams such as publishing, radio, documentaries and TV news. Sadhanand is one of the first bi-lingual anchors to have…
f: Sudha Sadhanand has spent more than three decades in various fields of mainstream media and allied streams such as publishing, radio, documentaries and TV news. Sadhanand is one of the first bi-lingual anchors to have worked with some of the earliest private news channels. She began her career in publishing with Penguin books and edited works of authors such as Pupul Jayakar and Professor Bipan Chandra. Her last stint was with Westland Amazon, where she led their non-fiction list and edited Pavan K. Varma and Vir Sanghvi, amongst others. Currently, Sadhanand is President, Editorial Affairs, at India Ahead.

b: Sudhir Hazareesingh is a Fellow in Politics at Balliol College, and a Fellow of the British Academy. He has written extensively about French political, intellectual and cultural history. His latest book, Black…
f: Sudhir Hazareesingh is a Fellow in Politics at Balliol College, and a Fellow of the British Academy. He has written extensively about French political, intellectual and cultural history. His latest book, Black Spartacus: The Epic Life of Toussaint Louverture , won the 2021 Wolfson History Prize.

b: Sudhir Mishra is an Indian film director and screenwriter known for directing critically acclaimed films like *Hazaaron Khwaishein Aisi, Dharavi* and *Chameli.* With a career spanning over 30 years, his work has been…
f: Sudhir Mishra is an Indian film director and screenwriter known for directing critically acclaimed films like *Hazaaron Khwaishein Aisi, Dharavi* and *Chameli.* With a career spanning over 30 years, his work has been recognised by the Government of India by receiving three National Awards from the President of India, as well as the Chevalier of the Ordre des Arts et des Lettres by the French government (equivalent to knighthood). He was one of the pioneers of the alternative independent cinema movement in India in the 1980s and remains one of the few directors from that era who continues to remain contemporary.

b: Sudipti writes on history, myths and the life of Indian women in a voice that is neither populist nor extremist. During her M.Phil, she identified and critically examined Mahesh Narayan’s poem ‘Swapna’ as the…
f: Sudipti writes on history, myths and the life of Indian women in a voice that is neither populist nor extremist. During her M.Phil, she identified and critically examined Mahesh Narayan’s poem ‘Swapna’ as the first work in Hindi modern poetry. Her findings were published in the journal Samkaleen Bhartiya Sahitya published by Sahitya Akademi and she came to be known as a critic in the Hindi public sphere. She is currently researching the renaissance period in Hindi literature.

b: Sugata is the Deputy Managing Director at Sage South Asia and a member of the India Board, overseeing South Asian business operations. He leads the publishing of journals, drives strategic sales and marketing…
f: Sugata is the Deputy Managing Director at Sage South Asia and a member of the India Board, overseeing South Asian business operations. He leads the publishing of journals, drives strategic sales and marketing initiatives for research and learning products, and heads corporate programs including CSR and sustainability at Sage India. With over 30 years in media and publishing, he previously worked with Encyclopaedia Britannica, Financial Express, Macmillan, and OUP. Sugata joined Sage in 2004, served as VP for books and journals acquisition until 2012, and rejoined in 2022. A PhD in Economics, he enjoys food entrepreneurship, reading, music, travel, and discussions on geopolitics, sports, and literature.

b: Suhasini Haidar is the Diplomatic Editor of The Hindu , writing regularly on India’s foreign policy and international relations. She has covered conflict in the region and beyond, as well as South Asian developments…
f: Suhasini Haidar is the Diplomatic Editor of The Hindu , writing regularly on India’s foreign policy and international relations. She has covered conflict in the region and beyond, as well as South Asian developments for more than two decades in her previous assignments as correspondent at CNN International and subsequently as Foreign Editor at CNN-IBN as well. She tweets @suhasinih

b: Suhel SETH is the CEO of Counselage, which is a branding and marketing consultancy. He advises Chairpersons and CEOs across the globe. He has been the principal brand advisor to MNCs who are either looking at entering…
f: Suhel SETH is the CEO of Counselage, which is a branding and marketing consultancy. He advises Chairpersons and CEOs across the globe. He has been the principal brand advisor to MNCs who are either looking at entering India or are in India. He is an author of three national best-seller books; a prolific actor both on stage and screen having acted in 167 plays and a well-known television commentator. He has over 4.7 million followers on Twitter. Suhel is the Chairman of the Branding Committee of India’s foremost business chamber CII for the year 2020-21.

b: Sujata Prasad is a writer, columnist, curator, and heritage conservationist. Her work and research interests cut across disciplines, intersecting with community health, education, rural livelihoods and the visual and…
f: Sujata Prasad is a writer, columnist, curator, and heritage conservationist. Her work and research interests cut across disciplines, intersecting with community health, education, rural livelihoods and the visual and performing arts. A former civil servant, she is currently advisor to the National Gallery of Modern Art. She also serves as an expert on the Ministry of Science and Technology’s advisory group on heritage research.

b: Sujata Shiven is a distinguished Hindi–Odia translator, poet, and writer with over 50 published translated books. She has been honored with the Government of India’s Non-Hindi Speaking Writers Award . For her…
f: Sujata Shiven is a distinguished Hindi–Odia translator, poet, and writer with over 50 published translated books. She has been honored with the Government of India’s Non-Hindi Speaking Writers Award . For her translation of Charu, Chivar aur Charya , she received the Aaj Tak Sahitya Jagriti Samman and the Kalinga Literary Festival Book Award . She has also served on juries and preview committees for prestigious platforms such as the National Film Awards, the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Film Festival, and the Jagran Film Festival.

b: Sujatha Gidla is the author of Ants Among Elephants: An Untouchable Family and the Making of Modern India . Gidla was born in Andhra Pradesh and migrated to America at the age of 26. She lives in New York and works as a…
f: Sujatha Gidla is the author of Ants Among Elephants: An Untouchable Family and the Making of Modern India . Gidla was born in Andhra Pradesh and migrated to America at the age of 26. She lives in New York and works as a conductor in the city’s subways. Ants Among Elephants is her first book.

b: Sujeev Shakya is an author, columnist, public speaker, coach, consultant and business leader. He is the bestselling author of Unleashing Nepal , a ready reckoner on the past, present and future of Nepal’s economy.…
f: Sujeev Shakya is an author, columnist, public speaker, coach, consultant and business leader. He is the bestselling author of Unleashing Nepal , a ready reckoner on the past, present and future of Nepal’s economy. From economies of developing countries to the economics of human beings, he moves across different worlds with his passion for the Himalayas being the axis.

b: Sujit Sivasundaram is Professor of World History at the University of Cambridge and Fellow of Gonville and Caius College, Cambridge. He is also Director of the Centre of South Asian Studies, Cambridge. His previous…
f: Sujit Sivasundaram is Professor of World History at the University of Cambridge and Fellow of Gonville and Caius College, Cambridge. He is also Director of the Centre of South Asian Studies, Cambridge. His previous books include, Islanded: Britain, Sri Lanka and the Bounds of an Indian Ocean Colony . He specialises in the histories of the Pacific and Indian oceans, their islands and the histories of science, race, the environment and culture.

b: Suketu Mehta is the author of Maximum City: Bombay Lost and Found , which won the Kiriyama Prize and the Hutch Crossword Award, and was a finalist for the 2005 Pulitzer Prize, the Lettre Ulysses Prize, the BBC4 Samuel…
f: Suketu Mehta is the author of Maximum City: Bombay Lost and Found , which won the Kiriyama Prize and the Hutch Crossword Award, and was a finalist for the 2005 Pulitzer Prize, the Lettre Ulysses Prize, the BBC4 Samuel Johnson Prize and the Guardian First Book Award. He has won the Whiting Writers’ Award, the O. Henry Prize and a New York Foundation for the Arts Fellowship for his fiction. Mehta’s work has been published in The New Yorker, The New York Times Magazine, National Geographic, Granta, Harper’s Magazine, TIME and Newsweek, and has been featured on NPR’s ‘Fresh Air’ and ‘All Things Considered.’ Mehta is an Associate Professor of Journalism at New York University. His latest book is This Land is Our Land. He is also working on a non-fiction book about immigrants in contemporary New York, for which he was awarded a Guggenheim fellowship.

b: Sukhadeo Thorat is an economist by training and has done research on rural poverty and agricultural growth and the economics of the caste system, amongst other subjects. He has served as the founding Director of the…
f: Sukhadeo Thorat is an economist by training and has done research on rural poverty and agricultural growth and the economics of the caste system, amongst other subjects. He has served as the founding Director of the Indian Institute of Dalit Studies, Chairman of the University Grants Commission and Chairman of the Indian Council of Social Science Research. Thorat has been awarded Honorary D.Litt, D.Sc, D.S. (Doctor of Education) and LLD Degrees by 12 universities. He has published 19 books and around 100 research papers. In 2008, Thorat was awarded the Padma Shri, India’s fourth-highest civilian award, the Mother Teresa International Award, the Babasaheb Ambedkar Ratna Award by the Delhi government for his dedication and extraordinary contributions on the works and thoughts of Dr. Ambedkar and, most recently, the Dr. Ambedkar National Award for Social Understanding and Upliftment of Weaker Section.

b: Suki Dusanj - Lenz is the Country Head for Fashion Revolution India. Calling for a fair, safe, and transparent fashion industry, the campaign has become the fastest-growing sustainability campaign in fashion. With a…
f: Suki Dusanj - Lenz is the Country Head for Fashion Revolution India. Calling for a fair, safe, and transparent fashion industry, the campaign has become the fastest-growing sustainability campaign in fashion. With a passion for technology, Dusanj-Lenz also works with Kickstart Innovation, Switzerland bridging startups with partners to further innovation.

b: Suki Kim is an investigative journalist, novelist and the only writer ever to have lived undercover in North Korea. She is the author of New York Times bestselling literary nonfiction Without You, There Is No Us:…
f: Suki Kim is an investigative journalist, novelist and the only writer ever to have lived undercover in North Korea. She is the author of New York Times bestselling literary nonfiction Without You, There Is No Us: Undercover Among the Sons of North Korea’s Elite and her first novel The Interpreter , a finalist for a PEN Hemingway Prize. She has written for many publications including The New York Times , Harper’s and The New Republic , where she is a contributing editor.

b: Sukrita Paul Kumar is a poet and critic. An Honorary Fellow of the prestigious International Writing Programme at the University of Iowa, she is also a former Fellow of the Indian Institute of Advanced Study, Shimla.…
f: Sukrita Paul Kumar is a poet and critic. An Honorary Fellow of the prestigious International Writing Programme at the University of Iowa, she is also a former Fellow of the Indian Institute of Advanced Study, Shimla. Kumar is Honorary faculty at the Durrell Centre at Corfu. Her books of poems include Dream Catcher and Without Margins in addition to bilingual collections such as Poems Come Home with translations by Gulzar. She was the Guest Editor of Crossing Over (University of Hawaii). A number of her poems have emerged from her experience of working with homeless people, tsunami victims and street children. She has also published many critical books and translations.

b: Suman Ghosh is a Professor of Economics at Florida Atlantic University. He did his BSc with a major in economics from Presidency College, Calcutta. After that, he obtained his master’s degree in economics from the…
f: Suman Ghosh is a Professor of Economics at Florida Atlantic University. He did his BSc with a major in economics from Presidency College, Calcutta. After that, he obtained his master’s degree in economics from the Delhi School of Economics before joining Cornell in 1996, where he did his PhD. Ghosh is a National Award-winning filmmaker who has directed films like Podokkhep, Dwando, Nobel Chor, Shyamal Uncle Turns off the Lights, Kadambari, Peace Haven, Basu Poribar, Searching for Happiness and Aadhaar (forthcoming). He also directed the documentary on Amartya Sen, titled The Argumentative Indian.

b: Suman Keshari is a distinct poetic voice in Hindi who is known for treating mythological themes and contemporary concerns with a holistic sensibility. She has published four collections of poems, with the latest being…
f: Suman Keshari is a distinct poetic voice in Hindi who is known for treating mythological themes and contemporary concerns with a holistic sensibility. She has published four collections of poems, with the latest being Nimitt Nahin (We Were Not The Cause), which articulates the anguish of women in the Mahabharata. She has also written a play called Gandhari and is currently working on another. Keshari has recently published a collection of ‘appreciations’ of important Hindi poems.

b: Sumana Chandrashekar is a ghatam player, writer, and researcher, and a long-time student of Carnatic vocal music. She has performed extensively and has been involved in several experimental and collaborative music…
f: Sumana Chandrashekar is a ghatam player, writer, and researcher, and a long-time student of Carnatic vocal music. She has performed extensively and has been involved in several experimental and collaborative music projects, as well as initiatives in music education. She has travelled widely across India and has worked closely with artists and artist communities.

b: Sumant Sinha is the Founder, Chairman, and CEO of ReNew, the first Indian clean energy company listed on Nasdaq. A global entrepreneur and climate thought leader, he's driven ReNew to a portfolio of 13.8 GW, offering…
f: Sumant Sinha is the Founder, Chairman, and CEO of ReNew, the first Indian clean energy company listed on Nasdaq. A global entrepreneur and climate thought leader, he's driven ReNew to a portfolio of 13.8 GW, offering comprehensive decarbonisation solutions. Sinha has been recognized for his climate advocacy, serving on global boards and receiving accolades, including the 2022 USISPF Global Leadership Award.

b: Sumanto Chattopadhyay, known as The English Nut , chats up words like old friends with scandalous pasts. An adman, actor and author of Stories of Words and Phrases , he shows how the hidden histories of language can be…
f: Sumanto Chattopadhyay, known as The English Nut , chats up words like old friends with scandalous pasts. An adman, actor and author of Stories of Words and Phrases , he shows how the hidden histories of language can be as gripping as detective fiction—curious, revealing and unexpectedly entertaining.

b: Sumeet Shetty is the President of Literati, India’s largest corporate book club, and Head of AI Tools at SAP, the world’s leading provider of enterprise application software. He has been honored with the GitHub AI…
f: Sumeet Shetty is the President of Literati, India’s largest corporate book club, and Head of AI Tools at SAP, the world’s leading provider of enterprise application software. He has been honored with the GitHub AI Champion Award. Harvard Business Review describes him as “an exceptional leader and coach, recognized for his track record of building high-performance teams.

b: Sumit Samos is a writer, artist, and anti-caste student activist from Odisha. He recently published a book titled Affairs of Caste: A Young Diary . His research interests are caste, cosmopolitan elites, Dalit Christian…
f: Sumit Samos is a writer, artist, and anti-caste student activist from Odisha. He recently published a book titled Affairs of Caste: A Young Diary . His research interests are caste, cosmopolitan elites, Dalit Christian history, and student politics. He completed his MSc in Modern South Asian Studies from Oxford.

b: Sumrit Shahi is an India. novelist, screenwriter and motivational speaker. He has authored three bestselling YA fiction novels and written for over 2000 episodes on television and the web. He wrote his debut novel at…
f: Sumrit Shahi is an India. novelist, screenwriter and motivational speaker. He has authored three bestselling YA fiction novels and written for over 2000 episodes on television and the web. He wrote his debut novel at 17. Awarded by the Hindustan Times in a list of top 30 young achievers under 30, he is also a TedX speaker.

b: Sundari Venkatraman is an author with 21 books to her name. All are Top 100 Bestsellers on Amazon around the world in both romance as well as Asian Drama categories. As a child, Venkatraman loved the ‘lived happily…
f: Sundari Venkatraman is an author with 21 books to her name. All are Top 100 Bestsellers on Amazon around the world in both romance as well as Asian Drama categories. As a child, Venkatraman loved the ‘lived happily ever after’ syndrome as she grew up reading fairy tales and comics. In her teens, she switched her attention to Mills & Boon. While she loved reading these, she tried to visualise what would have happened if there were similar situations happening in India. Her imagination took flight and then came the writing – a true bolt out of the blue! And Venkatraman has never looked back.

b: Sunil Amrith is the Renu and Anand Dhawan Professor of History at Yale University. He is the author of five books, most recently The Burning Earth . Amrith is the recipient of the 2024 Fukuoka Academic Prize, the 2022…
f: Sunil Amrith is the Renu and Anand Dhawan Professor of History at Yale University. He is the author of five books, most recently The Burning Earth . Amrith is the recipient of the 2024 Fukuoka Academic Prize, the 2022 Heineken Prize for History, a 2017 MacArthur Fellowship, and the 2016 Infosys Prize in Humanities.

b: Sunil Kant Munjal is one of the founder promoters of the Hero Group, India’s premier automotive manufacturing group that has evolved from being the world’s largest bicycle-maker to the largest two-wheeler maker. He…
f: Sunil Kant Munjal is one of the founder promoters of the Hero Group, India’s premier automotive manufacturing group that has evolved from being the world’s largest bicycle-maker to the largest two-wheeler maker. He is the Chairman of Hero Enterprise, with interests in insurance distribution, steel-making, real estate and corporate training. He has made strategic investments in several areas ranging from e-commerce to hospitality. He also supports start-ups on digital learning, community transportation, healthcare, women empowerment and education. He chairs the board that runs the Doon School and sits on the boards of the IIM Ahmedabad (IIMA), ISB, and SRCC. He has co-founded BML Munjal University (BMU) and is President of the Dayanand Medical College and Hospital, Ludhiana. He has also served as President of the CII and AIMA, been a member of Prime Minister’s Council on Trade and Industry and was on government taskforces that prepared the ground for India’s banking and insurance reforms. Munjal has set up the Serendipity Arts Foundation, which aims to revive patronage in the arts. He is also the President of the Ludhiana Sanskritik Samagam which supports performing arts across North India. He has also chronicled the incredible saga of Hero's founders in a book titled The Making of Hero , which featured amongst India's prominent bestsellers for several months and recently won the Business Book of the Year Award at the Tata Literature Live! Festival 2020.

b: Sunil Prasad Sharma has been serving in Rajasthan Police for the past 26 years and is currently posted as the Assistant Commissioner of Police at Ramganj, Jaipur. Publicly known for his service work and inspirational…
f: Sunil Prasad Sharma has been serving in Rajasthan Police for the past 26 years and is currently posted as the Assistant Commissioner of Police at Ramganj, Jaipur. Publicly known for his service work and inspirational videos on social media that have gathered thousands of views, Sharma is also an author, filmmaker, and avid poet. Having published five novels and produced many a short-films, he has been the recipient of many prestigious accolades, including the ‘Sanskriti Sanvardhan Samman Puruskar’, for his work in literature and the ‘Best Short-film’ Award at both RIFF and JIFF.

b: Sunil Amrith is the Mehra Family Professor of South Asian Studies and Professor of History at Harvard University. He is a 2017 MacArthur Fellow and recipient of the 2016 Infosys Prize in Humanities. His latest book is…
f: Sunil Amrith is the Mehra Family Professor of South Asian Studies and Professor of History at Harvard University. He is a 2017 MacArthur Fellow and recipient of the 2016 Infosys Prize in Humanities. His latest book is Unruly Waters: How Monsoons and Mountain Rivers Have Shaped South Asia’s History . He is also the author of Crossing the Bay of Bengal: The Furies of Nature and the Fortunes of Migrants , which won the John F. Richards Prize in South Asian History.

b: Sunita Kohli is an interior designer, a reputed leader in historical interior architectural restoration and, since 1972, a manufacturer of fine contemporary and classical furniture. She is the first interior designer to…
f: Sunita Kohli is an interior designer, a reputed leader in historical interior architectural restoration and, since 1972, a manufacturer of fine contemporary and classical furniture. She is the first interior designer to be conferred the Padma Shri in 1992 and the first woman to be appointed as the Chairperson of a ‘National Institute of Importance’, the School of Planning and Architecture, Bhopal. She developed a passion for cooking from her mother and enjoys trying new recipes. Widely travelled, Kohli brings influences from different cultures into her architecture as well as her cooking.

b: Sunita Toor is an academic and women’s rights activist on a mission to end violence against all women and girls. She leads Justice For Her, a project committed to improving access to justice for female victims of…
f: Sunita Toor is an academic and women’s rights activist on a mission to end violence against all women and girls. She leads Justice For Her, a project committed to improving access to justice for female victims of violence in India by working with the police and the communities they serve. Her work has combined academic research, activism, advocacy, journalism and spoken word to raise awareness of gender-based violence in India and highlight the importance of working together to combat it.

b: Sunny Singh is the author of five books. Her short stories, creative nonfiction and academic writing have been published across the world in key journals and anthologies. Singh is a founder of the Jhalak Prize for Book…
f: Sunny Singh is the author of five books. Her short stories, creative nonfiction and academic writing have been published across the world in key journals and anthologies. Singh is a founder of the Jhalak Prize for Book of the Year by a Writer of Colour and currently chair of the historic Authors' Club.

b: Supriya Dravid is the former editor-in-chief of ELLE India. She is the current editor of AJIOLUXE, a soon to be launched luxury e-commerce portal by the Reliance Group. Her novel A Cool, Dark Place was published by…
f: Supriya Dravid is the former editor-in-chief of ELLE India. She is the current editor of AJIOLUXE, a soon to be launched luxury e-commerce portal by the Reliance Group. Her novel A Cool, Dark Place was published by Penguin Random House.

b: Supriya Gandhi is a historian of Mughal India and teaches in the department of Religious Studies at Yale University. She grew up in India, received her PhD from Harvard University and also studied in Iran and Syria. She…
f: Supriya Gandhi is a historian of Mughal India and teaches in the department of Religious Studies at Yale University. She grew up in India, received her PhD from Harvard University and also studied in Iran and Syria. She is the author of The Emperor Who Never Was: Dara Shukoh in Mughal India.

b: Supriya Nair is a books columnist with Mumbai Mirror. She is the editor of a new magazine called Fifty Two and co-founder of the media company All Things Small.
f: Supriya Nair is a books columnist with Mumbai Mirror. She is the editor of a new magazine called Fifty Two and co-founder of the media company All Things Small.

b: Surender Mohan Pathak is India’s highest-selling crime writer with 298 Hindi novels to his name. His writing career began with his Hindi translations of James Hadley Chase and The Godfather . His first short story,…
f: Surender Mohan Pathak is India’s highest-selling crime writer with 298 Hindi novels to his name. His writing career began with his Hindi translations of James Hadley Chase and The Godfather . His first short story, Sattavan Saal Purana Admi ( The Man who Existed 57 Years Ago ), was published in Manohar Kahaniyaan , an extremely popular magazine of its time. His first novel, Puraane Gunaah Naye Gunahgaar ( Old Sins, New Sinners ) , was published in 1963 in another widely read magazine, Neelam Jaasoos . He then began publishing a series of novels with investigative journalist Sunil Chakravarty as its protagonist and the series running into 100 books. Another popular hero created by Pathak for his second series, the Sudhir Series , is private detective Sudhir Kohli. The Jeet Series features a petty thief who has taken to crime driven by a heartbreak. However, Pathak’s most loved novels come from the Vimal Series whose hero Sardaar Surendra Singh Sohal is a gangster with a conscience. Published in 1970, his novel Paisath Laakh Ki Dakaiti ( The 65 Lakh Heist ) was a blockbuster that has sold about 250,000 copies till date. Pathak’s novel Colaba Conspiracy was voted the most popular book on AmazoN in 2014. His latest, Heera-Pheri , topped the Nielsen Hindi charts in November 2017. His books have sold millions of copies, and he has a huge fan base across the Hindi heartland.

b: Sureshkumar Muthukumaran is the recipient of a Masters in Greek and Roman History from the University of Oxford and a PhD in History from University College London. He is currently a lecturer in history at the National…
f: Sureshkumar Muthukumaran is the recipient of a Masters in Greek and Roman History from the University of Oxford and a PhD in History from University College London. He is currently a lecturer in history at the National University of Singapore. His research focuses on interactions between peoples in ancient Afro-Eurasia with an eye to examining long-distance connectivity.

b: Surina Narula, MBE, founder and sponsor of the Jaipur Literature Festival, instituted the DSC Prize for South Asian Literature in 2010. As co-founder of the Consortium for Street Children, she put the rights of street…
f: Surina Narula, MBE, founder and sponsor of the Jaipur Literature Festival, instituted the DSC Prize for South Asian Literature in 2010. As co-founder of the Consortium for Street Children, she put the rights of street children at the UN level, increasing their visibility worldwide. Narula is the trustee of ‘Television for Environment’, which uses the power of films to help build a more sustainable planet, and ‘Difficult Dialogues’, an annual forum examining issues of contemporary relevance in South Asia.

b: Surinder S. Jodhka is professor of Sociology at the Jawaharlal Nehru University and fellow at the Centre de Sciences Humaines, New Delhi. He has published extensively, including Caste, Caste in Contemporary India and a…
f: Surinder S. Jodhka is professor of Sociology at the Jawaharlal Nehru University and fellow at the Centre de Sciences Humaines, New Delhi. He has published extensively, including Caste, Caste in Contemporary India and a co-edited work entitled Mapping the Elite: Power, Privilege, and Inequality. He is editor of the Routledge book series, Religion and Citizenship .

b: Surjit Patar is a celebrated Punjabi poet. The range of his work includes very strict metres as well as blank and free dramatic verse. He is a recipient of the Pash Puruskar, the Bhartiya Bhasha Parishad Puruskar, the…
f: Surjit Patar is a celebrated Punjabi poet. The range of his work includes very strict metres as well as blank and free dramatic verse. He is a recipient of the Pash Puruskar, the Bhartiya Bhasha Parishad Puruskar, the Anaad Award, MKS Award, D.Litt ( Honoris Causa), the Padma Shri and the Saraswati Samman.

b: Surjit S. Bhalla is Executive Director for India, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh and Bhutan at the IMF. He has served as A part-time member of PM Modi’s first Economic Advisory Council; and chaired the High Level Advisory…
f: Surjit S. Bhalla is Executive Director for India, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh and Bhutan at the IMF. He has served as A part-time member of PM Modi’s first Economic Advisory Council; and chaired the High Level Advisory Group on Trade (Commerce Ministry). Bhalla is also a regular contributor (over 1300 articles) to Indian newspapers, magazines and television on financial markets, economics, politics and cricket. He is the author of several academic articles as well as four books on globalisation, including The New Wealth of Nations . His first book, Between the Wickets: The Who and Why of the Best in Cricket, developed a model for evaluating performance in sports. His most recent book Citizen Raj: Indian Elections 1952-2019 analyzed Indian elections since 1952 and accurately forecast the Modi victory in 2019. He holds a PhD in Economics from Princeton University.

b: Susan Abulhawa is a Palestinian novelist, poet and political essayist. Her debut novel, Mornings in Jenin , was an international bestseller and translated into 28 languages. The Blue Between Sky and Water is currently…
f: Susan Abulhawa is a Palestinian novelist, poet and political essayist. Her debut novel, Mornings in Jenin , was an international bestseller and translated into 28 languages. The Blue Between Sky and Water is currently available in 22 languages. Abulhawa is also a biologist and the founder of Playgrounds for Palestine, a non-profit children’s organisation dedicated to upholding the Right to Play.

b: Susan Ferguson is the Country Representative for UN Women India. Ms. Ferguson has had a distinguished career in international development spanned by themes of gender equality and social justice. She has extensive…
f: Susan Ferguson is the Country Representative for UN Women India. Ms. Ferguson has had a distinguished career in international development spanned by themes of gender equality and social justice. She has extensive experience working in grass root development agencies, establishing and managing social services, working within Local, State and Federal Government in Australia. Ms. Ferguson was the Country Representative in Papua New Guinea.

b: Susan Jung is the food columnist for Vogue Hong Kong and academy chair for Asia's 50 Best Restaurants. A trained pastry chef, her cookbook Kung Pao & Beyond features fried chicken recipes from East and Southeast Asia.
f: Susan Jung is the food columnist for Vogue Hong Kong and academy chair for Asia's 50 Best Restaurants. A trained pastry chef, her cookbook Kung Pao & Beyond features fried chicken recipes from East and Southeast Asia.

b: Susana Torres Prieto is Associate Professor of Humanities at IE University (Madrid) and Associate Research Fellow at the Harvard Ukrainian Research Institute. Her research focuses on medieval Slavic studies,…
f: Susana Torres Prieto is Associate Professor of Humanities at IE University (Madrid) and Associate Research Fellow at the Harvard Ukrainian Research Institute. Her research focuses on medieval Slavic studies, particularly those centred around literary and manuscript issues. She has published extensively on literary transmission and the creation of ideologies of power.

b: Susan Bautista-Afan : An experienced leader in both the corporate and non-profit sectors, currently serving as President of the Ramon Magsaysay Award Foundation (RMAF), Asia’s premier prize and highest honor. Since…
f: Susan Bautista-Afan : An experienced leader in both the corporate and non-profit sectors, currently serving as President of the Ramon Magsaysay Award Foundation (RMAF), Asia’s premier prize and highest honor. Since 1957, the Ramon Magsaysay Award has celebrated “Greatness of Spirit” — recognizing over 340 transformative individuals and organizations who have offered impactful, selfless solutions to pressing human development challenges. After a 30-year career in the U.S. with Fortune 500 firm Robert Half International, retiring as District President of Southern California, Susan returned to the Philippines in 2014. She led the ABS-CBN Foundation for five years as Managing Director before joining RMAF. She is a graduate of Ateneo de Manila University.

b: Sushant Jha is an editor, translator, and journalist, with twenty years of experience. He has translated more than a dozen books, including the Gandhi series by Ramachandra Guha and Patrick French’s India: A Portrait .…
f: Sushant Jha is an editor, translator, and journalist, with twenty years of experience. He has translated more than a dozen books, including the Gandhi series by Ramachandra Guha and Patrick French’s India: A Portrait . He translated and edited the official history of Lithuania, and was commissioning editor at Penguin Random House for five years. Sushant has worked in the India Today group in various capacities, and also with Doordarshan. He also writes columns for leading Hindi newspapers and websites.

b: Susheela Raman is a London-born Tamil singer and composer who has released a string of acclaimed albums beginning with her award winning debut Salt Rain in 2001, to her latest Ghost Gamelan in 2018. She is currently…
f: Susheela Raman is a London-born Tamil singer and composer who has released a string of acclaimed albums beginning with her award winning debut Salt Rain in 2001, to her latest Ghost Gamelan in 2018. She is currently working on new musical settings of the visionary poetry of William Blake. Raman has created a body of collaborative work that crosses multiple genres and traditions.

b: Sushma Jansari is Tabor Foundation Curator South Asia at the British Museum. Her book Chandragupta Maurya: the creation of a national hero in India has recently been published. Currently, she is preparing a major…
f: Sushma Jansari is Tabor Foundation Curator South Asia at the British Museum. Her book Chandragupta Maurya: the creation of a national hero in India has recently been published. Currently, she is preparing a major exhibition about art, religion and power in ancient South Asia (opening May 2025).

b: Sutapa Sikdar is an NSD graduate who has been part of the Indian film and television industry since 1996. She began her career working with Govind Nihalani. She has written various television series including Banegi…
f: Sutapa Sikdar is an NSD graduate who has been part of the Indian film and television industry since 1996. She began her career working with Govind Nihalani. She has written various television series including Banegi Apni Baat and films like Kahani , Khamoshi and Shabd . She has also produced many best sellers and also films such as Madari and Qareeb Qareeb Singlle.

b: Suvir Saran is a Michelin-starred restaurateur, author, and cultural storyteller celebrated for his contributions to Indian cuisine. He founded Devi in New York, the first Indian restaurant in America to earn a Michelin…
f: Suvir Saran is a Michelin-starred restaurateur, author, and cultural storyteller celebrated for his contributions to Indian cuisine. He founded Devi in New York, the first Indian restaurant in America to earn a Michelin star, and currently serves as Culinary Director for Avas Wellness in Alibaug. The author of five books, including his memoir Tell My Mother I Like Boys , Suvir weaves his experiences in food, travel, and culture into his storytelling. Living between Mumbai and Delhi, he brings a profound curiosity, musical sensibility, and passion for learning to his work, exploring identity, heritage, and the transformative power of culinary artistry.

b: Suyash Dasgupta is a Grade 12 student at Singapore American School (SAS), with deep interests in environmental science and technology, poetry and songwriting. He grew up in India, South Africa and Bangladesh and is…
f: Suyash Dasgupta is a Grade 12 student at Singapore American School (SAS), with deep interests in environmental science and technology, poetry and songwriting. He grew up in India, South Africa and Bangladesh and is currently based in Singapore. Fluent in English, Mandarin, Bengali and Hindi, Dasgupta runs Digital Citizens, a service club focused on supporting first-generation learners at Anandalaya Public School in Jharkhand, India. His novel, Chosen, is part of a multi-sensory project which integrates hip-hop style poetry with an original soundtrack to create a unique experience.

b: Suzy Hansen is contributing writer to The New York Times Magazine and has written for many other publications. In 2007, she was awarded a fellowship from the Institute of Current World Affairs to do research in Turkey.…
f: Suzy Hansen is contributing writer to The New York Times Magazine and has written for many other publications. In 2007, she was awarded a fellowship from the Institute of Current World Affairs to do research in Turkey. She currently lives in Istanbul. Notes on a Foreign Country is her first book.

b: Swanand Kirkire is an award-winning screenwriter, actor, and lyricist known for iconic songs in films like Parineeta , Masaan , and Lage Raho Munna Bhai . His lyrics for Behti Hawa Sa Tha Woh and Bande Me Tha Dum earned…
f: Swanand Kirkire is an award-winning screenwriter, actor, and lyricist known for iconic songs in films like Parineeta , Masaan , and Lage Raho Munna Bhai . His lyrics for Behti Hawa Sa Tha Woh and Bande Me Tha Dum earned him two National Awards. From a family of classical musicians, Kirkire has built a celebrated career as both a playback singer and lyricist over the past two decades.

b: Swapan Dasgupta is a Member of Parliament and columnist for major Indian newspapers. A journalist for 30 years, he occupied senior editorial positions at the Times of India, Indian Express and India Today. He writes…
f: Swapan Dasgupta is a Member of Parliament and columnist for major Indian newspapers. A journalist for 30 years, he occupied senior editorial positions at the Times of India, Indian Express and India Today. He writes regular columns for the Times of India, Telegraph and Pioneer, and is a commentator on TV networks. He is the author of Awakening Bharat Mata: The Political Beliefs of the Indian Right . In 2015, he was awarded the Padma Bhushan and was nominated to the Rajya Sabha.

b: Swapna Liddle is a historian of Delhi, and the author of several books on the subject. Her recently published books, The Broken Script: Delhi Under the East India Company and the Fall of the Mughal Dynasty, 1803-1857,…
f: Swapna Liddle is a historian of Delhi, and the author of several books on the subject. Her recently published books, The Broken Script: Delhi Under the East India Company and the Fall of the Mughal Dynasty, 1803-1857, and Shahjahanabad: Mapping a Mughal City, are ground-breaking contributions in their field.

b: Swati Chaturvedi is an award-winning journalist who has worked for The Statesman , The Indian Express , Hindustan Times and ZEE news. Her first book, the murder myster Daddy’s Girl , was published in 2016. Her second,…
f: Swati Chaturvedi is an award-winning journalist who has worked for The Statesman , The Indian Express , Hindustan Times and ZEE news. Her first book, the murder myster Daddy’s Girl , was published in 2016. Her second, a non-fiction investigation, was published the same year to international acclaim. I am a Troll – Inside the BJP’s Secret Digital Army received wide coverage for its investigation into how ruling party is paying to abuse citizens in a democracy. Chaturvedi is a regular contributor of investigative stories and analysis to NDTV, DailyO ( India Today ), The Wire and Hindu Business Line . She maintains a lively presence on social media (@Bainjal) with many of her tweets setting the discourse and going viral.

b: Swati Chopra brings over two decades of experience in publishing, media, and journalism to her role as Publisher at Hachette India. She was most recently Editorial Director, Non-fiction, at Juggernaut Books and has…
f: Swati Chopra brings over two decades of experience in publishing, media, and journalism to her role as Publisher at Hachette India. She was most recently Editorial Director, Non-fiction, at Juggernaut Books and has previously worked with HarperCollins India, Penguin Random House India, and Roli Books. Throughout her career, she has championed a diverse non-fiction list spanning politics, history, memoir, investigative journalism, foreign policy, espionage, and current affairs, producing titles that are both commercially successful and critically acclaimed. An accomplished author herself, Swati has written five books, including Dharamsala Diaries and Women Awakened .

b: Swati Daftuar is an independent journalist, editor, and literary consultant. She is Consulting Editor at Speaking Tiger, commissioning fiction, translations, and idea-driven non-fiction. Previously, she served as…
