f: Swati Daftuar is an independent journalist, editor, and literary consultant. She is Consulting Editor at Speaking Tiger, commissioning fiction, translations, and idea-driven non-fiction. Previously, she served as Executive Editor at HarperCollins India and Deputy Editor at The Hindu , and she founded Delhi’s community-led Annual Book & Bake Sale. She also hosts The Bookshop Inc. Book Clubs and writes on books and culture for Scroll and The Hindu . Her first novel is set to be published by HarperCollins India in 2026.

b: Swati Lahoti is a writer by passion. She has variously worked as a placement consultant and copywriter. However, the role most dear to her heart is that of a mother to her two sons. Her book is about her redemption as a…
f: Swati Lahoti is a writer by passion. She has variously worked as a placement consultant and copywriter. However, the role most dear to her heart is that of a mother to her two sons. Her book is about her redemption as a student, teacher, mother and most importantly as a daughter.

b: Swati Pandey i s the Vice Chairman and Managing Director of the Maharashtra Airport Development Company and a distinguished career bureaucrat with nearly three decades of service across aviation, infrastructure, public…
f: Swati Pandey i s the Vice Chairman and Managing Director of the Maharashtra Airport Development Company and a distinguished career bureaucrat with nearly three decades of service across aviation, infrastructure, public policy, and financial inclusion. As Postmaster General of India Post, Mumbai Region, she led pioneering initiatives, including “Project Kamathipura,” now a Harvard-published case study. Her debut book, Invisible in Plain Sight , offers a powerful, empathetic portrait of the lives of Kamathipura’s commercial sex workers. A National Award–winning filmmaker for Elephants Do Remember and a TEDx speaker, Pandey continues to champion social equity, cultural preservation, and transformative public policy.

b: Swati Vashishtha is an independent writer, journalist and cultural advisor. A TEDx speaker, photographer and podcaster, Vashishtha has contributed to prominent publications including NPR , The Hindustan Times , CNN…
f: Swati Vashishtha is an independent writer, journalist and cultural advisor. A TEDx speaker, photographer and podcaster, Vashishtha has contributed to prominent publications including NPR , The Hindustan Times , CNN International , Reuters, ANI and CNN-IBN , where she served as Chief of Bureau in Rajasthan for 12 years. Her reportage and excellence in photography has earned her awards, including the Maharaja Sawai Ram Singh II Award. With a background in English Literature, Psychology and Indian Aesthetics, Swati brings a unique perspective to her diverse areas of work. She is an art and poetry enthusiast.

b: Swetha Yerram , an independent publisher and co-founder of Aju Publications, transitioned from data analysis to publishing in 2022. Aju Publications has gained recognition with the national bestseller Amma Diary lo…
f: Swetha Yerram , an independent publisher and co-founder of Aju Publications, transitioned from data analysis to publishing in 2022. Aju Publications has gained recognition with the national bestseller Amma Diary lo Konni Pajeelu , captivating Telugu readers worldwide. Yerram’s strategic use of social media and dedication to nurturing literary talent has positioned her at the forefront of modern Telugu publishing, bringing regional voices to a broader audience.

b: Syed Salman Chishty hails from the Chishty Sufi family of Ajmer Sharif, the Gaddi-Nashin (hereditary custodians) of the 11th century Sufi shrine of Hazrat Khawaja Moinuddin Hassan Chishty. His work involves the research…
f: Syed Salman Chishty hails from the Chishty Sufi family of Ajmer Sharif, the Gaddi-Nashin (hereditary custodians) of the 11th century Sufi shrine of Hazrat Khawaja Moinuddin Hassan Chishty. His work involves the research of Sufi traditions and their interaction with global cultures and traditions. He is a regular participant at international conferences on interfaith dialogue and has represented the Chishty Sufi Order in the Middle East, Asia, the United States and the United Kingdom. A founding member of the Chishty Foundation, he has served as its director for the last five years. He has also written several articles on Sufism and spiritual understanding for various national and international publications. Chishty also has an interest in photographing the ‘sacred’ and captured his Sufi journeys across the globe. His work has been exhibited at various events and exhibitions.

b: Syima Aslam is the founder and Director of the Bradford Literature Festival (BLF), which she established in 2014. A 10-day literary and cultural celebration, BLF welcomes more than 70,000 visitors to Bradford annually…
f: Syima Aslam is the founder and Director of the Bradford Literature Festival (BLF), which she established in 2014. A 10-day literary and cultural celebration, BLF welcomes more than 70,000 visitors to Bradford annually and is celebrated as the most socio-economically and ethnically diverse literary festival in the UK. Under her directorship, BLF has made a significant impact on the country’s literary landscape, hailed as ‘one of the most innovative and inspirational festivals in the UK’, bringing together literature from all genres, promoting intercultural fluency, providing a platform for marginalised voices and reflecting the changing face of contemporary Britain through a programme that celebrates diversity, empathy and artistic excellence.

b: Dr. Sankara Saravanan is an academic, writer, and translator with significant contributions to translation studies and educational publishing. He has played a key role in several translation projects for the Tamil Nadu…
f: Dr. Sankara Saravanan is an academic, writer, and translator with significant contributions to translation studies and educational publishing. He has played a key role in several translation projects for the Tamil Nadu Textbook Corporation, helping disseminate knowledge across languages. Actively associated with the Chennai International Book Fair and programmes linked to the Jaipur Literature Festival, he has also trained aspiring civil servants in Tamil language, literature, and Indian history. Currently serving as Principal of the All India Civil Services Coaching Academy, Government of Tamil Nadu, he has represented Tamil literature at international book fairs including Frankfurt, Sharjah, and Bologna.

b: Tadhg Mac Dhonnagáin is a multi-award-winning writer of fiction, non-fiction, screenplays and songs. He works predominantly in the Irish (Gaelic) language and draws on its rich tradition of song and myth in his work.…
f: Tadhg Mac Dhonnagáin is a multi-award-winning writer of fiction, non-fiction, screenplays and songs. He works predominantly in the Irish (Gaelic) language and draws on its rich tradition of song and myth in his work. His novel, Madame Lazare , was awarded a Special Mention at the European Union Prize for Literature, 2022.

b: Talat Ahmed is Lecturer in South Asian History in the School of History, Classics and Archaeology, Co-Director of the Centre for South Asian Studies at the University of Edinburgh and a Fellow of the Royal Asiatic…
f: Talat Ahmed is Lecturer in South Asian History in the School of History, Classics and Archaeology, Co-Director of the Centre for South Asian Studies at the University of Edinburgh and a Fellow of the Royal Asiatic Society. Dr. Ahmed is the author of Literature and Politics in the Age of Nationalism: The Progressive Episode in South Asia, 1932-56 with an upcoming second edition to be published soon. Her latest book is Mohandas Gandhi: Experiments in Civil Disobedience.

b: Talmiz Ahmad joined the Indian Foreign Service in 1974 and held positions in the Indian missions in New York, London and Pretoria. After retirement from foreign service, he is now a full-time academic and holds the Ram…
f: Talmiz Ahmad joined the Indian Foreign Service in 1974 and held positions in the Indian missions in New York, London and Pretoria. After retirement from foreign service, he is now a full-time academic and holds the Ram Sathe Chair in International Studies, Symbiosis International University, Pune. He has published three books: Reform in the Arab World: External Influences and Regional Debates, Children of Abraham at War: The Clash of Messianic Militarisms and The Islamist Challenge in West Asia: Doctrinal and Political Competitions after the Arab Spring . His latest book, West Asia at War: Repression, Resistance and Great Power Games , will be published shortly.

b: Tam Baillie was Scotland’s Commissioner for Children and Young People from 2009 to 2017 promoting and safeguarding children’s rights. Baillie has worked as a practitioner and manager for 40 years in the statutory…
f: Tam Baillie was Scotland’s Commissioner for Children and Young People from 2009 to 2017 promoting and safeguarding children’s rights. Baillie has worked as a practitioner and manager for 40 years in the statutory and NGO sectors in Scotland and England. Baillie has always worked with the most vulnerable children and young people.

b: Tania James is the author of The Tusk That Did the Damage , Aerogrammes and Atlas of Unknowns. The Tusk That Did the Damage was named a Best Book of 2015 by the San Francisco Chronicle, Guardian and NPR, and was…
f: Tania James is the author of The Tusk That Did the Damage , Aerogrammes and Atlas of Unknowns. The Tusk That Did the Damage was named a Best Book of 2015 by the San Francisco Chronicle, Guardian and NPR, and was shortlisted for the International Dylan Thomas Prize and longlisted for the Financial Times Oppenheimer Award.

b: Tania Singh is the CEO of a non-profit organisation called Make Love Not Scars (MLNS) that rehabilitates acid attack survivors MLNS has been the only organisation to win the CNBC TV-18 India Business Leader Award for…
f: Tania Singh is the CEO of a non-profit organisation called Make Love Not Scars (MLNS) that rehabilitates acid attack survivors MLNS has been the only organisation to win the CNBC TV-18 India Business Leader Award for Brand of the Year in 2017. She is the co-author of Being Reshma , a memoir of an acid attack survivor Reshma Qureshi, who is also the face of MLNS.

b: Tansen Sen is Professor of history, the Director of the Center for Global Asia at NYU Shanghai, and Associated Professor of History at NYU. He is the author of Buddhism, Diplomacy, and Trade: The Realignment of…
f: Tansen Sen is Professor of history, the Director of the Center for Global Asia at NYU Shanghai, and Associated Professor of History at NYU. He is the author of Buddhism, Diplomacy, and Trade: The Realignment of Sino-Indian Relations, 600-1400and India, China, and the World: A Connected History.

b: Tanuf Khan holds a Master’s degree in English Literature from Jamia Millia Islamia University and works as an editor and commissioning editor at Jaipur-based literary agency Paper Sparrows. Passionate about literary…
f: Tanuf Khan holds a Master’s degree in English Literature from Jamia Millia Islamia University and works as an editor and commissioning editor at Jaipur-based literary agency Paper Sparrows. Passionate about literary craft, she believes reading good books is the answer to life, the universe, and everything.

b: Tanuj Bhojwani is a storyteller who codes. He holds a chemical engineering degree from IIT Bombay, and also attended Ashoka University and studied liberal arts at the Young India Fellowship. His training in the sciences…
f: Tanuj Bhojwani is a storyteller who codes. He holds a chemical engineering degree from IIT Bombay, and also attended Ashoka University and studied liberal arts at the Young India Fellowship. His training in the sciences and humanities allows him to craft narratives about technology that are accessible without sacrificing technical depth. As a Fellow at iSPIRT Foundation, Bhojwani works on policy issues related to digital identity, payments, data protection and drones.

b: Tanuj Solanki is the author of three books of fiction. His most recent novel, The Machine is Learning , was longlisted for the JCB Prize for Literature 2020. Tanuj's short fiction has been published in the Caravan,…
f: Tanuj Solanki is the author of three books of fiction. His most recent novel, The Machine is Learning , was longlisted for the JCB Prize for Literature 2020. Tanuj's short fiction has been published in the Caravan, Hindu Business Line, DNA, Out of Print, and several other publications. In 2019, he was awarded the Sahitya Akademi Yuva Puraskar for his short-story collection, Diwali in Muzaffarnagar .

b: Tanwi Nandini Islam is the author of the critically-acclaimed Bright Lines , a finalist for the Center for Fiction First Novel Prize. She is the founder of Hi Wildflower, an independent beauty and fragrance house, and…
f: Tanwi Nandini Islam is the author of the critically-acclaimed Bright Lines , a finalist for the Center for Fiction First Novel Prize. She is the founder of Hi Wildflower, an independent beauty and fragrance house, and is working on her second novel, Stellar Smoke .

b: Tanya Abraham is an author and an art curator based in Kochi. She is also the founder of The Art Outreach Society, a non-profit organisation that works with the arts for mental health and innovative thinking. She worked…
f: Tanya Abraham is an author and an art curator based in Kochi. She is also the founder of The Art Outreach Society, a non-profit organisation that works with the arts for mental health and innovative thinking. She worked as the creative director of Kashi Art Gallery in Kochi and has recently founded Kula, a platform for public art and creative expression. She is the recipient of a number of awards including Iconic Women Creating Change awarded by the World Economic Forum in Birmingham, UK. She is currently pursuing a PhD in Practice in Curating.

b: Tara Gandhi holds an M.Sc degree in Zoology, specializing in Field Ornithology. Currently, she is a Trustee of the Wildlife Trust of India, New Delhi and serves on the committees of the Bombay Natural History Society,…
f: Tara Gandhi holds an M.Sc degree in Zoology, specializing in Field Ornithology. Currently, she is a Trustee of the Wildlife Trust of India, New Delhi and serves on the committees of the Bombay Natural History Society, Madras Naturalists’ Society and the Institutional Ethics Committee of the Indian Institute of Technology, Chennai, India.

b: Tara June Winch was born in Australia and is based in France. She is the author of award-winning novel Swallow the Air and After the Carnage . She was a recipient of the prestigious Rolex Mentor and Protégé Arts…
f: Tara June Winch was born in Australia and is based in France. She is the author of award-winning novel Swallow the Air and After the Carnage . She was a recipient of the prestigious Rolex Mentor and Protégé Arts Award, where she was under the tutelage of Nobel Laureate Wole Soyinka.

b: Taran N Khan is a writer and journalist based in Mumbai. She is the author of Shadow City: A Woman Walks Kabul, which won the Stanford Dolman Travel Book of the Year award and the Tata Literature Live First Book award.
f: Taran N Khan is a writer and journalist based in Mumbai. She is the author of Shadow City: A Woman Walks Kabul, which won the Stanford Dolman Travel Book of the Year award and the Tata Literature Live First Book award.

b: Dr. Tarana Husain Khan is a writer and culinary revivalist based in Rampur. Her works include the historical fiction The Courtesan, Her Lover and I and the bestselling debut novel The Begum and the Dastan . Her…
f: Dr. Tarana Husain Khan is a writer and culinary revivalist based in Rampur. Her works include the historical fiction The Courtesan, Her Lover and I and the bestselling debut novel The Begum and the Dastan . Her critically acclaimed Degh to Dastarkhwan: Qissas and Recipes from Rampur explores Rampur’s culinary history. She has co-edited Forgotten Foods: Memories and Recipes from Muslim South Asia and contributed to Desi Delicacies and Dastarkhwan: Food Writing from South Asia and Diaspora . Her writing appears in leading media outlets and scholarly journals. She was Research Fellow and Consultant at the University of Sheffield on the AHRC project Forgotten Food (2019–2024).

b: Tarini Mohan is the author of Lifequake: A Story of Hope and Humanity (Juggernaut Books, 2025), a memoir exploring love, identity, and the power of human connection after a traumatic brain injury. A writer and…
f: Tarini Mohan is the author of Lifequake: A Story of Hope and Humanity (Juggernaut Books, 2025), a memoir exploring love, identity, and the power of human connection after a traumatic brain injury. A writer and development professional working in public health, her work has appeared widely in national and international publications, both in print and online.

b: Tarun K. Saint , an independent scholar and writer, was born in Kenya, and has lived in India since 1972. His interests include the literature of the Partition and science fiction. He is the author of Witnessing…
f: Tarun K. Saint , an independent scholar and writer, was born in Kenya, and has lived in India since 1972. His interests include the literature of the Partition and science fiction. He is the author of Witnessing Partition: Memory, History, Fiction and editor of Bruised Memories: Communal Violence and the Writer . He has also co-edited Translating Partition and Looking Back: India’s Partition, 70 Years On . He has also edited Volumes 1 and 2 of The Gollancz Book of South Asian Science Fiction. His other co-edited works include the bilingual (Indian-Italian) science fiction anthology Avatar: Indian Science Fiction and the bilingual SF collection Kalicalypse: Subcontinental Science Fiction.

b: Tarun Khanna is the Jorge Paulo Lemann Professor at Harvard where he has taught at HBS and at Harvard College for 25 years, focusing on the role of entrepreneurs in developing countries. He is the first director of…
f: Tarun Khanna is the Jorge Paulo Lemann Professor at Harvard where he has taught at HBS and at Harvard College for 25 years, focusing on the role of entrepreneurs in developing countries. He is the first director of Harvard’s Lakshmi Mittal and Family South Asia Institute, a university-wide endeavor that brings together natural and social scientists with artists and humanists in joint academic pursuits. His latest book, *Trust,and his earlier **Billions of Entrepreneurs, chronicle creative ventures in China, India and beyond. He also co-authored **Winning in Emerging Markets*, a framework for building world-class enterprises in emerging markets. A related free online course on the edX platform, Entrepreneurship in Emerging Economies has been taken by around 600,000 students across 200 countries. He is the co-founder and board member of several commercial and non-profit ventures across emerging markets. Since 2015, he has been appointed to several national commissions by the Government of India on issues related to entrepreneurship and higher education.

b: Tarun Tahiliani started his professional career with a degree in Business Management from the Wharton School of Business, University of Pennsylvania. After returning to India, he saw the vast potential in the fine…
f: Tarun Tahiliani started his professional career with a degree in Business Management from the Wharton School of Business, University of Pennsylvania. After returning to India, he saw the vast potential in the fine clothing and couture industry that was evolving in the country, and in 1987, he opened India’s first multi designer boutique, Ensemble, heralding a fashion and retail revolution in India. In 1991, Tahiliani decided to hone his technical knowledge in design, and received an associate degree from the Fashion Institute of Technology, New York. He founded his design studio in 1995.

b: Tash Aw is the author of five novels, most recently The South , and a memoir of a Chinese-Malaysian family, Strangers on a Pier . His work has received major literary recognition, including the Whitbread Prize, the…
f: Tash Aw is the author of five novels, most recently The South , and a memoir of a Chinese-Malaysian family, Strangers on a Pier . His work has received major literary recognition, including the Whitbread Prize, the Commonwealth Prize, and an O. Henry Award, and has been nominated three times for the Man Booker Prize. Aw’s writing explores identity, migration, and belonging, often drawing on Southeast Asian histories and personal experience. His novels have been translated into 26 languages worldwide.

b: Tasneem Khan is a well-known writer and journalist. Her debut novel Ae Mere Rehnuma was recommended for the Bharatiya Jnanpith Navlekhan Award in 2015. Her second novel, Hamnawai Na Thi , and the short story collection…
f: Tasneem Khan is a well-known writer and journalist. Her debut novel Ae Mere Rehnuma was recommended for the Bharatiya Jnanpith Navlekhan Award in 2015. Her second novel, Hamnawai Na Thi , and the short story collection Dastan-e-Hazrat have also been published. Her latest short story collection, Bawalistan , was recently published by Unbound Script. Tasneem Khan has received several prestigious honors, including the Shakuntalam Award, Ladli Media Award, Chanderbardai Youth Award, Sikhwal Smriti Women’s Writing Award, and the Nirmal Verma Literature Award (2025).

b: Tathagata Bhattacharya is a journalist and sustainability expert who divides his time between the plains of Delhi and the mountains of Uttarakhand. He has over two decades of experience in writing and reporting as well…
f: Tathagata Bhattacharya is a journalist and sustainability expert who divides his time between the plains of Delhi and the mountains of Uttarakhand. He has over two decades of experience in writing and reporting as well as editorial management of diverse teams and media verticals. His current obsession is the mainstreaming of climate change – friendly habitats. He is the only child of cult Bengali writer Nabarun Bhattacharya and the only grandchild of noted playwright-director Bijon Bhattacharya and writer-activist Mahasweta Devi. General Firebrand and His Red Atlas is his first novel.

b: Tawfiq E. Chowdhury grew up in East Pakistan. He began his career as a lecturer at Dacca University and later joined the Civil Service of Pakistan before joining the Liberation War of Bangladesh. He was commissioned in…
f: Tawfiq E. Chowdhury grew up in East Pakistan. He began his career as a lecturer at Dacca University and later joined the Civil Service of Pakistan before joining the Liberation War of Bangladesh. He was commissioned in the Bangladesh Defense Forces, served as sub-sector commander in Sector 8 and was decorated as Bir Bikram for gallantry. He was one of the main organizers of the Proclamation of Independence and swearing-in ceremony of the Government of Bangladesh in Mujibnagar on 17 April, 1971. After serving as Secretary, he retired in 2002 and was made adviser to the Prime Minister of Bangladesh in 2009, a position he still holds. Chariot of Life is his first book.

b: Tejaswini Apte-Rahm is an award-winning writer from Mumbai. Her historical fiction, The Secret of More , won the 2023 Tata Literature Live! Book of the Year (Fiction) Award. It was also shortlisted for the JCB Prize for…
f: Tejaswini Apte-Rahm is an award-winning writer from Mumbai. Her historical fiction, The Secret of More , won the 2023 Tata Literature Live! Book of the Year (Fiction) Award. It was also shortlisted for the JCB Prize for Literature, Atta Galatta Prize and Tagore Prize. Her story collection, These Circuses That Sweep Through the Landscape was critically acclaimed.

b: Tejaswini Niranjana is the author of Musicophilia in Mumbai as well as several other monographs on music, gender and cultural translation. She won the DSC South Asia Prize for her translation of Jayant Kaikini's…
f: Tejaswini Niranjana is the author of Musicophilia in Mumbai as well as several other monographs on music, gender and cultural translation. She won the DSC South Asia Prize for her translation of Jayant Kaikini's stories, No Presents Please . In 2020, she was Chair of the JCB Literary Prize jury.

b: Tenzing Lamsang is the Editor of The Bhutanese . He was awarded the Best Investigative Journalism Award for four consecutive years by Bhutan’s Annual Journalism awards. Having worked with The Indian Express as a…
f: Tenzing Lamsang is the Editor of The Bhutanese . He was awarded the Best Investigative Journalism Award for four consecutive years by Bhutan’s Annual Journalism awards. Having worked with The Indian Express as a reporter, he moved to Bhutan’s national newspaper Kuensel as Chief Reporter in 2008 before working with Bhutan’s first business paper Business Bhutan as its News Editor from 2010. Lamsang launched The Bhutanese in 2012. He has contributed papers to the Institute of Defense and Studies Analysis think tank in New Delhi on Bhutan and has also written articles for various international publications on Bhutan.

b: Terence Ward’s works include Searching for Hassan: A Journey to the Heart of Iran, The Guardian of Mercy: How an Extraordinary Painting by Caravaggio Changed an Ordinary Life and his latest The Wahhabi Code: How the…
f: Terence Ward’s works include Searching for Hassan: A Journey to the Heart of Iran, The Guardian of Mercy: How an Extraordinary Painting by Caravaggio Changed an Ordinary Life and his latest The Wahhabi Code: How the Saudis Spread Extremism Globally.

b: Thant Myint-U is the author of four books on Burmese and Asian history, most recently The Hidden History of Burma: Race, Capitalism, and the Crisis of Democracy in the 21st Century . Educated at Harvard and Cambridge…
f: Thant Myint-U is the author of four books on Burmese and Asian history, most recently The Hidden History of Burma: Race, Capitalism, and the Crisis of Democracy in the 21st Century . Educated at Harvard and Cambridge University, he taught British imperial history from 1995-2000 as a Fellow of Trinity College, Cambridge. He has also served on three United Nations peacekeeping operations. Since 2007, he has been involved in numerous reforms efforts in Myanmar, including as a member of the National Economic and Social Advisory Council, a special adviser to the government on the peace process, the founder and chairman of the Yangon Heritage Trust and the chairman of U Thant House. He is the recipient of several honours, including the Padma Shri from the Government of India in 2018.

b: Thomas J. Bollyky is the inaugural Bloomberg Chair in Global Health at the Council on Foreign Relations (CFR), where he directs the global health program. A senior fellow for international economics, law, and…
f: Thomas J. Bollyky is the inaugural Bloomberg Chair in Global Health at the Council on Foreign Relations (CFR), where he directs the global health program. A senior fellow for international economics, law, and development at CFR, he is also a senior consultant to the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations and founding editor of Think Global Health .

b: Tiffany Tsao is a writer and literary translator. Her novel The Majesties was longlisted for Australia's Ned Kelly Prize, and her translation of Norman Erikson Pasaribu’s Happy Stories, Mostly was the winner of the…
f: Tiffany Tsao is a writer and literary translator. Her novel The Majesties was longlisted for Australia's Ned Kelly Prize, and her translation of Norman Erikson Pasaribu’s Happy Stories, Mostly was the winner of the 2022 Republic of Consciousness Prize and longlisted for the International Booker Prize. Her translation of Budi Darma’s People from Bloomington came out in 2022 with Penguin Classics.

b: Tilak Gitai is a maestro painter who is the recipient of the Padma Shri and the National Award. Tilak hails from the second generation of royal court painters, patronised by the erstwhile rulers of Bikaner. He…
f: Tilak Gitai is a maestro painter who is the recipient of the Padma Shri and the National Award. Tilak hails from the second generation of royal court painters, patronised by the erstwhile rulers of Bikaner. He specialises in Indian traditional miniature paintings, namely in Mughal, Rajasthani and Phadi painting styles. He has exhibited across the world including the Victoria Albert Museum, London; National Museum of Ethnology-Osaka Japan; National Crafts Museum-New Delhi.

b: Tilly Blyth co-presented a landmark 20-part Radio Series with the BBC on The Art of Innovation , includes a book and an Exhibition that looks at the shared cultures of art and science over the past 250 years. She is…
f: Tilly Blyth co-presented a landmark 20-part Radio Series with the BBC on The Art of Innovation , includes a book and an Exhibition that looks at the shared cultures of art and science over the past 250 years. She is Head of Collections and Principal Curator at the Science Museum in London, where she is responsible for a curatorial team that have developed award winning galleries and exhibitions on subjects as diverse as Information Age , Mathematics, Robots, Cosmonauts: the Russian Space story and Illuminating India: 500 years of science and technology . Dr. Blythe is a member of the British Academy of Film, Television and the Arts (BAFTA) and a trustee of the Bletchley Park Trust and the Rasberry Pi Foundation which aims to put the power of digital making into the hands of people all over the world.

b: Tim Adams has been a writer and editor at The Observer and at Granta in London. He is currently editor of the Observer's New Review.
f: Tim Adams has been a writer and editor at The Observer and at Granta in London. He is currently editor of the Observer's New Review.

b: Tim I Gurung joined the British Gurkhas at 17 and retired in 1993 as an Army Corporal, after which he became a businessman. Before his 50th birthday, he made a life-changing decision and became a full-time writer and…
f: Tim I Gurung joined the British Gurkhas at 17 and retired in 1993 as an Army Corporal, after which he became a businessman. Before his 50th birthday, he made a life-changing decision and became a full-time writer and has since written a dozen novels, including the acclaimed Gurkha book.

b: Tim Mackintosh-Smith , historian and translator, was born in England but has lived in the Arab world for forty years. His books include a travel trilogy on the fourteenth-century wanderer Ibn Battutah, and a 3,000-year…
f: Tim Mackintosh-Smith , historian and translator, was born in England but has lived in the Arab world for forty years. His books include a travel trilogy on the fourteenth-century wanderer Ibn Battutah, and a 3,000-year history, Arabs . He is a Senior Research Fellow of the New York University Library of Arabic Literature.

b: Tim Parks , an author and translator based in Italy, has published twenty novels, including Europa, Destiny and In Extremis. His non-fiction works include the bestselling Italian Neighbours and a memoir on chronic pain…
f: Tim Parks , an author and translator based in Italy, has published twenty novels, including Europa, Destiny and In Extremis. His non-fiction works include the bestselling Italian Neighbours and a memoir on chronic pain and meditation, Teach Us to Sit Still . He is a regular contributor to the New York Review of Books and the London Review of Books.

b: Timmie Kumar is a dedicated animal advocate and Managing Trustee of Help in Suffering (HIS), a nonprofit organization providing free veterinary treatment to animals in Jaipur. With a lifelong passion for animal welfare,…
f: Timmie Kumar is a dedicated animal advocate and Managing Trustee of Help in Suffering (HIS), a nonprofit organization providing free veterinary treatment to animals in Jaipur. With a lifelong passion for animal welfare, Timmie has worked tirelessly for over three decades, rescuing animals from circuses, rehoming strays, and caring for wildlife. Under her leadership, HIS has achieved remarkable milestones, including creating a rabies-free environment in Jaipur and establishing the Camel Rescue Centre in Bassi, a sanctuary dedicated to the treatment and care of camels. Recognised for her outstanding contributions, Timmie has received awards from Humane Society International and the "Pride of Jaipur" award.

b: Tina Brown is a writer and former editor of Tatler , Vanity Fair , The New Yorker , and founder of The Daily Beast . She ran Women in the World summits in New York, London, and Delhi. Author of The Vanity Fair Diaries ,…
f: Tina Brown is a writer and former editor of Tatler , Vanity Fair , The New Yorker , and founder of The Daily Beast . She ran Women in the World summits in New York, London, and Delhi. Author of The Vanity Fair Diaries , The Diana Chronicles , and The Palace Papers , her Substack newsletter is Fresh Hell: Tina Brown's Diary .

b: Tina Narang is the Executive Publisher of Children’s Books at HarperCollins India. Tina joined HarperCollins in 2017 and launched the children’s imprint, HarperCollins Children’s Books. Prior to this, she worked with…
f: Tina Narang is the Executive Publisher of Children’s Books at HarperCollins India. Tina joined HarperCollins in 2017 and launched the children’s imprint, HarperCollins Children’s Books. Prior to this, she worked with Scholastic India for over a decade.

b: Tinni Sawhney is the Chief Executive Officer of the Aga Khan Foundation in India. She has worked extensively on sustainable livelihoods, agriculture and livestock development for smallholder farmers in the rainfed…
f: Tinni Sawhney is the Chief Executive Officer of the Aga Khan Foundation in India. She has worked extensively on sustainable livelihoods, agriculture and livestock development for smallholder farmers in the rainfed regions of India, with a particular focus on strengthening gender perspectives.

b: TM Krishna is a vocalist in the Carnatic tradition. As a public intellectual, Krishna speaks and writes about issues affecting the human condition and about matters cultural. Krishna has started and is involved in many…
f: TM Krishna is a vocalist in the Carnatic tradition. As a public intellectual, Krishna speaks and writes about issues affecting the human condition and about matters cultural. Krishna has started and is involved in many organisations whose work is spread across the whole spectrum of music and culture. He has co-authored Voices Within: Carnatic Music: Passing on an Inheritance , a book dedicated to the greats of Carnatic music. His path-breaking book A Southern Music: The Karnatik Story , published in 2013, was a first-of-its-kind philosophical, aesthetic and socio-political exploration of the genre. For this, he was awarded the 2014 Tata Literature Award for Best First Book in the non-fiction category. His long-form essay ‘MS Understood’ for The Caravan was featured in The Caravan Book of Profiles , as one of their ‘twelve definitive profiles’. It has been translated into Tamil and published as the book Katrinile Karainda Tuyar . His 2018 book Reshaping Art asks important questions about how art is made, performed and disseminated and addresses crucial issues of caste, class and gender within society while exploring the contours of democracy, culture and learning. He is the driving force behind the Chennai Kalai Theru Vizha and the Svanubhava initiative. He has been part of inspiring collaborations, such as the Chennai Poromboke Paadal with environmentalist Nityanand Jayaraman, performances with the Jogappas (transgender musicians) and co-conceptualising and performing Karnatic Kattaikuttu, an unusual aesthetic conversation between art forms and communities that belong to two ends of the social spectrum. His musico-poetic partnership with India’s leading contemporary Tamil writer Perumal Murugan, is unprecedented. In 2016, Krishna received the prestigious Ramon

b: Toby Walsh is a Professor of AI at UNSW Sydney. He is a strong advocate for limits to ensure AI is used to improve our lives, having spoken at the UN, and to heads of state, parliamentary bodies, company boards and many…
f: Toby Walsh is a Professor of AI at UNSW Sydney. He is a strong advocate for limits to ensure AI is used to improve our lives, having spoken at the UN, and to heads of state, parliamentary bodies, company boards and many other bodies on this topic. He is a Fellow of the Australia Academy of Science, and was named on the international "Who's Who in AI" list of influencers. He has authored three books on AI for a general audience, the most recent entitled "Machines Behaving Badly: the morality of AI".

b: Tom Freston is a cofounder of MTV and the former CEO of Viacom, where he oversaw Paramount Pictures. After launching a successful clothing export company out of Afghanistan and India, Freston transitioned into the media…
f: Tom Freston is a cofounder of MTV and the former CEO of Viacom, where he oversaw Paramount Pictures. After launching a successful clothing export company out of Afghanistan and India, Freston transitioned into the media landscape, helping found MTV and bringing it to international fame in more than 150 countries. Before his Viacom roles, he ran MTV Networks for seventeen years, overseeing Nickelodeon, VH1, Comedy Central, and other legendary networks. He is a board member of Imagine Entertainment and a board member emeritus of both the American Museum of Natural History and the think tank New America. He currently serves as Board Chair of The ONE Campaign, an anti-poverty advocacy organization focusing on Africa. He is the author of the new memoir, UNPLUGGED: Adventures from MTV to Timbuktu.

b: Tom Holland , an award-winning historian, translator and broadcaster, is the co-presenter of Europe’s most downloaded history podcast, The Rest is History , and has written and presented several TV documentaries on…
f: Tom Holland , an award-winning historian, translator and broadcaster, is the co-presenter of Europe’s most downloaded history podcast, The Rest is History , and has written and presented several TV documentaries on subjects ranging from ISIS to dinosaurs. Holland has been described in The Times as “a leading English cricketer”.

b: Tom Miller is a writer specialising in Asian geopolitics and economic affairs. Resident in China for 14 years and a former journalist with the South China Morning Post , he has reported from a dozen countries in Asia…
f: Tom Miller is a writer specialising in Asian geopolitics and economic affairs. Resident in China for 14 years and a former journalist with the South China Morning Post , he has reported from a dozen countries in Asia and visited more than 100 Chinese cities. His most recent book is China’s Asian Dream: Empire Building Along the New Silk Road . Miller is an Indophile who speaks fluent Chinese.

b: Tom Segev is among Israel’s best known journalists and historians. Born 1945 in Jerusalem, his weekly column was published for 39 years in Haaretz. Segev’s books, which deal with Israeli history and the Holocaust,…
f: Tom Segev is among Israel’s best known journalists and historians. Born 1945 in Jerusalem, his weekly column was published for 39 years in Haaretz. Segev’s books, which deal with Israeli history and the Holocaust, have been published in 16 languages. His latest book is A State at Any Cost: The Life of David Ben-Gurion.

b: Tom Stoppard ’s first full-length play, Rosencrantz and Guildenstern Are Dead , was staged by the National Theatre in 1967. This was followed by other award-winning works, including Jumpers , Every Good Boy Deserves…
f: Tom Stoppard ’s first full-length play, Rosencrantz and Guildenstern Are Dead , was staged by the National Theatre in 1967. This was followed by other award-winning works, including Jumpers , Every Good Boy Deserves Favour (with Andre Previn), Travesties , Night and Day , The Real Thing , Hapgood , Arcadia , Indian Ink , The Invention of Love , The Coast of Utopia (a trilogy), Rock’n’Roll and The Hard Problem . His stage adaptations and translations include Undiscovered Country , On the Razzle , Rough Crossing , The Seagull , Henry IV , Heroes , Ivanov and The Cherry Orchard . Stoppard has also written for radio, television and film. His screen credits, as writer and co-writer, include Brazil , Empire of the Sun , Enigma and Shakespeare in Love , winner of an Academy Award for Best Original Screenplay. He also directed his own screenplay of Rosencrantz and Guildenstern Are Dead , which won the Golden Lion at the Venice Film Festival. Stoppard received a knighthood in 1997 and in 2000 was awarded the Order of Merit by Her Majesty the Queen.

b: Tomoko Kikuchi was born in Fukushima, Japan, and has been living in India since 1992. She earned her B.A. in Hindi from Maharani’s College, Jaipur, and completed her M.A., M.Phil., and Ph.D. in Hindi at Jawaharlal Nehru…
f: Tomoko Kikuchi was born in Fukushima, Japan, and has been living in India since 1992. She earned her B.A. in Hindi from Maharani’s College, Jaipur, and completed her M.A., M.Phil., and Ph.D. in Hindi at Jawaharlal Nehru University, New Delhi. Her work focuses on social issues and peace, particularly the impact of atomic warfare. Her publications and translations include Mahadevi Varma ka Vishvadrishti (2009) and several Japanese works translated into Hindi, such as Hiroshima no Pika . She received the 9th World Hindi Conference Award in South Africa (2012), among other honors.

b: Austrian author Tonio Schachinger was born in New Delhi in 1992. He studied language arts at the University of Applied Arts Vienna. Nicht wie ihr , his first novel, was shortlisted for the German Book Prize in 2019. In…
f: Austrian author Tonio Schachinger was born in New Delhi in 1992. He studied language arts at the University of Applied Arts Vienna. Nicht wie ihr , his first novel, was shortlisted for the German Book Prize in 2019. In 2023, he received the German Book Prize for his second novel, Echtzeitalter . Tonio Schachinger lives in Vienna.

b: Tony Joseph is the author of Early Indians , a critically acclaimed, award-winning bestseller on the population formation of India. The book has been translated into six languages, and a children’s edition was released…
f: Tony Joseph is the author of Early Indians , a critically acclaimed, award-winning bestseller on the population formation of India. The book has been translated into six languages, and a children’s edition was released recently. Tony is currently working on a sequel that will focus on India’s cultural formation

b: Tova Reich is the author of the novels Mother India, One Hundred Philistine Foreskins, My Holocaust, The Jewish War, Master of the Return and Mara . Her stories have appeared in the Atlantic , Harper’s , AGNI ,…
f: Tova Reich is the author of the novels Mother India, One Hundred Philistine Foreskins, My Holocaust, The Jewish War, Master of the Return and Mara . Her stories have appeared in the Atlantic , Harper’s , AGNI , Ploughshares , and elsewhere. She is the recipient of the National Magazine Award for Fiction, the Edward Lewis Wallant Book Award as well as other prizes.

b: Tridip Suhrud works on the life and thought of Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi and the intellectual and cultural history of modern Gujarat. His most recent work are the critical edition of Gandhi’s autobiography and a…
f: Tridip Suhrud works on the life and thought of Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi and the intellectual and cultural history of modern Gujarat. His most recent work are the critical edition of Gandhi’s autobiography and a translation of Govardhanram Tripathi’s four part novel Sarasvatichandra .

b: Tripurdaman Singh is a British Academy Postdoctoral Fellow at the Institute of Commonwealth Studies, University of London and a Visiting Fellow at the International Institute of Asian Studies, Universiteit Leiden. He is…
f: Tripurdaman Singh is a British Academy Postdoctoral Fellow at the Institute of Commonwealth Studies, University of London and a Visiting Fellow at the International Institute of Asian Studies, Universiteit Leiden. He is the author of Imperial Sovereignty and Local Politics: The Bhadauria Rajputs and the Transition from Mughal to British India, 1600-1900 and Sixteen Stormy Days: The Story of the First Amendment to the Constitution of India. His latest book is Nehru: The Debates that defined India .

b: Trisha Das is a bestselling author and award-winning filmmaker. Her books span romance, history, mythology, and contemporary fiction, often blurring the lines between the real and the ridiculous. She is the author of…
f: Trisha Das is a bestselling author and award-winning filmmaker. Her books span romance, history, mythology, and contemporary fiction, often blurring the lines between the real and the ridiculous. She is the author of Never Meant to Stay , the Ms Draupadi Kuru series, and Kama’s Last Sutra , among others. Before turning full-time to fiction, Trisha directed over forty documentaries, won India’s National Film Award, and was named the University of Georgia’s International Artist of the Year. Her writing has appeared in Cosmopolitan , Harper’s Bazaar , Hindustan Times , Scroll , and the feminist fantasy anthology Magical Women .

b: Tristram Hunt is Director of the V&A, the world’s leading museum of art, design and performance. Since taking up the post in 2017, he has championed design education in schools in the UK, encouraged debate around the…
f: Tristram Hunt is Director of the V&A, the world’s leading museum of art, design and performance. Since taking up the post in 2017, he has championed design education in schools in the UK, encouraged debate around the history of the museum’s global collections and overseen its transition to a multi-site museum.

b: Truda Spruyt FRSA has worked in the literary world for over 30 years and founded Collective Wisdom in September 2024. She specialises in devising and delivering integrated communications strategies and in leading teams…
f: Truda Spruyt FRSA has worked in the literary world for over 30 years and founded Collective Wisdom in September 2024. She specialises in devising and delivering integrated communications strategies and in leading teams on complex, high-profile projects. Truda has played a key role in developing the prestige and public profile of major literary prizes, including the International Booker Prize and the Baillie Gifford Prize for Non-Fiction. She is Honorary Secretary of the Book Society, a long-standing member of the organisation, and an Ambassador for the Blake Cottage Trust.

b: Tshering Tashi is a writer known for his works in the field of creative nonfiction. In the last two decades, he has authored numerous books on Bhutan and has made the country’s rich history and its diverse culture…
f: Tshering Tashi is a writer known for his works in the field of creative nonfiction. In the last two decades, he has authored numerous books on Bhutan and has made the country’s rich history and its diverse culture interesting, accessible, and engaging for the youth. Tashi is the Co-Director of the Bhutan Echoes Literary Festival.

b: Uday Bhatia is the author of Bullets Over Bombay: Satya and the Hindi film Gangster . He works as a film critic with Mint Lounge in Delhi. His writing has appeared in Time Out, The Caravan, The Indian Quarterly, GQ, The…
f: Uday Bhatia is the author of Bullets Over Bombay: Satya and the Hindi film Gangster . He works as a film critic with Mint Lounge in Delhi. His writing has appeared in Time Out, The Caravan, The Indian Quarterly, GQ, The Indian Express and other publications.

b: Uday Mahurkar is an author, historian and a former senior deputy editor of India Today magazine who has penned two books on PM Narendra Modi’s governance. His third book, Veer Savarkar: The Man Who Could Have…
f: Uday Mahurkar is an author, historian and a former senior deputy editor of India Today magazine who has penned two books on PM Narendra Modi’s governance. His third book, Veer Savarkar: The Man Who Could Have Prevented Partition , with a foreword by RSS Sarsanghchalak, Dr Mohan Bhagwat, was launched recently. He is currently a Central Information Commissioner with the Government of India.

b: Uday Prakash is one of the few Indian language writers who has been widely translated into vernacular and major foreign languages. Most of his short stories have been adapted for the stage and films. In 2015, he came…
f: Uday Prakash is one of the few Indian language writers who has been widely translated into vernacular and major foreign languages. Most of his short stories have been adapted for the stage and films. In 2015, he came into focus when he returned the Sahitya Akademi Award in protest against the murder of dissenting writers, which turned out to become a central nonconformist movement of writers and artists in India.

b: Uday S. Kulkarni has written three historical nonfiction books titled, Solstice at Panipat , The Era of Bajirao and The Bakhar of Panipat . He is currently writing his next book, The Mastery of Hindustan: A Narrative of…
f: Uday S. Kulkarni has written three historical nonfiction books titled, Solstice at Panipat , The Era of Bajirao and The Bakhar of Panipat . He is currently writing his next book, The Mastery of Hindustan: A Narrative of Maratha Paramountcy in 18th Century India . An alumnus of the Armed Forces Medical College in Pune and a surgeon by profession, Kulkarni served in the Indian Navy retiring in the rank of Surgeon Commander.

b: Udayan Mitra is Executive Publisher at HarperCollins India. In a publishing career spanning twenty-five years, he has led various functions within publishing and has published some of India’s finest authors and…
f: Udayan Mitra is Executive Publisher at HarperCollins India. In a publishing career spanning twenty-five years, he has led various functions within publishing and has published some of India’s finest authors and several award-winning and critically acclaimed books.

b: Ugo Astuto , Ambassador of the European Union to India since October 2019, entered the Italian Diplomatic Service in 1991. His career in the Italian Foreign Service spans experiences across embassies including Nairobi,…
f: Ugo Astuto , Ambassador of the European Union to India since October 2019, entered the Italian Diplomatic Service in 1991. His career in the Italian Foreign Service spans experiences across embassies including Nairobi, London, as alternate Director for Italy in the EBRD - European Bank for Reconstruction and Development, in the Permanent Representation in Brussels and in the Embassy in Delhi, where he served as Deputy Head of Mission. From February 2013 until July 2016, he was seconded to the European External Action Service (EEAS) in Brussels, first as Director for South and South East Asia and then as Deputy Managing Director/Director for Asia and the Pacific. From July 2016 to September 2019 he was the Principal Director for Asia in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Rome.

b: Ujan Dutta is a self-taught illustrator and graphic designer based in India. Dutta has been drawing the superhuman and the extraordinary since he first could hold a pencil. The ability of fantasy, in particular, to take…
f: Ujan Dutta is a self-taught illustrator and graphic designer based in India. Dutta has been drawing the superhuman and the extraordinary since he first could hold a pencil. The ability of fantasy, in particular, to take the viewer into a world of infinite possibility, the magical, unreal and unknown has always fascinated him. Magic realism, mystical, miraculous situations and vistas take centre stage in his work. While loosely based on the depictions of the divine in Hindu mythology, the style in these works is completely and inimitably his own. Dutta independent work has been exhibited in India and abroad. Professionally, he has worked on numerous visual communication projects including the ZEE Jaipur Literature Festival itself.

b: Ulrike Almut Sandig has published two books of short stories, four poetry collections and three albums of poetry in pop music. She has won many prizes and collaborates with filmmakers and musicians as the Mumbai-based…
f: Ulrike Almut Sandig has published two books of short stories, four poetry collections and three albums of poetry in pop music. She has won many prizes and collaborates with filmmakers and musicians as the Mumbai-based band ALIF.

b: Upamanyu Chatterjee is a former civil servant who has spent over 30 calm and undistinguished years in the Indian Administrative Service. During that time, he wrote six novels—when no one was looking. He retired (early…
f: Upamanyu Chatterjee is a former civil servant who has spent over 30 calm and undistinguished years in the Indian Administrative Service. During that time, he wrote six novels—when no one was looking. He retired (early and honourably) in 2016 to devote himself full time to running the household.

b: Upinder Singh is Professor of History, Ashoka University. She has published widely on various aspects of ancient Indian history, archeology, and the modern histories of ancient sites and monuments. Her most recent book…
f: Upinder Singh is Professor of History, Ashoka University. She has published widely on various aspects of ancient Indian history, archeology, and the modern histories of ancient sites and monuments. Her most recent book is Ancient India: Culture of Contradictions.

b: Urmimala Sarkar Munsi , has recently retired as the Dean and Professor from the School of Arts and Aesthetics, JNU. She is a dancer and choreographer and holds a PH.D. in Social Anthropology. Her recent books are Uday…
f: Urmimala Sarkar Munsi , has recently retired as the Dean and Professor from the School of Arts and Aesthetics, JNU. She is a dancer and choreographer and holds a PH.D. in Social Anthropology. Her recent books are Uday Shankar and his Transcultural Experimentations: Dancing Modernity , Mapping Critical Dance Studies in India , and The Dancing Body: Labour, Livelihood, Leisure .

b: Dr Ursula Weekes is an independent art historian based in London, specialising in Mughal and Rajput art and culture. She teaches at various academic and museum settings, including the Courtauld Institute of Art, the V&A…
f: Dr Ursula Weekes is an independent art historian based in London, specialising in Mughal and Rajput art and culture. She teaches at various academic and museum settings, including the Courtauld Institute of Art, the V&A Academy and formerly at JNU in Delhi. She is currently writing a book on Mughal Court Painting in India for Reaktion Books Ltd.

b: Urvashi Butalia is the Co-founder of India's first feminist publishing house, Kali for Women (1984). Butalia currently runs Zubaan, another feminist imprint. She is an independent writer and researcher, with a five…
f: Urvashi Butalia is the Co-founder of India's first feminist publishing house, Kali for Women (1984). Butalia currently runs Zubaan, another feminist imprint. She is an independent writer and researcher, with a five decade long involvement in the women's movement in India, writing and publishing widely on a range of issues regarding women and gender. Among her best known publications is the award-winning history of Partition, The Other Side of Silence: Voices from the Partition of India (winner of the Oral History Book Association Award 2001 and the Nikkei Asia Award for Culture 2003). Her new book on the life of a hijra, Mona: The Book of Sundays is forthcoming .

b: Urvashi Warman has been associated with the field of education for about three decades. A strong advocate of inclusive education, she is currently working as The Principal of The Palace School, Jaipur. Warman has…
f: Urvashi Warman has been associated with the field of education for about three decades. A strong advocate of inclusive education, she is currently working as The Principal of The Palace School, Jaipur. Warman has written a series of books on EVS and General Studies, and her book The Camel With A Japi , written under the initiative of Ek Bharat Shresth Bharat, has received a letter of commendation from Shri Dharmendra Pradhan, Hon’ble Minister of Education, Government of India.

b: Dr. Usha Mujoo Munshi is President, Information and Communication Society of India. A Fulbright Scholar, she has served at many prestigious organizations and is currently with India International Centre (IIC). She has…
f: Dr. Usha Mujoo Munshi is President, Information and Communication Society of India. A Fulbright Scholar, she has served at many prestigious organizations and is currently with India International Centre (IIC). She has contributed substantially to digital library and digitisation projects and been instrumental in setting up e-resources and e-research journal projects way back in 1999/2000. She has also contributed to the Open Access (OA) movement and initiated several initiatives in this direction. Having travelled widely, she has delivered several lectures across the world.

b: Usha Sharma currently holds charge of Chief Secretary, Government of Rajasthan from. She served as Secretary, Department of Youth Affairs in the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, New Delhi and additional charge of…
f: Usha Sharma currently holds charge of Chief Secretary, Government of Rajasthan from. She served as Secretary, Department of Youth Affairs in the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, New Delhi and additional charge of Director General, Archaeological Survey of India.

b: Usha Uthup is an Indian pop singer who has been spreading the message of love and unity through music for over five decades. She has recorded over a hundred albums and sings in seventeen Indian and eight foreign…
f: Usha Uthup is an Indian pop singer who has been spreading the message of love and unity through music for over five decades. She has recorded over a hundred albums and sings in seventeen Indian and eight foreign languages. Uthup has worked with innumerable NGOs supporting research for cancer, aids, women trafficking and child abuse, and was awarded the Person of the World by President Daniel Arap Moi and was honoured with the Key to Kenya by the late President Mzee Jomo Kenyatta for her contribution to bringing communities of the world together through music. Uthup is the recipient of the coveted Padma Shri Award, the Film Fare Award for the song "Darling" in 2011 and the Life Time Achievement Award from Radio Mirchi in 2017, among numerous others.

b: Ussama Makdisi is the inaugural May Ziadeh Chair in Palestinian and Arab Studies and Professor of History at the University of California Berkeley. His most recent book is Age of Coexistence: The Ecumenical Frame and…
f: Ussama Makdisi is the inaugural May Ziadeh Chair in Palestinian and Arab Studies and Professor of History at the University of California Berkeley. His most recent book is Age of Coexistence: The Ecumenical Frame and the Making of the Modern Arab World . Ussama co-hosts the Makdisi Street podcast.

b: V Tankha recently retired as Head of the Department of Philosophy from St Stephen’s College, the University of Delhi. His interests include ethics and ancient Greek literature and philosophy. His most recent book,…
f: V Tankha recently retired as Head of the Department of Philosophy from St Stephen’s College, the University of Delhi. His interests include ethics and ancient Greek literature and philosophy. His most recent book, Poetry and Politics in Ancient Greece , was published in 2019.
