f: V. V. Ganeshananthan is the author of Brotherless Night , which won the 2024 Women's Prize for Fiction and the 2024 Carol Shields Prize. The novel was also a New York Times Editors’ Choice and an NPR Book of the Year . She co-hosts Literary Hub’s Fiction/Non/Fiction podcast.

b: VJ James was born and brought up in Kerala and writes in Malayalam. An engineer by profession, he worked at the Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre. His debut novel Purappadinte Pusthakam (aka The Book of Exodus) bagged the DC…
f: VJ James was born and brought up in Kerala and writes in Malayalam. An engineer by profession, he worked at the Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre. His debut novel Purappadinte Pusthakam (aka The Book of Exodus) bagged the DC books Silver Jubilee Award & Malayattoor Prize. His novel Anti-Clock was shortlisted for the JCB Prize for Literature 2021 and has won the O.V. Vijayan Award & Thikkurissi Award. For Nireeswaran , one of the author’s most celebrated novels, he received the Thoppil Ravi award, Basheer Puraskaram, Kerala Bhasha Institute Award, Kerala Sahitya Akademi Award & Vayalar Award. The English translation of Chorashasthram was shortlisted for the Atta Galatta Bangalore Literature Festival Book Prize.

b: Vaibhav Budhraja is Senior Director and Head of Marketing at The/Nudge Institute , working at the intersection of social innovation, public systems, and capital to build resilient livelihoods and enable inclusive…
f: Vaibhav Budhraja is Senior Director and Head of Marketing at The/Nudge Institute , working at the intersection of social innovation, public systems, and capital to build resilient livelihoods and enable inclusive growth. Drawing on over 15 years across FMCG, Technology, Education, and Social impact sectors, he brings a practitioner’s lens to questions of scale, accountability, and durable social change.

b: Vaishali Mathur is the Publisher for Indian Languages at Penguin Random House India, overseeing Penguin Swadesh, the division dedicated to Indian-language publishing, with a focus on Hindi literature and translations.…
f: Vaishali Mathur is the Publisher for Indian Languages at Penguin Random House India, overseeing Penguin Swadesh, the division dedicated to Indian-language publishing, with a focus on Hindi literature and translations. Her editorial expertise spans literary and commercial fiction, non-fiction, and Mind-Body-Spirit genres. She has been instrumental in shaping the lists of imprints such as Penguin Metro Reads and Penguin Ananda, championing diverse regional voices and expanding their reach within a global publishing platform. Through her vision and editorial leadership, Vaishali continues to promote Indian-language literature, bridging local narratives with wider audiences and nurturing a vibrant literary ecosystem in India.

b: Vanamala Viswanatha has taught English language and literature over the last 40 years at various levels beginning from high school students to PhD scholars in premiere institutions in Bengaluru. Professor Viswanatha is…
f: Vanamala Viswanatha has taught English language and literature over the last 40 years at various levels beginning from high school students to PhD scholars in premiere institutions in Bengaluru. Professor Viswanatha is an award-winning translator who works with Kannada and English. She has served as Honorary Director for the Centre for Translation at Sahitya Akademi, Bangalore and a member of the Advisory Committee, National Translation Mission. Chief among her published works are the translations of Torgny Linndgren’s The Way of the Serpent into Kannada, Sara Aboobacker’s Kannada novel, Breaking Ties , into English, Lankesh’s anthology of short stories When Stone Melts , Raghavanka’s medieval epic Harishchandra Kavyam and Indira Bai , a forthcoming translation of the first social novel in Kannada.

b: Vandana Bhandari is a Professor at the National Institute of Fashion Technology, New Delhi and is the former Dean Academics of the Institute. Bhandari has also authored and compiled books on Fashion and Textiles. Her…
f: Vandana Bhandari is a Professor at the National Institute of Fashion Technology, New Delhi and is the former Dean Academics of the Institute. Bhandari has also authored and compiled books on Fashion and Textiles. Her works include Costume, Textiles and Jewellery of India – Traditions in Rajasthan; Jewelled Textiles: Gold and Silver embellished Cloth of India.

b: Vandana Saxena Poria is a counterfactual thinker, storyteller and curator, who alters mindsets for individuals as well as clients like Tata Sons. A Chartered Accountant and a serial entrepreneur, she has lived and…
f: Vandana Saxena Poria is a counterfactual thinker, storyteller and curator, who alters mindsets for individuals as well as clients like Tata Sons. A Chartered Accountant and a serial entrepreneur, she has lived and worked in 10+ countries. Along with the late Alyque Padamsee, she co-authored Let Me Hijack Your Mind: Restart Your Life With Freedom . She is a recipient of the Order of the British Empire.

b: Vandana Singh is a writer of literary science fiction, a professor of physics and a transdisciplinary scholar of climate change. Her highly acclaimed short stories have been reprinted in several Year’s Best volumes…
f: Vandana Singh is a writer of literary science fiction, a professor of physics and a transdisciplinary scholar of climate change. Her highly acclaimed short stories have been reprinted in several Year’s Best volumes and her recent collection, Ambiguity Machines & Other Stories, was a Crossword and Philip K. Dick Award Finalist

b: Vandana Singh-Lal is a forester and a writer. While living, observing and trying to align the world inside her head with the 'real' world around her, Singh, in the words of DeLillo, grew into novel hood. Her debut…
f: Vandana Singh-Lal is a forester and a writer. While living, observing and trying to align the world inside her head with the 'real' world around her, Singh, in the words of DeLillo, grew into novel hood. Her debut novel, So All Is Peace , was published by Penguin Random House in December 2019.

b: Vandana Vasudevan is a social science researcher who has written numerous articles for English dailies in India and authored three books, the latest of which is OTP Please! . She studied management at the Indian…
f: Vandana Vasudevan is a social science researcher who has written numerous articles for English dailies in India and authored three books, the latest of which is OTP Please! . She studied management at the Indian Institute of Management, Ahmedabad, and transitioned from the corporate sector to the development sector after completing a mid-career PhD in urban studies from the University of Grenoble, France.

b: Vanessa R. Sasson is a professor of Religious Studies in the Liberal Arts Department of Marianopolis College and a Research Fellow at the University of the Free State. She is the author of a number of academic books and…
f: Vanessa R. Sasson is a professor of Religious Studies in the Liberal Arts Department of Marianopolis College and a Research Fellow at the University of the Free State. She is the author of a number of academic books and articles. Yasodhara and the Buddha was her first novel; The Gathering: A Story of the First Buddhist Women is its sequel.

b: Vanessa Thorpe has written about books and entertainment for The Observer for two decades. Based in London, she is a veteran of the Hay Festival and also covers fine art, theatre, and cinema. After graduating in…
f: Vanessa Thorpe has written about books and entertainment for The Observer for two decades. Based in London, she is a veteran of the Hay Festival and also covers fine art, theatre, and cinema. After graduating in English, she trained in journalism and wrote for The London Evening Standard and The Independent on Sunday .

b: Vani Bhalla Pahwa is a dancer, columnist and medical fitness specialist. She performs multi-faceted roles with elegant and professional aplomb. An established Mohiniyattam dancer, she brings a distinct, refined…
f: Vani Bhalla Pahwa is a dancer, columnist and medical fitness specialist. She performs multi-faceted roles with elegant and professional aplomb. An established Mohiniyattam dancer, she brings a distinct, refined sensibility to this traditional dance-form. A senior-most disciple of Guru Padmashri Smt. Bharati Shivaji, she has captivated audiences with her exquisite grace and exposition at the most prestigious venues and festivals, nationally and internationally. She has many recognitions and distinctions to her credit, including receiving the Indira Gandhi Priyadarshini National Award for Mohiniyattam, being chosen the International MedFit Pro2020 by MedFit Organization (USA) and being one of the country’s first Cancer Exercise Specialist.

b: Vani Tripathi Tikoo is the youngest ever member of the Central Board of Film Certification. Her campaigns and outreach programmes have focused on encouraging women’s participation in politics as well as issues…
f: Vani Tripathi Tikoo is the youngest ever member of the Central Board of Film Certification. Her campaigns and outreach programmes have focused on encouraging women’s participation in politics as well as issues revolving around education, empowerment and employment. Tikoo has also worked in theatre, film and television, and has acted in nearly 50 plays, 40 television shows and six films. In 2011, she set up the Madhya Pradesh Natya Vidyalaya, the country’s first state run drama school. Tikoo is currently part of the core committee for the International Film Festival of India, Goa.

b: Vanshica Kant is a Climate, Human, and Social Development Expert at the Asian Development Bank, working on equitable infrastructure projects across sovereign and non-sovereign sectors. A World Economic Forum Global…
f: Vanshica Kant is a Climate, Human, and Social Development Expert at the Asian Development Bank, working on equitable infrastructure projects across sovereign and non-sovereign sectors. A World Economic Forum Global Shaper and Schwarzman Scholar, her expertise spans climate change, healthcare, urban development, crisis management, and gender equity. She holds degrees from St. Stephen's College, the University of Oxford, and Tsinghua University.

b: Varghese K George is Deputy Resident Editor of The Hindu. His book Open Embrace: India-US Ties in the Age of Modi and Trump is an exploration of how hypernationalist domestic politics are reshaping the strategic…
f: Varghese K George is Deputy Resident Editor of The Hindu. His book Open Embrace: India-US Ties in the Age of Modi and Trump is an exploration of how hypernationalist domestic politics are reshaping the strategic priorities of the world’s oldest and biggest democracies, and their relations. The book draws from his experience of covering domestic politics and foreign policy in both India and the US. He is a winner of the RNG Journalist of the Year and the Prem Bhatia Award for Excellence in Political Journalism.

b: Varud Gupta is an award-winning author and visiting professor. He has written the graphic novel Chhotu: A Tale of Love and Partition (Comic Con India 'Best Writer') and the travelogue Bhagwaan Ke Pakwaan: Food of the…
f: Varud Gupta is an award-winning author and visiting professor. He has written the graphic novel Chhotu: A Tale of Love and Partition (Comic Con India 'Best Writer') and the travelogue Bhagwaan Ke Pakwaan: Food of the Gods (Gourmand shortlist for 'Peace'). Gupta received his bachelor's in Finance from New York University and has taught with the Indian Institute of Art and Design, Center for Fiction, 826NYC, and Gotham Writers.

b: Varun Thomas Mathew is a writer and lawyer. His first novel, The Black Dwarves of the Good Little Bay , was published in 2019 and was shortlisted for the Tata Literature Live First Book Award.
f: Varun Thomas Mathew is a writer and lawyer. His first novel, The Black Dwarves of the Good Little Bay , was published in 2019 and was shortlisted for the Tata Literature Live First Book Award.

b: Varun Sivaram is a physicist, Chief Technology Officer of ReNew Power Ventures, India’s largest renewable energy firm, and a senior research scholar at the Columbia University Center for Global Energy Policy. Dr.…
f: Varun Sivaram is a physicist, Chief Technology Officer of ReNew Power Ventures, India’s largest renewable energy firm, and a senior research scholar at the Columbia University Center for Global Energy Policy. Dr. Sivaram’s previous roles include professor at Georgetown University, fellow and director of the energy programme at the Council on Foreign Relations, consultant at McKinsey & Co. and senior energy advisor to the Los Angeles Mayor and New York Governor’s Office. Forbes Magazine called him one of the 30 under 30 in Law and Policy, Grist selected him as one of the top 50 leaders in sustainability and PV Magazine named him the ‘Hamilton of the Solar Industry’. His books include Taming the Sun: Innovations to Harness Solar Energy and Power the Planet and Digital Decarbonisation: Promoting Digital Innovations to Advance Clean Energy Systems .

b: Vasamalli K is a social activist and a Toda language expert. The Akademi has published her collection of Toda Oral Literature into Tamil. She coordinated with Tribal women self-help groups to facilitate their…
f: Vasamalli K is a social activist and a Toda language expert. The Akademi has published her collection of Toda Oral Literature into Tamil. She coordinated with Tribal women self-help groups to facilitate their development and empowerment. She is working to publish a Toda Dictionary and write articles about the stories, songs and culture of Toda.

b: Vauhini Vara’s debut novel, The Immortal King Rao , was a New York Times Editors’ Choice and was shortlisted for the Center for Fiction’s First Novel Prize. She has also written and edited for The New Yorker, The…
f: Vauhini Vara’s debut novel, The Immortal King Rao , was a New York Times Editors’ Choice and was shortlisted for the Center for Fiction’s First Novel Prize. She has also written and edited for The New Yorker, The New York Times Magazine, The Atlantic, and other publications.

b: Vayu Naidu is a Royal Literary Fund Fellow at Royal Holloway University of London, History, Humanities 2019-2021. Her recent public conversation was with Daniel Hahn OBE on the significance of languages and literatures…
f: Vayu Naidu is a Royal Literary Fund Fellow at Royal Holloway University of London, History, Humanities 2019-2021. Her recent public conversation was with Daniel Hahn OBE on the significance of languages and literatures in translation. She is also Research Associate at the Centre for the Circulation of Literatures and Post-Colonial Studies at the South Asia Studies Institute at SOAS and is continuing her work with MULOSOGIE and the Being Human Project. Her PhD from the University of Leeds was in performance oral traditions. She was the first storyteller transposing the Ramayana and the Mahabharata in English with western orchestras and museums, and Arts Education for a Multicultural Society, commissioned by Arts Council England. She won the Humanities Teaching Award from the University of Kent for her work with tsunami survivors in villages from Chennai to Salem, Tamil Nadu in 2004. She was the Arts and Humanities Research Council Post-Doctoral Fellow in Creative and Performing Arts leading on intercultural storytelling in performance, multicultural literacy, mental health, and migration. Arts Council England funded the Vayu Naidu Company as a Regional Funded Organisation from 2004-2012. Her work includes plays for radio drama for BBC 4, theater storytelling for Contemporary Music, and her Ramayana at the Barbican and The British Library, touring from Scotland to Scandinavia. Her novels are Sita’s Ascent, which was nominated for the Commonwealth Book Award, The Sari of Surya Vilas , which was featured on ABC as Australia’s Book of the Week. Her short story is titled Madurai Mystery of Victoriana . Her next literary historical fiction set in 17th century England and India is about a time of trade and treacherous transition and the triumph of art over tyranny. It featu

b: Dr. Vedam Ramprasad is a scientist with several peer-reviewed publications to his credit. He believes in harnessing the power of genomics for providing better outlook to patients. He has been with MedGenome since its…
f: Dr. Vedam Ramprasad is a scientist with several peer-reviewed publications to his credit. He believes in harnessing the power of genomics for providing better outlook to patients. He has been with MedGenome since its inception and spearheads operations and strategy. He has been a prime driver in building the diverse genetic testing portfolio MedGenome offers. He is also credited for launching some of the critical genetic tests at an affordable price which include the Non-Invasive Prenatal test (NIPT), Carrier Screening test, and Liquid Biopsy to name a few. His commitment to adhere to the highest quality standards and processes has been instrumental in obtaining CAP accreditation for MedGenome. With over two decades of experience, Dr. Ramprasad was previously associated with Vision Research Foundation, Sankara Nethralaya, Spinco Biotech, and SciGenom labs. He holds a Master’s degree and a PhD from BITS, Pilani.

b: Veena Nagpal is known for her genre bending fiction featuring love, passion, intrigue and boldly etched characters exploring vital issues facing humankind. Radius 200 is her fourth novel. Her earlier novels include The…
f: Veena Nagpal is known for her genre bending fiction featuring love, passion, intrigue and boldly etched characters exploring vital issues facing humankind. Radius 200 is her fourth novel. Her earlier novels include The Uncommon Memories of Zeenat Qureishi , Karmayogi and Compulsion . She has also written four books for children.

b: Veena Rao is a storyteller, library educator, and the founder of RoRo Books. Drawing on her M.A. in Education from Azim Premji University, she combines her pedagogical expertise with publishing to create impactful…
f: Veena Rao is a storyteller, library educator, and the founder of RoRo Books. Drawing on her M.A. in Education from Azim Premji University, she combines her pedagogical expertise with publishing to create impactful children’s literature that seamlessly blends text and visuals.

b: Veena Venugopal is the author of two books, The Mother in Law , a study of the phenomenon of the Indian mother-in-law, and Would You Like Some Bread With That Book , a collection of essays on books and reading. She…
f: Veena Venugopal is the author of two books, The Mother in Law , a study of the phenomenon of the Indian mother-in-law, and Would You Like Some Bread With That Book , a collection of essays on books and reading. She works at The Hindu where she is the Editor of Briefcase, a mobile news app. She writes extensively on gender issues and books.

b: Veer Munshi studied fine arts (painting) at M.S. University Baroda and has lived in Delhi/Gurgaon since 1990. Over his three-decade career, his works have addressed various subjects, with exile being his primary focus.…
f: Veer Munshi studied fine arts (painting) at M.S. University Baroda and has lived in Delhi/Gurgaon since 1990. Over his three-decade career, his works have addressed various subjects, with exile being his primary focus. He has held solo shows worldwide, with his latest exhibition, HEALING WOUNDS , opening on January 30th at ICON Gallery, NY. His work has been featured in major group shows across the globe, including the 2023 India Art Fair and 2019 Kochi Muzris Biennale.

b: Veio Pou is the author of Waiting for the Dust to Settle , Literary Cultures of India’s Northeast: Naga Writings in English and Keeper of Stories: Critical Readings of Easterine Kire's Novels . He currently teaches in…
f: Veio Pou is the author of Waiting for the Dust to Settle , Literary Cultures of India’s Northeast: Naga Writings in English and Keeper of Stories: Critical Readings of Easterine Kire's Novels . He currently teaches in the Department of English, University of Delhi. Besides his academic engagements, he also likes to discuss issues on society, life, and faith at the popular level.

b: Venkat Sundaram has played cricket at the first-class and international levels. He has worn many hats in the cricketing world, serving as a cricketer, commentator, author, Chief Curator at BCCI, and Manager of the…
f: Venkat Sundaram has played cricket at the first-class and international levels. He has worn many hats in the cricketing world, serving as a cricketer, commentator, author, Chief Curator at BCCI, and Manager of the Indian team. Additionally, he has authored and edited three books on cricket: Cricket Coaching Handbook, The Sardar of Spin, and his latest work, Indian Cricket Then and Now.

b: Venki Ramakrishnan is a molecular biologist from Cambridge, England, who shared the 2009 Nobel Prize for his work on the structure and function of ribosomes. He served as president of the Royal Society from 2015-2020,…
f: Venki Ramakrishnan is a molecular biologist from Cambridge, England, who shared the 2009 Nobel Prize for his work on the structure and function of ribosomes. He served as president of the Royal Society from 2015-2020, and is the author of two books: Gene Machine , and Why We Die .

b: Vicky Roy , originally from West Bengal, overcame a challenging childhood to become a renowned photographer. After being rehabilitated by Salaam Baalak Trust, he studied at Triveni Kala Sangam and apprenticed under Anay…
f: Vicky Roy , originally from West Bengal, overcame a challenging childhood to become a renowned photographer. After being rehabilitated by Salaam Baalak Trust, he studied at Triveni Kala Sangam and apprenticed under Anay Mann. His works, showcased globally, include solo exhibitions, books, and recognition like Forbes Asia’s 30 Under 30.

b: Victor Mallet is a journalist, commentator and author with three decades of experience in Asia, Europe, the Middle East and Africa. He is currently Asia news editor for the Financial Times and was bureau chief in South…
f: Victor Mallet is a journalist, commentator and author with three decades of experience in Asia, Europe, the Middle East and Africa. He is currently Asia news editor for the Financial Times and was bureau chief in South Asia, based in New Delhi, from 2012-2016. Mallet has written numerous editorials, columns and features on security, politics, economics and business. He has twice won the Society of Publishers in Asia Award for opinion writing. In India, he was twice awarded the Ramnath Goenka Award for Excellence in Journalism as a foreign correspondent, once for a feature about the rise of Narendra Modi and later for a magazine article on the River Ganges. He is the author of The Trouble with Tigers , the highly praised book on the south-east Asian industrial revolution and the 1997-98 Asian financial crisis. His new book is Ganges, River of Life, River of Death: The Ganges and India’s Future .

b: Victor Sebestyen has covered the wars in former Yugoslavia and the collapse of the USSR for several British newspapers. He has written for The New York Times and was an editor at Newsweek . Apart from Lenin the Dictator…
f: Victor Sebestyen has covered the wars in former Yugoslavia and the collapse of the USSR for several British newspapers. He has written for The New York Times and was an editor at Newsweek . Apart from Lenin the Dictator , he is the author of Twelve Days, a History of the 1956 Hungarian Uprising , Revolution 1989 and 1946: The Making of the Modern World .

b: Victoria Hislop is a graduate of Oxford University and the multi-million-copy bestselling author of ten novels, including the international hit The Island . Her books have been translated into forty languages, and she…
f: Victoria Hislop is a graduate of Oxford University and the multi-million-copy bestselling author of ten novels, including the international hit The Island . Her books have been translated into forty languages, and she was executive producer on three Greek TV adaptations. An honorary Greek citizen, she divides her time between England and Greece. A Fellow of the Royal Society of Literature, she has received the British Book Award, the Livre de Poche Readers Award, and the 2025 Lord Byron Medal. She holds honorary doctorates from the University of Sheffield and the University of Patras, and serves as Vice-President of the British School at Athens. Hislop is also an Ambassador for Lepra and the National Literacy Trust.

b: Victoria Lautman is a cultural journalist and lecturer. After working at the Smithsonian Institution, she began writing for dozens of international publications and hosted several radio programmes in Chicago. Lautman…
f: Victoria Lautman is a cultural journalist and lecturer. After working at the Smithsonian Institution, she began writing for dozens of international publications and hosted several radio programmes in Chicago. Lautman has travelled extensively in India for 30 years where her obsession with stepwells resulted in The Vanishing Stepwells of India .

b: Starting in 1978 with his Oscar-nominated short film, An Encounter with Faces, Vidhu Vinod Chopra has won countless awards over the years for his path-breaking work as director, screenwriter and producer. His unique…
f: Starting in 1978 with his Oscar-nominated short film, An Encounter with Faces, Vidhu Vinod Chopra has won countless awards over the years for his path-breaking work as director, screenwriter and producer. His unique approach to filmmaking is evident in films such as Parinda, Khamosh, 1942: A Love Story and in the films that can today be defined as the modern classics of our era, Munna Bhai M.B.B.S. and 3 Idiots. In 1992, Abhijat Joshi wrote a critically acclaimed play, A Shaft of Sunlight, that Chopra happened to see in Birmingham. Their subsequent encounter was the start of an enduring and fruitful collaboration resulting in films like Mission Kashmir, Eklavya, and most recently, Shikara. The team of director Rajkumar Hirani, writer Joshi and producer Chopra has also helmed major blockbusters in recent years like Lage Raho Munna Bhai, 3 Idiots, PK and Sanju.

b: Vidya Dehejia , Barbara Stoler Miller Professor Emerita of Indian Art at Columbia University in New York, and recipient of the prestigious Padma Bhushan, is the author of a range of books on the history of Indian art.…
f: Vidya Dehejia , Barbara Stoler Miller Professor Emerita of Indian Art at Columbia University in New York, and recipient of the prestigious Padma Bhushan, is the author of a range of books on the history of Indian art. Her recent publications include The Thief Who Stole My Heart, India: A Story through 100 Objects, The Unfinished: Indian Stone Carvers at Work and The Body Adorned.

b: Vidya Krishnan is a writer and journalist based in India. Her non-fiction debut Phantom Plague: How Tuberculosis Shaped History was published in February 2022.
f: Vidya Krishnan is a writer and journalist based in India. Her non-fiction debut Phantom Plague: How Tuberculosis Shaped History was published in February 2022.

b: Vidya Mahambare currently serves as a Union Bank Chair Professor of Economics at Great Lakes Institute of Management, Chennai and is actively engaged in research and policy advisory work on gender, labour markets, and…
f: Vidya Mahambare currently serves as a Union Bank Chair Professor of Economics at Great Lakes Institute of Management, Chennai and is actively engaged in research and policy advisory work on gender, labour markets, and inclusive growth in India. Earlier, she was Principal Economist at CRISIL and with Cardiff Business School, UK.

b: Vidya Shah is a singer and musician from New Delhi, India. She was initially trained in Carnatic music, and later received guidance in the North Indian genres of Khayal (from Shubha Mudgal and Mujahid Hussain Khan) and…
f: Vidya Shah is a singer and musician from New Delhi, India. She was initially trained in Carnatic music, and later received guidance in the North Indian genres of Khayal (from Shubha Mudgal and Mujahid Hussain Khan) and Thumri Dadra, and Ghazal (from Shanti Hiranand). She has performed at national and international forums, including the Tansen Samaroh in Gwalior, The Kennedy Centre in Washington D.C, The Asia Society in New York and the Bode Museum in Berlin. A popular performer and a prolific composer, she is a recipient of the Charles Wallace Award and a Senior Fellowship from the Government of India for her project ‘Women on Record’, a performance highlighting the contributions of the forgotten women performers in the Gramophone era. * She writes and speaks on music and is the author of Jalsa: Indian Women's Journey from the Salon to the Studio . She is the Nana Shirgaokar Chair Professor for Indian Music at Goa University for 2016-21. She made her Bollywood debut for the film Manto, with the nazm ‘Bol’.

b: Vijai Trivedi is best known for his political reporting, parliamentary coverage and his unique style of interviewing top politicians, bureaucrats and celebrities. With more than 30 years of political reporting and a…
f: Vijai Trivedi is best known for his political reporting, parliamentary coverage and his unique style of interviewing top politicians, bureaucrats and celebrities. With more than 30 years of political reporting and a deep understanding of the Indian political arena, he softly puts the hardest of questions to his subjects without being shrill and roaringly loud. He has written four books focussing on how BJP evolved since the days of Atal Bihari Vajpayee to Narendra Modi and Yogi Adityanath. His latest book is on the journey of RSS-Sangham Sharnam Gachchhami. His earlier book, BJP, Kal, Aaj Aur Kal, drew a lot of attention where he thoroughly analysed the rise of BJP and its place and future in Indian politics. His other two books are Yada Yada hi Yogi on the emergence of Yogi Adityanath in BJP and Haar Nahi Manunga on former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee, the founding architect of the BJP. He worked for NDTV India for almost 17 years and rose to become its Consulting Editor. Later he became the National Affairs Editor of News Nation TV Channel and Editor-in-Chief of News State TV channel.

b: Vijay Kedia is an investor, a keynote speaker at IIM Ahmedabad & Bangalore, IIT Bombay, the London Business School and also a TEDx speaker. He was conferred with a doctorate degree and recognised as an 'ACE INVESTOR' by…
f: Vijay Kedia is an investor, a keynote speaker at IIM Ahmedabad & Bangalore, IIT Bombay, the London Business School and also a TEDx speaker. He was conferred with a doctorate degree and recognised as an 'ACE INVESTOR' by Hon'ble Union Minister Piyush Goyal and Hon'ble Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis. He has also written and sung 15 songs to educate investors.

b: Vijayalakshmi is a world-renowned Indian classical dancer, an acclaimed exponent of Mohiniyattam, the graceful classical dance form from South India. Daughter and disciple of Bharati Shivaji, Vijayalakshmi takes…
f: Vijayalakshmi is a world-renowned Indian classical dancer, an acclaimed exponent of Mohiniyattam, the graceful classical dance form from South India. Daughter and disciple of Bharati Shivaji, Vijayalakshmi takes Mohiniyattam to higher levels by constantly exploring uncharted territory and expanding traditional boundaries. She is also a choreographer, actress, speaker, feminist, writer and singer. A recipient of several prestigious awards, including from the Sangeet Natak Academy, she has performed at some of the most prestigious venues in India and around the globe, spanning over 30 countries, sponsored by the government of India, besides the Bolshoi Theatre, the Edinburgh International Festival and the Lincoln Centre. Her prominent productions include *Unniarcha,inspired from Kalaripayattu, the ancient martial art form, **Swan Lake, inspired by the great Russian composer Tchaikovsky's music and **Paryapti*,which draws upon the rich cultural ethos and music of Bengal. She has a Bachelors and Masters in English Literature from Lady Shriram College, Delhi University. She is the Artistic-Director of the Centre For Mohiniyattam, New Delhi & the Founder-Director of The Mohiniyattam Institute, Los Angeles.

b: Viju B is the author of the bestselling Flood and Fury and is Metro Editor of the Times of India , Kochi. He reports on issues at the intersection of development, ecology and culture. While working in Mumbai for various…
f: Viju B is the author of the bestselling Flood and Fury and is Metro Editor of the Times of India , Kochi. He reports on issues at the intersection of development, ecology and culture. He exposed the Sindhudurg mining scam in the Western Ghats. In his book, he has documented large-scale mining, quarrying, deforestation and mismanagement of water resources in the Western Ghats regions, mapping its micro-histories, cultures and environment.

f: Vikas Kumar Jha is a Hindi journalist and author with over 35 years in the media industry. Other notable works include The Queen of Indian Pop: The Authorised Biography of Usha Uthup , Raja Momo Aur Peeli Bulbul , Gayasursandhan , Varshavan Ki Roopkatha , Bihar: Criminalization of Politics , and Bhog .

f: Vikas is the Director of Jyotsna Prakashan, a renowned Marathi publishing house established in 1950, known for its pioneering work in children’s literature and art books. The house publishes simultaneously in Marathi and English and offers innovative products for early readers. Vikas oversees sales and marketing, representing the family business at major national and international book fairs, including the Frankfurt Book Fair, sustaining its 75-year legacy of excellence.

f: Vikas Singh has more than 19 years of experience in managing various brand portfolios and has won more than 263 international and national awards for his brand and advertising campaigns. His first book, Philatelic Handbook on Indian Railways , won a Bronze medal at the London Stamp Show. His second book, Coffee Table Book on Ujjain , has received good reviews and won a number of national and international awards. He edits the annual magazine of the Indian Steam Railway Society and writes regularly for various magazines and websites.

Chandra was one of India's best-known TV news anchors, presenting The Big Fight, 9 o’clockNews, Gadget Guru, Cleanathon, Greenathon, and Save our Tigers.

b: Vikram Jit Singh i s a correspondent of the proverbial trenches. And, a diehard romantic who sent miniature alpine flowers from battlefields in letters to his anxious fiancée. The author of Flowers on a Kargil Cliff ,…
f: Vikram Jit Singh i s a correspondent of the proverbial trenches. And, a diehard romantic who sent miniature alpine flowers from battlefields in letters to his anxious fiancée. The author of Flowers on a Kargil Cliff , he is a seasoned journalist and naturalist. Embedded with the Indian Army during counter-terrorist operations in Kashmir and the Kargil War, Singh was the only media person to scale enemy bunkers with assault troops. His reporting earned praise for its authenticity, including accolades from Lt. Gen. Sanjay Kulkarni (retd.). Singh has also contributed to With Honour and Glory: Five Great Artillery Battles . A journalist of 33 years, Singh writes columns on wildlife and the environment for The Times of India and Hindustan Times .

f: Vikram Patel is the Paul Farmer Professor at Harvard Medical School. He was listed in TIME Magazine’s 100 most influential persons of the year in 2015.

Since January 2018, he has been the President of Indian Council for Cultural Relations (ICCR) India’s soft-power promotion establishment. A Member of Parliament, Rajya Sabha (Upper House of Indian Parliament) from Maharashtra since July 2016, he is also Chairman of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Education. For six years, Dr. Sahasrabuddhe was also the National Vice President of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), India’s principal ruling party. Dr Sahasrabuddhe is also the Vice President of Rambhau Mhalgi Prabodhini, a unique institution of which he was the founder Director General. Previously, Dr. Sahasrabuddhe has worked on the management council of the university of Mumbai and was also vice president of the 208 year old The Asiatic Society of Mumbai between 2012-15. He has around half a dozen books in Marathi and English to his credit, some of which have won awards.

f: Vincent Cable is a former Secretary of State in the UK Coalition Government (Trade and Business) and former Leader of the Liberal Democrat Party. He is the author of Eclipsing the West , The Chinese Conundrum , Money and Power , The Storm , Open Arms , and How to Be a Politician .

f: Vineet Kumar teaches media and literature in Dr. B.R. Ambedkar College under Delhi University. He holds a PhD degree on Language-Culture of Prime Time Programmes of Hindi Entertainment Channels. f: Vinita Dawra Nangia is an associate editor, columnist and writer with the Times of India . As Director for Write India, she fronts a movement to identify and launch new writing talent. Nangia has launched several cutting edge editorial products that specialise in societal trends, dialogues on relationships and life commentary. Her Sunday column in the Times of India , ‘O-zone’, is an ongoing commentary on contemporary living. Her books include the bestselling It’s Your Life: Reflections on Contemporary Living & Relationships , Love is Always Right & Other Musings and Fashion Fair: The Journey of 13 Contemporary Designers . She edited Write India Stories , which launched several new winners of Write India as published authors.

b: Vinita Sharma lives and works in Jaipur. Her journey as an artist is marked by a series of impressive accomplishments. She has been invited to conduct several short courses and workshops on miniature painting techniques…
f: Vinita Sharma lives and works in Jaipur. Her journey as an artist is marked by a series of impressive accomplishments. f: Vinod Bharadwaj is a writer, journalist, and painter. He started his career as a Creative Director & Copywriter with Mass Communication & Marketing in New Delhi. He also worked with Dainik Bhaskar as a feature editor for eighteen years. During this time, he wrote numerous articles on art and culture. Bharadwaj edited two books, one on the famous Shayar Kaifi Azami and the other on journalism. Bharadwaj is the author of Gali Qasim Jaan , a novel based on the life of the great Urdu poet Mirza Ghalib. f: Vinod Bhardwaj is a writer and journalist. He started his career as a creative director and copywriter. During this time, Bhardwaj has written on a range of issues in numerous magazines. The editor of two books, one on Kaifi Azami and the other on Hindi journalism, Bhardwaj is the General Secretary of the Progressive Artists’ Group. He is currently working on a novel titled, Gali Qasim Jaan, based on the Urdu poet, Mirza Ghalib.

f: Vinod Kapri is an award-winning filmmaker and has won a national award for his 2014 film Can’t Take This Shit Anymore . Khanna is an Emeritus Fellow at the Institute of Chinese Studies and has co-authored India and China: The Way Ahead . Currently. He and Malini are currently translating C.Bulcke’s Ramakatha into English.

b: Vinod Paul , a pediatrician by training, has been on the faculty of the Department of Pediatrics, All India Institute of Medical Sciences, New Delhi, since 1985, and head of the department for nearly a decade. Professor…
f: Vinod Paul , a pediatrician by training, has been on the faculty of the Department of Pediatrics, All India Institute of Medical Sciences, New Delhi, since 1985, and head of the department for nearly a decade. Professor Paul has been closely associated with India’s health policy and programs in various roles for over three decades. India’s child and maternal health programs bear imprint of his research and expertise. As a globally recognised academic and public health exponent, Dr. Paul chaired the Technical Advisory Group on Women’s and Children’s Health for WHO’s South East Asia Region. He has been a co-chair of the board of the Partnership for Maternal, Newborn and Child Health. The Government of India appointed Paul as a Member of the National Institution for Transforming India, the NITI Aayog, in August 2017 where he leads the Health and Nutrition verticals. He has played a pivotal role in formulating the POSHAN Abhiyaan and the Ayushman Bharat initiative. Prof. Paul has recently been appointed as the Chairman of The Board of Governors of Medical Council of India. Prof. Paul is a fellow of all the three science academies of the country, and a recipient of the Dr. B. R. Ambedkar Centenary Award for Excellence in Biomedical Research and the Public Health Champion award. He was conferred the prestigious Ihsan Dogramaci Family Health Foundation Prize by WHO at the 2018 World Health Assembly.

f: Vir Das is an Emmy-winning comedian, actor, and writer, widely regarded as India’s most global stand-up voice. Praised by The New York Times for embodying the globalization of comedy, he has released four acclaimed Netflix specials, including the Emmy-winning Landing . One of India’s best-selling live acts, his record-breaking Mind Fool world tour spanned six continents and iconic venues worldwide. Beyond stand-up, Vir has starred in projects such as Hasmukh , Whiskey Cavalier , and Judd Apatow’s The Bubble . He is set to make his directorial debut with Happy Patel and release his first book, The Outsider .

b: Vir Sanghvi is probably the best-known Indian journalist of his generation. He became editor of Bombay magazine at twenty-two, making him the youngest editor in the history of Indian journalism. He went on to edit…
f: Vir Sanghvi is probably the best-known Indian journalist of his generation. He became editor of Bombay magazine at twenty-two, making him the youngest editor in the history of Indian journalism. He went on to edit Imprint and Sunday, then India’s largest-selling weekly newsmagazine. From 1999 to 2004, he was Editor of the Hindustan Times before being promoted to Editorial Director, a post he held till 2007, after which he continued at the paper as a columnist and advisor. His television career has included several award-winning television shows, and he has enjoyed a parallel career as India’s leading food and travel writer. His many books include the best- selling Men of Steel, and Rude Food , which won the Cointreau prize for Best Food Literature, as well Madhavrao Scindia, A Life and Mandate: Will of the People and A Rude Life: The Memoir

f: Pandit Vishwa Mohan Bhatt is one of the greatest musicians of our times who, along with a few others, has contributed immensely to popularising Indian Classical music across the globe. Vishwa Mohan developed the western guitar and made it into a unique classical instrument called Mohan-Veena, providing new scope and possibility for a mellifluous fusion of Indian Classical and Western music. In the last fifty years, Pt. Vishwa Mohan has performed in more than eighty countries for almost all the prestigious music festivals and concerts in the world. He has been honoured with the Padma Bhushan, Padma Shri, Grammy and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Puraskar, among numerous other awards.

His achievements have helped inspire a generation of chess players in India.

f: Vishwas Patil is an eminent novelist in Marathi literature. He has written thirteen novels on many realistic issues and adversities of the masses. He has also been awarded the Indira Goswami National Award and Priyadarshini National Award for literature. The author of critically acclaimed books like Not Gone with the Wind, Anna Bhahu: the Lion of Dalit Literature, Patil's famous play The Battlefield of Panipat, was directed by Waman Kendre and performed in India and USA.

f: Vivan Sharan is a public policy thinker and entrepreneur based in New Delhi. He is a Partner at the Koan Advisory Group, Secretary of the Esya Centre and Visiting Fellow at the Observer Research Foundation. He is the author of Wonked!: India in Search of an Economic Ideology.

f: Vivek Shanbhag is the author of ten works of fiction and three plays in Kannada. Ananthamurthy’s Hindutva or Hind Swaraj into English. Vivek is a visiting professor of creative writing at Ashoka University, Delhi, and the founder of Hyphen , a magazine dedicated to translating Indian-language literature into English. An engineer by training, he lives in Bangalore.

b: Viveka Kumari has had a diverse career as a drama teacher, theatre director, actor, and designer for interiors, textiles, and cinema. Having lived in cities worldwide, including Dhaka, Wellington, Bombay, Cairo, London,…
f: Viveka Kumari has had a diverse career as a drama teacher, theatre director, actor, and designer for interiors, textiles, and cinema.
