b: Dr. Vladimir Zaitsev is an art historian, museologist, writer, poet, educator, and curator based in New Delhi. He collaborates with IGNCA, the National Museum Institute, NGMA, and KNMA, and has curated numerous…
f: Dr. Vladimir Zaitsev is an art historian, museologist, writer, poet, educator, and curator based in New Delhi. He collaborates with IGNCA, the National Museum Institute, NGMA, and KNMA, and has curated numerous exhibitions on Russian and European art in recent years. His notable projects include 20th Century. Indian Art. Nicholas Roerich and India (Thames & Hudson, 2022); the exhibitions Kshetragya: The Illumined (Nine Masters of Indian Art) (2023) and Nicholas Roerich: The Eternal (NGMA, 2025); Bireswar Sen: Enchanted by the Himalayas, Masterpieces of Indian Modern Art (DAG, 2023); and the illustrated monograph Indian Odyssey: Art, Spirit, and Legacy of Nicholas Roerich (NGMA, 2025). He also edited a collection of articles on Nicholas Roerich for his 150th birth anniversary, a joint project by Indian and Russian scholars.

b: Volga is one of the most significant figures in Telugu literature today, having introduced a feminist perspective into the literary political discourse of Telangana and Andhra Pradesh. Her novels and short stories…
f: Volga is one of the most significant figures in Telugu literature today, having introduced a feminist perspective into the literary political discourse of Telangana and Andhra Pradesh. Her novels and short stories opened the floodgates for a host of women writers to articulate the doubts and challenges they experienced as women. Her novel, Swechcha marks a watershed in Women's writing in Telugu, and has been translated into all Indian languages by the National Book Trust of India. Her short story anthologies, such as Rajakeeya Kathalu and Vimukta , which portray the oppression and control of women’s bodies, have paved the way for feminist literature in Telugu. She has received many awards, including the Central Sahitya Akademi Award, and the Laldli Media Award for Gender Sensitivity.

b: V.R. Ferose is the founder of the India Inclusion Foundation, a Bengaluru-based nonprofit that aims to bring inclusion to the forefront in all sectors across India. He has co-authored several bestsellers, most notably…
f: V.R. Ferose is the founder of the India Inclusion Foundation, a Bengaluru-based nonprofit that aims to bring inclusion to the forefront in all sectors across India. He has co-authored several bestsellers, most notably The Invisible Majority: India’s Abled Disabled, Gifted: Inspiring Stories of People with Disabilities, and the GRIT series. Ferose has been included in various international lists of significance, such as ‘India’s Top 40 under 40’ in 2014 by Economic Times and Spencer Stuart, and was conferred ‘Young Global Leader’ in 2012 by the World Economic Forum. He currently heads the SAP Academy for Engineering in San Ramon and is on the board of the California-based publishing house, Heyday Books.

b: Wajahat Habibullah is a former chairperson of the National Commission for Minorities. Prior to this, he was the first Chief Information Commissioner of India. He was an officer of the Indian Administrative Service of…
f: Wajahat Habibullah is a former chairperson of the National Commission for Minorities. Prior to this, he was the first Chief Information Commissioner of India. He was an officer of the Indian Administrative Service of the J&K cadre from 1968 until his retirement in September 2005, having served in India and the US. He recently released My Years with Rajiv: Triumph and Tragedy.

b: Walter J. Lindner , born in Munich in 1956, is a diplomat, musician, lawyer and author. He began his diplomatic career in Bonn, Ankara, in 1988, after studying law. He then worked as a counsellor at the German…
f: Walter J. Lindner , born in Munich in 1956, is a diplomat, musician, lawyer and author. He began his diplomatic career in Bonn, Ankara, in 1988, after studying law. He then worked as a counsellor at the German representation to the United Nations in New York, and later, press spokesman for Joschka Fischer, and state secretary under Sigmar Gabriel. In Berlin, he headed, among other things, the crisis response centre, and was the director for African affairs, as well as a special envoy of the German chancellor during the fight against the Ebola epidemic. He was the German ambassador in Kenya, Somalia, Venezuela and South Africa, before taking over as head of the German embassy in India, in 2019. He now works as an author and speaker, and devotes himself with passion to his second life as a pianist, composer, and music producer. In March 2024, his book, with co-author Heike Wolter, Der Alte Westen und der Neue Süden, was published to much acclaim.

b: Warisha Farasat is a distinguished lawyer and human rights advocate, an alumna of NLSIU, Bangalore, and Columbia Law School, where she was a Henkin-Stoffel Fellow. She has worked with the International Center for…
f: Warisha Farasat is a distinguished lawyer and human rights advocate, an alumna of NLSIU, Bangalore, and Columbia Law School, where she was a Henkin-Stoffel Fellow. She has worked with the International Center for Transitional Justice, advising on international criminal law, reparations, truth commissions, and transitional justice. In India, she litigates high-profile criminal and constitutional cases defending minorities, marginalized communities, dissidents, and journalists wrongly charged under restrictive laws. Widely published on human rights, freedom of expression, and transitional justice, she authored Splintered Justice: Living the Horror of Mass Communal Violence in Bhagalpur and Gujarat . She enjoys historical non-fiction and Urdu poetry.

b: Warwick Ball is a Near Eastern archaeologist who has worked in Iran, Libya, Ethiopia, Afghanistan, Jordan, Syria and Iraq, and travelled in most countries between Europe and China over the past fifty years in the course…
f: Warwick Ball is a Near Eastern archaeologist who has worked in Iran, Libya, Ethiopia, Afghanistan, Jordan, Syria and Iraq, and travelled in most countries between Europe and China over the past fifty years in the course of his work. He is the author of numerous books on the history and archaeology of the region broadly. His latest work includes The Archaeological Gazetteer of Afghanistan, East of the Wardrobe: The Unexpected Worlds of C S Lewis, and The Eurasian Steppe.

b: Weijian Shan is chairman and CEO of PAG, a private equity firm with about $35 billion in capital under management. Prior to PAG, he was a partner of TPG, a San Francisco based private equity firm. Previously, Shan was a…
f: Weijian Shan is chairman and CEO of PAG, a private equity firm with about $35 billion in capital under management. Prior to PAG, he was a partner of TPG, a San Francisco based private equity firm. Previously, Shan was a managing director of JP Morgan, an assistant professor at the Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania, among other employments. Shan is the author of the book Out of the Gobi , My Story of China and America, and of many commentaries published in the Financial Times, The New York Times, the Wall Street Journal, Foreign Affairs and others.

b: William A. Haseltine , PhD, is the chair and president of ACCESS Health International, a nonprofit organisation he co-founded in 2007. Dr. Haseltine has an active career in both science and business. He was a professor…
f: William A. Haseltine , PhD, is the chair and president of ACCESS Health International, a nonprofit organisation he co-founded in 2007. Dr. Haseltine has an active career in both science and business. He was a professor at Harvard Medical School and Harvard School of Public Health from 1976 to 1993 where he was founder and the chair of two academic research departments, the Division of Biochemical Pharmacology and the Division of Human Retrovirology. He is well known for his pioneering work on cancer, HIV/AIDS and genomics. He has authored more than 200 manuscripts in peer reviewed journals and is the author of several books, including Affordable Excellence: The Singapore Healthcare Story and Every Second Counts: India’s Emergency Response System . He is the founder of Human Genome Sciences, Inc.and served as the chairman and CEO of the company until 2004. He is also the founder of several other successful biotechnology companies. He is chairman of the Haseltine Foundation for Science and the Arts. and of the US-China Health Summit. He is a member of the advisory board of the IE University, Madrid. He is also a Lifetime Governor of the New York Academy of Sciences, an honorary member of the Board of Trustees of the Brookings Institution, and a member of the Council on Foreign Relations.

b: William Feaver is an art critic and curator. He was the chief art critic for The Observer from 1975-1998 and has curated exhibitions from George Cruikshank to Frank Auerbach and Lucian Freud. He is the author of Frank…
f: William Feaver is an art critic and curator. He was the chief art critic for The Observer from 1975-1998 and has curated exhibitions from George Cruikshank to Frank Auerbach and Lucian Freud. He is the author of Frank Auerbach . His latest books are Lucian Freud and The Lives of Lucian Freud, Vol 1, the second volume of which will be published next September.

b: William O’Connor joined the Foreign Service in 2009. He is a public diplomacy officer and the current Deputy Counselor for Educational and Cultural Affairs in New Delhi. He most recently served in Romania, and has…
f: William O’Connor joined the Foreign Service in 2009. He is a public diplomacy officer and the current Deputy Counselor for Educational and Cultural Affairs in New Delhi. He most recently served in Romania, and has previously served in Estonia, the Philippines, Afghanistan, and Denmark.

b: William Sieghart is a renowned poet, publisher, and arts advocate. He founded the Forward Prizes for Poetry in 1991 and National Poetry Day with the BBC in 1993, now the BBC’s longest-standing arts partnership after the…
f: William Sieghart is a renowned poet, publisher, and arts advocate. He founded the Forward Prizes for Poetry in 1991 and National Poetry Day with the BBC in 1993, now the BBC’s longest-standing arts partnership after the Proms. Author of three volumes of The Poetry Pharmacy , he has toured widely, offering poetry prescriptions to thousands. An inspirational speaker, he has appeared at TEDx, 5x15, literary festivals, and corporate events. Chair of the Henry Smith Charity, he spearheaded initiatives like StreetSmart, raising over £12m for London’s homeless. He has contributed to British libraries, Somerset House, the London 2012 Olympics, and peace initiatives in the Middle East.

b: Yakub Mathew graduated from St. Stephen’s College Delhi. Despite coming from a politically influential family in India Yakub decided to leave his motherland and make his future overseas. After exploring several…
f: Yakub Mathew graduated from St. Stephen’s College Delhi. Despite coming from a politically influential family in India Yakub decided to leave his motherland and make his future overseas. After exploring several opportunities he was employed as the National Head of South Asian Banking at HSBC from 2002-2010. He joined Citi Private Banking in New York as Managing Director and Global Head USA of the Wealth Management arm in 2010 and worked there until 2022. In the same year he joined Wells Fargo Advisors as Managing Director investments New York. Yakub has 34 years experience between Citi Private Bank and HSBC in the Banking, Wealth Management and Advisory Services.

b: Yameer Adhar is an author, poet and wellness motivator. His debut book, Voices in my Head which achieved bestseller status, chronicles his journey from an asthmatic childhood to one free of all his ailments today. He…
f: Yameer Adhar is an author, poet and wellness motivator. His debut book, Voices in my Head which achieved bestseller status, chronicles his journey from an asthmatic childhood to one free of all his ailments today. He also hosts an ongoing wellness podcast titled, VOICES IN MY HEAD, which has been watched and heard by thousands of people across the globe.

b: Yamini is the President and Chief Executive of the Center for Policy Research, one of India’s leading think tanks. Yamini’s work sits at the intersections of research and policy practice. Her research spans the…
f: Yamini is the President and Chief Executive of the Center for Policy Research, one of India’s leading think tanks. Yamini’s work sits at the intersections of research and policy practice. Her research spans the field of social policy (education, health and social protection), governance and State capacity, federalism and the study of contemporary politics in India.In 2008, Yamini found the Accountability Initiative at the Centre for Policy Research. The initiative is credited with pioneering one of India’s largest expenditure tracking surveys for elementary education. Yamini has published widely in academic journals and the popular press. In addition, she serves on a number of government policy committees and boards of non-profits and think tanks. Yamini is an aluma of the London School of Economics, St. Edmund's College, Cambridge University and St. Stephen’s College, Delhi University.

b: Yann Martel is a Canadian writer, the author of five works of fiction, notably Life of Pi , for which he won the 2002 Man Booker Prize. The book was adapted to the silver screen by Ang Lee, garnering four Oscars.
f: Yann Martel is a Canadian writer, the author of five works of fiction, notably Life of Pi , for which he won the 2002 Man Booker Prize. The book was adapted to the silver screen by Ang Lee, garnering four Oscars.

b: Yaroslav Trofimov , a Kyiv-born author, has published three narrative non-fiction books and the novel No Country for Love . A foreign correspondent for The Wall Street Journal since 1999, he became the chief…
f: Yaroslav Trofimov , a Kyiv-born author, has published three narrative non-fiction books and the novel No Country for Love . A foreign correspondent for The Wall Street Journal since 1999, he became the chief foreign-affairs correspondent in 2018. He was a Pulitzer Prize finalist for international reporting in 2023 and 2022, and his latest book, Our Enemies Will Vanish , was a finalist for the 2024 Orwell Prize. Trofimov holds an MA from New York University, and his works have been translated into multiple languages.

b: Yascha Mounk is a writer and academic known for his work on the rise of populism and the crisis of liberal democracy. He is now a professor of the Practice of International Affairs at Johns Hopkins University. Mounk is…
f: Yascha Mounk is a writer and academic known for his work on the rise of populism and the crisis of liberal democracy. He is now a professor of the Practice of International Affairs at Johns Hopkins University. Mounk is also a senior fellow at the Council on Foreign Relations, a contributing editor at The Atlantic , the founder of the online magazine Persuasion and a publisher of Die Zeit. He is the author of The People vs Democracy: Why Our Freedom is in Danger and How to Save It and The Great Experiment: Why Diverse Democracies Fall Apart and How They Can Endure. Supported by Goethe-Institut/Max Mueller Bhavan

b: Yash Goyal is a journalist, author, critic, lensman and former bio-technology scientist. He is the winner of three literary awards from Rajasthan Patrika, Himachal Pradesh Bhasha-Sahitya- Sanskriti and Bhagwan Atlani…
f: Yash Goyal is a journalist, author, critic, lensman and former bio-technology scientist. He is the winner of three literary awards from Rajasthan Patrika, Himachal Pradesh Bhasha-Sahitya- Sanskriti and Bhagwan Atlani Katha as well as the prestigious journalism award, Manak Alankaran. He has authored four books on short stories, five on satires, three on children fictions, one on interview journalism and has done translations of Franz Kafka and Nobel laureate Jaroslav Seifert’s literary works. His latest books are Falsapha and Achche Din Tanj Ke . In addition to his literary work, he was first to clone desert trees in plant tissue culture in Jodhpur and American universities. After working with the Press Trust of India for 30 years, he is currently with The Tribune in Rajasthan.

b: Yashaswini Chandra is the author of The Tale of the Horse: A History of India on Horseback. She holds a PhD from SOAS University of London, and her research interests include the arts and cultures of the Himalayas,…
f: Yashaswini Chandra is the author of The Tale of the Horse: A History of India on Horseback. She holds a PhD from SOAS University of London, and her research interests include the arts and cultures of the Himalayas, Rajasthan and Mughal India, animal history, and women's studies. She is the incoming Lecturer in South Asian Art History at the University of Edinburgh.

b: Yashica Dutt is an author and a journalist who shifted the narrative on how Dalits were perceived in Indian media after she 'came out as Dalit' in 2016. Her first book, Coming Out as Dalit, was recently released in the…
f: Yashica Dutt is an author and a journalist who shifted the narrative on how Dalits were perceived in Indian media after she 'came out as Dalit' in 2016. Her first book, Coming Out as Dalit, was recently released in the Indian subcontinent to an overwhelmingly positive reception and has earned rave reviews from almost all major Indian publications. She is soon bringing the book to the United States and the rest of the world and hopes to bring powerful Dalit narratives in the global spotlight.

b: Yasmine El Rashidi is a regular contributor to The New York Review of Books , a Contributing Editor of the Middle East arts and culture journal Bidoun and the author of The Battle for Egypt: Dispatches from the…
f: Yasmine El Rashidi is a regular contributor to The New York Review of Books , a Contributing Editor of the Middle East arts and culture journal Bidoun and the author of The Battle for Egypt: Dispatches from the Revolution and Chronicle of a Last Summer, A Novel of Egypt , which was long-listed for the PEN Open Book Award. Her reportage and essays have been anthologised widely, including in Best American Nonrequired Reading , The New York Review Abroad: Fifty Years of International Reportage and Diaries of an Unfinished Revolution . She is a former fellow of the Dorothy and Lewis B. Cullman Center for Scholars and Writers at The New York Public Library and was a visiting professor at Princeton University. She is a Contributing Op-ed Writer to The New York Times.

b: Yatindra Mishra is a distinguished poet, author, music and cinema scholar. He has authored five poetry collections along with acclaimed works on Thumri singer Girija Devi, danseuse Sonal Mansingh, Shehnai maestro…
f: Yatindra Mishra is a distinguished poet, author, music and cinema scholar. He has authored five poetry collections along with acclaimed works on Thumri singer Girija Devi, danseuse Sonal Mansingh, Shehnai maestro Bismillah Khan, authorized biography of playback singer Lata Mangeshkar and filmmaker Gulzar. He edited anthology on Ghazal singer Begum Akhtar. Recipient of many awards, including Aajtak Shahitya Jagriti Lokpriya Lekhak Samman, Uttar Pradesh Sangeet Natak Akademi Puraskar, Kalinga Book Award, International Vatayan Poetry Award, London and many other. His book 'Lata: Sur- Gatha' won 6 awards in a year, including prestigious 64th National Film Award (Swarna Kamal) for best writing on cinema and Mami Mumbai Film Festival Award, Mumbai. Serve as Cultural Advisor to Prasar Bharati, Doordarshan's Channel D.D. Bharati, (Ministry of I&B, Government of India) 2014-2016. He was the Jury member for feature film category (central panel) of 70th National Film Awards, Jury Chairman for best writing of 69th National Film Awards, Jury Member for 66th National Films Awards, 52nd International Film Festival of India, Goa. Also, the member of Centenary Celebrations Committee of the 55th International Film Festival of India, which pays tribute to Indian cinema legends Raj Kapoor, Mohammed Rafi, Tapan Sinha, and Akkineni Nageswara Rao. Conceptualized and curated a 50 days musical celebration titled 'Shree Ram Raag Sewa' on the behalf of Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust at Ayodhya.

b: Yeshi Tsering was born in Urgelling village in Tawang, Arunachal Pradesh. He has a Master’s in History from Jawaharlal Nehru University, and an MBA in Public Administration from Birmingham University, UK. A 1983-batch…
f: Yeshi Tsering was born in Urgelling village in Tawang, Arunachal Pradesh. He has a Master’s in History from Jawaharlal Nehru University, and an MBA in Public Administration from Birmingham University, UK. A 1983-batch IAS officer for Assam-Meghalaya, Tsering served as the Deputy Commissioner of the Jaintia Hills and Ri-bhoi districts, and as Secretary, Principal Secretary, and Additional Chief Secretary in various departments, including Education, Social Welfare, Finance, PWD, etc., ultimately superannuating as the Chief Secretary of Meghalaya in March 2019. He has presently assumed charge as a Member of Lokayukta, Arunachal Pradesh.

b: Yogendra Kumar has served in several important capitals in different parts of the world during his diplomatic career starting in 1977. At headquarters, he has handled both bilateral and multilateral relations covering a…
f: Yogendra Kumar has served in several important capitals in different parts of the world during his diplomatic career starting in 1977. At headquarters, he has handled both bilateral and multilateral relations covering a wide range of subjects. Post retirement, he has been writing and lecturing in India and abroad on foreign policy and security issues. His latest book, Geopolitics in the Era of Globalisation: Mapping an Alternative Global Future , has been published by Routledge in US, Europe and South Asia editions.

b: Yogesh Maitreya is a poet, translator, essayist and a publisher at Panther's Paw Publication. He is also a PhD scholar at Tata Institute of Social Sciences (Mumbai), working on the history of anti-caste music in the…
f: Yogesh Maitreya is a poet, translator, essayist and a publisher at Panther's Paw Publication. He is also a PhD scholar at Tata Institute of Social Sciences (Mumbai), working on the history of anti-caste music in the state of Maharashtra.

b: Yogi Vaid is a writer and language enthusiast, though he is also active in his family’s seventy-five-year-old business exporting equestrian equipment. His literary journey began with A Remarkable Friendship , a book…
f: Yogi Vaid is a writer and language enthusiast, though he is also active in his family’s seventy-five-year-old business exporting equestrian equipment. His literary journey began with A Remarkable Friendship , a book dedicated to his friend of sixty-eight years, Aman Nath, and later evolved into their co-authored work Bapji: The King Who Would Be Man .

b: Born in 1964, he first visited India in 1986, which shaped his long-standing engagement with the country. After joining Kodansha in 1989, he founded Courrier Japon and later led major Japan–India projects, including…
f: Born in 1964, he first visited India in 1986, which shaped his long-standing engagement with the country. After joining Kodansha in 1989, he founded Courrier Japon and later led major Japan–India projects, including Suraj – The Rising Star , Mottainai Grandma , and JICA’s SDGs initiative, “Comics for Empowering Women in India.”

b: Yudit Kornberg Greenberg is professor and a Fulbright-Nehru scholar of religion, gender and sexuality and a leader in interreligious dialogue. Dr. Greenberg’s articles and books include modern Jewish philosophy,…
f: Yudit Kornberg Greenberg is professor and a Fulbright-Nehru scholar of religion, gender and sexuality and a leader in interreligious dialogue. Dr. Greenberg’s articles and books include modern Jewish philosophy, Encyclopedia of Love in World Religions , The Body in Religion: Crosscultural Perspectives and Dharma and Halacha: Comparative Studies in Hindu-Jewish Philosophy and Religion.

b: Yuliya Musakovska is an internationally acclaimed Ukrainian poet and translator. She is the author of six poetry collections, including The God of Freedom , available in English translation and named one of the Top 10…
f: Yuliya Musakovska is an internationally acclaimed Ukrainian poet and translator. She is the author of six poetry collections, including The God of Freedom , available in English translation and named one of the Top 10 Ukraine-related books of 2024 by the Kyiv Independent . She is a winner of the Asian Prize for Poetry 2025. Her work has been translated into more than thirty languages.

b: Yuvan is a writer, naturalist, educator and activist based in Chennai. His interests include reimagining an Earth-centric and child-centric education in schools, the reciprocity between languages and ecologies, and…
f: Yuvan is a writer, naturalist, educator and activist based in Chennai. His interests include reimagining an Earth-centric and child-centric education in schools, the reciprocity between languages and ecologies, and ground-up processes of change and politics. He writes on ecology, education, alternatives and activism. He is currently travelling and documenting stories along the Indian coastline.

b: Zac O'Yeah is a Swedish detective novelist and author of the Majestic Trilogy, which is set in his Indian hometown, Bengaluru, and being made into an Indian film. He has published 18 books including several fiction and…
f: Zac O'Yeah is a Swedish detective novelist and author of the Majestic Trilogy, which is set in his Indian hometown, Bengaluru, and being made into an Indian film. He has published 18 books including several fiction and nonfiction bestsellers. His travel writings have appeared in magazines such as National Geographic Traveller and Vagabond, and also featured in many anthologies. He has been published in over 20 languages including German, French, Russian, Chinese and several Indian languages. His most recent book is Digesting India. A European film company is adapting his sci-fi novel Once Upon A Time in Scandinavistan as a big-budget Hollywood extravaganza.

b: Zac O’Yeah is a Swedish detective novelist and author of the Majestic Trilogy, which is set in his Indian hometown Bengaluru. He has published 15 books including several fiction and nonfiction bestsellers. His Gandhi…
f: Zac O’Yeah is a Swedish detective novelist and author of the Majestic Trilogy, which is set in his Indian hometown Bengaluru. He has published 15 books including several fiction and nonfiction bestsellers. His Gandhi biography Mahatma! was ranked as the best nonfiction book in Sweden in 2008. His travel writings have appeared in magazines such as National Geographic Traveller , Outlook Traveller, RES and Vagabond , and also been included in many anthologies. All in all he has written for more than 75 different publications, including the Times of India , Indian Express , New Indian Express, Forbes, GQ, amongst others. His writings have been translated into German, French, Norwegian, Danish, Finnish, Russian, Chinese and Kannada. He is a founder-director of Bangalore’s World-Famous Semi-Deluxe Writing Programme, the first semi-professional writing school in India. His most recent books include the novel Tropical Detectiv e and the travelogue A Walk Through Barygaza .

b: Zachary Leader is Professor of English Literature at the University of Roehampton. He is the author of Reading Blake’s Songs, Writer’s Block, Revision and Romantic Authorship, The Life of Kingsley Amis , a finalist…
f: Zachary Leader is Professor of English Literature at the University of Roehampton. He is the author of Reading Blake’s Songs, Writer’s Block, Revision and Romantic Authorship, The Life of Kingsley Amis , a finalist for the 2008 Pulitzer Prize in Biography, and The Life of Saul Bellow , a two-volume biography. He is a Fellow of the Royal Society of Literature.

b: Zain Memon is a visionary game designer, who has created 'SHASN' and 'AZADI' - the award-winning political strategy board games that have become India’s most successful table-top IP. Zain’s games and authorship have…
f: Zain Memon is a visionary game designer, who has created 'SHASN' and 'AZADI' - the award-winning political strategy board games that have become India’s most successful table-top IP. Zain’s games and authorship have introduced India to modern board games and created a new culture of table-top gaming in the country. SHASN is now played in over 70 countries across the globe. SHASN and AZADI have also won some of the highest honours in the industry, including the ‘Games for Change’ award and the ‘IndieCade Award for Social Impact’.

b: Zakir Hussain has been hailed in both the field of percussion and in the music world at large as an international phenomenon. A classical tabla virtuoso, his consistently brilliant and exciting performances have not…
f: Zakir Hussain has been hailed in both the field of percussion and in the music world at large as an international phenomenon. A classical tabla virtuoso, his consistently brilliant and exciting performances have not only established him as a national treasure in his own country, India, but gained him worldwide fame. His playing is marked by uncanny intuition and masterful improvisational dexterity, founded in formidable knowledge and study. Widely considered a chief architect of the contemporary world music movement, Hussain’s contribution to world music has been unique with many historic collaborations, including Shakti, which he founded with John McLaughlin and L. Shankar, Remember Shakti, the Diga Rhythm Band, Making Music, Planet Drum with Mickey Hart, Tabla Beat Science, Sangam with Charles Lloyd and Eric Harland and recordings and performances with artists as diverse as George Harrison, YoYo Ma, Joe Henderson, Van Morrison, Airto Moreira, Pharoah Sanders, Billy Cobham, Mark Morris, Rennie Harris, and the Kodo drummers. His contribution to music was honoured in April, 2009 with four sold-out concerts at Carnegie Hall’s Artist Perspective series.

b: Zameer Uddin Shah spent 40 years in the Indian Army and has experience in diplomacy, judiciary and education. He has participated in the 1971 operations in Longewala, counter-insurgency operations in North East India…
f: Zameer Uddin Shah spent 40 years in the Indian Army and has experience in diplomacy, judiciary and education. He has participated in the 1971 operations in Longewala, counter-insurgency operations in North East India and Punjab and commanded the force that quelled the 2002 riots in Gujarat. He retired of Deputy Chief of Army Staff in 2008. He is the author of The Sarkari Mussalman .

b: Zeina Hashem Beck is a prize-winning Lebanese poet. Her books include Louder than Hearts , winner of the 2016 May Sarton New Hampshire Poetry Prize, and There Was and How Much There Was , a 2016 Laureate’s Choice,…
f: Zeina Hashem Beck is a prize-winning Lebanese poet. Her books include Louder than Hearts , winner of the 2016 May Sarton New Hampshire Poetry Prize, and There Was and How Much There Was , a 2016 Laureate’s Choice, selected by Carol Ann Duffy. Widely published in journals and anthologies, her work won Best of the Net and Poetry Magazine’s Frederick Bock Prize.

b: Zikrur Rahman is the Founding Director of the India Arab Cultural Centre. A former Indian diplomat who has served in a number of Arab countries, including as Ambassador to Palestine. As Editor-in-Chief of the…
f: Zikrur Rahman is the Founding Director of the India Arab Cultural Centre. A former Indian diplomat who has served in a number of Arab countries, including as Ambassador to Palestine. As Editor-in-Chief of the prestigious Arabic literary journal Thaqafatul Hind , Professor Rahman has extensively contributed to the promotion of India-Arab cultural and literary ties. He has authored and translated a number of books in English, Arabic, Urdu and Hindi languages. His major works are Short Stories from India, Arabic Language and Literature in Delhi after 1947: Institutions, Scholars and their Contribution and Indian Scholars and their Contribution to the Islamic Sciences. His translated works include The Indian Heritage and Selected Works of Sanskrit Poetry . He has also researched and edited the Arabic translation of The Ramayana . At present, he is working on a translation of Geeta in Arabic. He was honoured with India’s prestigious Arabic Scholar Award by the President of India in 2014.

b: Zorawar Daulet Singh is a historian and strategist based in New Delhi. He is a founder of the Northcap University, a State Private University located in Gurgaon and is an adjunct fellow with the Institute of Chinese…
f: Zorawar Daulet Singh is a historian and strategist based in New Delhi. He is a founder of the Northcap University, a State Private University located in Gurgaon and is an adjunct fellow with the Institute of Chinese Studies, New Delhi. For the past decade, he has been a regular commentator and columnist on India’s foreign policy. His recent books include Power and Diplomacy: India’s Foreign Policies During the Cold War and Powershift: India–China Relations in a Multipolar World. Daulet Singh holds a PhD in international relations from King’s College London.

b: Zukiswa Wanner is the author of four novels, two works of non-fiction, two children’s books and several short stories. She is the curator of Artistic Encounters in Nairobi, an initiative that brings two different art…
f: Zukiswa Wanner is the author of four novels, two works of non-fiction, two children’s books and several short stories. She is the curator of Artistic Encounters in Nairobi, an initiative that brings two different art forms on stage at the same time. When not writing, the 2018 JIAS Writing Fellow works on her pan-African publishing venture, Paivapo.

b: Zulfikar Hirji is a historian and anthropologist of Islam and Muslim societies. His publications include Diversity and Pluralism in Muslim Contexts , The Ismailis: An Illustrated History , Between Empires: Sheikh-Sir…
f: Zulfikar Hirji is a historian and anthropologist of Islam and Muslim societies. His publications include Diversity and Pluralism in Muslim Contexts , The Ismailis: An Illustrated History , Between Empires: Sheikh-Sir Mbarak al-Hinawy (1896-1959) and Approaches to the Qur’an in sub-Saharan Africa . He is Associate Professor of Anthropology at York University, Toronto.

b: Zuni Chopra is a young writer. At 17 years of age, she has published two poetry books, a novel and a collection of short stories. Her first novel, The House that Spoke, came out in January 2017. The Island of the Day…
f: Zuni Chopra is a young writer. At 17 years of age, she has published two poetry books, a novel and a collection of short stories. Her first novel, The House that Spoke, came out in January 2017. The Island of the Day Before was released in August 2018. Chopra has a passion for fiction, especially fantasy and poetry.

b: Zygmunt Miłoszewski is a novelist, screenwriter, and social activist. Author of ten novels, including detective stories, adventure novels, and literature for young people. One of the most popular Polish writers at home…
f: Zygmunt Miłoszewski is a novelist, screenwriter, and social activist. Author of ten novels, including detective stories, adventure novels, and literature for young people. Founding member of the trade writing association Literary Union. An avid sailor, he lives in Warsaw or on a sailing yacht.

f: Åsne Seierstad has worked as a correspondent since 1993 in Russia, China, the Balkans, Afghanistan, Iraq and Syria, and has received numerous awards for her journalism. She has written six books. The Bookseller of Kabul was translated into over 40 languages. One of Us, about the far right terrorist Anders Breivik and his massacre in Norway, was selected as one of the ten best books of 2015 by The New York Times and was awarded the Leipzig Book Award for European Understanding 2018. Her latest work, Two Sisters , about two Norwegian-Somali sisters who joined ISIS in Syria, is one of Norway’s most sold books ever and was awarded the Brage Prize in Norway.
